roles.title: Fish and Game Wardens
roles.description: Patrol assigned area to prevent fish and game law violations. Investigate reports of damage to crops or property by wildlife. Compile biological data.

tasks.label: Participate in search-and-rescue operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ground search for a lost hunter, hiker, hunter-with-medical-emergency, or wandering child in backcountry/rural terrain: warden hikes, rides ATV/horse, works a grid or hasty search through brush and timber, locates the subject, assesses and treats them, and escorts or carries/litters them out to a road or landing zone.

Water rescue on a lake, bay, or river: warden runs the patrol boat to capsized boaters, swimmers in distress, or a stranded craft, pulls people from the water into the boat, provides first aid/warming, and transports them to a ramp or ambulance.

Drowning victim search and body recovery: warden sweeps the area from a boat with side-scan sonar, works grappling hooks/dive team/ROV over hours or days in murky water and current, recovers the body, and brings it ashore for the coroner.

Aerial search support: UAS-qualified warden launches a thermal-equipped drone at night or dusk over fields, riverbanks, brush, or flooded terrain, flies a search pattern over a defined area, detects the subject's heat signature, marks GPS coordinates, and guides ground/boat crews to them.

Flood/swiftwater disaster deployment: warden in a flat-bottom or jet boat works flooded neighborhoods and river bottoms, takes stranded residents (some elderly, injured, or with pets) off porches, rooftops, and vehicles, and ferries them to dry ground.

Winter or remote-access extraction: snowmobile, UTV, or ice-rescue response to an injured rider, fallen ice angler, or hypothermic subject; packaging the patient in a litter or rescue sled and hauling them over snow, ice, or rough two-track to the ambulance.

sources.system: Texas Game Warden UAS program (DJI/Autel thermal drones)
sources.title: Drones deliver hope: how Texas wildlife officials used UAVs to aid flood victims
sources.claim: State game wardens run drone teams that fly thermal-equipped UAS to search for missing and stranded people, paired with swiftwater rescue boat crews; the aircraft are flown by warden pilots (human-piloted, not autonomous).
sources.transferJustification: Directly this task: establishes what warden participation in SAR looks like and that the fielded aerial tool is pilot-flown.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Patrol Deployments with Skydio X10
sources.claim: Skydio X10, in service with US public safety agencies, flies fully autonomously day or night outdoors, including obstacle avoidance in zero-light conditions, and carries a thermal payload used for emergency response and search and rescue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is police aerial overwatch/response; transfers to warden aerial search because it is the same class of thermal-imaging aircraft flying unstructured outdoor terrain to put eyes on a person on the ground.

sources.system: DJI Dock 3 with FlightHub 2 Auto Dispatch
sources.title: Dock as First Responder - DJI Enterprise
sources.claim: Dock-based 'drone as first responder' systems are fielded and auto-dispatch an uncrewed aircraft from a weatherproof dock to a scene without a pilot on site, delivering aerial imagery of the location in about 100 seconds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated aerial response to 911 calls; transfers to warden aerial search because launch, navigation to a search area, and streaming of the overhead/thermal view are performed by the machine over open, uncontrolled terrain.

sources.system: Kennesaw State autonomous SAR drone (AI infrared/thermal person detection)
sources.developer: Kennesaw State University (Ali Baheri lab collaboration)
sources.title: Drones paired with AI could help search-and-rescue teams find missing persons faster
sources.claim: A research drone flies an autonomous grid search over outdoor search areas and its onboard AI locates and identifies missing persons in infrared/thermal/color imagery, assessing whether the subject is upright or down and estimating condition.

sources.system: Iredell County Sheriff's Office lake enforcement ROV and sonar
sources.title: Sonar technology helps Iredell County Sheriff's Office lake enforcement team recover drowning victims faster
sources.claim: Underwater search and recovery of drowning victims by sheriff/lake-patrol units is done with a remotely operated vehicle plus sonar, with human operators driving the vehicle and interpreting the imagery; no autonomous recovery system is in service.

sources.system: Robobuoy (deep-learning drowning detection + unmanned surface vehicle)
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Applied System Innovation)
sources.title: Towards Intelligent Water Safety: Robobuoy, a Deep Learning-Based Drowning Detection and Autonomous Surface Vehicle Rescue System
sources.claim: Autonomous water-rescue vehicles that detect a drowning person and drive a flotation buoy to them exist only as research prototypes evaluated in controlled water; they deliver flotation and do not board, treat, or transport the victim.

sources.title: US Army seeks 'last mile' robot for medevac and resupply
sources.claim: As of 2026 the US Army is still soliciting an unmanned ground vehicle able to move casualties from the point of ...; this is a requirements notice, not a fielded capability, indicating no deployed robot performs casualty extraction over rough terrain.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is battlefield casualty evacuation over rough ground, the closest analogue to carrying an injured subject out of the backcountry; the state of the art is a solicitation, so no capability transfers.

tasks.label: Compile and present evidence for court actions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Protect and preserve native wildlife, plants, or ecosystems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Enforcement patrol and interdiction to protect protected wildlife/plants: driving, boating, ATV or foot patrol of an assigned district of forest, marsh, rangeland, lake or coast; watching for poaching, illegal netting, out-of-season take, protected-plant collecting or habitat destruction; contacting hunters/anglers, checking licenses and bags, pulling illegal nets/snares/traps, seizing gear, writing citations, and investigating reported habitat-damage or pollution incidents on private and public land.

Wildlife incident response and animal handling: darting, netting, trapping or hazing a nuisance bear, moose, alligator or cougar in a town or ranch yard; freeing entangled deer, raptors or sea turtles; capturing and transporting injured or orphaned animals; euthanizing and removing carcasses; all outdoors, in variable weather, around bystanders and pets.

Invasive and undesirable vegetation control to preserve native plant communities: spot-treating or mechanically removing weeds (knapweed, phragmites, kudzu, water hyacinth) from wildlife-management-area fields, food plots, refuge units, riparian strips and boat-ramp areas; maintaining native plantings free of competing weeds over a season.

Native vegetation establishment over degraded habitat: broadcast seeding or planting native grasses, forbs, shrubs or conifers across burn scars, eroded stream banks, retired fields or reclaimed sites, over areas of tens to hundreds of acres, with follow-up survival checks.

Habitat structures and access control: building and repairing wildlife-friendly fence, water guzzlers, nest boxes and platforms, brush piles, in-stream structures and fish passage; posting boundary and closure signage; blocking illegal off-road trails; hauling materials into remote sites with hand tools and an ATV/truck.

Population and habitat condition surveys supporting protective management: thermal or aerial counts of deer, elk, waterfowl or seabird colonies; acoustic/net fish abundance surveys on lakes and coastal waters; spawning-bed, nest and den checks; water-condition sampling — flown, boated or walked over open country and open water in variable conditions.

sources.system: Naïo Oz / Dino / Ted weeding robots
sources.title: Futuristic Farming Has Arrived with Weeding Robots - Modern Farmer
sources.claim: Naïo Technologies sells autonomous electric weeding robots (Oz, Dino, Ted) that navigate crop rows and mechanically remove weeds on commercial vegetable farms and vineyards without a driver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical weed removal among planted rows. Transfers to a warden's invasive/undesirable plant control on managed habitat plantings — same plant-vs-plant discrimination, same soil-level precision — but only where the ground is cultivated and laid out to a standard.

sources.title: Carbon Robotics introduces the new Carbon AutoTractor autonomy kit - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder identifies and kills weeds with computer vision and lasers, and its 2025 AutoTractor kit provides driverless operation of the tractor pulling it, with remote operators handling occasional interventions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: selective weed killing in a cultivated field. Comparable to removing invasive plants from a managed habitat unit — same targets (broadleaf/grass weeds), centimetre precision, and outdoor daylight/night operation — provided the site is a prepared, row-planted field.

sources.title: AI Weed Control: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder - Lidar News
sources.claim: Carbon Robotics' laser weeding machines are in commercial field service at scale across many countries, indicating routine production use rather than demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (selective weed removal); cited to establish deployment maturity of the weeding system in structured cropland.

sources.title: AirSeed Technologies, CAL International partner to plant 100M trees with drones - The Robot Report
sources.claim: AirSeed's octocopter drones take off autonomously, fly pre-programmed plans over degraded and deforested land, and dispense seed pods at high rate for commercial revegetation contracts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial broadcast planting of native tree/shrub seed over open, unimproved terrain — the same act a warden performs when seeding a burn scar or eroded bank, over the same kind of unmanaged ground.

sources.system: Reforestation seeding drone swarms (AirSeed, Mast Reforestation/DroneSeed)
sources.title: Johnny Appleseeds of the Sky: UAS for Reforestation - Inside Unmanned Systems
sources.claim: Reforestation seeding drone operators fly swarms over remote post-fire and degraded sites, each drone seeding roughly 150 acres per day under a single supervising flight team, with routes set from ecological data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: large-area native revegetation of wildland after fire, the same restoration act wardens support; supervision is one team for many autonomous aircraft, i.e. limited intervention.

sources.developer: Saildrone / NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center
sources.title: Ocean-Going Robots Effective At Surveying Pollock | NOAA Fisheries
sources.claim: NOAA Fisheries used Saildrone uncrewed surface vehicles sailing autonomously for a 60-day acoustic survey of the eastern Bering Sea, and the data contributed to an annual abundance estimate for the pollock stock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fish abundance survey used for resource protection decisions — the same survey product wardens help collect, delivered autonomously over open water taken as found.

sources.system: Thermal-imaging survey drones (DJI Matrice-class with thermal payload)
sources.developer: university wildlife research programs (reported by The Wildlife Society)
sources.title: WSB: Drones with thermal cameras estimate mammal abundance - The Wildlife Society
sources.claim: Thermal-camera drones flying repeatable programmed transects produced mammal population counts 90-92% accurate against known abundance in open country.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nocturnal thermal wildlife counts over rangeland — the same deer/elk survey wardens run, at accuracy comparable to accepted survey methods, with the aircraft flying pre-programmed transects.

sources.title: BurnBot can help US fight wildfires with safer, prescribed burns - Interesting Engineering
sources.claim: BurnBot's vegetation-treatment and prescribed-fire machines, used for habitat fuel reduction, are driven remotely by trained operators from up to 500 feet away rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized habitat fuel/vegetation treatment on wildland. Cited as a teleoperation counterexample: the leading field machine for this work still requires a continuous human operator, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Patrol assigned areas by car, boat, airplane, horse, or on foot to enforce game, fish, or boating laws or to manage wildlife programs, lakes, or land.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Truck patrol of an assigned rural district: driving gravel/forest roads, county highways and public-land access points during a hunting season, stopping at boat ramps and trailheads, watching for road-hunting, spotlighting and trespass, and making field contacts with hunters and anglers to check licenses, tags, weapons and bag limits, in mud, snow, dust and darkness.

Patrol boat operation on inland lakes and rivers: launching and running a patrol vessel in wind, chop and low light, approaching and boarding recreational boats for registration, life-jacket and BUI checks, inspecting live wells and creels against limits, and locating illegal trotlines, nets or unattended gear along shorelines.

Long-duration surveillance patrol of a large water body (Great Lakes, coastal bays, big-water commercial fishing grounds) whose output is detection and reporting of illegal vessel/fishing activity to enforcement, rather than routine boarding of every contact.

Foot and horseback patrol away from roads: hiking or riding into fields, timber, marshes, river bottoms or backcountry wilderness, often before dawn or after dark, to observe waterfowl blinds, deer stands and camps from concealment, check bait piles and tags, walk boundary and shoreline stretches, and contact people encountered off-road.

Aerial patrol in a fixed-wing aircraft or helicopter over a large district: flying river corridors, reservoirs, marshes and remote timber for several hours to spot baited fields, illegal nets, ATV trespass, night spotlighting or over-limit activity, and radioing coordinates to ground officers for interception.

Patrol of agency-managed lands and waters (wildlife management area, refuge, public access site): driving and walking the unit to check gates, signs, boundary markers, water-control structures and blinds, verify permit compliance by users, and record wildlife observations for program management.

sources.title: Coast Guard deploys autonomous vessels across the Great Lakes | WorkBoat
sources.claim: A fleet of 16 Saildrone ... is deployed under a US Coast Guard contract to conduct persistent, wind- and solar-powered autonomous patrol/surveillance of open water across the Great Lakes and ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: maritime domain awareness patrol for illegal fishing/border activity. It transfers to a warden's large-water surveillance patrol because the medium (open lake water taken as found), the sensing-and-reporting output, and the multi-week endurance on unimproved water are the same; it does not transfer to boarding or contact work.

sources.title: Coast Guard Deploys Saildrone Vessels On Great Lakes This Summer
sources.claim: The Saildrone USVs patrol all five Great Lakes from May through October 2026, monitoring vessel traffic and tracking illegal activity.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: persistent water patrol to detect illegal activity, matching the surveillance-only slice of warden boat patrol on big water.

sources.title: Knightscope Unveils Major K5 Robot Upgrade, Lands First Police Department Contract
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot performs unattended patrol of client premises (parking lots, campuses, facilities), providing deterrence and reporting rather than enforcement contact; navigation upgrades target larger facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: security guard patrol. It is the closest fielded analogue to ground patrol, but it runs on paved, mapped, institution-controlled premises and delivers only observation/alerting, so it does not carry over to off-road wildland patrol with license checks and citations.

sources.title: Orbit 5.0 adds features to Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped executes autonomous pre-mapped patrol missions inside industrial facilities, capturing inspection imagery at defined points of interest.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: legged autonomous foot patrol/inspection. Relevant to warden foot patrol as the best legged-mobility evidence, but demonstrations are on pre-mapped industrial premises, not off-trail marsh, timber or backcountry, and involve no person-contact enforcement.

sources.title: DSEI 2025: Skydio Dock for X10 Drone Enhances Autonomous Surveillance for Emergency Response and Infrastructure Security
sources.claim: Skydio X10 drones flying autonomously from a dock are used by US police departments for drone-as-first-responder aerial coverage under FAA beyond-visual-line-of-sight waivers, with a remote pilot in command supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial law-enforcement patrol/overwatch. Environment (open outdoor airspace) is comparable, but coverage is a short radius around a dock with ~30-40 minute endurance, far short of the multi-hour, district-wide wildland aerial patrol and violation identification in this task.

tasks.label: Investigate hunting accidents or reports of fish or game law violations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Responding to a report of fishing violations on a lake, river or shoreline: locating the party, boarding or approaching the boat, checking licenses, counting and measuring fish in coolers/livewells, inspecting nets, lines and gear, seizing illegal gear or over-limit fish as evidence, questioning the anglers, and issuing a citation or warning with a written report.

Night poaching / spotlighting investigation from a tip or shots-heard report on rural roads, fields and woodlots: locating a killed or wounded deer, examining and recovering the carcass, collecting projectiles, blood and tissue samples, photographing tracks and vehicle evidence, stopping and interviewing occupants of a suspect vehicle, seizing firearms and game, and documenting the case.

Follow-up investigation at a suspect's residence, hunting camp or outbuilding: knock-and-talk interview, consent or warrant search of freezers, garages, sheds and mounted trophies, comparing tags/licenses to seized animals, seizing contraband, and writing the case report.

Hunting accident / firearms-injury scene investigation in wooded or field terrain: securing the scene alongside EMS, locating the shooter's stand and the victim's position, measuring distances and angles, recovering casings, wads and pellets, examining and unloading firearms, photographing and diagramming the scene, interviewing witnesses, and preparing an incident reconstruction report.

Compliance investigation at a licensed commercial facility or check station (fish dealer, seafood processor, taxidermist, dock or big-game check station): auditing purchase and tagging records, counting/measuring and species-identifying product in coolers and freezers, verifying tags against paperwork, interviewing the operator, and seizing untagged or undersized product.

sources.system: Skydio X10 with Dock / DFR Command
sources.title: Transforming Drone as First Responder: Skydio's new Dock for X10 and DFR Command Solution
sources.claim: Skydio's Drone as First Responder system autonomously launches from a dock and flies to an incident scene to provide aerial imagery before officers arrive; it observes only and performs no evidence handling, questioning, seizure or citation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial response to crime/incident scenes. It is the closest deployed robotic capability to a warden responding to a violation report, but it delivers only a video feed: no scene examination, sampling, seizure, interviewing or report-of-record, so it cannot complete an investigation instance.

sources.title: How Undercover Robotic Animals Are Helping Catch Poachers
sources.claim: Custom Robotic Wildlife robotic deer decoys are used by state game wardens as bait in poaching enforcement operations; wardens hidden nearby observe the shot and then conduct the stop, interview, seizure and citation themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: the only robot routinely fielded in wildlife-law enforcement. Its head/tail motion is radio-controlled by an officer and it performs no investigative act, so it cannot substantiate completion of any instance.

sources.system: PRIME (Police Robot for Inspection and Mapping of underwater Evidence)
sources.developer: University of Bath / Avon and Somerset Police collaboration
sources.title: A prototype autonomous robot for underwater crime scene investigation and emergency response
sources.claim: PRIME is a prototype autonomous surface/underwater vehicle that surveys shallow water to locate items of evidentiary interest for police, tested with a mannequin in a harbour; it maps and images only and does not recover, document or adjudicate evidence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic search of an aquatic crime scene, nearest analogue to a warden investigating submerged illegal nets or evidence. It is a research prototype limited to sonar mapping, with no manipulation, interviewing or case output.

sources.title: How the K5 Robot Patrols Without Human Help
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot patrols fixed premises such as campuses and parking lots without human driving, streaming video and reading plates; it has no manipulator and takes no investigative or enforcement action.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ground patrol of a controlled facility (E2). It shows mobile autonomy in structured human facilities but provides no manipulation, sampling, questioning or evidentiary output, so it cannot complete a compliance investigation.

sources.system: Robotic fish processing and grading lines (e.g., Marel vision grading / robotic cutting cells)
sources.title: Can robots be incorporated into fish processing?
sources.claim: Robotic fish-processing lines with machine vision measure, identify and grade individual fish presented on a conveyor inside processing plants, performing cutting and sorting decisions automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated measuring and species/size grading of fish on a fixtured line (E1). It covers only one measurement sub-step of a dealer inspection and cannot audit records, question an operator, seize product or produce a legal case file, so it does not transfer to completing the instance.

tasks.label: Provide assistance to other local law enforcement agencies as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mutual-aid backup on a call for service in a rural county: warden self-dispatches to a roadside traffic stop, DUI, domestic disturbance or suspicious-vehicle call as the nearest sworn officer, drives to an unfamiliar rural road or private driveway at night, provides cover for the deputy, contacts and controls subjects, assists with handcuffing, frisk and vehicle search, and files a supplemental report.

Assisting a sheriff's office with a search-and-rescue or body-recovery call: ground search for a lost hiker, hunter, dementia patient or drowning victim across woods, fields, marsh or a lake, using patrol truck, ATV, boat and sonar in variable weather and terrain, then locating, assessing, first-aiding and extracting the subject to responders.

Emergency/disaster support on public roads and waterways: traffic control and road closure at a crash or downed-tree scene, scene perimeter for a fatality investigation, evacuation of residents during a flood or wildfire, swift-water rescue and shuttling of stranded people by patrol boat.

Assisting with searches and apprehensions on rural land: containing a perimeter and tracking a fleeing suspect into timber or swamp, serving a warrant at a remote camp, guiding deputies to illegal marijuana grows or dump sites, and searching brush and shoreline for discarded evidence.

Uniformed detail at a venue whose owner controls access — county fairground, festival, boat race, school or courthouse: crowd management, directing parking, intervening in disputes, checking credentials, and making arrests or ejections at the request of the local agency.

Specialized platform and logistical support to another agency: ferrying deputies or a K9 team by patrol boat, ATV or UTV into terrain their cruisers cannot reach, hauling and operating winches, sonar or dive gear, recovering vehicles from water, and transporting a prisoner or evidence back to town.

sources.title: Government | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped is fielded by more than 60 US and Canadian police bomb squads and SWAT teams for hazardous-scene entry and observation, but the vendor describes it as a platform an operator drives remotely; it does not autonomously handle law-enforcement scenes.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic analog to an officer providing on-scene assistance to another agency (SWAT/bomb-squad support). It shows the state of the art is remote investigation and observation, not autonomous scene control, subject contact, or rescue.

sources.title: Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR) Privacy Impact Assessment (VA)
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots patrol controlled institutional campuses (e.g., a VA health care system) without a driver, but their function is monitoring, deterrence and data collection for human police, not physical intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous uniformed-presence patrol on an institution-controlled campus (E2). Transfer fails for this task because the robot only observes and reports; it cannot manage crowds, intervene in disputes, detain, or render aid.

sources.title: Incident 77: Knightscope's Park Patrol Robot Ignored Bystander Pressing Emergency Button to Alert Police about Fight
sources.claim: A K5 robot patrolling a public park failed to respond when a bystander pressed its emergency button during a nearby fight, illustrating that autonomous security robots do not deliver officer-quality assistance at incidents.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting type as the venue/event-detail instance; documents that an autonomous patrol robot cannot perform the responsive, physical portion of law-enforcement assistance.

sources.system: Skydio X10 with Dock / DFR Command (LVMPD and other agencies)
sources.title: The BVLOS Revolution Continues: Introducing Multi-Drone Operations | Skydio
sources.claim: Drone-as-first-responder systems launch autonomously from docks to calls under a remote pilot who may supervise up to four aircraft, but their output is live video and situational awareness delivered to human officers who still respond on scene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial support to police calls and searches, the closest autonomous system to a warden's assistance role. It supplies imagery only and cannot search ground on foot, extract a victim, control traffic, or assist an arrest, so it cannot complete any instance.

tasks.label: Issue warnings or citations and file reports as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide advice or information to park or reserve visitors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Serve warrants and make arrests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field custody arrest during patrol in remote outdoor terrain (woods, marsh, field, boat ramp): after detecting a violation such as night hunting, spotlighting, or an over-limit take, the warden gives verbal commands to an armed hunter or angler, secures weapons, handcuffs and pat-searches the subject, walks them over uneven ground to the patrol truck, and transports them to a county jail.

Roadside or check-station arrest arising from a vehicle stop: warden runs the subject, gets a warrant hit or observes an arrestable offense (DUI, resisting, illegal transport of game), conducts field sobriety or questioning, handcuffs and secures the person and any firearms in the vehicle, and transports for booking.

Arrest on the water: vessel stop for a boating-under-the-influence or commercial fishing violation, boarding a rocking boat, controlling and restraining the subject on deck, securing the vessel and catch as evidence, and returning the person to a dock for transport.

Serving an arrest or search warrant at a private residence, hunting camp, or trailer, often with a partner or sheriff's deputy: knock and announce, identify the named individual among occupants, hand over or execute the papers, take the person into custody, and secure the scene against dogs, bystanders, and firearms.

Serving process or making an arrest at an institutionally controlled premises: a licensed fish dealer, taxidermy shop, processing plant, marina office, or a courthouse/jail handoff, where a business or agency controls access and the subject is generally compliant.

Non-compliant subject: the person flees on foot or by vehicle/boat or physically resists; the warden pursues, applies graduated force and control holds in mud, brush, or water, restrains and cuffs the subject, and manages any injuries before transport.

sources.title: Dublin, Ohio, robot cop sent back after zero arrests in parking garage
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot ('DubBot'), deployed by Dublin, Ohio police for roughly a year in a city parking garage, patrolled autonomously but produced no arrests, citations, or detentions, and was returned to the manufacturer in 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed law-enforcement patrol robot; it performs the patrol-and-detect portion of enforcement work in a structured facility but demonstrably does not detain, cite, or take anyone into custody, so it cannot substantiate arrest or warrant service.

sources.developer: Lubbock County Sheriff's Office / Lubbock Police (bomb squad platform)
sources.title: Wanted man barricaded in Lubbock motel room shot, gassed out and taken into custody
sources.claim: A remote-controlled bomb-squad robot was used by Lubbock, Texas authorities to gas and physically pin a barricaded armed suspect, after which human officers took him into custody.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (physically subduing a person during an arrest), but the machine is continuously remote-operated and only immobilized the suspect in an emergency standoff; human officers performed the restraint, search, and transport.

sources.system: Sacramento County Sheriff's Office FPV drone with magnet payload
sources.title: Robot Police Officers - Schneier on Security
sources.claim: A Sacramento County Sheriff's drone, flown by a human pilot wearing FPV goggles, removed a knife from an armed ... inside a house during a standoff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task of physically intervening on a suspect inside a dwelling during warrant/standoff service; it is fully piloted by an officer and only disarms, so it does not substantiate autonomous custody or service of process.

sources.developer: Various conservation programs (e.g., Save the Elephants partners)
sources.title: Drones: the fight against poaching in Africa - Save the Elephants
sources.claim: In wildlife law enforcement, drones are used to detect poachers and relay the information to human rangers, who carry out the interception and apprehension.
sources.transferJustification: Same occupational domain (wildlife enforcement patrol); shows that even where robotics is routine, the apprehension step is performed by human rangers, with the robot limited to detection and reporting.

tasks.label: Arrange for disposition of fish or game illegally taken or possessed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Big game (deer, elk, bear, antelope) seized in a poaching case: warden field-dresses or tags the carcass in woods, fields or on a roadside, drags/loads 100-200 lb of animal into a truck, hauls it out and routes it to a processor, charity freezer or evidence locker, documenting chain of custody.

Illegally taken fish at a boat ramp, dock, marina or shoreline creel check: over-limit, undersized or closed-season fish are counted, measured, photographed, then live fish are returned to the water and dead fish are iced, bagged for evidence or donated/destroyed.

Small game, waterfowl, turkeys or furbearers seized in the field, at a hunting camp or from a vehicle: birds/animals are bagged and tagged individually, held in a cooler, then frozen as evidence or given to a charitable recipient.

Transfer of already-seized game or fish into its final disposition at a facility: warden drives to the agency evidence freezer, a participating meat processor, jail kitchen or food bank, unloads bags/boxes, weighs and logs the donation, obtains receipts and completes chain-of-custody paperwork.

Spoiled or unsalvageable animals (wanton waste, roadside dumping, hot-weather kills, diseased animals): warden decides the meat is unfit, then drags the carcass off the road or into cover for scavengers, buries it, or hauls it to a landfill, incinerator or renderer.

sources.system: Marel F- and M-lines; Frontmatec AiRA; DMRI bung dropper
sources.developer: Marel, Frontmatec, Scott, Danish Meat Research Institute
sources.title: Robot Technology for Pork and Beef Meat Slaughtering Process: A Review (Animals 2023)
sources.claim: Commercial slaughterhouse robot lines from Marel, Frontmatec, Scott and DMRI autonomously handle, track and process whole pork/beef/lamb carcasses presented on a rail inside purpose-built cells, at 350-1400 carcasses per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and routing of whole large-animal carcasses. A seized deer or elk is the same object class, mass and floppiness as a lamb or pork carcass, and the disposition step (grip, move, route to a destination) is the handling the line already performs, in a fenced cell where carcasses arrive fixtured on a gambrel.

sources.system: LEAP X-ray Primal / automated lamb boning room
sources.developer: Scott Automation (Robotic Technologies Ltd) / Silver Fern Farms
sources.title: One giant LEAP for robo meatworks - Farmers Weekly
sources.claim: Scott Automation's X-ray guided automated primal lamb cutting system (LEAP) is installed and running in commercial meat plants, handling whole carcass sections without manual cutting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling/processing of carcasses of deer-comparable size in a fenced processing cell; shows commercially accepted quality and reliability for machine handling of whole carcass units brought to the machine.

sources.title: RFID SORT CHILLER Harvey Beef (AMPC final report)
sources.claim: In a commercial beef plant, carcass sides are automatically graded at a weigh station, assigned a chiller destination by the production system, and tracked by an RFID chip in the gambrel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated identity tagging and destination routing of individual carcasses. This is the machine analogue of tagging seized game and routing it to a designated disposition (evidence freezer, donation, destruction) with an auditable record.

sources.system: Marel SmartLine Grader / whole-fish grading systems
sources.title: Whitefish processing (JBT Marel brochure)
sources.claim: Marel/JBT whole-fish graders autonomously take whole fish from an automatic infeed, size and sort them in continuous flow, and deliver them to batch takeaway systems in fish plants worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated measurement and sorting of whole fish into destination bins, the same physical operation as measuring seized fish and routing them to evidence, donation or destruction, when the fish are presented to the machine on a conveyor.

sources.title: Through the tubes: Using pneumatic tubes to transport fish, this company's fish passage is in demand
sources.claim: The Whooshh Passage Portal autonomously scans wild fish, distinguishes hatchery, wild and invasive fish, and routes them accordingly at rates up to 40 fish per ..., deployed at Columbia River dams.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated species/origin identification and physical routing of live fish to different destinations, which is the disposition decision-and-transfer step a warden performs for live illegally taken fish, executed in a purpose-built fish-handling installation.

sources.title: Transfer Machine 102 / Crate Handling System - BAADER Poultry
sources.claim: Poultry plants use commercial automatic crate destacking, conveying and bird transfer machines that move whole birds between lines without manual handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling of whole bird carcasses presented by conveyor/shackle. Seized waterfowl, turkeys and small game are comparable objects, and the disposition step here is transfer into a container or freezer rather than cutting.

sources.title: Cold Storage Operations at Lineage Transforming Food Distribution
sources.claim: Cold-storage operator Lineage runs automated cranes and case-picking systems ... refrigerated facilities that receive, store, retrieve and dispatch frozen goods.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated receipt, identified storage and later retrieval/dispatch of frozen product, which is the physical core of holding seized game in an evidence freezer and later releasing it to a processor or charity, when goods are presented palletized to the machine.

sources.title: DHL to deploy 1,000 Boston Dynamics Robots in Warehouses
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cases from trailers in logistics warehouses and is deployed in multiple DHL sites, but its demonstrated scope is uniform cases in walled trailers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous case handling inside a structured human work facility. It bounds what is achievable at E2: uniform boxes from a trailer, not loose carcasses, coolers of fish or mixed game bags from a pickup bed, and no custody handoff.

sources.system: Broiler mortality removal robot; Birds Eye Robotics platform
sources.developer: University research groups; Birds Eye Robotics
sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: Challenges and opportunities - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Robots that autonomously find and pick up dead birds off the floor of poultry barns remain research prototypes, with collection success rates topping out around 90% under favourable lighting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pickup of loose bird carcasses from an unfixtured floor inside an institution-controlled facility. Its prototype status and error rate are why picking up seized birds or carcasses at E2 is not credited.

tasks.label: Promote or provide hunter or trapper safety training.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Warden teaches or co-teaches a classroom hunter education session at a school, sportsman's club, fire hall, or agency office: lecture on firearm safety, wildlife law, and ethics, video segments, question-and-answer, and administering/grading the written exam.

Warden runs or assists at an in-person 'field day': demonstrating safe firearm handling, walking students through a simulated trail with shoot/don't-shoot scenarios, supervising a live-fire exercise on a range, and evaluating each student's handling before certification.

Promotional and outreach work: staffing an agency booth at a county fair or sport show, giving talks to scout troops and civic groups, radio/TV interviews and social media posts urging hunters to take safety courses, and distributing course brochures to license vendors.

Program administration and volunteer-instructor support: recruiting, training, and certifying volunteer hunter-education instructors, scheduling classes, maintaining course rosters and certification records, and supplying training materials and inert props.

Informal one-on-one safety instruction during routine field contacts: advising a hunter found with an uncased loaded firearm, coaching a novice trapper on humane trap setting and check requirements, and referring people to formal trapper-education courses.

Delivering or coordinating specialized trapper-education and bowhunter-education sessions, including demonstrating trap types, trap setting and release techniques, and treestand safety to small groups.

tasks.label: Seize equipment used in fish and game law violations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field/roadside or boat-ramp enforcement contact with a hunter or angler present: warden establishes the violation, tells the subject their gear is being seized, takes custody of a rifle/shotgun/bow, spotlight, rods, decoys, or illegally taken game, unloads and makes the firearm safe, writes a property receipt, tags the items and secures them in the patrol truck for booking into evidence. Occurs on dirt roads, fields, woods, riverbanks, day or night, in all weather, with a potentially uncooperative or armed subject.

On-water vessel boarding: warden stops a boat on a lake, bay or river, inspects the catch and gear, and seizes illegal gill nets, trotlines, traps, undersized or over-limit fish, and sometimes the fishing gear itself, hauling wet, heavy, tangled net and coolers of fish across to the patrol boat in wind and chop while managing the people aboard.

Recovery of unattended/abandoned illegal gear with no suspect present: unmarked or illegal gill nets, set lines, fish traps, crab or lobster pots, snares, leg-hold traps or bait piles found during patrol; the warden pulls the gear from the water or ground (often submerged, muddy, entangled in vegetation), hauls it to the boat or truck, photographs and tags it, and transports it as evidence.

Seizure of a large conveyance or major equipment used in the violation: an ATV, truck, boat and trailer, or airboat used to take game unlawfully; the warden secures the machine, arranges towing or drives/tows it out over rough ground to an impound lot, and completes the impound paperwork.

Seizure at premises under a warrant or a commercial inspection: a fish house, seafood market, taxidermy shop, meat processor, or a private residence/garage; the warden serves process, sorts through freezers, coolers, shelves and workbenches to identify unlawful product and the processing or hunting equipment involved, boxes and inventories it, and hauls it out to a vehicle with an evidence freezer.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Los Angeles Police Department
sources.title: Unleashed: LAPD SWAT integrates 'robot dog' into the unit
sources.claim: Police use of a legged robot to pick up and remove a weapon from a scene is remotely piloted by an officer, not autonomous, showing that machine seizure of property from a person is not an autonomous capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: police removal of a weapon/contraband from a scene, the closest analogue to a warden taking custody of gear from a subject. It is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic arm identifies, grasps and moves individual items from a wide catalogue of diverse products inside caged robotic workcells in fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bin picking of varied objects into containers. Transfers to the containerizing step of seizure when items are presented fixtured at E1 — comparable object sizes and grasp precision — but only in a purpose-built cell, with the item already presented.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics (deployed by DHL Supply Chain)
sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: A mobile robotic arm autonomously unloads mixed cases from trailers in commercial logistics operations at high rates, handling stacking variation and fallen boxes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling and loading of boxed goods, comparable to boxing and loading seized product; but demonstrated only on standard cases presented in a trailer/dock lane, with no identification of contraband or legal custody function.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich / Subsea Tech and EU consortium
sources.title: Autonomous underwater waste collection soon to be a reality
sources.claim: An autonomous underwater robot detects, grasps and lifts submerged debris — including heavy items such as tires, metal ship parts and fences — from a harbor seabed with no crew aboard, demonstrated in the port of Marseille.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating and lifting submerged objects, akin to pulling an abandoned net or trap. It is a research demonstration in an institution-controlled port basin, on rigid litter rather than entangling nets, and with no evidence-handling or custody function.

sources.title: Smart acoustic tagging and robotic recovery systems for ghost gear pollution
sources.claim: Robotic ghost-gear recovery systems rely on remotely operated vehicles guided to gear that was pre-fitted with acoustic tags, rather than autonomous discovery and recovery of untagged illegal gear.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieval of lost fishing gear from the seabed. Autonomy is partial and it depends on pre-installed tags absent from illegally set gear, so it cannot support a positive judgment for seizing untagged illegal gear.

tasks.label: Address schools, civic groups, sporting clubs, or the media to disseminate information concerning wildlife conservation and regulations.

tasks.label: Recommend revisions in hunting and trapping regulations or in animal management programs so that wildlife balances or habitats can be maintained.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial
