tasks.label: Inspect commercial operations relating to fish or wildlife, recreation, or protected areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At-sea or dockside boarding of a commercial fishing vessel: check captain/crew licenses and permits, inspect the catch in the hold (species, size, quantity), measure fish, inspect gear (net mesh, escape panels, traps, tags), compare against logbooks/VMS, and document any violation. Wet, moving deck, weather, uncooperative or busy crew.

Inspection of a licensed seafood dealer, wholesaler, or fish processing plant: audit purchase/landing records and tags against product on hand, walk coolers and freezers, weigh and identify product, check for undersized or out-of-season species, and issue findings. Indoor plant with fixed layout under company control.

Inspection of a small commercial licensee premises — bait shop, license vendor, taxidermist, fur buyer, commercial deer/game processor: check the license posting, tag and record books, freezer contents and specimen tags, and interview the proprietor about discrepancies. Retail/back-room setting.

Field inspection of a commercial guide, outfitter, hunting lease, game farm, or shooting preserve: verify guide licenses and client licenses, check harvest/tagging records and captive-animal records, inspect camp, blinds, bait, pens and fences on private rural land in variable terrain and weather.

Inspection of commercial and public recreation operations: charter/head boats, marina and boat-launch concessions, campground and outfitter concessions in parks and refuges — check passenger licenses, catch limits, safety and permit compliance, and posted-area boundaries, on docks, ramps and shorelines open to the public.

Inspection of a permitted captive-wildlife or aquaculture operation: licensed exhibitor, rehabilitator, pet dealer, or fish farm — verify permits and acquisition/disposition records, count and identify animals or stock, check holding conditions and escapement/health rules, and write the compliance report.

sources.title: US Coast Guard Expands Maritime Surveillance With Saildrone Voyager Fleet
sources.claim: Saildrone Voyager uncrewed surface vessels operate autonomously for the US Coast Guard on missions that include monitoring illegal and unregulated fishing and fisheries monitoring in the Northeast, i.e. remote detection and imaging of vessels rather than boarding or inspecting them.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic analog to fisheries enforcement: it surveils commercial fishing vessels but performs no boarding, records check, catch measurement, or compliance determination, so it does not transfer to the inspection task.

sources.title: Supporting Coast Guard Missions in the Great Lakes and Northeast – Saildrone
sources.claim: Saildrone USVs are used by the Coast Guard to monitor fishing vessel activity where enforcement coverage is limited, providing persistent surveillance rather than inspection of operations.
sources.transferJustification: Same domain (commercial fisheries enforcement) but the capability is remote monitoring; the inspection task requires physical access to catch, gear and records aboard or ashore.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics’ Spot robot gets AI upgrade for fully automated industrial inspections
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds at hundreds of industrial sites, reading gauges, checking indicator lights and capturing thermal data — asset condition inspection inside structured facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility inspection rounds in an E2 plant. It transfers only for passive sensing of fixed assets; it does not open coolers, handle product, audit tag books, or make regulatory findings.

sources.title: Spot | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot is sold for planning and running autonomous inspection rounds and operator rounds in customer facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled inspection rounds in structured facilities; relevant because dealer/plant inspections occur in similar buildings, but the robot's output is equipment data, not a compliance inspection of records and product.

sources.developer: University of Aberdeen / Marine Laboratory Aberdeen
sources.title: Automated measurement of species and length of fish by computer vision - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: The CatchMeter machine-vision system identifies species and measures lengths of fish carried on a conveyor under a camera — automated catch measurement in a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: species ID and size measurement of catch, one physical sub-step of a catch inspection. It does not cover permits, logbook reconciliation, gear checks, or enforcement action, so it cannot complete an inspection instance.

sources.title: Drones For Inshore Fisheries Management - AIFCA
sources.claim: Drones used for inshore fisheries enforcement are flown by officers to obtain imagery and ... for evidence of closure or licensing breaches.
sources.transferJustification: Same enforcement domain; shows current robotic use is officer-piloted evidence gathering, which cannot substantiate autonomous completion of an inspection.

sources.title: Autonomous warehouse drones streamline inventory control | TechTarget
sources.claim: Verity autonomous drones fly warehouse aisles at night and scan barcodes/RFID to complete inventory audits, the closest commercial analog to auditing stock in a controlled facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous stock audit in an E2 facility. Transfer fails because it counts labelled pallets in fixed racking, not unlabelled fish and wildlife product requiring species/size determination and record reconciliation.

sources.system: NOAA OLE enforcement officer boardings (human baseline)
sources.developer: NOAA Fisheries Office of Law Enforcement
sources.title: Enforcement Officer @ NOAA Fisheries | Schmidt Marine Job Board
sources.claim: The human task, as defined by NOAA's enforcement officer role, comprises boarding and investigating vessels, gear, records and catch and building case packages — the scope any substitute system must match.
sources.transferJustification: Not robotic evidence; included only to fix the scope of the instance (records, gear, catch, case preparation) against which robotic capability is judged.

tasks.label: Design or implement control measures to prevent or counteract damage caused by wildlife or people.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Agricultural depredation abatement hardware: after a landowner damage complaint, the warden lays out and erects exclusion or electric fencing, stackyard panels, fladry, or netting around haystacks, orchard blocks, garden plots, or crop fields — driving posts on uneven ground near timber, stringing and tensioning wire, hanging gates, and returning to repair storm/animal damage.

Persistent scare-device deterrence at a chronic damage site: warden selects, sites, sets up and tunes non-lethal deterrents (propane exploders, distress-call units, effigies, lasers, reflective/scare devices) to keep waterfowl, blackbirds, cormorants, deer or elk off a crop field, aquaculture pond, hatchery raceway, or poultry range, and checks/repositions them over the damage season.

On-demand nuisance or dangerous-animal response in a developed area: warden drives to a residence/town edge, hazes a bear or moose with noise/pyrotechnics or dogs, sets and baits a culvert or live trap, immobilizes and loads the animal, hauls and releases it, and secures attractants (garbage, feeders, chickens).

Preventing people-caused resource damage in the field: warden installs and repairs signs, closure barriers, gates, boundary and closure fencing, bear-resistant containers, and vehicle blocks at trailheads, boat ramps, river accesses and wildlife management areas; rehabilitates illegal ORV routes and repairs vandalized structures.

Deterrent presence and monitoring at an agency-controlled facility (hatchery grounds, WMA headquarters, boat-launch parking lot, check station): warden implements a control measure against vandalism, dumping and after-hours trespass by patrolling, maintaining visible deterrence and recording violators for follow-up.

Habitat/infrastructure protection structures: warden installs beaver pond levelers and culvert exclusion fencing, riparian exclusion fence, erosion matting, or predator/bird netting frames over hatchery raceways, working in water and on soft, brush-covered banks with hand tools.

sources.system: AVIX Autonomic (Mark II) automated laser bird repellent
sources.title: Laser Bird Deterrent Discourages Wild Species from Poultry Operations - Quality Assurance & Food Safety
sources.claim: AVIX Autonomic is a commercially sold, fully automated laser bird-deterrent turret that, after a one-time configuration, continuously repels birds from farms, airports and other sites without an operator; a Wageningen study on a free-range poultry farm measured a 99.7% reduction in wild bird presence.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same control measure a warden implements against bird depredation on crops, ponds and hatcheries: a non-lethal dispersal device installed at the damage site, here running autonomously in open outdoor farm settings.

sources.title: Automated laser bird repellent system - AVIX Autonomic
sources.claim: Vendor documentation confirms the AVIX Autonomic runs unattended after installation, projecting programmed moving laser patterns 24/7 across the protected area.

sources.developer: Ohta Seiki (with Hokkaido University, Tokyo University of Agriculture); sold by Wolf Kamuy
sources.title: Did a Japanese Town Use Robotic 'Monster' Wolves To Scare Away Bears? | Snopes.com
sources.claim: Motion-sensor-triggered 'Monster Wolf' robots (about 70 units sold since 2018) were installed around farmland and at a town edge in Takikawa, Hokkaido, to drive bears and crop-raiding wildlife away; officials reported no bear encounters after installation.
sources.transferJustification: Same measure class as a warden's mammal-hazing/scare-device installation: a sensor-triggered deterrent placed at a chronic wildlife-damage site (farmland, town edge) that operates unattended.

sources.system: Autonomous rooftop pigeon detection and deterrence system
sources.title: Rooftop Drones for Autonomous Pigeon Harassment – UAS VISION
sources.claim: An EPFL system autonomously detects pigeons on urban rooftops with a fixed camera and neural network and dispatches a drone to chase them off; it was deployed autonomously 55 times over a 21-day period in a real outdoor urban setting.
sources.transferJustification: Bird dispersal to prevent property damage is the same control measure wardens implement against depredating birds; here the detect-and-haze cycle runs without an operator in an uncontrolled outdoor setting.

sources.developer: University of Minnesota team, Farm Robotics Challenge
sources.title: [2505.10770] Geofenced Unmanned Aerial Robotic Defender for Deer Detection and Deterrence (GUARD)
sources.claim: A UAV system for autonomous deer deterrence on a Minnesota farm combines real-time deer detection, coverage path planning and an autonomous charging station, and was evaluated in simulation and field testing.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same measure — keeping deer off a farmer's crop to prevent damage — demonstrated on working farmland, though only at prototype/field-test maturity.

sources.title: Knightscope Moves with Precision and Purpose | OMNIA Partners
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots patrol outdoor parking lots, campuses and public parks and are deployed as a physical deterrent against vandalism and trespass on institutional premises such as a California utility property.
sources.transferJustification: Implementing a measure to prevent damage caused by people: a visible autonomous patrol presence with recording, equivalent to the deterrent presence/camera measure a warden puts in place at an agency facility or access-area parking lot.

sources.developer: US Army ERDC with USDA National Wildlife Research Center
sources.title: Robot Coyotes Join U.S. Army to Guard Airfields as Wildlife Control
sources.claim: Robotic wildlife-hazing rovers used on US military airfields (Coyote Rovers, developed with USDA's National Wildlife Research Center) are currently remote-controlled; autonomous navigation and species identification are still under development.
sources.transferJustification: Mobile hazing of wildlife off a site is the warden's on-demand dispersal measure; this shows the mobile-robot version of it remains operator-driven, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.developer: Farmscan AG / SmartAG Systems with Kidd Farm Machinery and Harper Adams University
sources.title: Roto-Fence Project: Autonomous Fencing for Smarter Grazing - Farmscan AG
sources.claim: An autonomous fencing system (Roto-Fence) installs fence posts along a planned fence line on grazing land; at a September 2025 live demonstration it placed posts autonomously, but the project remains an Innovate UK development project aimed at temporary rotational-grazing fence.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to warden-built exclusion fencing, but it places posts for temporary grazing fence on open pasture and does not build a wildlife-exclusion fence (height, wire tensioning, gates, brushy/rough ground), so it does not substantiate completion.

tasks.label: Collect and report information on populations or conditions of fish and wildlife in their habitats, availability of game food or cover, or suspected pollution.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wildlife population counts and observations logged during patrol or dedicated surveys: thermal/spotlight deer counts on a management unit, waterfowl or colony counts on a marsh, turkey brood counts, sightings recorded and entered in agency reports. Open fields, forest, wetland; night or dawn; weather as found.

Habitat condition and game food/cover assessment on wildlife management areas, refuges and backcountry: extent and vigor of browse and forage, cover and canopy structure, invasive plant encroachment, wetland water levels; findings mapped and reported to agency biologists. Reached on foot, ATV or boat.

Fish population and harvest data collection: assisting biologist crews with gill-netting or boat electrofishing, netting, measuring, weighing and tagging fish and releasing them; dockside creel checks where the warden inspects and measures anglers' catches and asks about effort. Boat, ramp, shoreline.

Suspected pollution or fish kill complaint response on small waters and adjacent land: drive to a creek, ditch or farm pond, walk the bank, locate and photograph dead fish or a discharge, trace the likely source, collect water/tissue samples with chain of custody, and report to the environmental agency.

Condition monitoring of large water bodies: running a boat over a lake, reservoir, river or coastal bay to record water quality, algal bloom extent, turbidity, temperature and dissolved oxygen, and reporting conditions affecting fish habitat.

Biological sampling of harvested game at a check station: agency-run station or cooperating processor where the warden ages deer by teeth, weighs and measures carcasses, extracts retropharyngeal lymph nodes for CWD testing, labels samples, and records hunter-supplied harvest location and effort data.

sources.system: Thermal-infrared survey drones (MassDOT Aeronautics / MA DCR deer density survey)
sources.developer: Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation with MassDOT Aeronautics Division
sources.title: Drones provide precise deer count, justifying Quabbin Park hunt - Amherst Bulletin
sources.claim: Massachusetts DCR, with MassDOT's Aeronautics Division, flew thermal-infrared drones on autonomous transects over the 2,600-acre Quabbin Park to produce deer density estimates before and after a controlled hunt; the estimates matched pellet-survey results and were used to justify and evaluate the hunt.

sources.system: Thermal-camera drone wildlife abundance surveys (Beaver et al., Wildlife Society Bulletin)
sources.developer: Montana State University / Auburn University researchers
sources.title: WSB: Drones with thermal cameras estimate mammal abundance - The Wildlife Society
sources.claim: Research reported by The Wildlife Society found drone thermal counts of a known deer population were 90-92% accurate under optimal evening thermal contrast, comparable to or better than conventional survey methods.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (wildlife population counts); cited only for the accuracy of drone-based counts, not as the autonomy-establishing source.

sources.system: UAS waterfowl census workflow with deployable CNN (USFWS cooperative project)
sources.developer: US Fish and Wildlife Service with academic partners
sources.title: Progress toward automated migratory waterfowl census using drones and deep learning (ACM SIGSPATIAL workshop)
sources.claim: A cooperative USFWS project developed a UAS field survey workflow plus a deployable CNN model to census wintering waterfowl at federally managed refuges, automating the image-interpretation step of aerial population counts.

sources.system: Dendra Systems drone + AI ecosystem monitoring
sources.title: Dendra Systems: Environmental Technology for Ecosystem Restoration (Austmine)
sources.claim: Dendra Systems runs a commercial service using autonomous drone platforms and ecology-trained AI to capture and analyse vegetation cover, biodiversity and ecosystem-health data over large outdoor sites, delivering monitoring reports to land managers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vegetation-cover and ecosystem-condition survey for land managers. Transfers to assessing availability of game food and cover because the objects (vegetation patches, canopy, ground cover), the precision (mapped cover classes) and the unstructured outdoor environment are the same.

sources.title: Treeswift to automate forestry with swarms of drones - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Treeswift flies swarms of autonomous LiDAR-equipped drones that navigate forest stands to inventory and map timberland structure and biomass, piloting with commercial forest owners.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forest structure inventory. Transfers to habitat cover assessment because the measured quantities (stem density, canopy and understory structure, biomass) are the physical features a warden reports as cover, in the same unstructured forest terrain.

sources.system: SeaTrac USV carrying MBARI 3G Environmental Sample Processor (SHARC project)
sources.developer: NOAA GLERL / NOAA AOML / MBARI / SeaTrac Systems
sources.title: Failing Upwards: Developing an Autonomous Surface Vehicle to Advance 'Omics Research - NOAA/AOML
sources.claim: NOAA GLERL/AOML with MBARI deployed a solar-powered SeaTrac uncrewed surface vessel carrying MBARI's robotic 3G Environmental Sample Processor that autonomously navigated western Lake Erie for two weeks, collecting and preserving water samples to monitor harmful algal blooms; further deployments followed in Saginaw Bay.

sources.system: SPR/ESP/LRAUV (MBARI long-range AUV with Environmental Sample Processor)
sources.developer: MBARI with NOAA NCCOS and GLERL
sources.title: NOAA, MBARI Achieve Groundbreaking Milestone in Use of Uncrewed Vehicle to Monitor Freshwater Algal Toxins - NCCOS
sources.claim: NOAA NCCOS/GLERL and MBARI used a long-range autonomous underwater vehicle carrying an SPR toxin sensor integrated with the robotic Environmental Sample Processor to make underway microcystin measurements in western Lake Erie and report results ashore within two hours, guided by an onboard chlorophyll-based search-and-sampling algorithm.

sources.system: Saildrone uncrewed surface vehicles with acoustic echosounders
sources.developer: Saildrone Inc. with NOAA Alaska Fisheries Science Center
sources.title: Detecting Fish From Ocean-Going Robots To Complement Ship-Based Surveys | NOAA Fisheries
sources.claim: NOAA Fisheries equipped saildrone uncrewed surface vehicles with echosounders and ran 103-day autonomous acoustic surveys in the Bering Sea; walleye pollock detections compared well with those of the research ship Oscar Dyson.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fish stock abundance survey. Transfers to collecting information on fish populations in their habitat because the output (abundance and distribution data accepted by the managing agency) and the open-water environment are the same.

sources.system: VAKI Micro Counter / Smart Grader / SmartFlow
sources.title: VAKI Micro Counter - Merck Animal Health USA
sources.claim: VAKI counting and grading machines, sold commercially for hatcheries, automatically pass live fish through a channel, count them and record size data during transfers and grading operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hatchery fish counting and size grading. Transfers to collecting fish biological data because the objects (live fish), the measurements (counts, size class) and the recorded output match survey biometrics when fish are presented to the machine in a flow.

sources.system: Skala Maskon automated fish vaccination and sorting machine
sources.title: We automate the industry - Maskon
sources.claim: Skala Maskon's fully automatic fish vaccination machine pumps live salmon smolt through the machine, orienting, injecting and sorting up to 40,000 fish per hour with a single operator and no manual handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling, sorting and injecting of live fish in a hatchery line. Transfers to fish sampling and tagging work (handle fish, take a measurement, apply a mark) with the fish presented to the machine.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Orbit 5.0 autonomous inspection
sources.title: Orbit 5.0 adds features to Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped runs autonomous inspection missions in industrial facilities, and its Orbit 5.0 software automatically flags visual anomalies such as spills, debris and corrosion, generating alerts and inspection records without manual image review.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility inspection rounds that detect and report spills and leaks. Transfers to documenting and reporting a suspected contamination condition inside an institution-controlled facility, with the same visual evidence and reporting output.

tasks.label: Investigate crop, property, or habitat damage or destruction or instances of water pollution to determine causes and to advise property owners of preventive measures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crop or livestock depredation complaint on private farm/ranch land: warden drives to the property, meets the landowner, walks standing corn, hay, orchard rows or pasture, examines trampled/browsed plants or a dead calf or sheep (including rolling and skinning the carcass to look for subcutaneous hemorrhage and bite spacing), identifies the responsible species (deer, elk, bear, coyote, wolf), estimates acreage/dollar loss, and advises on fencing, hazing, harassment permits or a depredation permit.

Nuisance-wildlife property damage at a residence, cabin or small business: bear tearing into trash, beehives, freezers or an outbuilding; beavers damming a culvert and flooding a driveway or hayfield; raccoons/geese/deer damaging structures or landscaping. Warden inspects the damaged structure or flooded ground, confirms the species from sign, and advises on attractant removal, electric fencing, pond levelers or trapping options.

Water pollution or fish-kill report on a stream, farm pond or lake: warden responds to the bank, documents and counts dead fish, takes dissolved-oxygen/pH/temperature readings and collects water samples in bottles, then works upstream on foot through brush and mud to find the source (a discharge pipe, manure lagoon breach, chemical spill, silt plume), coordinates with the state environmental agency, and advises the responsible landowner on corrective and preventive steps.

Habitat damage or destruction investigation on public or private wildland: unpermitted stream channel alteration or bank riprap, wetland fill, off-road-vehicle rutting in a wildlife area, dredging, or logging slash in a riparian buffer. Warden hikes the site, photographs and GPS/measures the disturbed area, determines who did it and how, and advises the owner/operator on restoration and permitting to prevent recurrence.

Investigation at a permitted commercial or institutional facility whose premises are controlled and kept to a working standard (feedlot, fish hatchery, food plant, sand-and-gravel operation, industrial outfall): warden is escorted onto the site, inspects settling ponds, outfalls and sediment/erosion controls, samples the discharge, determines the cause of the release, and advises the operator on best management practices.

sources.title: Autonomous drones combat deer damage in crops
sources.claim: Airwyse markets a commercially available autonomous, self-charging drone system that patrols farm fields around the clock, detects deer and other wildlife, and alerts growers, providing data on when deer feeding peaks and on crop losses. It automates wildlife detection and field imagery over private farmland, but it does not inspect damage on the ground, diagnose non-wildlife causes, or counsel the landowner.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection and quantification of wildlife crop damage on farmland. It shares the objects (deer, damaged crops) and outdoor unstructured setting of the warden's depredation call, so it bounds what is automated today — aerial detection and imagery — while the warden's whole task (ground examination of carcasses/plants, cause determination, advising the owner) is not covered.

sources.system: Spot with Spot CAM+IR and FLIR MUVE C360
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped performs autonomous inspection rounds inside industrial plants, carrying thermal cameras and a Teledyne FLIR MUVE C360 gas sensor, and autonomously detected a pinhole combustible-gas leak at a midstream gas .... Detection of a pre-specified anomaly class on a pre-mapped route is the closest deployed analogue to a facility environmental inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous anomaly/leak inspection inside a controlled industrial facility (E2). It is the nearest robotic analogue to a warden's on-site pollution inspection at a permitted facility, but it runs a taught route looking for predefined anomalies and does not sample an outfall, reconstruct the cause of a release, or advise the operator.

sources.system: Autonomous surface vehicle with screen-printed-electrode microfluidic heavy metal detector (INTCATCH-derived)
sources.developer: De Vito-Francesco et al. (Univ. Verona / ICN2 / partners)
sources.title: An innovative autonomous robotic system for on-site detection of heavy metal pollution plumes in surface water | Environmental Monitoring and Assessment
sources.claim: A research autonomous surface vehicle fitted with a microfluidic heavy-metal analyser was built to run preprogrammed navigation on surface water with automatic sampling and on-board chemical analysis; the pollution-plume scenario was validated in simulated laboratory experiments and the vehicle is described as semiautonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic water sampling and on-site contaminant detection, the sampling sub-step of a pollution investigation. Autonomy is only partial (semiautonomous, preprogrammed) and validation was in simulated laboratory conditions, so it cannot substantiate completing a field fish-kill investigation.

sources.developer: EYDAP (Athens Water Supply and Sewerage Company) study team
sources.title: Use of Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) in Water Chemistry Studies
sources.claim: Uncrewed surface vehicles carrying multiparameter sensors were put to work by the Athens Water and ... for environmental monitoring of surface water ..., showing that boat-type robots are used operationally for water-quality survey work; the reported use is routine spatial monitoring rather than incident investigation, and the level of autonomy versus remote piloting is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operational water-quality monitoring of natural water bodies by a utility. It covers data collection on the water surface only; the warden's task also requires bank-side and upstream ground search, evidence handling, cause determination and landowner advice, none of which is shown.

tasks.label: Perform facilities maintenance work, such as constructing or repairing structures or controlling weeds or pests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On-site construction/repair of outdoor structures on wildlife management areas and public access sites: replacing broken gates, boundary fences and signposts, patching kiosks, blinds, docks, boat-ramp planking and wetland water-control structures. Warden hauls lumber/hardware by truck or UTV, digs post holes, saws, drills, bolts and welds in place, on uneven ground in variable weather.

Shop/yard fabrication and finishing at the agency maintenance shop or garage: cutting dimensional lumber and steel to length and assembling sign frames, wood duck boxes, picnic tables, gates and blind panels on a bench, then painting/staining them before they are hauled out for installation.

Terrestrial weed and brush control on agency land: mixing and applying herbicide to noxious/invasive weeds and woody regrowth on WMA fields, dike tops, food-plot edges, parking areas and access-road shoulders, using backpack or UTV/ATV sprayer, with applicator records and drift precautions.

Aquatic and wetland vegetation control: treating Phragmites, cattail, water hyacinth or hydrilla in marshes, impoundments, ponds and around boat ramps, working from a boat, on foot in muck, or contracting aerial application; access is difficult and non-target vegetation must be spared.

Mowing and vegetation maintenance of grounds and access infrastructure: mowing lawns and parking areas at offices, check stations and boat landings, plus levees, firebreaks, shooting-range lanes and trail edges with a riding mower or tractor/brush hog; obstacles include posts, culverts, stumps and litter.

Building upkeep and pest control at agency offices, check stations, storage sheds, cabins and pit toilets: fixing leaking plumbing, doors, locks and windows, replacing lights, minor roof and floor repairs, and knocking down wasp nests or setting rodent bait/traps inside the structures.

sources.system: Contractor agricultural spray drone (approx. 8-gal tank) used for prairie restoration herbicide application
sources.developer: Commercial drone application contractor (equipment class: DJI Agras-type spray UAS)
sources.title: Drones for Herbicide Application | grassland restoration network
sources.claim: Contractor spray drones autonomously fly a grid and apply herbicide to invasive species over a 40-acre stump-filled tract being restored to prairie at Shaw Nature Reserve; the drone detects when its tank is empty, returns to a fill point where staff refill it, and resumes where it left off.

sources.system: KCI aerial land management spray drone fleet
sources.title: Drones Offer Innovative Solutions to Treat Invasive Species - KCI
sources.claim: KCI ecologists use a fleet of spray drones with pre-programmed flight plans and auto-flight mode to apply herbicide to invasive cattail and Phragmites in wetlands across eight Wisconsin DNR state-managed natural and wildlife areas, treating up to 10 acres per hour with automatic treatment records.

sources.system: RPAS (spray drone) herbicide application for common reed control
sources.developer: University of Waterloo / Invasive Phragmites Control Centre / Drone Spray Canada
sources.title: Drone Herbicide Applications Prove Effective for Common Reed Control - Weed Science Society of America
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed research (University of Waterloo, published in Invasive Plant Science and Management) found a single targeted drone herbicide application suppressed invasive common reed in wetlands with more than 99% effectiveness, equal to or better than helicopter and backpack application.

sources.system: DJI AGRAS MG-1 with Rantizo spray upgrade kit
sources.title: Mapping and spot spraying invasive weeds with drones | Pix4D
sources.claim: A Rantizo application contractor working with Applied Ecological Services and the Wisconsin DNR spot-sprayed Phragmites from mapped shapefiles at the Turtle Valley Wildlife Area, a state wildlife area, using a DJI Agras spray drone.

sources.title: Scythe Robotics debuts video series for M.52 autonomous mower onboarding - Lawn & Landscape
sources.claim: The Scythe M.52 is a commercially sold autonomous ride-on-class commercial mower deployed with landscape contractors across 14 states as of early 2025, working varied turf types and terrains.

sources.developer: Scythe Robotics (acquired by Autonomous Solutions Inc.)
sources.title: Autonomous Solutions Inc. acquires Scythe Robotics to expand AI-powered autonomy | Landscape Management
sources.claim: In 2025 the Scythe M.52 autonomously mowed nearly 2 billion square ... of grounds for dozens of commercial landscape customers across 30 states, indicating production-scale reliability on maintained institutional and commercial properties.

sources.system: GUSS / Herbicide GUSS autonomous orchard sprayer
sources.title: John Deere Expands with GUSS Orchard & Vineyard Sprayers - control.com
sources.claim: More than 250 GUSS autonomous sprayers, including a dedicated Herbicide GUSS for weed control, are deployed worldwide in orchards and vineyards, with one operator supervising up to eight machines from ... vehicle rather than driving them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor herbicide/pesticide application on managed grounds. It transfers to warden weed control because the machine mixes route, targets ground-level weeds beneath vegetation, and applies labeled chemical at controlled rates over acreage, the same output a warden's UTV sprayer produces.

sources.system: House of Design robotic floor/roof truss fabrication line
sources.title: The Path to Automation - Offsite Builder Magazine
sources.claim: House of Design robotic truss lines place pre-plated wood chords and webs ... an assembly jig, automating fabrication of wood floor/roof trusses and wall panels in a fixtured production cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of dimensional-lumber structures from cut members and fasteners in a jig. This is the same class of work as shop-building sign frames, nest boxes or gate panels: comparable materials, fastening operations and carpentry tolerances, done with the workpiece fixtured.

sources.system: Automated robotic roof and floor truss systems
sources.developer: House of Design Robotics / Builders FirstSource
sources.title: Video Showcase: Robots at the truss plant | HBS Dealer
sources.claim: Robotic truss assembly systems are bought and installed at production scale by major US building-materials producers, showing the fenced, fixtured wood-assembly cell is a mature commercial technology rather than a demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the House of Design item: automated cutting, handling and fastening of dimensional lumber into finished wood assemblies within a fixtured cell.

sources.system: FANUC P-350iA/45 paint robot in automated finishing cell
sources.title: Painting Robots - Explore FANUC's Paint Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Industrial paint robots apply coatings to wooden components in automated finishing cells, a standard commercial installation for wood products such as cabinet doors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray finishing of fixtured wood parts. Painting/staining shop-built signs, boxes and tables is the same operation on similar flat/box wooden workpieces presented on a conveyor or rack in a booth.

tasks.label: Survey areas and compile figures of bag counts of hunters to determine the effectiveness of control measures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field/roadside contact with a hunting party at the end of a hunt (duck marsh, dove field, upland cover, forest road pull-off): warden opens game bags/coolers, physically handles and counts the harvested birds or animals, identifies species and sex from plumage/wings/head, checks the tally against daily bag and possession limits, and records the counts for the unit's harvest data. Weather, mud, water, and terrain are as found.

Agency-run harvest check station (big-game check station, refuge exit station, boat ramp check): hunters bring carcasses or bagged birds to a fixed, agency-controlled site with racks, scales and tables; the warden counts and classifies each animal by species/sex/age class and logs the figures on standard forms for the season tally.

Systematic survey of a hunt unit, refuge, or depredation area to count the game remaining (spotlight/road transects, aerial or thermal drone counts, foot transects of crop-damage fields), producing density/abundance figures that are compared with the season's harvest to judge whether the control measures worked.

Hunter-effort/use survey during a season: counting hunting parties afield, occupied blinds, boats on a marsh, and vehicles at access points and parking areas over a sampled period, to estimate hunter numbers and pressure that accompany the bag figures.

Office compilation: sorting check-station cards, wing envelopes and hunter report forms, entering the numbers into the agency harvest database, tabulating totals by species, sex and unit, and producing the summary figures/report used to judge the control program.

sources.system: Marel (JBT Marel) overhead 'weight and vision based' grading / IRIS vision grading
sources.title: Overhead grading and distribution | JBT Marel
sources.claim: Commercially deployed poultry grading lines use automated weight-and-vision equipment to assess and classify whole bird carcasses fully automatically at line speed, producing per-bird records used for distribution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated grading of whole bird carcasses presented on a shackle line. It transfers to tallying a hunter's bag when the harvest is brought to a purpose-built station: comparable objects (whole bird/animal carcasses), comparable precision (per-item classification and count), and the machine both handles and records every item.

sources.system: Whooshh PassagePortal (FishL Recognition / Gatekeeper), Chief Joseph Dam
sources.title: Through the tubes: Using pneumatic tubes to transport fish, this company’s fish passage is in demand - Responsible Seafood Advocate
sources.claim: A deployed fish-passage system scans each animal with machine vision, distinguishes species/origin, physically sorts it, and logs it, at rates of tens of animals per minute at a dam site built around the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated identification, counting and sorting of wild animals passing a purpose-built portal for fisheries management. It transfers to compiling bag/harvest counts at a fixtured station: same output (species-resolved counts recorded for management decisions) with the animals presented to the machine.

sources.system: Whooshh PassagePortal Model L / Model F
sources.title: Best Fish Passage Options for Modern River Management | Whooshh Innovations
sources.claim: The developer documents that the automated portal scans and sorts every fish in real time and that the resulting per-animal data are used for fisheries management decisions, including diverting invasive or hatchery fish.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: the machine's accepted output is a compiled, species-resolved count of animals used to judge management measures, which is the output the warden's bag-count tally provides.

sources.system: Thermal-sensor drone survey (Wake Forest Unmanned Systems Lab), Wildlife Society Bulletin study
sources.developer: Beaver et al., Wake Forest University / Montana State University
sources.title: WSB: Drones with thermal cameras estimate mammal abundance - The Wildlife Society
sources.claim: Thermal-camera drones flown on autonomous flight lines over a 430-acre deer facility produced population counts 90–92% accurate, but the deer counts themselves were made by researchers reviewing the footage rather than by the aircraft.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial abundance survey of game to inform harvest management. Flight is automated, but the count — the instance's accepted output — was produced by humans from the imagery, so it does not substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.system: White Buffalo thermal drone deer survey, DJI Matrice 30T, Martha's Vineyard
sources.developer: White Buffalo Inc. / Tick Free MV
sources.title: DJI Matrice 30 Is Counting Deer On Martha's Vineyard. The Ticks Are Not Happy About It.
sources.claim: In an operational island-wide deer survey commissioned to guide deer reduction, drones flew an autonomous grid, but a human pilot interrupted the flight to confirm each thermal signature and manually logged every deer as a waypoint.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field survey of a management unit to count game and judge whether control (hunting/culling) is sufficient. Shows the current operational standard is human identification and logging, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment in unstructured terrain.

tasks.label: Document the extent of crop, property, or habitat damage and make financial loss estimates or compensation recommendations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Row-crop damage complaint on a private farm (corn, soybeans, wheat, alfalfa) caused by deer, elk, wild pigs or geese. Warden meets the producer, walks/drives the field, delineates and measures the damaged acreage, confirms the responsible species from sign, photographs and GPS-tags the damage, and converts damaged area to bushels/tons and dollars for a damage claim or depredation permit recommendation.

Livestock or poultry depredation claim on pasture or open rangeland. Warden hikes to a dead calf, sheep or bird, rolls and skins the carcass, checks for subcutaneous hemorrhage, measures bite/tooth spacing, looks for tracks, scat and drag marks, judges whether the kill was predation or scavenging, photographs the evidence, and assigns a replacement value for compensation.

Close-range property and specialty-crop damage at farmsteads, cabins and residences: bear into beehives, garbage sheds, feed bins or a cabin interior; damaged buildings, equipment, gates and fencing; deer or bear damage to orchard trees, vineyard vines and nursery stock. Warden inspects at arm's length, itemizes destroyed items, counts damaged trees/hives, and estimates repair or replacement cost.

Landscape-scale property damage visible from above: beaver dams flooding hayfields, roads or timber; wild-pig rooting of pastures, lawns and golf turf; goose-damaged turf; downed fence lines and exterior structural damage. Warden documents the flooded/disturbed extent and estimates value of lost forage, crops or repairs.

Habitat or resource damage on open terrain: illegal off-road-vehicle ruts in a wetland, unauthorized fill or clearing, streambank disturbance, gravel removal or erosion from an unpermitted crossing. Warden maps and measures the disturbed area/volume, photographs and GPS-tags it, and prepares restoration-cost or resource-damage figures for the case file.

Aquatic or under-canopy resource damage: a fish kill below a discharge requiring dead fish to be collected, counted by species and size and valued from standard replacement-cost tables; in-stream substrate sedimentation; forest understory damage under closed canopy.

sources.system: Airwyse autonomous field drone and docking station
sources.title: Autonomous drones combat deer damage in crops (Farm Progress)
sources.claim: Airwyse markets a self-charging drone docking system placed in the middle of a crop field that flies repeated field missions without a human present, detecting deer and returning imagery and GPS data to the farmer's phone — autonomous drone operation over open farm fields.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that uncrewed aerial imaging of a private crop field, including detection of the damaging species, runs autonomously from an in-field base; it supplies the physical data-collection half of documenting crop damage.

sources.system: UAV RGB + UNet/SegFormer wildlife crop-damage segmentation (Poznan University of Technology)
sources.developer: Aszkowski, Kraft, Drapikowski, Pieczynski — Poznan University of Technology
sources.title: Estimation of corn crop damage caused by wildlife in UAV images, Precision Agriculture 25:2505-2530
sources.claim: Deep-learning segmentation of consumer-grade UAV RGB imagery determines the percentage and location of corn damaged by wildlife with IoU 0.88, trained on over 300 ha of fields, explicitly aimed at the compensation-claim workflow; code and trained model are public.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: quantifying the extent of wildlife damage in a crop field for compensation. Flight autonomy is not stated, so it is used only alongside the autonomous drone platforms cited separately.

sources.system: Drone imagery + custom deep-learning wild pig damage quantification
sources.developer: Friesenhahn et al., Caesar Kleberg Wildlife Research Institute / USDA-APHIS NWRC
sources.title: Using drones to detect and quantify wild pig damage and yield loss in corn fields throughout plant growth stages, Wildlife Society Bulletin 47:e1437
sources.claim: Drone orthomosaics classified with custom deep-learning algorithms quantified wild pig damage in Texas corn fields at all growth stages and were combined with harvest yield maps to estimate yield loss and support economic cost-benefit analysis of the damage.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: measuring extent of wildlife crop damage and converting it to yield and dollar loss; validated against the ground transect surveys wardens/appraisers traditionally use.

sources.title: EagleView Announces Launch of EagleView Assess Autonomous Drone-Sourced Property Intelligence (Roofing Contractor)
sources.claim: EagleView Assess is a commercially sold autonomous drone service that flies residential properties from the ground, detects damage anomalies and produces roof measurements used as claim evidence by contractors, adjusters and insurance carriers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task — documenting the extent of damage to private property and producing the measurements that drive a repair-cost estimate — on the same class of unstructured private premises a warden visits.

sources.title: How to Find the Best Drones For Roof Inspections (EagleView)
sources.claim: EagleView Assess generates automated damage reports and measurements that feed repair estimates, i.e. the automated pipeline delivers both the damage documentation and the basis of the financial figure.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the damage-documentation-to-cost-estimate output of an autonomous drone system is accepted commercially, the same output this task requires.

sources.title: DJI Dock 3 Delivers "Drone in a Box" Enterprise Solution For 24/7 Remote Operations
sources.claim: DJI Dock 3 is a commercially released, vehicle-mountable drone-in-a-box that runs 24/7 remote missions on automated flight routes with automatic detection, change detection and high-precision mapping payloads, with no pilot at the site.
sources.transferJustification: Provides the autonomous, pilot-free aerial platform (including mapping payloads) that can be repositioned by vehicle to a damage site in the field.

sources.title: American Robotics receives approval to operate automated drones without human operators on-site (AUVSI)
sources.claim: American Robotics received the first FAA approval to operate automated ... with no human operators on site; its Scout system flies, charges, processes and transmits data automatically from a field base station, with agriculture among its target uses.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms regulatory and technical feasibility of unattended autonomous drone survey flights over rural/agricultural sites, the physical component of on-site damage documentation.

sources.system: Drone stream-habitat monitoring and evaluation toolkits
sources.developer: Wu et al., University of Wisconsin-Madison
sources.title: Cost-effective drone monitoring and evaluating toolkits for stream habitat health, Environmental Monitoring and Assessment 198
sources.claim: A drone toolkit with automated flight-route design, Structure-from-Motion reconstruction and multi-metric index computation forms an end-to-end workflow for quantitative stream habitat evaluation at centimeter scale, scoring habitat against Wisconsin DNR and EPA guidelines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task — standardized quantitative documentation of habitat condition over natural stream corridors — produces exactly the mapped extent and scored condition a warden records when documenting habitat damage.

sources.system: Pix4D drone mapping workflow for crop insurance
sources.title: Using drone mapping for crop insurance (Pix4D)
sources.claim: Drone mapping is used operationally by crop insurance loss adjusters to identify and measure damaged areas of fields that were previously measured with a measuring wheel or tape, for compensation purposes.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in the insurance setting: measuring damaged field extent to set a compensation figure; cited as corroboration only, since flight autonomy is not stated.

tasks.label: Participate in firefighting efforts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Warden is first resource on a small, newly reported wildfire in backcountry or rural patrol area: drives/hikes in over unimproved terrain, sizes up the fire, and works it with hand tools (pulaski, shovel, McLeod), a backpack pump or slip-on pump unit — scratching line, knocking down flame in grass/brush/timber, holding until forestry engines arrive.

Warden assigned as a red-carded resource on a larger ongoing incident: holding and improving fireline, mopping up hotspots (digging out smoldering stumps, stirring ash, cold-trailing by hand), gridding the black for smokes, dragging hose lays, occasional structure protection in the wildland-urban interface, over multi-hour shifts in smoke, heat and steep or wet ground.

Warden supports a prescribed burn or backfire on a wildlife management area, refuge or private tract: carrying and lighting a drip torch along a burn line, holding the interior edge with a swatter or pump can, watching for spots across the line, and mopping up the perimeter afterward under a burn boss's plan.

Warden works the fire's public-safety perimeter: driving patrol roads and two-tracks, setting up road closures, cones and barricades, physically closing gates/boat ramps, going door-to-door and campsite-to-campsite to evacuate campers, boaters and residents, and moving/escorting people and livestock out of the fire area.

Warden provides transport and logistics support to the fire effort: hauling hose, pumps, fuel, drinking water and crew gear by patrol truck, UTV or boat over fire roads and shorelines; shuttling firefighters across a lake or river; refilling engine and backpack tanks; and staging-area/fire-camp support work.

sources.system: Autonomous Black Hawk with Sikorsky MATRIX flight autonomy + Rain wildfire mission autonomy
sources.title: Sikorsky and Rain Successfully Demonstrate Autonomous Flight with Wildfire Mission Autonomy to Rapidly Find and Suppress Test Fires
sources.claim: Sikorsky/Rain autonomous Black Hawk was commanded by tablet to take off, find a staged test fire and drop water from a Bambi Bucket, with safety pilots hands-off; targets were 12-inch propane fire rings on an airfield, i.e. an aerial suppression demonstration only, not ground firefighting work.
sources.transferJustification: Closest autonomous system to wildfire suppression; cited to show the frontier is aerial water delivery on staged targets, which does not cover the warden's ground tasks (handline, mop-up, evacuation, logistics).

sources.system: Rain wildfire autonomy / automated aerial firefighting drones
sources.developer: Rain; Sikorsky; industry (reported by ASCE Civil Engineering Source)
sources.title: Automated aerial firefighting drones to provide faster responses
sources.claim: Participants in autonomous aerial firefighting state the autonomous aircraft cannot perform mop-up or declare a fire out; that remains ground-crew work for the foreseeable future.
sources.transferJustification: Directly addresses whether the leading autonomous suppression system can complete the ground portions of a fire assignment that wardens perform.

sources.title: California agencies eye BurnBot for wildfire prevention
sources.claim: BurnBot RX2, the leading fielded prescribed-burn machine used with California agencies, lays black lines for prescribed burns but is remotely controlled by a trained on-site operator within 500 feet; autonomy is aspirational.
sources.transferJustification: Same work as the prescribed-burn instance (ignition and holding of a controlled burn in wildland fuels); shows the fielded machine is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.date: 2020-10-13 (in service; still operated per Oct 2024 trade press)
sources.title: LAFD Debuts the RS3: First Robotic Firefighting Vehicle in the United States
sources.claim: The Thermite RS3 firefighting robot operated by LAFD since 2020 is remotely operated by a human with a controller and video feedback; it works structural/industrial fires, not wildland line work.
sources.transferJustification: Most capable fire-suppression ground robot in US service; cited to establish that fielded suppression robots are teleoperated and therefore cannot support positive judgments.

sources.title: Paris Firefighters Used This Remote-Controlled Robot to Extinguish the Notre Dame Blaze
sources.claim: Colossus, the tracked firefighting robot used by the Paris Fire Brigade (including at Notre Dame), is a remote-controlled machine directed by firefighters from a standoff position.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the autonomy status of the most widely deployed firefighting ground robot; teleoperation means it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of any instance.

sources.title: Prediction and prevention: Robotic applications for wildfire management
sources.claim: A 2026 review of wildfire robotics describes hot-spot monitoring during mop-up as performed by remotely operated units, with ground robots used for vegetation clearing, controlled-burn support and resupply rather than autonomous suppression.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the mop-up and line-holding work in the warden instances; shows state of practice is remote operation, not autonomous completion.

emergingTasks.label: Operate drones for surveillance of large areas and tracking of wildlife.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Parking Enforcement Workers
roles.description: Patrol assigned area, such as public parking lot or city streets to issue tickets to overtime parking violators and illegally parked vehicles.

tasks.label: Enter and retrieve information pertaining to vehicle registration, identification, and status, using hand-held computers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On-street patrol of a metered downtown block: officer keys a license plate number and state into a handheld ticket-writer to query registration status (expired tabs, plate-to-vehicle match) before deciding whether to cite; output is the returned record on screen.

Writing a citation in a municipal lot or garage: officer enters vehicle identifiers (plate, state, make, model, color, sometimes VIN) and violation code into the handheld so the citation record is created and uploaded to the ticketing system.
Hotlist/scofflaw check: officer queries the handheld against outstanding-ticket, boot/tow-eligible, or stolen-vehicle lists and retrieves the vehicle's status to determine escalation.
Timed-parking enforcement: officer enters a plate and tire-valve position (or e-chalk mark) on the first pass, then retrieves the earlier entry on a later pass to confirm an overtime violation.
Permit-zone verification: officer enters a plate in a residential-permit or employee-permit district and retrieves permit validity/expiration from the handheld's synced database.

Back-office or vehicle-based follow-up: officer syncs or re-queries the handheld to correct a mis-keyed plate, look up an owner-of-record/registration detail for a contested ticket, or verify a status change before releasing a boot.

tasks.label: Maintain close communications with dispatching personnel, using two-way radios or cell phones.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Patrol an assigned area by vehicle or on foot to ensure public compliance with existing parking ordinance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Downtown/commercial-district foot beat: officer walks an assigned run of metered and time-limited blocks, checking pay-by-plate/meter expirations, double-parking, loading zone, hydrant, bus stop and crosswalk violations; works among pedestrians and moving traffic, in all weather, and fields questions from drivers and merchants.

Vehicle patrol of city streets: officer drives an assigned route through residential permit districts, time-limited zones, school and street-sweeping routes, often with a mobile plate reader, circling blocks, stopping to check permits/placards and flagging tow-away and abandoned vehicles in mixed traffic.

Patrol of municipal or public parking lots and multi-level garages (downtown garage, transit park-and-ride, airport lot): check payment/permit compliance space by space, ADA and fire-lane spots, occupancy, on premises controlled by the parking authority or operator.

Campus patrol at a university, hospital or large contracted private property: patrol permit lots and decks on foot or by cart, verify decals/plates against the permit list, log unauthorized vehicles, report hazards; institution controls access and layout.

Event and temporary-zone enforcement: game-day, festival, parade, film-permit, construction or snow-emergency patrol, with dense crowds, temporary signage and cones, ad-hoc no-parking zones, heavy public interaction and tow coordination.

sources.title: K5 Autonomous Security Robot | Knightscope
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot performs fully autonomous outdoor patrol, explicitly including patrol of parking lots and multi-level parking structures, 24/7 in weather, with plate recognition and public address.
sources.transferJustification: Security patrol of parking areas is the same locomotion-and-observation job as parking patrol: same setting (lots/decks), same objects (parked vehicles), same output (routine route coverage plus flagged vehicles); only the rule set checked differs.

sources.system: Knightscope K5 ASR (parking use case, ALPR)
sources.title: Parking | Knightscope
sources.claim: Knightscope configures multiple K5 ASRs for parking applications, with automatic license plate recognition generating alerts on flagged vehicles to the operator's security operations center.
sources.transferJustification: ALPR-based flagging of vehicles along a patrol route is the detection half of parking-compliance patrol: plate read, compared against a list, alert issued.

sources.title: Logistics | Knightscope
sources.claim: Knightscope specifies a K5 patrolling employee and visitor parking lots at logistics sites with the explicit purpose of assisting parking policy enforcement.

sources.system: Knightscope K5 ASR deployed by ABM
sources.title: ABM Deploys Knightscope Autonomous Robots in Major Parking Facility
sources.claim: ABM, one of the largest US parking service operators, deployed Knightscope autonomous robots for automated monitoring in a major parking facility - a third-party operational deployment of robot patrol in a managed parking facility.
sources.transferJustification: Automated monitoring patrol of a managed parking facility covers the same route-coverage and parked-vehicle observation work as parking-compliance patrol in that facility.

sources.title: Security robots to patrol parking lots at University of Nevada, Reno in the next few months
sources.claim: The University of Nevada, Reno contracted autonomous security robots to patrol its campus parking garage near the Student Center, including during games and events and overnight.

tasks.label: Identify vehicles in violation of parking codes, checking with dispatchers when necessary to confirm identities or to determine whether vehicles need to be booted or towed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Foot beat in a downtown metered/time-limited district: officer walks the block line, checks each parked vehicle against meter or pay-by-plate payment status and posted time limits (chalking or virtual chalking), reads plates, and queries the handheld/dispatch when a plate is unreadable or a payment record is ambiguous. Pedestrians, traffic, weather, temporary construction and street-cleaning signage all present.

Vehicle- or scooter-mounted patrol of residential permit zones and 2-hour zones on public streets: drive the route slowly, scan plates against the permit/payment database, revisit to establish overstay, confirm questionable permits or plate reads with dispatch before flagging a violation.

Patrol of an institution-controlled off-street facility (municipal garage, airport parking structure, university or hospital lot): identify vehicles without valid permits/hangtags, overstays, vehicles in ADA or reserved stalls and fire lanes, and confirm registration/permit records with the dispatch or parking office.

Standing/stopping violations in prohibited zones spotted on street patrol: vehicle at a fire hydrant, in a bus stop, crosswalk, bike lane, loading zone, or double-parked in a downtown corridor; officer must confirm the vehicle is genuinely in the restricted zone, record plate and evidence, and decide whether it is a tow candidate.

Scofflaw/boot-tow identification: officer works a hot list of plates with unpaid citations or warrants, matches an observed vehicle to the list, verifies plate (and sometimes VIN or obscured/missing plate) and contacts dispatch to confirm the record is current before a boot or tow is ordered. Occurs both on-street and in municipal lots.

tasks.label: Write warnings and citations for illegally parked vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On-street metered/overtime violation in a downtown business district: officer confirms the overtime or expired-meter condition, keys plate, VIN, make, location, meter number and violation code into a handheld ticket writer, captures photo evidence, prints the notice and serves it (windshield or, where the plate is captured, mailed).

Standing/parking prohibition violation on city streets (hydrant, bus stop, crosswalk, no-standing zone, double-parked, blocked driveway): officer documents the specific circumstance and measurements/photos needed to make the citation defensible, selects the correct ordinance section, and issues the notice, sometimes while the returning motorist argues.

Permit and space-type violations in an institutionally operated lot or garage (municipal lot, university, hospital, airport employee lot): officer checks permit/LPR list, verifies disabled placard validity or reserved-space misuse, and writes the citation or a written warning notice against the facility's rules schedule.

Written warning rather than a fine: first-offense courtesy warning, grace-period notice, expired-registration or street-sweeping advisory, or a 72-hour/abandoned-vehicle tag affixed and logged, requiring the officer to record the vehicle and start a clock for later follow-up.

Back-office and follow-up citation writing: composing or correcting notices from field notes, camera/LPR evidence or complaint reports, voiding and re-issuing erroneous tickets, and preparing mailed notices of violation to registered owners where no notice could be left on the vehicle.

tasks.label: Appear in court at hearings regarding contested traffic citations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Maintain assigned equipment and supplies, such as hand-held citation computers, citation books, rain gear, tire-marking chalk, and street cones.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shift start/end device care in the parking-enforcement office or equipment room: draw the assigned hand-held citation computer and spare battery from the charging rack, confirm charge and that the printer works, and at end of shift seat the unit in its dock/plug it in to recharge and upload the day's citations; swap a depleted battery pack.

Replenishing consumables from the stockroom/supply cabinet: draw citation books and forms, thermal paper rolls, tire-marking chalk, spare batteries and gloves; load a fresh paper roll into the hand-held citation printer and refill the kit bag to the standard load-out.

Stocking and unloading the patrol vehicle, cart or three-wheeler in the municipal yard/garage: loading stacks of street cones, signs, chalk box, rain gear and kit bag at the start of shift, unloading and stowing them at the end, and keeping the vehicle's gear organized and secured.

Cleaning and inspecting assigned gear at the yard/equipment room: hosing off and stacking dirty cones, hanging rain gear to dry, wiping down the hand-held and holster, checking for cracked cones, worn chalk holders or damaged devices, and tagging/turning in defective items for repair or replacement.

Upkeep in the field during patrol on public streets and sidewalks: swapping a dead battery or paper roll curbside, retrieving and repositioning cones set out at a tow or blocked-hydrant scene, stowing chalk and pulling out rain gear as weather changes, and keeping the kit intact while walking a beat.

tasks.label: Observe and report hazardous conditions, such as missing traffic signals or signs, and street markings that need to be repainted.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Downtown metered district, foot or scooter beat: while checking meters the officer notices roadway/streetside infrastructure problems — a knocked-down or missing parking or traffic sign, a faded crosswalk or curb paint, a dark or burned-out signal head — locates them by block and files a report to public works via radio or a mobile 311/works app.

Vehicle patrol (LPR-equipped car or three-wheeler) covering arterial and residential streets across a large zone: driving the route, the officer logs potholes, faded lane/parking-stall striping, obscured or damaged regulatory signs and other roadway defects with location, and forwards them at end of shift or in real time.

Rounds of a municipal surface lot or multi-level parking garage: burned-out lighting, faded stall lines and directional markings, potholes and broken pavement, damaged or missing signage, spills, ice or debris are noted and reported to the facilities/maintenance department.

Enforcement on an institution-controlled campus (university, hospital, airport) covering internal roads and lots: the officer reports damaged wayfinding/regulatory signs, faded markings, blocked or hazardous areas to campus facilities.

Urgent or unusual hazard encountered on a public street: a sign down in a travel lane, a dark signal at a busy intersection, street flooding, a downed line or spilled load — requiring prompt recognition, judgment about severity and immediate escalation to police/public works, sometimes standing by to warn traffic.

sources.system: Waymo Driver robotaxi fleet + Waze for Cities pothole pilot

tasks.label: Perform simple vehicle maintenance procedures, such as checking oil and gas, and report mechanical problems to supervisors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift (or post-shift) walkaround of the assigned patrol car/three-wheeler in the city motor-pool lot or garage: check tires, lights, mirrors and body damage, open the hood and check engine oil on the dipstick plus coolant and washer levels, look for leaks, then complete the vehicle check sheet and report any defect to the supervisor.

Mid-shift or end-of-shift refueling of the gasoline patrol vehicle at the municipal fuel island or a public gas station: pull up to the dispenser, open the fuel door and cap, authorize with fuel card/odometer entry, fill the tank, replace the cap and log the fuel/mileage.

Topping off fluids in the municipal garage or lot: adding a quart of engine oil when the level reads low, filling the windshield-washer reservoir, checking and adding coolant, and noting what was added on the log.

Checking tire pressures with a gauge and adding air to a soft tire at the garage air hose or a service-station air pump; also checking/replacing a burned-out bulb and cleaning the windshield and light bar.

Electric patrol cart/three-wheeler duty: checking state of charge on the gauge, plugging the charge connector into the vehicle at the depot or parking-structure charger at end of shift or for a midday top-up, confirming charging started, and reporting a charging fault.

tasks.label: Mark tires of parked vehicles with chalk and record time of marking, and return at regular intervals to ensure that parking time limits are not exceeded.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Downtown on-street time-limited zones (e.g., 2-hour free or metered curb parking): officer walks or rides a scooter/three-wheeler along a fixed beat, chalks the tire sidewall/valve stem of each parked vehicle (or scans plates), logs the time and space, and re-walks the loop every 1-2 hours to find overstays. Mixed pedestrian and vehicle traffic, weather, vehicles double-parked or tightly packed, occasional driver confrontation.

Residential permit districts and neighborhood/commuter-overflow streets: officer drives a patrol vehicle along multi-mile routes, chalking tires with a long-handled chalk stick or scanning plates, recording time, and returning on a set interval to catch vehicles exceeding the posted limit. Curb clutter, driveways, sloped and uneven streets, snow/rain, plates obscured or missing front plates.

City-owned downtown surface lots and municipal garages with posted 3-hour limits: officer walks the marked rows, chalks/records each vehicle and stall number at the start of the ..., and re-checks each row on schedule; institution controls the premises, striped stalls, lighting, standard layout.

University, hospital, or airport campus parking lots and multi-level structures: officer patrols permit and time-limited areas (e.g., 30-minute patient loading, 4-hour EV charge stalls, visitor spaces), marks/records vehicles and returns at intervals to identify overstays for citation or tow referral.

Private retail centers, apartment complexes and mixed-use lots enforced under contract: officer chalks or logs vehicles in 'customer parking only, 2-hour' stalls and returns on a set cycle to flag overstays for notices or tow; layout is fixed and property-managed, though signage and stall geometry vary by site.

sources.system: Knightscope K5 Autonomous Security Robot (ASR) with 360-degree ALPR and 'parking meter' thresholds in KSOC

sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 Autonomous Security Robot, a commercially deployed self-navigating outdoor patrol robot, has a parking-enforcement feature in which it tracks how long each vehicle has ... space during its patrols and alerts staff to vehicles violating time limits (e.g., 4-hour EV stall limits, non-24-hour garages) with plate numbers, map location and imagery.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in substance: periodic recording of each parked vehicle and its dwell time to detect time-limit overstays, i.e., the output tire-chalking produces.

tasks.label: Locate lost, stolen, and counterfeit parking permits, and take necessary enforcement action.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal on-street residential/visitor permit zone patrol: officer walks or drives a district, visually inspects hangtags and window decals displayed in parked cars, spots photocopied, altered or expired-looking permits and checks serial numbers against a hotlist of permits reported lost or stolen; on a hit, writes and affixes a citation to the windshield, photographs the permit as evidence, and may call a tow. Weather, mixed traffic, pedestrians and occupied vehicles are part of the conditions.

University / hospital / employer campus lot and garage patrol: officer patrols institution-controlled lots on foot or in a cart, checks hangtags and decals for counterfeit features (bad printing, altered dates, missing hologram, wrong lot color) and against a stolen-permit list on a handheld, then issues a citation, immobilizes (boot) or flags the vehicle for tow, confiscates the permit when accessible, and files a report to parking services / campus police.

Municipal public garage or metered surface lot sweep: enforcement worker walks decks checking dash-displayed permits and pay receipts, identifies duplicated or reported-stolen monthly permits, issues a citation, records evidence, and refers the permit holder's account for revocation; lot is owned and maintained by the parking authority.

Disabled-placard fraud check involving driver contact: officer inspects an accessible-parking placard on-street or in a public lot for hologram, expiry and serial, runs it against the state database, and — when it is counterfeit or belongs to a deceased/absent holder — contacts the driver, seizes the placard, issues the citation and forwards the placard and report to DMV or police.

Gated permit-controlled facility entry: worker staffing or monitoring a gated garage/employee lot entry lane catches a credential (RFID windshield tag, access card, registered plate) that has been reported lost or stolen or is being shared/duplicated, refuses entry, retains or deactivates the credential, and logs/reports the incident.

tasks.label: Provide assistance to motorists needing help with problems, such as flat tires, keys locked in cars, or dead batteries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dead battery in a city-owned garage, airport lot, or campus parking facility: officer responds in a patrol cart with a portable jump pack or cables, has the motorist pop the hood, identifies and clamps the 12V terminals (or a remote positive post) around engine-bay clutter, boosts, confirms the engine starts, and disconnects.

Keys locked inside a vehicle, curbside on a metered street or in an open lot: officer verifies ownership, then either works an air wedge and long-reach tool through the door seal without damaging weatherstripping, glass, wiring or airbags, or (per agency policy) waits with the motorist for a locksmith/tow.

Flat or badly underinflated tire on a vehicle at a curb space or in a lot: officer inflates it with a portable compressor, or helps the motorist jack the car, break loose and remove lug nuts, swap on the spare, and torque it, working alongside moving traffic in weather.

Stalled or disabled car blocking a travel lane, garage ramp, or drive aisle: officer sets cones/flares and a vest, directs traffic around it, helps push and steer the vehicle to the curb or an empty bay, and radios for a tow.

Non-mechanical aid in a patrolled garage or lot: motorist out of gas, unable to find their parked car, needing directions, an after-hours escort to the vehicle, or a call put in to dispatch/tow; officer walks them over or relays the request.

sources.title: RoboTire Installs First Revolutionary Tire Changing System at Discount Tire

sources.transferJustification: Related task: shop tire replacement. Transfers to roadside flat-tire assistance at E1 because the decisive manipulation is identical — locating lugs on a passenger-car wheel, unscrewing them to torque spec, pulling the wheel and refitting one.

sources.title: AI-powered RoboTire can change 4 tires twice as fast as a human

sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; this item establishes autonomy of the wheel removal/installation cycle.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: tire service. Shows current robotic tire work is confined to a purpose-built bay with the vehicle presented to the machine and parts hand-fed — evidence that E1, not E2/E3, is the reachable environment.
