tasks.label: Provide for public safety by maintaining order, responding to emergencies, protecting people and property, enforcing motor vehicle and criminal laws, and promoting good community relations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine mobile and foot patrol of an assigned public beat (residential streets, commercial strips, parks): driving/walking the area for visible deterrence, checking businesses and property, spotting and investigating suspicious persons or vehicles, initiating consensual contacts, and clearing or escalating what is found.

Motor-vehicle law enforcement on public roads: observing violations, initiating and conducting a traffic stop (positioning the cruiser, approaching a driver of unknown intent, collecting license/registration, issuing a citation or warning), plus manually directing traffic at crash scenes, dark signals, and school/event crossings.

Responding to dispatched emergency and priority calls at private homes and businesses (domestic disturbances, burglary/alarm calls, fights, injury crashes, medical/overdose calls): driving code, entering the location, separating and interviewing parties, rendering first aid, securing the scene, and producing an accepted disposition/report.

Physical control and custody: closing with a non-compliant or fleeing subject, applying hands-on control or force options, handcuffing, searching the person, loading into the cruiser, transporting, and booking — done in uncontrolled outdoor/indoor settings against a resisting human.

Assigned presence and community relations inside institution-controlled venues (school/university campus, transit station, stadium, courthouse, civic event): fixed post or foot patrol, crowd and access control, answering the public's questions, intervening in minor disorder, and school/community engagement.

sources.title: Autonomous public safety robots on patrol, connected by Verizon
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots patrol outdoor campuses, malls, hospital parking areas and lots commercially, but their function is continuous monitoring/alerting for human security personnel — they observe and report rather than contact, enforce, or intervene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is private/contract security patrol. It transfers partially to police patrol (same environments, same beat-coverage motion) but covers only the observe-and-report portion; no enforcement, contact, or intervention capability is demonstrated.

tasks.label: Identify, pursue, and arrest suspects and perpetrators of criminal acts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Traffic/vehicle stop on a public roadway that escalates to a custodial arrest: officer stops the car, contacts and identifies the driver (license, warrant check, impairment assessment), decides probable cause exists, orders the subject out, applies handcuffs, searches incident to arrest, secures the subject in the patrol car and transports to booking. Roadside, passing traffic, variable weather and lighting; subject may argue, flee, or resist.

Response to an in-progress or just-occurred call (disturbance, assault, domestic violence, theft) at a private residence, apartment, or street/parking lot: identify which person present is the suspect from statements and evidence, separate parties, and take the suspect into custody, often with verbal noncompliance, intoxication, mental-health crisis, or active physical resistance requiring hands-on control, handcuffing and search.

Active pursuit: suspect flees on foot through streets, yards, alleys and fences, or by vehicle; officer pursues running or driving, keeps the subject in sight, closes distance, takes the person to the ground or effects a felony vehicle stop, then handcuffs and secures the subject.

Planned apprehension / warrant service or investigative follow-up: officer identifies a wanted or suspected person from reports, photos, video or witness information, locates them at a home, workplace or on the street days later, verifies identity, and takes them into custody, usually with limited or no resistance; includes knock-and-talk arrests and arrests after a callback interview.

Arrest inside an institution-controlled facility: school or university campus, hospital, courthouse, transit station, airport terminal, or retail mall; officer is directed to a located subject by staff or security, confirms identity, handcuffs, and escorts the person through corridors to a patrol vehicle. Fixed layout, supervised premises, subject usually compliant but occasionally combative.

sources.title: Police 'Robot Dogs' Raise Concerns as More Departments Adopt Them (Governing/Bloomberg)
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot is deployed by 60+ US/Canadian bomb squads and SWAT teams for standoffs and building clearing, but it is driven by a human operator with a game-style controller; in the Hyannis hostage case it cornered the suspect while human officers made the apprehension.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fielded system to the pursue/apprehend step: it enters the same unstructured scenes (homes, motels, standoffs) but is remotely driven for decision making and never takes a person into custody, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of an arrest.

sources.system: Lubbock PD SWAT tracked ground robot
sources.developer: Lubbock Police Department (SWAT robot, vendor unspecified)
sources.title: Wanted man barricaded in Lubbock motel room shot, gassed out and taken into custody
sources.claim: In the closest documented case of a robot physically subduing a suspect, a Lubbock, TX police ground robot was driven by a human operator on top of a barricaded subject to pin him, after which the SWAT team took him into custody.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the physical-control step of arrest; it shows the state of the art is continuous teleoperation with humans performing handcuffing and custody, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Skydio X10 / Drone as First Responder
sources.title: SFPD Drone tracks car burglary suspect to arrest
sources.claim: Skydio drone-as-first-responder aircraft autonomously fly to scenes and autonomously maintain visual contact with suspects fleeing on foot or by vehicle on public streets, but the arrest is made by human officers guided by the drone video.
sources.transferJustification: Covers only the identify/pursue sub-steps of this task in E3 public settings; the aircraft has no means of physically detaining, handcuffing, searching or transporting a person, so it does not complete the whole instance.

sources.title: Knightscope Deploys First K5 Autonomous Security Robot (ASR) in Tennessee
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 Autonomous Security Robots patrol institution-controlled premises such as multi-story parking structures and distribution-center campuses autonomously, but their role is monitoring, data gathering and deterrence; they have no manipulators and do not detain or physically control people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous security patrol in an E2 facility. It shows autonomous mobile patrol is feasible in structured facilities, but the platform cannot identify, restrain or escort a suspect, so capability does not transfer to arrest.

sources.title: Chinese police trial amphibious crime-fighting robot sphere
sources.claim: China's RT-G spherical police robot has been trialed on patrol with police in a Wenzhou commercial zone and is described as able to chase suspects and carry net guns, but reporting does not establish autonomous operation and no verified case exists of it taking a person into custody.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest claimed 'chase and capture' police robot; autonomy is unclear so it is treated as teleoperated, and there is no evidence it completes an arrest.

tasks.label: Render aid to accident survivors and other persons requiring first aid for physical injuries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Motor-vehicle crash on a public roadway: officer is first on scene, approaches damaged vehicles, checks occupants for responsiveness and breathing, controls external bleeding with direct pressure/gauze, manually stabilizes head and neck, keeps the airway open, drapes/protects the patient, and monitors until EMS arrives. Traffic, weather, glass, fuel, entrapment, bystanders.

Unresponsive person from cardiac arrest or opioid overdose in a private home, vehicle, or public place: officer assesses pulse/breathing, starts chest compressions, applies AED pads and follows prompts, administers intranasal naloxone, places patient in recovery position, continues care until medics arrive. Cluttered rooms, confined spaces, distressed family.

Penetrating-trauma victim (gunshot, stabbing) at a violent-crime scene, street or residence: officer cuts away clothing, locates wounds, applies tourniquet high and tight or packs a wound with hemostatic gauze, applies a chest seal, and moves the patient to a safer position, in a dynamic, possibly unsecured scene.

Minor injuries in the field: lacerations, abrasions, nosebleeds, an elderly person who has fallen on a sidewalk or in a home, an injured child, a heat/cold-affected person. Officer cleans and bandages the wound, applies ice or a splint, assists the person up or keeps them still, and reassures them.

Injury response inside an institutional venue the agency polices: a school or university building, courthouse, stadium, transit station or airport concourse. Officer responds to a fall, fight injury, or medical collapse and renders first aid (bleeding control, AED, positioning) in a fixed-layout, controlled facility with staff support.

Injured person in custody or at the station/jail intake: arrestee with cuts, taser barb or restraint injuries, self-inflicted wounds, or an injured officer; officer provides first aid (wound cleaning, dressings, bleeding control, monitoring) inside a controlled agency facility before jail nurse or EMS assumes care.

sources.title: Sensor-guided robots could boost lifesaving combat casualty care | DARPA
sources.claim: DARPA in 2025-2026 solicited development of robots that could autonomously locate, assess and treat severe hemorrhage in casualties; Phase 1 begins summer 2026, indicating that autonomous robotic casualty care does not currently exist as a fielded or demonstrated capability.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to police first aid (locate and stop bleeding in a casualty). It is a research solicitation with functional systems only expected within 24 months of a summer-2026 Phase 1 start, so it substantiates no present capability at any tier.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection | Waterloo News | University of Waterloo
sources.claim: A robot autonomously performed an intramuscular needle-free injection on a human subject in a lab demonstration; the subject was cooperative and positioned for the machine, and the task was a single injection, not assessment and treatment of injuries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: administering a drug to a person (analogous to naloxone administration). Transfer fails because the demonstration requires a cooperative, correctly presented patient and covers only the injection step, not scene assessment, airway/breathing management, or bleeding control on an injured or unresponsive person.

sources.title: Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performs laparoscopic surgery on pig soft tissue without human help
sources.claim: A supervised-autonomous surgical robot performed laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis on anesthetized pigs in an operating-room/lab setting with ports placed and tissue exposed by humans and fluorescent markers applied.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation and closure of soft tissue. It represents the ceiling of autonomous robotic care on a body, yet it needs an anesthetized, fixtured, surgically prepared subject and human setup, so it does not substantiate rendering first aid to an injured person even in a purpose-built setting.

sources.system: Autonomous tape handling framework for robotic wound redressing
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Robotic wound redressing (removing tape and placing dressing tape) is at the research-prototype stage, evaluated on phantom surfaces, anatomical limb models and human skin in a laboratory, not as an accepted clinical or field first-aid capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a dressing to a wound, the core of minor-injury first aid. Transfer fails: it is a sub-step demonstrated on static phantoms/models under lab conditions, with no wound assessment, cleaning, or handling of a moving, distressed patient.

sources.system: Automated pneumatic tourniquet / AutoTQ-class device evaluated on an adaptive testing platform
sources.developer: US Army Institute of Surgical Research (Expeditionary Medical Systems Dept.)
sources.title: Automated pneumatic tourniquet for hemorrhage control evaluated using an adaptive testing platform | Frontiers in Medical Technology
sources.claim: An automated pneumatic tourniquet system can regulate inflation to stop limb hemorrhage, but a human must place the cuff on the correct limb; the automation covers only pressure control, not scene assessment or application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hemorrhage control. It is an instrumented device, not a robot that finds a casualty, exposes a wound and applies the cuff; a human performs every manipulation step, so it cannot support completion of the first-aid instance at any tier.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically handling an injured person in the field. Transfer fails because the platforms are remote-controlled transporters and render no aid, so they cannot substantiate first-aid completion.

tasks.label: Investigate illegal or suspicious activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dispatched or self-initiated response to a suspicious person/activity call on a public street, sidewalk or parking lot: locate the subject, observe behavior, approach and question, obtain identification, run records checks, conduct a pat-down or consent search if warranted, and resolve the contact (clear, warn, cite, or arrest) with a report.

Investigative traffic/vehicle stop of a suspicious vehicle on a public roadway: stop the car, approach, observe occupants and plain-view contraband, question driver and passengers, check documents and warrants, run field sobriety tests or a vehicle search as justified, seize evidence, and dispose of the stop.

Commercial burglar-alarm or 'check the building' call at a business, school, or warehouse: walk the perimeter checking doors, windows and gates for forced entry, look for suspects in the lot, enter and search the interior with a keyholder if open, and clear or escalate the call.

Preliminary investigation of a reported crime at a private home or small business (burglary, theft, vandalism, assault): interview the victim and witnesses, walk the scene, identify and photograph/collect physical evidence, canvass neighbors and pull video, identify suspects, and write the investigative report.

Proactive/follow-up investigation of suspected ongoing criminal activity (drug house, gang activity, prowlers, fencing operation) in a neighborhood: stationary or mobile surveillance, plate and person checks, knock-and-talks with residents, curbside/trash checks, and documentation supporting a warrant affidavit.

sources.system: Drone as First Responder (DFR) program, Minnetonka Police Department
sources.developer: Municipal police agencies with Skydio/Flock/Brinc platforms
sources.title: Drones as First Responders | City of Minnetonka, MN
sources.claim: Police drone-as-first-responder programs launch camera drones from docks to 911 calls to give officers and dispatchers live video before ground units arrive; the drone supplies situational awareness while officers still respond and act.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial overwatch of calls for service. It supplies observation only; the investigative acts in this task (contact, questioning, identification, search, evidence seizure, disposition) remain with human officers, so it does not transfer to whole-task completion.

sources.title: The BVLOS Revolution Continues: Introducing Multi-Drone Operations | Skydio
sources.claim: Even the most advanced police drone operations keep a human remote Pilot in Command directing missions; the newest FAA waivers only let one PIC supervise up to four Skydio X10s at once.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the autonomy status of the closest fielded police robotic system: a human pilot in command supervises each mission and interprets the video, so DFR cannot support a positive autonomous judgment.

sources.title: K5 - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 is an autonomous security robot that patrols malls, offices and parking lots watching for suspicious behavior; it records, detects anomalies and alerts humans rather than conducting an investigation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol and anomaly detection. Transfer is limited to the observation step; K5 has no manipulator and cannot approach or question a subject, check identification, search a vehicle or person, or collect evidence.

sources.system: Knightscope K5 (NYPD pilot; first police department contract)
sources.title: NYPD signs contract with Knightscope, plans to leverage robots for policing
sources.claim: Police agencies have contracted for K5 units, including an NYPD pilot placing a K5 in a Manhattan subway station, showing the deployed police role is monitored patrol presence rather than investigation.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of police-deployed autonomous ground robots: fixed-route patrol in a controlled transit facility, with all investigative contacts and decisions handled by officers.

sources.system: Spot quadruped in police/SWAT use (e.g., LAPD, NYPD)
sources.title: Boston Dynamics' robot dog Spot takes on growing police role (NZ Herald)
sources.claim: More than 60 US and Canadian bomb squads and SWAT teams use Boston Dynamics' Spot for standoffs, hostage rescues and inspecting suspicious packages, but the machines are remote-controlled by an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic reconnaissance inside buildings and around suspicious objects during police incidents. It is continuous teleoperation by an officer, so it cannot support a positive judgment on autonomous investigation.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot autonomously patrols corporate facilities and analyzes events, but human specialists remain in the loop for interaction and incident handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor alarm/anomaly investigation inside a structured facility. Transfer fails for police investigation because human specialists conduct all interaction and the robot cannot open or check doors, search rooms, or detain.

sources.title: Asylon DroneDog pitched as physical security for large solar sites
sources.claim: Asylon's DroneDog ground robot and Guardian drone-in-a-box perform autonomous perimeter patrols and alarm response at industrial and utility sites, with live human monitoring of every response.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous alarm response and perimeter checks at a controlled private site. It verifies whether an alarm is real for a remote human; it does not question subjects, search interiors, seize evidence, or resolve a police call.

sources.title: Ascento launches nimble Guard robot with wheel-leg design - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Ascento's Guard robot autonomously patrols outdoor industrial premises, detecting unwanted people and checking that doors and windows are ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor perimeter and door-status checking at a fixed industrial site, the closest analogue to a building-check call. It observes closure status only; it cannot test locks, inspect for pry marks up close, enter and clear an interior, or contact suspects.

sources.title: Drone as First Responder Programs: 2025 in Review | Electronic Frontier Foundation
sources.claim: A national review of 2025 DFR growth describes drones launched from pads to 911 calls, operated by pilots or with increasing automation, functioning as camera feeds into real-time crime centers.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates the deployment model and autonomy status of police aerial systems: sensing and streaming to human decision-makers, not autonomous completion of investigations.

tasks.label: Drive vehicles or patrol specific areas to detect law violators, issue citations, and make arrests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine marked-unit patrol of city/suburban streets with traffic enforcement: officer drives an assigned beat in mixed traffic, observes a moving violation (speeding, red light, expired tags), conducts a traffic stop at the roadside, approaches the vehicle, verifies license/registration, checks for warrants, and issues a written citation or warning before clearing the stop.

Patrol of a high-call-volume neighborhood or business district (vehicle plus periodic foot patrol): officer checks suspicious persons and vehicles, contacts subjects in parking lots, alleys and doorways, enforces local ordinances (open container, trespass, loitering) with warnings or citations, and occasionally takes a subject into custody by hand.

Arrest arising from patrol: officer detects a violator (shoplifter, wanted subject, fleeing person), makes physical contact, controls possibly resisting arms, applies handcuffs, searches the person incident to arrest, secures them in the caged patrol car, and transports to booking.

Night and rural/highway patrol: low-light driving at highway speeds, radar/lidar speed enforcement, DUI detection from driving pattern, roadside stop on a shoulder or unlit road, administering field sobriety tests, and either citing or arresting the impaired driver.

Patrol of institution-controlled property (university campus, transit station, airport, municipal parking garage or lot): fixed layout, standard signage, controlled premises; officer drives/walks the property, runs plates, enforces parking and permit rules by placing citations, cites or ejects trespassers, and detains offenders.

sources.system: PUG (Police Unmanned Ground) autonomous patrol cruiser
sources.developer: The Policing Lab / Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Fla. sheriff's office debuts 'PUG,' a self-driving cruiser equipped with drone, LPR technology (Police1/Miami Herald)
sources.claim: The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office 'PUG', described as the first US autonomous police patrol car, drives pre-determined routes as a visible deterrent with drone, LPR and cameras, but is explicitly not able to pull over vehicles or issue tickets, and carries a deputy in the front seat for at least its first year.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: an autonomous police patrol vehicle patrolling public streets; the source states it cannot perform the stop/citation portion of the task.

sources.title: DubBot robot 'retires' from Dublin police after less than a year of service (WOSU Public Media)
sources.claim: Dublin, Ohio's Knightscope K5 'DubBot' autonomously patrolled a municipal parking garage for about ten months and produced no identified criminal incidents, no citations and no arrests; the pilot was ended and the robot returned in 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in an institution-controlled facility: an autonomous patrol robot working a police patrol beat, documented as unable to detect violators, cite, or assist arrests.

sources.title: Micropolis Holding Co. Begins Final Phase of Autonomous Police Patrol Testing in Collaboration with Dubai Expo City and Dubai Police
sources.claim: Micropolis's M2 Autonomous Police Patrol pilot with Dubai Police tests autonomous driving, mission planning, license-plate recognition and behavior analysis; the platform is a patrol/surveillance unit and no citation-issuing or arrest capability is described.
sources.transferJustification: Most capable dedicated autonomous police patrol UGV; it demonstrates patrol and detection only, inside a managed venue, not stops, citations or arrests.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Public Safety: Skydio and Axon's Drone as First Responder (DFR) Programs
sources.claim: Dock-based Drone-as-First-Responder systems launch autonomously from rooftop docks and arrive over incidents in about 90 seconds, providing aerial observation for officers; the drones cannot contact violators, issue citations or make arrests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous aerial patrol and response over public areas); shows current autonomy is limited to observation and cueing human officers, with no enforcement contact.

sources.developer: Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX), Singapore
sources.title: Singapore testing robots to patrol pedestrian areas for 'undesirable social behaviors' (FOX 29)
sources.claim: Singapore's Xavier robots patrolled a public plaza autonomously to detect prohibited behaviours (illegally parked bicycles, smoking, hawking) and display warnings, alerting human officers rather than taking enforcement action themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous ground patrol for violation detection in a public precinct); enforcement output is limited to deterrence and officer notification, not citations or arrests.

tasks.label: Monitor, note, report, and investigate suspicious persons and situations, safety hazards, and unusual or illegal activity in patrol area.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine mobile beat patrol on public streets and neighborhoods: cruising the assigned sector day or night, scanning for suspicious persons, occupied vehicles, open gates, running plates on the mobile data terminal, driving past problem addresses, and logging or radioing anything noteworthy. Mixed traffic, pedestrians, weather; no control over the setting.

Field contact with a suspicious person or vehicle occupant spotted on patrol: pulling up, illuminating, getting out, approaching and questioning the subject, obtaining and checking ID, reading demeanor and watching for weapons, pat-down if warranted, then releasing, warning or detaining, and documenting the stop.

Nighttime premise and perimeter checks of closed businesses, warehouses and yards, parking lots and structures, schools after hours, and vacant property: walking or driving the perimeter, checking doors, windows and gates, lighting alleys and loading docks, noting broken glass, open doors or squatters, and reporting findings.

Patrol assignment inside an institution-controlled venue: school or college campus, transit station, hospital, courthouse, mall, airport concourse, or permitted special event. Walking or riding a fixed area, watching crowds, spotting unattended bags, loiterers, trespassers and hazards, reporting or checking on what looks wrong.

Safety hazard encountered on patrol requiring on-scene action: roadway debris, downed limb or power line, dark or malfunctioning traffic signal, flooding, leaking vehicle. Officer protects the scene with the patrol car, flares or cones, directs traffic around it, notifies public works or the utility, and stands by until cleared.

Unusual or illegal activity observed on patrol requiring immediate physical intervention: a traffic or equipment violation warranting a stop, a trespasser to eject, an open-door or alarmed building to check and clear, a disturbance or drinking-in-public group to break up, with follow-up documentation.

sources.title: Huntington Park Police Renews Knightscope Contract for 6th Year
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot has been contracted by the Huntington Park (CA) Police Department to patrol a public city park since 2019, renewed for a sixth year in 2024, with the city crediting it with reduced calls for service and crime reports.
sources.transferJustification: Same task performed for a police agency: the machine monitors a patrol area for unusual activity and records/reports it, which is the monitor-note-report content of this task.

sources.title: Privacy Impact Assessment: Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR)-E, U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
sources.claim: VA Police at the South Texas Health Care System operate a Knightscope K5 to monitor activity in patrolled areas of the hospital campus; the robot detects anomalies on its patrol path and alerts officers to respond, capturing video and license plates while patrolling VA-controlled property.

sources.title: Knightscope Unveils Major K5 Robot Upgrade, Lands First Police Department Contract
sources.claim: The K5 has been deployed across many institution-controlled facilities - schools, hospitals, corporate campuses, casinos, ..., storage facilities - and a January 2025 navigation upgrade extends it to large parking lots and logistics centers, with an Ohio police department signing a two-year agreement.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot autonomously runs scheduled and ad-hoc patrol routes of corporate facilities, performing security patrols and facility checks and flagging anomalies (people, doors held or forced open, suspicious items, leaks) to a monitoring platform and remote specialists.
sources.transferJustification: Private security rather than sworn patrol, but the monitored content is identical - unauthorized persons, open doors, suspicious items, facility hazards inside controlled premises - and detections are escalated to responders as in this task.

sources.title: The Ohio Police Department Hired An AI Bot To Catch Criminals And Issue Tickets, Then They Fired The $70k Robot Because It Didn't Do Anything
sources.claim: Counter-evidence on worker-quality substitution: Dublin, Ohio PD retired its Knightscope K5 ('DubBot') after about a year patrolling the Rock Cress parking ... because it produced no detections leading to enforcement or officer response.

sources.title: NYPD security robot, K5, that patrolled Times Square subway station in Midtown, Manhattan, NYC is no longer in use
sources.claim: The NYPD's K5 pilot in the Times Square subway ... ended after the robot was confined to the mezzanine because it could not use ... and had to be chaperoned by officers during its shifts.

sources.system: Chula Vista PD Drone as First Responder program
sources.title: How Chula Vista PD is using drones as first responders
sources.claim: Drone-as-First-Responder programs put an aerial camera over incidents in public areas, but the flight and the observation are run by a remote human pilot/teleoperator, and the drone cannot make contact or intervene physically.

sources.system: PUG Patrol Partner (Police Unmanned Ground vehicle)
sources.developer: Policing Lab / Perrone Robotics / Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Nation's first autonomous police vehicle is getting ready for Miami-Dade service
sources.claim: The only US self-driving patrol vehicle for public streets, the Miami-Dade Sheriff's PUG Patrol Partner unveiled in October 2025, was still a pilot not operating in the field months later.

sources.title: Computerized canines to join Tyndall AFB
sources.claim: The US Air Force integrated semi-autonomous quad-legged robots into perimeter patrol at Tyndall AFB, providing surveillance of installation perimeters fed to an operations center.
sources.transferJustification: Installation perimeter patrol is the same monitor-and-report activity; cited as supporting context only, since the degree of autonomy is not established.

tasks.label: Investigate traffic accidents and other accidents to determine causes and to determine if a crime has been committed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Minor non-injury collision at a city street or intersection: officer drives to the scene, protects it with the cruiser, checks occupants for injury, moves drivable vehicles off the travel lanes, collects licenses/registrations/insurance, walks the roadway to look at debris fields, skid marks, damage patterns and sight lines, interviews the drivers and any bystanders, judges the point of impact and who violated right-of-way, decides whether a citable/criminal offense (unlicensed, no insurance, reckless) occurred, and files an accepted crash report.

Serious injury or fatal crash on a highway or arterial: officer secures a large scene amid traffic, triages injuries, preserves and documents transient evidence (fluid trails, gouge marks, tire marks, vehicle final rest), measures/maps the scene, photographs, inspects vehicles for mechanical failure and restraint use, seizes EDR/black-box data and phones, canvasses witnesses, coordinates with reconstructionists and a medical examiner, and determines cause and criminal liability (vehicular homicide, hit-and-run).

Crash where impairment or another crime is suspected: officer detects odor/behavior cues, conducts standardized field sobriety tests at the roadside, administers a preliminary breath test, searches the vehicle for open containers/contraband, seizes evidence, makes an arrest decision, and documents the causal link between impairment and the collision.

Collision or hit-and-run on private property (retail parking lot, apartment lot, driveway) often reported after the fact: officer inspects vehicle damage transfer and paint, looks for the striking vehicle or debris, seeks private surveillance footage from the property owner, interviews the complainant, and determines whether the incident is a reportable crash and whether leaving-the-scene occurred.

Non-traffic accident at a home or business: fall down stairs, industrial machinery injury, accidental firearm discharge, drowning, carbon-monoxide or fire-related injury. Officer enters an uncontrolled setting, checks the injured party, examines the scene for consistency with the account given, photographs injuries and hazards, talks to family/coworkers, and determines whether the injury was accidental or the result of a crime (assault, child neglect, criminal negligence).

Station-counter or follow-up work: a citizen comes to the police station lobby days later to report a crash; the officer goes to the station lot to view and photograph the damaged vehicle, compares damage to the account, checks records/camera footage, and issues or declines a report or citation.

sources.system: Skydio X10 with 3D Scan / Map Capture
sources.title: Drones for Crash & Crime Scene Documentation
sources.claim: Skydio drones with 3D Scan/Map Capture autonomously fly a scan path over a vehicle crash scene and capture the imagery used to build orthomosaics and 3D reconstructions; the officer sets the scan boundaries and still runs the investigation, so the system covers only the scene-documentation sub-step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is crash-scene mapping/photogrammetry, one sub-step of accident investigation. It transfers only for measurement and imagery capture at outdoor roadway scenes; it does not carry over to injury triage, vehicle/evidence handling, interviewing drivers and witnesses, or the cause-and-criminality determination and report that define this task.

sources.title: Flock DFR — Drone as First Responder | Flock Safety
sources.claim: Flock's Aerodome Drone-as-First-Responder system launches drones automatically from docks on 911 call data and reaches scenes in about 86 seconds, but it delivers overhead video/situational awareness to human responders rather than conducting an investigation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated first-response overflight of incident scenes, including crashes. It transfers only as remote observation: the platform has no manipulators, cannot contact parties, test for impairment, seize evidence, or produce an accepted crash report determining cause and criminality.

sources.title: Knightscope on X: What is the Knightscope K5 Autonomous Security Robot (ASR)?
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots patrol defined routes in structured outdoor and indoor facilities such as parking structures and campuses, capturing and analyzing activity, but they are a monitoring/deterrence layer that escalates to humans rather than investigating incidents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous patrol and incident recording in parking lots and campuses, the setting of the private-property collision instance. It transfers only as passive sensing; the K5 cannot examine damage, interview a complainant, or determine whether a hit-and-run crime occurred.

tasks.label: Execute arrest warrants, locating and taking persons into custody.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Warrant service at a subject's home: officers drive to a residence or apartment on a warrant list, knock, talk with occupants who may deny the subject is there, confirm identity of the wanted person, handcuff and search him, secure children/pets/property, and transport him to booking. Layout unknown, occupants may be uncooperative, subject may flee out a back door.

Warrant discovered during a street or traffic contact: officer stops a vehicle or pedestrian, runs the name, gets a warrant hit, orders the person out, controls and handcuffs him at roadside, pats him down, secures the vehicle, and transports to jail. Roadside/sidewalk, live traffic, bystanders, possible flight or resistance.

Subject located at an institution-controlled premises — a workplace, store, school, hospital, or courthouse — where staff cooperate: officers meet the subject in a lobby, office, or ward, verify identity, handcuff discreetly, and escort him out to a patrol car with minimal disruption.

Low-conflict custody intake: subject turns himself in at the station or courthouse on a warrant, or is picked up from another agency's jail on a hold; officer verifies warrant and identity, cuffs, searches, completes paperwork, and transports the compliant subject.

High-risk fugitive apprehension: warrant task force or tactical team locates a violent or evasive subject at a motel, stash house, or vehicle; surveillance, containment, forced entry or vehicle takedown, physical control of a resisting or armed subject, then custody and transport.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot (police use, Massachusetts State Police, LAPD, Denver PD)
sources.title: Police 'Robot Dogs' Raise Concerns as More Departments Adopt Them
sources.claim: The most capable police ground robots in US service (Boston Dynamics Spot) are used for reconnaissance, approach, and negotiation with barricaded suspects; they are operated by a human with a controller and video feed, and human officers perform the actual apprehension.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic support in suspect apprehension. It is the closest fielded analogue to executing an arrest warrant, and it shows fielded police robots only observe, approach and communicate under teleoperation, while human officers take the person into custody.

sources.title: Can Robots Replace Human Security Guards?
sources.claim: Commercially deployed autonomous security robots patrol facilities and public areas but are explicitly limited to observing, reporting, and vocal warnings; they cannot physically detain or take custody of a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol and intruder response in structured facilities. It bounds the state of the art for autonomous robots interacting with non-compliant people: the most mature autonomous patrol robots do no physical control of persons at all.

sources.system: EngineAI T800 humanoid robot on police patrol, Shenzhen
sources.title: Humanoid 'Terminator' robot cop patrols with police officers in China
sources.claim: The frontier of humanoid robots in policing is escorted patrol presence alongside officers, not physical custody of persons.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: police patrol with a humanoid platform. Shows that even the most publicized humanoid law-enforcement deployment is a walking presence with unclear autonomy, providing no evidence of locating, restraining, or transporting a person.

tasks.label: Relay complaint and emergency-request information to appropriate agency dispatchers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Patrol specific area on foot, horseback, or motorized conveyance, responding promptly to calls for assistance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Marked patrol car on a municipal/suburban beat: roving the assigned district's public streets and lots for a shift, self-initiated observation, then responding (often code 3) to dispatched calls — disturbances, burglar alarms, fights, welfare checks, collisions — arriving, contacting citizens, and handling the incident.

County/rural or state-highway patrol unit: covering a large beat at highway speed on unlit two-lane and gravel roads, in weather, with backup far away; responding to crashes, stranded motorists, property/livestock calls and alarms at isolated addresses.

Foot, bicycle, or mounted patrol of a downtown entertainment district, plaza, park, or event crowd on public sidewalks: dense pedestrian contact, citizen flag-downs, intoxicated or disorderly persons, and immediate response to disturbances within sight or a block away.

Campus/school police officer patrol: walking building interiors, quads and parking lots of a university or school district, checking doors and lots, and responding to on-campus calls — intrusion alarms, student disputes, medical/behavioral incidents, thefts.

Transit, airport, or civic-complex detail: foot patrol of a station concourse, airport terminal, or government building footprint controlled by the operating institution, responding to calls inside that footprint (sick passenger, unattended bag, trespass, entry dispute).

Overnight directed 'presence' patrol of a fixed, low-traffic, agency-controlled footprint (municipal park paths, civic-center parking structures, city yard/impound lot): the deliverable is visible deterrence, roving observation and prompt reporting of suspicious activity or hazards to dispatch; citizen contacts are rare and any incident is referred to responding units.

sources.developer: The Policing Lab / Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Fla. sheriff's office debuts 'PUG,' a self-driving cruiser equipped with drone, LPR technology (Police1 / Miami Herald)
sources.claim: The only US autonomous police patrol car, the Policing Lab 'PUG' fielded by the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office, drives pre-determined routes as a deterrent/message platform, is speed-limited and barred from highways, and carries a deputy in the front seat for at least its first year; it is explicitly not a roving deputy that can make stops.

sources.title: SPF | Police Life | GIBSON: The Robotic Platform Transforming Policing at Changi Airport
sources.claim: Singapore Police Force's GIBSON robot patrols Changi Airport Terminal 4 departure hall autonomously, adding police presence; its response role is to be summoned as a rideable platform so human officers reach incidents faster.

sources.title: Huntington Park Police Renews Knightscope Contract for 6th Year
sources.claim: A police department has contracted a Knightscope K5 autonomous security ... to patrol a specific municipal area (Salt Lake Park) continuously for six consecutive years, providing autonomous patrol, alerting and two-way communication.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contracted police patrol of a defined municipal area. Transfers to the presence/observe/report leg of directed patrol over the same maintained paved footprint; it does not transfer to on-scene citizen assistance.

sources.title: Incident 77: Knightscope's Park Patrol Robot Ignored Bystander Pressing Emergency Button to Alert Police about Fight (AI Incident Database)
sources.claim: The same autonomously patrolling police K5 failed the 'respond to a call for assistance' leg: a bystander pressed its emergency alert button during a nearby fight and the robot did not summon help.

sources.title: NYPD security robot, K5, that patrolled Times Square subway station in Midtown, Manhattan, NYC is no longer in use (ABC7 New York)
sources.claim: NYPD's K5 trial in the Times Square subway ... required officers to chaperone the robot throughout its midnight-to-6am run, and the six-month trial ended without continuation.

sources.title: Asylon Celebrates 250K Combined Security Missions - Asylon Robotics
sources.claim: Asylon's DroneDog (Boston Dynamics Spot plus PupPack) runs autonomous programmed patrol routes with AI alerting and self-charging at commercial and critical-infrastructure sites, surpassing 250,000 automated security missions and 150,000 patrol miles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: security guard perimeter patrol. Transfers to the roving-presence, anomaly-detection and reporting legs of directed patrol over fixed routes in controlled facility footprints; it does not transfer to citizen contact or enforcement.

sources.title: The Force — Autonomous Security Force | Knightscope (K5 product page)
sources.claim: Knightscope markets the K5 for structured outdoor settings — parking lots, campuses and walkways — at pedestrian speeds, i.e. maintained, institution-controlled premises rather than open roadway or unstructured terrain.

sources.title: Security Robots: Practical Investment or Expensive Experiment in 2026?
sources.claim: Commercial patrol robots in 2026 are characterized as route-following data collectors that alert human operators; they are not independent decision ... and do not replace guard forces.

sources.system: Chula Vista PD Drone as First Responder
sources.developer: Chula Vista Police Department / DFR vendors
sources.title: 2025: The year drone as first responder programs went mainstream (Police1)
sources.claim: Drone-as-first-responder programs fly to 911 calls and often arrive before ground units, but flights are run by a teleoperator and the drone supplies only aerial overwatch; about a quarter of responses release ground units while the rest still require officers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: prompt response to calls for service. Covers only the aerial-observation leg with a human pilot in the loop; no ground patrol presence, citizen contact or physical assistance, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

tasks.label: Monitor traffic to ensure motorists observe traffic regulations and exhibit safe driving procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Stationary speed enforcement: officer parks the patrol unit at a known spot on a public street or highway, runs radar/lidar on approaching traffic, identifies a speeder, pulls out into traffic, stops the vehicle on the shoulder, contacts the driver, and issues a warning or citation.

Mobile patrol observation on city/suburban public streets: officer drives a patrol car in mixed traffic while watching for red-light and stop-sign violations, phone use, seatbelt and equipment violations, expired tags, and erratic driving; runs plates, decides whether to intervene, and initiates a stop.

Interstate/highway traffic patrol at high speed: monitoring lane discipline, following distance, aggressive drivers and commercial-vehicle behavior; pacing a violator, executing a stop on a live-traffic shoulder, and clearing safely back into traffic.

Night or DUI-focused traffic monitoring: low-light observation of impaired-driving cues (weaving, delayed starts, no headlights) on public roads during saturation patrol or at a checkpoint, followed by a stop and roadside evaluation.

Fixed-post, high-visibility monitoring at a school zone, work zone, special event, or congested urban intersection with mixed pedestrian, cyclist and motor traffic: deterrent presence, gestures/verbal corrections to violators, keeping traffic compliant and moving, and reporting violations rather than making stops.

sources.system: Hangzhou traffic management robot squad (first robot traffic police squad)
sources.developer: Hangzhou Public Security Bureau traffic management detachment (with industry partners)
sources.title: Meet China's first robot traffic police squad - People's Daily Online
sources.claim: A squad of 15 traffic-management robots deployed at key public intersections in Hangzhou autonomously monitors intersections around the clock, detects traffic violations, issues on-site voice warnings, performs signal-synchronized directing gestures, and escalates unresolved violations to a police early-warning centre; over 25,000 warnings issued in 647.7 hours of duty.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: monitoring traffic at a post on a public roadway to obtain compliance with traffic regulations. Limitation noted: demonstrated violation detection is of non-motorized riders and pedestrians, and the robot issues warnings rather than stopping motor vehicles.

sources.system: "Intelligent Police Unit R001" AI traffic policing robot
sources.title: AI-powered "RoboCops" take up traffic duties in Chinese cities-Xinhua
sources.claim: A humanoid traffic-policing robot on duty at a public intersection in Wuhu, Anhui autonomously identifies traffic violations by non-motorized vehicles ..., delivers on-site voice warnings, performs signal-synchronized traffic gestures, identifies illegal parking, and can navigate independently to assigned locations.
sources.transferJustification: Same task performed from a fixed roadway post: real-time road monitoring for regulation compliance with on-site correction. It does not detect moving motor-vehicle violations such as speeding, nor stop vehicles.

sources.system: PUG (Police Unmanned Ground vehicle) Patrol Partner
sources.developer: Policing Lab / Perrone Robotics, with Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Nation's first autonomous police vehicle is getting ready for Miami-Dade service - Refresh Miami
sources.claim: The first US autonomous police patrol vehicle (Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office pilot) is limited to patrol presence, 360-degree video and plate reading; it is operated with a deputy behind the wheel during the pilot and is explicitly not capable of pulling vehicles over or issuing tickets, with later phases planned to be teleoperable on predetermined geofenced routes.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (autonomous police patrol on public roads); establishes that the leading US system cannot perform the enforcement action that completes traffic monitoring.

sources.title: The Force — Autonomous Security Force | Knightscope (K5)
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot patrols structured outdoor settings such as parking lots and campuses at pedestrian speed, with plate recognition, thermal imaging and public address; commercial deployments include monitoring vehicle and pedestrian traffic and campus parking compliance at institutional sites such as a VA health care campus.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous vehicle/traffic monitoring inside an institution-controlled facility (E2). sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous driving and traffic perception on public roads covers the locomotion/observation portion of patrol, but there is no evidence of legally sufficient violation detection (calibrated speed measurement, driver identification) or of executing a traffic stop, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

tasks.label: Place people in protective custody.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Public intoxication hold: officer contacts a heavily intoxicated, unsteady and sometimes belligerent person on a street, bar parking lot or park; evaluates whether they are a danger to self, pats them down for weapons, physically supports or handcuffs them, walks/lifts them into the patrol car, transports them to a detox center or jail holding, secures property and completes the custody report.

Emergency mental-health hold (e.g., 5150/EDO) on a person in crisis at a residence or on the street: officer talks the person down, secures knives/firearms, may go hands-on with an agitated or self-harming subject, applies restraints, loads them into a cruiser or assists medics with a gurney, and delivers them to a hospital emergency department with the hold paperwork.

Child taken into protective custody at a home or scene: officer removes an infant or young child from an unsafe/neglectful home or from a crash or arrest scene over a caregiver's objection, carries or coaxes the child out, secures them in a car seat, comforts them, and transports to a hospital, CPS worker or emergency shelter.

At-risk vulnerable adult located in public: a dementia patient wandering a roadway, an elderly or medically impaired person found confused outdoors; officer physically steadies and guides them out of danger, checks for injury and ID, seats them in the car and delivers them to a hospital or caregiver.

Endangered victim or witness placed in protective custody: a domestic-violence or trafficking victim, or a runaway juvenile, taken from a volatile scene, screened for weapons, driven to a shelter, safe house or station, and kept under officer protection until handed to an advocate.

Custody maintained inside a controlled facility: at a hospital emergency department, station holding room or juvenile intake, the officer takes physical custody of the person from another unit, searches them, secures belongings, places them in a monitored room or restraints, watches them until the receiving agency signs the transfer.

sources.title: Dublin, Ohio, robot cop sent back after zero arrests in parking garage | Fox News
sources.claim: The most widely deployed US law-enforcement patrol robot, Knightscope's K5, is a wheeled sensor platform with no arms; after nearly a year of autonomous patrol for the Dublin, Ohio police it produced zero arrests, citations or criminal cases and was returned, showing deployed police robots do not take physical custody of people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous police patrol in a controlled parking structure. It bounds current police robotics: the deployed platform observes and alerts but has no manipulators and never took a person into custody, so it cannot perform protective-custody holds.

sources.title: China Tests Autonomous 'Spherical' Robot Police Unit in Cities | eWEEK
sources.claim: The most aggressive fielded police robot, the spherical RT-G used by Chinese police, at most immobilizes a suspect with non-lethal weapons (net gun, tear gas); it has no arms, cannot handcuff, escort, search, transport, or hand a person off to a receiving facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pursuing and immobilizing a fleeing suspect. Even this closest analogue stops at temporary immobilization with weapons and lacks the manipulation, transport and handoff steps that constitute placing someone in protective custody.

sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: Robots built to physically lift and move a compliant human — RIKEN's ROBEAR patient-transfer robot — remained an operator-guided laboratory prototype and the program was closed in 2015; no fielded system autonomously takes hold of a person and moves them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and transferring a human body between bed and wheelchair, the closest robotic analogue to physically moving an intoxicated or incapacitated person. It was operator-guided and never commercialized, so it cannot substantiate autonomous custody of a person.

sources.title: Battlefield Extraction-Assist Robot to ferry wounded to safety - New Atlas
sources.claim: The humanoid casualty-extraction robot BEAR, designed to lift and carry a person, is remotely controlled by a ... rather than autonomous, and never entered service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating, lifting and carrying an incapacitated human to safety — mechanically the same act as moving an unresponsive person into protective custody. Because it is continuously teleoperated, it cannot support a positive autonomy judgment.

tasks.label: Patrol and guard courthouses, grand jury rooms, or assigned areas to provide security, enforce laws, maintain order, and arrest violators.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fixed post at a courthouse entrance screening checkpoint: running the magnetometer and X-ray line, directing visitors and attorneys through, hand-searching bags and purses, wanding alarms, confiscating or refusing prohibited items (knives, pepper spray, tools), resolving disputes with entrants, and detaining anyone found with a firearm until backup arrives.

Post duty inside a courtroom or at a grand jury room door: controlling who enters, verifying jurors/witnesses, keeping unauthorized people and recording devices out, escorting jurors and in-custody defendants, quieting or physically removing a disruptive spectator, and handcuffing a defendant remanded into custody.

Routine interior patrol rounds and roving presence inside the courthouse or other assigned building: walking floors, corridors, stairwells and clerk's offices during business hours and after hours, checking that doors and offices are secured, watching for unattended bags or loitering persons, logging the round and reporting anomalies.

Exterior patrol of the facility grounds: foot or vehicle rounds of the parking lot/garage, loading dock, prisoner sally port and building perimeter, checking vehicles and plates, watching for break-ins, trespassers or protest activity at entrances, and reporting what is found.

Responding to an incident in the assigned area: a hallway fight or shouting match between litigants, an agitated or emotionally disturbed person, a defendant fleeing after sentencing, or a weapon found; the officer moves in, gives commands, physically separates or restrains, handcuffs and arrests the violator, walks them to holding, and writes the report.

Patrol of a general assigned area outside a controlled facility: a downtown beat, public park, transit plaza, school zone or special-event perimeter, on foot or in a marked unit, making citizen contacts, moving people along, enforcing ordinances and making arrests as needed.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot autonomously runs scheduled and ad-hoc patrol routes inside corporate offices, financial services and manufacturing facilities, conducting security patrols and facility ... with onboard processing and escalation to remote human specialists; sold commercially as robot-as-a-service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior guard patrol rounds of a human-occupied institutional building. Transfers to courthouse interior rounds — same corridors, doors and badge points, same deliverable of presence, anomaly detection and a logged report — but it covers only the observe-and-report portion, not hands-on intervention.

sources.title: Two More Clients Renew Knightscope K5 Contracts
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 Autonomous Security Robot is deployed under paid contracts patrolling the public lobby of a New York senior living/healthcare and rehabilitation center to improve safety and the visitor experience.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guard patrol of a busy public-facing institutional lobby. Comparable to courthouse lobby/corridor presence patrol — crowded human-built interior, deterrence plus detection and reporting as the accepted output.

sources.title: University of Nevada, Reno signs contract for Knightscope K5
sources.claim: The University of Nevada, Reno subscribed to Knightscope's K5 ASR service for 24/7/365 autonomous patrols of the parking garage near the Student Center, in support of the University Police Department.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: police-supported patrol of an institution's parking structure. Same as courthouse lot/perimeter rounds — vehicle rows, plate reads, deterrence presence, alerting officers — on premises an institution controls.

sources.title: There’s a new sheriff in Times Square … and it's an NYPD robot
sources.claim: In the NYPD's Times Square subway pilot, the leased Knightscope K5 patrolled the station concourse overnight but was escorted by two police officers throughout its shift; the pilot ended in early 2024 and the machine was withdrawn.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (police patrol of an assigned public area), and shows the limit: the robot required accompanying sworn officers and performed no enforcement, so it cannot substitute for an officer's patrol where contacts and arrests are expected.

sources.title: Ascento rolls out latest autonomous security patrolling robot with new $4.3m funding round
sources.claim: Ascento Guard, a wheel-legged autonomous outdoor security robot, is deployed doing outdoor perimeter patrols at large industrial sites, warehouses and pharma campuses, sold by the hour like a human guard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor perimeter guard rounds on institution-controlled grounds. Comparable to courthouse grounds/parking patrol — mixed paving and curbs, weather, vehicles and occasional pedestrians, with detection and reporting as the output.

tasks.label: Transport or escort prisoners and defendants en route to courtrooms, prisons or jails, attorneys' offices, or medical facilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Street arrest to jail: officer searches the arrestee at the scene (sidewalk, roadside, residence doorstep), applies handcuffs, guides a possibly intoxicated or resistant person into the caged rear seat of a patrol car, seat-belts them, drives to the jail sally port, then walks them into booking and hands off custody with paperwork.

Scheduled jail-to-courthouse run: deputies restrain and shackle a group of inmates at the jail sally port, load them into a secure transport van, drive a fixed route, unload at the courthouse sally port, and walk them to holding cells, maintaining head counts and control throughout.

In-courthouse escort: officer moves a defendant from a holding cell through secure corridors to the courtroom, removes/adjusts restraints per judge's order, stands custody during the hearing, and returns the defendant to holding, reacting to outbursts or escape attempts.

Medical facility trip: officer transports a prisoner (injured, ill, or on psychiatric hold) to an emergency room or clinic, escorts them in restraints through public hospital areas, stays with them during examination and treatment, and returns them to custody.

Long-distance or special transport: extradition, transfer to a state prison, or a run to an attorney's or mental-health office, involving highway driving, fuel/meal/restroom stops in public places, ongoing monitoring, and handling of uncooperative or special-needs detainees.

sources.system: DEKA Sentry robot (Cobb County Adult Detention Center pilot)
sources.developer: DEKA Research and Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Ga. sheriff's office piloting robot patrol program at jail to enhance security
sources.claim: The most advanced robots deployed inside US correctional facilities patrol and observe; they conduct perimeter patrols and security rounds with cameras and two-way audio, and do not restrain, handcuff, move, or take custody of inmates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: jail security patrol in the same institutional setting. It does not transfer to prisoner transport/escort because the robot only surveils and communicates; it never applies restraints, physically guides a person, or maintains custody of a resisting detainee.

sources.title: Meet the nearly 6-foot tall robots patrolling a Ga. jail
sources.claim: Corrections patrol robots are surveillance platforms (cameras, night vision, heat detection, two-way audio) with no manipulators or means of physically controlling a person, and a live operator takes over for complex tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: jail interior patrol. Shows the frontier hardware in this environment lacks arms or restraint capability, so the physical custody and escort elements of prisoner transport are unsupported.

sources.title: Waymo reports 250,000 paid robotaxi rides per week in U.S.
sources.claim: Driverless vehicles carry human passengers autonomously at commercial scale on public roads, covering only the vehicle-driving portion of a prisoner transport; the vehicle has no ability to search, restrain, secure, monitor, or maintain custody of a prisoner, or to hand off custody at a booking desk.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously driving a passenger between two points. Transfer is only partial: the ride itself is automated, but the task's defining elements — searching and restraining a person, physically controlling a resisting or ill detainee, guarding, and formal custody transfer — are entirely outside the system's capability.

tasks.label: Photograph or draw diagrams of crime or accident scenes and interview principals and eyewitnesses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Minor injury/property-damage traffic collision on a public street: officer photographs vehicle damage, final rest positions, skid marks and debris with a handheld camera, sketches a field diagram of the roadway and impact points, and interviews both drivers and any bystander witnesses, obtaining names, accounts and contact information amid live traffic and weather.

Property crime call at a private home or small business (burglary, vandalism, vehicle break-in): officer photographs the point of entry, pry marks, broken glass, ransacked rooms and where items were taken, sometimes sketches a rough floor diagram, and interviews the victim/occupant and neighbors about timeline and suspects.

Violent crime or disturbance scene (assault, domestic violence, shots fired, robbery) indoors or in a yard/alley: officer photographs injuries, weapons, blood, damage and evidence in place, notes positions for a diagram, and separately interviews victim, suspect-adjacent parties and eyewitnesses, often uncooperative or emotional.

Serious-injury or fatal collision requiring measured scene mapping (total station, 3D scanner, or drone photogrammetry), evidence markers and a scaled diagram for reconstruction, plus formal recorded interviews of surviving drivers, passengers and eyewitnesses, with the roadway closed.

Outdoor scene documentation where there is no one to interview: single-vehicle crash into a fixed object with occupants already transported, a hit-and-run scene the parties have left, or a shots-fired location with casings in the street; officer produces overall photos and a scaled diagram of the roadway scene.

Documentation inside an institution-controlled facility: photographing a seized vehicle in the police impound lot, evidence or a victim's injuries at the station, or a scene inside a school/campus building, and taking a written or recorded statement from the complainant or witness present.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan for Documenting Evidence for Public Safety | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan is adaptive scanning software on Skydio drones that autonomously plans and executes the flight to capture a complete photoset ... a scene after the operator selects a scan volume and resolution; Skydio markets and demonstrates it for police crime and crash scene reconstruction (Boston PD crime scene unit tested it).

sources.title: How to use drones for crime and accident scene documentation | Police1
sources.claim: Independent law-enforcement trade press describes Skydio 3D Scan as automating the data-capture process for crime and accident scene documentation by police.

sources.title: SkyeBrowse Comprehensive Knowledge Base
sources.claim: SkyeBrowse flies a DJI/Autel drone on an autonomous orbit over a crash or crime scene after the user taps a center point, then produces a measurable 3D model, orthomosaic and automatically generated 2D sketch diagrams used as court evidence.

sources.title: SkyeBrowse Launches AI Quality Control For Crash Scene 3D Mapping | DroneXL
sources.claim: SkyeBrowse is in operational use by US law-enforcement agencies for crash-scene 3D mapping, with officers reviewing the resulting models at scenes and in courtrooms.

sources.system: Drone photogrammetry with Global Mapper Pro (Pixels to Points)
sources.developer: Blue Marble Geographics / Windham (ME) Police Department
sources.title: Drone Mapping Transforms Police Crash Investigations: A Blue Marble Geographics Case Study | DroneLife
sources.claim: A US police department (Windham, Maine) documents serious crash scenes with drone flights and photogrammetry, producing court-ready orthomosaics, 3D models and annotated diagrams; the workflow still requires officers to place surveyed ground control targets and to trace and annotate evidence in software.

sources.system: Leica BLK ARC on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Leica BLK ARC now the first certified reality capture device available for Boston Dynamics' Spot | Leica Geosystems
sources.claim: Leica BLK ARC mounted on Boston ... Spot performs autonomous laser scanning missions inside enclosed structures, plants and warehouses, with the scanning Autowalk executed without human intervention; Leica lists fire investigation among applications.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor reality capture of building interiors. It shows a legged robot can traverse and 3D-document an enclosed space, the closest analogue to indoor scene documentation, but it requires a taught route and produces no evidentiary close-up photography or witness statements.

tasks.label: Direct traffic flow and reroute traffic in case of emergencies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Traffic control at a crash / disabled-vehicle / medical scene on a city street or arterial: officer parks the patrol car as a blocker with lights, deploys flares or cones around the wreck, then stands in the lane waving vehicles past the obstruction, holding traffic for arriving fire/EMS and tow operators, and moving gawkers and pedestrians back. Debris, fluids, injured people, darkness and weather are common.

Manual control of a signalized intersection when the signal is dark (power failure, knocked-down mast arm) or during heavy congestion: officer stands in the middle of the intersection in a hi-vis vest with whistle and gloves/flashlight, cycles right-of-way by hand signal according to observed demand, breaks the cycle for emergency vehicles and buses, and waves pedestrians across.

Road closure and detour for a larger emergency - structure fire, hazmat spill, downed power lines, flooding, gas leak, or a crime-scene perimeter: officer sets barricades/cones/patrol car across the roadway at an arbitrary location, turns approaching vehicles around, explains the detour to drivers, admits or refuses residents by judgment, and holds the post for hours.

Planned-event and detail traffic direction on public streets: parades, ball games, school dismissal, funeral processions, construction details. Officer overrides or supplements the signals at a fixed post, meters platoons of vehicles out of a lot or venue, stops traffic for groups of pedestrians, and coordinates by radio with officers at adjacent posts.

Freeway/highway incident lane closure at speed: officer positions the cruiser with a taper of flares or cones ahead of a crash or debris field, merges high-speed traffic out of the blocked lane, sometimes runs a rolling roadblock to slow or stop the flow, amid high noise, wind and passing-truck hazard.

sources.developer: Hangzhou Traffic Police Tactical Unit (with Chinese robotics partners)
sources.title: Hangzhou's AI Robot Police Officer Directs City Traffic
sources.claim: A named humanoid traffic robot stands a post at a busy public intersection in Hangzhou and performs standard stop/go traffic-direction motions to oncoming vehicles, with cameras, sensors and a whistle, integrated with the intersection's signal controller; it is an adjunct to human officers, not a replacement.

sources.system: Hangzhou robot traffic-management squadron / Kashgar traffic robot
sources.developer: Hangzhou Traffic Police; Kashgar traffic police
sources.title: China's robot police patrol cities during Labor Day holiday, signaling AI-powered urban governance-Xinhua
sources.claim: Chinese cities have put traffic-management robots on duty at public intersections; a robot in Kashgar has been directing traffic at a major intersection, while Hangzhou's 15-robot squad is scoped to managing non-motorized and pedestrian traffic, giving directions and assisting human officers, with its signals synchronized to the traffic lights.

sources.developer: Women's Technology / Therese Izay Kirongozi, Kinshasa Institute of Applied Techniques
sources.title: This Giant Robot Directs Traffic In The Congo - Fast Company
sources.claim: Permanently installed humanoid traffic robots regulate vehicle flow at busy Kinshasa intersections from a fixed post, using revolving traffic-light arms and cameras in place of a police officer or signal.

sources.title: Therese Kirongozi / Traffic robots in Kinshasa - Wikipedia
sources.claim: The Kinshasa robots physically imitate an officer's traffic-direction gestures from a fixed installation - rotating the torso and raising arms to stop one direction and release another - and some detect pedestrians and voice crossing instructions.

sources.title: Kratos Defense Self-Driving Trucks are on the Road Across the United States
sources.claim: The only self-driving vehicle in routine US roadway work-zone protection service is a truck-mounted attenuator that drives itself as the follower in a leader-follower platoon behind a human-driven lead truck; it shields a work area but does not assess a scene, place devices, or signal drivers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: protecting and channelling live traffic around a blocked lane on a highway - the same environment and traffic-control purpose as an officer's incident lane closure. It bounds capability: the machine only shields, and requires a human-driven lead vehicle.

sources.system: Automated Flagger Assistance Devices (AFADs, e.g. Wanco)
sources.title: Transforming Work Zone Safety Through Automation | AWP Safety
sources.claim: The commercially standard machine substitute for a person signalling stop/slow to live traffic in a US lane closure, the Automated Flagger Assistance Device, is operated remotely by a worker rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: flagging - the stop/slow signalling function an officer performs when holding and releasing traffic past an incident. It shows the deployed device is remotely driven by a human, so it cannot support an autonomous judgment.

sources.system: AEM Apex Flood Warning Station (with warning gates)
sources.title: Apex Flood Station | Advanced Flood Warning Station | AEM
sources.claim: Automated flood road-closure stations that lower gates and light beacons at known flood-prone crossings are triggered or overridden remotely by emergency managers rather than deciding and executing closures on their own, and exist only at pre-instrumented fixed sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closing a road and turning traffic back during an emergency (flooding) - the same rerouting purpose as an officer's barricade post. It is remotely commanded and site-fixed, so it cannot support an autonomous judgment.
