tasks.label: Process prisoners, and prepare and maintain records of prisoner bookings and prisoner status during booking and pre-trial process.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine booking of a cooperative adult arrestee at a municipal police station or county jail intake: escort from the transport car through the sallyport, remove handcuffs, conduct a search of the person, remove and inventory personal property into a bag with a signed receipt, roll fingerprints on a Live Scan device, take front/side booking photographs, take biographic data, and complete the booking sheet in the jail management system.

Booking an intoxicated, mentally ill, injured, or actively resisting arrestee: maintaining physical control, placing the person in a restraint chair or padded/sobering cell, arranging medical screening, delaying or repeating prints and photos once the person is compliant, and documenting force/refusal/medical clearance in the booking record.

DUI/chemical-test processing in a station breath-test room: 20-minute observation period, implied-consent advisement, administering the breath instrument and printing/attaching results, or escorting the arrestee to a hospital for a blood draw, then completing the booking and evidence paperwork.

Records preparation and maintenance at a station desk: writing the arrest report and probable-cause affidavit, entering charges and booking data into the RMS/JMS, scanning and attaching documents, transmitting the charging packet to the prosecutor and court, and updating prisoner status (bond, holds, court dates, transfers, release) through the pre-trial period.

Pre-arraignment custody care and movement inside the holding facility: periodic cell checks and welfare logs, meals and phone calls, escorting the prisoner to interview rooms, lineups, medical, or court holding, and transferring custody to jail deputies with the accompanying paperwork.

Processing away from the booking room: citation-in-lieu-of-custody at the roadside with a mobile fingerprint ID device and e-citation printer, or guarding an arrestee in a hospital emergency department and completing booking paperwork bedside, then transporting the prisoner over public roads to the jail.

sources.system: DEKA Sentry security robot (Cobb County Adult Detention Center pilot)
sources.developer: DEKA Research & Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Ga. sheriff's office piloting robot patrol program at jail to enhance security
sources.claim: The most advanced robots actually deployed inside US detention facilities are wheeled security-patrol platforms that provide cameras, night vision and two-way ... for perimeter patrols and dormitory rounds; complex tasks are handled by a live human operator. They perform no prisoner processing, searching, fingerprinting, or record-keeping.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic deployment to the task's setting (jail intake/holding area). Cited to establish that the robot capability actually present in these facilities is surveillance patrol, not the physical handling of prisoners or booking records required here.

sources.title: Ohio Police Fire Robocop for Helping Make Zero Arrests and Failing to Issue a Single Ticket
sources.claim: A limbless autonomous security robot placed in police service by a US police department produced no enforcement outputs over roughly a year and was returned; it cannot physically handle people or paperwork.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous policing duties in a controlled facility (parking structure). Cited to show that police-deployed autonomous robots today lack manipulators and perform observation only, so they cannot search, restrain, print, or book an arrestee.

sources.title: US: BMW deploys Figure 03 humanoid at smart factory for logistics
sources.claim: The frontier of autonomous humanoid manipulation in industry as of mid-2026 is sorting rigid factory components into trolleys inside a purpose-built plant logistics flow — not contact with people or handling of arrestee property and biometrics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous humanoid manipulation of objects in a structured facility. Cited to bound the state of the art: even in fixtured industrial settings the objects are rigid known parts, far from searching a person, rolling fingerprints, or restraining a combative arrestee.

sources.title: GXO Signs Industry-First Multi-Year Agreement with Agility Robotics
sources.claim: Commercially contracted humanoid work in structured human facilities is limited to repetitive tote movement between cobots and conveyors under a cloud orchestration layer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation in a structured human work facility (E2). Cited to show the deployed envelope is standardized totes in engineered flows, which does not transfer to person-search, biometric capture, or custody escort of a human prisoner.

tasks.label: Locate and confiscate real or personal property, as directed by court order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Writ of possession / eviction lockout: deputy arrives at a rented house or apartment at the scheduled time, knocks and announces, verifies the writ, orders occupants out, sweeps rooms for people, pets and hazards, stands by while a moving crew sets belongings at the curb and a locksmith rekeys, then delivers possession of the real property to the landlord. Occupants may be absent, refusing, or hostile; layout and clutter differ at every address.

Court-ordered firearms/weapons surrender or seizure at a private residence (domestic-violence protective order, red-flag/ERPO order): contact the respondent at the door, demand all firearms, ammunition and permits listed in the order, look through closets, safes, vehicles and outbuildings where authorized, clear and make each weapon safe, match serial numbers to the order, inventory and transport to the property room.

Seizure of a vehicle under a levy, replevin, or forfeiture order: locate the specific car, truck or trailer by plate and VIN at a driveway, curb, employer lot, or storage lot; verify it against the writ; take the keys or hook it to a tow truck; inventory loose contents; document the seizure and see it delivered to the impound/storage yard while handling the owner's protests.

Civil standby or levy on household goods at a residence: accompany one party into a home to retrieve the specific items a court order lists (clothing, tools, documents, a pet, a child's belongings), or catalog and seize non-exempt household property (electronics, tools, jewelry, furniture) under a writ of execution; decide what is and is not on the list, refuse contested items, and keep the peace between the parties.

Levy or replevin at a business: serve the writ on the manager at a store, shop, restaurant or warehouse, walk the premises, identify and tag non-exempt inventory, machinery, tills and cash on hand, or the one specific piece of equipment named in the order; inventory it, and either load it for removal to a storage facility or leave it under a keeper.

Take custody of property held by an institutional third party under court order: a self-storage unit, a bank safe-deposit box, a tow yard, a hospital patient-property room or a commercial warehouse custodian; verify authority with the custodian, cut a lock if authorized, inventory contents, and remove the property to court-designated storage.

sources.title: Improving the accuracy of "Stan", a fully autonomous parking and valet robot — Trimble case study
sources.claim: Stanley Robotics' 'Stan' is a fully autonomous outdoor robot that detects a vehicle handed over in a purpose-built drop-off cabin, lifts it by the wheels and moves ... into a secure, human-free storage area; commercially operational at Lyon Saint-Exupery and other airports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic valet parking. Transfers to the physical core of a court-ordered vehicle seizure at E1 — a vehicle presented in a purpose-built bay is identified against a booking record, lifted without keys, and relocated into a secured storage area, the same object class, precision and outcome (custody in an impound lot) as an impound under a levy.

sources.title: Introducing Stan: the robot valet parking cars at Lyon Airport — Airport Technology
sources.claim: Stan autonomously detects a vehicle, slides ... in a dedicated area of the airport car park; passengers drop the car at a kiosk-equipped bay and leave.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: autonomous key-free vehicle pickup and removal to a secured lot is the physical act of impounding a levied vehicle once the vehicle is presented to the machine in a purpose-built bay.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm uses computer vision and AI ... a specified item among mixed inventory presented in containers and place it into a designated tote, operating in caged workcells in fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: goods-to-robot item picking. Transfers to an E1 counterfactual seizure of specified goods: when the property is presented to the machine in containers, identifying the correct listed item and transferring it into a custody container is the same perception-and-handling problem with comparable object variety and precision.

sources.title: Police 'Robot Dogs' Raise Concerns as More Departments Adopt Them — Governing
sources.claim: Police use of legged and tracked robots (Spot, PackBot) in the field is operator-driven: the robot is guided by an officer with a tablet over a live video feed and relies on human operators for decision-making; it is used for standoff reconnaissance, not for taking custody of property.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's NEO humanoid — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Humanoid robots intended for homes, including 1X's NEO, are not able to complete household tasks autonomously start-to-finish; demonstrations are scripted or teleoperated, and homes are cluttered and vary household to household.

tasks.label: Serve statements of claims, subpoenas, summonses, jury summonses, orders to pay alimony, and other court orders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Civil process (summons and complaint, subpoena, family-court order) served at a single-family private residence in a suburban or rural area: deputy drives to the address, walks past gates/dogs/steps, knocks, asks for the named party, confirms identity, hands over the papers or substitute-serves a co-resident of suitable age, notes time and physical description, and files a sworn return of service.

Service at a multi-unit apartment or condominium: locked lobby, buzzer/callbox, stairwells and corridors, wrong or unmarked unit numbers, neighbors answering, frequent no-answer requiring re-attempt at a different hour.

Service at a workplace or business premises: entering a commercial lobby or store, asking reception, identifying the employee, registered agent, or manager legally authorized to accept (e.g., wage garnishment on an employer), handing over papers and completing the return.

Routine service at institution-controlled sites where the recipient's location is known and the encounter is cooperative: an inmate in the county jail, a party or records custodian at the courthouse, a patient at a hospital, staff at a school or agency office.

Posting or leaving process at the premises: taping/affixing an eviction notice, writ of possession, or 'nail-and-mail' notice conspicuously on the entry door of an occupied or vacant dwelling, photographing it, and documenting the attempt.

Hard-to-serve, evasive or hostile recipients: repeated attempts at early/late hours, stakeouts and surveillance, matching a person to a photo/description who denies their name, service of protective orders, contempt and alimony orders, and eviction lockouts where confrontation or resistance is likely.

sources.title: Starship passes 10 million deliveries as autonomous delivery moves toward mainstream adoption
sources.claim: Starship's sidewalk delivery robots operate at Level 4 autonomy with only remote standby assistance and have completed over 10 million ... on campuses and in neighborhoods, i.e., autonomous outdoor delivery of items to consenting, app-authenticated recipients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: last-mile parcel/food delivery. Shows autonomous travel to an address and release of a small item, but only to a customer who ordered and unlocks the lid; it does not locate or identify an unwilling named person.

sources.title: Veriff Collabs With Starship to Drive ID Verification for Autonomous Robot Delivery
sources.claim: Starship robots use an AI identity-verification service to authenticate recipients of age-restricted goods before release, though some checks are handled by remote human agents over video.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: age-restricted delivery. Identity checking before handing over goods is the analogue of confirming the named party before handing over process, but human video checks mean autonomy is not established.

sources.title: Serve Robotics Autonomous Sidewalk Delivery | NVIDIA case study
sources.claim: Serve Robotics' third-generation robots have completed over 100,000 autonomous deliveries in Los Angeles, Miami, Dallas, Atlanta ... with a 99.8% completion rate, including deliveries to customers' doors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: urban last-mile delivery. Demonstrates autonomous navigation of public sidewalks to residential addresses, but hand-off is to a cooperating customer via app, with no identity determination of a resistant party.

sources.system: RIVR / RIVR TWO doorstep delivery robot
sources.title: RIVR and Veho launch robot-powered parcel delivery
sources.claim: RIVR's wheeled-legged robots deliver parcels autonomously from the van to the front door in residential neighborhoods, handling stairs, gates and uneven terrain, in commercial pilots in Austin (Veho, 2025) and Zurich (Just Eat); Amazon acquired the company in 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: doorstep parcel delivery at private homes. Shows a robot can reach the actual entry door of a dwelling, but not knock-and-identify a named person, affix a notice, or judge substituted service.

sources.title: Singapore Hotel Jen properties install Relay autonomous robots
sources.claim: Relay delivery robots autonomously ride elevators and navigate corridors to a designated guest room, telephone the room, and open their compartment when the occupant opens the door, handing the item to the person at the door.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility item delivery to a person at a known room. Transfers to handing court papers to a cooperative recipient whose location within a controlled facility is known.

sources.title: BayCare Expands Autonomous Hospital Delivery with New Relay Robots at Winter Haven Hospitals
sources.claim: Relay robots are deployed across hotels, hospitals and commercial real estate with more than one million deliveries completed; BayCare expanded autonomous hospital delivery with new Relay robots in 2026 after a pilot with a 99.8% delivery success rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivery inside human work facilities. Establishes reliability and scale of autonomous item transport and hand-off inside institution-controlled buildings.

sources.system: Zena RX / TUG autonomous mobile robot
sources.title: ST Engineering Aethon Launches ZenaRx: Redefining Secure Delivery of Medications, Specimens and Sensitive Goods in Hospitals
sources.claim: Aethon's autonomous hospital robots carry items in locked compartments that only an authorized recipient can open using PIN codes and biometric (fingerprint) authentication, producing a logged, authenticated hand-off of a specific item to a specific person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: secure custody-chain delivery. The core physical act of releasing a document only to an authenticated, identified recipient and logging it is the machine analogue of handing papers to a verified party once that party is presented.

sources.title: Robotic Label Applicator | Signode
sources.claim: Robotic print-and-apply labelers autonomously take a printed document/label from a printer and apply it to a presented workpiece at a determined position on a production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated print-and-apply labeling. Affixing a printed sheet conspicuously to a presented surface is the same manipulation as posting a notice when the door/surface is fixtured and presented to the machine.

tasks.label: Detain persons found to be in violation of customs or immigration laws and arrange for legal action, such as deportation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Airport port of entry, federal inspection area: a traveler referred to secondary is found inadmissible or holding fraudulent documents. The officer takes the person into custody, conducts a pat-down/personal search, applies handcuffs when warranted, escorts them to a secure holding room, takes biometrics and property inventory, takes a sworn statement, and prepares expedited-removal or ICE-referral paperwork and return-flight arrangements.

Land border port of entry, vehicle and pedestrian lanes: a driver or passenger is found with concealed narcotics or an immigration violation at secondary. The officer orders the subject out of the vehicle in the outdoor inspection lot, controls and restrains them, walks them to the port security office/holding cell, processes them, and refers the case for prosecution or removal.

Uncooperative subject: a person attempts to flee the inspection area, physically resists handcuffing, or is intoxicated/medically distressed and combative. Officers use empty-hand control techniques, a takedown, and multi-officer restraint, then secure, search, and process the subject amid bystanders in the terminal or crossing.

Seaport or marine/air cargo environment: a stowaway or foreign crewmember found in violation aboard a vessel or in a marine terminal. The officer detains the person aboard or at the pier, escorts them down a gangway and across terminal apron, transports them to the port office, and arranges detention aboard the vessel, ICE transfer, or removal.

Custody maintenance and transfer: guarding detainees in a port holding facility (welfare checks, meals, cell and body searches), then moving a restrained detainee by government vehicle to a detention facility, or escorting a removable person through the terminal and onto a departing aircraft, and completing the custody transfer to ICE with the associated documentation.

sources.title: Security Robots 2026: Autonomous Patrol & Surveillance Systems Guide | Robotomated
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5, the most widely deployed autonomous security robot in the US, is an observation and deterrence ... that cannot physically intervene in incidents; humans handle confrontation and physical security action such as detaining a person.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: security-guard response to a detected violator. It transfers because detaining a person also requires physical control of a human body; the cited system's own documentation states it cannot perform physical intervention.

sources.system: Commercial autonomous security robots (patrol robots and security drones, 2026 market survey)
sources.title: Security Guards vs. Robots vs. Drones: 2026 Cost and Performance Comparison
sources.claim: As of 2026, the class of commercially fielded security robots does not physically intervene in incidents at all; their role is detection, documentation and alerting for human response.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is guard response/apprehension in controlled facilities; it bounds this task because taking a violator into custody is a strictly harder physical intervention on a possibly resisting human.

sources.title: Can robots help keep us safe? | National Geographic
sources.claim: Knightscope's fielded robots, deployed in corporate campuses, malls and parking structures, are explicitly not designed to police people or apprehend suspects.
sources.transferJustification: Apprehension of a suspect is the direct analogue of detaining a violator at a port of entry; the developer states the deployed system does not do it.

sources.title: RAD Announces HERO, the Humanoid Security Robot – The Monitoring Association
sources.claim: Even the humanoid security robot announced for security duty is scoped to presence, verbal warnings, access control and escalation to human responders — not to seizing, restraining, or holding a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is humanoid security officer duty; the announced capability set excludes any physical custody function, so it cannot substantiate detention even in a purpose-built setting.

sources.system: Property security robot fleet with remote human monitoring
sources.developer: Third-party security robot operator (Atlanta apartment complex deployment)
sources.title: Robot security helps catch break-in suspect at Atlanta apartments – WSB-TV
sources.claim: In a 2026 incident where security robots were credited with helping catch a break-in suspect, the robots provided remote camera coverage monitored by human personnel while police officers performed the detention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is apprehension of a suspect; the report shows the robot's contribution is human-monitored surveillance while sworn officers make the physical detention, so it cannot support robotic completion.

tasks.label: Inspect cargo, baggage, and personal articles entering or leaving U.S. for compliance with revenue laws and U.S. customs regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: International airport federal inspection area: traveler referred to baggage secondary. Officer places checked/carry-on bags on an exam bench, opens zippers and locks, hand-searches clothing, toiletries, souvenirs, food and medicines, feels linings and hard-sided panels for concealment, compares findings to the traveler's oral and written declaration, assesses duty on goods above the personal exemption, seizes prohibited agricultural or counterfeit items and currency over the reporting limit, then repacks the bags and releases or refers the traveler.

Land port of entry, passenger vehicle secondary lot: officer inspects a POV and its contents after an NII scan or canine alert - opens trunk, hood, glove box, spare-tire well and aftermarket compartments, unloads and opens suitcases, boxes, grocery bags and coolers, checks for undeclared merchandise, produce, meat, alcohol and tobacco quantities, and documents/seizes any violations before releasing the vehicle.

Seaport or land-border cargo examination (dockside tailgate exam or Centralized Examination Station): officer breaks the seal, opens container doors, has the load devanned, opens cartons and pallets, verifies commodity description, quantity, weight and country-of-origin marking against the manifest and entry documents, takes samples for the lab, probes for contraband and false walls, then reseals the container and records the exam result.

International mail branch or express consignment carrier facility: officer works a high-volume parcel belt, X-rays parcels, pulls selected packages, opens them, compares contents to the CN22/commercial invoice for value and description, assesses duty or refers for formal entry, seizes narcotics, counterfeits or restricted goods, and re-tapes and returns cleared parcels to the stream.

Other and outbound operations: outbound baggage and cargo exams at a jetway or air cargo dock (bulk currency, export-controlled goods), cruise terminal baggage exams, rail car and small-boat/general-aviation arrivals where the officer boards, opens lockers, holds and stowage areas and inspects personal articles and stores under variable weather and layout.

sources.system: CBP large-scale NII systems (drive-through X-ray portals, Multi-Energy Portal, Low Energy Portal)
sources.developer: U.S. Customs and Border Protection / Rapiscan, Leidos, Viken vendors
sources.title: U.S. GAO - Land Port Inspections: CBP Should Improve Performance Data and Deployment Plans for Scanning Systems
sources.claim: Large-scale non-intrusive inspection systems at land ports scan whole vehicles, but the resulting images are reviewed by CBP officers, and anomalies are resolved by officers physically searching the conveyance - the automated element is imaging, not examination.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: vehicle/cargo inspection at ports of entry. Shows the deployed automation covers imaging only; the compliance determination and any physical search remain with officers.

sources.system: CT X-ray with automated recognition technology for express consignment and mail parcel screening
sources.developer: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (vendor CT systems)
sources.title: United States Customs and Border Protection – AI Use Cases | Homeland Security
sources.claim: CBP's deployed automated parcel screening uses CT X-ray with automated recognition on inline conveyors, but the output is a highlighted anomaly image passed to CBP personnel for further inspection - no machine opens parcels or verifies contents against declarations.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: parcel inspection at mail and express consignment facilities. Establishes that the automated component stops at anomaly flagging, short of opening, verifying and assessing duty.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: Autonomous robots can unload floor-loaded boxes from shipping containers in logistics facilities at commercial scale, i.e. the devanning sub-step of a cargo exam, but they do not open cartons, verify commodity description or country-of-origin marking, sample, or judge compliance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: container devanning, a physical sub-step of a CBP intensive cargo exam. It transfers only for moving cases in a warehouse; it supplies none of the verification, sampling or contraband-search content of the exam.

sources.title: DHS Looking to Use Robotics in Airport Security Lines – MeriTalk
sources.claim: Robotic opening and searching of alarmed bags remains a research concept solicited by DHS S&T rather than a fielded capability; no deployed system opens and hand-searches passenger baggage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical bag opening and search for alarm resolution. It is a solicitation/concept, so it cannot substantiate completion; it documents the absence of a deployed baggage-search robot.

sources.title: Nuctech™ VR1000 Smart Robots – Chassis Inspection Robot
sources.claim: Customs-branded inspection robots in service abroad are imaging aids - a mobile under-chassis imaging platform operated by an officer - not autonomous examiners of goods.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vehicle inspection at border checkpoints. Operator-driven imaging of a chassis does not carry over to opening compartments, examining goods, or making an admissibility/duty determination.

sources.system: Yangshan Phase IV automated terminal AGVs feeding H986 NII equipment ('Customs Smart Inspection')
sources.title: Customs Smart Inspections in the Automated Terminal, Shanghai Customs District (WCO PTC paper)
sources.claim: In China's most automated container terminal, AGVs autonomously deliver customs-selected containers to fixed NII equipment for scanning; the customs inspection decision still rests on the scan and officer review, and unpacking inspection remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: moving cargo to inspection at a port. Automated conveyance plus scanning covers presentation and imaging, not the physical examination, verification and sampling that constitute the exam.

tasks.label: Locate and seize contraband, undeclared merchandise, and vehicles, aircraft, or boats that contain such merchandise.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land border port-of-entry secondary inspection: a passenger vehicle referred from primary is scanned by NII, sniffed by K-9, then physically searched — officers probe/drill gas tanks, pull door panels, quarter panels and spare tires, extract concealed bundles, field-test the substance, weigh and photograph it, take custody of the drugs, and seize the vehicle itself (driving it to the secure lot) with full chain-of-custody documentation.

Airport passenger processing: a traveler referred to customs secondary; officer opens and hand-searches checked and carry-on baggage and personal effects, identifies undeclared or prohibited goods (currency over $10k, agricultural products, counterfeit luxury items, narcotics in false-bottom bags or body-carried), removes the items, and executes seizure with receipts and documentation.

International mail branch / express consignment hub: high-volume small parcels move on conveyors past X-ray and K-9; officer pulls flagged parcels, opens them, identifies fentanyl/pill presses/counterfeit goods/undeclared merchandise inside varied packaging and concealment (books, toys, sealed bags), field-tests suspected narcotics, and seizes and vaults the item with a written record.

Sea/land cargo exam at a container examination station or seaport: an intensive exam of a container or commercial truck — breaking the seal, devanning pallets and cartons, opening and sampling merchandise, comparing goods to the manifest for undeclared, misdescribed, counterfeit or IPR-violating goods, and seizing the merchandise (and sometimes the conveyance).

Field/marine and general aviation searches: boarding a small vessel at a marina or anchorage, or searching a private aircraft on a general-aviation ramp, a rail car, or a bus — confined spaces, hidden compartments, weather and uneven footing — locating contraband, removing it, and seizing the boat, aircraft or vehicle that carried it.

sources.system: Unitree quadruped customs inspection robot (Ningbo-Zhoushan, Meishan Port Area)
sources.title: Robot dog patrols container stacks at the world's busiest port
sources.claim: A Unitree quadruped robot deployed by Chinese customs at Ningbo-Zhoushan Port autonomously navigates a container yard, reads container/seal numbers and enters empty containers looking for foreign objects — inspection only, with no manipulation, removal or seizure of goods.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing robotic system doing customs container inspection; it substantiates autonomous detection/inspection in a port yard but explicitly not the locate-inside-concealment, extraction, field-testing or seizure steps of this task.

sources.title: DHL buying 1,000+ Stretch robots from Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch performs autonomous case unloading (devanning) of trailers and containers in commercial logistics deployments, showing robots can empty a container of cartons but not examine merchandise against a manifest or seize violative goods.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: container devanning, a sub-step of an intensive CBP cargo exam. Comparable objects (cartons) and an institutional facility, but Stretch only moves sealed cases; it does not open, inspect for undeclared/counterfeit contents, or take custody.

sources.system: iBonnie Porter100 autonomous luggage handling robot
sources.title: NUCTECH | Top Robotics Solutions Company in APAC-2023
sources.claim: Nuctech markets an autonomous baggage-handling robot that removes flagged bags from a screening conveyor and takes them to a human inspection station for secondary screening — the physical search and any seizure remain with officers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routing screened baggage in a security checkpoint. It shows robotic transport of flagged bags in a structured facility, but the opening of bags, identification of undeclared merchandise and seizure are still done by human screeners.

sources.title: iCMORE | Smiths Detection
sources.claim: AI object-recognition software (iCMORE) automatically flags contraband in X-ray images of baggage, cargo, vehicles and containers; it is a detection algorithm on scanning equipment, providing no physical manipulation, extraction or custody of the goods.
sources.transferJustification: Addresses only the 'locate' sub-step and is software on an imaging machine, not an embodied system acting on the physical world; it cannot support a positive judgment for seizure.

sources.system: CBP large-scale NII with Anomaly Detection Algorithms
sources.title: Non-Intrusive Inspection Equipment to Counter Illicit Drug Flows (CRS Insight IN12601)
sources.claim: At US ports of entry, non-intrusive inspection imaging is still reviewed by people, with AI anomaly-detection only being trained toward operational readiness; physical search and seizure of concealed drugs remain officer work.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the current state of automation in this exact task: even the image-review step is human-in-the-loop, and no fielded system performs the extraction or seizure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Collect samples of merchandise for examination, appraisal, or testing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cargo examination at a seaport/airport Centralized Examination Station or warehouse: officer breaks down a flagged shipment, opens selected cartons, and removes a representative discrete unit of merchandise (a garment, shoe, hand tool, electronic device, packaged food item, piece of produce) for the CBP laboratory or for appraisal; sample is bagged, sealed, tagged and documented. Cluttered warehouse floor, pallets, forklifts, importer's packaging.

Cargo sample that must be cut or severed from bulk stock rather than picked as a unit: a swatch from a bolt/roll of fabric, a length of wire, tubing or steel from a coil, a slice of lumber or wood packing material, a section of a composite article, taken in situ in the exam warehouse and packaged for the lab.

Bulk liquid or dry commodity sampling at a terminal, land-border crossing or vessel berth: drawing representative samples of petroleum, chemicals, juice, honey, or grain from tank trucks, rail tank cars, drums, or bulk holds into approved sealed bottles/containers for laboratory analysis and duty classification.

Suspected narcotic or unknown substance that is already accessible (a taped brick, a bag of powder, loose pills, a bottle of liquid found in luggage, cargo, or a parcel): officer removes a small aliquot, runs a field identification test, and retains a sealed sample for the laboratory, in a secondary inspection room or exam bay.

Suspected contraband concealed within vehicle components, structural voids, machinery, or impregnated into goods: officer must locate the concealment, drill or dismantle to reach the material, extract a sample and test it, at a land-border secondary inspection dock or exam bay with a non-standard, modified conveyance.

International mail or express consignment facility: officer pulls a flagged parcel or envelope off the belt or from a bin, opens the heterogeneous packaging (padded envelope, poly bag, carton), extracts a sample of the contents (pills, powder, counterfeit goods, unlabeled product), then repackages, seals and forwards it for testing.

sources.system: Robotica ABOT M1 / ePack automated decant (FANUC robots)
sources.title: Warehouse Replenishment Automation for Fulfillment Centers | FANUC America
sources.claim: Robotica's ABOT automated box-opening/decant systems, built on FANUC robots, autonomously learn box dimensions and cutting parameters and open a wide range of shipping cartons without damaging the inner packs, then transfer contents into totes in production warehouse cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening shipping cartons and removing inner packs for decanting. It is the same access step CBP sampling requires — cutting open an importer's carton without destroying the goods and extracting units — on identical objects (mixed commercial cartons) at comparable precision.

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and handles individual products drawn from a huge, unstructured product mix inside fulfillment centers, moving single items between containers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item picking of arbitrary retail merchandise from a bin. Collecting a merchandise sample is the same physical act — identify and remove one representative unit of unfamiliar goods and place it in a designated container — on the same class of objects.

sources.system: GSI Automatic Grain Samplers (in-line / gravity chute spot sampler)
sources.title: Automatic Grain Samplers | GSI
sources.claim: GSI in-line and gravity-chute automatic samplers mechanically insert a sample tube into a moving product stream on an adjustable automatic schedule and deliver the extracted increment into a sealed container at grain handling facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on bulk commodities: extracting a representative increment of a dry commodity from a load and delivering it sealed for grading/testing, which is what CBP does when sampling bulk grain or granular imports.

sources.system: Automatic probe / cell in-line liquid sampling systems (API 8.2)
sources.title: AUTOMATIC SAMPLING API 8.2, ISO-3171 and ASTM D.4177 Sampling — Mechatest
sources.claim: Automatic in-line/probe sampling systems built to API MPMS 8.2, ASTM D4177 and ISO 3171 extract representative liquid samples from a pipeline or transfer line under PLC control and collect them in sealed sample receivers for laboratory quality analysis used in commercial and fiscal transactions.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on bulk liquids: representative sample extraction from a custody-transfer batch into a sealed receiver for laboratory determination of quality — the identical purpose (appraisal/duty and testing) CBP sampling of tankers serves.

sources.title: Alsys Lab Robots | Metrohm
sources.claim: Alsys/Metrohm laboratory robots fully automate sample preparation — decapping containers, weighing, diluting, transferring — and feed the prepared samples directly to analytical instruments, running unattended for days.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: taking an aliquot from a supplied container and submitting it to an identification instrument. That is the sampling-plus-field-test sequence an officer performs on a seized substance, on comparable powders/liquids and at higher precision.

sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory / UC Berkeley (with Google DeepMind)
sources.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of inorganic materials | Nature
sources.claim: The A-Lab operated autonomously for 17 days with robotic arms dosing and handling inorganic powders, transferring them between containers and instruments, and running automated X-ray diffraction characterization to identify the resulting solids.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic weighing, transfer and instrumental identification of unknown powders — the same manipulation and analysis chain as taking a powder sample and field-testing/submitting it for laboratory identification.

sources.system: SlitMaster automatic bag slitting machines (and equivalent automatic sack openers)
sources.developer: Indpro (and comparable vendors, e.g., Palamatic Minislit)
sources.title: Automatic Bag Slitting Machines | SlitMaster Series by Indpro
sources.claim: Automatic bag slitting/emptying machines cut open 10–50 kg paper, plastic, laminated, jute and woven-PP sacks and discharge their powder or granular contents into downstream equipment without manual ... or intervention, and are widely deployed in bulk-solids plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine opening of sealed sacks of powder to access the contents. This is the access step for sampling a wrapped package of bulk powder, on comparable packaging materials and contents.

sources.title: Robotic apple packing duo debuts at Interpoma | Fruitnet
sources.claim: The Aporo produce packer robotically picks and places individual loose fruit into trays on commercial packhouse lines, with the installed base having handled over a billion fruits.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of individual fresh produce items into designated trays — the same delicate grasp-and-place act as pulling representative fruit units out of an import carton into a sample container.

sources.title: OPEX Model 72 | Automated Envelope Opening Systems
sources.claim: The OPEX Model 72 automatically feeds mixed mail and mills envelopes open at up to 3,600 pieces per ... without damaging contents, then presents the opened pieces so the contents can be removed and sorted into bins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated opening of heterogeneous mail pieces without damaging contents — the access step for sampling flagged mail; note content removal here is still done by an operator, so it supports only the opening step.

sources.title: Sellafield trials robot swabbing tech | Nuclear Engineering International
sources.claim: Sellafield trialled Boston Dynamics' Spot with a swabbing tool to take contamination samples in hazardous decommissioning areas; partner RAICo demonstrated the platform under remote control rather than autonomous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Closest evidence of a mobile robot collecting samples inside a human-run facility (E2), but the demonstrations are remotely operated trials, so they cannot support a positive E2 judgment.

tasks.label: Monitor transit areas and conduct security checks to protect railroad properties, patrons, and employees.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-visibility foot patrol of a busy passenger station/terminal during service hours (subway, commuter rail, light rail): walking concourses, mezzanines, platforms, stairs and escalators amid crowds; observing riders, checking fare-gate areas, unattended bags, people in distress or acting out, and making contact with patrons and suspects.

Property checks of railroad-controlled land: rail yards, intermodal terminals, shops, bridges and right-of-way. Driving/walking the yard mostly at night, sweeping for trespassers, cargo-theft cutters, vandalism, checking fence lines, gates, container/railcar seals, thermal/low-light conditions, uneven ballast.

Onboard patrol of in-service trains and buses: boarding, riding, walking through moving cars end to end, scanning riders and vestibules, checking for hazards, disorder, unattended property, and disembarking at problem stops.

Watch-desk / control-center monitoring of transit areas: continuous surveillance of station, platform, yard and parking-facility camera feeds, spotting intrusions, trespass on tracks, loitering, fights or unattended objects, and passing detections to field units.

Rounds of peripheral agency facilities: park-and-ride lots and parking garages, station perimeters, maintenance shops, unstaffed suburban stations, elevators, restrooms and back-of-house corridors; overnight lock-up and closing sweeps, checking doors, gates and lighting.

Fixed-post and checkpoint security checks: random bag inspection tables at station entrances, employee credential checks at yard/shop gates, and screening/entry control for special events and high-alert periods, involving inspecting bags and interacting with each person screened.

sources.system: Knightscope K5 Autonomous Security Robot (NYPD Transit pilot)
sources.title: There's a new sheriff in Times Square … and it's an NYPD robot - Gothamist
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot was placed on overnight patrol in the Times Square subway ... but had to be escorted by two officers, could not use stairs, and the pilot was ended and the robot put into storage.

tasks.label: Apprehend or remove trespassers or thieves from railroad property or coordinate with law enforcement agencies in apprehensions and removals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pedestrian trespassers on the mainline right-of-way, bridges or tunnels outside any facility: the special agent responds to a report or spots people walking the ballast, makes contact on uneven outdoor terrain in variable weather, checks identity and warrants, warns or cites, and escorts them clear of the tracks; subjects may flee or be impaired.

Homeless encampments, squatters in idle railcars, or scrappers along an urban rail corridor: the officer posts notice, coordinates with city outreach and municipal police, and physically clears occupants and their belongings from railroad property over repeated visits, amid debris, brush and hazardous conditions.

Night response to cargo theft in a fenced intermodal or classification yard: agent detects container break-ins, closes on suspects among standing railcars and containers, conducts a foot pursuit, detains and handcuffs suspects, recovers stolen goods, and holds them for local PD booking.

Transit setting: removing a fare evader, intoxicated, disorderly or trespassing person from a train car, platform or station mezzanine during service hours, with bystanders present; verbal contact and escort out, escalating to physical restraint and custodial arrest in a minority of contacts.

Joint operation or handoff: the railroad/transit officer works a coordinated detail with municipal police, sheriff or task force across yard property and adjoining streets — holding a perimeter, chasing and taking a suspect into custody, transferring the prisoner and evidence, and completing the arrest report.

sources.title: NYPD subway robot pilot program ends after Times Square surveillance – NBC New York
sources.claim: The Knightscope K5, an autonomous wheeled security robot, was deployed on patrol in the Times Square subway ...; it functions as a moving camera with an intercom, required human escorts, and the pilot ended without the robot performing any contact, detention or removal of persons.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robot to this task's transit-station instance: same environment (subway station) and same policing purpose, but the robot only observes and alerts, showing that removal/apprehension of persons is not performed by the machine.

sources.title: NYPD Adds 'Spot,' the Robot Dog, to Force — and More Tech
sources.claim: The NYPD's Digidog (Boston Dynamics Spot) is a remote-controlled robot used to look into barricade and hostage scenes and deliver items; it is not used to apprehend, restrain or remove suspects, and it is human-piloted throughout.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: police response to a subject on premises. It is the most capable legged police robot in US service, yet its role is reconnaissance under continuous teleoperation, so it cannot substantiate autonomous apprehension or removal.

sources.system: SMP Robotics S5 / S5.3 security patrol robot

sources.claim: SMP Robotics' S5-series outdoor autonomous patrol robots are sold commercially for perimeter and area security; they patrol, detect and stream AI-analyzed video, while the vendor states that human security officers are the ones who detain trespassers and handle unpredictable criminal activity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor perimeter trespass response on industrial property, comparable to a rail yard. The vendor's own division of labor places detention with human officers, so the robot does not complete the trespasser-removal instance.

sources.title: UP: Rising to the Occasion: Union Pacific Drones Support Safe Operations
sources.claim: Union Pacific uses drones over rail yards and track for inspection and risk identification, and is still working toward autonomy for those inspection flights; railroad robotic/aerial assets are used for sensing and deterrence, not for contacting or removing trespassers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: railroad property surveillance in the exact settings of this task (yards and right-of-way). It establishes that deployed railroad robotics is aerial inspection/observation, with no capability to apprehend or remove a person.

tasks.label: Direct security activities at derailments, fires, floods, or strikes involving railroad property.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Patrol railroad yards, cars, stations, or other facilities to protect company property or shipments and to maintain order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Roving patrol of a busy urban transit or intercity passenger station during service hours — concourse, mezzanine, fare line, platforms, stairs and escalators, restrooms — with crowds present: visible deterrent presence, moving people along, checking on riders in distress, breaking up disputes, ejecting trespassers and responding to disorder as it appears.

Onboard patrol: riding trains and walking end-to-end through passenger cars (and climbing on or into equipment) while in motion or at layover, checking riders, spotting smoking/vandalism/unattended bags, responding to disturbances between cars and at door thresholds.

Off-hours or low-traffic property checks at commuter/suburban stations and station-adjacent facilities: park-and-ride lots and parking structures, platform shelters, ticket machines, closed station interiors, crew rooms and administrative buildings — driving/walking a route, looking for break-ins, vandalism, loiterers and suspicious vehicles, and reporting what is found.

Night patrol of a freight yard, intermodal terminal, or transit maintenance/storage yard: driving and walking the fence line and yard roads, checking gates and locks, lighting up strings of cars and container stacks with spotlight/thermal, spotting trespassers and cargo thieves, and calling in or confronting what is found.

Patrol of right-of-way away from facilities: remote and rural track sections, bridges, tunnel portals, grade crossings and railroad-owned land, looking for trespassers, dumping, vandalism, signal/bridge tampering and encroachment, reached by road vehicle, hi-rail or on foot over uneven ballast and brush.

Walking strings of parked railcars, trailers and containers in a yard to check shipment integrity: seals, hasps, door latches, roof hatches and evidence of tampering or pilferage, documenting anything broken or opened.

sources.title: Built for the Real World: How the K5 Robot Handles Weather, People, and Parking Lots
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots run continuous unattended patrols of paved outdoor lots and multi-level parking structures, routing around vehicles and people and reading plates; roughly three quarters of the deployed fleet is in this duty.

sources.developer: Knightscope / U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Police

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places

sources.title: NYPD 'robocop' no longer patrolling following end of pilot program
sources.claim: The only ground-robot patrol of a US transit station — a Knightscope K5 in the Times Square subway ... — could not use stairs, was escorted by officers throughout, and the pilot ended with the robot placed in storage.

tasks.label: Investigate or direct investigations of freight theft, suspicious damage or loss of passengers' valuables, or other crimes on railroad property.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cargo/freight theft case at an intermodal or classification yard: agent responds to a report of cut seals and pilfered containers, walks the string of cars amid debris fields of discarded packaging, photographs and documents breached seals and damaged doors, reconciles losses with terminal staff and shipment records, pulls gate/yard camera footage, interviews crew, drivers and yard employees, collects and logs physical evidence, and produces a case report referred to prosecutors or a task force.

Reported theft or suspicious loss/damage of a passenger's valuables (bag, phone, laptop) on a commuter train or at a station: agent takes the victim's statement, canvasses the platform and car, checks lost-and-found, reviews station and onboard CCTV to identify a suspect, interviews conductor and witnesses, attempts recovery of the property, and files the incident/investigative report.

Crime scene along the right-of-way or at unfenced trackside areas: looted container debris, copper wire or catalytic-converter theft, encampments adjacent to the tracks. Agent walks uneven ballast and brush, documents and photographs the scene, recovers stolen goods and tools, contacts and identifies persons present, sometimes detains or arrests, and writes the case up.

Other crimes on railroad/transit property (assault, robbery, vandalism/graffiti, drug incidents, vehicle-train collisions): agent secures the scene on a platform, train, or grade crossing, interviews victims and witnesses, collects and preserves physical evidence, canvasses for video, and completes the investigative report.

Directing and desk-based case work at a railroad police or transit police office: assigning and reviewing subordinate agents' cases, analyzing theft patterns from camera, gate and shipment data, coordinating with local law-enforcement task forces, conducting suspect interviews in an interview room, and preparing case files for prosecution.

sources.title: NYPD Launches Knightscope Security Robot Service in Manhattan Subway
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot was deployed on patrol in a Manhattan subway station with NYPD/MTA support, performing autonomous navigation and overnight patrol — i.e., surveillance presence only, not investigation of crimes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol in a transit station (same E2 setting as instances 1, 2 and 4). It does not transfer to this task: the robot only records and streams; it does not take victim statements, canvass witnesses, collect or preserve physical evidence, or produce an investigative case product.

sources.title: NYC retires 420-pound NYPD subway surveilling robot after pilot ends
sources.claim: The NYPD subway K5 pilot ended; the robot required human chaperones during its deployment, indicating it could not operate as an independent police resource in the station environment.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (station patrol). Cited as a negative bound: the most prominent transit-police robot deployment provided surveillance under human escort and was withdrawn, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of investigative work.

sources.system: Union Pacific rail-yard surveillance drones and AI camera network
sources.title: Union Pacific Enhances Cargo Security on Numerous Fronts
sources.claim: Union Pacific uses thermal-imaging drones and 70+ fixed camera units to surveil rail yards and mainline track for cargo theft, while human special agents on a law-enforcement task force conduct the actual theft investigations and arrests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial/fixed surveillance of the same rail-yard and right-of-way settings as instances 1 and 3. Capability does not transfer: the drones detect and cue, and the railroad's own account attributes the investigations and charging outcomes to human special agents.

sources.title: Duos Technologies Uses AI-Powered System for Railcar Inspection
sources.claim: Duos Technologies' Railcar Inspection Portal autonomously images passing railcars at track speed and flags anomalies such as open doors and mechanical defects, but it is a fixed sensing installation that performs no manipulation, evidence handling, or investigative follow-up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of railcar anomalies (open doors, damage) in a purpose-built trackside portal — the closest E1-style analogue to inspecting suspicious damage. It does not transfer: the portal only reports anomalies and cannot document a scene, recover property, interview people, or close a case.

sources.system: PRIME (Police Robot for Inspection and Mapping of underwater Evidence)
sources.title: A prototype autonomous robot for underwater crime scene investigation and emergency response
sources.claim: The state of the art in robotic crime-scene work is an autonomous surface vessel prototype that locates and highlights potential evidence for human divers within a police search process; it maps and inspects rather than conducting or completing an investigation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crime-scene evidence search. Cited as a bound on transfer: even this research prototype only flags regions of interest for human investigators and is not deployed, so no robotic system is substantiated as completing a criminal investigation end-to-end.

tasks.label: Examine credentials of unauthorized persons attempting to enter secured areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rail yard or maintenance shop gate/perimeter: officer encounters a contractor, vendor truck driver, or utility worker inside or at the entrance of a secured yard, asks for a contractor badge or company ID and work order, and verifies it against the access roster (often by radio to dispatch) before allowing or denying entry.

Transit station back-of-house: someone has passed through an employee-only door into a tunnel, control room, or equipment space; officer stops the person, inspects the agency employee ID or vendor badge, checks whether it authorizes that area, and records the outcome.

Track right-of-way, bridge, or outdoor restricted zone: officer contacts a trespasser or person with no visible credentials, requests a driver's license or other ID, runs the identity through a mobile data terminal or dispatch, and determines authorization status.

Staffed access-control checkpoint during heightened security or special events (e.g., hazmat train, dignitary movement, construction project entry post): officer inspects IDs and event or project credentials against a posted access list for a queue of arriving workers.

Persons claiming written permission — film crews, journalists, railfans, surveyors, or utility crews — present permits, letters of authorization, or right-of-entry paperwork that the officer reads, checks for validity/expiration, and confirms with the issuing department.

tasks.label: Enforce traffic laws regarding the transit system and reprimand individuals who violate them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Grade-crossing enforcement detail on a public road: the officer watches a highway-rail crossing, sees a driver drive around lowered gates or stop on the tracks, pulls the vehicle over in moving traffic, contacts the driver, checks license/registration, and issues a citation or formal warning.

Bus-lane, bus-stop and transit-mall traffic enforcement on city streets: vehicles standing in a bus-only lane, blocking a bus zone, or driving in a rail transit mall; the officer contacts the driver, orders the vehicle moved, writes a citation, or arranges a tow.

Parking and vehicle-rule enforcement on transit-owned property (park-and-ride lots and garages, station kiss-and-ride lanes, employee lots): patrol the lot, find vehicles in fire lanes, accessible stalls, or without permits, place citations on windshields, warn drivers who are present, and call for tows.

Verbal reprimand of pedestrians and cyclists violating crossing rules at street-level grade crossings: walking or riding around lowered gates, crossing against crossing signals, cutting along the right-of-way; the officer warns them off, confirms they clear, and logs the contact.

Verbal reprimand of passengers inside stations: people standing past the platform-edge line, crossing tracks between platforms, or riding scooters/bikes on platforms and in concourses; the officer admonishes them and ensures compliance before moving on.

Traffic control at an incident: crossing-gate malfunction, blocked crossing, collision, or special event; the officer stands in the roadway directing vehicles and pedestrians, overriding dark or malfunctioning signals, and reprimanding drivers who fail to obey directions.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous patrol of a US transit station; shows robot mobility in the station environment but no capability to stop, cite, or reprimand violators.

tasks.label: Investigate reports of animal attacks or animal cruelty, interviewing witnesses, collecting evidence, and writing reports.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dog bite / animal attack call: officer drives to a residential neighborhood, locates the victim, photographs wounds, knocks on doors to interview the victim, the dog's owner and neighbors, verifies rabies vaccination records, physically examines and identifies the biting dog, places it under home quarantine or impounds it into the truck, and writes the bite report/affidavit. Owners are often uncooperative; the dog may be loose or aggressive.

Neglect/cruelty complaint at a private home, yard or small rural property (thin dog on a chain, no water or shelter, sick or untreated animal, hot car): officer observes from the right-of-way or gains consent to enter, photographs the animal and conditions, body-condition-scores the animal, collects physical evidence (food/water containers, tether, medications), interviews the owner and complainant, may seize the animal, issues a warning or citation, and writes a documented report.

Large-scale cruelty case with law enforcement: hoarding house, backyard breeding/puppy mill, cockfighting or dogfighting property. Officer works a warrant service in filthy, biohazardous, unpredictable conditions, photographs and tags dozens of animals and carcasses, collects fighting paraphernalia and samples under chain of custody, interviews suspects and witnesses, coordinates seizure and transport, and writes a lengthy court-ready report.

Investigation at a licensed or commercial facility kept to a working standard: boarding kennel, pet store, grooming shop, riding stable, livestock barn or another shelter. Officer walks the premises with staff, photographs enclosures and animals, pulls vaccination and care records, interviews employees and the manager, collects samples or documents, and writes an inspection/investigation report.

Follow-up case work at the shelter/office: examining and photographing the impounded or quarantined animal in the kennel run (including with a vet for a forensic exam), logging and securing evidence in the property room, taking phone or in-person witness statements, reviewing video submitted by complainants, and assembling the case file and narrative report for the prosecutor.

sources.title: Police 'Robot Dogs' Raise Concerns as More Departments Adopt Them (Governing / Bloomberg)
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped is used by more than 60 US/Canadian bomb squads and SWAT teams for entering hazardous scenes and streaming video, but in law-enforcement use an operator guides it with a tablet; it does not interview people, collect physical evidence, or handle animals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sending a robot into an incident scene to gather visual information, the closest fielded analog to an officer documenting an attack or cruelty scene. It fails to transfer because operation is operator-guided and limited to reconnaissance, with no witness interviewing, physical evidence collection, animal handling, or report authorship.

sources.developer: Showing Animals Respect and Kindness (SHARK), commercial UAV platforms
sources.title: How a Small Nonprofit Uses Drones to Fight Animal Cruelty: Inside SHARK's Mission (DroneLife)
sources.claim: Nonprofit SHARK uses piloted camera drones to capture aerial video of cockfighting pits and abusive facilities that is then handed to police and agencies; the drones only record imagery and the human investigation follows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial documentation of animal-cruelty scenes. It does not substantiate the task because the aircraft are human-piloted, produce only overhead imagery, and cannot interview witnesses, seize or preserve physical evidence, examine animals, or write the case report.

sources.date: 2019 (on market in Europe; article undated, product launched 2018)
sources.title: Poultry farming: The robots are coming (WATTAgNet)
sources.claim: ChickenBoy is a commercially available ceiling-rail robot that autonomously patrols broiler houses and assesses bird health, welfare and ambient conditions, including locating dead birds - autonomous animal-condition monitoring inside an institution-controlled facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous assessment of live animals' condition inside a structured facility, resembling an officer documenting animal welfare during a kennel or barn investigation. It does not transfer: the robot is rail-bound and single-purpose, cannot enter novel premises, examine or seize individual animals, question staff, take custody of records, or produce an evidentiary report.

sources.title: Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR) - Privacy Impact Assessment, U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 is a fielded autonomous security robot that patrols facility grounds continuously, collecting sensor and camera data and raising alerts, but it performs no manipulation, no interviewing, and no case investigation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous patrol and incident detection/reporting on managed premises. It does not substantiate this task because the machine only records and alerts on fixed patrol routes; it cannot conduct an investigation, gather statements, collect and preserve physical evidence, or handle animals.

tasks.label: Examine animals for injuries or malnutrition, and arrange for any necessary medical treatment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shelter/impound intake exam: officer brings a stray dog or cat into the shelter intake room, lifts it onto a table or scale, scans for a microchip, palpates for wounds, embedded collars, fractures and dehydration, parts fur to find lacerations/maggots, assigns a body condition score, checks eyes/ears/teeth, records findings and flags the animal for the shelter veterinarian or a contract clinic.

Field exam at the pickup site: an injured or sick loose dog/cat found on a street, alley, driveway or yard is caught with a leash or net, checked on the spot for bleeding, limb use, mange, emaciation and shock in variable light and weather, then loaded into the truck and driven to an emergency clinic the officer phones ahead.

Cruelty/neglect investigation on private property (hoarding house, backyard kennel, small farm): officer enters cluttered, soiled premises with an uncooperative owner present, individually examines multiple dogs, cats, horses or livestock for emaciation, untreated wounds, parasites and matting, photographs and body-condition-scores each animal for the case file, and arranges veterinary examination or emergency seizure and transport.

Fractious or dangerous animal: an injured, frightened or aggressive dog, feral cat or dog-bite quarantine subject must be restrained with a catch pole, net or squeeze cage before any examination; the officer assesses injuries through the restraint and arranges chemical sedation or veterinary handling.

Injured wildlife or loose livestock on a roadway or public land: officer approaches a struck deer, raptor, raccoon or stray horse, judges injury severity and whether the animal is treatable, contains it, and arranges a wildlife rehabilitator, large-animal vet or humane disposition.

sources.title: Faromatics - EIT Food
sources.claim: ChickenBoy is a commercially deployed, ceiling-rail-mounted autonomous robot that patrols broiler houses and uses AI and sensors to flag flock health and welfare risks (e.g. manure/enteric disease analysis, thermal sensation, air quality); it does not handle, restrain or individually examine animals, and does not arrange veterinary treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated livestock health/welfare monitoring. Transfer to this task is limited: ChickenBoy senses flock-level indicators from a fixed ceiling rail in one purpose-fitted barn type, and never performs the hands-on individual examination (palpation, wound search, body condition by feel) or treatment arrangement the animal control task requires.

sources.title: Robot in the Chicken House | GTRI
sources.claim: A GTRI mobile robot demonstrated autonomous daily monitoring inside commercial breeder chicken houses, navigating among live birds; the demonstrated function is environmental/flock monitoring and egg handling, not individual injury or malnutrition examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic inspection rounds among live animals in an institutional animal facility. It shows robots can move safely among animals, but no cited capability to examine an individual animal for injury or malnutrition or to arrange its medical treatment.

sources.title: Control of salmon lice through optical delousing in commercial salmonid aquaculture - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Stingray optical delousing nodes are commercially deployed in salmon sea cages and autonomously detect sea lice on free-swimming individual fish with machine vision and destroy them with a laser — the closest deployed 'inspect an individual animal and treat it' robot, but it is a fixed node in an aquaculture pen treating one parasite, with no handling, no body-condition or wound assessment, and no arrangement of veterinary care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of a health problem on an individual animal followed by automated treatment. Transfer fails on objects and depth: salmon in water versus restrained mammals, a single visible ectoparasite versus lacerations, fractures, dehydration and emaciation assessed by sight and touch.

sources.system: Lely Astronaut automatic milking system with MQC-C cell count sensor
sources.title: The history of the milking robot Lely Astronaut
sources.claim: Commercial automatic milking systems (Lely Astronaut) autonomously attach to and milk cows that present themselves in a purpose-built box and automatically screen milk (somatic cell count, conductivity) to flag udder-health abnormalities for the farmer; the health assessment is a milk-sensor inference, not a physical examination of the animal's body for injuries or malnutrition.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot contacts a fixtured live animal and produces a health flag. It is the strongest E1-style analog (animal brought to the machine), yet it only measures milk from one species and cannot inspect a body for wounds or score emaciation, so it does not substantiate completing this task even at E1.

sources.developer: Australian Centre for Field Robotics, University of Sydney
sources.title: Meet SwagBot, the AI-powered robot cattle herder preventing soil degradation
sources.claim: SwagBot is a field robot that autonomously herds cattle on pasture and is reported to monitor livestock and pasture condition; it is a research/field-trial platform performing herd-level observation, with no individual physical examination or arrangement of veterinary treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor autonomous robot observing animals in an unstructured setting. It shows navigation and coarse monitoring outdoors, but no demonstrated capacity to catch, restrain, examine an injured individual animal, or arrange its treatment.

sources.title: The Automation Evolution | Today's Veterinary Business
sources.claim: In veterinary practice the robotic/automated systems described for pet consultations rely on a human owner positioning the animal and a remote human veterinarian, i.e. the physical examination of companion animals is not performed autonomously by machines.
sources.transferJustification: Directly adjacent task (examining a companion animal). It shows the state of the art is human handling plus remote human judgment, which cannot support an autonomous positive judgment for this task at any tier.

tasks.label: Remove captured animals from animal-control service vehicles and place animals in shelter cages or other enclosures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adoptable/manageable stray dog: officer opens the truck's rear compartment at the shelter sally port, leashes the dog, walks it through intake doors and corridors past other barking dogs, puts it in a kennel run, removes the leash and latches the gate without letting it bolt.

Cat, kitten litter, or small mammal arriving in a humane trap or carrier: officer lifts the trap/carrier out of the vehicle's compartment, carries it into the cat holding room, and either sets the trap inside a cage or transfers the animal into a cage/kennel with a trap divider or net, then secures the latch.

Fractious, fearful, or aggressive dog: animal must be extracted from the truck box with a control (catch) pole or by slip lead, possibly muzzled or lifted, moved to an isolation/bite-quarantine kennel, the pole loop released through the gate, and the gate secured — all without injury to handler or animal.

Injured, sick, sedated, or heavily matted/soiled animal (hit-by-car dog, neonatal kittens, unconscious animal): carefully lifted on a board, blanket, or in a carrier from the vehicle into a clinic table, incubator, or isolation enclosure, minimizing aggravation of injuries.

Wildlife in a trap, net, or snake bag (raccoon, skunk, opossum, bat, snake, waterfowl): moved from the truck's compartment into a species-appropriate holding enclosure in the wildlife/isolation room, with rabies-vector precautions and no escape.

Livestock or large animal (loose horse, goat, pig, sheep) hauled in a trailer: backed to the shelter's corral/large-animal pen, gate opened, animal driven or led off the trailer into the pen, pen gate secured.

sources.title: Meet the robot that's making cattle herding safer | Cargill
sources.claim: The most capable machine used to move large live animals in a controlled industrial facility (Cargill's CattleBot, used to move cattle in beef-plant pens) is driven by a human via remote control, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving live animals inside an institutional facility. It does NOT transfer to this task: the machine is continuously teleoperated and only pushes herds through gates; it does not remove individual animals from a vehicle or place them in enclosures.

sources.title: UniLoad - BAADER Poultry
sources.claim: Automated live-animal unloading exists only for uniform farmed poultry on a purpose-built processing line, where machines destack transport modules and convey drawers of birds; birds are conveyed en masse to a shackle line rather than individually placed into enclosures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading live animals from a transport vehicle. Transfer fails for this task: the objects are thousands of identical 2-kg docile broilers in fixtured drawers moved by conveyors, not individual dogs, cats or wildlife that must be leashed/poled, assessed, and secured behind a latched kennel gate.

sources.system: Skala Maskon automated fish vaccination machine
sources.title: Maskon automated vaccination machine for farmed fish | Business Norway
sources.claim: Fully automatic handling of individual live animals is demonstrated only for farmed fish pumped through a purpose-built vaccination machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling of live animals. Transfer fails: fish are hydraulically conveyed, uniform in size and non-resistant out of water; nothing in this system grasps, leads, or confines a struggling terrestrial mammal or places it into an enclosure.

sources.system: Robotic Cage Handling System for Tunnel Washers
sources.title: Robotic Cage Handling System for Tunnel Washers - Getinge
sources.claim: Robotic automation in animal-holding facilities (vivariums) handles the caging hardware — cages are presented to the robot in a known position after washing — while transfer of the live animals themselves is done by human technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of animal cages in an animal facility. Transfer fails: the robot manipulates empty, standardized cages at fixed poses; it neither removes an animal from a vehicle nor places a live animal into an enclosure.

sources.title: Tecniplast Vivarium Automation
sources.claim: Mobile robots in animal facilities autonomously transport cages and supplies between zones, i.e. logistics of containers rather than handling of animals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving animal cages inside a facility. Transfer fails: transport of standardized cages on an AGV does not include extracting an animal from a service vehicle, controlling it, or securing it inside a shelter enclosure.

tasks.label: Answer inquiries from the public concerning animal control operations.
