tasks.label: Capture and remove stray, uncontrolled, or abused animals from undesirable conditions, using nets, nooses, or tranquilizer darts as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Stray/at-large dog call in a residential neighborhood or public street: officer locates a loose, often fearful or evasive dog, approaches on foot, secures it with a slip lead, catch pole or net, checks for injury/microchip, then lifts or walks it into a truck kennel and transports it to the shelter.

Free-roaming/feral cats and kittens: baiting, placing and monitoring humane box traps in yards, alleys and colony sites, plus hand-retrieval of kittens from under porches, sheds, decks or vehicle engine compartments; carrying trapped animals to the vehicle and to the shelter.

Nuisance, sick or injured wildlife call: raccoon in an attic or trash can, opossum or skunk under a deck, bat or snake inside a house, injured deer or coyote on a roadway; capture with tongs, snake hook, net or trap and remove to a carrier for transport or euthanasia.

Aggressive, dangerous or severely injured animal, often with police backup: pursuit and restraint with catch pole, snare, net gun or (rarely) chemical immobilization by dart, in a fenced yard, under a house, in a vehicle, or in the open, with public safety and animal-welfare constraints.

Cruelty/hoarding/abandonment seizure executed under warrant: entering a cluttered home, kennel or rural property and removing multiple debilitated dogs, cats or livestock/horses, crating, documenting and loading them onto vehicles.

Animal loose inside a controlled institutional or commercial facility (school building, warehouse, big-box store, airport terminal), with staff cooperating to contain the area; officer corners and captures the animal and removes it.

sources.system: AI-based smart box trap system (YOLO + Jetson Nano trap controller)
sources.developer: Ehime University / ROBOMECH Journal authors (Okamoto et al.)
sources.title: Development of AI-based smart box trap system for capturing a harmful wild boar | ROBOMECH Journal
sources.claim: An AI-triggered box trap prototype autonomously recognizes wild boars and closes the trap gate in farmland — the closest demonstrated automation of live-animal capture — but it is a stationary trap that only confines the animal; it does not approach, restrain, crate or remove the animal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated live trapping of a wild animal. It substantiates only autonomous gate closure on an animal that voluntarily enters a baited fixed trap; it does not substantiate locating, approaching, noosing/netting, restraining or transporting an uncontrolled animal, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

sources.title: M.I.N.E. Trapping System - JAGER PRO Store
sources.claim: Commercial remote hog-trapping systems capture animals only when a human watching a cellular camera feed triggers the gate from a phone — human-in-the-loop, not autonomous capture, and removal of the trapped animals is still done by people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = field capture of nuisance animals. It fails the autonomy requirement (a person triggers the gate) and covers only confinement, not approach, restraint or removal, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Pentagon task force to deploy AI-powered UAS systems to capture drones
sources.claim: Autonomous net-capture of a moving target exists only against aerial drones: the DroneHunter uses radar and AI to pursue and net another drone and tow it away, in open airspace.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous net capture of a moving target. Transfer fails: the target is a rigid aerial machine with no welfare constraints, whereas this task requires netting a living animal without injuring it, then restraining, assessing and loading it into a transport kennel — none of which the system does.

sources.system: Hound Units (Boston Dynamics Spot-class patrol quadrupeds)
sources.title: Atlanta Just Put Robot Dogs on Patrol - Your Neighborhood Might Be Next
sources.claim: Mobile ground robots actually fielded in US streets and neighborhoods (quadruped 'robot dogs') perform patrol, surveillance and thermal imaging only; they have no capability to seize, restrain or transport an animal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous mobile operation in the same unstructured streets where stray-animal calls occur. It shows navigation is feasible there but provides no manipulation or animal-handling capability, so it cannot substantiate capture and removal.

sources.system: Catch pole / net gun (manual animal control equipment)
sources.developer: WVS Academy (training reference) / net gun vendors
sources.title: Net Guns for Dog Catchers & Animal Control Officers (2026)
sources.claim: Animal capture in the field is performed with hand-held tools by officers who must get within arm's reach or fire a net gun by hand; the equipment marketed to animal control is manual, with no robotic or autonomous option.
sources.transferJustification: Baseline evidence that the task as performed is manual; it is not a robotic system and supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Supply animals with food, water, and personal care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily feeding/watering rounds for impounded dogs in a municipal shelter's kennel runs: measuring kibble per the animal's diet card, carrying bowls into occupied runs while blocking dogs from bolting, dumping and refilling water buckets, noting which animals ate.

Care of caged cats and small animals in shelter cat rooms/holding: portioning wet and dry food into dishes inside stacked stainless cages, refreshing water, scooping or swapping litter pans, while handling fractious or feral cats.
Bathing and drying a filthy, flea-covered stray dog at intake in the shelter's wash tub before housing or adoption photos.

Other personal care of impounded animals in the shelter: brushing and dematting, nail trims, ear/eye cleaning, applying topical flea treatment, and giving routine oral medications to animals of unknown temperament.

Care of a just-captured animal in the field: offering water and a little food to a dehydrated stray held in the truck's transport compartment or a carrier at the roadside or a parking lot before it reaches the shelter.

Emergency food and water for neglected large animals or a hoarding-case group at the property pending seizure: throwing hay, filling troughs and buckets from a hose or hauled water, in a barn, paddock or cluttered yard taken as found.

sources.title: CalfRail & CalfRail DUO - Förster-Technik
sources.claim: CalfRail is a commercially sold rail-guided automatic feeding robot that travels to individually housed calves in their pens and delivers animal-specific liquid feed portions on schedule, fully automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: supplying feed to individually penned animals. Same problem class as kennel/cage feeding rounds in a purpose-built animal-housing row: a machine travels a fixed aisle of identical pens and dispenses a measured, animal-specific ration into each pen's receptacle with no caretaker present.

sources.title: Feed to Need with the Lely Vector – Smarter Feeding for Dairy & Beef Farming
sources.claim: The Lely Vector is an autonomous mixing-and-feeding robot that mixes and dispenses rations to cattle groups in barn feed alleys around the clock without a driver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: supplying feed to housed livestock. Transfers to supplying food to impounded livestock in a barn: same animals, same feedstuffs (hay/TMR), same delivery into a feed alley shared with the animals, at commercial reliability.

sources.title: Lely produces 1,000th Vector automatic feeding system
sources.claim: Lely Vector automatic feeding systems are in routine commercial use on cattle farms worldwide, not just demonstrations.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployed status of the barn feeding robot relied on for the livestock-feeding judgment.

sources.system: Lavakan automatic pet washing cabins (LVK 120 Silence / LVK 180 XL)
sources.title: Lavakan – Automatic Pet Washing Cabins | Made in Spain
sources.claim: Lavakan makes automatic dog washing and drying cabins with a fully automatic mode, sold worldwide; the dog is placed in the cabin and the machine runs the wash and dry cycle itself.

sources.system: Lavakan de Aste; PetSpa dog washing machines
sources.title: What are Dog Washing Machines? Alternatives to Bathing your Dog
sources.claim: Automated dog washing machines have been commercially manufactured since 1999 and are sold to grooming salons, pet stores, veterinary offices, kennels and boarding ....

sources.title: Nelson - Model 1200 Automatic Dog Waterer - System Equine
sources.claim: Automatic dog waterers that dispense water to penned dogs without a caretaker are marketed to and used by humane societies, animal control facilities and boarding kennels.

sources.system: Quick Feed automatic pet and animal feeders
sources.title: Quick Feed Automatic Feeders
sources.claim: Timer-controlled automatic feeders that dispense measured food to dogs, cats, horses and other animals are sold for household and commercial animal-housing applications.

sources.title: Litter-Robot 4 Automatic Litter Box
sources.claim: The Litter-Robot 4 is a widely sold automatic litter box that senses the cat and runs an unattended sifting cycle to keep a clean litter bed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: litter/waste management for caged cats, the sanitation half of the cat-care instance; same animals, same consumable, unattended operation.

sources.title: Kennel Cleaning Systems & Pressure Washers | Spraymaster
sources.claim: Searches for robots performing kennel care in animal shelters return only human-operated pressure-wash systems, indicating no autonomous system performs shelter feeding or kennel rounds.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as a negative indicator: the state of the art in shelter kennels is human-operated equipment, supporting the finding that no robot completes shelter kennel care at E2.

tasks.label: Euthanize rabid, unclaimed, or severely injured animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shelter euthanasia room: an unclaimed or unadoptable dog is walked from its kennel, lifted onto a table or floor mat, restrained (usually with a second staffer), a cephalic vein is raised and clipped, a weight-based dose of sodium pentobarbital is injected IV, death is confirmed by auscultation, the controlled substance is logged and the body moved to the cooler/freezer.

Shelter euthanasia of cats, kittens or neonates (unclaimed, panleukopenia/URI, unweaned litters): IM pre-euthanasia sedative given through carrier or with a towel wrap, then IV, intraperitoneal or intracardiac pentobarbital once unconscious; death confirmed, records completed, carcass bagged.

Feral, fractious or dangerous animal (feral cat in a live trap, aggressive dog in a quarantine run, injured raccoon in a trap): chemical restraint first by squeeze cage, pole syringe or dart, then handling into position and lethal injection, with staff safety and bite/rabies-exposure precautions throughout.

Field euthanasia of a severely injured animal on a roadside, in a ditch or on private property (deer or dog struck by a vehicle, downed livestock): approach and assess the animal, dispatch by firearm (or captive bolt) with correct anatomical placement while managing traffic, bystanders and backstop, confirm death, then drag/lift the carcass out of the roadway for disposal.

Rabies-suspect animal (bat, skunk, raccoon, or a biting cat/dog under quarantine): euthanize by a method that leaves the brain intact, then decapitate or package the specimen in PPE, chill it and complete the state lab submission paperwork.

sources.system: Portable autonomous venipuncture robot (VascuLogic / Rutgers, Balter et al.)
sources.title: Portable robot for autonomous venipuncture using 3D near infrared image guidance
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous venipuncture robots (Rutgers/VascuLogic) image and cannulate veins in human forearms; they are research/clinical-trial devices, and no equivalent has been shown inserting a needle into a vein of a furred, live dog or cat, let alone administering a lethal dose and confirming death.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated venipuncture/needle placement in a live subject. It is the closest existing capability to giving an IV euthanasia injection, but it is demonstrated only on immobilized human arms with visible superficial veins, not on restrained animals with fur, so it does not carry over to shelter euthanasia.

sources.system: Maskon VX-4/VX-8/VX-16 automatic fish vaccination machine
sources.date: Product line in commercial use; page updated April 2026
sources.title: Vaccination - Maskon
sources.claim: Fully automatic machines do inject live animals under machine vision, but only tiny anesthetized fish singularized and oriented by the machine itself; nothing comparable exists for injecting dogs, cats or wildlife.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated injection of a substance into a live animal inside a purpose-built machine. It shows the E1 ceiling for machine-administered injection: 30-130 g anesthetized fish handled by conveyor, which does not transfer to venous injection in a 5-40 kg conscious dog or cat, nor to confirming death and carcass handling.

sources.system: Euthanex SMARTBOX automated CO2 euthanasia system (MSVF-4/MSVF-8, EA-34004C)
sources.title: EUTHANEX SMARTBOX - Euthanex - PDF Catalogs | Technical Documentation
sources.claim: Automated euthanasia hardware in use today controls gas delivery to caged small laboratory rodents; the animal is placed, monitored and removed by a person, and the method is not accepted for shelter dogs and cats in the US.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled euthanasia of animals. It is limited to small laboratory rodents in cages; CO2 chambers are rejected for shelter dogs and cats (banned in many states, 'not recommended' by AVMA, 'unacceptable' per Association of Shelter Veterinarians), and the device performs no handling, death confirmation or disposal.

sources.title: Felixer, the grooming trap, works to control feral cats
sources.claim: An autonomous field device that lethally targets a species exists (Felixer grooming trap for feral cats), but it opportunistically poisons any passing cat with delayed death and no confirmation or carcass recovery; it cannot euthanize a designated rabid, unclaimed or injured animal to shelter standards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous lethal control of an animal in an unstructured outdoor setting. It targets healthy free-roaming cats by species discrimination rather than euthanizing a specific injured or rabid individual, uses a toxin (not an accepted euthanasia agent), and neither verifies death nor removes the carcass.

sources.system: Penetrating captive bolt stunning (industry practice review)
sources.developer: n/a (RSPCA assessment cited in industry review)
sources.title: Stunning in Slaughter Practices: Techniques and Effectiveness
sources.claim: Even in slaughter facilities, the single-animal killing step for large mammals by captive bolt remains a manual operator task; no automated captive-bolt system is in service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humane killing of a large mammal by ballistic/captive-bolt placement, the same physical act as field euthanasia of an injured deer or dog. The source indicates the act is not automated even inside purpose-built abattoirs, so it cannot be automated on a roadside.

tasks.label: Clean facilities and equipment such as dog pens and animal control trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily cleaning of occupied dog runs at the shelter/pound: shift or leash each dog out of its run, scoop feces and soiled bedding, hose and scrub floor, walls and gate, apply disinfectant, rinse and squeegee to the drain, replace bedding and toys, refill food and water bowls, return the dog.

Deep sanitizing of vacated dog runs or a whole kennel block between animals or after a disease exposure: pens empty, high-pressure wash of floor, walls, gates and drains, disinfectant applied with contact time, rinse and dry before restocking.

Cleaning the animal control truck at the shelter yard or municipal wash rack: pull out carriers, remove soiled bedding, hair and waste from the transport compartments, hose and scrub compartments and bed, apply disinfectant, rinse, and wash the vehicle exterior.

Cleaning and disinfecting field equipment in the utility/wash area: catch poles, nets, live traps, muzzles, leashes, plastic carriers and transport cages, bowls and litter pans - scrubbed, soaked or sprayed with disinfectant, rinsed, dried and restocked on the truck.

Cat and small-animal enclosure cleaning: spot-clean occupied cages, move the animal to a holding cage or carrier when needed, change litter pans and bedding, wipe and disinfect cage surfaces, refill food and water.
Routine hard-floor cleaning of the facility's work and public areas: scrubbing kennel aisles and mopping/scrubbing lobby, corridors, intake and exam room floors on a fixed daily schedule.

sources.title: Pipestone looks to Washpower and Danish farmers to automate power washing
sources.claim: Washpower ProCleaner pressure-washing robots clean pig pens after the animals are removed; more than 500 Danish pig houses and 1,100 units globally, with staff reduced to touch-up and disinfection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing and disinfecting animal pens in an animal-housing building. Same objects (concrete/steel pens fouled with feces and urine), same means (high-pressure water plus detergent/disinfectant) and comparable precision to washing down a kennel run; animals must be out of the pen in both cases.

sources.title: ProCleaner XT100 - Washpower
sources.claim: The ProCleaner XT100 adds an automated disinfection step and uses a light railing system installed in the barn to guide the robot, i.e. infrastructure built around the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: disinfecting emptied animal pens. Shows the wash-plus-disinfect cycle can be completed by the machine when the building is fitted with guide rails, i.e. in a purpose-built (E1) arrangement.

sources.title: EVO Cleaner for pig barns - Envirologic
sources.claim: The EVO Cleaner washing robot is taught barn washing routines once by joystick and then runs them unattended around the clock, notifying staff when finished.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-pressure washing of animal pens; establishes that after one teaching pass the machine washes pens without an operator, the mode a kennel-block washdown would use.

sources.title: Barn cleaner for solid floors | Lely Discovery Collector
sources.claim: The Lely Discovery Collector is a commercially sold autonomous robot that vacuums manure from barn floors and navigates among cows, alleys and gates on programmed routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing animal waste from the floor of an animal-housing facility with animals present. Shows autonomous waste pickup, but not the hosing, disinfecting, bedding and bowl work of a daily kennel clean.

sources.system: Allentown Activ Automation and Robotics Solution
sources.title: Automation Capabilities - Allentown
sources.claim: Allentown sells robotic cage-processing lines for laboratory animal facilities that scrape and dump soiled bedding, wash, dry and refill animal cages, tops, feeders and bottles under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning and disinfecting animal enclosures and husbandry equipment (cages, feeders, bottles). Same objects and soils as shelter carriers, transport cages and bowls, with the work conveyed to a fixed washing cell.

sources.title: Robotic Cage Handling System for Tunnel Washers - Getinge
sources.claim: Getinge supplies robotic cage handling systems that combine industrial robots with tunnel washers to process laboratory animal cages through cleaning in vivaria.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine washing of animal cages with robotic loading/unloading; the same fixtured, conveyor-fed cell would handle shelter carriers, transport cages and bowls.

sources.system: InterClean biosecurity truck wash and trailer washout systems
sources.title: Biosecurity Wash Systems For Farms and Transport Fleets
sources.claim: InterClean sells automated drive-through touchless wash systems with sanitizer arches that clean and disinfect livestock trailers, feed trucks and service vehicles, plus interior trailer washout systems that sanitize trailer interiors in under two minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing and disinfecting animal-transport vehicles fouled with manure. Same vehicle class and soils as an animal control truck, done in a purpose-built wash bay without manual pressure-washing.

sources.title: Tools and chemicals behind effective trailer washing | Fleet Maintenance
sources.claim: Istobal's HW'INTRAWASH is a mobile washing robot that enters a trailer and cleans and sanitizes the full interior of a 53-foot trailer in six minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated washing of a vehicle's cargo interior; the compartments of an animal control truck are the same kind of enclosed, hosed-out metal box.

sources.title: Avidbots releases floor-scrubbing robot for industrial spaces - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor scrubbers were deployed in over 1,000 units across more than a dozen countries as of 2023.

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals (Onshape case study)
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo floor-scrubbing robots operate autonomously in hospitals, airports, schools and other institutional buildings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine scrubbing/mopping of hard floors in an institutional building; a shelter's corridors, lobby and kennel aisles are the same floor-cleaning job in the same class of facility.

sources.title: Poultry Technology: Rise Of The Robots - Canadian Poultry Magazine
sources.claim: Octopus Poultry Safe is an autonomous robot that drives through poultry houses spraying disinfectants and sanitizers until the target area is covered.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of disinfectant inside an animal-housing building, the disinfection step of a kennel-block sanitation cycle.

tasks.label: Organize the adoption of unclaimed animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal shelter kennel ward: after the stray hold expires on an unclaimed dog or cat, the officer leashes/nets the animal out of its run, handles it for a temperament note and adoption photo, checks microchip/vaccination status, and creates the adoption listing in the shelter database and on Petfinder. Animals may be fearful, jumpy, or lightly reactive.

In-shelter meet-and-greet: a walk-in adopter is screened at the counter, then the officer retrieves the specific animal from the kennel, brings it to a visitation room or fenced yard, manages it on leash around strangers and children, reads its body language, answers questions, and counsels the family on fit (housing, other pets, kids).

Finalizing the adoption at the shelter lobby: verifying the adopter's ID and local licensing, completing and signing the adoption contract, collecting the fee, confirming spay/neuter, rabies and microchip registration, fitting a collar/tag, and safely loading the animal or carrier into the adopter's vehicle.

Off-site adoption event: crating and van-transporting several unclaimed animals to a pet-store parking lot, farmers' market, or community fair; setting up pens and signage; handling animals in a crowd of strangers and loose dogs for hours; then returning unadopted animals to the shelter.

Placement of long-stay or hard-to-place animals through partners: phoning/emailing breed rescues and transport groups, assembling health and behavior records, scheduling a transfer, and crating and loading animals into a partner's transport van at the shelter loading area.

Adopter follow-up and problem placements: conducting a home visit or yard/fence check at a private residence, delivering an animal to the adopter's home, or receiving a returned adoption and re-handling a stressed or behaviorally difficult animal.

sources.title: Tibot launches new poultry robot - Poultry News
sources.claim: The most capable robots working among live animals are barn-floor mobile robots that merely drive among poultry to stimulate movement; they do not catch, restrain, leash, or individually handle animals. Commercially deployed on hundreds of farms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation among live animals in an animal-housing facility. Cited to show the frontier of live-animal robotics is untouched locomotion around a flock, not individual restraint, leashing, presentation to a member of the public, or an adoption transaction; it therefore does not transfer to organizing adoptions.

sources.developer: research team reported via Ars Technica
sources.title: Humanoid Robots Controlled By Surgeons Did World-First Operation On Live Pigs - Slashdot
sources.claim: Dexterous manipulation performed on live animals by humanoid robots was achieved only under continuous remote human control, not autonomously, as of mid-2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic physical contact with a live animal. Even in a fully controlled, fixtured, anesthetized setting the manipulation was teleoperated, so it cannot support autonomous handling of a conscious shelter dog or cat.

sources.title: Robot cowboys: GrazeMate bets on fully autonomous cattle mustering drones
sources.claim: Autonomous aerial robots can move herds of livestock in open pasture by responding to animal behavior, but they influence animals at a distance and never handle an individual animal or interact with a customer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous machine control of live animal movement. Herding at a distance in open pasture involves no grasping, leashing, crating, or person-facing transaction, so it does not carry over to shelter adoption work.

tasks.label: Examine animal licenses, and inspect establishments housing animals for compliance with laws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine or renewal inspection of a licensed commercial animal establishment (boarding kennel, doggy daycare, pet shop, groomer): officer walks the runs and cage banks, measures enclosure sizes, checks sanitation, ventilation/temperature, food and water, isolation of sick animals, verifies the posted license and vaccination/intake records, opens gates and handles some animals, then discusses deficiencies with the operator and writes a compliance report.

Field verification of individual animal licenses and rabies tags: at doorsteps during canvassing, at complaint calls, at impound, or roadside - reading the tag on a collar, scanning a microchip, restraining the animal briefly, cross-checking the owner's paper certificate against agency records, and issuing a warning or citation for an unlicensed animal.

Complaint-driven or pre-license inspection of a private residence used as a hobby breeder, foster home, or small rescue: cluttered yard, garage, or basement housing; variable and often poor conditions; officer assesses shelter adequacy, body condition of animals, sanitation, and whether the number of animals exceeds permit limits, sometimes with an uncooperative owner present.

Inspection of an institutional animal-housing facility (municipal shelter, rescue organization, veterinary clinic, or other permitted animal facility) for compliance with state/local law: walk-through of holding areas and quarantine, review of disease-control protocols, euthanasia drug and disposition logs, staffing and license documentation, exit interview with management.

Inspection of temporary or outdoor animal venues and operations: pet adoption events, petting zoos, traveling exhibits/circuses, riding stables, backyard livestock premises, or an animal transport vehicle stopped for inspection - variable layouts taken as found, weather exposure, permits checked on site along with water, shade, tethering, and enclosure security.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Orbit/autonomous missions

Transfer is limited: Spot repeats a taught route in one instrumented plant and outputs sensor readings on fixed assets; it does not open enclosures, handle animals, examine license or vaccination paperwork, interview an operator, or render a legally defensible compliance determination, so it does not substantiate completion of an animal-establishment inspection at any tier.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection rounds in a structured human work facility. It shows legged robots can traverse plants and log asset condition, but the checked items are fixed industrial assets on a pre-mapped route, with no document/records examination, no animal handling, and no regulatory judgment, so it cannot stand in for a compliance inspection of an animal establishment.

It is the closest system to inspecting an establishment housing animals, but it is a permanently installed management tool on rails in one purpose-fitted barn that reports environmental metrics to the farmer; it does not examine licenses or records, cannot move between different establishments, and produces no compliance finding.

tasks.label: Conduct private investigations on a paid basis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Insurance/workers'-compensation or disability claim investigation: multi-hour covert stakeout from a parked vehicle on a residential street, discreet video of the claimant's activities, mobile follow when the subject drives to a gym, store or job site, then a time-stamped activity log, video evidence package and written report for the carrier.

Domestic/family case (infidelity, child custody, cohabitation): evening and weekend mobile surveillance through public streets, parking lots, restaurants and hotels; discreet photography and video of a specific named person; verification of addresses and companions; report and media delivered to the private client.

Background, due-diligence, asset or skip-trace investigation: office desk work querying proprietary and public databases, retrieving records at courthouses and county offices, phone/email verification with employers and references, corroborating identity, and drafting a compliant written report.

Litigation-support field work for attorneys or claims defense: driving to residences and businesses to canvass and knock on doors, taking recorded witness statements, photographing and measuring accident or incident scenes on roadsides and private property, and preparing a signed statement/scene documentation package.

Corporate/internal investigation on a client's premises: employee theft or policy-violation case in a warehouse, office or retail store — covert observation of staff, installing and reviewing covert cameras and CCTV, undercover shifts, interviewing employees, and a findings report supporting discipline or prosecution.

sources.title: Prevent Crime with Knightscope | Knightscope

sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous security patrol/monitoring on institution-controlled premises. It covers only the passive-observation sub-step of an on-premises investigation; it does not perform case intake, covert targeted observation of a named employee, interviews, or a legally defensible findings report, so it does not transfer to completing the whole investigation instance.

sources.system: Skydio X10 / X10D with Dock and Skydio Autonomy

instances.label: Retail asset-protection/store detective: working a chain store's sales floor and CCTV room during trading hours, watching customers, spotting selection-concealment behaviour, keeping continuous observation of a suspect to the exit, and capturing video/stills that document the complete theft sequence for apprehension or prosecution.

Retail internal-theft investigation: covert observation of employees at registers, stockrooms and loading docks (concealed camera plus POS exception video), building a documented case of employee theft or policy violation for an interview and prosecution package.

Insurance / workers' compensation / disability claimant surveillance: 6-10 hours parked in an unmarked vehicle on a residential street or in a shopping-centre lot, long-lens video and binoculars documenting the claimant's physical activity (yard work, lifting, driving), with a mobile follow if the subject leaves; output is time-stamped video plus a chronological activity log.

Domestic relations / child custody / legal-case mobile surveillance: discreetly following a subject on foot and by car through public streets, parking lots, restaurants and hotels, obtaining identifiable photos and video of who the subject meets, without being detected.

Client-premises watch at a business or institution (warehouse yard, office park, apartment complex, construction yard): monitoring the site for trespass, vandalism or after-hours theft and documenting any incident with usable video and vehicle/plate details for the client and police.

Fixed covert-camera surveillance of a location over days: siting and concealing a pole/covert camera covering a residence, rural property or business exterior, servicing it, then extracting and documenting the relevant comings and goings from the recorded footage.

instances.label: Cashier till audit in a retail store or restaurant: the loss-prevention investigator pulls a cash drawer at shift end or in a surprise spot-check, counts bills and coin by denomination in the back cash office, compares the total with the POS X/Z report and start bank, and records the over/short against the named cashier.

Client-site cash and records examination during an internal-theft/embezzlement engagement: count the safe, petty cash and prepared deposit bags at a client's business office, then match the counted cash to deposit slips, sales checks and bank records to quantify the shortage.

Desk review of transaction records at the investigator's or client's office: work through register tapes/electronic journals, void, refund and no-sale slips and sales checks for a period, verify totals and amounts, and identify shortages and suspicious patterns by cashier.

Undercover integrity shop / service audit: the investigator poses as a customer in a bar, restaurant or store, pays cash, observes whether the sale is rung into the register, then afterwards counts the register drawer against the tape to document skimming.

Field cash audits of unattended cash points on a route: coin and small-bill collections from vending, laundry, parking or amusement machines at scattered sites, counted on site or in the vehicle and reconciled against meter/counter readings.

tasks.label: Lock doors and gates of entrances and exits to secure buildings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Close-of-business lockup round in an office/commercial building: guard walks a route, pulls suite, stairwell, lobby and perimeter doors shut, throws deadbolts/turns keys from a key ring or secures badge-controlled doors, checks each door latched, secures side and loading exits.

Retail store or mall closing: guard locks storefront glass doors with keys, pulls down and padlocks roll-down security grilles, secures stockroom and rear/alley exits after last staff leave; hardware is worn and sometimes sticks.

School, hospital, campus or government facility lockup with a master key ring: locking classroom/wing doors, exterior egress doors, courtyard and athletic-field pedestrian gates; occupants may still be inside and doors are sometimes propped with wedges or chairs.

Warehouse/distribution or industrial site at shift end: lowering and locking overhead dock doors, locking man-doors, swinging chain-link perimeter vehicle gates shut and securing them with chain and padlock, outdoors in wind, rain, snow or darkness.

Mobile/contract patrol officer securing unattended sites (construction sites, vacant buildings, storage and equipment yards, parks): each site has different, often improvised or damaged hardware (hasps, chains, padlocks, plywood-covered openings), obstructed gate paths and no fixed layout.

tasks.label: Patrol industrial or commercial premises to prevent and detect signs of intrusion and ensure security of doors, windows, and gates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: After-hours interior patrol of a multi-tenant office or corporate building: walking mapped corridors, stairwells and lobbies on a tour route, confirming suites/server rooms and exterior doors are closed and latched, looking for propped doors, lights, people who should not be there, and logging checkpoints.

Night perimeter/yard patrol of an industrial site, warehouse or distribution center: driving or walking the fence line, dock doors and vehicle gates in weather and darkness, confirming gates are shut and locked, dock doors down, no cut fencing or trespassers, radioing findings to the dispatcher.

Patrol of a retail center, mall or mixed-use commercial property during open hours with the public present: circulating sales floors, parking structures and back-of-house corridors, checking stockroom/mechanical doors and emergency exits, deterring loitering and theft, responding to what is observed.

Patrol of a manufacturing plant, data center or utility facility, inside and on the grounds: fixed route past production areas, electrical rooms, substations and access-controlled doors, verifying doors/gates secured, badge-controlled areas unbreached, and reporting anomalies.

tasks.label: Respond to medical emergencies by administering basic first aid or by obtaining assistance from paramedics.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Minor injury inside an institution-controlled building (office tower, mall, warehouse, school, casino): an employee or visitor has a cut, scrape, minor burn, nosebleed, or twisted ankle. The guard walks to the person, retrieves the first-aid kit or AED cabinet supplies, cleans and dresses the wound or applies ice, judges whether further care is needed, offers reassurance, and writes the incident report.

A person collapses, faints, has a seizure, a diabetic or asthma episode, or chest pain in a lobby, concourse, store aisle, or garage. The guard responds within minutes, checks responsiveness/airway/breathing, positions the person (recovery position, loosens clothing), calls 911 and relays details, keeps bystanders back, props doors/holds an elevator, meets paramedics at the entrance, escorts them to the patient, and hands over what was observed.

Cardiac arrest in a guarded facility: unresponsive adult, not breathing normally. Guard starts chest compressions, sends someone for the wall-mounted AED or fetches it, bares the chest, places pads, follows AED prompts, continues CPR cycles until EMS takes over, then assists with the handoff.

Serious trauma at a controlled worksite, distribution center, event venue, or parking structure: fall from height, machinery or forklift injury, vehicle strike, or a stabbing. Guard controls severe bleeding with direct pressure, dressings or a tourniquet, keeps the patient still and warm, shields the scene, calls EMS, and secures the area until responders arrive.

Outdoor or public-facing patrol taken as found (public plaza, transit stop, apartment perimeter, construction site, hospital exterior grounds): guard finds an unresponsive or semi-conscious person, possibly intoxicated or overdosing, in variable weather, on uneven ground, with unpredictable bystanders. Guard assesses, may administer naloxone, places the person in recovery position, calls EMS, and stays until they arrive.

tasks.label: Answer alarms and investigate disturbances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: After-hours interior alarm at a corporate office, logistics facility, or data center: a door-forced/door-held-open, motion, or tailgating alarm annunciates at the guard desk. The officer walks or takes the elevator to the alarm point, checks the door and surrounding area, confirms no intruder, clears or escalates the alarm, and logs an incident report.

Outdoor perimeter or yard alarm at a fenced industrial, warehouse, utility, or solar site at night: fence-line sensor, gate-open, or camera analytic alert. The officer drives or walks the perimeter, illuminates and inspects the fence, gate and yard in darkness/weather, verifies whether an intruder or damage is present, and reports to the client or police.

Disturbance involving people during business hours at a retail store, mall, casino, or entertainment venue: EAS/shoplifting alarm, argument, intoxicated or unruly patron, refusal to leave. The officer approaches, assesses, verbally intervenes, escorts the person out or detains for police, recovers merchandise, and files a report.

Disturbance at a hospital, clinic, school, or university campus: agitated patient or visitor, code-gray call, fight in a hallway or ED. The officer responds on foot within minutes, de-escalates verbally, and may take hands-on control or assist clinical staff with a restraint, then documents the event.

Night alarm at an unattended outdoor property taken as found - construction site, contractor equipment yard, auto dealership lot, or vacant building. The officer responds, checks fence line, gates, trailers, doors and windows with a flashlight over uneven, cluttered ground, looks for signs of forced entry, theft or trespassers, and files a report; most such alarms are false.

Fire, panic-button, or other life-safety alarm inside a staffed facility: the officer reads the panel, proceeds to the zone, checks for smoke/fire or a person in distress, assists or directs occupants to evacuate, meets responding fire/EMS crews, and resets or silences the panel afterward.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial office building or corporate campus during occupied hours: the guard walks lobbies, floors, stairwells and internal garages among employees, contractors and visitors; verifies badges, watches for tailgating and propped doors, greets and directs people, notes hazards, and radios/logs anything abnormal. Shopping mall / retail center common areas and attached parking structures: the guard makes visible rounds of concourses, food court, entrances and garage decks among shoppers, deterring loitering, vehicle break-ins and vandalism, answering questions and reporting problems to the control room.

Inside a big-box, department or grocery store sales floor: the guard/loss-prevention officer walks aisles among shoppers, makes deliberate contact with suspected shoplifters, approaches and questions people, moves loiterers along, escorts offenders out or holds them for police, and intervenes in customer disputes.

Hospital, clinic, school or public/government building interior: the guard circulates through waiting rooms, corridors and cafeterias among patients, students, staff and the public; enforces rules, verbally de-escalates agitated or intoxicated individuals, assists staff with combative persons, and physically escorts people out.

Entertainment venue, bar/nightclub, casino gaming floor, stadium/concert event, or hotel corridor at night: the guard moves through dense, often intoxicated crowds, checks credentials, breaks up altercations, ejects patrons, handles noise and unruly-guest complaints, and manages crowd flow.

Outdoor grounds and parking of institution-controlled property with people present: gated apartment/HOA communities, corporate or industrial/logistics campuses, warehouses, utility yards, transit and parking facilities. The guard makes roving rounds among residents, employees and passengers, deters trespass, theft and vehicle break-ins, checks access points, and reports what is found.

instances.label: Retail store or shopping mall during trading hours: guard/loss-prevention officer observes a shoplifter or a person breaking store rules (open container, harassment, prior trespass ban), issues a warning, then physically stops, detains or escorts the person out and holds them for police; subject may resist.

Bar, nightclub, stadium or concert venue: bouncer/event guard tells an intoxicated, fighting or ticketless patron to stop or leave, then physically ejects them through a crowd, sometimes using restraining force and handing off to police.

Corporate office building or campus during business hours: guard confronts a tailgating/unbadged visitor, solicitor, protester or terminated employee in a lobby or restricted floor, warns them of the policy, verifies identity, and walks them off the property.

Hospital, school, courthouse or transit facility: guard warns an agitated visitor, patient or passenger violating rules (weapons, smoking, curfew, disruptive behavior), de-escalates verbally, and if that fails helps a team physically restrain or remove them.

After-hours patrol of an institution-controlled private site (industrial yard, data center, parking structure, closed retail center): guard finds a trespasser or loiterer, orders them off the property by voice, confirms they leave, logs the incident and calls police if they refuse.

Patrol of an unstructured outdoor property taken as found (active construction site, vacant lot, apartment-complex grounds, lot adjoining a public sidewalk): guard warns trespassers, loiterers, skateboarders or illegal dumpers and moves them along, mostly gaining voluntary compliance.

instances.label: Fixed entrance checkpoint at a courthouse, city hall, or federal/state office building: guard directs visitors to divest into bins, runs bags through an X-ray conveyor and reads the images, operates the walk-through metal detector, wands and hand-searches on alarm, physically takes custody of or turns away prohibited items (knives, pepper spray, tools), and handles arguments and non-compliant visitors during morning rush.

Stadium, arena, or large-event entry gates: guard staffs magnetometer or AI weapons-detection portals at outdoor/indoor gate banks, watches flag output, opens and hand-inspects bags against a clear-bag/prohibited-items policy, wands flagged patrons, confiscates bottles/weapons, in dense crowd surges and weather.

Corporate lobby, campus building, or hospital entrance: lower-volume visitor and staff screening with a walk-through detector or free-flow weapons-detection sensors plus handheld wand and bag inspection; guard combines screening with badge/visitor check-in and responds to alerts among patients, families, and employees.

K-12 school morning entry screening: students file through walk-through or OPENGATE-style detectors with backpacks; staff/guard resolves nuisance alerts (laptops, binders, water bottles), opens and searches flagged backpacks, and confiscates prohibited items, all within a short arrival window.

Nightclub, bar, or concert door: guard/bouncer wands patrons in the entry queue, performs hands-on pat-downs and purse/bag searches for weapons and drugs, judges intoxication, and physically refuses entry to people who fail screening or resist.

Employee/contractor entry or exit screening at a warehouse, plant, correctional facility, or airport worker checkpoint: a compliant, badged population divests into trays at a fixed portal, passes a metal-detection or millimeter-wave portal and turnstile, with random or alarm-driven bag/locker checks for contraband or theft.

instances.label: Interior rounds at a fixed commercial or institutional site (office tower, hospital, school, data center): on each patrol the guard verifies that access-control readers, door contacts/locks, CCTV cameras and housings, emergency exits, duress buttons and extinguishers are in place and functioning, looks for pried doors, defeated latches, covered or turned lenses, makes minor corrections (secure a propped door, clear an obstruction, reset a device) and logs exceptions to the control room.

Exterior/perimeter rounds at an institution-controlled site (industrial plant, logistics yard, utility substation, corporate campus, storage facility): inspect fence line, gates and barrier arms, padlocks and seals, lighting, cameras and call boxes; detect cut fabric, ladders, cut or swapped locks, dislodged or blinded cameras, dead lights; re-secure gates, clear obstructions, and report defects. Night and all weather.

Screening checkpoint equipment checks (courthouse, stadium, government building, airport): power up the walk-through metal detector and x-ray unit, run the required daily operational test with test pieces/OTK, confirm alarms and image quality, check handheld wands and batteries, adjust sensitivity/settings, and complete the test log before opening the lane.

Scheduled functional testing and adjustment of alarm and access-control devices around a facility: trigger duress buttons, door contacts and motion sensors, confirm signal receipt at the panel/console, reset devices, adjust door closers/strikes and camera aim, swap batteries, and document the test.

Contract mobile patrol across multiple, varying client sites (construction sites, vacant buildings, retail strips, residential complexes, equipment yards): at each stop check alarm boxes, padlocks and seals, camera housings, light towers and generators, look for pry marks, cut locks, painted lenses or unplugged equipment, re-secure what can be re-secured, and file a site report.

tasks.label: Escort or drive motor vehicle to transport individuals to specified locations or to provide personal protection.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Controlled facility (corporate HQ, data center, plant, hospital, government building): the guard meets a vendor, contractor, or visitor at reception, checks them in, then walks them through mapped interior corridors and elevators to a specified work area or meeting room, keeps them inside permitted areas during the visit, and walks them back out. Cooperative subject, fixed layout, business or after-hours conditions.

Night escort on foot: a nurse, office worker, student, or closing retail clerk asks to be walked from a building exit across an institution-owned surface lot or parking structure to their parked car. Dark, uneven lighting, moving vehicles, occasional loiterers; the guard walks alongside at the person's pace, scans surroundings, waits until the person is in the car and moving, and radios dispatch if anything goes wrong.

Guard drives a marked patrol vehicle, van, or cart to transport an individual to a specified location: a staff member ending a night shift taken to a remote lot, a student using the campus safe-ride line taken to a dorm or nearby address, an employee moved between buildings. Site roads plus adjacent public streets, night traffic, weather.

Escorting an uncooperative person: a trespasser, intoxicated patron, agitated visitor, or terminated employee walked off the premises, or a detained shoplifter kept escorted until police arrive. Requires command presence, verbal de-escalation, and the possibility of hands-on control or restraint.

Close personal protection: the guard accompanies an executive, physician, celebrity, or dignitary on foot through lobbies, sidewalks, garages, and public venues and drives them between sites, screening surroundings, managing crowds, and interposing between the principal and any threat.

instances.label: Control-room console watch in an office tower, hospital or campus building: guard sits at the building-automation-system (BAS) workstation, watches HVAC/boiler/chiller alarms and space temperatures, acknowledges alarms, nudges setpoints or issues overrides, and logs actions during the shift.

Mechanical/boiler room round during patrol: guard walks the plant rooms, reads pressure/temperature gauges and the boiler water-level glass, confirms pumps, fans and chillers are running, checks for abnormal heat, noise or leaks, and records readings on a log sheet, flagging anomalies to engineering.

Hands-on adjustment at the equipment: guard turns a thermostat or dial, opens/closes a valve, throws a switch or breaker, repositions a damper, or resets a tripped unit in a mechanical room or tenant space, then verifies the system responds.

Scheduled after-hours start/stop in a school, church, arena or office: guard turns HVAC zones and lighting on before an early event or off at closing using wall panels, timeclock overrides or switchgear, on a fixed routine.

Off-hours alarm response: a boiler low-water, high-temperature or chiller fault alarm sounds at night; the guard goes to the equipment, assesses it, takes the prescribed action (silence/shut down/isolate), and escalates to the on-call building engineer.

roles.title: Crossing Guards and Flaggers
roles.description: Guide or control vehicular or pedestrian traffic at such places as streets, schools, railroad crossings, or construction sites.

tasks.label: Direct or escort pedestrians across streets, stopping traffic, as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elementary-school crossing at an uncontrolled or stop-controlled intersection on a public street during the AM/PM peak: guard steps into the roadway with a handheld STOP paddle, halts vehicles from two or more approaches, escorts groups of children (some running, on scooters/bikes), watches for turning and distracted drivers, works in rain, glare and darkness.

Mid-block or T-intersection marked school crosswalk on a residential/collector street: lighter but continuous traffic, guard must judge and create gaps in moving traffic, escort small groups including parents with strollers and cyclists, then return to the curb.

Signalized multi-lane arterial crossing near a middle/high school or transit stop: guard reinforces the walk phase, physically holds right-turning and left-turning vehicles, escorts children plus elderly or mobility-impaired pedestrians across a wide crossing within the signal cycle.

Construction/utility work-zone flagger on a public street: routes pedestrians around a closed sidewalk and across the roadway through a shifting temporary layout, stopping vehicles and coordinating with truck and equipment movements and lane closures.

Crossing on institution-controlled premises: school driveway/parking-lot crossing at dismissal, or campus/stadium lot during event egress, where the institution controls the premises, the layout is fixed and the vehicles present are those it admits.

tasks.label: Guide or control vehicular or pedestrian traffic at such places as street and railroad crossings and construction sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School crossing guard at a marked crosswalk on a public street near an elementary school: steps into the roadway with a hand-held STOP paddle, halts approaching and turning vehicles, holds and escorts groups of children (some running, on scooters/bikes) across, waves late arrivals back, works two short shifts in rain, snow, glare and darkness.

Flagger on a two-lane rural/suburban road lane closure: stationed at one end of a one-lane section, alternates traffic with a STOP/SLOW paddle, coordinates by radio with the flagger at the other end, releases queues, admits work vehicles and emergency vehicles, over a multi-hour shift with no driveways or side roads inside the zone.

Flagger at an urban/suburban construction or utility site access point: stops street traffic to let dump trucks and mixers in and out of a driveway, hand-signals backing trucks, holds sidewalk pedestrians, cyclists and residents' cars, and coordinates continuously with the crew in a changing, congested work area.

Flagger controlling a busy intersection or multi-lane arterial approach: directs several conflicting movements by hand during a signal outage, staged construction, or special event, admits construction equipment across traffic, and coordinates with police and other flaggers.

Crossing watch at a highway-rail grade crossing on a public street: stops road vehicles and pedestrians while trains or maintenance equipment occupy or approach the crossing, e.g., during a warning-system outage or track work.

Traffic control inside an institution-controlled facility: quarry, plant yard, port terminal, or school parking lot, stopping and releasing trucks and cars at a fixed entry/checkpoint and holding them for crossing pedestrians or equipment.

tasks.label: Monitor traffic flow to locate safe gaps through which pedestrians can cross streets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elementary/middle school crossing guard posted at a marked crosswalk on a residential or collector street during morning arrival and afternoon dismissal: watches two-way traffic approaching from both directions, estimates vehicle speeds and closing distances, and identifies a gap long enough for a group of several children (some slow-moving) to clear the roadway.

Guard at a signalized or multi-leg intersection: monitors the signal phase plus vehicles turning right-on-red or left across the crosswalk, watches for red-light runners and rolling stops, and determines the moment when the conflicting movements are actually clear rather than merely permitted by the signal.

Flagger at a construction/utility work zone where the sidewalk is closed and pedestrians must be routed across or along a live travel lane: tracks one-lane alternating traffic, dump trucks and equipment entering and leaving the site, and the other flagger's releases to spot a usable gap for pedestrians.

Degraded-visibility conditions on a busy multi-lane arterial: rain, snow, fog, pre-dawn darkness, or low-sun glare, with sightlines blocked by parked cars, stopped school buses, or queued vehicles; the worker must judge gaps with partial and intermittent views of oncoming traffic.

Occasional postings such as special events, parade or game-day routes, railroad grade crossings, and school parking lots/drop-off loops: monitoring irregular, low-speed but unpredictable vehicle flow (including reversing vehicles) to find gaps for pedestrians.

tasks.label: Communicate traffic and crossing rules and other information to students and adults.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Direct traffic movement or warn of hazards, using signs, flags, lanterns, and hand signals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fixed one-lane, two-way alternating control at a work zone on a two-lane public road (paving, utility cut, bridge repair): the worker stands at one end of the closure with a STOP/SLOW paddle, coordinates by radio with a second flagger at the other end, releases and holds platoons for hours, day or night, in live public traffic.

Active short-duration work zone in mixed urban/suburban street traffic: the worker stops and releases traffic on demand as dump trucks, excavators and utility rigs enter and back into the work area, waves vehicles around a shifting operation and past driveways, and keeps pedestrians and cyclists clear of the work.

School crossing post on a public street or intersection: at arrival and dismissal the guard steps into the roadway with a hand-held STOP paddle, halts through and turning vehicles, signals children when to cross, and reacts to drivers who roll through, block the crosswalk or fail to stop.

Fixed vehicle control point on institution-controlled premises: a construction-site or plant entrance, quarry/port haul road, or parking-structure ramp where the worker signals one vehicle at a time to stop or proceed through a single controlled lane past a known, fixed conflict point.

Event and lot traffic marshalling on institution-controlled premises (stadium, fairground, school or mall lot, funeral procession staging): the worker uses flags and hand signals to wave surging streams of cars into rows, aisles and exits, changing the pattern as the lot fills.

Highway–rail grade crossing duty on a public road: warning and stopping road traffic when trains approach (crossing watch, or temporary crossing protection during rail or roadway work), using flags, lanterns at night and hand signals.

instances.label: Freeway/expressway lane closure: a traffic-control crew distributes 80-300+ traffic cones from a moving truck along a taper and tangent at MUTCD spacing, in the shoulder/closed lane adjacent to live high-speed traffic, often at night.

Urban arterial or rural two-lane road closure for paving, striping or utility work: cones and delineators laid along the closure line from a truck moving through the work area, past driveways, intersections and parked vehicles.

Advance-warning sign package for a work zone: unloading folded roll-up signs and tripod/A-frame stands from the truck and erecting them upright at spaced points on grass, gravel or paved shoulders (ROAD WORK AHEAD, FLAGGER AHEAD, etc.), adding flags and sandbag ballast.

Small hand-set job: the flagger walks out a dozen cones, delineators and a sidewalk-closed barricade around an excavation, bucket truck or driveway, threading between curbs, parked cars and pedestrians on a public street.

School crossing: the guard carries portable in-street pedestrian signs, A-frame school-crossing signs and cones from a storage box or vehicle to the crosswalk, sets them at designated points before duty, and removes them afterward on a public street.

Flagging on institutionally controlled premises (quarry, plant yard, port terminal, closed airfield project): cones and delineators placed along a defined internal haul route or lane on a site whose owner controls access and keeps the surface to a working standard.

tasks.label: Stop speeding vehicles to warn drivers of traffic laws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School crossing guard at a marked crosswalk near an elementary school: a car approaches above the 15-25 mph school-zone limit; the guard steps off the curb into the travel lane with a handheld STOP paddle and hand/whistle signals to halt it, then tells the driver the school-zone limit and points out children, waves the car on, and may note the plate for the school or police. Public street, mixed traffic, all weather.

Two-lane rural/suburban highway work zone flagger controlling alternating one-way traffic: a vehicle closes on the taper too fast; the flagger, standing in or beside the travel lane with a STOP/SLOW paddle and high-visibility gear, stops the vehicle, advises the driver of the reduced work-zone speed limit and of workers and equipment ahead, then releases it through the zone.

Urban street utility or construction flagger at a lane closure or site driveway: stops speeding through-traffic to warn about the posted work-zone speed and trucks entering, while simultaneously managing pedestrians, cyclists, parked cars, driveways and cross-street turns.

Night, dusk, glare or bad-weather stop (rain, fog, snow): guard or flagger uses an illuminated paddle, flashlight or wand to detect and halt a speeding vehicle with poor sight lines and reduced driver reaction time, then delivers the speed-law warning at the window.

Noncompliant or hostile driver: the vehicle ignores the paddle and signals, forcing the guard/flagger to abort the stop, retreat out of the lane, record the vehicle description and plate and radio the crew, police or school; or the driver stops but argues, requiring de-escalation before release.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-street admonishment of road users who break traffic rules. It shows an embodied machine autonomously detecting a violation and delivering the spoken traffic-law warning that is the point of this task; it does not halt a moving motor vehicle, so it covers only the warning element once a vehicle has been brought to a stop.

In a purpose-built lane the gate performs the physical 'stop the vehicle' element under machine control, triggered by lane detection, which is how an E1 setting would present a speeding vehicle, stopped, to a warning robot.

sources.transferJustification: Same task family: halting road traffic in a live work zone. Cited as a negative - the only fielded roadside machines that stop traffic require a human flagger operating them cycle-by-cycle, and they neither single out speeders nor speak to drivers.

sources.title: Crossing guard robot: What to know - NBC Bay Area
sources.claim: CrossBot, a Fresno State research robot equipped with lidar, radar, cameras, speaker and screen, drives into a school-zone intersection and signals pedestrians when it is safe to ...; it is a prototype meant to fill in when a crossing guard is unavailable and does not stop speeding motorists or warn their drivers.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic analogue to the school crossing guard role on a public street. It is a prototype that guides pedestrians only; nothing in it flags down a speeding car or delivers a roadside warning, so it supports the negative judgment at E3.

instances.label: Lane-closure work zone on a state highway or arterial: a driver slows or pulls up to the flagger and asks where the closed route goes; the flagger tells them the detour (e.g., 'take the next right onto Main, follow the orange signs') and points down the detour path while traffic continues past.

Full road closure on a residential or downtown street: the flagger stationed at the closure point turns back each approaching vehicle and explains the posted detour route, repeating the same verbal directions dozens of times per shift to local and through traffic.

Night or adverse-weather highway detour onto a crossover/diversion: the flagger conveys the routing to approaching drivers with illuminated paddle/wand gestures and shouted or brief verbal instructions over traffic noise, in low visibility.

Access questions from residents, business patrons, and delivery drivers whose destination is inside or beyond the closure: the flagger explains an individualized way around the work area (which side street is open, where to park, when the block reopens).

Special vehicles - emergency responders, school buses, transit, oversize/overweight trucks - needing routing guidance around the work zone; the flagger relays the route verbally or by radio, sometimes coordinating with the crew or police before answering.

tasks.label: Patrol or monitor recreational areas, such as trails, slopes, or swimming areas, on foot, in vehicles, or from towers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Public/community pool or municipal aquatic center: lifeguard sits an elevated chair or stands a deck station, scans an assigned zone of clear water on a 10/20 pattern, rotates stations, walks the deck, watches crowded shallow water and slides, enforces rules.

Ocean/surf beach: guard scans a swim zone from an elevated tower and patrols the shoreline on foot, in an ATV or truck; surf, glare, wind-blown sand, dense crowds, shifting rip currents, swimmers drifting outside the flags.

Inland open water (state-park lake beach, camp waterfront, reservoir/river swim area): watch from shore or tower plus patrol by rescue board, kayak or small boat over a buoyed area; murky water, weeds, boat traffic.

Ski patrol during operating hours: skiing assigned runs and riding a snowmobile to monitor guests, spot fallen or injured skiers, check rope lines, closures and boundaries, in cold, wind, flat light and falling snow.

Ski patrol pre-opening / post-storm slope check: scouting runs, closed courses and off-piste avalanche terrain for hazards and instability before the area opens, reporting which terrain can be opened.

Park and recreation grounds patrol: covering trails, bike paths, campgrounds, picnic areas and boardwalks on foot or in a UTV/patrol vehicle, watching for visitors in trouble, hazards and rule violations, and being visibly present.

tasks.label: Rescue distressed persons, using rescue techniques and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal/community pool or waterpark: guard spots a conscious distressed or actively drowning swimmer (often a child) among a crowd, enters the water with a rescue tube, controls the panicking victim, tows them to the wall or shallow water, and removes them from the pool to the deck for assessment.

Indoor or outdoor aquatic facility: submerged, unresponsive victim on the bottom of a deep pool; guard performs a surface/feet-first dive, brings the inert body to the surface, tows to the wall, and extricates (with backboard if spinal injury suspected) to the deck where staff take over.

Surf beach: rip-current rescue of one or several conscious swimmers in breaking waves, wind and current, using rescue tube and swim, rescue board, or personal watercraft; secure victim(s), keep them afloat, and bring them through the surf to the sand.

Inland lake, reservoir, or summer-camp waterfront with murky water and a marked swim area: distressed swimmer near a dock or raft, or a swimmer who has gone under and must be located and brought up (line/rescue-boat search), then brought to dock or shore.

Ski resort in-bounds groomed run: patroller responds to a fallen, injured skier/snowboarder, secures the scene, assesses and splints/packages the patient, loads them into a rescue toboggan, and sleds them down variable snow to the base aid room.

Off-piste, tree-well, avalanche debris, cliff-band, or stalled-chairlift rescue: patroller reaches the subject in deep snow or steep exposed terrain in poor weather, digs out/extricates or performs a rope/lift evacuation, packages the patient and evacuates to a transfer point.

tasks.label: Contact emergency medical personnel in case of serious injury.

tasks.label: Examine injured persons and administer first aid or cardiopulmonary resuscitation, if necessary, using training and medical supplies and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pool or waterpark lifeguard treats a minor injury at the deck or guard-station first-aid kit: scraped knee from a wet deck, cut foot, bloody nose, bee sting, minor burn. Guard sizes up the patron (often a child), dons gloves, cleans the wound, controls bleeding, applies antiseptic and an adhesive dressing or ice pack, checks for further injury, and records the incident.

Aquatic facility emergency: an unresponsive or near-drowning patron is brought onto a wet pool deck. Guard performs a primary assessment (responsiveness, airway, breathing, pulse), positions the head, delivers rescue breaths with a pocket mask or bag-valve mask, starts chest compressions, applies AED pads and follows prompts, manages vomit/water in the airway and possible spinal injury, and continues until EMS takes over.

Open-water/beach lifeguard on sand or in the surf line: assesses and treats jellyfish or stingray stings, surfboard-fin lacerations, heat exhaustion, near-drowning, or a suspected spinal injury in shallow breaking waves, using a small kit and oxygen, amid wind, sand, glare, tide and a crowd of bystanders.

Ski patroller reaches a fallen skier or rider on a run, in trees, or off the groomed edge: performs a hands-on assessment through bulky winter clothing (suspected femur/tibia fracture, shoulder dislocation, head or spinal injury, hypothermia), applies a cervical collar, traction or vacuum splint, controls bleeding, insulates the patient, and packages them into a toboggan, in cold, wind, snow and on a slope.

Patient brought into a ski-area aid room, camp/amusement-park first-aid room, or facility treatment station: secondary assessment on a treatment table, vital signs, wound cleaning and dressing or suturing-adjacent care, splinting, ice and monitoring, decisions about release versus ambulance transport, and documentation.

It touches the 'examine injured persons' half of the task in outdoor, unstructured mock-disaster settings, but it is sensing-only scoring of triage category, with no palpation, wound care, splinting, ventilation or compressions, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task at any tier.

tasks.label: Maintain quality of pool water by testing chemical levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal/community aquatic center (indoor or outdoor): lifeguard on rotation draws a water sample at poolside every 1-2 hours, runs DPD free/combined chlorine and pH tests with a test kit, records results on the health-department log, and adjusts the feeder setpoint or notifies the pool operator when readings drift.

Hotel/resort/apartment or HOA pool with an attached spa: attendant or lifeguard tests both bodies several times per day (spa chemistry swings fast under heat and bather load), logs readings for inspection, and corrects sanitizer/pH.

Waterpark or multi-body aquatic complex (wave pool, lazy river, slide catch pools, splash pad): staff sample each body of water through the operating day, compare manual DPD results against equipment-room controller readings, and adjust dosing for peak bather loads.

School/college/YMCA indoor pool, routine shift chemistry: free and combined chlorine, pH and temperature checks each shift with a test kit or photometer, logged, with liquid acid/chlorine feed corrections.

School/college/YMCA indoor pool, periodic full panel: weekly/monthly total alkalinity, calcium hardness and cyanuric acid tests by titration/photometer, followed by hand additions of granular products (bicarbonate, calcium chloride, stabilizer, shock) and re-testing.

Small seasonal camp or neighborhood pool with basic equipment (erosion tablet feeder, little or no automation): lifeguard tests chlorine and pH before opening and periodically during the day, hand-doses chemicals, and keeps the paper log.

sources.system: Approved automatic chemical monitoring and control systems (e.g., BECS, ProMinent, Pentair controllers on county-approved lists)
sources.developer: Multiple manufacturers; acceptance set by California Dept. of Public Health / county enforcing agents
sources.title: Cal. Code Regs. Tit. 22, § 65523 - Operation Records
sources.claim: California's public-pool regulation permits the mandatory daily disinfectant-residual and pH tests of record to be performed by an approved, calibrated automatic chemical monitoring and ... rather than by a person, establishing that machine testing is accepted output at public pools.

sources.system: Automatic chemical controllers (probe + controller + chemical feed pumps) on public spas
sources.developer: Multiple manufacturers; requirement set by Ohio Department of Health
sources.title: Ohio Admin. Code 3701-31-04 - Responsibilities of the licensee
sources.claim: Ohio's pool code requires every public spa to have an automatic chemical controller that continuously senses pH and disinfectant level and regulates the dosing rate to hold them in range - unattended machine testing plus correction is the legal norm at these venues.

sources.system: BECSys5 / BECSys7 water chemistry controllers with BECSys Alkalinity Meter

sources.claim: BECS Technology's BECSys5/BECSys7 commercial controllers, with the BECSys Alkalinity Meter, automatically measure pool total alkalinity and switch dosing between acid and CO2 to hold TA and pH at operator setpoints, removing routine manual bicarbonate testing and additions.

sources.system: BECS CP-1 Free Chlorine/Bromine sensor with BECSys controllers
sources.title: CP-1 Free Chlorine-Bromine Sensor - Aquatics International
sources.claim: BECS's CP-1 sensor gives BECSys controllers a direct free chlorine/bromine ppm residual reading (not merely ORP), so the controller measures the same parameter a lifeguard measures with a DPD kit and doses against a ppm setpoint.

sources.title: Swimming Pool Automation Controllers - Chloramine Consulting
sources.claim: Industry technical source states that chemical automation is the norm rather than the exception at US commercial pools, which are run around the clock on controller-driven sensing and dosing.

sources.title: PC6000 Chemtrol Chemical and Filter/Pump Integrated Controller - Poolweb
sources.claim: Chemtrol PC6000 integrated controllers automatically control pH/ORP/free-chlorine dosing and filtration and are supplied for commercial aquatic facilities, waterparks, universities and hotels - the multi-body venues of instance 3.

sources.system: WaterGuru SENSE S2/S3 with C5 cassette

sources.claim: The Sutro floating monitor autonomously draws pool/spa water and runs reagent-based pH, free chlorine and total alkalinity tests three times a day, reporting results and dosing instructions - autonomous wet-chemistry testing in a pool taken as found.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: residential pool/spa chemistry testing. Same analytes (FC, pH, TA) and same reagent chemistry as a lifeguard's test kit, performed unattended on unmodified pool water, so the sampling-and-testing capability transfers to a poolside grab sample.
