tasks.label: Instruct participants in skiing, swimming, or other recreational activities and provide safety precaution information.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal or community indoor/outdoor pool: lifeguard on duty explains facility rules and safety precautions to arriving patrons and school/camp groups — depth markings, diving and breath-holding rules, slide and diving-board procedures, buddy system, non-swimmer wristbands — and answers patron questions verbally from the deck.

Ocean or lake beach: lifeguard briefs swimmers, waders, and surfers on rip currents, the flag/warning system, surf and tide conditions, designated swim areas, and marine hazards; gives short informational talks to beachgoers and youth groups at the tower or on the sand.

Waterpark or amusement attraction: ride/slide attendant instructs each rider group before dispatch — how to board the tube or mat, required body position, hand placement, height and health restrictions, mandatory life-jacket use — repeating the same briefing many times per hour.

Ski area: ski patroller or mountain-safety host delivers on-hill safety instruction to skiers and snowboarders — Your Responsibility Code, slow zones, terrain-park smart rules, closures, avalanche/weather and lift-safety warnings — at the base area, lift lines, and on trails, in cold and variable weather.

Learn-to-swim / water-safety session: lifeguard leads a beginner swim or water-safety class for children or adults, demonstrating floating, kicking, and basic strokes, distributing kickboards, and coaching learners in shallow water, occasionally steadying a nervous beginner.

Camp waterfront, marina, or rafting outfitter: worker gives a pre-launch orientation to paddlers — fitting and checking PFDs, paddle grip and strokes, capsize/self-rescue procedure, boundaries and signals — to a small mixed-experience group before they go on the water.

tasks.label: Inspect recreational equipment, such as rope tows, T-bars, J-bars, or chair lifts, for safety hazards and damage or wear.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pool lifeguard's pre-opening / shift-change safety check at a municipal, school, or hotel aquatic facility: walk the deck and check rescue tubes, ring buoys, backboard and straps, spineboard head blocks, first-aid kit and AED, lifeguard stand, ladders and rails (tug/wiggle for looseness), diving board and fulcrum, starting blocks, lane-line reels, and secured/undamaged main-drain covers visible through the water; log findings and tag anything worn or broken out of service.

Waterpark / pool-slide attendant or head guard pre-opening ride check: inspect flume sections and joints for cracks, gouges, protruding fasteners or gel-coat wear; check tube/mat condition and inflation, restraint straps and handles, run-out pool depth and catch nets, dispatch gates, stairs and railings, and water flow at the slide head before the ride is cleared to open.

Ski area lift operator / lift mechanic daily pre-opening check at the drive and return terminals: inspect gearbox, motor, bull wheel, brakes and brake pads, hydraulic lines and oil levels, safety switches and gates, loading/unloading ramps and carpets, terminal sheave trains and grips passing through, listening for abnormal noise and looking for leaks, ice buildup, and worn components inside the terminal building/machine room.

Line check of the lift itself on the mountainside: ride the chair or traverse the lift line by snowmobile/ski, inspecting each tower's sheave assemblies, liners, catchers and deropement guards, tower hardware and alignment, the haul rope's position and condition (splices, broken wires, corrosion), chairs/T-bars/J-bars, restraint bars, and rope-tow rope and splices — outdoors in cold, wind, snow, flat light, and variable snowpack.

Beach or open-water lifeguard's equipment check at a public beach or lakefront: inspect rescue boards and tubes, fins, torpedo buoys, backboard, tower/stand structure and ladder, warning flags and signage, buoy/swim-area lines and anchors, and the rescue ATV or watercraft, in sand, salt spray, and public-access conditions before and during the shift.

Other recreational venues: camp challenge-course/zipline hardware (harnesses, carabiners, cable, trolleys), climbing-wall holds and belay gear, ice-rink boards and skate-rental blades, tubing-hill conveyor 'magic carpet' and tow rope, marina rental boats/PFDs, or skate-park ramps — a mixed set of gear and structures checked for wear, cracks, fraying, or damage and tagged out if unsafe.

sources.system: Spot (Boston Dynamics) with Spot Cam/thermal + acoustic payloads and Orbit route autonomy
sources.title: Boston Dynamics' robot dog patrols 1.5 million-square-foot factory
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot is deployed inside a 1.5-million-sq-ft aerospace manufacturing plant, autonomously patrolling routes and inspecting critical machinery with thermal and acoustic payloads to find overheating, abnormal vibration, and leaks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine condition inspection of powered machinery (motors, gearboxes, pressure vessels) on a fixed round inside a controlled facility. A ski-lift drive/return terminal machine room presents the same class of assets and the same check (hot bearings, abnormal noise, leaks, visible wear), so performance carries over to the terminal portion of lift inspection.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics sells Spot thermal inspection as scheduled autonomous rounds with alarm thresholds and trending, i.e. automated detection of degrading equipment, not just image capture.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: automated condition assessment of fixed plant equipment on a repeating route, which is the machinery-condition half of a lift terminal inspection.

sources.transferJustification: Demonstrated flights covered snow generators, slope sections and infrastructure zones at a working ski resort; ropeway inspection flights are the same platform, same site, same sensors (8x optical zoom plus thermal) applied to lift towers and rope line, so the outdoor alpine capability transfers to the lift-line check.

sources.system: SCARA captures alpine drone system at Melchsee-Frutt
sources.title: Drones for Inspection and Monitoring - Seilbahnen International
sources.claim: The same alpine drone deployment produced condition assessments of resort infrastructure judged reliable and time-saving in daily operations.

sources.title: Percepto gains nationwide US waiver to remotely deploy and operate automated drones for critical infrastructure monitoring
sources.claim: Percepto's autonomous drone-in-a-box systems run inspection missions with no on-site pilot at utility, oil and gas, solar and mining sites, and hold an FAA nationwide BVLOS waiver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended, repeat visual/thermal inspection of outdoor fixed infrastructure (towers, lines, plant) for defects. Comparable objects (steel towers, cables, machinery) and comparable inspection judgments to a lift-line tower and haul-rope check.

sources.system: reflectCONTROL Automotive robotic surface-defect inspection system

This is the E1 counterfactual for checking recreational gear (boards, tubes, flume panels, hardware) for cracks, gouges and surface wear once the item is fixtured and conveyed to the inspection station.

sources.title: Automotive Automatic Paint Defect Inspection System
sources.claim: The robotic paint-defect inspection system is installed in production plants, e.g. Daimler's Sindelfingen plant, integrated into the conveyor line that presents each body to the robots.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the fixtured, conveyor-fed robotic inspection cell is a real production deployment, supporting E1-level completion of item-by-item damage/wear inspection.

tasks.label: Inspect recreational facilities for cleanliness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Indoor municipal/YMCA aquatic center: lifeguard makes opening, hourly and closing rounds — walks the pool deck checking for trash, hair, bandaids, spilled drinks and slip hazards; checks water clarity and floating/bottom debris; empties skimmer baskets; checks locker rooms, restrooms and showers for soiling and supply issues; logs findings on a facility checklist and reports items needing custodial follow-up.

Outdoor hotel/resort, community or water-park pool complex: lifeguard inspects pool basin and surface for leaves and debris, deck and lounge-chair areas for cups, towels and glass, splash pad and slide run-outs, trash barrels, and adjacent restrooms/changing rooms; conditions include sun, wind-blown litter and continuous patron traffic.

Ocean or lake beach lifeguard: walks or drives an assigned beach section before and during the shift, scanning sand and shoreline for litter, broken glass, fish hooks, dead marine life, dog waste and overflowing barrels; removes or flags hazards and radios cleanup crews; terrain, tide line and crowd density change daily.

Ski area patroller: checks base lodge, warming huts, on-mountain restrooms and lift-line/loading areas for trash, spilled food and debris, and sweeps trailside rest stops and picnic decks for litter; done in cold, snow, gloved, often on skis between other duties.

Other recreation venues (campground, park playground/skate park, marina and boat launch, ropes course, rec-center gym): daily grounds walk checking picnic areas, equipment, docks and restrooms for litter, broken glass and soiling; removes small debris and files maintenance/custodial requests.

sources.title: Orbit 5.0 adds features to Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped robot — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped autonomously patrols facilities on fixed routes and, with Orbit 5.0, automatically flags visual anomalies such as debris and spills from captured imagery, replacing clipboard walkthrough inspections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility inspection rounds in industrial plants. It is the same act as a cleanliness walkthrough — traverse a fixed route through a human work facility, image defined points, flag debris/spills/missing items, and log the result to a report — with the same target objects (litter, spills) and no fine manipulation required.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Spot's autonomous inspection use expanded in 2025 from equipment checks to whole-facility rounds at named industrial customers, with patrol missions that pause and alert when people are detected.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment maturity and whole-facility (not single-asset) scope for the autonomous inspection rounds cited above.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot autonomously drives scheduled and ad-hoc routes through occupied corporate facilities performing security patrols and facility checks, escalating detected anomalies to a monitoring team.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: indoor patrol and facility condition checks. The traversal, perception and exception-reporting loop is the same one a cleanliness walkthrough requires, performed in facilities occupied by people.

sources.system: Cobalt Robotics security robot (leak and spill detection)
sources.title: Security Robot: New Spill and Leak Detection Technology | Buildings
sources.claim: Cobalt's autonomously patrolling indoor robots include sensing that detects leaks and spills in defined areas and notifies a specialist for follow-up.
sources.transferJustification: Spills and wet floors are the specific defects a pool-deck or lobby cleanliness round looks for; this shows the detect-and-report step is automated in occupied buildings.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's autonomous bathroom cleaning robot is deployed in hospitals and airports, where it enters restrooms during operating hours and cleans fixtures and floors and picks up trash.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restroom cleaning in public facilities. It covers the locker-room/restroom leg of the inspection round — the robot navigates to and inside restrooms, opens doors, perceives soiling and trash, and brings them to standard.

sources.title: Avidbots Neo Cleaning Robot Used by Many of the Newly Named Top Cleanest Global Airports
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor scrubber ... deployed at many of the world's busiest and cleanest airports, navigating large public terminals amid crowds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: floor cleaning of large human-occupied facilities. Demonstrates reliable autonomous coverage of an entire public facility floorplan among patrons — the traversal demand of a cleanliness round in a rec center or aquatic center.

sources.system: Dolphin Wave 60/80/90i commercial robotic pool cleaners
sources.title: Maytronics Dolphin Wave 60 Automatic Pool Vacuum
sources.claim: Maytronics' Dolphin Wave commercial robotic cleaners run unattended scanning cycles that clean floor, walls and waterline and are in routine use at public and commercial swim centers, hotels and water parks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pool-basin cleaning. It covers the water/basin portion of a pool cleanliness check — mapping the basin, detecting and removing debris from floor, walls and waterline — in exactly the commercial pools this occupation staffs.

sources.title: Parks & Grünflächen — Angsa Robotics
sources.claim: Angsa Robotics' outdoor robot autonomously detects and picks small litter such as cigarette ... and bottle caps on grass and gravel in parks and festival grounds, and has run supervised trials with Berlin's municipal cleaning service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor litter removal on unimproved ground. Closest available system to an unstructured-setting grounds check, but limited to small litter on grass/gravel in pilot use — it does not perform the wider hazard/restroom inspection and reporting the instance requires.

tasks.label: Observe activities in assigned areas, using binoculars, to detect hazards, disturbances, or safety infractions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pool lifeguard at a municipal, school, or hotel aquatic facility scanning an assigned zone (surface, mid-water, bottom) from an elevated stand or walking the deck, watching for distressed or submerged swimmers, running on deck, rough play, or unsupervised children; scanning rotations every 10-30 seconds under glare, splash, and crowding.

Open-water/beach lifeguard on a surf tower or truck using binoculars to scan a stretch of shoreline: swimmers drifting into rip currents or past flags, boats or watercraft entering swim zones, surfers colliding with bathers, incoming weather; long sight lines, glare, wave occlusion, and fluctuating crowds.

Ski patroller observing runs, terrain park, and lift-loading areas from a vantage point or while riding a lift, watching for collisions, fallen or missing skiers, reckless speed, closed-trail/rope-duck infractions, and snow/weather hazards; cold, snow, fog, flat light, and dispersed subjects across a large mountain.

Waterpark or wave-pool attendant monitoring a slide, lazy river, or wave attraction for rider-behavior violations (height/weight rules, improper riding position, tube stacking), dispatch spacing, and swimmers in trouble in turbulent, aerated water.

Other recreational protective worker — lake/marina or campground patrol, ranger-style monitoring of a swim beach or boat ramp, amusement ride queue observation — scanning from a tower, boat, or vehicle for hazards, unauthorized entry, and rule violations over a wide, partly wooded or open-water area.

tasks.label: Operate underwater recovery units.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal/community indoor pool or waterpark: guards run in-service underwater search-and-recovery — sweep the bottom of the deep end (10-13 ft) and retrieve a submerged weighted rescue manikin (or 10-lb brick) with a surface dive, bring it to the surface and tow it to the wall. Clear chlorinated water, tiled flat bottom, known depths, staff-controlled facility.

Pool or waterpark: an actual unconscious swimmer is spotted on the bottom (or a head-count discrepancy triggers a bottom search). Guard enters, locates the body, brings it to the surface without dropping it and moves it to the wall where the rest of the team waits with a backboard. Time-critical, bystanders in the water.

Lake, pond, quarry or camp waterfront: a swimmer is missing and the guard team runs a lost-swimmer line search of the roped swim area — murky low-visibility water, silt/weed bottom, variable depth, unknown victim location — sweeping with mask, fins and feet until the victim is found and brought ashore.

Guarded natural swim area (lake/pond beach): a submergence is witnessed from the tower, so the victim's position on the bottom is known within a few metres at 2-4 m depth. Guard dives, secures the body, surfaces it and carries it the short distance to the shore/dock where responders wait.

Ocean/surf beach: recovery of a submerged victim in or just beyond the surf zone, with breaking waves, currents, sand-scoured bottom and poor visibility; guard swims or works from a rescue board/boat, sometimes with mask and fins or with the agency dive team.

Agency underwater recovery unit (public-safety dive team / marine recovery team) operating sonar, an ROV and scuba to locate and recover a drowning victim's body, plus associated gear, from deeper open water or a river beyond the guarded swim area — a multi-hour operation with search grids, tenders and chain-of-custody handling.

sources.system: Fraunhofer IOSB-AST underwater rescue robot (DEDAVE-derived prototype)
sources.developer: Fraunhofer IOSB-AST with Wasserrettungsdienst Halle e.V.
sources.title: An autonomous underwater robot saves people from drowning — Fraunhofer press release
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IOSB-AST's autonomous underwater rescue robot completed a full open-water recovery: an 80 kg dummy placed at 3 m depth in the Hufeisensee swimming lake was located, picked up, secured against slipping, brought to the surface and carried 40 m to shore in about two minutes.

sources.title: Underwater rescue robot - Fraunhofer IOSB-AST
sources.claim: The same robot's swimming-pool configuration sits in a docking station on the pool floor and is cued by ceiling-mounted surveillance cameras that send the drowning person's coordinates; on arrival it locates the person with cameras and carries them to the surface, with a fixation device preventing lifeless bodies from sliding out. In murky lakes acoustic sensors replace the optical ones so the robot can autonomously head for and pick up the target.

sources.system: Phoenix 5 ASV with RESON T20 multibeam echosounder
sources.title: Detecting drowned bodies using an autonomous surface vessel | Hydro International
sources.claim: Autonomous surface vessels can run the search leg of an underwater recovery: TNO and Aquatic Drones used the Phoenix 5 ASV with a multibeam echosounder to survey for a 1.8 m CPR manikin laid on the seabed at 2-9 m in Scheveningen harbour and nearshore, with the sonar analyst working from shore. Detection only — the ASV performs no retrieval.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the sonar search phase of an underwater recovery operation, with a human-sized manikin as the target. It substantiates autonomous area search in murky open water but not the grasp, lift and transport of the body, so it cannot by itself substantiate completion of the recovery.

sources.system: Colorado Parks and Wildlife Marine Evidence Recovery Team ROV (sonar + camera + claw)
sources.title: Colorado team uses sonar, underwater drone to recover drowning victims and evidence - CBS Colorado
sources.claim: Real underwater recovery units in the US recover drowning victims and sunken evidence with piloted, tethered ROVs plus towed sonar; team members function-test the propellers and claw and then fly the vehicle from a monitor on the boat.

tasks.label: Provide assistance with staff selection, training, and supervision.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Senior lifeguard at a municipal pool assists the aquatics coordinator with seasonal hiring: reviewing applications, sitting on interview panels, administering and scoring pre-employment swim/brick-retrieval screenings, and recommending candidates.

Head guard leads in-service training at a pool or waterfront: explaining and demonstrating rescue technique, spinal backboarding, and CPR/AED sequences, running drills, and giving corrective feedback to junior guards.

Shift supervision at a waterpark or beach: assigning zone rotations and breaks, observing guards' vigilance, conducting surprise audits (e.g., dropped-manikin tests), coaching and correcting performance in real time.

Veteran ski patroller mentors new patrollers and candidates on the mountain: running toboggan-handling and avalanche/beacon refreshers, evaluating skills during hiring clinics, and advising the patrol director on selections.

Office/administrative side of the task: tracking certification expirations and training records, building schedules, drafting written performance evaluations and disciplinary documentation for management review.

tasks.label: Provide assistance in the safe use of equipment, such as ski lifts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pool lifeguard/attendant at a municipal, YMCA or hotel pool: issues and fits US Coast Guard-approved life jackets on children and weak swimmers (sizing, buckling, checking fit), hands out and checks kickboards/noodles, and assists patrons using the pool stairs, rails or ADA pool lift. Wet tile deck, crowded, wriggling children, continuous patron flow.

Waterpark slide/attraction attendant at the dispatch platform: hands riders a tube or mat, positions them in the flume in the correct riding posture, checks height/weight rules, times dispatch intervals, and assists riders out of tubes at the splash pool. Wet, noisy, fast cycle times, riders of all ages.

Ski area lift attendant at a detachable or fixed-grip chairlift base terminal: manages the maze/gates, positions guests on the load line, steadies or slows the chair for children and novices, helps loading guests with dropped poles or a fall at the load point, and stops the lift when needed. Cold, snow, ice, wind, variable light.

Ski area attendant at a top unload ramp, or at a beginner surface lift / magic carpet: helps guests off the chair, physically assists fallen riders up and clears the ramp before the next chair, coaches and steadies beginners and small children on the platter/rope tow or conveyor, and restarts the lift.

Beach or open-water lifeguard on an unenclosed public shoreline: fits PFDs on children, checks and assists patrons with rental or personal equipment (bodyboards, kayaks, SUPs, tubes), demonstrates safe use in surf, and moves people off unsafe gear in wind, waves and shifting sand.

Recreation attendant at a ropes course, climbing wall, zip line, tubing hill or ice rink: fits and checks harnesses, helmets, trolleys, skate aids or tube handles on guests, verifies buckles and attachment points, and coaches correct use at the start point.

sources.system: MIT CSAIL safe robot-assisted dressing system (robot arm + safety-aware motion planner)
sources.developer: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
sources.title: Getting dressed with help from robots | MIT CSAIL
sources.claim: MIT CSAIL demonstrated a robot arm autonomously helping put a jacket onto a cooperative human's arm using a safety-aware motion planner; this is the closest analog to fitting a life jacket or harness on a patron, but it is a laboratory demonstration with a single seated, cooperative adult, not a working-speed service task.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing. It involves manipulating a compliant garment onto a live human body, the same class of contact as fitting a PFD or harness. Transfer fails on conditions: lab setting, one cooperative seated adult, minutes per sleeve, no buckling or fit verification, versus a lifeguard fitting jackets on squirming children in seconds on a wet deck.

sources.system: Robotic dogs (quadrupeds) at Lianhua (Lotus) Mountain Ski Resort
sources.developer: Lianhua Mountain Ski Resort / Chinese quadruped suppliers
sources.title: Robotic dogs go on duty at ski resort in China - CGTN
sources.claim: Quadruped robots deployed at a Chinese ski resort perform autonomous patrol, transport, first-aid support and tourist interaction, but no cited system provides physical loading assistance to guests at lift terminals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: resort patrol and material transport at a ski area. Shows mobile robots can operate on groomed resort terrain, but the demonstrated functions are locomotion, monitoring and hauling, with no physical handling of guests or lift equipment, so it does not carry over to lift-loading assistance.

sources.system: Doppelmayr D-Line 'Camelot 6' chairlift with automatic safety bar system and loading conveyor, The Highlands, Harbor Springs, Michigan
sources.title: The Midwest's First Bubble Chairlift Opened This Weekend at The Highlands
sources.claim: A deployed Doppelmayr D-Line chairlift in the US has fully automatic restraint-bar closing, locking and opening plus a height-adjustable loading conveyor; this machinery secures riders automatically but is the ride equipment itself and does not perform the attendant's assistance work (positioning novices, helping fallen guests, clearing the ramp, judging when to slow or stop the lift).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic securing of chairlift passengers. It replaces one narrow sub-step (closing and locking the bar) inside a purpose-built lift terminal; it performs no perception of guests, no manipulation, and no exception handling, so it cannot substitute for the attendant's assistance across an instance.

sources.title: Autonomous drone can deliver life jackets to people that fall overboard
sources.claim: An autonomous drone can locate a person overboard and deliver an inflatable life jacket to them; robotic aquatic safety systems that exist today deliver flotation for rescue rather than assisting patrons in the correct use and fitting of equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous delivery of flotation equipment in water rescue. It shows machine perception of people in water and payload drop, but never contacts or fits equipment on a person, so it does not transfer to fitting PFDs or coaching safe equipment use.

tasks.label: Participate in recreational demonstrations to entertain resort guests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Resort or hotel pool: recreation-trained lifeguard leads and demonstrates poolside activities for guests — water volleyball/basketball, pool games, dive-in contests, aqua-aerobics — entering the water, modeling the moves, calling participants in, adapting to mixed-age walk-up crowds on a wet, crowded deck.

Beach or lakefront resort waterfront: staff take part in on-water recreation demonstrations for guests — water-ski/wakeboard show run, kayak/paddleboard/snorkel gear demo, rescue-board paddle-out — in surf, chop and wind, launching from sand with spectators on the beach.

Staged rescue/safety demonstration presented as guest entertainment: lifeguards enact a tube rescue, spinal-board extraction or CPR sequence with a staff 'victim' at the pool or shoreline, narrated for a watching crowd.

Ski resort on-snow demonstration: patrol or snow-sports staff make a demonstration run for guests down a groomed marked trail — technique/formation run, rescue-toboggan descent, evening torchlight parade — in cold, wind and variable snow with guests watching from the base or trailside.

Resort dry-land staged routine or appearance for a gathered audience: a scheduled athletic/entertainment routine, mascot-style appearance or photo interaction in a base-area plaza, pool deck stage or resort lawn, performed on a flat prepared surface in front of seated or standing guests.

Resort dry-land hands-on skill/equipment demonstration: avalanche-transceiver search demo with a buried beacon and shovel/probe, toboggan and harness rigging demo, snorkel/PFD fitting demo — manipulating varied gear while explaining and answering guest questions.

sources.system: Ski Robot Challenge humanoid skiing robots (Skiro, RoK-2 and others)
sources.developer: Korean universities and companies (Ski Robot Challenge organizers)
sources.title: [Video] Humanoid robots compete for gold in alpine skiing on sidelines of PyeongChang Olympics - The Korea Herald
sources.claim: Eight self-driving humanoid robots skied an 80 m giant-slalom course on a run at Welli Hilli Park ski resort without human intervention, as a spectator event held alongside the PyeongChang Olympics; performance was mixed, with several robots crashing.
sources.transferJustification: This is the task in near-identical form: a machine performing a skiing run on a resort slope in front of a watching crowd, i.e. a recreational demonstration that entertains resort guests.

sources.title: Carved Turn Control with Gate Vision Recognition of a Humanoid Robot for Giant Slalom Skiing on Ski Slopes
sources.claim: A 1.23 m, 23-DOF humanoid ski robot recognized slalom gates with onboard vision and autonomously completed giant-slalom runs with carved turns on actual outdoor ski slopes under varying weather.
sources.transferJustification: Peer-reviewed evidence that skiing a marked course on a real resort slope is done autonomously and repeatably, which is the physical core of an on-snow demonstration run for guests.

sources.system: Unitree G1 and H2 humanoid robots
sources.title: Kung fu, somersaults and scale: Unitree eyes 20,000-robot output in 2026 after gala | South China Morning Post
sources.claim: Unitree G1 and H2 humanoids performed a live martial-arts routine, including trampoline somersaults and wall climbing, on the 2026 Spring Festival Gala stage before a live and broadcast audience; the company states the kung fu segment ran fully autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: executing a scheduled athletic performance routine before a live audience in a controlled venue. It transfers to a dry-land staged recreational routine for resort guests — same flat prepared surface, same performance-for-spectators output — but not to in-water or gear-handling instruction.

sources.system: Quadruped patrol robot dogs at Lianhuashan ski resort
sources.title: Xinhua Headlines: With AI robots and creative products, China embraces winter sports boom
sources.claim: Quadruped robots are deployed at Lianhuashan ski resort in Jilin, China, patrolling, carrying first-aid supplies and posing for photos with skiers; the reports do not establish autonomous operation for the guest-facing interactions.
sources.transferJustification: Guest-facing robot presence at a ski resort; cited as context only, since autonomy of the guest-interaction behaviour is not established and it is therefore treated as teleoperated.

sources.title: BDX Droids - Disney Research
sources.claim: Disney's free-roaming BDX droids, the leading guest-facing entertainment robots in theme parks, appear at parks and events as puppeteered characters driven by a human operator, with onboard control limited to balance and gait.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed analogue to a robot 'entertaining guests' by interacting with a crowd; it shows the interactive guest-entertainment role is currently human-operated rather than autonomous.

sources.system: Imagineering aquatic animatronics (hydrofoil manta ray, robot dolphins)
sources.title: Aquatic Animatronics: Exploring the Latest Innovations at Imagineering
sources.claim: Walt Disney Imagineering's aquatic performing robots — a six-foot hydrofoil manta ray and a planned fleet of synchronized robot dolphins for lagoon shows — are prototypes still in development, not deployed performers.
sources.transferJustification: Best-funded effort at autonomous in-water performers for guest entertainment; its prototype status supports the negative judgment for pool and open-water demonstration instances.

sources.system: Hollywood Fire Rescue & Beach Safety lifeguard rescue drone program
sources.title: Hollywood Beach lifeguards debut drone-based rescue system
sources.claim: Beach lifeguard rescue robotics in service are piloted, not autonomous: Hollywood Beach's drone rescue system is flown by a lifeguard operator to drop a flotation device to a swimmer, as shown in a public demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the staged rescue-demonstration instance: the rescue hardware used in front of the public is human-piloted, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of a rescue demonstration.

roles.title: Transportation Security Screeners
roles.description: Conduct screening of passengers, baggage, or cargo to ensure compliance with Transportation Security Administration (TSA) regulations. May operate basic security equipment such as x-ray machines and hand wands at screening checkpoints.

tasks.label: Inspect carry-on items, using x-ray viewing equipment, to determine whether items contain objects that warrant further investigation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Search carry-on or checked baggage by hand when it is suspected to contain prohibited items such as weapons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Checkpoint carry-on bag search with the passenger present: after a CT/X-ray alarm the TSO calls the bag over to the search table, asks the passenger about contents, opens the zippers/compartments, removes and unpacks items around the alarm region (electronics, toiletry kits, food, clothing), swabs for explosive traces, resolves the alarm, repacks the bag and returns it, keeping the lane moving.

Checked-bag physical inspection in the checked baggage resolution area: an EDS-alarmed suitcase arrives on the conveyor at a search table under CCTV; the TSO opens it (cutting or opening TSA-approved locks as needed), unpacks packed clothing and shoes to reach the alarm object, swabs and clears it, repacks, inserts the Notice of Baggage Inspection, closes/zips the bag and returns it to the belt.

Search that uncovers a genuine prohibited or hazardous item — a loaded firearm, ammunition, large knife, aerosol, flammable liquid or lithium battery pack — requiring careful handling and safing of the item, isolation, notification of the supervisor/law enforcement, and documentation before the bag continues.

Difficult or sensitive bags: overstuffed or oddly packed luggage, fragile/high-value contents (cameras, musical instruments, medical devices), medically necessary items, religious articles, or a passenger requesting a private screening room, where the search requires tactile inspection of linings and pockets, delicate handling, and explanation to the owner.

Non-checkpoint hand searches: air cargo, mail, employee or crew bags at an access-control point, or an unattended/suspicious bag inspected in a designated area, often with law enforcement present and additional documentation.

sources.system: Baxter research robot checked-baggage inspection testbed
sources.title: Towards an Automated Checked Baggage Inspection System Augmented with Robots
sources.claim: Lab proof of concept (WPI, SPIE 2014) in which an autonomous Baxter robot located a lighter lying on top of clothes in an already-open suitcase, picked it up, dropped it in a bin and placed a TSA notice in the bag; the paper lists opening luggage, searching for other prohibited items and closing bags as future work.

sources.system: Baxter research robot checked-baggage inspection testbed
sources.title: Towards an Automated Checked Baggage Inspection System Augmented with Robots
sources.claim: Same WPI paper explicitly states that opening luggage, searching for prohibited items beyond lighters, and closing bags had not been achieved and remained future work.

sources.system: Mechanical Search (Dex-Net based push/suction/grasp policies, ABB YuMi)
sources.developer: UC Berkeley / Stanford (Danielczuk, Kurenkov, Goldberg et al.)
sources.title: Mechanical Search: Multi-Step Retrieval of a Target Object Occluded by Clutter (arXiv:1903.01588)
sources.claim: Research system that autonomously retrieves a known target object buried in a heap of 10-20 rigid objects in a bin using push/suction/grasp policies, in lab bin-picking setups.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: extracting a target item from clutter resembles digging an alarm item out of a packed bag. Transfer fails, however: the demo uses rigid, separable objects loose in an open bin with a pre-specified known target, and never opens a zippered bag, judges whether an unknown item is prohibited, swabs it, or repacks and closes the bag to worker standard.

sources.system: Chongqing Jiangbei airport baggage-handling robotic arms
sources.developer: subsidiary of a Chinese airport technology supplier (reported by Aviation Week)
sources.title: How Robotics Are Changing Airport Operations | Aviation Week
sources.claim: Deployed airport baggage robotics handle bags as closed objects — vision-guided robotic arms at Chongqing airport load check-in bags into carts at 180 bags/hour — but no deployed airport robot opens or searches bag contents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of luggage in an airport. It substantiates only moving closed bags; the hand search requires opening, unpacking deformable contents, threat determination and repacking, none of which this system performs.

sources.system: Checked Baggage Inspection System (CBIS) with EDS units and search-table stations
sources.title: Checked baggage inspection system at Missoula International Airport | TSA
sources.claim: TSA's own description of the deployed checked-baggage automation: conveyors and CT explosive detection systems are automated, but physical opening, searching and repacking of an alarmed bag is performed by a human officer at a search table under CCTV.

tasks.label: Check passengers' tickets to ensure that they are valid, and to determine whether passengers have designations that require special handling, such as providing photo identification.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Peak-hour travel document checker (TDC) podium at a US airport checkpoint: routine domestic adult hands over a REAL ID driver's license or US passport plus a mobile or paper boarding pass; officer inserts the credential into the CAT unit, confirms authenticity, name/flight match and vetting status, returns the document and waves the passenger into the correct lane, roughly every 8-12 seconds.

International or non-US traveler at the TDC podium presenting a foreign e-passport, visa, permanent resident card or other acceptable non-US credential together with a boarding pass; officer must confirm the document is genuine and unexpired and that it matches a valid reservation.

Passenger whose record carries a designation: TSA PreCheck eligibility, an SSSS selectee flag requiring enhanced screening, known-crewmember/airline crew, or an armed-officer/LEO designation; officer must recognize the flag from the credential check and route or announce the passenger to the proper screening lane.

Human-judgment presentations at the podium: families with children under 18 who need no ID, elderly or wheelchair passengers who cannot present documents themselves, non-English speakers, and confused or agitated travelers whose documents must still be checked while the officer manages the interaction and keeps the line moving.

Exception resolution: passenger arrives with no ID, an expired, damaged or altered credential, a name mismatch, or a boarding pass for the wrong day/airport; officer inspects the document for fraud indicators (tactile/UV), initiates the alternative identity verification process (TSA ConfirmID), and escalates to a supervisor or law enforcement.

Non-checkpoint credential checks: employee/vendor badge and crew credential verification at staff access points and exit lanes, or ticket-and-ID checks at other transportation facilities (rail, ferry, cruise terminals) staffed by transportation security screeners.

sources.developer: Clear Secure, Inc. with the Transportation Security Administration
sources.title: TSA eGates public-private partnership enhances traveler experience | Transportation Security Administration
sources.claim: TSA-sanctioned biometric eGates installed at US airport security checkpoints automatically match a traveler's live face against their identity document and boarding ... and open a physical barrier admitting them to screening, replacing the officer-staffed travel-document-checker podium check.

sources.title: Clear marks successful Q1 with new airport deployment, partnership | Biometric Update
sources.claim: The TSA checkpoint eGates have moved beyond a three-airport pilot to broad deployment across US airport checkpoints, verifying identity in seconds before the traveler proceeds to physical screening.

sources.title: Facial Comparison Technology | Transportation Security Administration
sources.claim: TSA's second-generation Credential Authentication Technology units, fielded at roughly 350 US airports, automatically authenticate a traveler's ID document and pull their flight reservation and vetting status (including PreCheck/selectee designation); TSOs remain responsible for directing travelers to the proper lane.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, machine-assisted: CAT-2 performs the document-validity and designation determination that this task describes; it is a fixed reader without actuation, so it is cited as corroboration alongside the actuated eGates.

sources.developer: UK Home Office / Border Force (gates supplied by Idemia, Vision-Box and others)
sources.title: Eight- and nine-year-olds to use UK airport e-gates from July in family-friendly border upgrade
sources.claim: UK Border Force operates about 290 automated self-service passport gates at 13 airports plus juxtaposed rail/port controls; the gates read the passport chip, match the traveler's face and open a barrier, and eligibility rules exclude young children, who must be handled by officers at staffed desks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated border document control. Same objects (passports, e-passport chips, walk-up travelers), same airport terminal environment, and a stricter fraud-detection standard than a boarding-pass/ID match, so capability transfers to checking travel documents for validity.

sources.system: Automated Border Control System (New Clearance Concept automated lanes)
sources.title: ICA | Passport-less Clearance Fully Rolled-Out at Changi Airport
sources.claim: Singapore's immigration authority has fully replaced manned document counters with automated barrier lanes at all four Changi Airport terminals, clearing walk-up travelers of many nationalities on biometrics alone and referring only exceptions to officers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated travel-document/identity clearance at an airport. Same traveler population and documents, same institution-controlled terminal setting, and equal or higher accuracy demands than checking a boarding pass and photo ID.

sources.title: SITA Smart Path Gates use case / SITA Smart Path Gates product page
sources.claim: Commercially sold self-boarding gates use barrier arms, presence sensors and facial recognition to validate a passenger's boarding authorization and admit or refuse them at the gate, with staff freed to handle only passengers who need personal service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: validating a passenger's ticket/boarding entitlement at an airport barrier. Identical artifact (the reservation/boarding record) and identical decision (admit, or refer for special handling), in the same terminal environment.

tasks.label: Test baggage for any explosive materials, using equipment such as explosive detection machines or chemical swab systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Checkpoint trace test of a carry-on item that needs no unpacking: officer takes the bag/laptop/stroller off the belt (random selection or a trace-only referral), swabs exterior surfaces such as handles and zippers, feeds the swab into a desktop explosives trace detector, reads clear/alarm and returns the item. Busy airport checkpoint, passengers present.

Checkpoint alarm-driven bag search plus swab: CT/X-ray flags an anomaly, officer opens the packed carry-on, locates and handles the suspect item (electronics, powders, food, dense clutter), swabs that item and interior surfaces, runs the ETD, then repacks and clears or escalates. Airport checkpoint, passenger watching.

Checked-baggage explosives screening on the EDS: bags arrive by conveyor (in-line CBIS) or are lifted onto a stand-alone CT/EDS unit; the machine tests each bag for explosive material and the officer clears non-alarm bags and sends alarms to resolution. Baggage screening room / airport lobby matrix.

Checked-bag alarm resolution (Level 3) in the checked baggage resolution area: officer opens the alarmed suitcase, correlates the flagged region with contents, swabs the specific item and bag interior, runs the ETD, then repacks, reseals and re-inducts or escalates the bag.

Screening of liquids, gels, powders and medically necessary items at the checkpoint: officer inspects the container, uses a bottled liquid scanner or swabs the container/contents and runs the ETD, then clears the item. Checkpoint search table.

Oversize/out-of-gauge baggage and air cargo or parcels: items screened in the oversize baggage room or a cargo screening facility by swabbing surfaces and running ETD, or by feeding them through a large conveyor EDS approved for freight.

sources.system: In-line Explosives Detection Systems (CT-based EDS) in checked baggage handling systems
sources.developer: TSA / EDS vendors (Leidos, Smiths Detection, Analogic)
sources.title: Technology | Transportation Security Administration
sources.claim: TSA's in-line checked baggage systems use automated CT-based explosives detection systems on conveyors that screen, sort and track every checked bag without a human running the test; officers only resolve anomalies the machine flags.

sources.system: Checkpoint CT scanners (Analogic ConneCT, Smiths HI-SCAN CTiX, Rapiscan 920CT)
sources.developer: Analogic / Smiths Detection / Rapiscan, deployed by TSA
sources.title: What Travelers Should Know About TSA's New CT Scanners – Business Traveller
sources.claim: Computed tomography carry-on scanners with automated explosives detection are deployed at scale in US checkpoints (1,162 units, 296 airports as of early July 2026), testing carry-on baggage for explosive material as bags ride a conveyor through the tunnel.

sources.system: Automated Screening Lanes (ASL) with CT scanners
sources.developer: TSA with vendors (e.g. Vanderlande, Smiths Detection)
sources.title: TSA installs new automated screening lanes with computed tomography scanners at MSY Airport checkpoint
sources.claim: Automated screening lanes physically move bins into the CT tunnel and mechanically divert alarmed bags to a separate conveyor without an officer handling them, i.e. machine control of the bag flow through the explosives test.

sources.title: Products | Smiths Detection
sources.claim: Conveyor CT cabin-baggage machines are certified for automatic detection of both solid and liquid explosives inside bags (ECAC EDS CB C3, TSA APSS 6.2 Level 1), covering the liquids/LAGs screening decision without a manual swab or bottle test.

sources.system: CT for Advanced Cabin Baggage Screening (C3 standard)
sources.title: Computed Tomography (CT) Implementation Guide – Advanced Cabin Baggage Screening
sources.claim: Industry implementation guidance confirms that current CT cabin-baggage screening allows automated detection of a defined list of solid and liquid ..., with liquids left inside the bag on the conveyor.

sources.system: Smiths Detection EDS / SDX conveyor screening systems for checked baggage and cargo
sources.title: Automatic detection at your security checkpoint | Aviation | Smiths Detection
sources.claim: Conveyor-fed EDS units certified by ECAC and TSA are marketed and used for automatic explosives detection in checked baggage and cargo/freight packages, including oversized and break-bulk items.

sources.system: AnBot manipulator-based trace explosives detection system
sources.developer: National University of Defense Technology (NUDT), China
sources.title: A Manipulator-based Trace Explosives Detection System for Baggage (IEEE)
sources.claim: A manipulator-based system autonomously performs the trace-explosives sampling of baggage that a screener does by hand: a vision-guided UR3 arm wipes the bag surface and delivers the sample to an explosives trace detector at a fixed sampling station.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: robotic swab sampling of a bag surface followed by explosives trace analysis, i.e. the screener's chemical swab test performed at a fixed station.

sources.system: Automated explosives trace detection equipment for carry-on luggage (air-jet sampler + mass spectrometer)
sources.developer: Hitachi with Hitachi Power Solutions / Univ. of Yamanashi
sources.title: Technology to automatically detect explosive substances adhering to carry-on luggage (phys.org)
sources.claim: A prototype machine automates the officer's wipe/swab test for carry-on luggage: air jets strip particles from bags of varying size moving on a conveyor, a cyclone preconcentrator collects them and mass spectrometry gives an explosives result in about five seconds.
sources.transferJustification: Directly automates the chemical trace test the screener performs by swabbing luggage; same objects (carry-on bags), same output (explosive residue present/absent).

sources.system: Vanderlande robotic build cell / automated baggage hall solutions
sources.title: Towards a fully automated baggage hall – Vanderlande
sources.claim: Robotic cells fed by baggage conveyor lines handle checked bags autonomously in airport baggage halls, showing machines can physically present bags of the kind screened by EDS.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (baggage handling): shows robots can grasp and move the same checked bags in an airport baggage hall, which is how work would be presented to an EDS in a purpose-built cell.

tasks.label: Perform pat-down or hand-held wand searches of passengers who have triggered machine alarms, who are unable to pass through metal detectors, or who have been randomly identified for such searches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard airport checkpoint: passenger cleared through advanced imaging technology (AIT) triggers an anomaly box on the generic body outline. Same-gender officer explains the procedure, performs a targeted pat-down of the flagged area (waistband, back, chest, groin using back of hand), may run a trace-detection swab of gloves, resolves the alarm (belt buckle, tissue, folded clothing), and clears the passenger within roughly a minute while the lane keeps moving.

Passenger who cannot be screened by AIT or walk-through metal detector: wheelchair or scooter user, person with cast/crutches, pacemaker or implant, or unable to hold the pose. Officer performs a hand-held metal detector sweep over the seated or standing body plus a limited pat-down of the alarming area and of the wheelchair seat/cushion, with verbal explanation and assistance.

Full-body pat-down: passenger opts out of AIT, or alarms a walk-through metal detector in a lane without imaging technology. Officer conducts head-to-toe pat-down including collar, waistband, hair/headwear, and sensitive areas, checks pockets and footwear, swabs hands or gloves for explosive trace, and clears or escalates to a supervisor/law enforcement.

Modified-procedure screening of special populations: children, elderly travelers, passengers with disabilities, autism, or medical devices (ostomy, insulin pump), religious head coverings or bulky/loose garments, service-animal handlers. Requires communication and de-escalation with an anxious, sometimes uncooperative or non-English-speaking passenger, possible private screening room with a witness, and careful handling of the person and their devices.

Random or secondary selective screening away from the main lane: gate-area random passenger checks, exit-lane or employee/crew screening, and random selection at the checkpoint. Officer wands and/or pat-downs a selected person in a less-fixed spot (jet bridge area, gate podium, employee door), often under time pressure before boarding.

sources.title: AI-Powered Massages? Automated Massage Robots Already at Work | Associated Bodywork & Massage Professionals
sources.claim: Aescape's robotic massage table uses AI-driven robotic arms that map and make sustained physical contact with a client's body autonomously, and is commercially deployed in gyms, spas and hotels — showing autonomous robot-to-human body contact is achievable in a purpose-built fixture, but the system performs bodywork, not search for concealed items on a clothed, standing person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation in contact with a human body. Considered as the closest analogue to sweeping a wand or hands over a passenger. Transfer fails: the client is disrobed, prone and fixtured on the machine's own table, the objective is pressure delivery rather than detection of concealed objects through clothing, and there is no alarm-resolution or clearing decision.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital research team
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv)
sources.claim: An autonomous ultrasound robot was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department and autonomously positioned and moved an imaging probe over volunteers' abdomens to acquire clinically relevant views — autonomous sensor-over-body scanning, but on a stationary supine patient over a small anatomical region, in a pilot clinical study.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously moving a hand-held sensor across a human body and interpreting its signal, analogous to a hand-held metal-detector sweep. Transfer fails: bare skin on a stationary supine patient over one small region, mounted by an assistant, with no full-body coverage of a clothed standing passenger, no contraband decision, and no pat-down resolution of an alarm.

sources.system: Autonomous airport patrol security robots (Changi T4; Kansai Airport patrol robots)
sources.title: Security robots: Automating safety and monitoring operations | HowToRobot
sources.claim: Security robots deployed in airport terminals, including Singapore Changi Terminal 4 and Kansai Airport, perform autonomous patrol, camera monitoring and presence — they do not touch, wand, or search passengers, and complement rather than replace human security staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic security work inside an airport terminal (E2 setting). It establishes that robots can navigate the checkpoint environment, but the demonstrated function is surveillance only; no physical search of a person is performed, so it cannot substantiate completion of a pat-down or wand search.

sources.system: Humanoid robots in JAL airport operations trial
sources.title: JAL Tests Humanoid Robots for Airport Operations
sources.claim: Humanoid robots trialled in airline ground operations are confined to structured, repetitive tasks in controlled zones, with judgment calls, unusual situations and passenger interaction explicitly left to human staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid robot work inside an airport (E2). Cited to show the state of humanoid deployment in this exact environment excludes passenger-facing, judgment-laden work such as resolving alarms by pat-down.

sources.system: DHS S&T Screening at Speed hand-held screening wand (Spectral Labs, TeraMetrix)
sources.developer: DHS Science and Technology Directorate / SBIR performers
sources.title: Feature Article: S&T Technology is Keeping our Skies Safe | Homeland Security
sources.claim: The government's own program aimed at reducing pat-downs develops hand-held imaging wands that a transportation security officer carries and sweeps over the passenger; the screening act itself remains officer-performed, with no robotic manipulator in the concept.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task technology: the state of the art for resolving alarms without a pat-down is a sensor held and swept by a human officer, not a robotic system, confirming no fielded machine performs this task.

tasks.label: Notify supervisors or other appropriate personnel when security breaches occur.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Send checked baggage through automated screening machines, and set bags aside for searching or rescreening as indicated by equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Medium/large hub with an in-line checked baggage inspection system (CBIS): bags inducted at airline ticket counters and self-bag-drops ride the automated conveyor network; each bag is fed through the CT/EDS unit; cleared bags are routed to make-up and non-cleared bags are put onto the alarm/CBRA line. TSO oversees induction and system status in an institution-controlled baggage hall.

Checked Baggage Resolution Area at an in-line airport: alarmed bags arrive on the diverted alarm line; the TSO takes each bag off the line and stages it at the inspection station for search, then puts the bag back into the system for rescreening/dispatch after resolution.

Small/medium airport or lobby stand-alone EDS operation (also used when an in-line system is down): the TSO takes each checked bag from the airline counter or a bag cart, lifts it (up to 50-70 lb) onto the EDS belt, removes it, sets alarmed bags aside on a search table, and returns cleared bags to the airline's belt or cart.

Oversize / out-of-gauge and non-conveyable items (skis, golf clubs, surfboards, car seats, strollers, boxed goods, instruments) taken to an oversize screening station; screened by a dedicated EDS where they fit, otherwise staged for ETD swab or physical search, and set aside as the equipment indicates.

Exception and peak handling: belt jams and equipment faults, untagged/no-read or mis-sorted bags, bags that fall off the line, wet, leaking or overweight bags, and surges requiring the TSO to pull bags from carts or chutes and induct them one at a time.

sources.system: Checked Baggage Inspection System (CBIS) with integrated EDS, Missoula International Airport
sources.title: Checked baggage inspection system at Missoula International Airport | Transportation Security Administration
sources.claim: TSA's deployed checked baggage inspection systems are automated conveyor networks that move each checked bag from the airline ticket counter ... EDS screening to the aircraft loading point, at US airports including small ones such as Missoula.

sources.system: Fully automated CBIS, Saipan International Airport (SPN)
sources.title: TSA debuts state-of-the-art Checked Baggage Inspection System at Saipan International Airport
sources.claim: A TSA-certified, fully automated CBIS screens all departing checked bags at Saipan International Airport; cleared bags continue to the aircraft with no TSA contact and TSOs no longer lift or move bags.

sources.system: CBIS / BHS decision-point diverters per TSA Planning Guidelines and Design Standards v7.0
sources.title: Planning Guidelines and Design Standards for Checked Baggage Inspection Systems V7.0
sources.claim: US design standards for checked baggage inspection systems specify that the baggage handling system itself routes bags according to the screening equipment's decision: cleared bags to make-up, non-cleared bags onward to the CBRA line, with no-decision bags defaulted to non-clear automatically.

sources.system: BEUMER CrisBag Independent Carrier System (ICS) in-tote screening
sources.title: Baggage Screening at Airports: Integrated Screening with ICS
sources.claim: Tote-based independent carrier screening systems automatically carry alarmed baggage to the CBRA while cleared baggage is conveyed onward to sortation, removing manual re-handling between screening and search.

sources.system: CrisBag ICS at SFO Harvey Milk Terminal 1
sources.title: First tote-based baggage handling system goes live in the US with CrisBag at San Francisco Airport
sources.claim: The first tote-based ICS in the US went live at San Francisco International Airport's Harvey Milk Terminal 1, and BEUMER's totes were the first approved by TSA for US in-tote checked baggage screening.

sources.title: How to Optimise CBIS and CBRA Screening Capacity
sources.claim: In tote-based CBRA operations the system presents and returns the bag, so TSA operators do not lift bags from one conveyor ... or drag them to a lifting table and back onto the cleared line.

sources.system: Autonomous baggage loading robot, Amsterdam Schiphol baggage halls
sources.developer: Royal Schiphol Group with baggage automation suppliers (Vanderlande)
sources.title: Lifting aid available at every workstation in Schiphol's baggage halls
sources.claim: A robot has been autonomously picking departing checked bags and loading them into carts and containers in Schiphol's baggage halls for over six months as of mid-2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic picking of individual departing checked bags off a conveyor and placing them elsewhere. Same objects (arbitrary passenger luggage), same precision, same airport baggage-hall setting, so it supports machine handling of bags on and off screening lines.

sources.title: Towards a fully automated baggage hall - Vanderlande
sources.claim: Robotic bag loading has been in operation for years in the baggage halls of Amsterdam Schiphol and London Heathrow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pick-and-place of checked bags in a live airport baggage hall. It demonstrates that machines handle the same objects the screener moves on and off screening machines, in the same class of facility.

tasks.label: Follow those who breach security until police or other security personnel arrive to apprehend them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Checkpoint breach at a busy airport passenger checkpoint: an individual walks past the walk-through metal detector or grabs a bag and moves into the sterile concourse. The screener follows on foot through dense passenger crowds, gate areas, food courts, keeping continuous visual identification and radioing a description/location until an LEO responds.

Wrong-way / exit-lane breach: a person enters the sterile area through an exit lane or unattended door. The screener follows through connecting corridors, escalators, moving walkways, elevators, and possibly an inter-terminal train, maintaining contact until police arrive.

Landside flight: a passenger refuses screening or is caught with a prohibited item and walks/runs away from the checkpoint into the ticketing lobby, out the doors, across the curb roadway, into a parking garage, sidewalk, or shuttle lot; screener follows outdoors in traffic and weather until police intercept.

Non-airport screening variants (rail/transit terminals, cruise terminals, federal-building or air-cargo screening posts): an unscreened person or vehicle driver bypasses the screening station; the screener follows through the station hall, warehouse aisles, or truck yard until security/police arrive.

Insider/secure-area breach: an employee or intruder passes a badge-access door or enters a checked-baggage room, sterile corridor, or ramp door without authorization. Screener follows through back-of-house baggage areas, service corridors, and possibly out onto the ramp apron until airport police arrive.

sources.transferJustification: Directly comparable: maintain continuous contact with a non-cooperative person who has crossed a security line until responding officers take over. Difference is environment (open terrain) and that the follower is aerial.

tasks.label: Inspect checked baggage for signs of tampering.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-line checked baggage inspection system (CBIS) screening room at a large US airport: a bag is conveyed to an alarm-resolution/ETD search station and the screener examines its exterior before and after search for signs of tampering — cut or resewn seams, slit fabric, forced or cut locks, pried zippers, broken TSA/airline security seals, mismatched or re-applied tape — at high throughput on very heterogeneous soft- and hard-sided bags.

Ticket counter, bag-drop, or stand-alone ETD/x-ray position at a smaller or non-inline airport: the screener receives the checked bag directly from the passenger or agent, looks it over for evidence of tampering (opened compartments, damaged closures, foreign tape/seals) before it is accepted and injected onto the belt, in a public lobby with passengers waiting.

Oversize/odd-shaped baggage screening area: skis, golf bags, strollers, musical instrument cases, hard cases with declared firearms. Screener handles the item off-conveyor, verifies locks, latches, cable seals and declaration tags are intact and unaltered, and confirms nothing has been opened since acceptance.

Bags retrieved from tubs, carts, ULDs or a held/unclaimed-bag storage area, and inbound/transfer or re-screened bags: the screener locates the specific bag, pulls it out, turns it to view all sides including the bottom, and checks that security seals, tape and locks match the chain-of-custody record and show no tampering.

Adverse or ambiguous cases: plastic-wrapped bags, heavily worn or wet/dirty soft-sided bags, previously damaged luggage, peak-rush conditions — the screener must distinguish ordinary wear or handling damage from deliberate tampering, then escalate, document, and notify the airline or supervisor.

sources.title: VISY adds AI-backed damage inspection – WorldCargo News
sources.claim: VISY's Automatic Damage Detection System uses fixed multi-camera portals at container terminal gates, rail portals and cranes to autonomously image all visible sides of each container in motion and classify damage — including holes, punctures, breaches, open or damaged door handles and bent locking bars — replacing manual stop-and-inspect checks; earlier versions are already deployed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inspecting a sealed transport unit for integrity/tamper indicators at a working facility. Comparable output (flag units whose closure or shell shows breach/interference, divert them for human follow-up), comparable throughput and in-motion presentation to a checked-bag conveyor; the port is an institution-controlled facility (E2).

sources.title: Turnkey Gate Automation for Yards & Terminals - Outpost
sources.claim: Outpost's AI gate-automation system autonomously verifies seal, lock and latch ... on trucks and containers in motion, day and night, and flags tampering; brought to market commercially in 2025 for yards and terminals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying seal/lock integrity and detecting tampering on closed transport units passing a fixed inspection point in an institution-controlled facility — the same perceptual decision a screener makes on a checked bag's locks, zippers and security seals.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: grasping, lifting and repositioning checked bags of arbitrary size, weight and softness inside an airport baggage hall. It substantiates the manipulation and bag-presentation component of tamper inspection in that same E2 environment.

tasks.label: Close entry areas following security breaches or reopen areas after receiving notification that the airport is secure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Alarm or minor breach at a passenger checkpoint (prohibited item, unresolved alarm, person moving past the podium): the screener immediately closes the entry to one or more screening lanes — halting the divest queue, pulling a retractable belt or 'lane closed' sign across the lane entrance, holding waiting passengers back — and reopens the lane once the supervisor/LEO gives the all-clear. Busy indoor terminal checkpoint, general public present.

Wrong-way breach at a fixed access point — the exit lane, a checkpoint door, or an employee/secure-area door: the screener physically blocks the portal so no unscreened person reaches the sterile side, holds the post until law enforcement responds, then reopens the portal after notification the area is secure.

Confirmed breach requiring full checkpoint shutdown and partial sterile-area evacuation: all lanes stopped, hundreds of queued and already-screened passengers moved back out to landside, the checkpoint area cordoned and held clear during the police sweep, then the area reopened and everyone re-screened.

Reopening after 'airport is secure' notification: reopening the closed entry doors/gates and lane entrances, confirming the area is clear of people, restoring normal one-way flow, and restarting passenger movement through the access points.

Closing off a non-checkpoint area after a breach or unattended item — a baggage claim entrance, a corridor, a curbside door, or a checked-baggage/cargo area: cordoning an arbitrary footprint with tape, cones or stanchions, standing post to keep the public out, then removing the cordon and reopening.

Patrol of an air-cargo screening facility or airport service/staging area (warehouse floor, dock, staging pallets, secure yard): checking for unattended packages, tampered freight, items left outside secured zones; industrial, badge-controlled site, some vehicle traffic.

Start-of-shift, end-of-shift or post-incident detailed sweep of the checkpoint and adjacent areas: inspecting bins and bin carts, under divest tables and podiums, inside trash receptacles, behind search tables and in storage cabinets for left-behind, concealed or suspicious items, with the area closed or low traffic.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Checkpoint carry-on bag search with the passenger standing at the search table: after an X-ray or CT alarm, the officer opens a tightly packed bag, digs through clothing, electronics and toiletries to the flagged location, extracts the prohibited item (oversized liquid/gel/aerosol, pocket knife, multi-tool, lighter fluid), explains the disposal options, drops the item in the surrender/disposal bin, repacks and returns the bag, all within a minute or two while the line waits.

Checked-baggage resolution area (CBRA): a bag alarms in the in-line system and is delivered to the officer's search station; the officer unzips the bag or cuts the lock, searches through packed personal effects to find hazardous material (butane lighters, aerosols, spare lithium batteries, flammable liquids, camp fuel, matches), removes it, repacks and closes the bag, inserts a notice of inspection, places the item in the designated hazmat container and notifies/hands off to the airline.

High-consequence or complex find: a firearm, loose ammunition, compressed-gas cylinder, replica explosive, or a leaking/unidentified chemical in an opened bag. The officer stops the search, isolates the bag, summons law enforcement or the hazmat coordinator, and participates in a documented chain-of-custody transfer of the item to the airline, hazmat contractor or police, with paperwork and passenger/airline coordination.

Periodic turnover of accumulated confiscated property: the officer empties surrender bins and hazmat containers, sorts the mixed items into the correct disposal categories (sharps, lighters/flammables, aerosols, liquids), logs quantities, and moves the sealed containers to the airline representative or disposal contractor at the pickup point.

sources.transferJustification: Same task setting (CBRA alarm resolution): the robot performs only bag transport and presentation while the confiscation step remains manual, bounding what deployed airport robotics does today.

instances.label: Busy checkpoint lane, mid-size US airport: the CT/x-ray image flags an oversized liquid, gel or aerosol (shampoo, water bottle, sunscreen) in a carry-on. The officer pulls the bin to the search table, opens the bag in front of the passenger, digs out the container, tells the passenger it exceeds 3.4 oz and that they may surrender it, take it to their car, or check it, and drops the surrendered bottle into the disposal barrel. Line pressure, passenger watching, bag returned in a minute or two.

Bag check for a sharp or tool: pocket knife, multi-tool, scissors over 4 in, or a screwdriver/wrench over 7 in found in a carry-on. Officer opens the bag, locates the item among packed clothing and cords, removes it, states it is prohibited in the cabin, and places it in the surrendered-property container after the passenger declines to leave the checkpoint.

Prohibited item found on the passenger's person: knife or lighter in a pocket revealed by the AIT scanner alarm or a pat-down, or handed over during divestiture. The officer must obtain the item directly from the traveler, keep control of a sharp object next to a queue of people, and dispose of it, sometimes over the traveler's objection.

Informing rather than confiscating: the passenger wants to keep the item (a knife of sentimental value, an expensive tool, a full-size cosmetic). The officer explains the mail-back service or kiosk available at that airport, or the return-to-vehicle / check-the-bag options, hands the bag and item back, directs the traveler out of the queue to the mailing station or ticket counter, and handles voluntary abandonment if they change their mind.

Hazardous or special-handling item: fireworks, bear spray or other self-defense spray, a flammable aerosol, camp fuel, or an oversize/damaged lithium battery. The officer isolates the item, calls a supervisor or the airport's hazmat/bomb appraisal officer, keeps the passenger and lane clear, and routes the item into segregated hazardous-waste disposal rather than the ordinary surrender bin.

Checked-baggage resolution room behind the ticket counters: an alarm or prohibited-item hit sends a checked suitcase to the search station. The officer unzips or unlatches the closed bag, works through packed contents to find the item (aerosol, over-limit ammunition, flammable), removes it for disposal, places a notice-of-inspection card inside, and re-closes the bag for the outbound conveyor.
