tasks.label: Present bills and accept payments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant dining room: supervisor prints and drops the check in a folder at a seated table mid-rush, judges when the party is ready, returns to collect a credit card or cash, runs it at the POS station, and brings back the card/change, signature slip and receipt; split checks, comps and tips are common.

Quick-service / coffee-shop front counter register: supervisor steps onto a register during a rush, totals the order on the POS, states the amount due, takes cash and counts change back from the drawer or runs a tapped/inserted card, and hands over the printed receipt.

Bar or counter tab close-out: a guest closes a running tab; the supervisor prints the tab, takes the credit card handed across the bar (often already held behind the bar), runs it, presents the slip for tip and signature, and returns the card and copy.

Drive-thru payment window: supervisor covers the cash window during peak, exchanging cash, cards, coupons and receipts through the window with drivers in stationary vehicles, counting change back while keeping lane times down.

Institutional cafeteria or stadium/concession checkout line: supervisor works the register at the end of the serving line, rings up trays and items, takes meal-card, cash or card payment and issues a receipt as a queue moves through a fixed line.

Off-site catering or banquet function: supervisor presents the final banquet check/invoice to the event host at the client's venue, obtains a signature, and collects payment by card on a mobile reader, cash, or a company check, issuing a receipt.

tasks.label: Perform various financial activities, such as cash handling, deposit preparation, and payroll.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift till count and reconciliation at a QSR or casual-dining restaurant: the supervisor pulls each cashier's drawer from the POS register, carries it to the back office, counts bills and coins, runs the POS shift report, records over/short in the cash log, and sets the next shift's starting bank.

Deposit preparation on premises: bundling and strapping the day's counted cash, completing the deposit slip and store cash sheet, sealing it in a tamper-evident bag, logging the bag number, and locking it in the drop safe for armored-carrier pickup.
Off-site bank run: carrying or driving the sealed deposit bag to the bank branch or night depository after close, obtaining the receipt, and picking up a coin/change order to bring back to the store.

Cash handling during service: issuing starting banks/floats to cashiers and drive-thru, breaking large bills and supplying change rolls, making mid-shift skims/drops from drawers that exceed the till limit into the safe, authorizing cash refunds, and paying a COD vendor delivery in cash.

Tip handling at shift end: counting cash tips and credit-tip payout amounts, applying the tip-pool/tip-out formula, dispensing and distributing cash payouts to servers, bartenders and bussers, and recording the distribution.

Payroll administration in the back office: reviewing and correcting employee time punches and missed clock-ins on the terminal, approving hours in the payroll/labor system, transmitting to corporate or the payroll provider, and distributing paper paychecks and pay stubs to employees.

tasks.label: Supervise and participate in kitchen and dining area cleaning activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Closing deep clean of the hot line in a restaurant kitchen: supervisor works alongside the closing crew scraping and degreasing the flat-top/char grill, breaking down and wiping fryers and filtering oil, pulling hood filters, disassembling slicers/mixers/soft-serve heads, scrubbing shelving and reach-in gaskets, and signing off the checklist.

Dish pit: scraping plates, racking mixed dishware, glassware and flatware, running the conveyor or door-type machine, hand-scrubbing sheet pans, stock pots and steam-table inserts, three-compartment sink work, then drying and putting wares away; supervisor jumps in during rushes and checks sanitizer strength.

Dining room reset and table care: bussing dirty dishes, glasses and trash from tables and booths, wiping table tops, seat backs and high chairs with sanitizer, cleaning up spilled drinks and dropped food, restocking and wiping condiment/drink stations, while directing bussers.

Whole-floor cleaning of a large open dining area (fast-food dining room, cafeteria, food court, c-store food area) after close or during slow periods: sweeping and damp-mopping or scrubbing the main open floor to a visible standard.

Floor cleaning in confined or hostile floor space: tight dining rooms with fixed booths and table pedestals, plus the greasy kitchen floor with rubber mats, floor drains, equipment legs and tight aisles - degreaser, deck brush and mop work.

Clean-as-you-go during service: sanitizing prep tables and cutting boards between tasks, changing sanitizer buckets and towels, wiping expo line and reach-in handles, pulling trash and grease/recycling to the dumpster, spot-cleaning spills while service continues.

tasks.label: Control inventories of food, equipment, smallware, and liquor, and report shortages to designated personnel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Period-end physical food count: supervisor walks the dry storeroom, walk-in cooler and freezer of a full-service restaurant with a count sheet or tablet, counting sealed cases, #10 cans, bags, boxes, partially used packages and house-prepped bulk containers (weighing or eyeballing partials), then enters totals and reports shortages/variances to the GM or purchasing.

Pre-shift and mid-service par-level checks in a working kitchen: supervisor scans line reach-ins, prep pans, holding cabinets, walk-in shelves, condiments and paper goods during or just before a rush, identifies items below par, tells prep cooks/manager what to pull or make, and adds shorts to the order guide.

Receiving a delivery at the back door: supervisor checks incoming cases, cartons and catch-weight items against the invoice/packing slip, inspects produce and protein quality and dairy/frozen temperatures, notes shorts, substitutions and damages, signs off with the driver, puts stock away, and reports shortages to vendor and manager.

Bar/liquor inventory: supervisor counts full and back-stock bottles, kegs, wine and beer in the bar and liquor room and estimates or weighs partial bottles to tenths, reconciles counts against POS depletion, and reports shortages and pour-cost variances to management.

Smallware and equipment inventory: supervisor counts plates, glassware, flatware, hotel and sheet pans, utensils and small appliances across the dish room, shelving and service stations, notes breakage, loss and unserviceable items, and reports shortages for a replacement order.

sources.title: IERA Award 2026 Goes to Flying Warehouse Robots by Verity from Switzerland
sources.claim: Verity's autonomous indoor drones fly warehouse aisles without GPS or human intervention, scan barcodes/labels at storage locations, identify and report inventory discrepancies, and are in use in roughly 200 warehouses worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cycle counting stock in a storage facility and reporting discrepancies. It transfers to the supervisor's stock count only where inventory is presented as machine-readable, labelled units in fixed, known locations with clear aisles — the E1 presentation — not to a cramped restaurant walk-in of stacked, opened cases.

sources.claim: Gather AI's drones autonomously fly warehouse aisles capturing images of inventory locations for cycle counting, sold commercially as an inventory monitoring service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replacing manual cycle counts in a stockroom. Same objects (labelled cases/pallets) and same output (on-hand counts and discrepancy reports) as the supervisor's count, given machine-readable presentation.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous counting of discrete, individually tagged items and reporting variance against expected stock — the same output as a smallware count, provided every item carries a tag and lives in a fixed, scannable location (E1 presentation).

tasks.label: Inspect supplies, equipment, and work areas to ensure efficient service and conformance to standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift/opening walkthrough of a QSR or fast-casual kitchen: shift manager circulates through a cramped, hot line checking that fryers/grills/holding cabinets are on and at temperature, sanitizer buckets are made and at strength, each station is stocked to par (pans, condiments, cups, wrappers), surfaces and floors are clean and free of hazards, and small wares/utensils are present; deficiencies are fixed or assigned on the spot before doors open.

During-shift food-safety line check in a restaurant or institutional kitchen: probing internal temperatures of hot-holding and cold-holding foods with a calibrated thermometer, reading walk-in cooler/freezer thermometers, checking date labels and FIFO rotation on prepped containers, titrating sanitizer with test strips, discarding out-of-spec product, and logging results on the line-check/HACCP sheet.

Receiving and storeroom supply inspection: meeting a delivery at the back door, inspecting cases of produce, dairy, and protein for quality, damage, pack size, count against the invoice, and product temperature; rejecting or noting nonconforming items; then checking dry storage and walk-in organization, par levels, and expired or damaged stock.

Front-of-house/service-area inspection during service at a full-service restaurant, hotel banquet, cafeteria, or buffet: checking table and booth cleanliness and settings, steam-table/buffet product levels, appearance and holding temperatures, beverage and condiment stations, service ware supply, floors and spills, and restrooms; directing servers or bussers to correct what is found while guests are present.

Closing/sanitation verification walkthrough: verifying that grills and fryers were cleaned and filtered, slicers and mixers broken down and sanitized, hood filters and drains clean, prep tables and reach-ins wiped and organized, chemicals stored properly, trash and grease handled, floors mopped, and equipment shut down or set for overnight, signing the closing checklist and re-tasking staff for anything missed.

Equipment condition and functionality inspection in an institutional kitchen (school, hospital, corporate cafeteria): verifying dish machine wash/final-rinse temperatures and chemical concentration, checking refrigeration gauge temperatures and door seals, ice machine, steam kettles and gas equipment, identifying malfunctions, tagging units out of service and reporting work orders.

sources.title: Harmons Deploys Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot In Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Tally is an autonomous shelf-scanning robot that audits store shelves for out-of-stocks, low stock, misplaced items and pricing errors while operating among shoppers and staff; deployed across 17 Harmons grocery stores after a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: auditing supplies on shelves against a stocking standard, i.e. 'inspect supplies ... conformance to standards' inside an E2 facility. Transfer is only partial: Tally reads barcoded, faced product on open ambient shelving and reports; it cannot open coolers, judge food quality or dates on kitchen containers, or check equipment and work-area cleanliness.

sources.title: Badger Technologies and Stop & Shop Stores Upgrade Marty the Robot at 300+ Locations to Improve Customer Shopping Experiences
sources.claim: Marty is an autonomous multipurpose robot that patrols grocery sales floors detecting spills and floor hazards and, after upgrade, performs shelf product checks; rolled out at 300+ Stop & Shop stores since 2019.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patrolling a public-facing floor of a food-retail facility to detect hazards (spills/debris) and stocking gaps, comparable to a supervisor's service-area sweep in an E2 facility. Transfer is limited to floor-hazard and shelf-gap detection on open aisles; it does not cover table/buffet condition, holding temperatures, restrooms, or corrective action.

sources.system: Spot with Orbit / Autowalk autonomous inspection
sources.title: Transforming Manufacturing Reliability Inspections with Mobile Robots | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot runs scheduled autonomous inspection missions in industrial facilities (including food and beverage plants), reading analog gauges and capturing thermal, acoustic and vibration data with alerting on out-of-range readings, at thousands of automated inspections per week across a deployed fleet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous equipment-condition inspection rounds in a structured human work facility. Transfer to a kitchen equipment check is partial: Spot reads instrumented gauges and thermal signatures on fixed plant assets along wide fixed routes, but cannot verify dish-machine rinse temperature with a probe/thermolabel, titrate chemical concentration, or assess greasy hood filters in a cramped wet kitchen.

sources.system: TOMRA Neon / KATO260 / TOMRA 5B optical sorters and graders
sources.title: How food processor and packhouses are improving efficiencies with new solutions powered by artificial intelligence
sources.claim: TOMRA's AI-driven optical sorters and graders inspect food presented on a line and physically accept or reject items against quality specifications (defects, clusters, unripe or undersized fruit, foreign material) without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grading incoming food supplies against quality standards and removing nonconforming product — the same accept/reject judgment a supervisor makes inspecting a delivery, on comparable objects (produce, protein) at equal or better precision, in a purpose-built E1 line where product is presented singulated on a belt.

sources.system: Cognex vision systems (date and lot code OCR/OCV)
sources.title: Lot Code and Expiration Date Inspection with OCR | Cognex
sources.claim: Cognex machine-vision systems verify lot, date and expiration ... and label presence/correctness on food production lines in real time, flagging nonconforming packs for removal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying date/lot marking of food supplies against standards — the machine analogue of a supervisor checking date labels on incoming cases — where product is presented on an E1 line. It does not extend to unlabeled prepped containers stacked in a walk-in.

sources.system: TDI Packsys conveyorized inspection systems with automatic reject
sources.title: Conveyorized Metal Detectors – TDI Packsys
sources.claim: Conveyorized food inspection systems carry integrated automatic reject mechanisms (push bar, flipper, air jet) that physically remove nonconforming or contaminated product from the line without stopping it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: supplies the physical actuation that makes line inspection an embodied act — the machine removes supplies failing the standard, producing the accept/reject output a supervisor's supply inspection yields, in an E1 line setting.

sources.system: Optris Xi 400 in-line thermal inspection with automatic defect removal
sources.title: Infrared Temperature Monitoring for Ice Cream Cones
sources.claim: An Optris thermal imaging camera monitors product temperature in-line, and a machine in the production process automatically removes parts whose temperature indicates nonconformance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: temperature-based conformance screening of food with automatic removal of failures on a purpose-built line. Transfer to a kitchen line check is limited: it is a surface/thermal measurement of product presented on a belt, not internal probe verification of held food across stations, coolers and steam tables.

tasks.label: Evaluate new products for usefulness and suitability.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sample of a new food item or ingredient (new vendor's chicken tenders, a substitute cheese, a corporate limited-time menu item) arrives at the unit. The supervisor prepares it per spec on the line, tastes and looks at it, checks portion yield, cook time, holding behavior and plate appearance, compares it against the incumbent product, and gives a keep/reject recommendation.

Trial of a new piece of equipment or smallware in the kitchen (immersion blender, sheet pans, portion scoops, a holding cabinet, a dish rack). The supervisor installs/sets it up, uses it through one or more shifts, watches cooks and dishwashers use it, judges capacity, durability, cleanability and fit with the line workflow, then reports whether to adopt.

Evaluation of new disposables, packaging or serving supplies (to-go containers, lids, cups, gloves, portion cups). The supervisor fills them with hot and cold product, checks for leaks, heat retention, stacking, whether they fit existing holders/shelves/bags, how fast staff can assemble them, and recommends adoption or rejection.

Evaluation of a new cleaning or sanitizing chemical, dispenser, or a new food-safety supply. The supervisor mixes per label, verifies concentration with test strips, uses it on surfaces and in the three-compartment sink, judges effectiveness, residue, odor, contact-time practicality and staff safety, and decides whether it suits the operation.

Vendor or distributor presentation: a rep brings samples and spec/price sheets to the back office, or the supervisor attends a distributor food show. The supervisor inspects and tastes small samples, reviews case pack, cost-per-portion, allergen and label specs, and reports a judgment on usefulness for the unit.

Product evaluation away from a fixed unit: an off-site catering event, a food truck, or a school/community taste-test event in a variable venue. The supervisor sets out samples of a new product under uncontrolled conditions, watches how it holds and how customers respond, and forms a suitability judgment.

sources.system: Cambridge/Beko robot chef 'taste as you go'
sources.developer: University of Cambridge Department of Engineering with Beko
sources.title: Taste of the future: robot chef learns to 'taste as you go' | University of Cambridge
sources.claim: A research robot 'chef' from Cambridge/Beko autonomously assesses one attribute (saltiness) of a fixed dish using a conductance probe in a laboratory rig; it does not judge a product's overall suitability for an operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic taste sensing during cooking. It is the closest published capability to sensory product evaluation, but it covers a single attribute of one pre-defined dish in a lab rig, so it does not transfer to judging a new product's flavor, texture, yield and workflow fit at worker quality.

sources.title: Chef Robotics Advances Bi-Manual Physical AI System for Prep Table Food Assembly Powered by a Food Foundation Model
sources.claim: Deployed commercial food robots perform repetitive assembly and frying of known items on conveyor or fry-station lines; none of the deployed systems is described as evaluating new products or issuing adoption recommendations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic food handling/assembly in production kitchens. It establishes the state of deployed foodservice robotics (repetitive manipulation of known items) but provides no sensory judgment or product-adoption decision, so it does not transfer to product evaluation.

sources.title: Miso Robotics develops smaller, faster Flippy | Restaurant Dive
sources.claim: Flippy, the most widely publicized restaurant kitchen robot, operates a fry station in a small number of quick-service restaurants; its role is cooking known items, not trialing or evaluating new products or equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic frying in a commercial kitchen. It shows in-restaurant robots handle a fixed, pre-programmed cooking station; it demonstrates no capability to trial an unfamiliar product or equipment and report a suitability judgment.

tasks.label: Compile and balance cash receipts at the end of the day or shift.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quick-service or fast-casual restaurant (burger, pizza, chicken, coffee chain): at end of shift the manager pulls each cashier's till in the back office, counts bills and coin, compares the count to the POS drawer/sales report, records over/short, seals a deposit and drops it in the safe.

Full-service restaurant or bar close-out: servers and bartenders check out with cash, credit-card slips and declared tips; the supervisor verifies each server bank, pays out cash tip-outs and credit tips, counts the house bank, ties the total to the POS sales/tender report, and prepares the deposit.

Institutional food service (school, hospital, college, corporate or military cafeteria): registers hold heavy coin and small bills; the food-service supervisor counts each register, reconciles to the POS/meal-count report, completes a daily cash sheet, and sends a sealed bag to the campus business office or night depository.

Largely cashless cafe or fast-casual unit: only a small cash float and a handful of cash sales; the shift lead counts a light drawer, closes the card batch, reviews the POS end-of-day report on a terminal or tablet, and logs the totals.

Concession stand, catering event, or food truck: several cash boxes, aprons or bank bags come back after the event; the supervisor counts them in the truck, a trailer, or a tent with no fixed back office, reconciles to ticket/POS counts, and holds the deposit until the next business day.

sources.system: Loomis SafePoint Titan smart safe (Fowler Foods, 88 KFC/Taco Bell units)

tasks.label: Maintain sanitation, health, and safety standards in work areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sanitizing food-contact and work surfaces on the active line: wiping prep counters, cutting boards, condiment/assembly tables and small equipment (toaster, slicer, shake machine parts) with sanitizer bucket and cloth between products and at shift change, moving pans, containers and utensils aside, working in a cramped aisle beside hot equipment while other crew move through.

Cleaning cooking equipment at close or between dayparts: scraping and degreasing the flat-top/clamshell grill, cleaning grease traps and drip trays, filtering or changing fryer oil, boiling out and scrubbing fry vats and baskets, wiping hood surfaces and holding cabinets — hot, heavy, greasy work with chemicals.

Kitchen floor care: sweeping debris, lifting and hosing anti-fatigue mats, mopping/degreasing greasy quarry-tile floors including under and behind fryers and grills, cleaning floor drains, plus immediate spill cleanup and wet-floor signage during a busy service period.

Warewashing: scraping and soaking pans, utensils, fry baskets, trays and smallwares, loading and running the commercial dish machine or three-compartment sink at correct sanitizer concentration, then racking, drying and putting items away.

Waste handling: emptying kitchen and lobby trash cans, changing liners, hauling bags across the lot to the dumpster or compactor, breaking down boxes, rinsing and sanitizing bins and keeping the dumpster corral clean.

Food-safety compliance actions: probing and logging holding/cooling temperatures, checking hold timers and discarding expired product, date-labeling and rotating prep, testing sanitizer concentration, hand washing and glove changes, and correcting hazards flagged on a line check.

tasks.label: Clean food preparation areas, cooking surfaces, and utensils.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-service wipe-down and sanitizing of the prep station and counters in a busy QSR kitchen: clearing crumbs, food debris and spills, moving pans/tools aside, spraying quat sanitizer and wiping counters, cutting boards, reach-in handles and equipment fronts between orders while coworkers work around the robot.

Cleaning the cooking surface during and between cooking cycles: scraping carbonized grease and residue off the hot flat-top griddle/clamshell into the trough, wiping with a grill cloth, and cleaning the spatula/turners used, several times per shift.

Washing rackable smallwares and utensils: scraping/pre-rinsing tongs, scoops, portion containers, lids and cutting boards, racking them, running the commercial dish machine, and unloading/air-drying and putting away.

Hand-scrubbing heavily soiled items at the three-compartment sink: fry baskets with carbonized batter, sheet pans and food pans with baked-on grease, shake/beverage machine parts, using scrub pads, wash-rinse-sanitize sequence and air-dry.

Fryer-station cleaning: skimming crumbs, filtering the fryer oil through the filtration unit, cleaning the fry baskets and crumb screens, and wiping down the fryer cabinet and surrounding grease splatter.

End-of-shift/closing deep clean of the cook line: degreasing the griddle with grill brick and screens, disassembling equipment (toaster crumb trays, shake machine parts, slicers), cleaning hood filters, splash walls, shelving, drains and sweeping/mopping the prep area floor.

tasks.label: Operate large-volume cooking equipment, such as grills, deep-fat fryers, or griddles.

instances.label: Fry station at a burger/general QSR (McDonald's, Wendy's, Jack in the Box type): pull frozen fries, nuggets, hash browns, onion rings from freezer, load and drop baskets in a multi-vat fryer, shake/drain on timers, dump and salt into the holding bin, and pace batches to order flow through lunch rush.

Fry station at a chicken/seafood chain (Popeyes, KFC, Zaxby's, Long John Silver's type): batter/bread bone-in chicken, tenders, wings or fish, stage loads into open or pressure fryers, manage longer cook times and temperature recovery across several vats, and hold cooked product to time standards.

Fryer work at a high-surge non-traditional venue: stadium, arena, airport or food-court concession stand running tenders, tots and fries in bulk during a compressed rush, with fixed equipment and institution-controlled premises.

Grill/griddle station at a burger QSR: lay frozen or fresh patties on a clamshell or flat-top griddle in ordered rows, sear/flip, season, check doneness, toast buns on the bun toaster, and move cooked patties to the holding cabinet while a second person calls orders during peak.

Breakfast and specialty griddle work: crack eggs into rings or fold omelette-style eggs, cook sausage patties, bacon and hotcakes simultaneously on one flat top, grill tortillas/quesadillas or marinated chicken and steak on a charbroiler, timing several different products at once.

In-shift management of the cooking equipment itself: preheat and verify temperatures, top off and filter fryer oil between loads, respond to equipment alarms/oil quality issues, and adjust cook programs when volume or product changes.

instances.label: Fry station at a high-volume burger/mixed QSR (White Castle, McDonald's, Jack in the Box type): dropping and timing baskets of fries, nuggets, hash browns and onion rings so the exact counts on several concurrent drive-thru and counter tickets come up hot together; standard fryer bank in an existing kitchen with crew working alongside.

Batch prep of sauces, dressings, salsas, batters and shake/dry mixes: measuring liquid and dry ingredients to recipe, mixing/blending, straining, portioning into squeeze bottles, pans and dispensers, labeling and dating.
Portioning prepped ingredients into line pans and inserts for the day (shredded cheese, bacon, cooked proteins, toppings, garnishes) and staging them at the cook line and makeline rails.

tasks.label: Clean, stock, and restock workstations and display cases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-shift restock of the make/assembly line in a busy QSR kitchen: cook notices lettuce, cheese, sliced tomato, sauces or portioned meat running low, walks to the walk-in cooler, pulls the right pans, carries them through a narrow crowded line, pulls the near-empty pan from the rail, rotates remaining product, drops the fresh pan in, and returns/discards the old one — all during service around coworkers.

Stocking dry goods and packaging at the assembly, drink and pack-out stations: cups, lids, straws, wrappers, cartons, bags, napkins, condiment packets, sauce pouches, buns. Cook fetches cases from the stockroom or shelving, cuts them open, breaks down the cardboard, and fills dispensers, caddies and under-counter bins to par.

Wiping and sanitizing the workstation during and after the shift: clearing tongs, pans, scoops and trays off the counter, brushing crumbs and food debris, spraying and wiping prep tables, cutting boards, reach-in door handles, shelves and the exterior of equipment with sanitizer per the store's cleaning checklist, working around hot, live equipment.

End-of-shift cleaning of the cooking equipment at the station: scraping and degreasing the flat-top/grill, wiping down and boiling out or filtering the fryer, cleaning the toaster/conveyor, breaking down and washing removable parts of a shake or sandwich unit, and reassembling the station for the next shift.

Washing the station's smallwares in the dish area: greasy hotel pans, inserts, spatulas, tongs, scoops, baskets and utensils are carried to the dish sink/machine, scraped, racked, run, and returned to the station.

Stocking and rotating display cases and holding equipment: refilling a customer-facing grab-and-go or bottled-drink cooler from case stock, and loading heated holding cabinets or pastry/food display cases with cooked product, rotating older product forward and pulling items past hold time.

tasks.label: Prepare dough, following recipe.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-store pizza dough at a QSR pizza chain: scale flour, water, yeast, oil and sugar per the chain's recipe card, run a spiral/planetary mixer to a set time and dough temperature, dump the dough, divide and hand-ball to target weight, oil and tray the balls, cross-stack and move to the walk-in to retard. Done once or twice a shift in a standard chain kitchen.

Buttermilk biscuit dough at a fast-food breakfast chain: pour a bagged biscuit mix and measured buttermilk into a bowl/mixer, mix and fold briefly by hand, turn out onto a floured board, roll or pat to a set thickness, cut with a hand cutter, and pan the rounds. Repeated in small batches every 20-30 minutes during the breakfast daypart.

Yeast-raised sweet dough at a donut/coffee QSR or a pizza chain's side-item station: mix donut, cinnamon-roll or breadstick dough from mix plus water/yeast, let it rest, then sheet/extrude and cut or roll pieces, pan and move to the proofer.

Flour tortilla / masa / flatbread dough at a fast-casual Mexican or Mediterranean unit: mix flour or masa harina with water, fat and salt to the right feel, rest, portion into balls, and press/griddle to order or in batches.

Larger dough batches at a chain commissary or a store's dedicated dough room supplying several stores: 100-300 lb mixer batches, bulk ingredient bins, divider/rounder use, trays racked and cooled, with weight and temperature checks logged.

Off-standard batch: a partial or corrected batch made by feel — adjusting hydration for humidity or flour lot, salvaging an over/under-mixed batch, or making a low-volume novelty dough (gluten-free crust, limited-time-offer item) on shared, busy equipment with no dedicated setup.

tasks.label: Order and take delivery of supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine scheduled distributor delivery (2-3x/week) at a standalone quick-service unit: driver rolls stacked cases in through the rear door on a hand truck; cook checks each line against the invoice, spot-checks frozen/refrigerated product condition and temperature, signs, then carts/carries 30-80 mixed cases (patty cases, fry boxes, buns, sauces, cups, paper) into the walk-in freezer, walk-in cooler and dry storage, stacking to FIFO order on wire shelving in a tight back-of-house.

Placing the order: walking the walk-in cooler, freezer and dry-storage racks with a count sheet or tablet, counting full cases, partial cases and opened containers, comparing on-hand to par levels and projected sales, then submitting the order through the supplier portal or POS ordering screen.

Small between-delivery drop during service hours: local bakery/produce/dairy vendor or a sister-store transfer leaves a few cases, racks or crates at the back door or by the counter; cook checks them against the packing slip, eyeballs freshness, and puts them away in the cooler or under-counter storage while the line is running.

Delivery with a problem: items short, wrong SKU, crushed/leaking cases, or frozen product arriving soft; cook inspects, refuses the item to the driver, marks the shortage/refusal on the invoice, notes the credit, notifies the manager or supplier, and adjusts the next order.

Delivery at a constrained or non-standard site: urban storefront where the truck double-parks and cases must be moved across a public sidewalk and through the dining room, or a mall food court / airport / stadium unit where goods arrive at a shared dock and are carted through public corridors and service elevators during trading hours.

tasks.label: Mix ingredients, such as pancake or waffle batters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Breakfast batter batch in a QSR/fast-food kitchen: worker pulls a bag of pancake/waffle dry mix from dry storage, scales or scoops it into a Cambro or mixer bowl, adds measured water/eggs/oil, whisks or runs a countertop mixer until lump-free, then transfers to squeeze bottles or a waffle-batter dispenser and dates/refrigerates it. Done at open or during breakfast daypart, on a shared prep table next to other cooks.

Beverage base batches: mixing lemonade/iced tea/fruit-punch concentrate with water in a dispenser urn or bulk container, reconstituting shake or smoothie base powder with milk/water, or filling a blender with base plus flavoring for frozen drinks. Ratios per brand spec, mixed with a paddle, immersion blender, or the dispenser's own agitator, then loaded into the front-counter dispenser.

Cold-prep combining in a tub: chicken/tuna salad, coleslaw, pico or guacamole, seasoned taco meat — dumping pre-portioned components (protein, dressing/mayo, chopped veg, spice packet) into a bus tub or bowl and folding with a paddle or gloved hands until uniform without breaking down soft solids, then panning into a walk-in.

Sauces, dressings and marinades built from a recipe card: measuring liquids, oils, and dry seasoning blends into a container and whisking to emulsify/disperse, or tossing cooked product (wings, chips, fries) with sauce or seasoning in a bowl or tumbler during service.

Breading and fry-batter mixing: combining seasoned flour/breader in a dredge pan, mixing wet batter (tempura, corn-meal, buttermilk) to spec, and topping up/re-tempering the batter to keep viscosity and level correct through a rush at the fry station.

tasks.label: Monitor and record food temperatures to ensure food safety.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-cook verification in a school/hospital/college production kitchen: after batch-cooking entrees (roast chicken, meatloaf, casseroles, soups) the cook inserts a calibrated stem/thermocouple probe into the thickest part of several pans or pieces, confirms the item reached its required endpoint (e.g., 165F poultry, 155F ground meat), returns undercooked pans to the oven, and writes the reading, time and item on the HACCP production log.

Hot-holding checks during meal service on the cafeteria/serving line and in transport carts to satellite sites or patient floors: every 1-2 hours the cook probes food in each steam-table well or holding cabinet, verifies >=135F, discards or reheats out-of-range product, and records each well's temperature on the holding log. Line is crowded with servers and diners nearby.

Cold-holding checks: probing chilled items on the cold line, salad bar, milk cooler and reach-ins during service (deli salads, cut melon, milk, dressings), verifying <=41F, and recording readings on the cold-holding log.

Storage-unit readings: at the start and end ... shift, reading the walk-in cooler, freezer and reach-in unit thermometers (dial/digital gauges) and transcribing the values onto the daily temperature log, reporting units that are out of range.

Cooling and reheating verification: probing bulk cooked food (chili, rice, sauces, roasts) as it cools in shallow pans, ice baths or a blast chiller at ~2-hour intervals to prove the 135-70-41F cooling schedule, and probing reheated leftovers to 165F, logging each time/temperature pair.

Receiving deliveries at the dock/back door: probing between cases or into product on incoming refrigerated and frozen loads (milk crates, boxed meat, frozen vegetables, fresh produce), verifying temperatures against spec, rejecting out-of-temp product, and recording readings on the receiving log.

sources.title: Automated Core Temperature Probe | CME Automation Systems
sources.claim: CME Automation Systems markets an Automated Core Temperature Probe: an in-line machine that automatically samples product from a food production line, measures core temperature without an operator, sterilises and self-calibrates the probe, logs the data tamper-proof and raises alarms on out-of-spec temperatures.
sources.transferJustification: Same task as the cook's: measuring the internal temperature of cooked food and creating the food-safety record. Objects (cooked meat/RTE portions) and required precision (core temperature to fractions of a degree at a CCP) are comparable; it operates as a fixed, fenced in-line cell.

sources.system: Automated core temperature measurement system (CME Ltd / Industrial Technologies Ltd, McQueen Cairns)

sources.claim: Trade press describing the same automated core-temperature system reports that it removes product from the line at programmable intervals, uses machine vision to place the probe correctly and to a set depth/dwell, generates an electronic record in place of paper, and alarms on under/over-cooked product; at the January 2021 date the first unit had not yet been built.
sources.transferJustification: Describes the mechanism of the same probing-and-recording task the cook performs (probe placement in the correct position, dwell time, electronic record), substantiating that the machine performs the measurement act rather than only holding a sensor.

sources.title: Flippy the Burger Flipping Robot Is Now Cooking at the CaliBurger Fast Food Chain | KTLA
sources.claim: Flippy, deployed commercially in CaliBurger restaurant kitchens, autonomously senses patty and grill temperature with thermal imaging and 3-D vision to decide when to flip and remove burgers; it measures surface temperature for doneness control and does not probe internal temperature or produce a food-safety temperature log.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-kitchen (E2) automated food-temperature sensing: same broad purpose (knowing food temperature during cooking) in a human commercial kitchen, but non-contact surface sensing for cook control, so it does not deliver the internal-temperature reading and record the task requires.

sources.title: Karakuri unveils its first robotic canteen set to change the global food and hospitality industry
sources.claim: Karakuri's DK-One robotic canteen, unveiled as a pre-production machine for workplace catering, holds ingredients in its own hoppers and provides real-time monitoring of ingredient temperatures with health-and-safety data logging; it monitors only food inside the machine, not food held in a kitchen's ovens, wells or coolers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated holding-temperature monitoring and food-safety logging inside a human canteen (E2). It substantiates only self-monitoring of food inside the machine's own hoppers, not the cook's task of measuring temperatures of food held across a serving line.

tasks.label: Cook foodstuffs according to menus, special dietary or nutritional restrictions, or numbers of portions to be served.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: K-12 school cafeteria: cook/batch-heat the day's menu items (entrées, casseroles, chicken pieces, vegetables, pasta) for several hundred servings from a production record, using convection/combi ovens, steamers and tilt skillets; pans loaded and pulled by hand, temps logged, timed to two or three lunch waves.

Hospital or long-term-care kitchen: cook multiple medium and small batches to therapeutic and nutritional specifications (low sodium, carb-controlled, renal, texture-modified/pureed) alongside the regular menu, matching diet-office counts for patient trays and holding to strict temperature and timing standards.

College dining hall or corporate cafeteria hot line: batch-cook soups, sauces, stir-fries, roasted proteins and vegetables in kettles, tilt skillets and ovens; taste and adjust seasoning, judge doneness, and re-fire small batches continuously through a two-hour service.
Cafeteria fry station during service: drop and time baskets of fries, tots, breaded chicken and onion rings from frozen, shake, drain, salt and hold to order volume through the lunch rush.

Cafeteria grill/griddle and made-to-order station: cook burgers, chicken breasts, eggs, pancakes, grilled sandwiches and made-to-order bowls/pasta to individual customer requests during service, adjusting doneness per order.

Correctional facility or central production kitchen: high-volume standardized-recipe cooking (hundreds to thousands of portions) in steam kettles, braising pans and large ovens, often on a cook-chill cycle with strict HACCP records and portion counts.

tasks.label: Rotate and store food supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: A truck delivery of dry goods arrives at a school/hospital cafeteria: the cook breaks down the pallet or hand-truck load of mixed cases (#10 cans, 25-50 lb sacks of flour/rice, boxes of pasta, condiment cases), carries them into the dry storeroom, pulls existing stock forward, places new cases behind or below it on wire shelving of varying heights, and marks receipt dates.

Refrigerated and frozen delivery put-away: cases of milk, produce boxes, raw meat/poultry and frozen cases are moved into the walk-in cooler and freezer within the required time window, stacked by food-safety order (raw below ready-to-eat), older product rotated to the front and new product to the back, in 35F/0F spaces with wet floors and tight aisles.

End-of-service storage of prepared food and leftovers: transferring hot/cold prepared items from steam-table pans and kettles into storage pans or containers, covering, applying a date/use-by label, and placing them in the correct cooler location in rotation order.

Routine rotation/date audit of dry storage and walk-ins: walking the shelves, reading date labels, checking produce and dairy for spoilage, pulling expired or damaged items for disposal or credit, consolidating partial cases, and straightening/wiping shelves.

During-service replenishment: moving packaged product and prepped stock from bulk storage to reach-in coolers, beverage cases and prep-line refrigeration, placing new stock behind existing product so the oldest is used first.

tasks.label: Wash pots, pans, dishes, utensils, or other cooking equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-service dish room in a school or hospital cafeteria: worker scrapes and racks several hundred plates, compartment trays, bowls, cups and flatware from bus tubs and the soiled-dish table, runs them through a rack-conveyor or flight-type dish machine, then unloads, sorts and stacks clean sanitized ware on carts. High peak throughput, hot and wet, mixed food soils.

Heavy cookware washed by hand at the three-compartment pot sink after cooking: 40-qt stockpots, steam-table/hotel pans, sheet pans, roasting pans, kettle inserts with baked-on, burnt or starchy residue. Scrape, soak, scrub with pads/green scour, rinse, chemical or hot-water sanitize, air-dry on the rack; items too large for the dish machine.

Smallwares washed continuously during prep and cooking: knives, cutting boards, mixing bowls, whisks, ladles, tongs, measuring cups, food-processor bowls and blender jars, cleaned and sanitized between uses at the prep sink (allergen/raw-protein changeovers) and returned to service mid-recipe, interleaved with cooking.

Cleaning powered cooking and prep equipment: disassembling the 60-qt mixer, slicer, buffalo chopper or grinder, carrying removable parts to the sink or washer, washing and sanitizing them, scrubbing and wiping fixed bodies, steam kettles, tilt skillets, steamers and grills in place, then reassembling for the next shift.

Washing bulk transport and holding equipment in the pot room or wash bay: sheet-pan racks, food-transport and insulated tray-delivery carts, ingredient bins and lugs, milk crates — pressure-rinsed or run through a rack/cart washer, then drained and returned to storage.

instances.label: End-of-shift cleaning of large cooking equipment in a school/hospital/corrections kitchen: scraping and degreasing flat-top griddles and ranges, wiping out combi ovens and racks, scrubbing steam-jacketed kettles and tilt skillets, boiling out and filtering fryers, cleaning grease trays and backsplashes. Baked-on carbon, hot surfaces, caustic chemicals, tight aisles.

Cleaning and sanitizing work surfaces during and after production: stainless prep tables cluttered with pans and containers, cutting boards, sinks, shelving, cooler door handles; scrape debris, wash with detergent, rinse, apply quat/chlorine sanitizer at correct concentration, air dry. Repeated between tasks under time pressure.

Breaking down, washing, sanitizing and reassembling small appliances: meat slicer (guard, blade, carriage), mixer bowls and attachments, food processor, immersion blender, can opener, coffee brewer; hand-wash or run parts through the dish machine, then reassemble and verify guards operate.

Kitchen and servery floor and drain cleaning after service: sweeping food debris, degreasing and scrubbing quarry tile under and around equipment, lifting and hosing rubber floor mats, cleaning floor drains and grease traps, hauling trash and washing bins.

Inspection rounds to ensure functional operation: recording cooler/freezer and hot-holding temperatures, verifying dish machine wash/rinse temperatures and sanitizer strength with test strips, checking gaskets, pilot lights, thermostats, slicer blade condition, spotting leaks or frayed cords, completing HACCP/sanitation checklists and reporting faults for repair.

Cleaning the serving line and beverage area: draining and scrubbing steam-table wells, hot-holding and refrigerated display cabinets, sneeze guards, tray rails, milk coolers, ice machine bins and beverage dispenser nozzles; descaling and sanitizing.

Ongoing on-shift coaching during the trainee's first weeks: observing work at speed during meal service, correcting errors, giving feedback, and signing off a competency checklist for the supervisor.

Receiving a distributor delivery at the dock/back door: counting cases off the pallet against the invoice, checking case counts, damage and refrigerated/frozen product temperatures, noting shorts and credits, and entering receipts into the stock record.

Smallwares and equipment inventory: counting sheet pans, hotel pans, Cambros, serving utensils and knives across storage racks and dish areas, and checking that mixers, slicers, warmers and their parts are present, complete and working; recording missing/broken items.

Full count of a large central storeroom or district commissary warehouse: palletized cases in racking with case labels in ambient and freezer rooms, counted and reconciled against the inventory system.

roles.title: Cooks, Private Household
roles.description: Prepare meals in private homes. Includes personal chefs.

tasks.label: Peel, wash, trim, and cook vegetables and meats, and bake breads and pastries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily mise en place in the employer's home kitchen: peeling potatoes/carrots, washing and spinning salad greens and herbs, coring and trimming lettuce, broccoli and green beans in small mixed quantities on the household's counters, with the family's own knives, sink and cutting boards.
Meat prep in the home kitchen: trimming fat and silverskin from steaks and roasts, breaking down a whole chicken or fish, portioning cuts to the household's serving sizes on a home cutting board.

Cooking the household's main meal on the client's own range and oven: sautéing and roasting proteins and vegetables, simmering sauces, seasoning and adjusting to the family's taste, timed so everything is hot at the family's dinner hour.
Baking in the household kitchen: yeast bread or rolls, plus a pie, tart, muffins or cookies — mixing, kneading, proofing, shaping, and baking in the household's domestic oven.

Weekly batch meal-prep service performed in a rented licensed commissary or a client's commercial-grade kitchen: cooking five to ten dishes in quantity from prepped ingredients and portioning them into labeled containers for the week.
Special-occasion multi-course dinner in the client's home for guests: coordinated courses, fine plating and garnishing, guest dietary restrictions and on-the-fly substitutions, served to a timetable.

sources.system: TOMRA Eco Steam Peeler / TOMRA Peeling Line
sources.title: TOMRA Eco Steam Peeler | PotatoPro
sources.claim: TOMRA's steam peeling line autonomously peels potatoes and a wide range of vegetables, adapting to variation in incoming produce without operator intervention, on a purpose-built conveyor-fed processing line.
sources.transferJustification: Same operation as the task's 'peel' element on the same objects (potatoes, carrots, root vegetables), but with the produce delivered in bulk on a purpose-built line rather than handled piece by piece at a kitchen sink.

sources.title: How the best steam peelers can significantly reduce food waste on vegetable processing lines
sources.claim: Steam peeling machines of this type are in widespread industrial operation worldwide, i.e. deployed rather than experimental.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment maturity for the peeling evidence above.

sources.system: KRONEN processing and packaging line for lettuce and vegetables (GS 10-2 cutter, GEWA/HEWA washer, KS 100 spin dryer)
sources.title: Processing lines for lettuce & vegetables – KRONEN
sources.claim: KRONEN supplies automated complete lines that core, cut, wash, dry, weigh and pack lettuce and vegetables without hand work at those stations.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the 'wash' and 'trim' (coring, stem removal) elements of the task on the same vegetables a household cook handles, performed on a fixture-and-conveyor line.

sources.title: U.S. retailer installs fresh-cut fruit and vegetable processing lines | FreshPlaza
sources.claim: A US retailer has installed KRONEN fresh-cut fruit and vegetable processing lines combining cutting machines, conveyors, washing machines and spin dryers, showing real deployment of automated wash/cut lines.
sources.transferJustification: Deployment evidence for automated washing/cutting of produce; note the same article shows irregular whole produce is still hand-trimmed at human trimming tables, bounding the capability to line-fed commodity work.

sources.title: A review of robotic and automated systems in meat processing | Frontiers in Robotics and AI
sources.claim: Mayekawa's HAMDAS-RX robot performs automated deboning of pork ham, including bone extraction, at industrial rates in meat plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic butchery. Boning and cutting raw meat with knife/blade end-effectors under vision guidance covers the 'trim meats' element on comparable objects and requires equal or greater cutting precision, but only with the carcass fixtured on a purpose-built line.

sources.system: Scott Automation rib-scribing robot / ROC robotic primal cutter
sources.title: Robotics and sensing technologies in red meat processing: A review — ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Scott Automation's robotic system performs vision-guided saw cuts on beef carcasses in processing plants, and robotic primal cutting/boning systems are installed commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated carcass breakdown. Demonstrates machine-controlled cutting/portioning of raw meat with vision guidance, the industrial analogue of trimming and portioning cuts, in a fixtured plant cell.

sources.title: Robotic kitchen in a box cooks, cleans and serves 120 meals an hour | Interesting Engineering
sources.claim: Circus SE's CA-1 is a glass-enclosed robotic kitchen cell that collects ingredients from its own stores, cooks, plates and cleans without a human cook, and has been placed in operation inside a REWE supermarket.

sources.title: Automated cooking at REWE supermarket: Robot Circus — EuroShop
sources.claim: The CA-1 installation at REWE Düsseldorf controls the whole cooking process from ingredients through serving, with customers ordering at a terminal.

sources.title: BreadBot maker raises $3 million in seed round | Baking Business
sources.claim: The BreadBot is an enclosed automated bread bakery that mixes, forms, proofs, bakes ... loaves on its own after ingredients are loaded into its hoppers; the first commercial unit was deployed into a grocery store.

sources.title: Croissant production with RONDO croissant lines
sources.claim: RONDO's croissant machinery sheets, cuts and curls laminated dough to produce croissants and other pastries automatically at artisanal quality, and fully automatic bakery production lines are sold for bread, donuts and croissants.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the 'bake pastries' element: laminated-dough make-up and baking, the same product a household cook would bake, produced on a purpose-built dough line.

sources.title: Miso Robotics Reveals Updated Flippy Robot | Hospitality Technology
sources.claim: Flippy 2 works an entire restaurant fry station in real quick-service kitchens (White Castle), identifying binned food with AI vision, frying it and moving it to holding without human intervention mid-process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cooking a protein item to a set standard. Shows the current ceiling for robots working inside an ordinary human commercial kitchen — a single fry station fed with pre-portioned frozen items, not general stove-top cooking.

sources.title: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly | AgFunderNews
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' arms portion and assemble multi-ingredient meals into containers at food manufacturers at production volume.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning cooked food into containers, the closing step of batch meal-prep; same foods and containers, performed at fixed line stations with trays presented by conveyor.

sources.title: A $105,000 robot arm nobody needs cooked me a delicious lunch — Engadget
sources.claim: The only marketed home 'robotic chef' requires humans to pre-prepare ingredients and place them in pots at fixed positions, its arm lacks vision/sensing, and no unit had been installed in a customer home as of the review.

tasks.label: Cool, package, label, and freeze foods for later consumption and provide instructions for reheating.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Personal chef doing a weekly cook-day in a client's private home kitchen: after cooking 5-10 dishes, portions each into the client's assorted glass/plastic containers, cools them on the counter or in the fridge, snaps or screws lids on, hand-writes or prints labels with dish name and date, stacks them in the household fridge/freezer, and leaves a written card of reheating instructions.

Household cook packaging surplus food and leftovers after the family's daily meal service in the employer's home kitchen: irregular quantities of roast meat, sides, rice and salads scraped from serving dishes into whatever containers or freezer bags are on hand, cooled, labeled with masking tape, and put in the freezer with a note on reheating.

Personal chef batch-cooking for several clients in a rented licensed commissary/commercial kitchen: portions meals into deli containers or vacuum-seal pouches, blast-chills, applies printed labels with contents, date and heating directions, freezes in a reach-in freezer, and packs coolers for delivery with reheating sheets.

Freezing liquid and specialty preparations at the employer's home: stocks, soups, sauces and baby-food purees ladled into jars, cube trays or zip bags, headspace left, cooled in an ice bath, labeled with quantity and date, laid flat to freeze, with thaw/reheat guidance for the caregiver.

Make-ahead meals for a family's travel or an event at the employer's home: casseroles and entrees assembled in disposable foil pans or the family's bakeware, cooled, covered with foil/wrap, labeled with detailed oven temperature and time instructions, and frozen for later use by the family or a house sitter.

sources.title: Breaking: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-driven meal-assembly robot arms are commercially deployed on ready-meal production lines at food manufacturers, autonomously depositing cooked ingredients into meal trays across a high-mix product range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning cooked food into meal containers. It is the portioning/packing step of this task, on the same objects (cooked dishes, proteins, sauces) and at the portion tolerances a household cook uses.

sources.system: Chef Robotics robots integrated with Packline tray-sealing systems (Cafe Spice line)
sources.title: Chef Robotics and Packline Partner on End-to-End Meal Production Automation
sources.claim: A combined Chef Robotics + Packline installation forms an end-to-end automated line in which trays are de-nested and conveyed, robots deposit cooked food into compartments, and the trays are automatically sealed; running in production at Cafe Spice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling and hermetically sealing portioned cooked meals. This is the 'package' step; the containers are equivalent to a chef's portion containers and are closed to a sealed, freezer-ready state.

sources.title: Food Safety Compliance Automatic Labeling Machine
sources.claim: Automatic print-and-apply labeling machines place compliance labels carrying date codes, allergen and storage/handling instructions onto ready-to-eat containers and meal trays as they pass on a line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: variable-data label printing and application on food packs. It delivers the 'label' step and the written storage/reheating instructions the chef otherwise hand-writes.

sources.title: Spiral Immersion — FPS Food Process Solutions
sources.claim: Conveyor-based spiral chilling/freezing systems automatically chill and freeze packaged food products in line, without manual handling of each pack.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: rapid chilling and freezing of packaged portions. It performs the 'cool' and 'freeze' steps on sealed containers of cooked food, the same objects and the same food-safety endpoint the chef must reach.

sources.system: pi-0.5 vision-language-action model on a mobile manipulator
sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: The most capable generalist home-manipulation model reported operating in previously unseen real homes succeeds only intermittently on multi-step kitchen chores, well short of employer-acceptable reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: multi-step tidying and manipulation in unseen home kitchens. It bounds what is achievable in a private kitchen (E3): partial success on simple object handling, with no demonstrated container filling, lidding, labeling or freezer loading.

sources.title: Figure AI's Helix 02 Completes 4-Minute Autonomous Kitchen Task, Setting New Humanoid Robotics Benchmark
sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid autonomy in a full-size kitchen is demonstrated on a staged dishwasher loading/unloading sequence, not on portioning, sealing, labeling and freezing food.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous multi-step work in a human kitchen. It is the nearest home-kitchen capability found, but handles rigid dishware rather than deformable cooked food, lids, labels or freezer loading, so it does not substantiate this task at E2/E3.

tasks.label: Shop for or order food and kitchen supplies and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weekly main grocery run for the household's menu plan: chef drives to a supermarket or supercenter, works a list of ~40-80 items (packaged staples, dairy, chilled meat, pre-packed produce), compares brands/prices/dates, checks out and pays on the employer's account, loads the car, and carries bags into the client's kitchen; includes occasional same-day top-up trips for a missed ingredient.

Ordering rather than shopping: building an order from the menu plan and a pantry/fridge inventory and placing it online or by phone with a grocery delivery service, produce purveyor or meat/seafood supplier, then receiving the delivery at the residence, checking it against the order, and rejecting or flagging substitutions and damaged goods.

Hand-selected fresh shopping at a farmers market, fishmonger or butcher counter: judging individual specimens by ripeness, firmness, smell, colour and marbling, asking for custom cuts or portioning, buying by weight from vendors, and swapping menu items to whatever looks best that day.

Specialty errands for named items: cheese shop, ethnic grocer, spice and imported pantry goods, bakery, wine and spirits - buying specified SKUs or vendor-recommended equivalents rather than grading quality, then transporting them to the residence.

Bulk restock of staples and kitchen consumables at a warehouse club or restaurant-supply store: cases of oil, flour, paper goods, foil, cleaning supplies and storage containers; heavy cartons onto a flatbed cart, checkout, load and unload.

Purchasing kitchen equipment and smallwares: evaluating and buying pans, knives, sheet trays, a stand mixer or small appliance in a restaurant-supply store or online, arranging payment and delivery, transporting and unboxing the item at the residence.

sources.system: Ocado On-Grid Robotic Pick (OGRP) with Ocado bot fleet / OSP customer fulfilment centres
sources.title: The technology Re:Imagining online grocery - Ocado Group
sources.claim: Ocado's On-Grid Robotic Pick arms assemble customer grocery orders (picking and packing individual grocery items from the storage grid into customer bags/totes) in commercial operation across 14 fulfilment centres for eight retail partners, with over 350 million picks and about 50% of order volume at the Luton CFC picked robotically across a 45,000-SKU grocery range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = e-grocery order fulfilment. It is the acquisition half of 'shop for or order food': same objects (supermarket SKUs across a 45,000-item assortment), same output (a bagged order matching a list) at commercial accuracy, with the assortment brought to the machine - exactly the E1 counterfactual for shopping.

sources.title: Ocado's AI-powered robotic arms: Levelling efficiency
sources.claim: OGRP is described by its developer as a robust autonomous system using machine vision and machine learning that picks and packs products with no prior model of them, fulfilling customer orders without human touch ....
sources.transferJustification: Establishes autonomy (not teleoperation or step-by-step scripting) for the grocery order-assembly system cited above.

sources.system: Ocado OGRP at Kroger customer fulfillment centers
sources.title: Kroger to deploy Ocado robotic pickers at fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Kroger is deploying Ocado's on-grid robotic pickers in its US customer fulfilment centres; the arms traverse the grid selecting the items on customer orders.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (grocery order assembly) in a US commercial setting, confirming the capability is not confined to one UK site.

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm picks individual products of widely varying shape and size out of inventory bins in fulfillment centers, handling millions of distinct item types.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = piece-picking general merchandise into customer orders. Kitchen smallwares, boxed equipment and non-food supplies are the same class of rigid retail goods, so procuring a specified item from an assortment transfers directly in a purpose-built pick cell.

sources.title: These retail robots travel through store aisles, scanning shelves for inventory and insights (Fast Company)
sources.claim: The robots actually deployed inside US supermarkets navigate the sales floor autonomously but only scan shelves for inventory and pricing data; they do not pick items, build baskets or check out.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of the art for autonomous robots working the aisles of a structured retail facility (E2) - shelf auditing only - which is why in-store shopping at E2 is not substantiated.

sources.title: Starship Technologies Doubles Down on Grocery Delivery in EU and US Markets
sources.claim: Starship's sidewalk robots complete grocery deliveries fully autonomously on public sidewalks at commercial scale (over 10 million deliveries, 3,000+ robots), covering the transport leg from store to residence but not selection or purchase of the items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = last-mile grocery transport, one leg of a shopping trip. It shows the haul leg is solved at E3, but the robot never selects, inspects or pays for goods, so it cannot carry the whole task.

sources.title: Helix: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Generalist Humanoid Control
sources.claim: Figure's Helix VLA model showed two humanoids autonomously putting away unfamiliar groceries in a kitchen; this is a laboratory demonstration of home-side grocery handling, not a deployment with evidence of worker-level reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = handling grocery items in a home kitchen, the residence end of a shopping trip. It is a staged demo without reliability evidence, so it cannot support an E3 judgment.

tasks.label: Prepare meals in private homes according to employers' recipes or tastes, handling all meals for the family and possibly for other household staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weekday family dinner in the employer's home kitchen built around a single cooked main: curry, stew, stir-fry, pasta, soup or braise served with rice or bread. Cook washes, peels and chops raw produce, browns and simmers on the household range, seasons to the family's taste, serves at a set hour.

Weekday family dinner with multiple components: roasted or grilled protein plus two hot sides and a dressed salad, timed so everything is ready together, carved/portioned and plated on the family's dishes.

Personal-chef weekly batch session in a client's home: cook four to six multi-serving dishes (proteins, grains, roasted vegetables, sauces) in one visit using the client's own range, oven and pans, portion into containers, label with reheating notes, clean the kitchen.

Everyday breakfasts, lunches and simple meals for the family and other household staff: eggs and toast to order, sandwiches, salads, soups, snacks for children, made on demand at varying times in the household kitchen.

Meals prepared to strict dietary specifications set by the employer (severe allergy avoidance, gluten-free, low-sodium/medical, kosher or halal practice, elimination diets), requiring exact ingredient control and avoidance of cross-contact, otherwise ordinary home cooking.

Dinner party or holiday entertaining at the residence: multi-course menu for guests, canapes, courses fired and plated to the pace of service, garnishing and presentation to the employer's standard, coordination with serving staff.

sources.title: Circus SE completes first production of CA-1 robots in high-volume facility - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Circus SE's CA-1 is an autonomous cooking cell whose robotic arms dispense ingredients from refrigerated silos, cook in induction pots and plate the finished meal in three to four minutes; it is in industrial production and delivery.

sources.system: Circus SE CA-1 ('Fresh & Smart' at REWE)
sources.title: Automated cooking at REWE supermarket: Robot Circus - EuroShop
sources.claim: A CA-1 robot has been deployed in a REWE supermarket in Duesseldorf where it cooks fresh hot meals on demand from refrigerated ingredients after customers order digitally, with no human cook at the station.

sources.title: Botinkit's AI-Powered Wok Robot Seeks to Revolutionize Restaurant Kitchens in Asia and Beyond
sources.claim: Botinkit's Omni/ChefBot is a commercially sold automated wok station deployed in restaurant and hotel kitchens; a chef cooks a dish once and the machine records and reproduces the recipe, running stir-fries and stews hands-off with automatic seasoning dispensing.

sources.title: Posha (company) - Wikipedia
sources.claim: Posha is a shipping countertop cooking robot for homes: the user loads chopped ingredients into hoppers and selects a recipe, and the machine then dispenses, stirs and controls heat by itself, with a library of 500+ dishes and tolerance for ingredient substitutions.

sources.title: Physical AI Company Chef Robotics Completes 100 Million Servings in Production
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' arms have autonomously portioned and assembled more than 100 million servings of prepared meals in customer food-production facilities since 2022; the company states it avoided commercial kitchens because those tasks remain too complex for robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning cooked proteins, grains and vegetables into meal containers is the portion-and-pack half of a batch meal-prep session; same deformable foods, same containers, same accuracy requirement.

sources.title: Miso partners with Roboworx on restaurant automation solutions
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy Fry Station autonomously cooks fried items (fries, onion rings, chicken, tacos) ... was operational in roughly 20 quick-service restaurant locations including Jack in the ... in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fry-station cooking shows a robot holding an entire hot-cooking step to commercial quality, but only inside a purpose-built station with automated hoppers, which is why it supports E1 rather than free operation of a human kitchen.

sources.title: Figure AI's Helix 02 Completes 4-Minute Autonomous Kitchen Task, Setting New Humanoid Robotics Benchmark
sources.claim: The frontier of general-purpose autonomous manipulation in an ordinary, unmodified kitchen is dish handling: Figure's Helix 02 ran a complete dishwasher load/unload sequence in a full-sized kitchen without human intervention; no comparable system cooks a meal there.
sources.transferJustification: Boundary evidence: dishwasher loading in a normal kitchen is the closest demonstrated autonomous work in an unmodified (E2/E3) kitchen; it involves rigid crockery, not knife work, heat control or seasoning, so it does not transfer to cooking a meal.

sources.title: CES 2026: Autonomous kitchens | VML
sources.claim: Countertop cooking robots let a household enter its own recipes: at CES 2026 Nosh demonstrated a machine where ingredients are placed in the unit and it measures and adds them at the right time, with 500+ recipes and user-programmable recipes.

tasks.label: Keep records pertaining to menus, finances, and other business-related issues.
