tasks.label: Stock, organize, and clean kitchens and cooking utensils.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: After serving a family dinner in a client's private home, the chef clears and cleans the tableware and small utensils: scraping plates, rinsing glasses and flatware, loading and running the household dishwasher, hand-washing the few items that can't go in, and unloading/drying. Ordinary residential kitchen, no commercial dish machine.

Hand-washing cookware and tools that cannot go in the dishwasher: greasy saute pans, stockpots, sheet trays, cast iron/carbon steel, chef's knives, cutting boards, blender and food-processor parts; scrub, rinse, dry and set aside. Done at a residential sink between and after cooking.

End-of-cooking wipe-down of the kitchen: clearing ingredients and appliances off counters, wiping counters and backsplash, cleaning the cooktop/range of splatter and grease (occasionally degreasing hood filters or oven spills), scrubbing the sink, wiping appliance fronts, and emptying the kitchen trash and recycling.

Floor care in the client's kitchen at the end of the shift: sweeping crumbs, vegetable trimmings and spilled flour, and mopping up spills and grease spots around the range and prep area, working around furniture, pet bowls and family traffic.

Stocking after a shopping trip or grocery delivery: carrying in bags/crates, putting dry staples on pantry shelves, refrigerating and freezing perishables (produce, eggs, dairy, meat, deli), rotating older stock forward, discarding spoiled items, and refilling salt/oil/spice containers in a home pantry and fridge of the household's own design.

Organizing storage: putting clean dishes, glassware, flatware, pans and tools back into their assigned cabinets, drawers and racks; tidying and re-arranging the pantry and spice shelf; laying out the equipment needed for the next meal service in the household's idiosyncratic kitchen layout.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics' three-arm dishwashing system runs autonomously 24/7 in real restaurant dish rooms, picking dirty plates, cups and silverware out of bus tubs, loading and pushing in dish-machine racks, with only occasional staff intervention prompted by an on-screen alert.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (washing dishes, glassware and flatware) but in a commercial dish room; the article notes the human dishwasher was moved to prep and pots and pans, indicating cookware is still hand-washed by people.

sources.title: Nala Robotics Introduces Autonomous Dishwasher (Perishable News)
sources.claim: Nala Robotics' Spotless is an AI-enabled robotic dishwashing cell added to professional kitchens that scrubs, rinses, dries, stacks and stores cookware, cutlery, dishware and glassware; the company says it is being deployed in restaurants and senior living venues.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers washing cookware/utensils and storing clean wares, the same objects a household cook handles, but as a fixed machine cell to which wares are brought.

sources.title: Robot automates dishwashing in commercial kitchens | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Dishcraft Robotics built a purpose-built automated dish-cleaning machine in which humans wheel carts of pre-stacked dirty dishes into the unit and a robot arm picks, scrubs, rinses, inspects and stacks each item; used for corporate food service clients.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (cleaning and stacking dishware) executed in a machine-centred cell with custom magnetic-base dishes, illustrating what dish cleaning looks like when the environment is built around the robot.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom cleaning robot autonomously cleans fixtures and floors, disinfects, vacuum-dries and picks up trash in mapped restrooms of office buildings during normal facility operations, sold as a monthly service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spraying, scrubbing and drying hard surfaces and fixtures in a room. It shows machine-executed surface cleaning of standardized, uncluttered fixtures; kitchen counters loaded with appliances, food and utensils are not covered.

sources.title: Worlds leading autonomous floor scrubbing robot (Avidbots Neo 2W)
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo is a fully ... deployed at scale in airports, warehouses, manufacturing sites, ..., mapping the facility and cleaning without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sweeping/scrubbing floors of a working facility. Same physical action (debris pickup and wet mopping) on floors kept to an institutional standard; not demonstrated on a cluttered residential kitchen floor.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocking robot was mass-produced for 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, autonomously replenishing refrigerated shelves with bottled and ... drinks, with remote operators taking over only when an error such as a dropped or misplaced item occurs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stocking shelves with grocery items. Comparable objects (packaged drinks) and placement precision, but limited to known bottle/can SKUs on a rail-mounted arm at fixed cooler shelves.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics reveals RightPick 3 item-handling robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Fleets of RightHand Robotics RightPick piece-picking cells work autonomously in fulfillment centers, grasping a high volume of diverse consumer packaged goods from totes and placing them at designated destinations; RightPick 4 extended the SKU range and item weight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring individual packaged goods from a presented tote into designated storage positions - the manipulation core of putting groceries away - in a fixtured, machine-built cell.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization (pi0.5)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 vision-language-action model drives a mobile manipulator to clean ... in real homes not seen in training - closing cabinets, putting items in drawers, wiping spills and placing dishes in the sink - but the developers state the model is far from perfect and frequently errs.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (kitchen tidying/cleaning) in real private homes, but a research demo with acknowledged frequent errors, not output an employer would accept in place of a cook's.

sources.title: Figure humanoid robots use Helix VLA model to demonstrate household chores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Two Figure 02 humanoids running the Helix VLA model autonomously put away groceries they had not seen before in a kitchen setting after a single prompt, identifying objects and placing them in appropriate locations - a lab demonstration, not a deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the grocery put-away portion of stocking a kitchen, but a staged single demonstration in the developer's facility with no reliability or throughput data.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid - The Robot Report
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, shipping to consumer homes, relies on teleoperation by remote human experts for household chores; commentators note no humanoid has yet shown an end-to-end household chore autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the same home-kitchen chores (dishwasher unloading, wiping counters) in the actual E3 setting, but under teleoperation, so it cannot support a positive judgment at E3.

tasks.label: Direct the operation and organization of kitchens and all food-related activities, including the presentation and serving of food.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Solo personal chef running the day's kitchen operation in a client's private home: sequencing the work, keeping bench and cooktop organized, then portioning finished dishes into containers or onto plates with attention to how each meal looks, labeling and refrigerating them.

Plating and serving a meal to the employing family at their dining table: composing plates and garnishing, timing courses, carrying and placing dishes in front of diners, refilling, clearing between courses.

Dinner party or holiday event in the residence with hired temporary help: directing setup, deciding and overseeing canape/buffet presentation, calling the timing of courses and the flow of service by the hired servers.

Keeping the household kitchen organized and to standard: setting up workstations, receiving and putting away grocery/produce deliveries, checking and rotating pantry and refrigerator stock, enforcing sanitation and equipment upkeep.
Large estate with kitchen staff: assigning prep work to an assistant cook, inspecting output against the household's standards, coordinating with butler/server on meal timing across residences.

sources.title: Chef Robotics completes 100M meal servings milestone - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' ChefOS-driven arms autonomously portion and assemble multiple variable food ingredients into meal trays on production lines, deployed at more than a ... with over 100 million servings produced; the company states commercial kitchens remain too complex for its robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning and arranging cooked components into meal trays. Same physical act as a private chef's portioning and plating of batch-cooked meals - same deformable foods and container-placement precision - so performance transfers to the presentation step of this task.

sources.system: Chef Robotics assembly line (with Packline packaging)
sources.title: Chef Robotics and Packline Partner on End-to-End Meal Production Automation | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: A Chef Robotics + Packline integrated meal-production line runs with only one QA person and ..., indicating the robotic assembly operates without step-by-step human control.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (meal portioning and packing); cited to establish limited-intervention autonomy of the plating line.

sources.title: Sweetgreen's automated makeline shows robots and humans can coexist | Restaurant Business
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen is a conveyor-and-dispenser makeline behind the restaurant counter that fills, dresses and mixes each customer's bowl automatically, with staff adding only a couple of finishing items before the bowl is handed over.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: composing and portioning a served dish and presenting the finished item to the diner at a service line. Comparable foods and portioning precision; covers the presentation and hand-off part of serving.

sources.title: Sweetgreen Goes All-In with Automated Restaurants - QSR Magazine
sources.claim: The Infinite Kitchen dispenses ingredients along a conveyor at up to 500 bowls, plates ... and Sweetgreen moved to roll it out across its restaurants.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as evidence 2; cited for throughput and commercial maturity of automated presentation and serving.

sources.title: Robots are waiting tables at an Italian restaurant in Howard County - The Banner
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi autonomously runs plated food and drinks to guests' tables and busses dishes in working restaurant dining rooms, navigating around diners with LiDAR and cameras; commercially sold and deployed in US restaurants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering plated courses from kitchen to diners. Same objects (plates, glasses) and a dining-room setting comparable to household table service, so it substantiates the transport half of serving in a structured facility.

sources.title: pi_0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization (arXiv)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 mobile manipulator autonomously tidies kitchens in homes it was not trained in (putting items away, wiping a spill, dishes to the sink), but this is a research demonstration rather than a deployed service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tidying and organizing a home kitchen. Closest published work to organizing a household kitchen; cited to show the capability exists only at research-demo level, not at worker quality.

sources.title: Introducing Helix 02: Full-Body Autonomy | Figure
sources.claim: Figure's Helix 02 humanoid autonomously unloaded and reloaded ... in a four-minute end-to-end task with no human intervention - a single-task demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: kitchen housekeeping in a human kitchen. Cited to show that general-purpose kitchen work by humanoids remains demo-stage, supporting negative E2/E3 judgments.

tasks.label: Specialize in preparing fancy dishes or food for special diets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Multi-course 'fancy' dinner for a client's guests, cooked and plated in the client's home kitchen: canapés, a plated entrée with pan-seared protein, a reduction sauce, garnishes and side components, dessert, all timed to service; ingredients from the client's fridge and the chef's shopping, on the home's own range and cookware.

Weekly batch meal-prep session in the client's home for a medically restricted diet (low-sodium/renal, diabetic, allergen-free): 12-20 portions of a handful of straightforward dishes (braises, curries, soups, grain bowls, roasted protein and vegetables), cooked from raw groceries, portioned into labeled containers, kitchen cleaned.

Everyday family dinner adapted to a dietary restriction (gluten-free, vegan, keto, nut-free): one main dish plus a side, cooked in the client's home kitchen from whatever produce and staples are on hand, served hot at a set time.

Personal chef cooking special-diet meals for several clients in a licensed commissary or shared commercial kitchen, then packing and labeling portioned meals for delivery; standard commercial ranges, sinks and worktables, premises controlled by the kitchen operator.

Specialty item requiring craft technique made in the client's home: fresh pasta, artisan bread, a plated dessert or celebration cake (often also allergen-free or sugar-free), shaped, baked/finished and decorated by hand.

sources.title: Robotic kitchen in a box cooks, cleans and serves 120 meals an hour
sources.claim: Circus SE's CA-1 Series 4 is a self-contained, glass-enclosed robotic kitchen that autonomously performs the whole meal-preparation cycle — fetching ingredients, cooking, plating and cleaning — and has been in commercial operation cooking customer orders inside a REWE supermarket in Düsseldorf since 29 October 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same activity — cooking and plating a portioned hot dish — but from pre-loaded chilled ingredient silos rather than a human kitchen's raw stores.

sources.title: Automated cooking in the supermarket with robot Circus at REWE
sources.claim: The CA-1's dish repertoire and ingredient handling: up to 36 chilled ingredients held in silos, up to five dishes cooked at once, self-cleaning utensils; menu covers pasta, soups, curries and sweet dishes such as porridge — i.e. one-vessel dishes assembled from pre-prepped components.
sources.transferJustification: Shows both the capability (cooked, plated dishes with exact ingredient control, suitable for diet-specific recipes) and its limits (one-vessel dishes from silo-presented ingredients).

sources.title: Breaking: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI meal-assembly arms are deployed on production lines at food manufacturers including Sunbasket and Amy's Kitchen, dispensing accurate portions of many different foods into trays; over 40 million meals served, weight-sensed portion accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning cooked components into meal containers for diet-specific prepared-meal brands — the packing/portioning half of a personal chef's special-diet batch prep, done on a fixtured conveyor line.

sources.title: Posha: The Best Inventions of 2025 (TIME)
sources.claim: Posha is a commercially shipping countertop home cooking robot that autonomously dispenses, stirs and adjusts heat using computer vision, but the user must chop and load ingredients into compartments and it is limited to one-pot dishes.

sources.title: Can a Cooking Robot for Home Really Make Dinner?
sources.claim: Posha's own documentation confirms the human does the mise en place: the cook prepares ingredients and loads them into designated compartments before the machine runs the cooking sequence.

sources.title: NEO humanoid designed for household use, available for preorder
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, the leading home-deployed general-purpose robot, is autonomous only for basic navigation and simple retrieval; complex household work is handled by scheduling a human teleoperator.

sources.title: Mobile ALOHA: Learning Bimanual Mobile Manipulation using Low-Cost Whole-Body Teleoperation
sources.claim: Mobile ALOHA, a research bimanual mobile manipulator, autonomously performs single cooking sub-steps such as sautéing and serving a piece of ... after 50 human demonstrations per task, with success rates around 80-90%.
sources.transferJustification: Closest research evidence for free-standing cooking manipulation in an ordinary kitchen; it covers only one scripted sub-step at demo reliability, so it cannot substantiate whole-meal completion.

sources.title: $340,000 Moley robotic kitchen is ready to make you dinner
sources.claim: The Moley Robotic Kitchen, the flagship 'robot chef' product, is a purpose-built installed kitchen whose arms replay 3D motion-capture recordings of a human chef's actions rather than perceiving and cooking independently.

sources.title: Unifiller launches robot cake decorator
sources.claim: Industrial bakery robots such as Unifiller's HIRO robot cake decorator and its ACIS icing line automate decorating and icing steps within large bakery plants, integrating into existing decorating systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piping and icing decorated cakes in a plant; it covers only the decorating step of a bespoke pastry item, not mixing, shaping, baking and finishing.

tasks.label: Plan and prepare food for parties, holiday meals, luncheons, special functions, and other social events.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intimate seated dinner party in the employer's private home: 6-12 guests, 3-5 courses planned with the client, cooked on the household's own range/oven in a kitchen laid out for family life, adjusted for guest allergies and late changes, each course plated and often served, kitchen left clean.

Holiday meal for extended family in the private home (Thanksgiving, Christmas, Passover): a large roast plus 6-10 side dishes, gravies, breads and desserts, all timed to one service, oven and burner space juggled while family members move through the kitchen.

Luncheon, brunch or tea for 8-20 in the residence: composed salads, quiches or tarts, sandwiches, hot side, baked goods and a dessert, arranged as a buffet on the dining table and replenished during the event.

Large special function at the residence (30-100 guests): menu planning and ordering, two days of advance prep, passed canapes plus buffet stations, grilling or an outdoor tent, coordination of hired servers, food held and replenished through the event.

Planning and advance preparation for an upcoming event: menu design with the client, sourcing and shopping at markets and specialty stores, then a prep day of stocks, sauces, doughs, marinades, knife work, par-cooking and baking in the client's kitchen or a rented licensed kitchen.

Casual gathering spread (game day, kids' birthday, informal family party): one or two large-batch one-pot/one-pan hot dishes (chili, curry, pasta, taco filling) cooked from prepped ingredients, portioned into bowls or pans and held hot for a self-serve buffet.

sources.system: goodBytz robotic kitchen / SAM (Sustained Autonomous Meals)
sources.developer: goodBytz (Germany), fielded by US Army 19th Expeditionary Sustainment Command
sources.title: The Army is testing out a robotic kitchen that can cook for soldiers downrange
sources.claim: goodBytz's Sustained Autonomous Meals (SAM) robotic kitchen, with refrigerated storage, eight induction stoves and two robotic arms, cooks and plates hot meals autonomously at a US Army dining facility at Camp Walker, South Korea, with humans only loading prepped ingredients and supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: institutional hot-meal cooking. Transfers to the bulk one-pot party dish instance because the objects (raw prepped ingredients, pots, portioned servings) and the cook-and-portion output are the same; it does not transfer to multi-course plated or baked menus.

sources.title: Robotic kitchen in a box cooks, cleans and serves 120 meals an hour
sources.claim: Circus SE's CA-1 autonomous robotic kitchen, deployed inside a REWE supermarket in Dusseldorf, prepares fresh hot meals end-to-end - gathering ingredients, cooking, plating and cleaning - without a human cook.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fresh pot/bowl meal cooking in a purpose-built enclosed cell. Comparable ingredients and cooking steps to a large-batch one-pot party dish; menu is limited to single-vessel dishes, so it does not transfer to roasts, baked goods or plated courses.

sources.title: Botinkit's AI-Powered Wok Robot Seeks to Revolutionize Restaurant Kitchens in Asia and Beyond
sources.claim: Botinkit's Omni is a commercially sold automated wok/cooking station for restaurant kitchens that dispenses seasonings, controls pan temperature and stir-fries or stews a dish, i.e. cooks single-vessel dishes from pre-portioned ingredients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial stir-fry/stew cooking. Same class of dish and ingredient handling as a bulk one-pot party dish, but restricted to one vessel and a loaded recipe, so it says nothing about multi-dish event menus.

sources.title: We've Raised a $43.1M Series A to Accelerate Our AI-Enabled Robot Deployments
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' arms assemble and plate meals in high-mix food production facilities (Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Cafe Spice), having produced tens of millions of servings; the robots portion pre-cooked ingredients into trays rather than cooking dishes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-volume meal assembly/plating. Shows the frontier of purpose-built food-robot cells is portioning pre-cooked components, not cooking or composing a bespoke event menu.

sources.title: Sweetgreen accelerates deployment of automated kitchens
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen automated makeline, deployed in dozens of restaurants, dispenses ingredients into bowls but explicitly does not perform prep work or finishing touches, which remain human jobs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: salad/bowl assembly, the closest automation analogue to composing a luncheon plate; the vendor's own scope statement shows prep and finishing are not automated.

sources.title: Posha Delivers Autonomous Countertop Cooking Experience
sources.claim: Posha is a commercially shipping countertop home cooking robot that autonomously cooks one-pot meals in a private kitchen, but the user must still prep and load the ingredients and it makes a single dish at a time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: home cooking of a single dish. Shows the in-home frontier is a purpose-built appliance cooking one loaded recipe, far from planning and executing a multi-dish event menu on the household's own equipment.

sources.title: Robot Showcases Culinary Skills! OpenAI's 1X Humanoid Robot Neo Beta Perfectly Cooks Medium-Rare Steak
sources.claim: The widely publicised demonstration of the 1X NEO Beta humanoid cooking a steak dinner in a home kitchen was performed under VR teleoperation, not autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task (cooking in a home kitchen); establishes that the leading home-humanoid cooking demonstration is teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Watch this robot cook shrimp and clean autonomously
sources.claim: Stanford's Mobile ALOHA cooked a three-course meal only under human supervision/teleoperation; autonomy was demonstrated on isolated sub-skills such as cooking shrimp.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task (multi-course meal preparation); shows the research frontier for multi-dish cooking in an ordinary kitchen is teleoperated, with autonomy limited to single short skills.

sources.title: pi-0.5: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 generalist policy controls a mobile manipulator to clean ... kitchens and bedrooms in previously unseen homes; the demonstrated home skills are tidying and cleaning, not cooking a meal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: long-horizon manipulation in unseen private homes. It marks the state of the art for autonomous work in E3 home kitchens and covers tidying, not cooking or plating meals.

tasks.label: Create and explore new cuisines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Personal chef develops a brand-new dish in the employer's home kitchen: works from whole raw ingredients (breaking down fish or poultry, knife work, building a sauce), improvises technique, tastes and corrects seasoning repeatedly, plates it and serves it to the household for reaction. Kitchen layout, cookware and stove differ from client to client.

Chef explores an unfamiliar regional cuisine: researches the tradition, shops specialty/ethnic markets for novel ingredients, then attempts unpracticed techniques in the client's kitchen (hand-forming dumplings, tempering whole spices, fermenting or pickling, unfamiliar doughs) and judges whether the result is authentic enough to add to the rotation.

Iterative tasting trial in the client's kitchen: chef cooks several small variants of a candidate dish, plates them for the client's tasting, takes verbal feedback ('too acidic', 'more heat'), adjusts seasoning, texture and garnish on the spot, then finalizes and writes up the recipe.

Adapting a newly explored cuisine to household constraints: reworking a dish to be gluten-free, vegan, low-sodium or allergen-safe, substituting ingredients, cooking and tasting test versions to confirm flavor holds, while preventing cross-contact in the home kitchen.

Recipe R&D away from the client's home: the personal chef tests and scales candidate dishes in a rented commissary/commercial kitchen or a dedicated test kitchen with standard equipment, batch-cooks trial versions, standardizes quantities and timings, and documents the recipe for later service.

sources.title: Posha Delivers Autonomous Countertop Cooking Experience | Let's Data Science
sources.claim: Posha is a commercially shipping countertop home cooking robot that autonomously executes recipes from a fixed library using computer vision, a stirring arm and automated dispensers, but the human must prep and load the ingredients and choose an existing recipe; it does not devise or sensorily evaluate novel dishes.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fielded analogue to a private-household cook: it cooks real food in real home kitchens, so its limits (closed recipe library, human ingredient prep, no tasting or iteration) bound what home cooking robots can do on new-dish development.

sources.title: Moley Robotics reveals robotic $330,000 smart kitchen - Gearbrain
sources.claim: The Moley Robotic Kitchen cooks only by replaying motion-capture recordings of professional chefs from a fixed recipe library, with ingredients pre-prepped and placed in known positions; adding a dish requires recording a human chef, so the machine does not create cuisine.
sources.transferJustification: Same domain (cooking complete dishes in a residential kitchen); shows the most capable purpose-built home robotic kitchen is scripted playback of human-authored recipes rather than creative development.

sources.title: Chef robotics firm: 'Possible to open a cloud kitchen in 24 hours' | Foodservice Equipment Journal
sources.claim: Nala Robotics runs purpose-built autonomous robotic kitchens in restaurants, but new menu items are developed by human engineers and culinary experts who prepare, taste-test and refine the dishes before the recipes are uploaded for the robot to execute.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (multi-cuisine dish production in a machine-built kitchen): shows that even in the most structured cooking environment the creative development and taste validation of new dishes is done by humans, which is exactly what this task asks of the worker.

sources.system: Nala Chef with generative AI recipes
sources.title: Nala Robotics incorporates generative AI into restaurant robot recipes - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Nala Robotics states that generative AI lets its autonomous robotic chefs prepare almost any recipe in its purpose-built kitchen cells — a vendor claim about executing supplied recipes, with no established autonomous loop of inventing, cooking and validating a new dish.
sources.transferJustification: Strongest candidate for machine-side recipe creation in robotic cooking; autonomy of the creative and tasting loop is not established, so per the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Cambridge/Beko robot chef with salinity sensor
sources.developer: University of Cambridge Bio-Inspired Robotics Lab with Beko
sources.title: Taste of the future: robot chef learns to 'taste as you go' | University of Cambridge
sources.claim: A University of Cambridge research robot arm fitted with a conductance/salinity probe 'tasted as it cooked', evaluating nine variations of a scrambled eggs and tomatoes dish in the lab — the closest demonstrated machine analogue of a chef's taste-and-adjust loop, limited to saltiness in one simple dish.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the core sub-skill of the task (tasting a dish under development and adjusting seasoning), but as a lab proof of concept on a two-ingredient dish it is far short of developing a new cuisine dish end to end.

sources.developer: University of Cambridge, Department of Engineering
sources.title: Robot 'chef' learns to recreate recipes from watching food videos | Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge
sources.claim: A Cambridge robotic salad chef learned recipes by watching videos of a human making eight five-ingredient salads and generated a ninth recipe on its own — a laboratory proof of concept whose 'creation' is limited to arranging pre-cut fruit and vegetable pieces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (a robot devising a new recipe), but performed in a lab with pre-cut produce and no cooking technique, unfamiliar ingredients, tasting, or plating to an employer's standard.

sources.title: 1X NEO Home Robot Review: Price, Features & Capabilities 2026
sources.claim: The 1X NEO home humanoid, the leading general-purpose robot shipping into private homes, is not fully autonomous and depends on remote human teleoperators for complex tasks including kitchen work.
sources.transferJustification: General-purpose home manipulation is the only pathway to open-ended cooking in an as-found private kitchen; documented teleoperation dependence means it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Serve meals and snacks to employing families and their guests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Everyday family dinner in a private home: the cook dishes up plated portions in the kitchen, carries plates through the house to the dining table, sets one in front of each of 2-6 family members, brings water/condiments, returns with seconds. Children, pets and moving chairs in the way; china and hot plates.

Snacks and beverages taken to family members wherever they happen to be: an after-school snack at the kitchen island, a tea tray carried upstairs to a study, cold drinks and nibbles brought out to the pool or terrace. The cook must find the person, carry an open tray over thresholds/stairs, and set it down.

Entertaining: a plated multi-course dinner for the family and invited guests. Courses timed with the host's cues, plates set and removed between courses, wine and water poured at the table, guests' requests answered mid-meal.
Family-style / buffet service: platters, tureens and serving bowls carried out and set on the dining table or sideboard, hot dishes replenished, fresh platters brought as they empty.
Breakfast or light-meal service: coffee, juice, toast and eggs brought to the breakfast bar, patio or a bedroom tray; coffee poured and refilled while the family eats.

sources.title: What is the latest restaurant automation technology in indoor food delivery robot technology? | RobotLAB
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi autonomously navigates restaurant dining rooms to bring food to a designated table, but human servers load the trays and diners lift their own dishes off the robot; it is marketed as a server assistant, deployed in thousands of venues.
sources.transferJustification: Restaurant food running is the closest commercial analogue to a household cook carrying plated food to diners; cited to show what deployed E2 systems do and do not do (no picking up or setting down of plates).

sources.title: Hotel Delivery Robot Deployed in Los Angeles, California
sources.claim: Relay hotel delivery robots autonomously drive corridors and elevators to deliver snacks, food, drinks and amenities to guests in their rooms; staff load the bin and the guest removes the item.
sources.transferJustification: Delivering a snack or drink to a person in a guest room is the structured-facility analogue of carrying a snack tray to a family member elsewhere in the house; cited to show autonomous transport but human loading/unloading.

sources.system: FOODOM Tianjiang Food Kingdom skyrail dish delivery (Qianxi Robot Catering Group)
sources.title: Here's what China's latest robot restaurant looks like | World Economic Forum
sources.claim: At the Foodom/Qianxi robot restaurant complex, cooked dishes are conveyed by an overhead skyrail directly down onto the diners' table in a dining room purpose-built around the delivery machinery.

sources.system: Express Line automated food delivery lane / sushi train (Hong Chiang Technology)
sources.title: Automated Food Delivery System Express Line | Sushi Bar Conveyor Belt - Hong Chiang
sources.claim: Commercially sold express-lane / sushi-train delivery systems route an ordered dish along dedicated rails to the assigned table and push the tray out onto the customer's table, replacing the human food runner in a restaurant built around the equipment.

sources.title: Meet ADAM, the Nvidia-Powered NHL Arena Bartender Robot | Technology Magazine
sources.claim: Richtech's ADAM dual-arm robot prepares and hands over coffee, boba and cocktails from a fixed, purpose-built bar/kiosk counter in venues including a Brooklyn coffee bar, Walmart, Kennedy Space Center and a Las Vegas NHL arena.
sources.transferJustification: Making and handing over drinks at a fixtured counter is the beverage half of serving snacks and refreshments; objects (cups, drinks) and precision are comparable, and the station is purpose-built.

sources.title: Introducing Helix 02: Full-Body Autonomy
sources.claim: The current frontier for autonomous humanoid dish handling is a four-minute dishwasher load/unload in the developer's own full-sized test kitchen; no autonomous meal service in customer homes has been shown.
sources.transferJustification: Dish manipulation in a home-scale kitchen is the nearest related task to carrying and placing plates for a household meal; it is cited because it marks the limit of demonstrated home capability (a company test kitchen, tidying rather than table service).

sources.title: 1X Neo is a $20,000 home robot that will learn chores via teleoperation - Engadget
sources.claim: 1X's NEO, the consumer humanoid shipping into private homes, relies on human teleoperators for anything beyond a few basic autonomous behaviours such as fetching items and opening doors.

sources.title: π0.5: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 mobile manipulator autonomously performs household tidying (putting dishes in the sink, wiping spills) in homes not seen in training, but the developers state it is far from perfect ... often makes mistakes.
sources.transferJustification: Kitchen tidying in unseen homes is the closest evidence of manipulation in unstructured private homes; it involves dishes and cups but at research reliability and does not cover carrying and presenting food to diners.

tasks.label: Travel with employers to vacation homes to provide meal preparation at those locations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Multi-day stay at the employer's own vacation home (beach, lake or mountain house): chef travels with the family, agrees menus, shops at unfamiliar local markets, then cooks 2-3 meals a day for 4-8 people for several days in a kitchen laid out and equipped differently from the primary residence, plating, serving and cleaning down each service.

Holiday or weekend at the vacation home with invited guests: multi-course plated dinners for 8-16, canapes, desserts, wine-paired courses timed to guests' arrival, dietary restrictions accommodated, service coordinated with household staff.

Routine casual family dinner at the vacation home cooked from ingredients on hand: a single main one-pot or one-pan dish (curry, stew, pasta sauce, stir-fry, risotto, chili) prepared from chopped ingredients and served family-style.

Breakfast and casual lunch service at the vacation home: eggs cooked to order, pancakes, toast and pastries, fruit plates, salads and sandwiches, grilled fish, plus packing picnic or beach/boat lunches for the family and children.

Cooking at a rented villa, remote lodge or yacht galley: unfamiliar or minimal equipment (two burners, unreliable oven, small fridge, moving vessel), ingredients bought at local markets, menus improvised around what is available that day.

Travel and kitchen set-up logistics: packing and transporting knives, pans, pantry staples and pre-made components to the vacation property; on arrival, provisioning, unpacking and organizing the kitchen and fridge; closing the kitchen down at the end of ... stay.

sources.title: A $105,000 robot arm nobody needs cooked me a delicious lunch - Engadget
sources.claim: Moley Robotics' X-AiR robotic kitchen cell (single Universal Robots arm on a bespoke countertop with fixed shelves and pots) cooks a recipe unattended after staff pre-prepare the ingredients and place them in known positions; it has no vision, makes 8-10 portions of one dish per session, and as of the hands-on none had been installed in a customer home.

sources.title: A $105,000 robot arm nobody needs cooked me a delicious lunch - Engadget
sources.claim: The same hands-on documents the limits of the purpose-built robotic kitchen: no perception of its environment, batch limited to 8-10 portions, and no ability to adapt or improvise when the exact expected ingredients are not in the bins.

sources.title: Meet Posha, a countertop robot that cooks your meals for you | TechCrunch
sources.claim: Posha is an enclosed countertop cooking robot (four ingredient hoppers, spice carousel, induction cooktop, overhead camera) shipping to US homes since January 2025 at about $1,500-1,750; the user selects a recipe and loads measured ingredients into its hoppers, and it then dispenses, stirs and controls heat to cook a one-pot dish autonomously, tolerating substitutions.

sources.title: Meet Posha, a countertop robot that cooks your meals for you | TechCrunch
sources.claim: Posha does not do the surrounding kitchen work: the human still plans, shops, chops and loads every ingredient into the machine's fixtures and cleans up afterwards; the robot automates only the active stovetop cooking of one dish at a time.

sources.system: pi-0.5 vision-language-action model on mobile manipulators
sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization (pi-0.5)
sources.claim: The most capable generalist home-robot policy demonstrated in previously unseen real homes, Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5, performs tidying chores (dishes to the sink, clothes to a basket, drawer organizing) with acknowledged frequent errors; no meal cooking in a novel kitchen is demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household chores in unfamiliar homes. It is the closest evidence to a robot working in a vacation home taken as found, and shows that current open-world home manipulation reaches pick-and-place tidying, not meal preparation, so it cannot substantiate cooking at E3.

sources.title: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly - AgFunderNews
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI food-assembly arms are deployed in food-production kitchens (Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Chef Bombay, Cafe Spice), autonomously portioning pre-prepped ingredients into trays on fixtured production lines, with tens of millions of meal servings assembled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling meals from prepared ingredients. It shows that when ingredients arrive in fixtured hoppers on a line, robots portion food reliably at scale (supporting E1-style dispensing), but it involves no cooking, knife work, menu decisions, or work in a domestic kitchen.

roles.title: Cooks, Restaurant
roles.description: Prepare, season, and cook dishes such as soups, meats, vegetables, or desserts in restaurants. May order supplies, keep records and accounts, price items on menu, or plan menu.

tasks.label: Ensure food is stored and cooked at correct temperature by regulating temperature of ovens, broilers, grills, and roasters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start of shift in a casual-dining kitchen: fire and set the whole battery - gas range and char-broiler valves, convection and combi ovens, salamander, fryers, holding units - dial in setpoints, then verify with an oven thermometer or probe that each unit actually reaches spec, and flag units running hot or cold.

High-volume standardized station during a rush (fry station, flat-top with patties, or pan/wok station): keeping oil and plate temperature at setpoint, adjusting cook cycles as loads change, so fries, patties and pan dishes come out fully cooked and not burned.

Char-broiler / salamander / saute line during service: continuously modulating burner and broiler heat and shifting varied items (steaks to ordered doneness, chicken, fish, vegetables) between hot and cool zones, judging by sight, sound and feel, while ticket mix and grill load change minute to minute.

Oven work: setting and adjusting oven temperature for roasts, braises, chicken, casseroles and baked items, inserting a probe or spot-checking internal temperature, dropping or raising heat to land the item at the target core temperature, then holding it there until service.

Hot holding: setting and monitoring steam tables, soup wells, roasters and holding cabinets so product stays above 135F, probing held items, adjusting thermostats or water levels when readings drift, and recording temperatures on the food-safety log.

Cold storage: checking walk-in cooler and freezer, reach-ins and prep-table wells at intervals, recording temperatures on HACCP/food-safety logs, adjusting thermostats, and taking corrective action when a unit is out of range (moving or discarding product, icing down, calling refrigeration service).

sources.title: White Castle Uses Robots to Cook French Fries (The Batch, DeepLearning.AI)
sources.claim: Flippy 2 autonomously runs a QSR fry station in working White Castle kitchens, using thermal-imaging cameras and vision to classify foods and adjust cooking times ....

sources.title: Miso Launches the Newest Flippy: The Fry Station Robot Built From Millions of Baskets of Real-World Data
sources.claim: The current-generation Flippy Fry Station is in commercial service at White Castle and Jack in the Box, running fried product faster than human fry cooks.

sources.title: iCookingSuite. iCombi Pro.
sources.claim: The iCombi Pro combi oven, standard equipment in commercial kitchens, senses the load and core probe and autonomously regulates cabinet temperature, climate, fan speed and time to bring food to a target doneness and hold it.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: regulating oven temperature so food reaches and holds the correct internal temperature; the oven's sensors and controller replace the cook's dial adjustments and probe checks for oven-cooked items.

sources.title: Botinkit's AI-Powered Wok Robot Seeks to Revolutionize Restaurant Kitchens in Asia and Beyond
sources.claim: Botinkit's Omni AI cooking robot is deployed in ordinary commercial kitchens (chains, hotels, caterers, supermarkets) in Asia and Singapore, cooking stir-fry and stew dishes unattended.

sources.title: BOTINKIT: Realising the Dream of the Automated Kitchen | InvestHK

tasks.label: Inspect and clean food preparation areas, such as equipment, work surfaces, and serving areas, to ensure safe and sanitary food-handling practices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-service upkeep of the cook's own station: scraping food debris off cutting boards and stainless prep tables, wiping and spraying quat sanitizer between proteins and allergens, wiping cooler tops and reach-in handles, all amid pans, squeeze bottles, cambros, hot surfaces and other cooks moving through a tight line.

End-of-shift cleaning of cooking equipment: scraping and degreasing the flat-top griddle and char-grill grates, wiping down range tops and salamanders, boiling out or filtering the fryer and wiping fryer cabinets, cleaning oven interiors and pulling hood filters, dealing with carbonized, baked-on grease.

Breaking down small equipment and the wash area: disassembling a slicer, mixer, food processor or immersion blender, washing parts in the three-compartment sink or dish machine, sanitizing, air-drying and reassembling them correctly, plus scrubbing sinks, drainboards and the prep-sink area.

Cleaning serving and holding areas: expo counter and heat lamps, steam-table wells and hot/cold holding units, sneeze guards and refrigerated display cases, wiping spills and dried sauce, changing water in wells, sanitizing surfaces between shifts.

Closing floor and general area cleanup in the kitchen: sweeping debris, lifting and hosing rubber mats, degreasing the floor under and behind the cook line, squeegeeing to drains and cleaning drain covers, taking out trash and wiping down trash areas.

Inspection and verification round: walking the line to check surfaces, equipment and reach-ins for residue, grease and debris; testing sanitizer bucket concentration with strips; checking cooler and hot-hold temperatures; looking for pest signs; signing off the sanitation checklist and flagging items for re-clean.

tasks.label: Ensure freshness of food and ingredients by checking for quality, keeping track of old and new items, and rotating stock.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Walk-in cooler/freezer FIFO rotation during prep shift: cook enters a cold, cramped walk-in, pulls older labeled deli containers, hotel pans, cambros and produce cases forward, stacks newly delivered stock behind, checks prep dates/use-by labels, and pulls anything past date for discard.

Sensory quality inspection of fresh produce and proteins at receiving or immediately before prep: opening cases of lettuce, tomatoes, herbs, fish, chicken and dairy; looking for wilt, mold, bruising, discoloration, slime; smelling proteins; checking case temperature; rejecting or discarding what fails.

Line reach-in / mise-en-place check during service: verifying date-and-time labels on pans of prepped sauces, cut vegetables, portioned proteins in the line coolers and rail, pulling pans that have aged out or look/smell off, and swapping in fresh backups mid-rush.

Dry-storage rotation: shelving new deliveries of canned goods, dry pasta, flour, oils behind existing stock, checking best-by dates, and pulling dented, rusted, swollen or infested packages out of circulation.
Date-labeling and record work tied to rotation: applying prep/use-by labels to newly made items as they go into storage, logging cooler temperatures and recording discarded product on a waste sheet.

tasks.label: Weigh, measure, and mix ingredients according to recipes or personal judgment, using various kitchen utensils and equipment.

instances.label: Batch prep in a restaurant prep kitchen: weighing bulk solids on a digital scale and measuring liquids from bulk containers to build a batch of sauce, dressing, marinade, brine or soup base, then combining/blending it (whisk, immersion blender, stock pot, buffalo chopper) and holding it for service.

Portioning and combining measured amounts of prepped ingredients into dishes during service on an assembly-style line (grain/salad bowls, pizzas, plated components): scoops, ladles, portion cups per spec, then tossing or combining the finished dish, at service pace.

Weighing and mixing doughs, batters and breading: scaling flour/water/yeast/eggs for pizza dough, pancake or tempura batter, biscuit or dessert mixes; running a planetary or spiral mixer, scraping the bowl, folding or hand-kneading to a target consistency.

Cold prep hand-mixing in bowls or tubs: meatball/burger/meatloaf mixes, sausage seasoning blends, slaws, tuna and potato salads, marinating proteins, dressed salads - measured ingredients combined by hand or paddle to an even mix without over-working.

Mixing by personal judgment rather than a written recipe: tasting a batch and adjusting salt, acid, heat or thickness; correcting an over-seasoned or broken batch; scaling or improvising a mix for a special from what is on hand.

tasks.label: Turn or stir foods to ensure even cooking.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Burger-forward casual restaurant / diner flat-top: cook flips uniform beef patties (and similar uniform griddle items) partway through the cook so both sides sear evenly, judging doneness by color and time during a lunch rush, then pulls them to the assembly board.

Grill, char-broiler and diner griddle with mixed items: turning and quarter-turning steaks cooked to different ordered temperatures, chicken breasts, salmon, pork chops, plus eggs, bacon, hash browns and vegetables, each item entering and leaving at different times and needing a spatula/tongs feel judgment.

Fry station in a casual restaurant: lowering baskets of fries, wings, tenders, calamari into hot oil and shaking/agitating them mid-cook so pieces separate and brown evenly, then draining and dumping to the pass.

Wok or sauté station in an Asian or Italian restaurant: continuous high-heat tossing and stirring of stir-fries, fried rice, noodles, or pasta finished in sauce in a pan, so ingredients cook through evenly without sticking or scorching.

Range/stockpot work: stirring simmering soups, marinara, gravies, chili, grits, risotto and sautéed vegetables in assorted pots and pans on open burners, scraping the bottom periodically over long simmers to prevent scorching, and stirring in additions as they go.

Upscale / fine-dining a la carte sauté: basting and turning delicate proteins - fish fillets, scallops, duck breast, filet - in a pan of foaming butter, turning at the moment judged by sight, sound and touch to reach an exact ordered doneness.

tasks.label: Observe and test foods to determine if they have been cooked sufficiently, using methods such as tasting, smelling, or piercing them with utensils.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Grill/broiler station of a chain casual-dining restaurant (burgers, chicken breasts, portion-controlled steaks). Cook judges doneness by press/touch, cut, and instant-read thermometer against spec temps, at ticket pace on a standard flat-top/charbroiler line.

Fry and griddle station of a casual or fast-casual restaurant: baskets of fries, wings, breaded appetizers, quesadillas. Doneness judged by color, float/crispness, timer, and occasional thermometer probe of thick items.

Saute/sauce/soup/pasta station: cook repeatedly tastes and smells sauces, soups, braises and stocks and bite-tests pasta, rice and vegetables to decide whether they are cooked through, tender, or need more time.

Independent full-service restaurant (diner, family, ethnic) where one cook runs several stations with a varied, frequently changing menu on non-standard equipment; doneness of many different dish types judged mostly by sight, smell, sound and touch.

Steakhouse/fine-dining grill with large irregular cuts (bone-in ribeye, whole fish, duck breast, rack of lamb) cooked to each guest's ordered doneness, judged by finger-press, skewer/probe placement in the thickest point, and carryover during rest.

tasks.label: Substitute for or assist other cooks during emergencies or rush periods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chain casual-dining / family restaurant, lunch or dinner rush: the cook jumps onto the fry station to help the fry cook — pulling frozen fries, wings and breaded appetizers from the freezer bins, loading and dropping several baskets, timing and shaking them, and dumping cooked product into the holding pan/landing zone for expo, on a standard commercial fryer bank with staff moving behind.

Fast-casual restaurant, digital-order rush: the cook steps onto the bowl/salad/burrito assembly line, portioning bases, grains, proteins and toppings into bowls per ticket, adding dressing/sauce, and passing the container to the finish/pack point.

Full-service or casual-dining hot line, dinner rush: the cook takes over or backs up the grill/broiler/sauté station — firing 6-10 open tickets at once, cooking steaks and chicken to requested temperature, sautéing pastas and sauces, timing dishes to go out together, plating with sides and garnish to spec on the pass.

Pantry/cold station coverage during a rush: building house and entrée salads, tossed Caesars, cold appetizers and plated desserts — portioning many cold ingredients to spec, arranging toppings/proteins on the plate or bowl, sauce drizzle and garnish, at ticket speed.

Emergency call-out: a cook does not show, and another cook runs that whole station for the shift — knife prep and mise en place from raw product (chopping, portioning, sauces), setting up the station and steam table/lowboy, cooking through service, restocking mid-shift, then breakdown, wrap-down and cleaning.

Assisting rather than substituting during a rush: fetching and restocking mise from the walk-in and freezer, grabbing clean pans and utensils, running plates to the pass/expo window, wiping the pass, and jumping in to help another cook plate or garnish for a few minutes at a time.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Back-of-house raw prep in a restaurant kitchen: at a cutting board, trimming fat cap, silverskin and gristle from boneless subprimals (beef strip loin, pork loin, veal, lamb top round) and portioning them into fixed-weight steaks, cutlets or medallions to menu spec, working amid other prep tasks and staff traffic.

Carving cooked roasts in the kitchen for hot plated service: slicing prime rib, roast pork loin, baked ham or leg of lamb to a specified thickness/weight, trimming excess fat and end cuts, holding slices hot for the line during service.

Slicing cooked or cured meats for cold service and sandwiches: ham, roast beef, pastrami, porchetta, corned beef; trimming the piece, seating it on a deli slicer or hand-slicing thin, portioning by weight for sandwich builds and cold platters.

Butchery of bone-in and whole cuts in a scratch kitchen or steakhouse: breaking a bone-in ribeye into steaks, removing the chine, frenching a rack of lamb, seaming out a leg of lamb or fabricating a whole pork shoulder, tying roasts.

Guest-facing carving at a banquet/buffet carving station in the dining room: carving prime rib, ham or roast turkey/lamb to each guest's request (thickness, end cut versus rare center), trimming fat, and placing portions on guests' plates during service.

sources.title: DSI™ Waterjet Portioning Systems | JBT Marel
sources.claim: JBT Marel's DSI waterjet portioning systems scan each piece of meat to locate fat and determine shape/thickness/weight, then computer-positioned waterjets trim fat and cut fixed portions; sold and installed as commercial production equipment on conveyorized lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial fat-trimming and fixed-weight portioning of beef/pork/poultry primals. Same objects and cuts a restaurant cook trims and portions, at equal or tighter weight tolerance; only the presentation of work (conveyor and fixtures) differs, which is the environment dimension being rated.

sources.title: I-Cut 11 PortionCutter for meat | JBT Marel
sources.claim: Marel's I-Cut PortionCutter is a commercial vision/laser-guided machine that cuts fresh boneless meat (pork loin, tenderloin, flank, skirt) into fixed-weight and fixed-length portions with minimal giveaway.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixed-weight portion cutting of boneless pork/beef loins. This is the same cutting operation a cook performs when portioning a trimmed loin into steaks or cutlets, on the same materials, with tighter weight accuracy.

tasks.label: Estimate expected food consumption, requisition or purchase supplies, or procure food from storage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Line cook restocking their station during service: repeatedly stepping to the lowboy/reach-in and the walk-in cooler to pull backup hotel pans, labeled deli containers, squeeze bottles and cambros of prepped sauces, proteins and garnishes (2-25 lb), then setting them into the rail or under-counter cooler; hot, wet, crowded kitchen with other cooks moving fast.

Prep cook at shift start pulling raw materials for the prep list: cases of produce and boxes of protein out of the walk-in and freezer, bulk bags, #10 cans and dry goods off storeroom shelving (up to 40-50 lb), checking dates for FIFO, moving other stock aside, loading a cart and staging at the prep table.

Receiving a vendor delivery at the back door: checking cases and weights against the invoice, rejecting damaged/off-temp product, then carrying and stacking cases into the correct walk-in, freezer or dry storage location and rotating existing stock.

Estimating expected food consumption for the coming shift or day: using sales history, reservations/covers, weather, specials and on-hand product to set par levels and write the prep list / requisition sheet. Purely informational output, no physical act required.

Taking inventory in the storeroom and walk-in (counting cases, eyeballing or weighing partially used containers and open produce) and then requisitioning from the commissary or placing the purchase order with vendors by phone or online portal.

sources.title: Sweetgreen Goes All-In with Automated Restaurants - QSR Magazine
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen, an automated makeline deployed in operating restaurants, autonomously dispenses stored ingredients from refrigerated hoppers into bowls on a conveyor at high rate, with staff only adding finishing touches.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated ingredient delivery at the point of use. It substantiates a machine taking food out of on-board chilled storage and moving the right quantity of the right ingredient to the assembly point in a working restaurant - the same objects (produce, proteins, dressings) a cook procures from storage - but only when ingredients are pre-loaded into machine-accessible hoppers.

instances.label: Poultry fabrication at the prep station of a restaurant kitchen: breaking down cases of whole chickens into airline breasts, wings, drums and thighs, deboning thighs, trimming fat/cartilage, saving carcasses for stock. Mixed sizes, wet hands, shared board and knife, done between other prep duties.

Red-meat fabrication: receiving subprimals (beef striploin, ribeye, tenderloin, pork loin, lamb racks) and trimming fat/silverskin, frenching racks, and portioning to house steak/chop weights and thicknesses on a cutting board with a boning/scimitar knife.

Whole finfish: scaling, gutting, heading, filleting and pin-boning whole fish (salmon, branzino, snapper, flatfish) of varying size delivered on ice, then skinning and portioning for the menu; carcasses reserved for stock.
Crustacean prep: peeling and deveining shrimp, splitting/killing lobsters and breaking down crabs, picking meat, cleaning heads and shells for stock.
Bivalve/mollusk prep at the raw bar or prep station: shucking oysters and clams to order on the half shell without shell chips or cut meats, debearding mussels, cleaning squid.

Whole-animal breakdown in a whole-animal-program restaurant: taking a whole hog, lamb or goat carcass (or side) and seaming it out into primals, chops and roasts, plus dressing whole fowl (ducks, rabbits) delivered undressed.
