tasks.label: Clean food preparation equipment, work areas, and counters or tables.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-service wipe-down of the cook line: sanitizing cutting boards, prep tables, sandwich/salad station rails and reach-in tops, wiping up spills and grease splatter around hot equipment, done quickly between tickets while food containers, utensils and other staff occupy the space (diner, fast-food, deli, food truck).

Cleaning the flat-top griddle/charbroiler between cook cycles and at shutdown: scraping carbon and food residue off the plate, pushing grease into the trough/grease drawer, degreasing with grill brick/water, emptying and wiping the grease container.

Breaking down and washing food preparation equipment and smallwares: slicer, blender jar, mixer bowl, toaster/conveyor parts, fryer baskets, pans and utensils — disassembling, carrying to the three-compartment sink or dish machine, scrubbing baked-on soil, sanitizing, air-drying and reassembling.

End-of-shift deep clean of the station: filtering fryer oil or boil-out, pulling and washing hood filters, degreasing backsplash and wall behind the grill, wiping equipment exteriors and under-counter refrigeration, sweeping/mopping the floor and mats around the work area.

Front-of-house surfaces in counter-service/diner formats: clearing crumbs, dishes and condiment debris from the customer counter and tables between guests and wiping/sanitizing them while patrons are present.

sources.title: Alpha Grill - Automated Burger Grill for Commercial Kitchens
sources.claim: Aniai's Alpha Grill, a commercial double-sided griddle robot, uses a built-in robotic spatula that automatically scrapes the griddle plate clean and pushes leftover grease ...; units are installed in restaurant chains in Korea and the US.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element as the short-order griddle scrape-down: same soils (grease, carbon, food residue) on the same kind of hot steel cooking surface, but the plate is a fixtured part of a purpose-built machine rather than a free-standing diner flat-top.

sources.title: Aniai installs 15 hamburger grill robots in South Korea
sources.claim: Fifteen Alpha Grill units were deployed across South Korean burger chains including Lotteria, where the machine transfers cooked patties and then performs its self-cleaning cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms the automated griddle-cleaning function is a fielded deployment, not a demo; the cleaning step matches the cook's griddle scrape-down.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics' three-arm dishwashing system runs autonomously around the clock in real restaurant dish rooms, picking greasy plates, glassware and silverware out of bus tubs, racking them and running the dish machine; the second installation operates without any company staff on site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is warewashing rather than prep-equipment cleaning; it transfers to washing pans, fryer baskets and disassembled equipment parts because the objects are the same greasy, wet, variably shaped kitchen items presented at a dedicated wash station, but it does not cover disassembling or reassembling a slicer or mixer.

sources.title: Rosie™ by CleanBotix | Robotic Sanitation for Food Plants
sources.claim: CleanBotix's Rosie is a mobile 6-DOF arm robot that autonomously executes rinse, foam, rinse and sanitize cycles on food and beverage plant equipment and open production areas at night.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is nightly food-plant sanitation: it cleans food-contact stainless equipment and work areas with protein/grease soils to a swab-verified hygiene standard, the same output the cook's cleaning must reach, but by hose/foam methods that require a washdown-rated room with drains.

sources.title: CleanBotix Builds Autonomous Food-Processing Robot with MoveIt Pro to Accelerate Market Launch
sources.claim: Rosie's R6 model reached production readiness and pilot deployments with poultry processors, cleaning at 80% of human speed with fewer re-cleans and ... over four to five hour autonomous sessions.
sources.transferJustification: Documents worker-comparable cleaning quality and speed for food equipment sanitation, the closest measured analogue to a cook's end-of-shift equipment and work-area cleaning; missions are taught then executed by the robot rather than teleoperated.

sources.title: Circus SE completes first production of CA-1 robots in high-volume facility
sources.claim: Circus SE's CA-1 is a glass-enclosed autonomous robotic kitchen with robotic arms and induction pots that includes a self-cleaning system and a dedicated hygiene module for low-maintenance operation.
sources.transferJustification: The cleaning covered is of the machine's own cooking vessels and enclosed work surfaces — the same food-soil removal a cook performs — but only inside a purpose-built, fixtured cell where every surface is in a known position.

sources.title: Robotic kitchen in a box cooks, cleans and serves 120 meals an hour
sources.claim: A CA-1 unit deployed inside a REWE supermarket in Düsseldorf runs the entire meal cycle, including cleaning, on its own while serving customers.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the self-cleaning cooking cell operating unattended in a live retail food-service deployment; the cleaned items are cooking vessels and work surfaces, matching the task, inside a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.title: Everyday Robots comes out of Google Moonshot Factory with robots that can learn variety of tasks
sources.claim: Alphabet's Everyday Robots fleet of more than 100 mobile manipulators performed office tasks autonomously at Google campuses, including wiping cafeteria tables with a squeegee attachment; the program was later shut down.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is cafeteria table wiping: same motion and surface type as wiping counters and tables, but demonstrated on cleared, uncluttered tables in an office cafeteria, without clearing dishes or meeting a food-code sanitizing standard.

tasks.label: Restock kitchen supplies, rotate food, and stamp the time and date on food in coolers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-shift restock of the cook's station in a diner/QSR/grill kitchen: pulling backup hotel pans of prepped ingredients, portioned patties, cheese, sliced produce and squeeze bottles from the reach-in and walk-in and refilling the sandwich rail, refrigerated drawers and station bins while the line is running; crowded aisles, wet/greasy floors, mixed container types and weights.

Portioning prepped items into cambros, deli cups and hotel pans, then applying a day-dot/printed label or date stamp with item, time and date and stowing the container in the cooler; varied container shapes and sizes, wet and cold surfaces, labels must be legible for health-inspection compliance.

FIFO rotation inside the walk-in cooler/freezer: reading handwritten and printed dates on mixed containers and cases, moving older stock forward and new stock behind, consolidating partial pans, and pulling expired or spoiled product; heavy, unstable, mixed loads on wire shelving in a cold, tight space.

Receiving a distributor delivery and putting it away: breaking down the pallet/hand-truck load, checking case dates and counts, and storing cases in dry storage, cooler and freezer in their designated spots behind existing stock.
Restocking non-food kitchen supplies: to-go containers, paper goods, foil, film, gloves, cleaners and sanitizer, carried in cases from the stockroom to under-counter and overhead station storage.

sources.date: 2022-08 (deployment to 300 FamilyMart stores; product still in service through 2025)
sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA is a rail-mounted robot installed in the cold compartment of convenience stores that autonomously detects low shelves and restocks bottles and cans onto refrigerated display shelves, succeeding automatically more than 98% of ... with remote operators only for rare failures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restocking a refrigerated retail cooler. It transfers rigid packaged goods from a staged supply into a known shelf layout inside a chilled space, the same pick-and-place-into-cooler-shelf motion as restocking cooler/station stock, though with uniform bottles rather than kitchen pans.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: TX SCARA's supply is staged for it: store workers keep the storage shelves behind the ... filled, and the robot works from a pre-registered camera scan of the shelf layout — i.e., the work is brought to a fixed machine in a defined workspace.
sources.transferJustification: Same system as above; establishes that the demonstrated restocking depends on staged supply and a pre-registered shelf map, which is the E1 (work-brought-to-machine) presentation rather than a cook fetching mixed pans from a walk-in.

sources.date: product line commercial since ~2014; spec sheet current as of 2026
sources.title: Print & Apply Labeler with Intelligent Motion Videojet 9550 (specification sheet)
sources.claim: Print-and-apply labelers automatically print variable date/lot information and physically apply the label to packages and cases moving on a production line, without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic date/lot coding and label application on a conveyor line. It performs the physical act of the cook's 'stamp the time and date' step on food packages presented in a fixed position, i.e., the E1 form of the labeling instance.

sources.system: Quadrel automatic labeling systems (food safety compliance labelers)
sources.title: Food Safety Compliance Automatic Labeling Machine
sources.claim: Automatic labeling machines used in food production print batch and date codes and press labels onto a range of food package styles automatically for traceability compliance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying date-coded labels to filled food containers (including clamshells and tray packs) on a line — the same output as a cook's date/time label, produced when containers are conveyed to the machine.

sources.system: Swisslog cold-store AS/RS (Vectura pallet cranes with SynQ WCS/WMS)
sources.title: Using Warehouse Automation to Support and Enhance Food Safety | Refrigerated & Frozen Foods
sources.claim: Automated storage and retrieval systems in refrigerated and frozen warehouses execute stock rotation automatically, storing and retrieving loads on a FIFO/FEFO basis under warehouse control software, replacing manual rotation of chilled product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stock rotation of chilled/frozen food inventory. It achieves the purpose of the cook's 'rotate food' step (oldest product used first, expiry tracked) in a cold environment, but only within purpose-built racking with machine-readable loads.

sources.system: Symbotic robotic case-handling system (SymBots, robotic depalletizing/palletizing arms)
sources.date: 2021-07 article; systems in operation since 2017 and expanding through 2025
sources.title: Walmart plans to automate 25 distribution centers with Symbotic | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: Symbotic's system autonomously receives inbound pallets, uses machine vision to audit the load, depalletizes cases with robotic arms, and has autonomous mobile robots put each case away in a software-assigned storage location; deployed across Walmart regional distribution centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: receiving a delivery and putting cases away in assigned storage with system-managed rotation — the same objects (cases of food and supplies) and the same start-to-finish outcome as the cook's delivery put-away, but with the load presented to a purpose-built structure.

sources.title: Humanoid Robots Now Deploy in Eight Weeks: Kitchens, Warehouses, and Hotels
sources.claim: A wheeled humanoid marketed for quick-service restaurant, warehouse and hotel work is deployed at customer sites, but early deployments run at roughly 70% autonomy with teleoperation and remote ... still part of the service, and its documented paying deployment is packing work at a golf course rather than kitchen restocking.
sources.transferJustification: Closest candidate for a mobile manipulator working inside a real restaurant kitchen; cited to show that as of mid-2026 such deployments still rely on teleoperation and are not doing kitchen restocking/rotation autonomously, so they cannot support an E2 judgment.

tasks.label: Complete orders from steam tables, placing food on plates and serving customers at tables or counters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Diner/short-order counter: cook works a hot line with a steam table of hotel pans (chili, gravy, hash, vegetables, rice), portions items with standard scoops and tongs onto plates as tickets come in, garnishes, and slides the finished plate across the counter to a seated counter customer during a rush.

Institutional cafeteria serving line (school, hospital, corporate, military dining hall): cook stands behind a steam table and portions entrées and sides onto plates or compartment trays for a moving queue of patrons, adjusting portions to requests, over a 60-90 minute meal period.

Hot-bar / buffet-style takeout counter (deli, Chinese takeout, Indian buffet, hot-bar combo): cook builds made-to-order combination plates or clamshell containers from 8-20 steam-table wells, weighs or eyeballs portions, closes the container and hands it to the customer at the counter.

Small diner/cafe with table service: cook plates hot food held on the steam table, then carries two or three plates out into the dining room and places them in front of seated guests at tables, returning for condiments or refills.

Banquet, catering, or institutional tray-line plating: cook portions hot held food from steam-table pans onto plates or patient/meal trays moving down a line, covering them for transport to a dining room or floor.

sources.system: RoboEatz ARK (Fresh Take Eatery) with ABB robotic arm
sources.title: WellSpan Health launches AI-powered robotic kitchen at York Hospital
sources.claim: RoboEatz/ABB 'Fresh Take Eatery' Autonomous Robotic Kitchen deployed at WellSpan York Hospital (March 2026) stores up to 80 fresh ingredients, cooks made-to-order meals in four modules, and performs automated plating and serving to campus customers 24/7 from a 400 sq ft purpose-built robotic unit.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the task: completing made-to-order meals by portioning held/cooked components onto plates and serving them to customers at a counter, in an institutional foodservice setting.

sources.title: The Robot in the Kitchen: Is Automated Cooking Finally Coming to America?
sources.claim: Trade coverage confirms the WellSpan robotic kitchen runs without human handling of the food and produces hundreds of made-to-order hot meals, indicating autonomous operation at accepted service quality.

sources.title: Sweetgreen Goes All-In with Automated Restaurants - QSR Magazine
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen automated makeline, in commercial restaurant operation since 2023 and expanded to roughly 25 more locations in 2025, dispenses portioned ingredients into bowls and plates moving on a conveyor at up to 500 units per hour with 'near perfect' order accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: portioning held food components onto plates/bowls to complete customer orders at production speed; differs only in that ingredients sit in machine hoppers rather than steam-table pans.

sources.title: Sweetgreen opens its robotic Infinite Kitchen restaurant
sources.claim: The Infinite Kitchen line is not fully hands-free: a human worker at the end of the conveyor adds finishing touches before the order is handed to the guest, showing the automated makeline covers portioning but not the final handoff without staff.

sources.title: Chef Robotics completes 100M meal servings milestone - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-enabled arms have autonomously portioned 100 million servings of cooked, deformable food into meal trays across more than a dozen ... as of April 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scooping and depositing hot cooked food into trays on a moving line is the same manipulation as plating from steam-table pans onto plates/trays, at commercial accuracy and speed, but in a robot-built line.

sources.title: Chipotle and Cava Invest $25 Million in Hyphen to Advance Restaurant Automation
sources.claim: Chipotle's pilot of Hyphen's automated makeline at its Cultivate Center processed up to 350 meals ..., portioning ingredients into bowls travelling beneath the counter.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: assembling customer orders by dispensing measured portions of held food into serving vessels; the test center line is a purpose-built machine environment.

sources.title: Dexai Robotics' Alfred Acts as Sous Chef at Boston BONAPITA Restaurant - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Dexai's Alfred cobot used AI and machine vision with standard kitchen utensils to assemble salads and bowls in unmodified commercial kitchens, deployed at a BONAPITA restaurant and at the Monarch Dining Facility, Travis Air Force Base; it performs kitchen assembly only and does not serve customers at counters or tables.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning ingredients from standard pans with standard utensils into bowls inside an as-found human kitchen — the plating half of this task — but limited to cold/prep items and with no counter or table service demonstrated.

sources.system: Servi / BellaBot indoor food delivery robots
sources.title: What is the latest restaurant automation technology in indoor food delivery robot technology?
sources.claim: Commercial food-running robots (Bear Robotics Servi, Pudu BellaBot, Keenon) navigate restaurant dining rooms autonomously to tables, but staff must load the dishes onto the robot's trays and guests remove their own plates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting plated food to guests at tables — the serving half of this task — but the plate-loading link from the plating station is performed by humans in every cited deployment.

tasks.label: Plan work on orders so that items served together are finished at the same time.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Morning rush at a diner or coffee shop: several tickets in flight, each a table's worth of breakfast plates — eggs cooked to order (over easy, scrambled, poached), pancakes or French toast off the griddle, bacon/sausage, hash browns, buttered toast — all to hit the pass hot at the same moment for the whole table.

Lunch at a diner, luncheonette or deli: varied griddle and fryer work — patty melts, grilled cheese, clubs, cheesesteaks, quesadillas, BLTs, tuna melts — with customer modifications, multiple tickets at once, each plate's sandwich, side and garnish finished together and picked up by servers within seconds.

Burger-and-fried-side plates at a diner counter or drive-in: cook drops fries or rings, times patties on the flat top, toasts buns, dresses the burger, and gets burger plus hot side to the window together, several such orders in parallel.

Bar, pub, casino or convenience-store snack counter fry station: an order of fried items — wings, tenders, mozzarella sticks, fries, rings — with different cook times, dropped so they finish, get sauced/seasoned, and go out to the table or counter together, hot and crisp.

Limited-menu quick-service counter, food truck, concession stand or food-hall stall: burgers, dogs, tacos, chicken sandwiches and fries; high-volume bursts, cramped fixed layout, orders bagged with all items hot at handoff.

Institutional grill station (hospital or college cafeteria, hotel, country club) cooking to order for a queue: omelets and eggs at breakfast, burgers and sandwiches at lunch, each customer's items finished together as they wait at the counter.

sources.title: Miso Robotics Unveils Flippy 2 | Food On Demand
sources.claim: Flippy 2 runs an entire fry station autonomously, with an AutoBin system that lets it cook several different menu items in separate baskets with their own cook times and keep them separate at the end.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running a fry station. Sequencing several items with different cook times so each comes out correctly timed is the fry-station form of planning work so items served together finish together.

sources.title: Miso Robotics develops smaller, faster Flippy | Restaurant Dive
sources.claim: Flippy fry robots are installed and operating in ordinary fast-food kitchens (White Castle and Jack in the Box), i.e. human-built restaurant kitchens rather than purpose-built robotic cells, though only in a small number of stores.

sources.title: Miso Robotics launches Flippy 2 for QSRs | Fast Casual
sources.claim: Flippy 2 assumes the work of a whole fry station including basket filling, emptying and ... load and unload baskets at the right times.

sources.title: AI Company Nala Robotics Introduces The Wingman
sources.claim: The Wingman is an autonomous fry station that cooks, seasons and plates several different fried items simultaneously, with a multi-fryer configuration routing different foods to their own seasoning bins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fried-item order production. Cooking wings, tenders and fries at once and delivering them seasoned and plated together is the same timing problem as finishing an order's fried items simultaneously.

sources.system: The Wingman (Nala Robotics) at Re-Up convenience stores
sources.title: Re-Up to deploy Nala Robotics automated frier in its convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Wingman fry robots are being put into convenience-store food service counters in a modified configuration for a small fried menu (chicken tenders, fries, wings).

sources.system: CaliExpress by Flippy (Cucina grill robot + Miso Flippy)
sources.title: World's First Fully Autonomous, AI-Powered Restaurant Opening in Southern California | Miso
sources.claim: CaliExpress by Flippy is a restaurant built around its robots in which both the grill station (patty grinding and cooking) and the fry station are fully automated and driven by the customer's order.

sources.title: A Behind the Scenes Look at the Robot-Run Restaurant CaliExpress by Flippy | Food On Demand
sources.claim: In operation, CaliExpress still relies on a human employee to prep and assemble/finish the food after the robots cook it, so the machines cover the cooking of a two-item order but not the whole finish-together step.

sources.title: ABB Automates Burger Production With Burger Bots
sources.claim: The BurgerBots cell in Los Gatos assembles a made-to-order burger from a cooked patty on a conveyor-carried, QR-tagged box, tops it, closes the box and adds a box ..., completing a two-item order in about 27 seconds inside a self-contained robotic cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: made-to-order burger assembly. Delivering the burger and its fried side boxed together at a fixed cycle time is the machine equivalent of finishing the items of one order at the same time.

sources.title: Aniai Expands Automated Grilling Robots Across U.S. Restaurants and Enterprise Partnerships, as Total Funding Reaches $19 Million
sources.claim: Aniai's Alpha Grill automated griddle is installed in more than 50 ordinary commercial kitchens and cooks patties to specified doneness on fixed cycle times, automating the grill station within a human kitchen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grill-station cooking. It shows station-level automation of cook timing in ordinary kitchens, but only one item stream, not coordination across an order's items.

sources.title: Circus successfully launches its autonomous AI robotics system CA-1 in REWE supermarkets
sources.claim: Circus SE's CA-1 is an enclosed dual-arm robotic cell producing complete cooked meals autonomously, launched in operating REWE supermarkets in Germany; it produces one dish per order rather than coordinating several items to finish together.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cooked-meal production. Shows a machine can cook a whole dish to order unattended, bounding what current systems do — single dishes, not synchronized multi-item plates.

tasks.label: Grill, cook, and fry foods such as french fries, eggs, and pancakes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quick-service fry station: cook drops standardized frozen product (french fries, nuggets, tenders, onion rings) into deep fryers to order and in batches during rushes, times/shakes baskets, salts and moves product to hot-holding, in a chain restaurant kitchen with fixed layout and standard fryers.

Griddle/flat-top protein station in a QSR, fast-casual or burger restaurant: cook portioned patties, chicken breasts, sausage and bacon to a set doneness/temperature, press and flip, offload to holding or the assembly line, high volume with standardized portions.

Breakfast egg station with a limited repertoire (fried sunny-side up, scrambled, omelet with a few chosen fillings) cooked to order for guests at a hotel, cafeteria or QSR breakfast line with standard equipment and steady product supply.

Diner flat-top breakfast plate: eggs cooked to a customer-specified style (over easy/medium/hard, basted, scrambled soft), plus pancakes or French toast, hash browns and bacon cooked simultaneously on a shared griddle so all components finish hot together for one ticket.

Rush at an independent diner, bar-and-grill or coffee shop: several tickets fired at once across griddle, charbroiler and fryer with a wide item mix (burgers, melts, philly steaks, wings, gyros, quesadillas), custom modifications and substitutions, doneness judged by eye and touch, timing coordinated by the cook.
Food truck, concession stand or small mobile kitchen: griddling and frying a compact menu in a cramped, non-standard equipment layout, cooking to order with limited holding and variable power/space.

sources.title: Miso Robotics’ Flippy Fry Station robot surpasses 5M baskets | Fast Casual
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy Fry Station robot is deployed in live U.S. restaurant kitchens (White Castle, Jack in the ..., Wing Zone, Insert Coin) across seven states and has cooked more than 5 million baskets of fried food.

sources.title: Restaurant Automation Products | Miso AI
sources.claim: Flippy Fry Station runs the fry station without step-by-step human control: staff deposit product and take finished items, while the robot dispenses, cooks, agitates baskets and detects doneness with AI vision at ~100 baskets/hour.

sources.system: Flippy Fry Station, next generation (Miso Robotics)
sources.title: Miso Robotics refines Flippy Fry Station with AI and partners - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The current-generation Flippy automates preparation of a full fried menu (french fries, onion rings, chicken, ...) in existing QSR kitchens, with an NVIDIA-developed vision system and overnight installation into human kitchen layouts.

sources.title: Aniai Expands Automated Grilling Robots Across U.S. Restaurants and Enterprise Partnerships (PR Newswire)
sources.claim: Aniai's Alpha Grill, an automated clamshell grilling robot with a robotic spatula for automatic offloading, cooks burgers, chicken, steak, eggs and pancakes and is operating in live U.S. restaurants during daily service.

sources.claim: Alpha Grill automates loading, cooking and discharge on a clamshell griddle, transfers finished product to holding and self-cleans between cycles; demonstrations covered burgers, chicken, steak, eggs and French toast.

sources.developer: Kurve Automation / Millennium Hotels and Resorts

sources.claim: AUSCA, an autonomous egg-cooking robot chef, was deployed at six Millennium Hotels properties in Singapore, cooking guests' eggs to order (sunny-side up or omelet with chosen toppings) in about a minute at the breakfast service.

sources.title: About Our Company — Popcake
sources.claim: The Popcake commercial machine is a fully automatic counter-top pancake maker (batter dispensing, cooking, flipping, delivery) with 12,000 units installed in hotels, airport lounges and buffets serving over 400,000 pancakes a day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cooking pancakes on a griddle. The machine performs the same physical cooking step (batter portioning, griddling to color, turning, delivery of finished pancakes) that the short-order cook performs on a flat-top, with the same product and acceptance standard.

sources.title: Shin Starr Brings Robot-Made Korean BBQ to Bay Area With Olhso Food Trucks – The Spoon
sources.claim: Shin Starr's OLHSO Korean BBQ food trucks are unmanned robotic mobile kitchens operating in Foster City, CA, where robotic auto-woks cook and assemble customer orders and the only human required is a driver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: to-order hot cooking of menu items in a cramped mobile commercial kitchen. High-heat wok cooking with automated portioning, cook-time control and transfer to the serving container involves comparable objects, heat control and confined-space constraints as griddle/fry work in a food truck.

sources.title: Photos: This robot cooks 120 dishes an hour with no staff, replaces entire restaurant | Interesting Engineering
sources.claim: Circus SE's CA-1 is a self-contained autonomous cooking unit that dispenses ingredients, cooks and plates meals to order and was in commercial pilot processing customer orders in REWE supermarkets in Germany.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cooking a stream of different to-order hot dishes back-to-back in one enclosed purpose-built unit; shows machine-side handling of ingredient presentation, cook control and plating for varied orders, relevant to the multi-ticket short-order case when work is brought to the machine.

tasks.label: Perform food preparation tasks, such as making sandwiches, carving meats, making soups or salads, baking breads or desserts, and brewing coffee or tea.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Diner/deli/QSR line: build sandwiches, burgers, wraps and clubs to order — grab bread or bun, toast it, layer sliced meats, cheese, lettuce, tomato, spread condiments, close, cut and plate, during a lunch rush with tickets stacking up.

Cold station: assemble salads, side salads, slaws and cold plates to order from prepped components held in a cold well or hotel pans — scoop greens, portion proteins and toppings, dress, plate for pickup.
Beverage station: brew drip coffee and iced tea in urns/batch brewers, keep them fresh, and pull espresso drinks (shot, steamed milk, pour) at a counter café or diner.
Back-of-house batch prep: make the day's soup or sauce — chop mirepoix and other vegetables, sauté, add stock and seasoning, simmer and stir in a stockpot or tilt kettle, taste and adjust, hold hot.
Meat handling: slice roast beef, turkey, ham and cheese on a deli slicer to thickness; carve a roast, rotisserie chicken or gyro cone; portion patties and steaks for the line.
Baking: mix and bake breads/buns, biscuits, cookies, muffins or simple desserts in a commercial kitchen or in-store bakery; pan, proof, bake, cool and finish.

sources.system: Grote Robotic Sandwich Assembly Line (Stäubli TX2-60 HE)

sources.claim: Grote Company's Robotic Sandwich Assembly Line uses a Stäubli TX2-60 HE six-axis robot with 3D vision to place the top bread slice onto a filled bottom slice and orient the sandwich for cutting, at industrial rates on a conveyor line.

sources.system: Grote slicers / bread feeders and cutters
sources.title: News: Robot automates sandwich production | Stäubli Robotics
sources.claim: The same industrial sandwich-making equipment family includes automated slicers for sausage, ham and cheese and bread feeders/cutters, i.e. machine slicing of deli meats and cheese in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial deli-meat and cheese slicing. It is the same act as a short-order cook's slicer work — uniform slices of ham/cheese to a set thickness — performed by machine at production rates.

sources.title: 'Robotic burger chef in a box' comes to campus | Chain Store Age
sources.claim: RoboBurger is a fully autonomous burger vending robot that grills the patty, toasts the ... and assembles the finished burger; deployed in a New Jersey mall and at St John's University dining with Chartwells.

sources.title: ABB and BurgerBots unveil robotic burger-making to revolutionize fast food prep | ABB News center
sources.claim: BurgerBots, a restaurant opened in Los Gatos, CA in April 2025, assembles made-to-order burgers in a self-contained robotic cell using ABB's IRB 360 FlexPicker and ... cobot.

sources.title: Chef Robotics completes 100M meal servings milestone - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI meal-assembly robots portion and deposit cooked ingredients into trays on production lines at food manufacturers, passing 100 million servings since first deploying at Amy's Kitchen in 2022.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning proteins, grains and vegetables into meal trays. Same objects and precision as building a salad bowl or filling a sandwich, but with trays presented on a conveyor and ingredients in fixed hoppers.

sources.title: The military's newest robot technology wants to make your salad - Fast Company
sources.claim: Dexai's Alfred robotic sous-chef, installed on a counter in the Travis Air Force Base dining hall, uses standard utensils to scoop ingredients from ordinary tubs into bowls, making grab-and-go salads; DoD contracted 10 units for dining facilities.

sources.title: Dexai Robotics' Alfred Acts as Sous Chef at Boston BONAPITA Restaurant - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Dexai installed Alfred as a food-preparation robot in a working fast-casual restaurant (BONAPITA, West Roxbury, MA), where it learns the chef's recipes in the existing kitchen; Dexai designs Alfred to work without altering customers' kitchen layouts.

sources.developer: Sweetgreen / Spyce (sold to Wonder in Nov 2025)
sources.title: Sweetgreen's robotic Infinite Kitchen is finally open | Restaurant Business
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen is an automated makeline in operating restaurants (e.g., Willis Tower, Chicago) that assembles salads and bowls to order as they travel on a conveyor past ingredient dispensers.

sources.title: Artly debuts mini Barista Bot at National Restaurant Association 2025 show
sources.claim: Artly's Barista Bot, a robotic arm running a vision-language-action model trained on motion-captured human baristas, makes espresso drinks with latte art in 15 US café locations, approaching one million cups served.

sources.title: Aramark and RoboEatz launch robotic meal service for healthcare workers
sources.claim: Aramark and RoboEatz deployed the Autonomous Robotic Kitchen (ARK) with ABB arms at WellSpan Health, serving hot and cold bowl meals around the clock in a 400 sq ft footprint from ingredient storage bins.

sources.title: RoboEatz Shows Off Ark 03 Autonomous Robotic Meal Making Kiosk - The Spoon
sources.claim: The RoboEatz ARK 03 kiosk holds 110 fresh ingredients including 30 liquids such as soups and dressings and cooks in an induction cooker, with humans needed only for refilling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hot bowl/soup cooking from ingredient bins. Same operation as short-order soup batch work — combining liquids and solids in a heated vessel with stirring and timing — inside a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Chinese start-up touts robot chefs, AI as the future of restaurant kitchens (SCMP via Yahoo Finance)
sources.claim: Botinkit's Omni is a commercially sold enclosed automated wok station that stir-fries and stews, doses seasoning and self-cleans with limited manual intervention; vendors report thousands of installations in restaurants, hotels, hospitals and cafeterias.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stewing/stir-frying with automated seasoning and stirring in a commercial kitchen. Soup and sauce batch cooking is the same operation — controlled heat, stirring, timed seasoning — with ingredients loaded into the station.

sources.system: Scott Automation robotic beef/lamb cutting systems
sources.title: A review of robotic and automated systems in meat processing - Frontiers in Robotics and AI
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed reviews of red-meat processing describe commercially fielded robotic cutting systems: Scott Automation combines robots, scribing saws and 3D/X-ray sensing to locate the carcass and make accurate cuts in processing plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic primal cutting/boning of carcasses. It covers the same physical act as carving and portioning meat — vision-guided blade paths through variable meat and bone — at higher force and comparable precision, in a fixtured plant cell.

sources.title: Stop & Shop to debut 'The Breadbot' | Grocery Dive
sources.claim: Wilkinson Baking's BreadBot is a standalone in-store machine that mixes, forms, proofs, bakes ... loaves from pre-loaded dry mix, introduced at a Stop & Shop supermarket.

sources.title: How automation is changing the face of bread production | Bake Magazine
sources.claim: By late 2022 the BreadBot had moved past pilots to a permanent grocery installation with additional units being built.

sources.title: Chipotle Rolls Out High-Efficiency Equipment and Automation Technologies to Optimize Kitchen Operations
sources.claim: Chipotle's Autocado cobot cuts, cores and peels avocados in about 26 seconds inside restaurant kitchens, while its automated bowl/salad makeline remains in refinement before broader rollout.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine cutting/coring/peeling of produce for cold prep. Shows produce knife-work is completed only by a purpose-built loader-fed machine, not by a robot working the cook's cutting board.

tasks.label: Perform general cleaning activities in kitchen and dining areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cook-line cleaning at shift change/close in a diner or grill: scrape and degrease the flattop/griddle and charbroiler, wipe grease off equipment exteriors, splash guards and reach-in handles, and scrub pots, pans, spatulas and small wares in the three-compartment sink. Hot, greasy, cluttered line, done under time pressure between or after rushes.

Warewashing during and after service: take bus tubs of dirty plates, glasses, cups and silverware, scrape and pre-rinse, rack them, run the commercial dish machine, then unload, air-dry and stack clean ware back on the line. High volume, mixed and slippery items.

Back-of-house floor care: sweep food debris and mop/degrease the kitchen floor behind the cook line, around fryers, under prep tables and rubber mats, plus immediate spill and grease response during service in a narrow, obstacle-filled aisle.
Front-of-house floor care: sweep, vacuum or mop the dining room, counter area and entry between rushes and at close, on an open dining floor with tables, booths and chairs.
Dining-area surface cleaning: clear and wipe/sanitize tables, counter tops, booth seats and menus, refill and clean condiment caddies and the drink station, reset the table after guests leave.

Waste handling and periodic deep cleaning: empty and reline kitchen and dining trash cans, haul bags and cardboard to the outside dumpster, pull and wash hood filters, clean walk-in shelving, move equipment to clean underneath and behind, clean floor drains and grease trap.

tasks.label: Order supplies and stock them on shelves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Diner/fast-food back door: a distributor delivery arrives on a hand truck or pallet jack — 20-50 lb cases of frozen patties, cooking oil jugs, produce boxes, dairy crates, cases of canned goods. Cook checks items against the invoice, hand-trucks them through a narrow kitchen, and puts them away on wire racks in the walk-in cooler, freezer, and dry storeroom.

Mid-shift restocking of the cook line and prep stations: fetching tubs of sliced tomatoes, cheese, portioned meat and sauces from the walk-in, refilling sixth-pans and squeeze bottles at the sandwich/grill station, topping off the fry hopper, and replenishing cups, lids, wraps and foil under the counter while service continues around them.

Weekly/biweekly inventory and ordering cycle: walking the walk-in, freezer and dry storage with a par sheet, counting full and partial cases, bags and containers, judging what will be needed, then phoning the distributor or entering the order in a vendor portal/tablet.

Storeroom and walk-in upkeep: rotating stock front-to-back by date (FIFO), moving older cases forward when new ones land, checking dates and pulling spoiled produce or expired product, consolidating partial cases, and breaking down and disposing of cardboard boxes.

Restocking uniform packaged goods: loading cans and bottled drinks, single-serve milk and juice into the reach-in/display cooler and stacking identical cases of a single SKU onto a designated shelf, in a fixed, standardized location.

tasks.label: Accept payments, and make change or write charge slips as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cash payment at a diner or fast-food counter register: customer hands over bills for a short-order ticket, the cook/cashier rings the sale, opens the till, counts out bills and coins, and returns change with a printed receipt during a lunch rush.
Card payment at the counter point-of-sale: the cook rings the order, the customer taps/inserts or hands over a card, and the worker returns the card, the receipt and a tip/signature slip.
Payment collected away from the register: the cook/counter worker carries the check to a booth or table, takes cash or a card back to the register, and returns change or a slip for signature.
Food truck, cart or outdoor festival window: mixed cash and phone-attached card reader, outdoor weather, noise and a crowd pressing at the service window; change made from an apron bank.
Non-routine transactions: split checks, coupons and gift cards, employee/house-account or hand-written charge slips, comps and voids, and correcting a mis-rung ticket.

tasks.label: Clean and sanitize work areas, equipment, utensils, dishes, or silverware.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dish room of a restaurant or institutional cafeteria: scrape and pre-rinse plates, cups, glasses and silverware out of bus tubs, rack them, run the commercial dish machine, unload, sort silverware and stack clean ware for service; continuous flow during and after service.

Wiping and sanitizing work areas between and after prep jobs: clearing debris from prep tables, cutting boards, deli counters and hand sinks, washing with detergent and applying sanitizer solution at correct concentration, working around stored ingredients, tools and coworkers in a busy kitchen.

Breaking down and cleaning food preparation equipment: deli slicer, food processor, mixer, blender, juicer, coffee brewer and urns - disassemble removable parts, wash and sanitize them, wipe and sanitize the housing, then reassemble and test.

End-of-shift and deep cleaning of the work area: sweeping and mopping greasy kitchen floors around equipment and drains, emptying trash and recycling, wiping walk-in shelving, scrubbing sinks and cleaning hood filters or vent screens.

instances.label: Restaurant kitchen during service: prep worker responds to cooks' spoken requests on the fly — grabbing a backup pan of prepped protein from the reach-in, a squeeze bottle of sauce, a clean sauté pan or hotel pan, a stack of plates — carrying it through a hot, crowded, wet line and setting it where the cook can reach it, plus topping off line pans as they run low.

Institutional or high-volume kitchen (hospital, school district, corporate cafeteria, senior living, catering commissary): pulling cases and bulk pans from receiving, dry storage and the walk-in, breaking them down, and staging them at cooks' stations, kettles and steam tables through the shift; putting away deliveries and retrieving specific stock when a cook asks.

Ad hoc prep help on a cook's direction: scooping, portioning and panning ingredients, filling hotel pans and bowls, weighing portions, plating garnishes and cold components into pans the cook will finish, done at a bench in the kitchen with pans of ingredients at hand.

Ad hoc knife work requested mid-shift: dicing onions or peppers, slicing tomatoes or bread, trimming and portioning proteins so the cook has cut product for the next batch, using a board and knife at a prep bench.

Dish-room / clean-ware support so cooks keep working: clearing bus tubs and dirty dishware, glassware and silverware, racking and running them through the commercial dish machine, and returning clean ware and smallwares to the line.

Odd-job support in non-standard conditions: scrubbing burnt pots and pans by hand, wiping and sanitizing benches and equipment during turnaround, hauling trash and grease, and assisting cooks at off-site catering or banquet setups in a space taken as found.

tasks.label: Take and record temperature of food and food storage areas, such as refrigerators and freezers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Storage-area temperature round in a restaurant or institutional kitchen: walk through the kitchen and back-of-house, read the walk-in cooler, walk-in freezer, reach-in refrigerators, prep-table wells and ice-cream freezer (external digital displays or hanging dial/spirit thermometers inside the box), and enter each value with time/initials on a paper log or tablet app; flag any unit out of range to the manager. Done at open, mid-shift and close.

Hot-holding line check during service: with a calibrated stem or thermocouple probe, take the internal temperature of each pan of food on the steam table/serving line (soups, chili, gravies, roasted meats, rice), waiting for the reading to stabilize, sanitizing the probe between items, then record each value on the hot-holding log and re-heat or discard items below 135 F. Steamy, crowded line, food in varied pans and consistencies.

Cold-holding check: probe the internal temperature of prepped cold foods in the salad bar, sandwich/deli display case, cold wells and walk-in shelves (cut melon, deli salads, sliced meats, dressings), sanitize the probe between items, record on the cold-holding log and act on anything above 41 F.

Receiving check at the back dock: as a refrigerated/frozen delivery is unloaded, open cases and probe product or take between-package/product temperatures of milk, meat, seafood and frozen goods, record temperatures on the receiving log against the invoice, and reject or set aside out-of-temperature product. Pallets and cases arrive in varying positions, packaging and load order.

Cooking, cooling and reheating monitoring: probe the thickest part of cooked batches (chicken, roasts, casseroles) to verify final cook temperature, and take timed temperature readings of large batches cooling in shallow pans, ice baths or a blast chiller (e.g., at 2 hours and 6 hours), recording each time/temperature pair on the cooling or production log and taking corrective action if the cooling curve is missed.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped runs scheduled autonomous inspection rounds with a thermal payload, capturing temperature readings at defined points and centralizing them with thresholds and trend history — i.e., taking and recording temperatures on a fixed route through a facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous thermal inspection rounds in an industrial facility. Transfers to reading and logging refrigerator/freezer temperatures: same act of visiting fixed points on a route, capturing a temperature value and writing it to a timestamped record with alarm thresholds, in an institution-controlled indoor facility; no fine manipulation is required.

sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: A midstream gas plant deployed Spot for autonomous inspection routes across the site that include thermal inspections and reading analog gauges, with the robot navigating the whole facility on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous gauge/thermal rounds at a process plant. A walk-in cooler's wall-mounted digital display or dial thermometer is the same class of instrument as the analog gauges Spot reads, and the deliverable (a logged reading plus an out-of-range alert) is the same.

sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot reads analog gauges across a site using a computer-vision add-on, records the values in Boston Dynamics' Orbit software for trending, and raises alerts on abnormal readings, removing the need for manual rounds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated instrument reading and record-keeping. Recording a refrigeration unit's displayed temperature into a compliance log is the same perceive-value-then-record loop, on comparable dial/digital readouts, inside a facility with a fixed layout.

sources.title: Automation and digitalization with ANYmal — the case at BASF | ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot performed autonomous inspection rounds at a BASF chemical production plant, reading gauges and checking the environment for ... with its integrated thermal camera, with data fed into the operator's systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous instrument-reading and thermal rounds in a working plant. It transfers to storage-area temperature logging because the objects (wall/equipment-mounted temperature readouts), the required precision (read a displayed number correctly) and the setting (institution-controlled facility with a fixed route) are comparable.

sources.title: How Security Robots Can Save Money and Lives | Cobalt

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous environmental-condition rounds inside a human work facility. Recording area temperatures on a repeated indoor route and escalating anomalies is the same output as a refrigerator/freezer temperature log, in the same class of institution-controlled indoor setting.

sources.title: Flippy, the World's First Autonomous Robotic Kitchen Assistant, Now Cooks Burgers at CaliBurger | Miso Robotics
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy uses thermal plus 3D and visual sensing to monitor food temperature autonomously while cooking on a grill in a commercial restaurant kitchen, but it judges doneness for cooking control rather than probing internal temperatures of held foods and writing them to a food-safety log.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed food-temperature sensing in a commercial kitchen, cited to show the limit of current capability: it infers grill doneness for one product with non-contact sensing and does not insert, stabilize, sanitize and log a calibrated internal probe reading, so it does not complete the probing instances.

tasks.label: Carry food supplies, equipment, and utensils to and from storage and work areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restaurant/commercial kitchen: prep worker walks to the walk-in cooler or dry storeroom, finds the needed items among mixed stacked stock on wire shelving (case of lettuce, 25-lb bag of flour, 6 quart-tubs of dressing), lifts them, opens the insulated door, and carries them through narrow wet aisles past moving coworkers to the prep table.

Institutional food service (hospital, university, school district, large cafeteria): loaded carts, tray racks, and speed racks of supplies and equipment are moved between the storeroom/loading dock, main kitchen, and prep or serving areas over long corridors, ramps, and elevators; dirty carts are returned to the dish room.

Small wares runs: carrying clean sheet pans, hotel pans, mixing bowls, cutting boards, bus tubs of knives/utensils, and containers from warewashing racks or the pot/pan shelf to individual work stations, and returning dirty/used ones to the dish area during and after the shift.

Receiving a delivery: breaking down pallets and stacks of cases at the back door or dock, checking them, and moving produce, dairy, dry goods and frozen items into the dry store, walk-in cooler and freezer, stacking them on shelves in rotation order.

Moving filled/heavy items during service prep: hotel pans of prepped food, stock pots, ingredient bins, and sheet trays of product carried from the prep area to the cook line, steam table or salad bar, and leftovers carried back into the walk-in at close; spill-sensitive and sometimes hot.

Off-site/mobile food service: catering event, food truck, stadium concession stand or farmers-market booth — carrying coolers, cambros, cases and equipment from a van across parking lots, ramps, gravel or turf into an unfamiliar temporary work area.

tasks.label: Remove trash and clean kitchen garbage containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-shift bag swap in a busy restaurant/commercial kitchen: pull the full, wet, unevenly loaded liner out of a 32-gal can wedged under a prep table, tie it off, carry it through the cook line and out the back door into the dumpster, then re-line the can and slide it back into place — all while cooks and servers work around.

Institutional kitchen (hospital, university dining, school district commissary): haul full waste, recycling and compost carts/barrels from the kitchen and dish room, down service corridors and elevators, to the loading dock / trash compactor holding area, and bring empty carts back.

Institutional kitchen, disposal end of the same run: tip the heavy barrels/carts into the compactor or dumpster hopper, then wash and sanitize the emptied carts before they go back to the kitchen floor.

End-of-shift deep clean of the garbage containers themselves: take cans to the mop sink or outdoor wash pad, hose them out, scrub with degreaser inside and out, sanitize, drain/dry, and re-line before service.

Small independent kitchen with no dock: carry tied bags out through a shared back alley at night, break down cardboard, separate recycling and grease containers, drag wheeled totes over uneven pavement to the curb or shared dumpster corral, weather and passersby included.

Continuous emptying of small under-counter scrap bins, prep-station trim containers and grease catch pots during prep: dump into the main can, rinse the small container, return it to the station without contaminating food surfaces.

sources.system: Tesla Optimus; Loki Robotics wheeled cleaning robot (as assessed by Epoch AI)
sources.developer: Tesla; Loki Robotics (assessment by Epoch AI)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI

sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the waste-hauling leg of the task in an institutional facility: full waste carts collected from departments and delivered to trash compactors, with empty carts returned.

tasks.label: Store food in designated containers and storage areas to prevent spoilage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restaurant/cafeteria prep station at end of a prep block: worker portions prepped or leftover cold and hot foods (salads, cut fruit, sauces, cooked grains) into deli containers and hotel pans, lids or plastic film applied, day-dot/date label written, containers carried into a walk-in cooler and shelved in the designated zone.

Putting away an incoming delivery in a restaurant, school, hospital or grocery-deli kitchen: mixed cases, bags and boxes moved from the receiving area to walk-in cooler, freezer and dry-storage shelving; existing stock pulled forward for FIFO rotation, damaged/short items set aside, all within the temperature-abuse time window.

Covering filled hotel pans and sheet trays with lids or film after batch prep, then loading them onto speed racks/sheet-pan racks and rolling the rack into the walk-in or blast chiller; pans of varying depth and weight, stacked without spilling.

Storing raw proteins and shellfish: fish and shellfish drained and re-iced in perforated pans, raw meats bagged/panned and placed on lowest shelves away from ready-to-eat items in reach-ins and walk-ins, cross-contamination hierarchy observed.

Transferring bulk dry goods (flour, sugar, rice, pasta) from opened sacks and cases into labeled lidded ingredient bins in dry storage, sealing partially used bags, and shelving remaining stock off the floor.

Off-premise catering or food truck: packing prepped foods into insulated cambros, hotel pans and ice chests at an event site or client kitchen taken as found, holding them cold/hot and restocking coolers through service.

sources.system: Chef Robotics Chef+ meal assembly robot

sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning prepared foods into food containers on a line. sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads floor-loaded cases from trailers and containers onto conveyors at up to 700–1,000 cases per hour in logistics facilities, with DHL committing to up to 1,000 units.

tasks.label: Weigh or measure ingredients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restaurant or in-store bakery prep: scaling dry bulk ingredients (flour, sugar, rice, breading, spice blends) out of storage bins and bags into containers on a digital scale for the day's batch recipes; quantities from grams to several kilos, many different ingredients per recipe.

Measuring pourable liquids that sit in a plumbed or loaded reservoir - water for dough, dressings, syrups, juice/dairy bases - into a mixer, pitcher or container to a specified volume during batch prep.

Measuring oils, stocks, dairy and other liquids poured from bulk jugs/cambros into measuring cups, pots or pitchers for a batch recipe in an ordinary kitchen, with human-scale vessels and no dedicated dispenser.

Portioning prepped foods to standard portion weights on a scale: 4-oz scoops of salad/protein into deli cups or hotel pans, weighed sliced meat/cheese portions, weighed bowl/tray components for assembly during prep and service.

Institutional or commissary kitchen (school, hospital, catering commissary): weighing large-batch quantities (10-50 lb of rice, beans, flour, sauce base) on a floor/bench scale and charging them into a tilt kettle or floor mixer.
Beverage-station measuring: dosing coffee grounds by weight for brewing/espresso, measuring tea, drink mixes, concentrates and syrups to recipe amounts at a cafe or restaurant beverage station.

sources.title: First Look at Sweetgreen's Technology-Enabled Infinite Kitchen Concept - McMillanDoolittle
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen is an automated makeline deployed in dozens of operating restaurants; suspended ingredient containers dispense exact portions of each ingredient into bowls moving on a track, replacing human portioning.

tasks.label: Vacuum dining area and sweep and mop kitchen floor.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift floor care of a restaurant/café dining area: chairs placed on tables or pushed in, carpet vacuumed or hard floor swept and damp-mopped, crumbs, napkins, straw wrappers and dried spills under and around tables and booths, edges and entry mats included; done after close with no guests present.

End-of-shift sweep and mop of the commercial kitchen: greasy quarry tile or epoxy floor, rubber anti-fatigue mats lifted and moved, food debris and packaging swept from tight aisles between hot line equipment, prep tables and dish machine, degreaser applied with mop/deck brush and rinse water pushed to floor drains.

Mid-shift response in the dining area to dry debris — spilled crackers, popcorn, french fries, tracked-in dirt near a table or entry — swept up with broom and dustpan or a quick vacuum pass while guests are seated nearby.

Mid-shift response to a wet or hazardous spill: dropped tray of food, spilled drink or broken glassware in the dining area or on the kitchen line; debris and shards picked up, area mopped and dried, wet-floor sign placed, all within a couple of minutes while service continues around it.

Institutional dining hall / cafeteria / hotel banquet room floor after a meal period: large open carpeted or hard-floor area on a fixed layout, vacuumed or scrubbed with a machine, tables and chairs in standard positions, cleaned between or after service periods.

Detail and deep floor cleaning: sweeping and mopping corners, baseboards, under and behind prep tables, fryers and reach-ins, under booth seats, dish-area and walk-in floors; mats hauled out and hosed, small furniture and trash cans moved and replaced.

tasks.label: Wash, peel, and cut various foods, such as fruits and vegetables, to prepare for cooking or serving.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restaurant prep station mise en place: a prep worker at a stainless table in a full-service or fast-casual kitchen washes greens, peels garlic/carrots/onions, and hand-cuts several products in modest batches to differing specs (dice, julienne, chiffonade) using knives, a peeler, and a food processor, working from ungraded case produce with judgment trimming of bruises and wilted leaves.

High-volume institutional kitchen (school district, hospital, university dining, corporate cafeteria, catering commissary): bulk commodity prep of 50-300 lb lots of potatoes, carrots, onions, cabbage, celery and lettuce, washed in a prep sink or vegetable washer, peeled, and run through a buffalo chopper or commercial vegetable cutter to a uniform cut for cooking or salad bar.

Fresh-cut fruit prep in a supermarket deli/produce prep room, juice bar, or hotel breakfast kitchen: washing, peeling, coring and cutting melons, pineapple, citrus, apples, grapes and berries for fruit cups, platters and salad bar pans, with ripeness sorting and trimming of soft spots, then panning or packaging.

QSR/deli line prep during service hours: repeated small batches of washed and spun lettuce, sliced tomatoes, onions, cucumbers, pickles and lemon wedges portioned into pans on a crowded make line, done quickly between service peaks with standard equipment (slicer, wedger, spinner).

Small operation with high variability: independent cafe, food truck, or small caterer's kitchen where one worker washes, peels and cuts whatever mixed produce arrived that day in very small quantities, on a single cutting board with a knife and peeler and little or no powered prep equipment.

tasks.label: Prepare a variety of foods, such as meats, vegetables, or desserts, according to customers' orders or supervisors' instructions, following approved procedures.

instances.label: Restaurant/fast-casual prep kitchen mise en place: from a supervisor's prep list, wash, peel, core and cut mixed produce (onions, peppers, lettuce, tomatoes, melon) to specified cuts and sizes with knives, boards and a mandoline/buffalo chopper; pan, label, date and refrigerate. Shared kitchen aisle, wet floors, other staff working alongside.

Protein and seafood prep in a restaurant back-of-house or supermarket meat/seafood department: trim, slice and portion raw meats and poultry to weight spec, slice deli meats/cheeses on a slicer to a customer's requested thickness, peel/devein shrimp, shuck or clean shellfish; weigh, wrap, label.

Made-to-order salads and grain bowls at a fast-casual or cafeteria line: read the ticket, portion greens, grains, proteins and toppings from standard pans with scoops/tongs into a bowl, dress and mix, close and stage for the customer; peak-hour pace, frequent order variety and pan restocking.

Made-to-order sandwiches, wraps, deli platters and cold plates: layer breads/spreads/fillings, arrange portioned components on trays or platters to a spec picture, garnish, wrap and label for a customer order or catering pickup.

Institutional kitchen (hospital, school district, university, corrections) bulk prep and tray assembly: portion cold salads, fruit cups, sides and desserts into trays/compartments per menu and diet-order tickets on a tray line, at high volume against a service clock.

Dessert and bakery-adjacent prep: portion and plate cakes/pies, pipe icing or whipped topping, decorate and garnish desserts, cut fruit for platters, assemble parfaits per recipe card or a customer's special-order instructions.

tasks.label: Assemble meal trays with foods in accordance with patients' diets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital kitchen cook-serve conveyor trayline at meal time: worker stands at an assigned station (starter, hot entree, cold food, beverage) and, reading each patient's diet ticket as the tray passes, places the correct plated entree, sides, bread, dessert and beverage on the tray at roughly 4-6 seconds per tray for several hundred standard-diet trays per meal.

Same trayline or central-kitchen line, but therapeutic and texture-modified orders: pureed, mechanical-soft, renal, low-sodium, carb-controlled, thickened-liquid and allergy trays, where portion sizes and item substitutions must match the diet order exactly and errors are clinically consequential.

Hospital room-service model: an individual patient order arrives on a screen and the worker assembles one complete tray to order (hot plate under a dome, cold items, beverage, condiments, flatware, napkin, printed ticket) within a 30-45 minute promise window, with items and combinations varying order to order.

Skilled nursing / long-term-care facility: worker assembles resident trays at a steam table or counter from resident diet cards, plating portions, adding adaptive dishes, cups and clothing protectors, verifying against the card and loading trays into delivery carts for each unit.

Cold-side and between-meal work: assembling cold trays, snack and nourishment trays in advance (salads, desserts, juices, milk cartons, prepackaged condiment/utensil packs, supplements), labeling and loading them into refrigerated or retherm carts ahead of the meal.

instances.label: Restaurant/institutional kitchen: put away a delivery into the walk-in refrigerator, freezer and dry-storage cupboards — break down cases, rotate stock FIFO, shelve varied items (produce boxes, dairy tubs, bagged greens, cans, deli containers) on standard wire shelving in a cold, wet, cluttered space shared with other staff.

Cafeteria/supermarket dining area during service: tend a self-serve cold salad bar — watch levels, top off or swap out inserts of cut vegetables, dressings and proteins from backup pans in the walk-in, keep ice/temperature right, pull expired product, wipe spills, replace tongs and plates while customers are at the bar.

Hotel banquet, buffet restaurant or institutional cafeteria: tend a hot buffet/steam-table line — carry hot pans from the kitchen, refill or exchange chafer pans, keep the presentation neat, check holding temperatures, restock plates and serving utensils during a service period.

Kitchen prep/line stocking before and during service: fill line reach-ins, cold wells and prep-station cupboards — portion prepped foods into inserts and deli containers, fill condiment/topping containers, label and date, and place items at the correct stations.
Off-site catered buffet at a client venue or outdoor event: transport and set up chafers, sterno and pans in a space taken as found, then replenish food and supplies through the event.

tasks.label: Use manual or electric appliances to clean, peel, slice, and trim foods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk produce prep by hand in a restaurant or institutional (school/hospital/cafeteria) kitchen: washing lettuce and vegetables at a prep sink, hand-peeling potatoes/carrots/onions, and knife-cutting them into dice, strips or slices on a cutting board at a prep table, working from a prep list before service.

Bulk produce prep using powered appliances in the same kitchen: loading a batch abrasive potato peeler, running a buffalo chopper/food processor with dicing plates, running cheese/vegetable through a mandoline or bench slicer, emptying and re-loading between products, then panning and labeling output.

Grocery/deli counter and sandwich-shop slicing: retrieving logs of deli meat and blocks of cheese, mounting them on an electric gravity slicer, setting thickness, slicing to weight for customers or for a par-stock case, trimming ends and wrapping/panning the product.

Protein prep in a restaurant, deli or supermarket meat/seafood room: trimming fat and silverskin from primals and portioning, cleaning and filleting whole fish, peeling and deveining shrimp, shucking or cleaning shellfish, working on a cutting board or bench.

Small-batch, varied prep for plating and à-la-carte service: turning/tourné cuts, carved or decorative garnishes, fanned fruit and mixed fruit platters, trimming individual items to a chef's spec in small quantities during service, with frequent changes of item and cut.

tasks.label: Load dishes, glasses, and tableware into dishwashing machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant dish pit during service: bus tubs of mixed soiled plates, bowls, cups and flatware arrive from the dining room; the worker scrapes/pre-rinses, sorts items into peg racks and flatware cylinders, pushes racks through a door-type or rack-conveyor machine, and stacks clean ware. Wet, hot, greasy, fast-paced.

High-volume institutional cafeteria (hospital, school, university, corporate dining): soiled trays come back on a tray-return conveyor or in carts; the worker breaks down trays, separates dishes, glasses and silverware, and feeds a flight-type or rack-conveyor warewasher continuously through a rush. Standardized dishware, high throughput.

Bar/café glass and cup work: loading pint glasses, stemware, mugs and to-go cups into glass racks and running an undercounter glasswasher or door machine repeatedly through a shift; delicate, transparent ware, sticky residues.

Prep-area smallwares: the prep worker loads used mixing bowls, hotel and sheet pans, cutting boards, utensils, food-processor parts, deli containers and lids into racks for the dish machine between prep tasks; bulky, odd-shaped, heavily soiled items.

Banquet/hotel or stadium event dish room: waves of hundreds of identical plates, side plates and glasses arrive on carts after each course; the worker rapidly racks uniform ware and cycles it through a high-capacity conveyor machine.

Off-site catering or mobile setting: dishes and glassware are handled at a rented hall, tent or client site with a portable/temporary warewasher, or trucked back and staged in an improvised area; layout differs event to event.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

Full-service restaurant kitchen during service: placing portioned cold appetizers, salads, cheese/charcuterie, sides and desserts directly onto plates, arranging components and garnish to the house presentation standard, wiping rims, and passing to the pass.

Back-of-house prep kitchen/commissary between services: dividing bulk-prepared foods (soups, sauces, salads, cooked proteins) into portioned deli containers, hotel pans or portion bags to a target weight, covering with film or lids, labeling/dating and racking for later service.

Institutional foodservice (hospital, school, senior living, airline/central kitchen): portioning standardized servings onto plates, trays or compartment trays on a tray line or serving line, matching each tray to a menu/diet card, covering or lidding, and loading carts.

Grocery deli / prepared-foods counter or catering kitchen: weighing bulk salads, sliced meats and cheeses into deli containers or onto trays and platters, wrapping in film or paper, applying weight/price labels, and setting product in the case or on the buffet.

tasks.label: Add cutlery, napkins, food, and other items to trays on assembly lines in hospitals, cafeterias, airline kitchens, and similar establishments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital / nursing-home patient tray line: worker stands at a station on a moving belt in the hospital kitchen and, reading each patient's printed diet ticket, adds the assigned items (entrée plate under a dome, side dish, bread, condiment packets, wrapped cutlery, napkin, beverage) to each tray; every tray differs by diet order (puree, low-sodium, NPO changes), 200-600 trays per meal period against a hard delivery clock.

School district / college / corrections central-kitchen batch tray or clamshell line: identical standardized meals assembled at speed on a conveyor — entrée into the compartment, sides, fruit cup, milk carton, wrapped cutlery-napkin kit — a fixed menu for the day, run in batches for satellite sites or housing units.

Airline / rail catering kitchen tray setting: very high volume, highly standardized casserole trays and tray sets — placing cutlery packs, napkin, salad/dessert cups, bread roll, condiment sachets in exactly specified positions on trays moving down a setting belt, to a strict spec sheet and a flight departure deadline.

Cafeteria/commissary grab-and-go and boxed-meal assembly: packing sandwiches, salads, sides, dressing cups, plus condiment-and-cutlery kits into boxes, clamshells or trays on a table-and-conveyor line for retail coolers, catered drop-offs or meal programs; standard recipe cards, batch runs.

Small facility manual tray assembly with no conveyor: in a small hospital unit, nursing home or assisted-living kitchen, the worker builds trays on a counter or cart directly from a steam table and reach-ins — mixed crockery, special diets, late/ad-hoc requests, staff moving through the same space.

tasks.label: Place food trays over food warmers for immediate service, or store them in refrigerated storage cabinets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Institutional cafeteria (school, hospital, university, corporate) hot serving line: worker carries full-size and half-size hotel pans of hot prepared food from the cookline or holding oven and seats them into steam-table wells/over food warmers, swapping and rotating pans during service. Pans are heavy, hot, liquid-laden, and the line is crowded with staff and diners.

Restaurant or commissary kitchen cold storage: worker covers, labels, dates, and racks sheet pans, hotel pans, and cambros of prepped cold foods onto wire shelves in reach-in and walk-in refrigerators; shelves are partly full, spacing varies, floors are wet and aisles tight.

Hospital / long-term-care tray line: assembled patient meal trays coming off the belt are slid into slots of heated-refrigerated delivery carts (or held in refrigerated cabinets) on a strict meal-period deadline, with trays holding open beverages and plated hot and cold items.

Catering / banquet work, on- and off-premise: pans of finished food are loaded into insulated hot-holding cabinets and refrigerated transport carts in banquet kitchens, tents, loading docks, and client sites; layout and equipment placement differ event to event.

QSR / fast-casual prep: pans of prepped ingredients placed into refrigerated prep-table wells and reach-in coolers, and trays of batch-cooked items placed in holding cabinets under heat lamps, in a small standardized back-of-house during service.

QSR cook station transfer for immediate service: cooked batch (fries, rings, tenders) moved from the cooking equipment into the hot-holding bin/warming area at the fry or grill station so it is ready for assembly.

sources.claim: Robotray's automated rack loading/unloading system loads and unloads trays, pans and boards into and out of single or double bakery racks at 14-24 trays per minute without employee handling.
