The rack slots of a bakery rack, an oven rack, a hot-holding cabinet and a refrigerated storage cabinet are the same mechanical target; precision and object type (full-size pans/trays) match the foodservice task, with the trays presented to the machine by conveyor.

sources.developer: Cimcorp (for Kroger / Mountain View Foods, Denver)
sources.title: Kroger — Cimcorp Customer Case Study
sources.claim: Cimcorp gantry robots at Kroger's Mountain View Foods dairy perform packing, picking and palletizing of product crates inside the cold-storage areas of the plant entirely by automation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting food containers into and out of refrigerated storage. Comparable objects (stackable food crates vs. pans/trays), comparable precision (stack and slot placement), and it establishes robot operation inside refrigerated space in a purpose-built automated facility.

sources.title: Miso Robotics launches Flippy 2 for QSRs — QSR Web
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy 2, deployed in operating White Castle restaurant kitchens, autonomously identifies the food, cooks it in the correct basket, and places the finished product into a hot-holding area for immediate service.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the 'place food for immediate service into hot holding' step at a QSR cook station, in a working restaurant kitchen; the carrier is a fry basket/holding bin rather than a hotel pan, but the purpose, timing and destination (warming/hot-holding station) are the same.

sources.system: RoboEatz Autonomous Robotic Kitchen (ARK) / Fresh Take Eatery
sources.developer: RoboEatz with ABB Robotics (deployed by WellSpan Health)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving food containers into and out of refrigerated holding and hot service positions. sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics runs three 7-DoF arms autonomously in the dish pits of multiple operating restaurants around the clock, handling plates, glasses and bus tubs; it is the closest system to unmodified-kitchen manipulation, but it works at a fixed dish station and does not move loaded food pans to warmers or into refrigeration.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E2 judgment: it is the most capable manipulator documented working in an ordinary commercial kitchen, yet its demonstrated scope is dish handling at one fixed station, so it does not substantiate carrying loaded pans to steam wells or racking them in walk-in coolers.

sources.title: Automating tray management with a new robot — Baking Business
sources.claim: Apex Motion Control's Baker-Bot collaborative robot is sold to bakery and snack manufacturers to automate loading and unloading of trays ... to and from conveyors and racks, with dual-racking so one full rack is removed while another loads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of full trays and pans onto racks in food production. Same objects and placement precision as racking pans in heated or refrigerated cabinets, in a line built around the robot.

tasks.label: Prepare and serve a variety of beverages, such as coffee, tea, and soft drinks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Café/coffee-bar counter: made-to-order espresso drinks (lattes, cappuccinos, Americanos) during a morning rush — grind, dose, tamp, pull shots, steam milk, add syrups, lid and hand off, wiping the wand and dumping pucks between drinks.

Cafeteria, diner, hospital or corporate dining kitchen: batch-brewing drip coffee and iced tea into urns/airpots, brewing hot tea, keeping the beverage station stocked with cups, lids, ice, creamers, discarding stale batches and cleaning brew equipment.

Quick-service restaurant counter/drive-thru: filling fountain soft drinks and iced beverages to order — grabbing the right cup size, ice, pour, lid, straw, staging with the order for pickup at peak throughput.
Juice/smoothie bar or restaurant: blended and mixed non-alcoholic drinks — smoothies, milkshakes, boba/milk tea, fresh lemonade — measuring ingredients, blending, pouring, sealing/lidding.
Banquet, stadium or catered event at a hotel/venue: staffing a beverage station where guests come up — dispensing coffee, tea, soda and mocktails to guests at the station and keeping it replenished.
Dining room, patient trayline or banquet floor: pouring drinks and carrying trays of filled cups/glasses to seated diners, topping up coffee and water at the table on request.

sources.title: A robot barista represents a larger vision for bringing robotics to more areas of retail - Modern Retail
sources.claim: Richtech's dual-arm ADAM robot barista makes most of the drinks at the Clouffee & Tea café in Las Vegas, with one or two human workers restocking the ingredients it reaches; the station is built around the robot.

sources.title: CES 2025: Artly the Robot Barista Uses AI and Motion Capture Technology

tasks.label: Mix ingredients for green salads, molded fruit salads, vegetable salads, and pasta salads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Limited-service/fast-casual or cafeteria serving line: worker builds individual salads and salad bowls to order from pans of prepped greens, cut vegetables, grains, proteins and toppings, adds dressing, and hands off; standard steam-table/cold-well line, high order rate at peak.

Full-service restaurant pantry station during service: worker combines greens, vegetables, cheese and croutons in a mixing bowl, tosses with dressing to coat, plates the salad with garnish to the restaurant's presentation standard, one order at a time.

Restaurant or catering commissary morning prep: mix 5-20 lb batches of house salad mix, pasta salad or slaw in large bowls/tubs to a recipe, fold in dressing, transfer to lexans/hotel pans, date and hold in the walk-in.

Supermarket deli / prepared-foods back kitchen: scale ingredients for 20-40 lb recipe batches of pasta, potato or macaroni salad and coleslaw, combine in a floor mixer or tub, fold in dressing, pan into display trays and label.

Institutional cafeteria (school, hospital, college, military dining): large-batch vegetable and fruit salads to standardized recipes for hundreds of covers, panned into hotel pans for the salad bar or tray line, occasionally including molded gelatin fruit salads.
Off-site catering or banquet work: salads mixed in a rented, host or on-site event kitchen with variable layout, borrowed equipment and improvised work surfaces, on a tight service timeline.

sources.title: Dexai Robotics signs $1.6 million contract with DLA - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Dexai's Alfred cobot arm was deployed prepping salads in the kitchen of a US military base dining facility, using AI and computer vision and switching utensils on its own, as the first of 10 units under a $1.6M Defense Logistics Agency contract.

sources.title: Dexai Robotics' Alfred Acts as Sous Chef at Boston BONAPITA Restaurant - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Alfred was installed commercially (robotics-as-a-service, per-dish fee) at a fast-casual restaurant to prepare salads and bowls in the existing kitchen, using standard utensils and requiring no change to the restaurant's layout or recipes.

sources.title: Sweetgreen Goes All-In with Automated Restaurants - QSR Magazine

sources.claim: Hyphen's under-counter automated Makeline assembles salads and bowls from hundreds of ingredients at high accuracy and throughput; it is commercially deployed and piloted with fast-casual chains.

sources.title: Batch Weighing System for salad mix & vegetable mix | KRONEN GmbH
sources.claim: KRONEN sells an automated batch weighing system that composes precise recipe-based salad and vegetable blends in 10-300 kg batches on a continuous processing line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recipe-based composition of bulk salad blends in a processing plant. Same objects (cut lettuce, vegetables, fruit), same operation (weighing ingredients to a recipe and combining them), at batch sizes equal to or larger than a deli or cafeteria batch.

sources.system: KRONEN K120 / K230 salad and delicatessen mixing machines
sources.title: Mixing machines | KRONEN GmbH
sources.claim: KRONEN's K120/K230 salad and delicatessen mixing machines mix cut vegetables, lettuce, herbs, fruit and delicatessen products homogeneously and gently at up to 1,800 kg/h with semi-automatic loading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial mixing of salad and delicatessen batches. The physical act (gentle homogeneous blending of cut produce, pasta/deli components and dressings) is the same as the worker's bulk salad mixing, with the batch brought to the machine.

sources.title: We've Raised a $43.1M Series A to Accelerate Our AI-Enabled Robot Deployments | Chef Robotics
sources.claim: Chef Robotics operates a fleet of AI-enabled robot arms in North American food production facilities that portion and assemble prepped ingredients into meal containers on production lines, having handled ~2,000 ingredients and produced tens of millions of servings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recipe-accurate portioning and combining of prepped food components (grains, pasta, cut vegetables, proteins, sauces) into containers on a line. Same ingredient variability and precision demands as combining salad components to a recipe.

tasks.label: Receive and store food supplies, equipment, and utensils in refrigerators, cupboards, and other storage areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restaurant/café back-of-house receives a mixed vendor delivery at the back door: 15–40 assorted cases and crates (produce, dairy, boxed meat, dry goods, frozen). Worker checks counts and temperatures against the invoice, carts loads through a narrow, busy kitchen, and shelves items in the walk-in cooler, freezer and dry storeroom with FIFO rotation, breaking down cartons.

Institutional or high-volume kitchen (hospital, school district, university dining, catering commissary) takes a palletized bulk delivery at a loading dock; moves pallets with a pallet jack to a staging area, breaks pallets down to cases, stores them in walk-ins, freezers and dry stores, and logs temperatures/dates.

Mid-shift replenishment inside the kitchen: fetching packaged stock from bulk dry storage and the walk-in and refilling prep-station reach-in coolers, line rails, beverage coolers and cupboards, rotating so the oldest stock is in front, while cooks work around the aisles.

Putting away clean smallwares coming out of the dish area: sheet pans, hotel pans, mixing bowls, cutting boards, cutlery and hand utensils, stacked and sorted onto shelves, drawers, hanging racks and cupboards.

Receiving and storing non-food supplies and equipment: paper goods, to-go containers, cleaning chemicals, small equipment; bulky or heavy cartons carried into storerooms and stacked on high or low shelves per storage rules (chemicals separated from food).

sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch mobile manipulator autonomously unloads cases from trailers and containers onto conveyors in commercial deployments at DHL Supply Chain — the receiving/unloading half of taking in a delivery of mixed cartons.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: truck/container unloading of mixed cartons. It is the receiving step of this task with the same objects (cases of consumer goods, including food), performed where deliveries arrive; it substantiates machine handling of an incoming mixed delivery in a purpose-built dock/conveyor setting.

sources.system: Symbotic warehouse automation system (robotic depalletizers + autonomous case-handling mobile robots)
sources.title: Walmart plans to automate 25 distribution centers with Symbotic
sources.claim: Symbotic's system automates inbound receiving through storage: robotic arms depalletize incoming shipments and autonomous mobile robots carry each case to its assigned storage location in the structure; deployed at Walmart regional distribution centers since 2017 and rolling out across 25+ RDCs as of 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inbound case put-away in a grocery distribution center. Same act as this task — breaking down an incoming delivery to case level and placing each case in a designated storage location — with the same objects (grocery cases), in a setting built around the machine.

sources.system: AutoStore Multi-Temperature Solution (R5 grid robots), integrated by StrongPoint

sources.claim: AutoStore's Multi-Temperature grid, installed at grocery wholesaler Haugaland Storhusholdning, has robots store and retrieve food goods across frozen, chilled and ambient zones, removing the need for staff ... enter the freezer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage/retrieval of chilled and frozen food stock. It substantiates that robots can place and keep food supplies in refrigerated and frozen storage areas when the goods are presented at a port, i.e. the storage half of this task in a purpose-built setting.

sources.date: 2022-08 (300-store rollout; service continuing, extended with TX Ghost 2025)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf replenishment inside a refrigerated case. Same act as storing food supplies in a refrigerator — picking packaged product from presented crates and placing it on cooler shelves in rotation — with comparable objects and precision.

sources.title: Walmart brings autonomous forklifts to 4 distribution centers
sources.claim: Fox Robotics' FoxBot autonomous forklifts, deployed at Walmart distribution centers, unload pallets from delivery trucks and move them to induction into an automated storage and ... catalogs and stores the goods.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dock-side pallet receiving. It covers the palletized-delivery handling step of this task — taking pallets off a truck and delivering them to a storage system — with the same equipment (pallets, pallet handling) used in institutional kitchen receiving.

sources.title: Dishcraft Robotics raises funding to help caterers, cafeterias reopen – The Robot Report
sources.claim: Dishcraft Robotics' purpose-built robotic dish hub autonomously sorted, cleaned, inspected and racked dishware and cutlery for corporate, hotel and hospital cafeterias, returning clean wares in racks — machine handling and stowing of clean foodservice smallwares.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sorting and racking of clean dishware and cutlery. Racking clean wares into their storage racks is the same act as putting clean utensils away on shelves, with the same objects, in a facility built around the machine.

sources.title: Figure AI's Helix 02 Completes 4-Minute Autonomous Kitchen Task, Setting New Humanoid Robotics Benchmark
sources.claim: Figure's Helix-02 humanoid completed a four-minute end-to-end autonomous kitchen task with no human intervention: walking to a dishwasher, unloading ..., crossing the room and stacking items in cabinets, then ... the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading clean dishes and stowing them in cabinets. Same objects (plates, cups, utensils) and same act as putting clean smallwares away, but shown as a single staged demonstration rather than sustained commercial output.

tasks.label: Stir and strain soups and sauces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant/hotel kitchen: prep worker tends simmering stocks, soups and pan sauces on the range - stirring pots and rondeaus with a ladle or whisk every few minutes to prevent scorching, then lifting the pot and pouring the finished stock or sauce through a china cap/chinois into a bain or Cambro, working shoulder-to-shoulder with cooks on a crowded, hot line.

Institutional kitchen (school district, hospital, college, corrections, senior dining): 40-100 gallon batches of soup, gravy or sauce in steam-jacketed kettles and tilt skillets - stirring with a long paddle during cooking, stirring again in steam-table pans through service, occasionally straining stock or gravy into transfer containers.

Chain restaurant / fast-casual / QSR: reheating and stirring pre-made soup bases and sauces in rethermalizers, saucepans or steam-table pans to a standard recipe card, stirring held soup periodically through service; straining is rare and small-scale (skimming solids or passing a sauce through a fine sieve).

Central commissary, catering production kitchen or supermarket prepared-foods kitchen: batch production of soups, stocks and sauces in agitator/mixer kettles, stirring during cook and cool-down and straining stock into containers or bags for packaging and distribution.

Off-site catering, banquet setup, food truck or pop-up: soups and sauces held on portable burners, induction plates and chafers in rented halls, tents or client sites; worker stirs pots in a layout that differs at every job and strains with a handheld strainer into whatever vessel is available.

sources.system: T-chef Tech / Chinese chain cooking robots (Home Original Chicken, Xiaocaiyuan)
sources.developer: T-chef Tech and other Chinese cooking-robot makers
sources.title: China's restaurant chains turn to robots after backlash against pre-made dishes (KrASIA/36Kr)
sources.claim: Cooking robots with mechanical stirring arms are deployed in the back kitchens of Chinese restaurant chains (about 388 Home Original Chicken locations; ~200 Xiaocaiyuan locations); staff pour pre-portioned ingredients into the robot's wok and the machine cooks and stirs the dish in under two minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Automated wok cooking is the same physical act as this task's stirring: continuous powered agitation of a hot liquid/semi-liquid in a vessel under heat control, done to prevent scorching and uneven mixing; the machines also include 'smart soup cookers'.

sources.title: Commercial Ramen Soup Strainer Machine | RichSoup | Yamato Noodle
sources.claim: Yamato's RichSoup is a commercial stock-straining machine sold to ramen shops that replaces hand-straining through a 60 cm chinois: once the cooked stock is loaded, the machine strains it by centrifuge automatically (60 L of thick tonkotsu in about 5 minutes).

sources.system: Cleveland Cook-Chill Horizontal Agitator Mixer Kettles (HAMKDL / TMKDL / HAMKGL-HMI)
sources.title: Cook Chill Systems & Tumble Chillers | Cleveland Range
sources.claim: Cleveland Range sells cook-chill mixer kettles (40-150 gal) with electrically or hydraulically driven horizontal agitators, variable mixer speed, scraper blades, temperature probes and draw-off valves, used in institutional and commissary kitchens to cook and continuously stir soups, sauces, stews and dressings.
sources.transferJustification: The agitator kettle performs this task's stirring directly - powered, programmed agitation of soups and sauces during cooking and cooling - with the batch loaded into the machine's own fixtured vessel.

sources.title: Firex solutions for centralized kitchens
sources.claim: Firex's Cucimix is a fully automated braising pan/kettle with programmable multi-arm mixers (reversible, adjustable speed) used in high-volume and centralized kitchens to cook and stir sauces, soups and stews to a programmed recipe.

sources.claim: Four cooking robots have been in use at Soonggok Middle School in Seoul since 2023 handling frying, stir-frying and the preparation of soups and stews in the school cafeteria kitchen; the school-kitchen workers' union disputes that the machines can perform a cooking task properly without human ....

sources.title: What are robot chefs cooking up for Korea's struggling school kitchens? - The Korea Herald
sources.claim: A commercial automatic stirrer shown at Korea's 2025 Food Service Fair executes user-programmed recipes, uses camera-based imaging to monitor surface temperature and cooking status, adjusts heat automatically, and stops via lidar when a person approaches - unattended machine stirring of large-batch dishes for foodservice kitchens.

sources.title: Miso Robotics Unveils AI-Powered Flippy 2 Robot, Gets Put to Work at White Castle as a Fry Cook
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy Fry Station autonomously runs an entire fry station - filling baskets, lowering them into hot oil, lifting and draining them and emptying them - and has surpassed 5 million baskets across White Castle, Jack in the ... restaurants.

tasks.label: Make special dressings and sauces as condiments for sandwiches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Deli/sandwich-shop back of house, morning prep: worker makes a batch of a house spread (chipotle mayo, herb aioli, remoulade) — scoops mayonnaise from a food-service jar or bucket, measures spices, relish, acid and hot sauce, whisks in a Cambro or mixing bowl, transfers to squeeze bottles, labels/dates and refrigerates.

Full-service or upscale restaurant kitchen: prep cook builds a scratch emulsified dressing/sauce (vinaigrette, garlic aioli, comeback sauce) with an immersion blender or food processor from raw components (garlic, mustard, eggs, oil, citrus), tasting and adjusting seasoning before it goes on the sandwich station.

Institutional kitchen (school, hospital, corporate cafeteria, prison, university dining): large standardized-recipe batch of sandwich dressing made from bulk #10 cans/pails in a floor mixer or large container, scaled to a production sheet, panned and held under HACCP temperature/labeling rules.

Chain commissary or supermarket-deli central kitchen: bulk production run of the chain's proprietary sandwich sauces from bulk raw ingredients, blended/emulsified, then filled into tubs or bottles and distributed to outlets.

During service at the sandwich line: small made-to-order or top-off batch of a special sauce mixed in a cramped station amid other work — combining a few measured components in a bottle or small bowl and shaking/whisking to order.

sources.system: INOXPA batch mayonnaise/sauce production plant (500 L vacuum mixer + dosing hoppers + Siemens PLC/SCADA recipe control)
sources.title: Plant for batch production of mayonnaise sauce - INOXPA Case Studies
sources.claim: INOXPA supplied a fast-food chain a batch sauce/mayonnaise plant that makes the chain's different sauces for its outlets: 80 L hoppers dose solids (spices, egg powder, garlic paste), a 400 L hopper doses liquids, and a 500 L vacuum mixing tank with in-line high-shear mixer emulsifies, all run from recipes stored in an industrial PC/SCADA with PLC control.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, done in a purpose-built setting: producing the chain's special sauces/condiments to recipe, including emulsified mayonnaise-type dressings, with texture, viscosity and taste specified by the customer.

sources.system: Readco Kurimoto Continuous Processor (CP) for sauce production
sources.title: Increasing Sauce Production with Industrial Food Mixers | Readco Kurimoto, LLC
sources.claim: Continuous processors used in commercial sauce production automatically meter raw ingredients into a mixing chamber with calibrated loss-in-weight feeders and pumps and mix them, replacing large batch tanks; sold as production equipment for sauce manufacturers.
sources.transferJustification: Same operation as the task's core step — proportioning ingredients to a recipe and mixing/emulsifying them into a sauce — carried out by machine in a purpose-built processing line.

sources.system: Blendid autonomous robotic food kiosk (incl. Jamba by Blendid)
sources.title: Walmart brings smoothie-making robot Blendid to California store | Grocery Dive
sources.claim: Blendid's autonomous kiosk combines a robotic arm, blenders, refrigeration and ingredient dispensers to portion liquids, produce and powders and blend made-to-order drinks with no staff; kiosks operate in Walmart stores and other public venues.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making a blended, on-demand food product. It dispenses measured liquid, semi-solid and powdered ingredients into a vessel and blends them — the same combine-and-emulsify operation, comparable ingredient viscosities and dosing precision, in a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.title: Botrista raises $10M for its drink-mixing robot | Restaurant Business
sources.claim: Botrista's DrinkBot, a soda-fountain-sized unit installed on restaurant counters in 37 states, automatically portions, dispenses and mixes multi-ingredient recipes from interchangeable bag-in-box ingredient packs at the push of a ... in about 20 seconds.

sources.system: Chef Robotics 'Arms of Chef' food-assembly robots
sources.title: Chef Robotics completes 100M meal servings milestone - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-driven robot arms work on food-production lines at manufacturers such as Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket and Chef Bombay, autonomously portioning hundreds of ingredient types including sauces and curries into trays; the company reported 100 million servings produced at customer facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling and portioning of viscous, sticky sauces and curries at production quality on a conveyor line, evidencing that machines meet worker-quality standards for the sauce-handling and filling steps in a purpose-built food line.

sources.title: Sweetgreen accelerates deployment of automated kitchens | Restaurant Dive
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen automated makeline, deployed in dozens of restaurants, dispenses ingredients (including dressings) into bowls at 500 bowls per hour, but the company states it does not perform prep work; employees still do prep and finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated portioning of dressings onto food inside a working restaurant. Cited to show that in-restaurant automation is confined to a purpose-built dispensing machine and explicitly excludes back-of-house prep such as making the sauces.

tasks.label: Scrape leftovers from dishes into garbage containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant dish area during service: bus tubs and stacks of soiled plates, bowls and platters arrive continuously; worker knocks/scrapes leftover food, sauces, bones, napkins and straw wrappers off each piece into a garbage or compost can (or scrap trough) and racks the ware, at hundreds of pieces per hour under time pressure and splashing water.

Institutional dining (school, hospital, college, corporate cafeteria) tray-return line: trays with plates, bowls, cups and disposables come off a return window or conveyor; worker empties leftovers into a waste bin, pulper or disposal, sorts silverware, and racks ware at steady high volume.

Prep-station cleanup during a prep shift in a commercial kitchen: scraping mixing bowls, food processor bowls, cutting boards of trim and peels, and sheet pans of baked-on residue into a garbage can with hands or a rubber spatula, in a crowded aisle alongside other workers.

End-of-service disposal in a restaurant or cafeteria kitchen: dumping leftover product out of steam-table/hotel pans, buffet inserts, deli containers and dated storage tubs into garbage or compost containers, then stacking the empties for washing; heavy, awkward, sometimes liquid-heavy loads.

Off-premise catering or personal-chef work at a client's home or rented venue: a temporary dish station where returned plates and platters are scraped into trash bags or a household bin before packing out; modest volume, layout different at every site.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong's dual/triple-arm system runs autonomously in real restaurant dish rooms 24/7, picking greasy, food-soiled plates, cups and silverware out of messy bus tubs and racking them for the dish machine; reporting describes picking, gripping, racking and washing, but does not document the robot emptying leftovers into a garbage container.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic dish handling in a commercial dish room. It shows robots can work at commercial pace on food-soiled ware in a working kitchen, but the scraping-leftovers-into-waste step is not described as within the robot's scope, so it cannot by itself substantiate completion of this task.

sources.system: Connected Robotics Dish Washing System (food-service dishwashing robot)
sources.title: Dish Washing System (食洗機・ラッキングロボ) | PRODUCTS | Connected Robotics Inc.
sources.claim: Connected Robotics' deployed dishwashing robot automates only the pre-wash and racking; the company's own description of the job states that the leftover food on the plates is thrown into the garbage bin by workers before washing begins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial-kitchen dish handling. Cited as a scope limit — a deployed dish-room robot in a structured kitchen still leaves the scraping of leftovers into the garbage to human staff.

sources.title: Sunday Robotics | The helpful robotics company
sources.claim: Sunday Robotics' Memo autonomously clears a dining table in homes, throwing food scraps into the trash bin and loading the dishwasher; company videos are labelled autonomous and played at 5x speed, and the robot is stated to work in homes it has not seen before.

sources.title: Sunday Unveils "Memo": A Wheeled, Domestic Robot That Learns From $200 Gloves | Humanoids Daily
sources.claim: Independent coverage of Memo's reveal describes demonstrated autonomous 'Table-to-Dishwasher' cycles that include scraping food waste off dishes, with a consumer beta program planned for 2026.

sources.title: New robotic dishwasher for restaurants is taking the dirty work out of the kitchen (CNBC)
sources.claim: Dishcraft Robotics' purpose-built machine, deployed in Bay Area corporate cafeterias, automatically lifted each soiled plate or bowl and mechanically removed the food residue with a rubber scraping wheel, using vision to verify the ware was clean; the company has since ceased operating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated removal of leftover food residue from dishware at cafeteria volume. The physical act — separating leftovers from each plate and sending them to the waste stream — is the substance of this task, performed on ware presented to the machine in fixtures.

sources.title: Robotic dish-scrubber for commercial kitchens could cut dishwashing staffs in half (Axios)
sources.claim: Dishcraft's system required the ware to be presented to the machine in dedicated carts with slots, i.e. the work was brought to the machine in a fixtured, purpose-built presentation.
sources.transferJustification: Same system as the preceding item; cited to establish that the presentation of the work was purpose-built (fixtured carts), which fixes the environment tier of the demonstration at E1.

sources.system: JEROS Industrial Tray Cleaner / automatic tray cleaning system
sources.title: Industrial Tray Cleaner | Automatic tray cleaning system from JEROS
sources.claim: JEROS' commercial automatic tray-cleaning line uses a pre-scraper and brushes to strip baked-on food deposits off trays and deliver them into a waste collection container as trays are fed through the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanically scraping food residue off trays/pans into a waste container. Objects (sheet pans/trays), residue type (baked-on food) and endpoint (waste container) match the pan-and-tray portion of this task; the work is fed to the machine, which is the E1 presentation.

sources.system: MEIKO + Fizyr + Yaskawa automated dishwashing cell
sources.title: Automatica: Autonomous Dish Sorting Robot for Commercial Kitchens - Rocking Robots
sources.claim: A Meiko/Fizyr/Yaskawa system demonstrated at Automatica 2025 used vision AI on a Motoman arm to detect, pick and load used plates, bowls ... off a conveyor belt into an ... in a purpose-built dish-handling cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of used, food-soiled dishware presented on a conveyor. It substantiates that the dish-presentation and per-item handling half of the task is solved in a purpose-built cell, complementing the Dishcraft/JEROS evidence for the residue-removal half.

tasks.label: Distribute food to waiters and waitresses to serve to customers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant, dinner rush: prep worker at the pantry/expo end of the line takes completed hot plates from cooks plus their own cold plates and desserts, checks each against the ticket, adds sides/garnish/sauce ramekins, wipes rims, sets plates under the heat lamps on the pass in course order and calls the server. Crowded line, mixed plateware, hot slippery plates, seconds matter.

Institutional foodservice (hospital, nursing home, school, corporate dining): worker stands at a serve counter or patient tray conveyor, portions standardized items from hotel pans onto plates/trays, matches each tray to the diet card or ticket, and passes it to the server/aide who delivers it. Fixed layout, standard tableware, repetitive high volume.

Banquet/catering plating line: hundreds of identical plates assembled in a batch under a captain's timing, covered, and loaded onto trays, racks or hot boxes that banquet servers pick up for the ballroom. Standardized portions and plateware, extreme throughput in a short window.

Diner, coffee shop or casual counter service: worker brews coffee/tea, pours beverages, plates simple cold items (soup, salad, pie) and hands them across the pass counter or window to waitstaff on demand throughout the shift, keeping up with call-outs and tickets.

Hotel room service / private club: worker assembles a complete order on a tray or rolling cart — covered plates, cutlery roll, condiments, bread basket, coffee pot or glassware, check — verifies it against the order and hands it to the server for delivery.

sources.title: Sweetgreen accelerates deployment of automated kitchens | Restaurant Dive
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen is a purpose-built automated makeline, deployed in dozens of US restaurants, that dispenses ingredients into bowls to order at 500 bowls/hour and moves them to a finishing station where an employee completes the order; the machine does not do prep or finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a to-order meal and presenting it at a hand-off point for a staff member to serve. Same objects (bowls/portioned food), same ticket-driven sequencing, and the output is food staged for a human to carry to the customer, which is what distributing food to servers requires.

sources.title: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly | AgFunderNews
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI food-assembly robots are commercially deployed on prepared-meal production lines (Amy's Kitchen, Cafe Spice, Chef Bombay, Sunbasket), autonomously picking and portioning multiple ingredients into varied trays and compartments on moving conveyors, with tens of millions of meals assembled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-volume portioning of prepared food into plates/trays presented on a conveyor. Comparable objects (scoopable prepared foods, compartmented trays), comparable precision (portion weights within 1% of target), and it is the plating-and-staging step of a tray line brought to a machine.

sources.title: Amy's Kitchen Boosts Yields and Production with Chef Robotics | Automation World
sources.claim: Amy's Kitchen has run Chef Robotics systems on up to two shifts ... at 34 bowls per minute, with better portion accuracy and better food placement aesthetics than human line workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repetitive batch plating at banquet-scale throughput. Establishes worker-quality output (accuracy and appearance at or above human line workers) for portioning food into serving containers presented to the machine.

sources.title: WellSpan Health Launches 24/7, AI-Powered Robotic Kitchen with RoboEatz and ABB Robotics
sources.claim: WellSpan York Hospital operates 'Fresh Take Eatery', a 400 sq ft RoboEatz Autonomous Robotic Kitchen with ABB robotic arms that, on receiving an order, retrieves ingredients from autonomous storage, cooks in four modules and handles the final ..., serving made-to-order meals 24/7 to patients, visitors and staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing an ordered dish and plating it for hand-off at a service point. The plating and presentation of a made-to-order meal into a serving vessel, ticket-driven, in an institutional foodservice operation, is the same act as staging a plate at the pass for a server.

sources.title: Haidilao opens smart restaurant in Beijing | China Daily
sources.claim: Haidilao's Panasonic-built smart restaurant kitchen in Beijing uses rows of robotic arms that automatically retrieve ordered pre-plated dishes from cold storage and stage them for delivery to diners' tables by serving robots.
sources.transferJustification: Directly analogous: robotic arms select the dishes for a given order and hand them off to whoever carries them to the table. Same objects (plated dishes on trays) and same purpose (dispatching finished food for service), in a purpose-built automated kitchen.

sources.title: Cafe X - Robotic Coffee Bars — Republic
sources.claim: Cafe X operates enclosed robotic coffee bars that prepare espresso drinks and present them at pickup windows, running unattended and fully autonomously at high volume in locations such as San Francisco International Airport.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: brewing coffee/tea drinks and handing the finished beverage to a person at a fixed pickup window — the beverage half of distributing prepared items to servers, at commercial volume and reliability.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing | The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics has autonomous three-arm systems installed in operating full-service restaurant dish rooms, running 24 hours a day handling dirty plates, glasses and silverware without an on-site babysitter; installations were done without closing the restaurant and arms move out of the way for staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: perceiving and manipulating restaurant dishware at speed inside an ordinary commercial kitchen. It shows E2-level dish handling exists, but only for soiled dishes at a dedicated dish station — not for staging food-laden plates against tickets — so it bounds rather than establishes E2 for this task.

sources.date: 2023-08 (product guide; robots in commercial restaurant use)
sources.title: Food Delivery Robots: The Comprehensive Guide | Richtech Robotics
sources.claim: In current restaurant deployments of Richtech's Matradee L food-running robots, the robot waits at the expediting area and a human chef or expeditor loads the prepared food onto its trays and selects the destination table; the robot only performs the transport.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, opposite side of the hand-off: it documents that in real restaurant kitchens (E2) the act of taking plated food and passing it on is still performed by a human expeditor, with robots only carrying what a person loads.

sources.title: Chef Robotics Physical AI Models Can Help Automate Produce Packing | Chef Robotics
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' systems also place discrete items — whole fruits into clamshells and snack boxes — and portion scoopable ingredients into trays for applications including airline meal kits, hospital and care-facility meals and school lunch boxes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a complete meal tray from multiple discrete and scoopable components on a line — the closest demonstrated analogue to building a room-service or patient tray, with comparable rigid items and placement precision.

tasks.label: Operate cash register, handle money, and give correct change.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Deli / sandwich / pizza counter in a supermarket or small restaurant: after preparing the order, the worker rings items into a touchscreen POS, states the total, takes cash (bills and coins), makes correct change from the drawer, hands over receipt and food; card taps handled on the same terminal; steady walk-up traffic.

School, hospital, corporate or campus cafeteria serving line: worker at the register end of the line identifies unpackaged plated foods and grab-and-go items with no barcodes, keys or scans them, applies meal-plan/ID-card deductions, takes cash and returns correct change during a 30-minute rush.

Coffee, juice or snack bar counter: many small-ticket transactions, mostly card/mobile taps with some cash, tip prompts, occasional refund or void; worker alternates between brewing/assembling drinks and running the register.

Opening and closing register duties: count and set up the starting float, keep the drawer secure during the shift, count down the drawer at shift end, reconcile cash to the POS sales report, fill out a cash-out sheet and prepare the deposit/drop for the manager or safe.

Off-site catering, food truck or event concession: portable POS or cash box at a fair, festival, ballpark stand or client site; variable layout, outdoor conditions, crowding, high cash share and fast small transactions with change made from an apron or box.

sources.title: McDonald's, With Kiosks That Take Cash, Continues to Move Away From Cashiers | NACS
sources.claim: McDonald's has rolled out a US restaurant format with self-order stations that accept cash and dispense ... autonomously, letting customers bypass the staffed register entirely.

sources.system: Glory CASHINFINITY CI-10X point-of-sale cash recycler
sources.title: GLORY Announces Next Generation Retail Cash Recycling Solutions (Business Wire)
sources.claim: Glory's CASHINFINITY CI-10X point-of-sale cash recycler is an electromechanical machine that accepts, authenticates and dispenses notes and coins under POS control, automating the cash-tender and change-giving steps of a counter transaction.

sources.system: Glory CASHINFINITY CI-500X back-office cash recycler
sources.title: GLORY Announces Next Generation Retail Cash Recycling Solutions (Business Wire)
sources.claim: Glory's back-office recycler automates the start- and end-of-day cash duties — float preparation and store reconciliation — that constitute a worker's drawer set-up and count-down.

sources.system: Glory CASHINFINITY CI-300 cash recycler at Eataly
sources.title: Eataly case study | Improved staff experience with Glory's CASHINFINITY CI-300 Cash Recycler
sources.claim: In a deployed food-hall/retail setting (Eataly), Glory cash recyclers count and issue cash to prepare tills for up to 50 cashiers per location, replacing hand-counting of drawers at shift end.

sources.system: NCR FastLane SelfServ Checkout (note and coin recycling)
sources.title: Self-checkout system with flexible, convertible design - iXtenso
sources.claim: Mass-deployed grocery self-checkout terminals accept stacks of bills and handfuls of coins and recycle them back out as change, completing tendered cash transactions without a cashier.

sources.title: Mashgin expands AI-powered checkout to 50 campuses | Kiosk Marketplace
sources.claim: Mashgin's computer-vision checkout kiosks ring up unpackaged prepared foods and un-barcoded items automatically and are deployed in university dining halls and grab-and-go markets, plus stadiums and c-stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item entry at the register. Mashgin performs the ring-up step for exactly the objects a cafeteria food-prep worker keys in (plated food, un-barcoded grab-and-go) in the same facility type; cash tender/change is supplied by cited recycler hardware.

sources.title: S'pore's first robot barista ELLA to be deployed at 30 MRT stations | Vulcan Post
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic barista kiosk takes customer orders, processes payment and serves drinks unattended in transit-station retail spaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: counter-service order taking and payment collection. ELLA autonomously registers the order and collects payment (cashless) at a beverage counter, the same transaction the worker runs; cash tender/change is covered by the cash-recycler evidence.

sources.system: Glory CASHINFINITY retail cash recycling range
sources.title: GLORY Confirmed as Global Leader in Retail Cash Recycling Solutions by RBR Data Services
sources.claim: Retail cash recycling hardware that automates POS and back-office cash handling is deployed at commercial scale across segments including quick-service restaurants, with Glory holding leading deployment share.

tasks.label: Distribute menus to hospital patients, collect diet sheets, and deliver food trays and snacks to nursing units or directly to patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Meal-time bulk transport: after the tray line finishes, the aide takes loaded enclosed meal carts (200-300 lb) from the kitchen, moves them through service corridors and staff elevators to several nursing units on different floors, parks them at the unit's designated galley/elevator-lobby spot on schedule, and returns empty carts to dish room.

Bedside tray passing on a med-surg unit: aide pulls each tray from the cart in the corridor, matches the tray card to the patient's name/room/bed and diet order, enters the room, clears and positions the overbed table, sets the tray within reach of a patient who may be bedbound, opens cartons/removes lids, and greets the patient.

Menu rounds: aide walks the unit with printed selective menus, hands a menu to each patient, sometimes reads options aloud or marks selections for patients who cannot write, later returns to each room to collect the completed diet sheets from bedside tables, and carries them back to the diet office/kitchen.

Between-meal nourishments and snack restock: aide assembles a tote/cart of supplements, sandwiches, juices and applesauce and takes it to nursing units, handing it off at the unit galley or nurses' station for unit staff, including ad hoc runs when a floor is short.

Late trays, missed trays and special requests delivered directly to a single patient room, including restricted areas (ICU, isolation rooms requiring gown/glove precautions, behavioral health) where the aide must gown up, verify the patient, and hand or place the tray.

sources.title: Franciscan Health Installs 6 Aethon Robots for Food Service and Environmental Logistics
sources.claim: Aethon TUG T3 autonomous mobile robots at Franciscan Health Crown Point tow carts of meal trays and linens from the kitchen to hospital floors, opening doors and riding staff elevators, automatically dropping the cart at the destination and notifying floor staff; staff load the carts manually.

sources.developer: Aethon / Scripps Memorial Hospital La Jolla
sources.title: Robotic Carts Help Scripps Hospital Deliver Meals - Scripps Health
sources.claim: Ten TUG robotic carts at Scripps Memorial Hospital La Jolla carry patient meal trays from the kitchen to floors, travelling hallways and using elevators on their own; food-service staff meet the robot in the elevator lobby and are the ones who deliver food to patients. TUGs are also used for ad hoc snack (applesauce) runs to floors.

sources.title: BayCare Expands Autonomous Hospital Delivery with New Relay Robots at Winter Haven Hospitals
sources.claim: Relay hospital delivery robots deployed at BayCare's Winter Haven hospitals move specimens, pharmacy orders and clinical supplies point-to-point between departments and units, navigating elevators and badge-access doors without human intervention at high reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital delivery of small items (specimens, meds, supplies). Same corridors, elevators and unit drop points as delivering a nourishment tote to a nursing station; comparable payload and no fine manipulation required.

sources.title: How TIAGo Delivery and Conveyor help hospitals fighting COVID-19
sources.claim: PAL Robotics' TIAGo Conveyor was tested in two Barcelona hospitals carrying a food tray to a patient's room and transferring it by actuated conveyor onto a table in the room; the use case was limited to isolated patients who are themselves autonomous (ambulatory).

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator is deployed in more than 25 ... and has completed over one million autonomous deliveries of supplies, medications and specimens to nursing units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transport of clinical items to nursing units. Same hospital corridors/elevators and unit hand-off points used for snack and tray-cart delivery; establishes reliable institution-wide unit-level delivery, not bedside service.

tasks.label: Package take-out foods or serve food to customers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quick-service/fast-casual restaurant: assemble a take-out or delivery order — portion entrees into clamshells or bowls, add sides, sauce cups, napkins and utensils, lid/seal, label, bag it and stage it on the pickup shelf during a rush.

Cafeteria or steam-table serving line (school, hospital, corporate or senior-living dining): portion hot entrees, starches, vegetables and cold sides onto customers' plates or compartment trays as the queue moves, honoring 'light on that / extra sauce' requests and handing the plate across the sneeze guard.

Supermarket deli / prepared-foods counter: take a customer's order, slice meats and cheeses to a requested thickness and weight or scoop salads and hot-bar items, wrap or box, weigh, print and apply the label, and hand it over the counter.

Grab-and-go cold packaging in a store prep room or commissary: fill clamshells and cups with made sandwiches, salads, cut fruit and cold sides, seal or lid them, weigh, date-label, and stock the refrigerated case.
Counter beverage service in a cafe, deli or convenience store: brew coffee/tea, pour or build the drink to order, cap it and hand it to the ... at the counter.
Off-site catering or banquet buffet at a venue taken as found (tent, client site, hall): set up chafing dishes, portion onto guests' plates along the buffet, and replenish pans through the event.

sources.title: Breaking: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI robots autonomously portion high-mix ingredients into conveyed meal trays on production lines at food manufacturers, with tens of millions of meals produced in commercial operation.
sources.transferJustification: Portioning prepared foods into take-out-style containers is the same manipulation as packaging take-out foods; here it occurs on a purpose-built conveyed line rather than a restaurant counter.

sources.system: Chef Robotics + Packline integrated meal line
sources.title: Chef Robotics and Packline Partner on End-to-End Meal Production Automation
sources.claim: Chef Robotics and Packline integrate robotic assembly with tray de-nesting, conveyance and sealing equipment, giving an end-to-end fill-and-seal packaged-meal line already run together by Cafe Spice.
sources.transferJustification: Supplies the sealing/closure step that 'packaging take-out foods' requires beyond portioning, on the same automated line.

sources.title: Chef Robotics | Robotics for Food Manufacturers | Cafe Spice Case Study
sources.claim: At Cafe Spice, Chef robots plus a conveyor system fill up to 30 meal trays per minute, replacing most of the 8-10 workers previously needed per manual meal-assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates worker-replacement quality and throughput for filling portioned food containers, the core of packaging take-out foods when brought to a purpose-built line.

sources.system: Hyphen automated digital makeline at Chipotle
sources.title: CHIPOTLE TEAMS UP WITH HYPHEN TO BEGIN TESTING NEW DIGITAL MAKELINE
sources.claim: In an actual restaurant the automated digital makeline assembles the bowl but a human still lids it, adds sides and places it in the pickup area — the packaging steps are not machine-completed in the human kitchen.

sources.title: Chipotle and Cava Invest $25 Million in Hyphen to Advance Restaurant Automation
sources.claim: Hyphen's enclosed under-counter makeline assembled digital/take-out bowl orders at up to 350 meals per ... in Chipotle's test kitchen.

sources.title: Sweetgreen's Automated 'Infinite Kitchen' Readies for a Step Up in 2025
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen robotic makeline is deployed in roughly 25 restaurants, but every bowl it produces still has to be completed by ... human at a finishing station.

sources.title: PizzaForno kiosk chain plans 40 new locations in Michigan
sources.claim: PizzaForno automated pizzeria kiosks bake and dispense a boxed hot pizza to the customer unattended, 24/7, at gas stations and other sites across North America.
sources.transferJustification: Closes the loop of packaging a take-out item in its box and handing it to a paying customer without staff, inside a purpose-built machine enclosure.

sources.system: Weber deli slicing line (weLOAD infeeder, wePICK pick-and-place robot)
sources.title: Efficient & hygienic solutions for deli production | Weber
sources.claim: Weber's deli line solutions slice whole-muscle deli products to controlled weight and use pick-and-place robots and automatic infeeders to load and pack the sliced portions.
sources.transferJustification: The deli-counter task (slice to a requested weight, then wrap/pack and label) brought to a purpose-built line: same product, precision and weight control, machine-fixtured.

sources.title: RoboBatcher Flex for Meat | Marel
sources.claim: Marel's RoboBatcher Flex uses robotic arms to batch fixed-weight portions and place them into retail trays in a styled arrangement in food plants.
sources.transferJustification: Fixed-weight portioning into consumer trays is the packaging/weighing step of deli and grab-and-go work, performed with the work presented to the machine.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics' ADAM serves drinks at Kennedy Space Center
sources.claim: Richtech's ADAM robot makes and serves specialty drinks to walk-up customers at a commercial cafe, having served over 16,000 drinks since February 2025, and has been placed at other public venues.

sources.title: CES 2025: Artly the Robot Barista Uses AI and Motion Capture Technology
sources.claim: Artly's robot-barista stations run nine coffee retail locations and have produced over 350,000 cups of espresso drinks served to customers.

sources.title: Dexai Robotics signs $1.6 million contract with DLA
sources.claim: Dexai's Alfred cobot, using vision and interchangeable utensils, prepped salads on the line at a military base dining facility under a 10-robot federal contract.
sources.transferJustification: Scooping portions into a customer's bowl on a dining-facility line is the manipulation used on a cafeteria serving line; cited to test whether E2 service-line work is substantiated.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi autonomously runs plated food across dining rooms in restaurants, hotels and senior living, but staff load it and diners or servers unload it.
sources.transferJustification: Covers only the transport half of 'serve food to customers' in an E2 dining room; cited to show what is and is not machine-completed there.

tasks.label: Cut, slice or grind meat, poultry, and seafood to prepare for cooking.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restaurant kitchen prep (full-service or fast-casual): a prep worker breaks down and portions raw proteins by hand on a cutting board - trimming a beef top round into steaks, cubing pork for stew, slicing flank steak thin, cutting whole chickens into eight pieces, butterflying breasts - in small mixed batches, several different products per shift, in a shared kitchen with cooks working nearby.

High-volume institutional kitchen or commissary (school district, hospital, university, catering, central prep kitchen): bulk single-product batches - cases of boneless chicken breast cut into uniform 4-6 oz portions or strips, pork loins sliced into chops, cooked roasts cubed - to a spec sheet, on stainless tables with buffalo choppers/dicers available.

Supermarket deli / prepared-foods counter: loading whole-muscle cooked or cured meats (turkey breast, ham, roast beef) onto a gravity or automatic deli slicer, slicing to a set thickness and target weight for sandwiches, party trays and self-service packs, then collecting and weighing the slices.

Seafood prep at a restaurant, sushi bar, or seafood counter: filleting and skinning whole fish, pin-boning and portioning salmon or tuna loins into steaks/blocks, peeling and deveining shrimp, splitting lobster, prepping shellfish - highly variable individual fish sizes, delicate flesh, high yield expectations.

Grinding: feeding beef chuck/trim, pork, or poultry through a bench or floor grinder to make ground meat for burgers, meatballs or sausage - cubing the meat first, running it through the plate once or twice, keeping the product cold, in a butcher's back room, restaurant prep area, or deli.

sources.title: Fuel your portioning with jet power - DSI Waterjet Portioner - JBT
sources.claim: JBT/Marel DSI inline waterjet portioning systems automatically scan and cut poultry, red meat and seafood into fixed-weight portions, fillets, strips, chunks and fat-trimmed products on a production line, replacing hand cutting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial portion cutting of the same objects (raw chicken breast, pork/beef muscle, fish fillets) into the same outputs a prep worker produces (fixed-weight portions, strips, cubes, trimmed pieces), at equal or better weight precision; the difference is only that work arrives fixtured on a conveyor, which is exactly the E1 presentation.

sources.title: Marel I-Cut 122 dual-lane high-speed portion cutter for poultry | The National Provisioner
sources.claim: Marel's I-Cut 122 portion cutter, integrated with the RoboBatcher as a 'robot with a knife', cuts boneless fresh poultry to fixed weight or uniform ... using real-time vision and weight data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: plant-line portioning of boneless chicken. Same material and same required output as kitchen portioning (uniform cutlets/strips to weight); vision-driven cut placement handles the natural size variation a prep cook handles by eye.

sources.system: TORIDAS MARK II MT-04 (DAS series deboning robots)
sources.title: Automatic deboning robotics - Mayekawa (Thailand) Co., Ltd.
sources.claim: Mayekawa's TORIDAS deboning robots take bone-in chicken whole legs and automatically measure each leg and separate bone from meat at yields claimed comparable to skilled manual deboning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic deboning of bone-in poultry, the hardest knife work in the prep instance (breaking down a whole leg/bird); it demonstrates machine-controlled cutting around bone on individually varying carcass parts at human yield.

sources.system: Scott Automation automated lamb boning room / X-ray primal system
sources.title: Safety and yield benefits from automation project at ANZCO's lamb boning room | Scott
sources.claim: Scott Automation has commercialised and installed automated robotic lamb boning rooms, using X-ray and 3D vision to guide robotic primal cutting and deboning of red-meat carcasses in operating plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic red-meat primal cutting and boning. Same objects (raw lamb/beef primals) and comparable knife/saw precision to a prep worker breaking down and trimming a primal, performed autonomously in production.

sources.title: BAADER 582 - BAADER Fish
sources.claim: BAADER filleting machines automatically fillet whitefish and salmonids with computer-controlled cutting tools, producing fillets of quality needing little added trimming.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine filleting of whole fish, the same operation a seafood prep worker performs by knife, on individually varying fish, with yield and quality the buyer accepts.

sources.system: Laitram Model A Automatic Shrimp Peeler
sources.title: ASME-Landmark: The Lapeyre Automatic Shrimp Peeling Machine - ETHW
sources.claim: Laitram's Model A automatic shrimp peeler has been in commercial use since 1949 and peels roughly 1,000 pounds of shrimp per hour across a wide size range without manual handling of each shrimp.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanised shellfish peeling/deveining, the same shrimp-prep output a food prep worker delivers, done continuously and autonomously once product is fed to the machine.

sources.system: Weber weSLICE slicers with weLOAD feeding systems
sources.title: Slicer - Discover the portfolio of the world market leader | Weber
sources.claim: Weber supplies high-speed slicing lines for deli meats that combine automatic loading/feeding, slicing and portioning of whole-muscle deli products into weight-controlled packs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial deli slicing. Identical objects (whole-muscle cooked/cured turkey, ham, roast beef) and identical output (uniform slices to a target weight); machine feeding replaces the worker's hand loading of the slicer carriage.

sources.system: Collaborative meat-processing robot arm (robot arm with knife and camera)
sources.developer: Scientific Reports study on meat-processing automation
sources.title: Safely and autonomously cutting meat with a collaborative robot arm | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: A collaborative robot arm with vision autonomously performed pork-loin butchery tasks - slicing a loin into chops, ... - after a human placed the meat in front of it.

instances.label: Mid- and end-of-shift glassware washing at a full-service bar/restaurant: collecting used pint glasses, rocks glasses and stems from the bar top and service well, dumping ice, straws, fruit and napkins, racking them, running the under-counter glasswasher (or a three-compartment sink), then unloading and stacking the clean glasses.

Washing bar tools during service at the well: shaking tins, mixing glasses, Hawthorne/fine strainers, jiggers, bar spoons, muddlers, blender jars and juice containers get rinsed or washed and must be back in use within seconds; residues include sticky syrups, dairy, egg white and citrus pulp, in a crowded 24-inch-wide well.

Pre-service glassware finishing: taking still-damp glassware from the racks, polishing stemware and cocktail coupes with a linen cloth (often steam), inspecting each for spots, lipstick, film or chips, discarding damaged ones, and restocking glass shelves, rail racks and hanging stem racks.

Closing deep clean of the bar's fixed equipment and surfaces: pulling and soaking soda gun nozzles and holsters, emptying and scrubbing the ice bin and dump sinks, cleaning drains, speed rails, rubber floor mats, bar top, rail, and wiping down back-bar bottles and shelves.

Cleaning and flushing the drink-making machinery: blender jars and blades, frozen-drink/slush machine, espresso machine group heads, portafilters and milk system, juice and soda dispenser nozzles — mostly rinse/flush cycles plus brush work on nozzles and gaskets.

Periodic system cleaning on a schedule: flushing draft beer lines and faucets with cleaning solution, sanitizing the ice machine bin and evaporator, and delimiting/descaling the glasswasher and cleaning its filters and spray arms.

tasks.label: Collect money for drinks served.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Card/contactless payment for a round at an indoor restaurant, hotel or casual bar: patron hands over or taps a card, bartender rings the drinks on the POS, runs the card, returns it, and presents a printed slip with a tip line; indoor, institution-controlled premises, moderate pace.

Cash payment at a neighborhood bar/pub: patron pays with bills for drinks served, bartender rings the sale, opens the drawer, counts out correct change, returns change and receipt, and handles cash left on the bar as a tip; must avoid shorting the till and detect bad bills.

Running and closing a tab: patron's card is taken and held (pre-authorized) behind the bar, drinks are added over an hour or more, then at close-out the bartender retrieves the right card, prints the slip, captures the tip, settles the charge and returns the card.

High-volume rush at a nightclub, stadium concourse bar or event bar: crowded, loud, patrons pressing three deep, rapid-fire card taps and cash for multiple rounds, ID/age checks, keeping each payment matched to the right order while the queue moves.

Off-premise / mobile bar: catered outdoor event, wedding cash bar, festival or street fair; portable bar setup that varies site to site, cash box or handheld reader, drink tickets/vouchers, weather and patchy connectivity.

tasks.label: Balance cash receipts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Independent neighborhood bar or restaurant bar: at end of shift the bartender pulls the drawer, counts bills and coins, runs the POS Z/shift report, records over/short, subtracts the starting bank, prepares a deposit envelope and drops it in the back-office safe.

High-volume nightclub or sports bar: several drawers and bartenders, mid-shift cash drops into a drop safe, large bill volume, counterfeit checking, closing count of each drawer against POS sales plus tip-out and bank rebuild, done in the back office after close.

Casino or hotel bar: bartender draws an imprest bank from the cage at shift start, drops receipts, and returns/settles the bank at the cashier cage or count room under strict audited procedures with signatures and variance reporting.

Mostly-cashless craft cocktail bar or brewery taproom: only a few hundred dollars in cash, quick drawer count, plus settling the card batch, matching signed slips, and reconciling tips before handing the report to the manager.

Off-premise mobile/festival/catering bar: cash box or apron bank counted on site at a folding table or back in the van/commissary, reconciled against a tablet POS or ticket count, with wind, poor light and no fixed layout.

tasks.label: Plan, organize, and control the operations of a cocktail lounge or bar.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Stock bar with beer, wine, liquor, and related supplies such as ice, glassware, napkins, or straws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift beer restock at a neighborhood bar or casual restaurant: bartender walks to the walk-in cooler or basement storeroom, hauls cases and six-packs of bottled/canned beer, cuts cases open, and loads under-counter reach-ins and floor coolers, rotating older stock forward (FIFO), working in a 24-30 inch aisle with cords, mats, drains and other staff present.

Mid-service top-off of the back-bar sliding-door bottle cooler from cases already staged behind the bar: robot-accessible fixed cooler shelves are refilled and faced with bottles and cans as they sell down, done repeatedly during a shift in a busy but institution-controlled bar.

Ice runs: filling the bar's ice wells, bottle coolers and service bins with bulk ice from an ice machine or ice bin, using scoops, buckets or an ice caddy; repeated several times per shift, including icing down bottled beer in a tub for a busy period.

Liquor and wine restock: replacing empty bottles in speed rails and on back-bar shelves, hauling wine cases from storage, loading wine racks and under-bar wine fridges, facing labels and organizing by brand at a full-service bar or hotel bar.

Glassware: retrieving racks of clean pint, rocks, wine and specialty glasses from the dish area, unloading them onto back-bar shelves and overhead racks, polishing spotted glasses, and filling the glass chiller/froster before service.

Bar sundries and draft supplies: refilling napkin caddies, straw and pick holders, coasters, stir sticks, cut-fruit garnish trays and mixers; plus moving half-barrel kegs into the keg cooler and hooking them up when a line blows.

sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA is a rail-mounted robot arm built specifically to restock refrigerated store shelves with beverage bottles and cans; it was mass-produced for installation in 300 FamilyMart convenience stores ... and replenishes up to 1,000 containers per day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: refilling a refrigerated beverage case with bottles and cans is the same object class, precision and placement problem as topping off a bar's back-bar bottle cooler from staged cases.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: TX SCARA runs around the clock relying almost entirely on its GORDON AI to decide when and where to stock, with only rare remote teleoperated recovery; store staff, however, still keep the robot's rear storage shelves supplied, so the fetch-from-storeroom step is not automated.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; the article also documents the limit that humans replenish the robot's feed shelves, which bounds how much of a bar restock the system could do.

sources.title: Telexistence Deploys AI and Remote-Controlled Robots in 300 Convenience Stores, Utilizing Azure
sources.claim: TX SCARA remains in commercial service at roughly 300 convenience stores as of 2025, confirming the deployment is durable rather than a one-off pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms continuing deployment of the beverage-shelf restocking system cited for the bar cooler top-off instance.

sources.title: Automated Bottle Production Line in Traditional Brewery | Kawasaki Robotics
sources.claim: At Westheimer Brewery, fenced Kawasaki BX200L robots unload glass beer bottles from crates onto a conveyor and pack filled bottles back into crates, with a CP500L palletizing full cartons of beer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: de-crating and re-crating glass beer bottles is the same object handling (grip, lift, place into slotted holders) as unloading cases of beer into cooler racks or setting liquor bottles into a speed rail, when the crates and racks are presented in fixed positions.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and placing full half-barrel kegs is the identical object and payload as moving kegs into a bar's keg cooler; it is demonstrated only where kegs arrive fixtured on pallets and conveyors.

sources.claim: ABB's IRB 365 FlexPicker delta robot is a commercial high-speed picker used in food, beverage and consumer-goods packaging lines to pick, reorient and place lightweight items such as candies, small bottles and shelf-ready packages at up to 120 picks per minute.

sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse

sources.title: Cheers to AI: ADAM Robot Bartender Makes Drinks at Vegas Golden Knights Game | NVIDIA Blog
sources.claim: Richtech Robotics' ADAM dual-arm robot works as a bartender in human venues, serving over 16,000 drinks at a Las Vegas cafe and pouring drinks at T-Mobile Arena, using onboard vision to detect cups and correct pours.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bar-side manipulation of cups and bottles inside a hospitality venue; it shows robots can work at a bar station but ADAM's ingredients, cups and ice are replenished by human staff, so it does not perform stocking.

tasks.label: Serve snacks or food items to customers seated at the bar.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual restaurant/pub bar: bartender picks up plated hot food (burger, wings, appetizer) from the kitchen window, adds silverware, napkin and condiments, and sets it in front of a specific guest seated at the bar amid glassware and other guests' items, then clears the plate afterward.

Neighborhood/dive bar: complimentary or simple snacks - scooping nuts, pretzels or popcorn into bowls, placing and refilling them along the bar top, or handing packaged chips/jerky over the counter to seated patrons.

High-volume sports bar or nightclub during a rush: baskets and shared plates delivered to a bar packed with seated and standing patrons, loud, spills and a crowded bar top, orders fired continuously, extra napkins and plates handed across the counter.

Upscale hotel bar or cocktail lounge: small plates, olives/charcuterie, amuse-bouche served to presentation standards, coursing and timing, guest modifications and allergy checks, plate set precisely in front of a seated guest.
Arena, casino or airport bar: pre-packaged or simple snacks handed quickly over a counter to patrons at the bar, high throughput, institution-controlled concourse.

Off-premise/mobile bartending: catered private event, festival or wedding pop-up bar set up in a space taken as found; snack bowls and passed bites served over a temporary bar, layout differs site to site, sometimes outdoors.

tasks.label: Mix ingredients, such as liquor, soda, water, sugar, and bitters, to prepare cocktails and other drinks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume nightlife service: neighborhood bar, nightclub, or stadium/arena concession bar. Bartender builds simple mixed drinks (well highballs, vodka soda, rum and coke, gin and tonic, shots) by the round, in a crowded, loud, fast-paced environment, with ice, standard pours, and a lime wedge; orders come verbally or on POS tickets.

Restaurant or hotel service bar: bartender makes standard cocktails to recipe from server tickets and guest orders (margarita, martini, mojito, old fashioned, cosmopolitan), shaking or stirring, straining, adding standard garnishes, at moderate steady pace across a shift.

Craft cocktail bar, on-menu drinks: shaken sours and spirit-forward stirred cocktails built from house menu specs with pre-batched juices and syrups on hand, standard glassware and a fixed garnish tray.

Craft cocktail bar, bespoke work: dealer's-choice drinks improvised to a guest's stated preferences, plus fresh-squeezed citrus, muddled herbs and fruit, egg-white/aquafaba shakes, house infusions, hand-cut or clear ice, expressed peels and elaborate plated garnishes, with tasting and adjustment before service.

Resort, casino, cruise or poolside bar: frozen and blended drinks (frozen margaritas, daiquiris, pina coladas) made in a blender, plus batched punches, pitchers and carafes of the same cocktail for groups and banquet service.

Off-premise/mobile event bartending: wedding tent, backyard party, or catered corporate event, where the bar is a folding table or portable unit, supplies are limited to what was brought, and the bartender mixes signature cocktails and simple highballs for a crowd.

sources.title: Boozy bots could serve you up your next cocktail (MIT Technology Review)
sources.claim: The same Makr Shakr installation at Tipsy Robot has been reported to produce up to 120 drinks per hour at commercial prices, indicating throughput in the range of a human bartender for simple mixed drinks.

sources.title: Robot Bartenders at the Bionic Bar on Royal Caribbean - Cruise Critic
sources.claim: Royal Caribbean's Bionic Bar, powered by Makr Shakr, has operated on nine cruise ships since 2014; two robotic arms mix cocktails and mocktails from ... ordered on tablets and deliver them to guests, at about two drinks per minute, with human attendants only assisting guests and cleaning spills.

sources.title: Makr Shakr On The Road | Carlo Ratti Associati
sources.claim: The Makr Shakr system is a fully automated bartending system whose arms perform the standard cocktail mixing motions - shaking, stirring, muddling, straining and measured pouring - across dozens of ingredients with milliliter precision.

sources.title: Makr Shakr opens robotic bar in Amsterdam - Globetrender
sources.claim: Makr Shakr sells a relocatable mobile robotic bar unit (Bruno) rented for events, and has installed its automated bar at temporary event sites such as EXPO Milan, showing the purpose-built robot bar can be brought to off-premise event settings.

sources.title: Humanoid bartender robot ADAM debuts at Texas Rangers stadium - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Richtech Robotics' ADAM dual-arm robot bartender is installed in a stadium bar at the Texas Rangers' Globe Life Field, preparing cocktails and mocktails from its own purpose-built station next to human bartenders; it was Richtech's tenth ADAM installation.

sources.title: ADAM: The Nvidia-Powered Bartender Robot at the NHL Arena - AI Magazine
