Frozen blended cocktails involve the same manipulation class - dispensing measured liquids, ice and fruit into a blender jar, blending, and pouring into a serving cup at a pickup point - with comparable objects, precision and a purpose-built kiosk environment.

tasks.label: Slice and pit fruit for garnishing drinks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift bulk citrus prep: barback/bartender washes cases of limes and lemons and cuts them into 6-8 wedges each on a cutting board behind the bar or in the adjoining prep area, filling garnish caddies for the night's service; consistent wedge size and no seeds/pith mess expected.

Bulk slicing of wheels and other fruit: orange wheels and half-wheels, cucumber slices, pineapple spears, strawberries, apple slices sliced to uniform thickness (including thin wheels destined for a dehydrator) and stored in containers for the cocktail menu.
Pitting and seeding: pitting fresh cherries for old-fashioneds, pitting olives or dates for savory drinks, flicking seeds out of cut citrus wheels before they go in the caddy.

Mid-service top-ups: during a rush the bartender grabs two or three limes and quickly cuts wedges or an orange half-wheel on a small board in a cramped, wet, crowded well between drink builds, then drops them into the rail caddy within seconds.

Craft/decorative garnish work: hand-cut citrus twists and channel-knife peels, fruit fans, flags, carved or shaped garnishes to a specific cocktail spec, varying drink to drink and cut to order in a craft cocktail bar.

sources.title: SupraCut™ Systems | Automatic Citrus Wedger
sources.claim: SupraCut is a commercially sold, countertop automated citrus wedger for bars, restaurants and venues that wedges lemons, limes and ... ( an optional 'courtesy slice') at ~15 whole fruit per minute once fruit is placed in it.

tasks.label: Arrange bottles and glasses to make attractive displays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Opening/closing shift at a neighborhood bar or casual-dining restaurant: arranging the back-bar spirits display on tiered, often mirrored shelves — grouping bottles by category and price tier, stepping bottles by height, turning labels forward, pulling forward and filling gaps after a restock, and shifting existing (partly full, sometimes sticky) bottles around in cramped clearances.

Glassware display work: after polishing, arranging clean glassware for show — hanging stemware foot-first into overhead rail racks, setting even rows of rocks/pint/coupe glasses on the back-bar shelf and speed shelf, and inverting stacks neatly for the visible display.

Loading and facing the refrigerated bottled-beer/mixer display case behind the bar: uniform bottles and cans placed in rows in known lanes, faced forward so labels are visible to guests, restocked from cases during the shift.

Building a themed or promotional display: a seasonal/holiday arrangement, a brand feature with supplier point-of-sale props and signage, or a stacked bottle pyramid/champagne-glass tower — the bartender chooses the composition using novel decor items on hand.

Banquet, hotel or event bar setup inside the venue: laying out bottles and glassware attractively on a portable bar or service station before a function — rows of glasses, featured bottles fronted, garnish and display items arranged, done to a house standard under time pressure.

Off-site catered or pop-up bar (private home, tent, outdoor festival stand): improvising an attractive bottle-and-glass arrangement on a folding or rented bar with whatever surfaces, lighting and crates are available at the site.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA is a rail-mounted robot arm deployed in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores that autonomously scans display shelves and places bottled and canned beverages into them, succeeding automatically more than 98% of ... with remote operators only handling rare failures.

It transfers to a bartender loading and facing the bar's bottled-beer/mixer cooler — same objects (glass and PET bottles, cans), same act of placing them in ordered, forward-faced rows on a display shelf, at the same placement precision, inside an institution-controlled facility.

sources.title: Telexistence Deploys AI and Remote-Controlled Robots in 300 Convenience Stores, Utilizing Azure

tasks.label: Create drink recipes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During service at a neighborhood or restaurant bar, a guest asks for 'bartender's choice' or an off-menu drink ('something gin-forward, not too sweet'). The bartender improvises a new combination from the bottles, juices and garnishes on hand, builds and tastes/checks it, serves it, and notes the spec if it works.

Craft cocktail bar or hotel bar: the bar manager/lead bartender develops new seasonal menu cocktails. Multiple bench trials at the back bar or prep area, varying ratio, dilution and modifiers, making house syrups and infusions, tasting and adjusting, costing the pour, then writing a spec sheet staff can execute and getting owner/chef sign-off.

Chain restaurant or casual bar: bartender creates a house special or promo drink within brand constraints, using well spirits, pre-made sour mix, purees and standard glassware; tests one or two versions, has the GM taste it, and submits a simple spec and price.

Banquet/event or high-volume venue: developing a batched cocktail, punch bowl or draft/keg cocktail. Scaling a single-serve spec, adjusting pre-dilution, acid and sugar for holding time, tasting the batch cold, and documenting the batch recipe for the event bar.

Competition entry, brand-ambassador or media recipe creation, often worked out offsite (home kitchen, pop-up, brand training room) with unusual ingredients, homemade cordials and clarifications; repeated tasting, then a written and photographed recipe submitted to a sponsor or publication.

sources.developer: Makr Shakr / Carlo Ratti Associati with MIT Senseable City Lab
sources.title: Makr Shakr - Carlo Ratti Associati
sources.claim: Makr Shakr's robotic bartending system (deployed as Royal Caribbean's Bionic Bar and Tipsy Robot Las Vegas) mixes drinks with robotic arms, but the recipes are composed by human users through a smartphone app; the robot executes and does not originate or evaluate recipes.
sources.transferJustification: The related task is drink mixing/serving, not recipe creation. Cited to show the state of deployed bar robotics: the creative and sensory step (composing and validating a recipe) is done by humans and only the pouring is automated, so capability does not transfer to this task.

sources.title: Meet Cecilia, the World's First Robot Interactive Bartender Who Can Mix Drinks and Tell Jokes - NBC Chicago
sources.claim: Cecilia.ai's interactive robotic bartender, deployed at FIU and other venues, converses with guests and dispenses cocktails, but its specialty drinks are recipes authored by human bartenders and then programmed into the machine.
sources.transferJustification: The related task is guest interaction plus drink dispensing. It shows that even the most conversational deployed bar robot pours human-written recipes and there is no evidence it invents or taste-validates a new spec, so it does not transfer to recipe creation.

sources.system: Cambridge robot chef with electronic tasting probe
sources.developer: University of Cambridge Department of Engineering with Beko
sources.title: Taste of the future: robot chef learns to 'taste as you go' - University of Cambridge
sources.claim: A Cambridge/Beko robot 'chef' fitted with a conductance-probe tongue can assess the saltiness of a simple dish during simulated chewing, but the work is explicitly a proof of concept limited to a single taste dimension.
sources.transferJustification: The related task is robotic taste feedback during cooking, the sensory step recipe creation depends on. It demonstrates only proof-of-concept saltiness estimation on a scrambled-egg dish, far short of judging balance, aroma and palatability of a cocktail, so it cannot substantiate whole-task completion.

sources.title: Robotic optimization of powdered beverages leveraging computer vision and Bayesian optimization - PubMed
sources.claim: An EPFL robot arm autonomously optimizes preparation parameters for powdered beverages (cappuccino) in a laboratory rig using computer-vision feedback and Bayesian optimization, but the objective is visual foam quality of one fixed product rather than creation of a novel flavored recipe.
sources.transferJustification: The related task is autonomous beverage-parameter optimization in a purpose-built rig, the closest robotic analogue to bench-testing a drink. It tunes process settings for a single powdered product against a visual metric, with no flavor judgment or novel formulation, so it does not complete recipe creation.

sources.developer: Research group publishing in RSC Digital Discovery
sources.title: Automated odor-blending with one-pot Bayesian optimization - Digital Discovery (RSC)
sources.claim: A laboratory system blends liquid odorants with automated syringe pumps under Bayesian optimization driven by an olfactory sensor array, autonomously converging on blends that match a target sensory profile in a purpose-built benchtop setup.
sources.transferJustification: The related task is automated liquid formulation toward a sensor-defined target, a sub-step of recipe development. It matches a pre-specified odor target using pure odorants in glassware; it does not originate an appealing drink concept, work with bar ingredients, or produce a spec an employer would accept.

Mobile/outdoor vending: food truck, street cart or festival stand taken as found on a sidewalk or field — cash box plus a mobile card reader, no fixed layout, weather and crowd conditions, change made from a pouch.

tasks.label: Balance receipts and payments in cash registers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift till count at a fast-food store: the cashier or shift lead pulls the drawer, takes it to the counter-back or office, counts bills and coins, compares the total to the POS X/Z report, records over/short, and signs off.

Start-of-shift bank verification: worker receives an assigned till (e.g., $150 in mixed denominations), counts it against the stated starting amount, loads it into the register, and confirms the opening balance in the POS.
Mid-shift skim/drop: worker pulls accumulated large bills out of a busy drawer during peak, counts the skim, records the drop amount in the POS, and secures it in the store safe.

End-of-day close-out by a counter lead/shift manager: consolidating several cashiers' drawers plus drive-thru drawer, counting the safe and coin, reconciling the day's cash against sales/refunds/payouts, and preparing the bank deposit or armored pickup.

Resolving an over/short discrepancy: recounting the drawer, re-running the register report, checking voids, refunds, coupons and paid-outs against receipts, and documenting the variance for the manager.

instances.label: Front-of-house self-serve and counter restock during service: refilling napkin, straw, lid and cup dispensers, sauce/condiment packet caddies, pumps, sweetener and coffee-condiment bar, cup sleeves, and topping off the self-serve drink station; done in the customer dining area with guests moving through, between order transactions.

Behind-the-counter production line restock: pulling cases/tubs from the walk-in cooler, freezer and dry storage and refilling make-line ingredient pans, topping bins, cheese/produce containers, sauce pumps and bagged product on the fry/grill station; portioning into pans, dating/labeling, rotating older product forward, in a hot, cramped kitchen during a shift.

Receiving a delivery and putting it away: meeting the truck at the back door, checking cases against the invoice, moving frozen, refrigerated and dry cases to freezer, walk-in and stockroom racks, and rotating existing stock FIFO.

Monitoring levels and ordering: walking the line, stockroom and walk-in counting on-hand cases and units against par levels, noting shortages, and submitting the order through the supplier portal/tablet or phoning it in.

tasks.label: Perform cleaning duties, such as sweeping, mopping, and washing dishes, to keep equipment and facilities sanitary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sweeping and mopping the customer-facing dining room/lobby of a fast-food restaurant: crumbs, fry salt, drink spills and tracked-in grit over open tile, around fixed and loose tables, chairs, high chairs, trash-can corrals and entry mats, done at off-peak times or after close.

Mopping/degreasing back-of-house floors: narrow aisles between fryers, grill and walk-in, greasy quarry tile under rubber floor mats, around floor drains and carts, plus spot-mopping spills behind the counter during a rush while coworkers keep working.

Warewashing at the dish station: scraping and dumping bus tubs of trays, cups, lids, small utensils and pans, racking them, running the commercial dish machine, unloading, air-drying and stacking clean wares back on the line.

Wiping and sanitizing during service: dining tables and chair seats between customers, trays, condiment/beverage station, counters and the drink-machine drip area, using a sanitizer bucket and cloth, plus clearing napkins/food debris to the trash.

Scheduled cleaning of food equipment and pot-sink work: scraping and cleaning the grill, filtering or boiling out fryers, disassembling and brush-washing shake/soda machine parts and nozzles, hand-washing pans, fry baskets and utensils in a three-compartment sink, sanitizing and reassembling.

Cleaning the customer restroom: toilets, urinals, sinks, mirrors and ..., emptying restroom trash, checking and wiping fixtures between rushes in a small fixed-layout restroom that customers may enter.

tasks.label: Brew coffee and tea, and fill containers with requested beverages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: QSR counter/drive-thru fountain drinks during a lunch rush: read the order screen, grab the right cup size, scoop ice, fill from the multi-valve soda fountain, cap, and set the cup in the carrier/holding rack, dozens of times an hour in a crowded crew aisle.

Batch-brewed drip coffee, hot tea, and iced tea in a fast-food breakfast station, convenience store, or cafeteria: load grounds/filters, run the brewer, keep urns and iced-tea dispensers full, and pour/dispense cups of hot coffee, hot water with a tea bag, or iced tea to order.

Made-to-order espresso and handcrafted coffee drinks at a cafe or coffee counter: grind and tamp, pull shots, steam or pour milk, add syrups/ice/cold foam, build hot or iced lattes to customer modifications, and lid the cup for pickup.

Blended and frozen beverages: smoothies, frappe-style coffee drinks, milkshakes, slushes, and boba/milk teas—portioning ingredients, blending, adding boba/toppings or whipped cream, and filling the cup.

Bulk and non-standard containers: filling 96-oz coffee travelers, carafes and airpots for catering, gallon jugs/pitchers of brewed iced tea for the self-serve station, and filling customers' own reusable tumblers.

sources.title: Automation putting faster in the fast-food industry

tasks.label: Clean and organize eating, service, and kitchen areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dining-room upkeep during open hours at a quick-service restaurant: walking the lobby, clearing trays, cups, wrappers and leftover food that customers left on tables, wiping tabletops and booth seats with a sanitizer cloth, pushing in chairs and picking up dropped litter, all while guests are seated and moving through the room.

Floor care in the dining room and front service area: sweeping crumbs and debris, spot-mopping drink spills during service, and running a full sweep/mop or scrub of the hard-floor lobby and counter area at open or close.

Cleaning the kitchen line during and after a shift: wiping and sanitizing prep tables and landing zones, scraping and cleaning the grill, cleaning fryer surrounds and filtering/changing fryer oil, cleaning the shake/beverage machine nozzles, and cleaning the greasy floor behind the line.

Organizing and restocking the service area: refilling napkin, straw, lid and cup holders, restocking condiment/pump stations and sauce caddies, tidying and wiping the front counter and drink station, and bringing supplies out from the stockroom to their designated spots.
Trash handling: emptying dining-room and kitchen bins, tying and pulling full bags, fitting new liners, wiping bin lids, and hauling bags out the back door to the dumpster or compactor.

Wash-up of smallwares and dish area: scraping, racking and running trays, utensils, pans, fry baskets and drink pitchers through the dish machine, unloading and putting them away, and cleaning the sinks and dish station.

sources.title: Pudu CC1 At QT: How A 4-in-1 Floor Cleaning Robot Delivers Real ROI In Convenience Stores

tasks.label: Prepare daily food items, and cook simple foods and beverages, such as sandwiches, salads, soups, pizza, or coffee, using proper safety precautions and sanitary measures.

instances.label: Fry station in a burger/chicken QSR: pull frozen fries, nuggets, onion rings or tots from the freezer, load baskets, drop into the fryer bank, shake and time several baskets at once during a lunch rush, dump, salt and hold to the chain's hold-time standard.

Cooking and assembling hot made-to-order items: griddling burger patties, chicken or eggs and toasting buns, then building and boxing the sandwich; or, at a pizza counter, pressing/stretching dough, saucing, cheesing, topping to the order, baking, cutting and boxing.

Fast-casual makeline: building salads and grain bowls to order (base, grains, proteins, chopped vegetables, cheese, dressing), portioning by scoop to spec, mixing where requested, lidding and labeling, for in-line guests and digital/delivery orders.

Deli/sub counter: building subs, wraps, burritos and breakfast sandwiches to individual customer instructions - opening and toasting the roll or tortilla, layering meats/cheese/produce, sauces to taste, folding or rolling, cutting and wrapping in paper.

Beverage station in a coffee shop or QSR: brewing batch coffee and iced tea, pulling espresso shots, steaming and pouring milk drinks, building iced and blended drinks to order, and keeping cups, syrups and milk stocked.

Opening/daily prep and sanitation in the back of house: washing and slicing tomatoes, lettuce and onions; portioning proteins; batching soups, salads and sauces; filling and rotating steam-table/cold wells; date-labeling and discarding expired product; sanitizing boards, utensils and surfaces.

sources.title: Miso Launches Next-Gen Flippy Fry Station - Food + Beverage Technology

tasks.label: Prepare and serve cold drinks, frozen milk drinks, or desserts, using drink-dispensing, milkshake, or frozen-custard machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quick-service restaurant front counter / mobile-order station at ordinary pace: crew member reads the order off the KDS, grabs the right cup size, fills with ice and soda or iced tea/lemonade from the crew-side fountain tower, caps it, adds a straw, and sets it on the counter or hands it to the guest. Standard fixed equipment, institution-controlled premises.

Drive-thru during a peak rush: three- and four-drink orders built in seconds, mixed sizes and flavors, lidded and bagged/trayed, then handed out the window to a driver in a car whose height and reach position vary; cars arrive continuously and seconds per order matter.

Café / boba / juice-bar counter (baristas are in this SOC): poured and assembled cold drinks — iced coffee, cold brew, iced tea, refreshers, boba milk teas with tapioca — scooping ice, pouring milk/syrup/tea from dispensers and pitchers, adding pearls, sealing or lidding the cup, marking it and handing it to the named customer.

Milkshakes, malts, Frosty-type frozen milk drinks and blended frappés at a fast-food or drive-in counter: hold the cup under the shake machine spindle/nozzle and draw the product, or scoop ice and pour base into a blender jar and blend, then add whipped cream or a candy mix-in, cap, and serve at the counter or window.

Ice cream / frozen custard stand: swirl a soft-serve cone or fill a cup from the custard machine, dip in chocolate shell or add sundae toppings, sauces and sprinkles, hand the fragile cone across a counter or through a walk-up window without dripping or dropping it, in a shop kept to a standard layout.

Fixed concession bar/stand at a stadium, arena or movie theater during an event: pouring fountain sodas, frozen carbonated drinks and mocktails into branded cups, lidding and handing them across the bar to fans, restocking cups and ice, working alongside other stand staff in an institution-controlled venue.

sources.title: Artly debuts mini Barista Bot at National Restaurant Association 2025 show

tasks.label: Wrap menu items such as sandwiches, hot entrees, and desserts for serving or for takeout.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Burger/chicken-sandwich QSR assembly station during a lunch rush: worker folds a paper or foil-lined wrapper around each hot assembled sandwich (or seats it in a clamshell carton), marks/labels special-order items, and slides it to the heated landing zone. Standard kitchen, crowded, items vary in height and are hot and greasy.

Burrito/wrap/taco line (Chipotle-, Taco Bell-, breakfast-burrito-style): worker folds the tortilla around a custom fill, rolls it, then wraps it in foil or paper and twists/tucks the ends for takeout. Highly deformable item, variable fill volume, made to order.

Hot entrees and sides from a steam table or fry station packed into clamshells, boxes, or bags: fried chicken box, pizza into a box, plate meal into a hinged container; lid closed, container bagged with utensils and napkins for takeout. Standard counter/kitchen line.

Coffee-shop/bakery counter desserts: cookies, donuts, pastries, or cake slices picked with tissue paper or tongs and bagged, boxed, or sleeve-wrapped for the customer, often in front of the customer at the display case.

Made-to-order deli/sub counter: overstuffed sandwich cut in half, wrapped tightly in deli paper or plastic film, taped and labeled with the order name for pickup or delivery courier. Item shape and fill vary widely order to order.

sources.title: Wrap Producer Automates Production with Grote Robotics (FPSA)
sources.claim: Grote Company installed a robotic twin-lane line at a UK sandwich and wrap producer that automates wrap handling, aligning and ... at 100 wraps/minute, eliminating six operators per shift, in a food plant production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial handling and finishing of the same deformable tortilla wraps and sandwiches the counter worker wraps; it shows machine-controlled manipulation of these items to a packaged, saleable state when work is presented on a fixtured conveyor.

sources.system: Grote robotic sandwich assembly line (Stäubli robots)

tasks.label: Set up dining areas for meals, and clear them following meals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quick-service restaurant dining room upkeep during service: as guests leave, the worker wipes tables and seat surfaces, picks up trays, cups, wrappers and spilled food guests left behind, pushes in chairs, spot-sweeps under tables and empties lobby trash bins, all while customers move through the room.

Pre-meal setup of a counter-service dining area: sanitize and dry tables, align tables and chairs to the standard layout, put out napkin dispensers, condiments, straws, wrapped cutlery, trays and high chairs, restock the self-serve beverage/condiment station and place table tents or signage.

Institutional cafeteria (school, hospital, corporate) after a meal period: collect trays, plates, cups and cutlery left on tables, scrape waste, stack into bus tubs or a dish cart, wheel them to the dish room, then wipe tables and benches and sweep the floor before the next seating.

Buffet, food-hall or catered-group service: set tables with place settings (rolled silverware/folded napkins, cups, plates), reconfigure table and chair layout for a booked group, then after the meal strip the tables of dishes, glasses and linens and reset them.

Coffee shop / cafe seating area during the day: continuously clear cups, plates, pastry bags and crumbs from small tables with guests seated close by, wipe tables and counters, tidy chairs, and restock the milk/sugar condiment bar.

Outdoor patio, curbside or food-truck seating area: clear trays and drinkware from outdoor tables, wipe furniture, deal with wind-blown litter, uneven paving and weather, and stack or chain chairs at close.

sources.system: pi0 (π0) on UR5e / bimanual lab platforms
sources.title: π0: Our First Generalist Policy
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi0 generalist policy was fine-tuned to bus a table: autonomously picking dishes, cutlery, cups and trash off a table and sorting them into a bussing bin and a trash bin, on lab robot platforms (UR5e, bimanual ARX/Trossen), scoring 0.97 (easy) and 0.88 (hard) on graded evaluations.
sources.transferJustification: Bussing a table is exactly the clearing half of this task — same objects (plates, cups, cutlery, food waste) and the same sort-into-bin decisions — but performed at a fixtured lab station rather than in a live dining room.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics' three-arm dishwashing cell runs autonomously 24 hours a day in multiple live restaurants, picking dirty plates, glasses and silverware out of bus tubs (including tubs full of spilled liquid) and running them through the dishwasher, washing over a million dishes a ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dish handling at the dish station. It substantiates commercial-grade, worker-rate manipulation of exactly the soiled dishware a busser clears (greasy plates, stacked plates, glassware, silverware) when that work is brought to a fixtured robotic station.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics unveils Dyna-1: Autonomous robot achieves 24-hour dexterous task performance
sources.claim: Dyna Robotics' DYNA-1 model, running a pair of stationary arms, folded 700-900 napkins to restaurant standard over 24 hours with >99% success and no human intervention, at about 60% of human speed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: napkin folding / silverware rolling is the preparation step of dining-area setup; it shows worker-rate, production-quality dexterous handling of the exact linens used to set tables, at a purpose-built two-arm station.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Raises $120 Million to Advance Robotic Foundation Models on the Path to Physical Artificial General Intelligence | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Dyna Robotics reported its robots deployed with customers in hotels, restaurants, laundromats and gyms, running sixteen hours a day ... commercial scale six months after launch.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the fixtured dual-arm station is a real commercial installation inside restaurants and hotels, not only a lab rig, for the setup-preparation portion of this task.

sources.title: Alphabet's X has 'Everyday Robots' test fleet that autonomously performs office maintenance tasks
sources.claim: Alphabet's Everyday Robots operated a fleet of over 100 mobile manipulators autonomously performing tasks in Google's Bay Area offices, including sorting trash and wiping cafeteria tables with a squeegee attachment; the program was later shut down by Alphabet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiping cafeteria tables and sorting discarded cups/trash is the surface-cleaning half of clearing a dining area; it substantiates autonomous table wiping, though the pilot fleet was retired and never demonstrated a full worker-rate dining-room reset.

sources.title: Iris Ohyama to acquire service robot maker Smile Robotics - The Robot Report

tasks.label: Collect and return dirty dishes to the kitchen for washing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quick-service restaurant dining room sweep: during and after a lunch rush the counter worker circulates the seating area with a tray or tub, collecting trays, baskets, cups, lids and any ceramic/reusable dishware left on tables, booths and the self-bus/trash station, then carries the stack through the counter door to the dish sink area and drops it for washing. Customers, children and strollers are moving through the room; spills and dropped food are common.

Counter-service cafe or coffee shop: the barista/counter worker walks the floor several times a shift gathering used ceramic mugs, glassware, small plates, saucers, spoons and reusable tumblers from small tables, window bars and the condiment station into a bus tub, then carries the tub behind the counter and unloads it into the dish pit / three-compartment sink for washing. Items are fragile, wet and stacked unevenly.

Institutional cafeteria (school, hospital, campus or corporate dining) counter attendant: collects loaded trays, plates, bowls, cups and flatware from dining tables and from the dish-return window or conveyor, stacks them into racks or a bussing cart, sorts flatware into a soak bin, and wheels the cart into the dishroom for the dish machine operator.

Bulk service-ware return from the front counter and beverage station: at shift change or after a rush the worker gathers accumulated bus tubs, dish racks, utensil bins, empty serving pans, scoops, blender jars, drink pitchers and coffee urns from the service line, steam table and drink bar and hauls them back to the dish area, unloading them onto the soiled-dish table.

Outdoor patio, drive-in curbside or off-site event service: the worker walks a patio, parking-lot carhop stalls, or a catered/event serving area collecting trays, baskets, glassware and reusable service ware from tables, car window trays or folding tables, and carries them back to the kitchen or a mobile dish station. Wind, weather, uneven paving and unpredictable passers-by.

sources.date: 2022 (product page current 2026; joint trials from April 2021)
sources.title: W-Robo ❘ Dish Sorting Robot
sources.claim: TechMagic's W-Robo (sold as 'finibo' with Fujimak) is a commercial dish-sorting robot installed inside restaurant/canteen washing areas behind a safety fence; it uses machine-learning vision to recognize and sort soiled tableware of varied shapes into the washing process at up to 600 pieces per hour, and is operating in actual kitchens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: receiving soiled tableware presented at the dish-return/wash station and moving it into the washer. Under the E1 counterfactual the dirty dishes are brought to the machine already presented on a fixture, so the remaining work of this task — taking the dirty dishes and getting them to washing — is exactly what W-Robo does, on the same objects (plates, bowls, cups, flatware) at above-human throughput.

sources.title: TechMagic K.K. & fujimak corporation Start Trials for Automatic Dish-sorting Robot「finibo」
sources.claim: finibo, the automatic dish-sorting robot jointly developed ... and commercial-kitchen maker Fujimak, entered field trials in real commercial kitchens in Japan.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the W-Robo item: the robot takes soiled dishware handed to it at the wash station and moves it into the dish machine, which is the accepted-output end of 'return dirty dishes to the kitchen for washing' when the work is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Nala Robotics Introduces Autonomous Dishwasher
sources.claim: Nala Robotics' Spotless is a camera- and machine-learning-driven robotic dishwashing cell installed in professional kitchens that takes soiled dishware, removes leftovers, rinses and loads it through the wash cycle; the vendor states it is being deployed in restaurants and senior living centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling incoming soiled dishware in the dish pit. It substantiates that, when dirty dishes are brought to a purpose-built station, a robot can pick them up, scrape them and move them into washing — the terminal step of this task under the E1 counterfactual, on the same objects (dishware, glassware, cutlery, cookware).

sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi line of autonomous restaurant robots is deployed at large scale (16,000+ robots shipped into commercial service) and autonomously navigates dining rooms to run food out and carry bus tubs of dirty dishes back to the ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transport of a loaded bus tub from dining room to dish pit inside a working restaurant. It carries over only for the transport leg of this task; it does not address picking dishes off tables or unloading them at the dish station.

sources.title: Bear Robotics (Servi) — Kitchen Software | RestaurantTools.ai
sources.claim: Deployed bussing/delivery robots such as Servi have no manipulator: restaurant staff must load the dirty dishes onto the robot and unload them at the dish pit, so the collecting half of the task remains human work.

sources.title: Iris Ohyama to acquire service robot maker Smile Robotics - The Robot Report

sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0 model performs an autonomous table-bussing task in which the robot picks dishes, cups and cutlery off a table into a bussing bin and trash into a ...; this is a laboratory demonstration on fixed test tables with partial success rates, not a restaurant deployment.

sources.title: Sunday Unveils "Memo": A Wheeled, Domestic Robot That Learns From $200 Gloves
sources.claim: Sunday Robotics' Memo, a wheeled home robot, has been shown running a 'table-to-dishwasher' cycle — clearing dishes from a table, scraping food waste and loading a dishwasher, including fragile glassware — in homes; it is a pre-launch demonstration with beta deployments planned, not a commercial food-service system.

tasks.label: Scrub and polish counters, steam tables, and other equipment, and clean glasses, dishes, and fountain equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During-shift wipe-down and sanitizing of the front service counter, beverage/condiment station and tray-return area while the store is open: crumbs, spilled soda and syrup, ketchup; items (napkin dispensers, cups, POS terminal, straw caddies) must be moved and replaced; sanitizer bucket and cloth; done quickly between customer transactions.

Closing wipe-down and polishing of behind-counter stainless work surfaces, prep counters and the exteriors of small equipment (toaster, coffee brewers, microwave, shake-machine housing, hood fronts) per the brand's cleaning checklist, after the line is shut down.

Warewashing episode at the dish station: scraping and racking used pans, utensils, blender pitchers, glasses/mugs and trays from bus tubs, running the commercial dish machine (or three-compartment sink), then unloading, air-drying and stacking clean ware for reuse.

Cleaning of fountain and beverage equipment: pulling dispenser nozzles and diffusers, drip trays and ice-bin covers, soaking and brush-scrubbing them, sanitizing, wiping down the dispenser tower and valves, and reassembling so the unit is ready for service.

Steam-table / hot-holding serving line breakdown at close: pulling and washing food pans, draining and de-liming the water wells, scrubbing baked-on food from wells and rails, and polishing the stainless exterior and sneeze guard.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics' three-arm dish-station system runs unattended in a restaurant dish room, picking dirty plates, cups and silverware out of bus tubs, racking them and pushing racks through a standard commercial dish machine 24 hours a day; the second installation runs with no vendor staff on site.

sources.title: Armstrong Raises $12M to Bring General-Purpose Robots to Kitchens
sources.claim: Armstrong's robots are deployed in a major US full-service restaurant chain's kitchens, working with the restaurant's existing commercial dish machines and washing over a million dishes a ... on a subscription basis.

sources.title: Rosie™ by CleanBotix | Robotic Sanitation for Food Plants
sources.claim: CleanBotix's Rosie is a mobile manipulator that autonomously executes rinse, foam, rinse and sanitize cycles on food and beverage plant equipment during the nightly sanitation shift, i.e. machine-performed scrubbing/sanitizing of soiled stainless food equipment and work surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nightly wash-down sanitation of food-processing equipment. It involves the same objects (soiled stainless food-contact equipment and work surfaces), the same soils (grease, protein, syrup residues) and the same accepted output (a surface passing sanitation swabs), so it transfers to scrubbing counters, steam tables and equipment when those surfaces are presented in a machine-oriented washdown setting.

sources.title: CleanBotix Builds Autonomous Food-Processing Robot with MoveIt Pro to Accelerate Market Launch
sources.claim: Rosie's production R6 units ran paid pilots in poultry plants, cleaning four to five hours per session at 80% of human cleaning speed ... than human crews; the control stack supports taught cleaning trajectories and semi-autonomous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (plant equipment sanitation); the ATP-swab result is the quality metric a foodservice employer would apply to a scrubbed counter or steam table, showing machine cleaning of food equipment meets human-crew quality.

sources.system: Douglas Machines commercial pot, pan and utensil washers
sources.title: Commercial Pot, Pan and Container Washers | Douglas Machines Corp.
sources.claim: Douglas Machines builds NSF/ANSI 3 certified automated pot, pan, utensil and parts washers used in commercial kitchens and food plants: staff load the items, press a button, and the cabinet washes and sanitizes up to ten batches an hour unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated washing and sanitizing of pans, utensils and small equipment parts. The removable pieces of a steam table (food pans, well covers) and of a fountain dispenser (nozzles, diffusers, drip trays) are exactly these objects, so when the parts are presented to the machine the cleaning and sanitizing step is completed to NSF standard.

tasks.label: Deliver orders to kitchens, and pick up and serve food when it is ready.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: QSR front counter: worker sends the order to the kitchen (verbal call-out or KDS ticket), monitors the heat-lamp pass, pulls the assembled bag or tray when it appears, checks it against the ticket, and hands it across the counter to the named customer amid a queue.

Drive-thru window: order is relayed to the kitchen, the bagged food and drinks are staged at the window station, and the worker gathers them, seats drinks in a carrier, and hands the bag out through the window into a car during a timed rush.

Coffee/snack counter (café, food court, convenience store): worker calls or rings the drink to the bar, retrieves the finished cup or heated pastry from the bar/oven pass, lids and sleeves it, sets it on the hand-off plane and calls the customer's name.

Fast-casual or cafeteria table running: worker carries plated food or a loaded tray from the kitchen pass through a dining room of seated guests to a numbered table and sets the items down, returning for the next run.

Concession/stadium/theater/airport counter during a rush: order shouted or keyed to the back line, worker pulls hot items from a warmer or holding bin, assembles the order in trays/carriers, and serves it over a high counter to a moving line.

Counter service with special instructions: worker verbally relays a modification or allergy request to the cook, tracks it, retrieves the item when the cook calls it, verifies the modification, and serves it to the specific customer.

sources.title: McDonald's unveiled an automated store. Some consumers aren't loving it. - CBS News

tasks.label: Distribute food to servers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: QSR kitchen, peak hours: transfer cooked items (fries, nuggets, patties) out of the fryer/grill station into the hot-holding bins and staging trays from which the assembly and counter/window crew take them; hot oil, timers, crew moving through a tight line.

Fast-food / fast-casual: finish and stage completed customer orders  esed and bagged sandwiches, fry cartons, bowls, drinks - on the pickup/heat shelf or hand them directly to the counter and drive-thru crew, matched to order tickets and called out.

Cafe / coffee counter: place finished espresso and iced drinks, plus warmed pastries on plates or in bags, on the hand-off plane for the counter server or customer; varied cup sizes, lids, sleeves, names called from tickets.

Cafeteria or institutional serving line (school, hospital, corporate, buffet): portion food from steam-table hotel pans onto plates and trays and pass them down the tray line to the servers, and carry replacement hotel pans out to the servers' stations during service.

Full-service restaurant expo/pass: check each plated dish against the ticket, add garnish or sauce cups, wipe plate rims, group a table's dishes together and set them under the heat lamps for the servers to run.

tasks.label: Plan, prepare, and deliver meals to individuals with special dietary needs.

instances.label: Quick-service restaurant front line: a customer orders a hot item with a dietary modification (gluten-free bun, no cheese for lactose intolerance, no sauce for a nut/sesame allergy). Worker confirms the request, follows the chain's allergen protocol (glove change, clean utensils/board, separate assembly), cooks/assembles the item on the standard grill-fry line, bags it and hands it over at the counter or pickup shelf during a rush.

Coffee/beverage counter: drinks for customers with dietary needs utions - oat/soy/almond milk for dairy allergy or lactose intolerance, sugar-free syrup or unsweetened for diabetics, decaf, no-whip. Worker builds the drink on standard espresso/blender equipment, labels it and hands it to the customer at the pickup bar.

Build-to-order bowl, salad or sandwich counter (fast-casual or cafeteria action station): customer specifies vegan, vegetarian, keto, low-sodium, no-pork or an allergen omission; worker assembles the cold/ambient components from pans on a standard makeline or steam table using separate utensils, portions to spec, and passes the finished bowl over the counter.

Institutional cafeteria/senior or school dining counter: worker reads a diet order or resident preference card (diabetic, low sodium, soft/pureed, renal), plans and plates the appropriate components from the steam table onto a tray, adds the correct beverage/dessert substitute, and carries or runs the tray to the diner's table in the dining room.

Special/complex request: a customer with celiac plus multiple allergies (or a small group order, e.g., a halal or kosher-style plate) discusses the menu with the counter worker, who checks ingredient labels, plans a compliant meal or substitution set, prepares it with dedicated equipment, and delivers it to the table or pickup point with the allergen call-out.

tasks.label: Wash dishes, glassware, and silverware after meals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cafeteria / food-court counter operation: after the meal rush, soiled plates, trays, glasses, mugs and flatware come back in bus tubs or at a soiled-dish window. Worker scrapes and pre-rinses, racks the ware, runs a door-type or rack-conveyor dish machine, unloads hot clean ware, sorts flatware and stacks it for the serving line.

Coffee shop / counter cafe: ceramic mugs, glass tumblers, small plates and teaspoons are bussed to the back counter during and after service; worker rinses them, loads an undercounter dish machine (or washes at the bar sink), then dries, polishes and stacks the ware for reuse within minutes.

Quick-service / counter kitchen smallwares: at shift close, tongs, spatulas, scoops, whisks, plastic prep containers, trays, blender jars, milk-steaming pitchers and shake/soft-serve machine parts are disassembled, hand-washed in a three-compartment sink (wash-rinse-sanitize) with brushes for crevices, then air-dried on a rack.

Heavy cookware and service equipment: stock pots, steam-table/hotel pans with baked-on cheese or sauce, sheet pans, fryer baskets and coffee-urn parts are soaked, scrubbed with an abrasive pad at the pot sink, rinsed, sanitized and air-dried.

Concession stand, food truck or off-site catering event: utensils, serving pans, pitchers and glassware washed in cramped or improvised setups with limited hot water, portable sinks and no fixed dish area; layout and equipment differ from site to site and event to event.

sources.claim: State-of-the-art general manipulation models can pick up dishes and place them in a sink in previously unseen real homes, but this is research-grade demonstration of relocating ware, not washing and sanitizing it to a commercial standard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: kitchen cleanup in unstructured settings, cited only to bound E3 - the demonstrated behaviour is relocating dishes to the sink, well short of washing, sanitizing and stacking at worker quality.

tasks.label: Arrange tables and decorations according to instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Reconfiguring the dining room of a quick-service restaurant for a large group (birthday party, sports team, tour bus): pushing free-standing tables together into a specified layout, squaring them up, lining up and tucking chairs, clearing an aisle, then restoring the standard floor plan afterward, often while other customers are seated nearby.

Installing the flat portion of a corporate seasonal/promotional decor kit per a planogram: swapping poster inserts in wall and menu-board frames, applying window clings/decals at marked positions, and distributing new table tents and counter cards.

Installing the three-dimensional portion of the decor kit: taping a banner over the counter, hanging ceiling danglers and garland from clips or wire, stringing streamers and inflating/tying balloon bunches, much of it overhead from a step ladder in a dining room with fixtures and lights.

Setting up a party/celebration table in the dining area: spreading and smoothing a paper or vinyl tablecloth, placing plates, cups, napkins and party favors at each seat, positioning a centerpiece and a small sign, adding a high chair or booster.

Routine open/close reset of the dining room: sliding tables and chairs back to marked standard positions, straightening booth signage, and placing table tents, condiment caddies and napkin holders on every table according to the manager's diagram.

Off-site catering or event setup at a customer's location (office break room, school gym, park pavilion): unloading and unfolding folding tables, draping linens, laying out chafing dishes, serving utensils, signage and simple centerpieces to a layout that varies site to site with unknown obstacles and surfaces.

sources.developer: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
sources.title: ALORE: Autonomous Large-Object Rearrangement with a Legged Manipulator
sources.claim: ALORE, a legged manipulator system, autonomously pushes/pulls large furniture (chairs, tables, bins) to specified target positions and orientations, including a long-horizon trial rearranging 32 chairs in 8 continuous loops over ~40 minutes without failure, in indoor test areas at HKUST (Guangzhou).
sources.transferJustification: The related task is furniture rearrangement to a target layout. Objects (chairs, tables) and required precision (target position and orientation on a flat indoor floor) are the same as arranging dining-room tables and chairs, so performance carries over in a comparably controlled space.

sources.title: Video: Figure's humanoid robots organize room, hang clothes, and make bed without humans
sources.claim: Two Figure Helix-02 humanoids autonomously reset a staged bedroom in under two minutes, repositioning furniture (pushing a chair under a ...), placing small objects, hanging clothes, and jointly spreading and smoothing a comforter (a large deformable fabric) with no teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: The related task is a bedroom reset: spreading/smoothing a comforter and placing objects to a tidy target state. Spreading a tablecloth and laying out plates, cups and a centerpiece involve the same class of deformable-sheet and light-object manipulation on a fixed surface in a controlled room.

sources.system: FANUC iRPickTool vision-guided pick-and-place / case packing cells
sources.developer: FANUC America (and integrators e.g. Stac Material Handling, AMT)
sources.title: Picking & Packing Industry's Most Trusted Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Vision-guided FANUC pick-and-place cells commercially sort items from conveyors and place them ... trays and cases in specified arrangements, with a second robot sealing and applying labels; the vision systems locate randomly presented parts rather than relying on fixed scripted positions.
sources.transferJustification: The related task is vision-guided placement of items at specified positions on a presented workpiece, plus adhesive label application. Placing table tents, plates, cups, caddies and centerpieces on a table brought to the machine, and applying flat window clings/poster inserts, require the same object sizes and sub-centimeter placement precision inside a fenced cell.

sources.title: Nissan Motor Presents the World's First Automated "Intelligent Parking Chair"
sources.claim: Nissan's Intelligent Parking Chair automatically drives office chairs back to designated positions around a table in a camera-instrumented room, restoring a standard seating layout without a human pushing them.
sources.transferJustification: The related task is restoring chairs to a standard layout. It shows chair-level positioning accuracy is achievable when the room is instrumented for the machine, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual for dining-room reset work.

tasks.label: Clean or sanitize work areas, utensils, or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-service cleaning at the espresso bar during a rush: wiping the counter and machine tops of milk/coffee splatter, purging and wiping the steam wand between drinks, rinsing steam pitchers, knocking out and rinsing portafilters, mopping up spills — all around customers, cups, and other staff in a tight bar space.

Washing wares: ceramic mugs, glassware, cutlery, plates from bussed dishes, plus steam pitchers, blender jars and small utensils — scraping, loading and unloading the under-counter/commercial dish machine, hand-washing and sanitizing items in the three-compartment sink, and putting clean ware away.

Cleaning brewing equipment on a scheduled routine: backflushing group heads with detergent, brushing screens and gaskets, soaking portafilters and baskets, running milk-system/blender clean cycles, brushing out the grinder chute and hopper, emptying and washing the knock box and drip trays.
Floor care in the customer seating area and service lobby: sweeping and mopping or vacuuming the open floor during and after service in a café whose layout is fixed and maintained by the operator.

Customer-facing area upkeep: wiping and sanitizing dining tables between guests, cleaning the condiment/milk station, wiping the pastry case glass, and emptying and re-lining trash and recycling bins.

End-of-day deep clean and sanitize: scrubbing sinks and drains, cleaning the ice bin and ice machine, wiping the walk-in/under-counter fridge shelves, cleaning syrup pumps, degreasing behind and under the bar equipment, refreshing sanitizer buckets, and pulling floor mats to clean behind the bar.

sources.system: Costa Coffee Creations robotic kiosk (Briggo-derived technology, with Delaware North)

sources.claim: Costa Coffee Creations, an enclosed robotic coffee kiosk deployed at Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, prepares espresso drinks and keeps itself running, including internal hygiene, without human attendance for up to a week.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended beverage production. Running seven days unattended implies the machine's own prep chamber, milk path and brewing equipment are cleaned/sanitized by machine-controlled cycles rather than by a barista, which is the E1 form of this cleaning task.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: equipment cleaning by the equipment itself. The internal brew group and milk-system cleaning is the same cleaning work a barista performs manually (backflush, milk-line sanitation), executed under machine control on fixtured, purpose-built internals.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong's dishwashing robot works live in restaurant dish rooms, taking dirty bus tubs and producing clean stacked dishes with standard commercial dish machines, running 24 hours a day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restaurant warewashing. Café ware (ceramic mugs, glassware, cutlery, plates) is the same class of objects, handled in the same kind of dish pit with the same standard commercial dish machines, so performance transfers to a café's dishwashing instance.

sources.claim: Armstrong has multiple dishwashing robots installed at a large full-service restaurant chain, operating around the clock at scale with standard commercial dish machines.

sources.claim: Nala Robotics' Spotless is a vision-guided robot-arm dishwashing system being installed in restaurants and senior living kitchens that pre-cleans, washes, dries, stacks and stores kitchenware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial kitchen warewashing including cutlery and glassware, the same objects and soils a barista washes; the installation sits in an ordinary kitchen dish area, matching the café setting.

sources.system: PUDU CC1 / CC1 Pro cleaning robot
sources.title: Pudu CC1 At QT: How A 4-in-1 Floor Cleaning Robot Delivers Real ROI In Convenience Stores
sources.claim: The Pudu CC1 autonomous floor cleaning robot is deployed across QuikTrip convenience stores, sweeping, scrubbing, vacuuming and mopping customer floor space on a schedule without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hard-floor cleaning in a small, high-traffic food-and-beverage retail space with customers present — the same floor soils (spills, coffee, foot traffic) and comparable footprint to a café's seating and service floor.

sources.system: Tennant autonomous scrubbers powered by BrainOS
sources.title: Brain Corp: Sam's Club Deploying Autonomous Robots
sources.claim: Hundreds of BrainOS-powered Tennant autonomous floor scrubbers clean sales floors in Sam's Club and Walmart stores nationwide during business hours.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hard-floor scrubbing in a public retail facility; same cleaning output (swept and mopped floor) as the café floor-care instance, in an institution-controlled human work facility.

sources.title: Table Cleaning Robot Tried at Hawker Centers - Weston Robot
sources.claim: Weston Robot's table cleaning robot autonomously navigates to dining tables in a Singapore hawker centre and wipes them with cloths using a collaborative arm, in a government-supported trial.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiping public dining tables with cloths — the same surfaces, soils and tool as a barista wiping café tables; it is a trial rather than a deployment, so it supports the fixtured (E1) form of the wipe rather than routine café-quality service.

sources.title: Jamba launches automated smoothie station with robotics company Blendid
sources.claim: At the Jamba/Blendid robotic smoothie kiosk, cleaning and restocking of the machine remains a human employee's job even though drink making is automated.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant limit: even at deployed beverage-robot installations, cleaning of exterior surfaces and the surrounding work area is still performed by human staff, which caps open-café cleaning below E2.

tasks.label: Receive and process customer payments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Card / contactless / mobile-wallet payment at the café counter: barista rings the order into the POS touchscreen, presents the terminal, customer taps, dips or swipes, tip prompt is answered, receipt printed or emailed, card handed back if presented physically.

Cash payment at the counter: customer hands over bills and coins, barista verifies large bills, opens the till, counts out change and hands change plus receipt back, keeping the drawer accurate during a rush.

Drive-thru window payment at a coffee drive-thru (e.g., Starbucks, Dutch Bros): barista leans out the window, takes a card or cash from a driver seated in a vehicle, runs the tender, and returns card/change/receipt through the window in whatever weather.

Non-standard tender at the counter: gift card swipe or reload, loyalty/rewards redemption, promo or employee discount code, split tender across two cards or card-plus-gift-card, prepaid app order verification.

Payment exceptions: refunds and voids for a remade or wrong drink, correcting an overcharge, declined-card handling, suspected counterfeit bill, till discrepancy or receipt dispute — usually requiring judgment and a manager override.

Mobile cart / pop-up espresso stand at an outdoor event, farmers market or sidewalk pitch: barista takes cash and card payments on a tablet reader in an as-found setting with variable weather, crowding and no fixed layout.

sources.title: McDonald's Rolls Out Cash Accepting Kiosks, as Labor Costs Rise | Food On Demand
sources.claim: McDonald's has rolled out self-order kiosks in US restaurants that physically accept cash and mechanically dispense change, completing the tender without a cashier at the counter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: taking counter payment at a quick-service food counter. Same currency denominations, same ticket sizes, same institution-controlled counter setting as a café register, so cash acceptance, validation and change provision carry over to a barista's cash transaction.

sources.claim: Glory's CI-10X point-of-sale cash recycler automates the whole cash transaction at the point of presentment, ... counting the tender and providing change, so staff never handle the money.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cash tendering and change-making at a retail/food-service register. The machine performs exactly the physical sub-acts a barista performs with cash (accept notes and coins, validate, count, dispense change), at the same counter.

sources.system: Glory CASHINFINITY family (POS and back-office cash recyclers)
sources.title: GLORY Confirmed as Global Leader in Retail Cash Recycling Solutions by RBR Data Services
sources.claim: Retail cash recycling machines of this type are in widespread commercial deployment across food-service and small-store formats, not laboratory prototypes.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment scale for the cash-handling evidence above; same task (counter cash tender and change) in convenience-store and QSR settings comparable to a café counter.

tasks.label: Prepare or serve hot or cold beverages, such as coffee, espresso drinks, blended coffees, or teas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hot espresso-milk drinks (latte, cappuccino, cortado, mocha, americano) made to order at a coffee-shop bar: grind, dose, tamp, pull shots, steam/texture milk (dairy or oat/almond), add syrups, pour, lid, and hand off at the pickup counter with common modifications (extra shot, temperature, sweetness).

Simple hot beverages: batch-brewed drip coffee poured to cup, pour-over, hot tea steeped from bag or leaf, chai and matcha lattes, hot chocolate; add milk/lids/sleeves and pass to the customer at the counter.

Cold beverages: iced coffee and cold brew, iced/shaken espresso drinks, iced lattes, iced tea and fruit refreshers - scoop or dispense ice, pour espresso/coffee/tea and milk, add syrup, lid and straw, hand off.

Blended and specialty texture drinks: frappe-style blended coffee, fruit/protein smoothies, bubble tea with tapioca pearls - load cup, dose ingredients and ice, run the blender, top with whipped cream or foam, deliver to pickup.

Peak-rush production: a continuous queue of customized drinks (in-store, mobile-order, and drive-thru) made in sequence at high throughput on a shared bar, sequencing several orders at once and keeping wait times acceptable.

Table and lounge service: carrying finished hot and cold drinks on a tray from the bar to seated guests in a cafe dining room, hotel lobby lounge, or bookstore cafe, and setting them down for the guest.

tasks.label: Take customer orders and convey them to other employees for preparation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Clean service or seating areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-shift table turnover in an indoor cafe seating area: clear cups, plates, lids and trash left by departing customers into a bus tub/trash, wipe the tabletop and chair seats with a sanitizer cloth, push chairs in, brush crumbs off, all while other customers are seated nearby and bags, laptops and strollers occupy the floor.

Cleaning the service counter/espresso bar during the shift: wipe down counters and the pastry-case front, purge and wipe the steam wand, empty the knock box, rinse and wipe drip trays and milk pitchers, mop up small spills behind the bar, and tidy/restock the self-service condiment station (napkins, lids, sleeves) between customer orders.
Floor care in the customer seating area: sweeping or vacuuming crumbs and debris from the dining floor and damp-mopping the open floor area, including responding to a drink spill during the shift.

Closing-time deep clean of the seating area: lift/stack chairs onto tables, clean under tables and along baseboards, sanitize every tabletop, wipe entry-door and window glass, empty and re-line all trash and recycling bins, and haul bags to the outside dumpster.

Outdoor patio or sidewalk seating cleanup: wipe weathered metal tables and chairs, sweep leaves, cigarette butts and litter off the patio surface, empty the outdoor trash bin, and straighten furniture, in wind, sun or rain.

sources.system: pi-0 (Physical Intelligence) on UR5e / bimanual fixed-arm workstations
sources.title: cf0: Our First Generalist Policy
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0 model was fine-tuned to bus a table: an autonomous policy running on fixed robot arms at a table clears dishes, cutlery, cups and trash into a bussing bin and a trash bin, scoring 0.875 on the 'Bussing Hard' evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Table bussing is the clearing half of a barista's table reset: same objects (cups, plates, cutlery, paper trash) on a table surface, same accepted output (bare table, waste sorted).

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 controls a mobile manipulator to clean ... entirely new kitchens and bedrooms, including using a sponge to wipe ..., autonomously, though it does not always succeed ....
sources.transferJustification: Wiping a spill with a sponge and putting dishes in the sink are the same manipulation primitives as wiping a cafe table/counter and clearing crockery; objects and precision are comparable.

sources.title: A VLA that Learns from Experience
sources.claim: The RL-trained pi*0.6 model ran a professional espresso machine autonomously for an entire day (13 hours straight), roughly doubling throughput and halving failure rate versus imitation-only training, at a fixed bimanual coffee-bar workstation.
sources.transferJustification: Espresso drink making at a purpose-built bar station involves the same counter objects and precision as bar cleanup (portafilter handling, pitchers, liquids), and shows sustained worker-like throughput and reliability at a fixtured station.

sources.claim: A Google robotics team demonstrated a mobile manipulator that autonomously plans and executes wiping motions to clean crumbs and spills off tables, validated in simulation and on hardware with zero-shot sim-to-real deployment.
sources.transferJustification: This is the wiping half of the barista table-reset task, on the same object (a table with crumbs and liquid spills) with the same accepted output (a visibly clean, dry surface).

sources.title: 70% of Total Revenue: How Pudu's Commercial Cleaning Robots Became the Core Growth Engine (Interclean)

sources.title: 17 Examples of Robots Being Used in the Hospitality Industry
sources.claim: SoftBank Robotics' Whiz autonomous vacuum is deployed in hotel corridors and lobbies at brands including Marriott and Hilton Garden Inn, with a measured rise in cleanliness scores after deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous vacuuming of public floor areas in a hospitality facility is the same floor-care work a barista does in the seating area, on comparable floor surfaces and traffic conditions.

tasks.label: Prepare or serve menu items, such as sandwiches or salads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Morning rush at a coffeehouse: barista takes a wrapped pre-made breakfast sandwich or panini from the refrigerated case, loads it into the rapid-cook/panini oven, monitors, removes it hot, plates or bags it with a napkin, and hands it over the counter while several tickets queue.

Customer orders a ready-made item from the grab-and-go/display case (boxed salad, wrapped sandwich, parfait): barista retrieves the correct item from the case, bags or plates it, adds utensils, and serves it at the counter.
Made-to-order sandwich or avocado toast at the café prep counter: toast the bread, spread condiment, layer meats/cheese/greens/tomato, season, cut, and plate for the customer.
Salad or grain bowl built to order: portion greens or base into a bowl, add customer-selected toppings, dress and toss, close the container or plate it for pickup.
Back-of-house batch prep during a slow period: slice produce, portion sandwich fillings, assemble and wrap/label sandwiches and salads for the display case, then restock the case.
Café with limited table service: run a plated sandwich or salad from the pass to the customer's table in the seating area and set it down.
