sources.title: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly | AgFunderNews
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI food-assembly arms portion variable ingredients into trays on conveyor lines at multiple food manufacturers, with tens of millions of servings produced in production settings.
sources.transferJustification: Portioning variable fresh ingredients (proteins, grains, vegetables) into a container is the same manipulation and portion-control problem as building a salad bowl or portioning sandwich fillings.

sources.system: Robotic Sandwich Assembly Line (Stäubli TX2-60 HE + Grote)
sources.title: Case study: Robot automates sandwich production | Snack Food & Wholesale Bakery
sources.claim: A Stäubli TX2-60 HE six-axis robot autonomously assembles sandwiches on a Grote production line, placing the top slice on the filled bottom slice and positioning the sandwich for cutting and packaging.
sources.transferJustification: Industrial sandwich assembly handles the same deformable objects (bread, fillings) and the same closing/cutting steps as café sandwich making, but with the work presented on a conveyor rather than a human prep counter.

sources.title: Robot automates sandwich production | The National Provisioner
sources.claim: Grote Company automates production lines that slice, fill ... at industrial throughput, work previously done manually.
sources.transferJustification: Slicing product, portioning fillings and cutting/packing sandwiches is the same batch-prep work a barista does back-of-house, performed on fixtured lines.

sources.title: Miso Robotics Unveils AI-Powered Flippy 2 Robot, Gets Put to Work at White Castle as a Fry Cook - TechEBlog
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy autonomously runs an entire fry station in QSR kitchens — filling, emptying and returning baskets and dispensing cooked food — without employee assistance at peak times.
sources.transferJustification: Loading food into a cooking appliance, timing the cook, unloading it and dispensing it for service is the same loop as toasting a sandwich in a café rapid-cook oven, at comparable food-safety standards.

sources.title: Miso Robotics' Flippy Fry Station robot surpasses 5M baskets | Fast Casual
sources.claim: Flippy fry stations are in commercial service at White Castle, Jack in the ... other chains across seven US states, surpassing five million baskets cooked.

sources.title: PizzaForno rolls out automated vending machines at California colleges | Chain Store Age
sources.claim: PizzaForno automated pizzerias bake and dispense hot pizza to customers in under five minutes, with over 60 units deployed across North America including college campuses.
sources.transferJustification: Retrieving a refrigerated pre-made item, heating it in an oven and delivering it hot to the customer is the same sequence as a café warming a packaged sandwich.

sources.title: Farmer's Fridge – Bridging the gap between fresh and convenient | Food Business News
sources.claim: Farmer's Fridge operates more than 600 automated refrigerated units that store and dispense packaged fresh salads, wraps and bowls to customers in hospitals, airports, offices and universities.
sources.transferJustification: Selecting the customer's chosen packaged salad/wrap from chilled stock and handing it to them is exactly the grab-and-go serving instance, performed by machine in a purpose-built dispensing unit.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm uses computer vision and AI ... and pick individual packaged products out of cluttered containers and place them into designated totes in fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Identifying and picking a specific packaged item from mixed stock and placing it in a container is the manipulation core of retrieving a boxed salad or wrapped sandwich from a case and bagging it, at an E1 goods-to-robot station.

sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated shelves with packaged drinks in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores, with remote operators intervening only for rare errors.
sources.transferJustification: Restocking packaged chilled products in a retail store is the closest E2 analogue to café case work, but it is rail-mounted shelf replenishment from crates, not order-specific retrieval and customer hand-off.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Introduces Servi Q: the Compact Service Robot That Goes Where Others Can't
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi robots autonomously deliver food and bus tables in restaurants, cafés and hotels using LiDAR/camera navigation, without changes to the floor plan, and are deployed in thousands of venues.

sources.title: A robot barista represents a larger vision for bringing robotics to more areas of retail - Modern Retail
sources.claim: At Richtech's own robot café, the ADAM robot autonomously makes and serves the drinks while human workers still prepare the food items and replenish the robot's ingredients.

tasks.label: Wrap, label, or date food items for sale.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Café counter during service: barista uses tongs to take a customer-selected pastry, cookie, muffin or bagel from a mixed display case, drops it into a paper bakery bag or wraps it in deli tissue (sometimes a box for multiples), and hands it over — done in seconds amid a queue, with assorted item shapes and sizes.

Opening/case-prep in the café's back counter area: baked goods arrive loose in bakery boxes or on sheet trays; barista individually wraps or bags some items in cellophane/film, applies product or price stickers, and arranges them on trays in the display case.

Back-of-house prep area and under-counter/walk-in fridge: barista applies day-dot/use-by labels (written or printed) to opened milk cartons, cold-brew and syrup containers, cut fruit, and prepped deli containers, then shelves them in date rotation.

Grab-and-go program: barista assembles or receives sandwiches, wraps or salads, seals them in deli paper/clamshells with a sticker, adds a printed label with contents, price and use-by date, and stocks the cold case.

Retail merchandise: barista weighs and bags whole-bean coffee to order or in advance, seals the bag, and labels it with origin/roast date; also packages cookies or bars into bags/clamshells with price and date labels for the retail shelf.

sources.system: Schubert Flowmodul flow wrapper with pick-and-place robots (La Petite Bretonne installation)
sources.developer: Gerhard Schubert GmbH (installed at La Petite Bretonne)
sources.title: Pick-and-Place Robots, Flow Wrapper, Fuel High-Volume Bakery | Packaging World
sources.claim: A commercial bakery in Quebec runs an installed Schubert line that combines four pick-and-place robots, 3D vision, and a Flowmodul flow wrapper to individually flow-wrap delicate croissants and Danish pastries at high volume — i.e., machine wrapping of baked goods for sale on a purpose-built conveyor line.

sources.system: Syntegon bakery packaging solutions (robotic handling + flow wrapper)
sources.title: Bakery Packaging Machine | For Fresh Products (Syntegon)
sources.claim: Syntegon supplies robotic handling plus flow-wrapping equipment specifically for bakery products of variable size and shape, gently transporting products to the flow wrapper in continuous motion with vision-based quality checks.

sources.system: Bizerba GLM-Ievo / GLM-I weigh price labeller
sources.title: Weigh Price Labeller System GLM-Ievo 100 | Bizerba
sources.claim: Bizerba's GLM weigh-price labelling systems automatically weigh pre-packed food items and print and apply labels (price, weight, and variable data such as dates) to individual packs at up to 100+ packs per minute in food production settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying price/weight/date labels to packed food. Same objects (packaged baked goods, deli packs) and same output (a correctly labelled, dated retail item) as the barista's labelling and dating work.

sources.system: Domino Vx-Series TTO / Ax-Series CIJ / print & apply labelling for bakery
sources.title: Uncovering the best coding and marking solutions for the bakery industry | Domino
sources.claim: Date and batch coding of bakery items — including cakes and biscuits in trays or wrappers — is routinely performed inline by thermal-transfer overprinters, inkjet coders and print-and-apply labellers integrated into packaging lines.

sources.system: Weber/Bluhm Legi-Air 4050 print-and-apply labellers at Coop Schafisheim bakery
sources.title: Coop – Labelling in Switzerland's largest bakery | Weber Marking
sources.claim: Switzerland's largest bakery distribution centre (Coop, Schafisheim) uses installed Bluhm/Weber Legi-Air print-and-apply systems that automatically print and apply labels carrying best-before dates in continuous operation, at up to 80 labels per minute on product surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic printing and application of date labels in a bakery facility. Same act (generate a date and affix a compliant label to a food unit) that the barista performs with day-dots and use-by stickers.

sources.system: Chef Robotics meal-assembly robots (with ILPRA tray sealer)
sources.title: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly | AgFunderNews
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-driven arms are deployed on production lines at food manufacturers (Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Chef Bombay, Cafe Spice), autonomously portioning ingredients into trays; the company also partners with ILPRA so the filled trays are automatically sealed and packaged.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning food into retail containers that are then sealed and labelled inline. Comparable objects (sandwich/salad/deli portions in clamshells and trays) and the same accepted output — a sealed, dated grab-and-go pack.

sources.title: Coffee Bagging Equipment | Tinsley Company
sources.claim: Coffee bagging equipment that automatically weighs, fills and seals retail pouches of whole bean or ground coffee is sold commercially, and such machines commonly integrate date stamping of pack details.

sources.system: Bakisto (FANUC cobot + WIESHEU oven + Wanzl BakeOff i)
sources.title: Robots in the Bakery | International Federation of Robotics
sources.claim: The most advanced in-store retail bakery robot demonstrated to date, 'Bakisto', is a purpose-built cell (cobot on rails with a dedicated oven, trolley and AI display unit) that loads trays and stocks display compartments in supermarkets; it does not wrap, label or date items, and remains a prototype.

sources.title: Breadbot baking machines debut in North Idaho | KREM
sources.claim: The BreadBot, a fully automated bread-making machine deployed in grocery stores, still relies on store employees to retrieve, slice and bag the finished loaves — the wrapping/bagging step in the retail setting is not automated.

sources.title: Physical AI and Humanoids Lead Automate 2026 | Packaging World
sources.claim: As of mid-2026, trade press covering the largest US automation show reports that humanoid, general-purpose robots — the class that would be needed to work at a human café counter without purpose-built fixturing — are not yet ready for production deployment.

tasks.label: Check temperatures of freezers, refrigerators, or heating equipment to ensure proper functioning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Opening/closing-shift round of front-of-house refrigeration: barista walks the bar line and reads the external digital readouts on under-counter milk fridges, the reach-in fridge/freezer and the cold pastry case, compares each to the required range, and records the readings in a paper or tablet temperature log.

Units with no external readout: barista opens the fridge or freezer door (magnetic gasket, low under-counter or reach-in door), reads the hanging/interior thermometer or takes an interior air reading, closes the door quickly to limit warming, and logs the value.

Hot-side equipment: reads the espresso machine boiler pressure/temperature gauge or PID display, the hot-water tower, the oven/panini press/hot-holding case thermometer, confirms each is at operating temperature before service, and records it.

Back-of-house walk-in cooler/freezer check: reads the exterior wall-mounted digital thermometer, visually checks for ice build-up, condensation, a defrost cycle or a door left ajar, occasionally stepping inside to read the interior thermometer, and logs the result.

Out-of-range event: re-verifies the reading with a second/handheld thermometer, adjusts the thermostat dial or resets the unit, relocates or discards affected milk and food, notifies the shift manager, and writes the corrective action into the log.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with thermal payload / Orbit inspection software
sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot's inspection software provides an end-to-end thermal inspection workflow that autonomously captures equipment temperatures on scheduled missions and triggers notifications when equipment exceeds preset ... — the same read-compare-alert loop as a fridge/heater temperature check.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine equipment temperature/gauge inspection rounds. Transfer: the physical act is identical — approach fixed equipment at a waypoint, obtain a temperature value, compare it to an allowed range, and record/alert; the targets (equipment surfaces and instrument faces) and reading precision are comparable to café refrigeration and hot-holding checks.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / AB InBev Leuven brewery
sources.title: Energy Savings and Predictive Maintenance at AB InBev's Largest European Brewery | Boston Dynamics case study
sources.claim: Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds inside a working brewery (a food-and-beverage production facility), using a thermal camera to find overheating equipment and automatically generating alerts and work orders for staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled thermal inspection of production equipment in a food/beverage facility. Transfer: same objects (motors, gearboxes, plant equipment whose temperature must stay in range), same output (a logged reading plus an out-of-range alert to staff), and an institution-controlled facility comparable to a café's back-of-house.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot fleets autonomously navigate recorded inspection missions and collect data on large numbers of industrial assets in factories and other facilities, showing routine autonomous inspection rounds are a deployed, at-scale capability rather than a one-off demo.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility inspection rounds. Transfer: establishes that repeated, unattended visit-and-read rounds at fixed instrument locations are reliably executed in institution-controlled facilities, which is the navigation and repeatability requirement of a barista's fridge/freezer/heater temperature round.

sources.system: Levatas AI Inspections models running on Spot and other mobile robots
sources.title: AI Inspections - Levatas.com
sources.claim: Computer-vision inspection models deployed on mobile robots such as Spot read analog gauges and digital meters and detect thermal anomalies, so numeric refrigerator/freezer display readings can be captured automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated meter/gauge reading on inspection robots. Transfer: a refrigerator or hot-case thermometer is a digital meter or analog dial of the same kind these models read, and the required output (a numeric value compared to a set range) is identical.

sources.title: ANYmal - Autonomous Robotic Inspection Solution - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYmal is a commercially available autonomous inspection quadruped whose standard payload takes precise non-contact temperature readings across a wide range while executing autonomous data-collection routes in complex facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous thermal inspection of plant equipment. Transfer: the −40 °C to 550 °C non-contact range spans freezer, refrigerator and hot-holding/espresso equipment temperatures, and the robot performs the readings on autonomous routes in institution-controlled facilities.

sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Autonomous door opening by Spot's arm during inspection missions exists only as a beta feature for building doors; other arm manipulation such as turning valves and flipping levers is offered only semi-autonomously with an operator in the loop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot manipulation of facility controls and doors. Relevant as a limit: opening appliance doors and adjusting thermostats during an unattended round is not substantiated as autonomous, so instances requiring those acts cannot be credited.

tasks.label: Take out garbage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Closing or mid-shift trash run at a standalone coffee shop: pull the full liner from the behind-counter and lobby cans (heavy, wet with milk, ice, syrup and liquid cups), cinch and tie it, carry it through the back room and out the rear door to the dumpster in the alley or parking lot, hoist it over a chest-high lid, then fit a fresh liner in each can.

Cardboard and recycling: break down milk/cup/bean shipping boxes, stack them, and haul flattened cardboard plus a recycling bin of bottles and cans out to the recycling dumpster or baler corral behind the shop.
Wet waste: empty the espresso knock box and the coffee-grounds bucket, plus the food-waste/compost bin, into the organics dumpster outside; heavy sloppy load, then rinse the bucket or bin.

Cafe located inside a mall food court, airport terminal, campus or hospital: tied bags go into a wheeled cart or bin and are rolled down interior service corridors, sometimes via a service elevator, to a trash room or compactor and dumped there.

Trash handled during service hours with customers present: swap the liner in the lobby or patio can, pick up litter and abandoned cups around the patio, and carry the bag out through the seating area and sidewalk to the bin.

Problem cases: a bag leaks or splits and must be double-bagged with the drip trail mopped up, broken glass or a spilled ice bin must be handled, or the dumpster is overfull, blocked by a parked car, or padlocked and the waste must be compressed, redistributed or staged; often at night or in rain, ice or snow.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: A 2026 assessment of autonomous robot capabilities classifies 'take out the trash' (remove bag from bin, close it, navigate to an outdoor bin, deposit it) as showing significant limits in lab: no robot has demonstrated removing a ... or closing a bag.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: the assessment's task definition (remove a trash bag from its bin, close it, carry it to an outdoor bin) is the barista trash run minus liner replacement.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: Loki's wheeled cleaning robot has carried a trash bag out of a building using an elevator and has run shifts in corporate/campus facilities, but it has one arm, cannot close the bag, runs about ten times slower than a ..., and relies on remote teleoperation for many edge cases.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task (bagged waste removed from an occupied building), cited as a negative: teleoperation-assisted, one-armed, and far below worker speed.

sources.title: Loki Robotics on X: a day in the life of a Loki deployed in a commercial office space
sources.claim: Loki states its building-cleaning robots combine autonomy with remote teleoperation ... in commercial office space.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (janitorial waste and cleaning rounds in an occupied building); establishes the deployment is not fully autonomous.

sources.title: Tesla's Optimus robot takes out trash, vacuums, cleans like a pro
sources.claim: Tesla's Optimus humanoid was shown picking up a trash bag, ... dropping the bag in, staged in a controlled training warehouse; Tesla's autonomy claims for Optimus demos have been publicly disputed.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act as the dumpster step, but autonomy is unestablished and the demo was staged in a controlled warehouse, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots pick up, transport and drop ... heavy waste carts through hospital corridors to trash compactors and utility rooms; a five-robot fleet at Froedtert Hospital moved millions of pounds of trash in 2024. Humans still load the carts and dump them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: waste haulage inside a structured facility. It covers only the transport leg; bin emptying, bag handling and dumping into the compactor remain human work.

sources.title: C&D Waste | Sorting Bulky Waste | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker robots autonomously grasp bulky, heavy mixed waste weighing up to 40 kg off a sorting line and place it into target containers, running unmanned around the clock in commercial waste facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy mixed-waste handling. Objects (bagged and loose refuse, cardboard, wood, bottles) and precision (grasp, then drop into a container) match the dumpster step once waste is presented at a fixed station in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Business Talk AI: Let's talk about Artificial Intelligence for recycling with AMP Robotics
sources.claim: AMP Cortex robotic sorting systems autonomously identify, pick and place mixed waste and recyclables at 80-120 picks per minute with up ... in material recovery facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling cafe-type refuse (cups, bottles, cans, cardboard) in a purpose-built line, showing that moving this waste into the correct container is reliably automated when material is conveyed to the machine.

sources.system: MACPAL ABB Robotic Palletizer for Bags
sources.title: ABB Robotic Palletizer for Bags, Fully Assembled - Mesh Automation
sources.claim: Commercially sold robotic palletizing cells pick filled, soft-sided sacks with shifting contents at up to 25 kg per ... place them accurately, operating inside light-curtain-protected cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and depositing a heavy, floppy filled bag. Weight, deformability and placement precision match hoisting a tied refuse bag into a container when the bag is presented at a fixed pick point.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR autonomously cleans commercial restrooms, including picking up trash, and is deployed in hospitals and airports with near-zero staff intervention over eight- to sixteen-hour shifts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: janitorial work inside a structured facility; shows litter pickup is automated in E2 settings, but it does not empty bins, tie liners, or transport bags to a dumpster.

tasks.label: Describe menu items to customers, or suggest products that might appeal to them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Demonstrate the use of retail equipment, such as espresso machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Behind the bar of a café, showing a newly hired barista how to run the espresso machine and grinder: purge the group, dose and level the basket, tamp, lock in the portafilter, watch the shot, steam and texture milk, then hand over and correct the trainee's grip, tamp pressure and pitcher angle over repeated attempts.

At the counter during service, a customer asks how the drink is made; the barista operates the espresso machine and grinder in the customer's view, narrating grind size, dose, extraction time and milk steaming while finishing the order.

On the retail floor of a coffee shop that sells brewing gear, demonstrating merchandise for sale to a shopper: a home espresso machine, burr grinder, French press, AeroPress or pour-over kit — handling the display unit, brewing a sample, explaining settings, descaling/cleaning and comparing models while answering questions.

Showing staff (or a franchisee/relief shift lead) end-of-day equipment maintenance: backflushing with detergent, pulling and scrubbing group screens and baskets, purging and wiping the steam wand, emptying and calibrating the grinder, changing water filters.

Scheduled public demonstration for an audience in a controlled venue — an in-store tasting/latte-art demo or a vendor booth at a trade show or convention — running the equipment while spectators watch, handing out samples and taking questions.

Offsite pop-up demonstration at a farmers market, street festival or catering event: gear set up on folding tables under a tent, variable power, weather and crowd, brewing and showing methods to passersby.

sources.title: Scaling craft coffee: How ClickHouse powers Artly's barista bots
sources.claim: Artly's Barista Bot is a fully autonomous robotic arm barista deployed in commercial coffee locations, performing the full espresso workflow (grind, tamp, steam, pour, latte art).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing espresso drinks. Operating the espresso machine and grinder in front of an onlooker is the physical core of demonstrating that equipment; the objects (portafilter, pitcher, cups), precision and café setting are identical.

sources.title: Artly Coffee: The Barista Bot
sources.claim: Developer description of the Barista Bot's equipment-handling repertoire: grinding, tamping, steaming and pouring at expert precision.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: the manual steps a barista performs when showing how the machine is used are the steps the arm executes.

sources.title: The Robot Barista at Muji Has Sparked a Surprising Amount of Debate - Vancouver Magazine
sources.claim: An Artly robot barista works an open coffee counter inside a public MUJI retail store, making drinks for shoppers who watch it operate.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the environment: a human-facing retail store counter (E2), not a fenced cell, with customers watching the machine being operated.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics debuts robot-run cafe in Las Vegas
sources.claim: Richtech's ADAM robot barista runs the Clouffee & Tea café in Las Vegas, detecting customers, conversing, taking spoken orders and preparing/serving beverages.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: customer-facing drink preparation with spoken interaction. Supports the narrated, in-view operation of coffee equipment that a counter-side demonstration to a curious customer consists of.

sources.title: A robot barista represents a larger vision for bringing robotics to more areas of retail - Modern Retail
sources.claim: ADAM units are leased for events and conventions, and Richtech has fielded hundreds of robots across the US.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: staffing an event beverage station. Shows the same autonomous drink-making performed in front of an audience at convention venues, the setting of an in-venue demonstration.

sources.title: Artly debuts mini Barista Bot at National Restaurant Association 2025 show | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Artly's mini Barista Bot performed espresso drink preparation and latte art on the trade-show floor at the 2025 National Restaurant Association show; the product is aimed at coffee shops, event venues and restaurants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: booth beverage service before spectators. A public brewing/latte-art demonstration for an audience consists of running the equipment while onlookers watch, which is what the bot does at the show.

sources.title: We Can't Stop Thinking About These Five Things From the 2024 Specialty Coffee Expo - Fresh Cup Magazine
sources.claim: At the 2024 Specialty Coffee Expo, Wingman Cobot's robotic barista arms brewed coffee and espresso drinks for watching attendees at the vendor booth.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trade-show beverage preparation. Confirms multiple commercial robot baristas operating espresso equipment as a watched demonstration inside a controlled exhibition hall.

tasks.label: Order, receive, or stock supplies or retail products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-shift replenishment of the bar and counter during service: refill cup/lid/sleeve/straw stacks, napkins and the condiment station, swap in fresh milk jugs at the under-counter fridge, replace empty syrup/sauce bottles, restock to-go bags and stir sticks — done in a narrow aisle behind the espresso bar with customers queued and coworkers moving past.

Restock the refrigerated grab-and-go case with bottled and canned beverages and packaged drinks brought out of the walk-in cooler in crates/cases: pull forward remaining stock, load new bottles/cans, face labels out.

Stock the pastry/food display case and self-serve bakery shelves at open or after a bake: move baked goods from delivery trays or the freezer onto plates, tiers and shelves with tongs/gloves, arrange the display, label, and pull or rotate day-old product.

Receive a delivery: meet the driver at the back/side door or curb, count cases and crates against the invoice/packing slip, check for damage and cold-chain issues, sign for the load, then hand-truck or carry the cases through the store into the stockroom and walk-in.

Put away and organize back-of-house stock: break down cases of beans, cups, lids, syrups and paper goods onto stockroom shelves, stack milk crates in the walk-in, rotate stock FIFO, date-label, and consolidate partial cases in a cramped, variably arranged storeroom.

Count inventory to par and place the order: walk the bar, stockroom and walk-in counting whole and partial cases, milk, pastries and retail merchandise, note shortages, then enter counts and submit the order to the distribution center or vendor on a tablet/portal.

sources.title: Telexistence to install AI re-stocking robots in 300 convenience stores across Japan
sources.claim: TX SCARA, a rail-mounted AI restocking robot, was commercially deployed to 300 FamilyMart convenience stores in ... to replenish chilled beverage display shelves with bottles and cans from crates, running autonomously with rare remote VR-based error recovery.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class as a barista restocking a chilled retail display: standardized bottles/cans taken from crates and placed onto refrigerated display shelves inside a retailer-controlled store.

sources.title: Telexistence and Physical Intelligence Announce Partnership to Automate Drink-Restocking Operations in Retail Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's successor robot TX Ghost has been ... automating the majority of drink-restocking work, with remote teleoperation retained only for unpredictable error recovery; pilots expanded to 7-Eleven stores in Tokyo in September 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Restocking chilled retail beverage displays from backroom crates is the same handling task and object set as a barista restocking a grab-and-go cooler.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cartons from trailers and containers onto conveyors in DHL warehouses; commercially deployed since 2023, with units running case unloading across three countries as of June 2025 at about 700 cases per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Receiving a delivery is, at the machine-presented (E1) form, exactly carton unloading from a docked trailer onto a conveyor for put-away; comparable box sizes and weights to café case deliveries.

sources.title: How Fox Robotics went from scrappy startup to making self-driving forklifts for Walmart
sources.claim: Walmart deployed 19 FoxBot autonomous forklifts across ... to unload trailers at the shipping and receiving dock without a human driver.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the transport half of receiving a delivery — moving incoming palletized goods off the vehicle into the facility — in a purpose-fitted dock configuration.

sources.title: Walmart plans to automate 25 distribution centers with Symbotic
sources.claim: Symbotic's system, deployed in Walmart regional distribution centers, uses machine vision to audit inbound inventory, robotic arms to depalletize cases, and autonomous mobile robots to put each case away at a system-determined storage location.
sources.transferJustification: Stockroom put-away is case-level receiving, verification and storage with location and rotation control — the same operation Symbotic performs autonomously in a purpose-built structure.

sources.title: Simbe scales inventory robotics deal with BJ’s Wholesale Club
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomous inventory robot is deployed chainwide at BJ's Wholesale Club (237-244 stores), scanning shelves to count stock and generate replenishment and restocking guidance including expiration-based suggestions.
sources.transferJustification: The physical part of ordering supplies is counting stock on hand against par and producing the replenishment order; Tally performs that count autonomously on standardized retail racking.

sources.system: ABB IRB 360 FlexPicker with PickMaster vision (CKF Systems integration)
sources.title: High-speed robots pick and pack fragile snacks
sources.claim: Vision-guided ABB IRB 360 FlexPicker delta robots with PickMaster vision are installed on food manufacturers' packing lines, picking fragile food items off a moving conveyor and placing them into packs at high rate under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Filling holders and display trays with baked goods, cups, lids and packaged items — when the supply is presented on a conveyor and destinations are fixed — is the same vision-guided pick-and-place of food-grade items these cells run in production.

tasks.label: Serve prepared foods, such as muffins, biscotti, or bagels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Café counter service: a customer points at a specific muffin, scone or biscotti in the open display case; the barista uses tongs/deli tissue to select that exact item, bags it or plates it with a napkin, and hands it across the counter during a queue.

Warm-and-serve: bagel sliced and run through the toaster, croissant or breakfast sandwich warmed in the small oven/panini press; the hot item is wrapped or plated with butter/cream-cheese cups and handed over or called out at the hand-off bar.

Pre-packaged grab-and-go: wrapped biscotti, muffin, protein box or yogurt parfait pulled from a case or shelf, bagged with the drink, order accuracy checked, handed to the customer at the counter or drive-thru window.

Table service in the café seating area: the plated pastry or warmed food is carried on a tray from the counter to the seated guest's table (with utensils/napkin) in a full-service or hotel-lobby café.
Custom handling on request: slice a loaf cake or cut a bagel/sandwich in half, split an item onto two plates, use fresh gloves/separate tongs for an allergy request, unwrap and portion for a child.
Mobile coffee cart or catering pop-up at an outdoor event, farmers market or office lobby: pastries served out of bakery boxes and crates on a folding table, improvised layout, weather and crowding.

sources.title: Here's What's Up With the Cookie Shot Robot at Caesars Palace | Vital Vegas
sources.claim: RoboChef SmartKiosk, a robotic-arm kiosk deployed at Dominique Ansel Bakery in Caesars Palace, holds an inventory of delicate ... bakery items and dispenses a finished item to each customer order.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: retrieving a specific delicate baked good from stored inventory and delivering it to a paying customer on order, in a retail bakery.

sources.title: Smart Kiosk - Commercial Fryer Robot for Restaurants (RoboChef)
sources.claim: RoboChef describes Smart Kiosk as a fully automated self-service food ... running customer orders with no staff intervention, citing pastry service at Dominique Ansel Las Vegas and sandwich service at another site.

sources.title: Le Bread Xpress and Canteen Vending Services to Install Bake Xpress Micro-Bakeries Nationwide - Perishable News
sources.claim: Bake Xpress robotic micro-bakery machines store, bake and deliver croissants, quiche, pastries, pizza and sandwiches to customers; piloted in universities, corporate break rooms and manufacturing sites and rolled out with Canteen vending services.

sources.title: New Bake Xpress Robot Vending Machine Makes Croissants and Pizzas – The Spoon
sources.claim: Inside Bake Xpress each pastry/sandwich box is barcoded and stored at a known location; on order the machine retrieves the box and heats the ... before delivering it to the customer.
sources.transferJustification: Directly analogous to warming a bagel or croissant to order and handing the hot item to the patron: same objects, same heat-and-serve output.

sources.title: Storage, Cooking, Delivery | PizzaForno Documentation
sources.claim: PizzaForno automated kiosks hold refrigerated prepared food, mechanically load it with its box into a convection oven and deliver the hot boxed item to the customer; indoor units are sited in transit hubs, cafeterias, hospitals and dorms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (heat-and-serve prepared food to a walk-up customer); comparable objects (boxed baked food), comparable precision, and unattended indoor/outdoor siting.

sources.title: Automated pizzeria adds 39 U.S. locations through the first half of 2024 | Vending Market Watch
sources.claim: PizzaForno's automated kiosks are commercially deployed at scale in the US, adding 39 US locations in the first half of 2024, including relocatable outdoor units that fit a standard parking space.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment scale and maturity of unattended heat-and-serve food kiosks, including outdoor siting relevant to event/cart service.

sources.title: FANUC Relieves the Heat for In-store Bakeries (FANUC case study)
sources.claim: A FANUC CRX cobot with 3D vision and food-grade printed grippers, integrated by ASA Automation for WIESHEU, picks randomly positioned baked goods from crates, loads baking trays, and transfers baked goods to customer-facing sales racks in in-store bakeries, working unguarded beside staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (handling individual baked goods without damaging them and placing them where patrons buy them); same object class as muffins and bagels and the same gentleness requirement.

sources.title: Robots in the Bakery | International Federation of Robotics case study
sources.claim: The FANUC/WIESHEU/Wanzl 'Bakisto' in-store bakery robot system, which loads trays, works the oven and stocks the displays, was shown as a prototype at EuroShop 2023 rather than as a fielded product.
sources.transferJustification: Same object class and setting (retail bakery display stocking); cited to bound the maturity of in-store baked-goods handling.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi robots autonomously transport food and run drinks across restaurant, café and hotel dining rooms in commercial deployments, with staff loading and unloading the trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (running prepared food and drinks to seated guests in a dining room); the objects (plated food on trays) and the venue match café table service.

sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocking robots operate autonomously in 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, restocking refrigerated shelves with bottles ..., with remote human takeover only in rare failure cases.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous manipulation of packaged retail food items inside a store built for people); cited to test whether E2 in-store handling extends to serving patrons.

tasks.label: Stock customer service stations with paper products or beverage preparation items.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-shift top-off of the customer self-serve condiment station in a café lobby: refilling napkin dispensers with compressed stacks, sugar/sweetener/stirrer caddies, lid holders by size, cup sleeves and straws, swapping the half-and-half carafe, all while customers stand at and reach across the bar; the barista judges by eye what is low, fetches stock from an under-counter cabinet, and wipes spills.

Restocking the behind-the-bar beverage preparation station during service: cup stacks by size into wells, lids, sleeves, syrup bottles onto rails, milk jugs from the under-counter fridge, tea bags, pitchers and pumps, in a cramped aisle shared with two or three coworkers moving quickly through a rush.

Opening or closing full replenishment to par: pulling cases from the stockroom or walk-in on a cart, box-cutting cartons open, breaking down and disposing of cardboard, loading backup bins and dispensers for cups, lids, napkins, bags, carriers and paper goods across all stations.

Drive-thru or mobile-order handoff station restock: bags, drink carriers, straws, napkins, lids, stoppers and condiment packets kept within arm's reach in a narrow booth, refilled repeatedly during peak with cars queued and orders continuing.

Satellite/self-serve coffee station in a hotel lobby, hospital cafeteria, campus dining hall or airport kiosk: rolling a supply cart to a stand away from the main bar, swapping and refilling airpots, refilling creamers, sugars, cups, lids, and napkins, and tidying the counter.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: TX SCARA is a fixed AI restocking robot deployed in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores that autonomously moves bottled and canned drinks from delivery crates onto refrigerated display shelves, with remote teleoperated recovery only on errors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing a customer-facing beverage display in a retail store. It is the closest deployed analogue to stocking a service station, but it handles only rigid bottles and cans presented in standard crates at one fixed, purpose-installed cooler location, not paper products, packets or dispenser cartridges on a café counter.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's robot runs autonomously in normal operation, with a remote operator taking over only after a drop or misplacement.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (retail beverage shelf replenishment); cited to establish autonomy level rather than a new capability.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm works inside fenced fulfillment-center robotics cells, autonomously detecting and transferring individual diverse consumer products out of containers and into specified totes at production scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: single-item pick-and-place of heterogeneous packaged goods (sachets, small cartons, poly-bagged paper goods) from a presented container into a designated receptacle — the same motion and object class as transferring packets, sleeves, lids and cups from stock into holders when the work is fixtured in a cell.

sources.system: ValTara PKR-Dual Delta Robot case packing cell
sources.title: Paxiom's ValTara introduces a Dual Delta Robot Pick-and-Place Case Packer

sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-rate placement of sugar-packet-like sachets, pouches and small cartons from a fixtured infeed into a target container — mechanically the same as loading condiment packets, stirrer sleeves and paper goods into caddies when the caddy is presented as a fixture.

sources.title: Warehouse Robots & Cobots for Fulfillment & Distribution | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC sells warehouse robotic cells in which a robot autonomously cuts inbound boxes open after scanning, as part of automated case handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening shipping cartons with a blade under machine control — the case-cutting step of a bulk par restock, performed on cartons presented on a conveyor in a fenced cell.

sources.title: AutoCase | End-to-end automated case handling for AutoStore
sources.claim: AutoStore's AutoCase product automates opening inbound cartons and decanting their contents into bins within a robotic goods-storage installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unpacking cases of goods and transferring the contents into destination containers — the core of a bulk stockroom-to-par replenishment when the cases are brought to the machine.

sources.title: CES 2025: Artly the Robot Barista Uses AI and Motion Capture Technology
sources.claim: Artly's Barista Bot is a robotic-arm coffee cell operating at multiple retail locations, handling cups through the full drink cycle; humans, not the robot, restock its consumables.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling of cups and lids from fixtured dispensers inside a purpose-built beverage cell, showing that cup/lid manipulation at a beverage station is solved when the station is engineered around the machine (and that these kiosks are themselves restocked by people).

tasks.label: Set up or restock product displays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restocking the bakery/pastry display case in a café: carrying trays of unwrapped croissants, muffins, cookies and scones from back-of-house, rotating older product forward, arranging items with tongs on parchment-lined trays or plates inside a countertop or refrigerated case, wiping crumbs, and setting price/allergen cards, often mid-shift with customers queued.

Restocking the grab-and-go refrigerated merchandiser: loading bottled/canned drinks, packaged sandwiches, yogurt parfaits and fruit cups into the reach-in case, pulling expired product, rotating FIFO and facing labels forward.

Restocking retail shelving and counter displays with packaged merchandise: bags of whole-bean coffee, boxed tea, mugs, tumblers, syrup bottles and snack bars; opening cases in the back, carrying stock out, filling gaps, facing and straightening product on standard store shelves.

Setting up a new seasonal or promotional display: building/positioning a display table, tiered riser or cardboard unit per the corporate planogram, filling it with product, adding signage, sample cups and price cards, usually before opening or at a promotion changeover.

Restocking the customer self-serve condiment/supply station: reloading cup and lid dispensers, sleeves, napkins, stir sticks, sugar and sweetener caddies, milk carafes, and straightening the station during service.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA rail-mounted robot arm autonomously restocks refrigerated beverage display shelves inside working convenience stores, with remote human takeover only when the AI fails.

sources.title: Robots deployed for re-stocking shelves in convenient stores | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: TX SCARA was mass-produced for 300 FamilyMart stores and can autonomously replenish up to 1,000 bottles and ... in refrigerated display shelves.

sources.title: Telexistence Expands Beverage Shelf-Stocking Service with "TX Ghost" Robots
sources.claim: Telexistence extended its beverage shelf-stocking service with a newer TX Ghost robot, in pilot operation at selected 7-Eleven stores in Tokyo; the company builds both remote-controlled and AI-driven robots, so autonomy of this unit is not established.

sources.system: Chef Robotics piece-picking / baked goods tray assembly

It transfers to arranging a pastry display because the objects are the same class of fragile unwrapped baked goods, placement must meet visual presentation standards, and the destination is a tray - but only where product and tray are presented to a fixtured cell.

sources.title: Robotic Case Packer Handles Petfood Cups | Packaging World
sources.claim: A Cama robotic case-packing system at Simmons Foods picks cups and varied product shapes and places them into shelf-ready retail display cases and grooved trays on a packaging line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading product into shelf-ready display cases. It transfers to filling a merchandising display and to handling stacked cups because the objects (cups, rigid containers) and the required ordered placement into a display tray match, given the tray is fixtured and product presented.

sources.system: Fallas Model D3-LV retail-ready robotic case packer
sources.title: Automated case packing handles 450 bags/min at Pepperidge Farm | Packaging World
sources.claim: A Fallas retail-ready robotic case packer at Pepperidge Farm picks bagged product off a conveyor and loads it into shelf-ready display trays at production speed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading bagged consumer goods into shelf-ready display trays. It transfers to restocking bagged coffee onto a display because the objects (flexible retail bags) and the ordered, faced placement are comparable, when the display is fixtured and bags are presented on a conveyor.

sources.system: Mobile manipulator autonomous supermarket stocking system

sources.claim: A ROS2 mobile-manipulator system for autonomous supermarket shelf stocking achieved over 98% pick-and-place success in laboratory conditions replicating a supermarket, using ArUco markers for shelf alignment, but the authors state current autonomous systems remain inferior ... human workers.

sources.title: Galbot brings in $300M to scale mobile manipulator deployments - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Galbot's G1 wheeled mobile manipulator staffs autonomous 'Galbot Store' retail units in over 30 Chinese cities; the company says the robot is designed to automate inventory, replenishment, delivery and packaging, but no independent demonstration of in-store shelf replenishment at worker quality is given.

tasks.label: Weigh, grind, or pack coffee beans for customers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Customer buys a pre-packaged 12 oz/1 lb retail bag of whole beans at the café counter and asks for it ground for a home brewer (drip, French press, pour-over). Barista opens the bag, sets the burr grinder to the requested coarseness, empties the beans into the hopper, grinds, returns the grounds to the same bag, folds/reseals the tin-tie and hands it over — done between drink orders at a busy counter.

Bulk-bin sale: barista scoops whole beans from a gravity bin or bulk hopper, weighs to the customer's requested amount (e.g., half pound, one pound) on a tared digital scale, funnels them into a kraft valve bag, folds/seals it and writes or applies an origin/roast-date/price label at the retail counter.

Back-of-house batch pre-packing during slow periods at a café or roaster-café: barista weighs coffee from bulk totes into 20–50 retail bags, fills, heat-seals or tin-ties them, applies date/origin labels and stocks the retail shelf.

Large order for an office, catering or wholesale customer: weigh out several pounds, grind the whole quantity to a specified setting (drip or urn grind), and pack into multiple labelled bags for pickup or delivery.

Non-standard requests: grinding a customer's own beans brought from elsewhere, filling a customer's reusable jar or container with tare, very fine Turkish or very coarse cold-brew grinds requiring purging and cleaning the grinder between orders, or small sample amounts.

sources.system: Viking Masek VFFS and rotary premade pouch coffee packaging machines with multihead/auger fillers
sources.title: The essential guide to coffee packaging machines :: Viking Masek
sources.claim: Commercially sold rotary premade-pouch and vertical form-fill-seal coffee packaging machines automatically meter a weighed dose of whole bean or ground coffee (via multi-head scales or augers) into a bag and seal it, in roastery packaging lines.

sources.claim: Automatic weigh-and-fill scales for coffee dose beans or ground coffee to a preset target weight (e.g., 250 g or 1 kg) and release the portion into a bag; in Load-Pack-Seal configurations weighing, filling and sealing are connected with no manual handling, with date printing available.

sources.system: Fully automated coffee packing machines; SOVDA Precision Fill
sources.title: How to Scale Coffee Packing Capacity in 2026 — SOVDA
sources.claim: Coffee packing equipment maker states that fully automated packing machines form, fill and seal every bag without a human, and that its weighing filler holds each bag to within ±2 grams — the accuracy and output a retail bag requires.

sources.system: Robotiq palletizing solution on Universal Robots UR10e cobots at Cascade Coffee
sources.developer: Robotiq / Universal Robots / Olympus Controls (integrator), user Cascade Coffee

sources.claim: A coffee co-packing plant runs six Universal Robots UR10e cobot palletizing cells handling its 12-oz, 20-oz and 2-lb retail coffee bags (as cases) after packaging, in production since about 2023-2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line robotic handling of the same packed retail coffee bags. It shows robots working reliably on this exact product in a purpose-built coffee packaging plant, supporting that the weighing/filling/sealing stages they feed from are machine-completed at commercial quality.

sources.system: Turnkey coffee grinding and packing production lines (industrial grinders + automatic bag fillers + heat sealing/labeling)

sources.claim: Integrated commercial coffee plant lines chain industrial grinders set to a chosen fineness directly into automatic filling, sealing, labeling and date-printing of whole-bean or ground bags.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grinding coffee to a requested fineness and packing it into retail bags is the same physical operation a barista performs for a customer's grind request, on the same product and to the same output (a sealed labelled bag of ground coffee).

sources.title: Sovda Launches the Precision Fill Mini Coffee Bagging Machine — Daily Coffee News
sources.claim: Benchtop weigh-and-fill baggers sized for small roasteries and café back rooms remain semi-automated: the machine weighs and drops the dose while a person holds the bag and triggers a foot pedal, and then seals it.
sources.transferJustification: Same task at café/small-roastery scale; cited only as context showing human bag handling is still required at that scale, not to support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Create signs to advertise store products or events.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily/weekly specials board inside the café: barista wipes down the counter or wall chalkboard menu and re-letters it with liquid chalk markers — drink of the day, seasonal latte name, price, a small doodle or border — standing on the floor behind the bar while the shop is open and customers are present.

Sidewalk A-frame promo board: barista draws a colorful hand-lettered chalk panel ("Try our new cold brew ...", event date) on the A-frame or a removable insert board, then sets it out on the public sidewalk at open and brings it in at close, weather permitting.

Small point-of-sale cards: hand-printed pastry-case labels, price tags for retail bean bags, and table tent cards for a new item; written on card stock or mini chalk tags at the back counter and slotted into holders, clips, or the display case.

Printed flyer/poster for an event or promotion (open-mic night, holiday hours, new seasonal drink): laid out on the shop's computer, printed on the shop printer, trimmed, and taped or pinned to the door, window, corkboard, or register area.

Installing a roaster/corporate point-of-purchase kit that arrives in a box: peeling and applying window clings, sliding posters into existing frames, clipping menu-board strips, setting table tents, and stripping out the previous promotion's materials, following a planogram sheet.
Updating a changeable letter board or grooved letter menu: pulling old plastic/vinyl letters, sorting them, and inserting new letters to spell out the current special or event announcement.

sources.claim: Roland VersaSTUDIO BN2 desktop printer/cutters print and contour-cut finished signs, posters, decals, labels and stickers in one machine, with media loaded into the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: producing the physical printed promotional sign, poster, window decal or price label that the barista would otherwise print and trim by hand.

sources.claim: Scribit is a commercially shipped write-and-erase robot that hangs from two anchor points on a smooth vertical surface and autonomously draws uploaded or generated content such as a restaurant's daily menu on that dedicated wall.

tasks.label: Slice fruits, vegetables, desserts, or meats for use in food service.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Café prep station before/during service: barista slices citrus and other fruit for beverage garnishes, infused water, fruit cups and smoothie/bowl toppings (lemons, oranges, limes, strawberries, bananas, occasionally avocado), on a cutting board with a chef's knife, in small on-demand batches; ripeness and size vary, slices must look presentable.

Pastry case work: portioning baked goods and desserts — cutting whole cakes into wedges, loaf cakes/banana bread into slices, brownie and bar trays into squares, halving scones/muffins — with clean, uniform, presentable cuts on delicate crumb and frosted surfaces.
Bread work: slicing loaves, splitting bagels, croissants and rolls for sandwiches and toast, either in bulk during morning prep or a few at a time to order, using a knife or a countertop slicer.

Sandwich/panini component prep in the café back-of-house: slicing tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, peppers and avocado, and slicing deli meats and cheeses to a specified thickness, then stacking/panning them for the sandwich station.

Made-to-order cutting at the counter during peak service: halving or quartering a heated panini/sandwich before plating or bagging, and halving a pastry a customer requested, done in seconds amid queue pressure on a shared counter.

sources.title: CHIPOTLE DEBUTS AUTOCADO AND THE AUGMENTED MAKELINE BY HYPHEN IN RESTAURANTS
sources.claim: Autocado, a hopper-fed avocado processing cobot developed by Vebu, autonomously cuts, cores and peels avocados (about 26 s each) and has been operating in a Chipotle restaurant back-of-house since September 2024; it adapts to variability in fruit size.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: cutting/portioning fresh fruit for food service. Demonstrates machine-controlled knife work on soft, variable, ripe fruit at foodservice quality, with the product bulk-loaded into the machine rather than handled as found.

sources.title: ACCUSONIC-100FS | Ultrasonic Sheet Cake Cutting Machine
sources.claim: FoodTools ACCUSONIC-100FS is a commercially sold ultrasonic cake slicer with a servo-driven conveyor, multi-axis cutting head and automatic onload/offload that portions fresh sheet and round cakes into wedges and shapes.

sources.title: VSI Automatic Vertical Slicer | Precision Food Slicing | Bizerba USA
sources.claim: The Bizerba VSI is a fully automatic vertical slicer sold for delis and commercial kitchens that slices meats, cheeses and produce to set thickness and deposits them in stacked or shingled patterns once the operator loads and sets up the product.

sources.title: Efficient Automatic Bread Slicers for Retail Stores & Bakeries | Bizerba USA Inc.
sources.claim: Bizerba sells automatic bread slicers for bakeries and retail that slice large numbers of loaves per hour with uniform slices once loaves are fed to the machine.

roles.title: Waiters and Waitresses
roles.description: Take orders and serve food and beverages to patrons at tables in dining establishment.

tasks.label: Collect payments from customers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service casual/fine-dining restaurant, card payment at the table: server drops a check presenter, returns to pick up the folder with a credit card, walks the card to the POS station, swipes/inserts it, brings back the printed slip and card, then retrieves the signed slip with the written tip. Dining room is crowded, tables and chairs shift, guests hand the card directly to the server.

Pay-at-table with a handheld terminal: server carries a wireless POS/tablet device to the table, itemizes, hands the device over or holds it while the guest taps/inserts a card and selects a tip on screen, waits for approval, prints or emails the receipt, and returns the card.

Cash payment at the table: guest leaves bills in the folder, server counts the cash, carries it to the register/cash drawer, rings the sale, counts out exact change in bills and coins, returns the change and receipt to the table, and later collects the cash tip left behind.

Diner/family-restaurant or bar-counter style checkout: the guest carries the check to a front register or bar station on the way out and pays there with cash or card; the server or host operates the terminal/cash drawer, gives change and receipt at a fixed counter inside the restaurant.

Complex or contested payments: large party splitting one check across several cards, mixed cash-and-card tender, gift cards and coupons with partial balances, comps and voids after a complaint, declined cards, and manual tip adjustments — usually handled at the table plus multiple trips to the POS.

instances.label: Casual full-service restaurant (chain or independent): server takes food and drink orders verbally from a party of 2-4 at a table, jots shorthand on a guest check pad or memorizes, then walks to a POS station and keys the items, modifiers, and seat positions so tickets print or appear on the kitchen display.

Tableside handheld/tablet ordering: server enters each guest's order directly into a handheld POS device at the table as the guest speaks, selecting modifiers, temperatures, sides, and allergy flags, and firing courses to the kitchen from the table.

Fine dining or upscale restaurant where writing is discouraged: server memorizes the full order for a table including seat numbers, wine pairings, and dietary restrictions, then reconstructs it accurately at the POS and communicates special requests to the kitchen expediter.

High-volume diner, breakfast house, or bar service: rapid-fire order taking from large or turning-over parties in a noisy room, handwritten tickets clipped to the rail or fast POS entry, frequent substitutions, split checks, and re-fires added mid-meal.

Complex or non-standard orders: banquets, large parties, off-menu items, severe allergy accommodations, or child/senior guests needing clarification, where the server must confirm details with the guest and the kitchen and annotate the ticket with free-text instructions.

tasks.label: Remove dishes and glasses from tables or counters, and take them to kitchen for cleaning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual/family full-service restaurant: a party leaves and the server clears the vacated table — stacking dirty plates with leftover food and sauce, gathering glasses, silverware, ramekins, crumpled napkins and trash into a bus tub or onto an arm/tray, then carrying it through a crowded dining room to the dish pit and dropping it at the dishwasher.

Clearing finished courses while guests remain seated: the server judges who is done, reaches between/around seated diners and their belongings, removes used plates and empty glasses without disturbing the remaining settings, and carries them to the kitchen mid-service.

Bar top and counter service: clearing pint glasses, stemware, cocktail glasses, small plates and cups from the bar and high-tops during busy service, emptying liquid, and placing them into glass racks or the under-bar/dish sink area.

Fine dining or banquet service: coordinated removal of china, chargers, crystal stemware and flatware, carried on trays or by hand to a tray jack and then to the dish room; high value fragile ware, low tolerance for chips, breakage or noise.
Outdoor patio or sidewalk seating: clearing dishes and glassware from tables on uneven pavement, with wind, weather, pedestrians and steps or a threshold between the patio and the interior kitchen.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: the dish-pit end of bussing. It handles the same objects (restaurant plates, cups, glasses soiled with food) with the work presented at a fixed station, which is exactly the E1 form of 'take dishes to the kitchen for cleaning'.

tasks.label: Clean tables or counters after patrons have finished dining.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual full-service restaurant: a party leaves a four-top; the server clears plates with leftover food, glassware, flatware, condiments and napkins into a bus tub, wipes the table with a sanitizer cloth, brushes crumbs off chairs/booth, and resets placemats and rollups — all within a couple of minutes while other guests are seated nearby.

Fast-casual / food-court table partially self-bussed: worker removes leftover trays, cups, wrappers, half-eaten food and spilled drinks, wipes the tabletop and the adjacent counter/condiment station, and pushes in chairs during a busy lunch rush.
Coffeehouse/café table that patrons already cleared themselves: worker wipes crumbs, cup rings and small spills from the tabletop, squares the chairs, and moves on — no dishware to remove.

Fine dining: between courses the server clears plates and used stemware one at a time, crumbs the linen with a scraper and plate, changes soiled napkins/linen, and resets silverware and glasses to exact cover positions without disturbing seated guests.

Bar/counter service: bartender clears empty glassware, bottles, coasters and wet napkins from a crowded bar top, wipes sticky/wet surface and rail, and resets the spot for the next guest in a tight space with patrons at adjoining stools.

Outdoor patio or banquet/event room turnover: many tables cleared at once after a seating or event — stacked plates, glassware, linens and outdoor debris (leaves, wind-blown napkins), tables wiped and reset for the next group.

tasks.label: Perform cleaning duties, such as sweeping and mopping floors, vacuuming carpet, tidying up server station, taking out trash, or checking and cleaning bathroom.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Closing side work in a casual/family restaurant: after the last guests leave, sweep and mop the hard-floor dining room, entry mat area, aisles and host stand, with chairs stacked on tables; food debris, grease spots and dried spills, finished before lock-up.

Vacuuming the carpeted dining room, banquet/private room or lounge after service in a mid-scale or fine-dining house: crumbs and dropped food under and around tables, edges along booths and walls, done after close or between seatings of a private party.

Mid-service floor cleaning in the server's own section while guests are seated: sweeping crumbs and dropped food from under a 4-top or booth during a two-minute table turn, mopping a spilled drink in a busy aisle, picking up broken glass or a dropped napkin, working around chairs, table bases and walking guests.

Tidying and restocking the server/wait station between rushes and at close: wiping down the counter and shelves, straightening trays, menus and check presenters, refilling napkin, straw, condiment, sweetener and to-go container supplies from back-of-house stock, restocking glassware and ice, clearing crumbs and clutter.

Taking out the trash: pulling full liners from dining-room, server-station and restroom bins, tying them off, carrying them through the kitchen and out the back door to the dumpster, heaving them in, and re-lining the bins (sometimes also breaking down cardboard).

Checking and cleaning the guest restroom during and after the shift: picking up paper off the floor, wiping the sink counter and mirror, cleaning the toilet/urinal, restocking toilet paper, paper towels and soap, mopping the floor, emptying the trash.

sources.title: Hugo the Hotel Hero: Gausium Phantas Winning Hearts at Hotel Prinz Rudolf in Italy
sources.claim: Gausium's compact Phantas autonomous cleaning robot has been deployed since November 2024 at Hotel Prinz Rudolf, where it cleans hotel floors (lobby and dining areas), covering up to 400 m2 per day with consistent results.

sources.title: Robots Are Coming To A Hotel Near You, But Are Consumers Ready?

sources.claim: Pudu's CC1 four-in-one floor robot is deployed at fleet scale across a national convenience-store chain (1,200+ QuikTrip locations), autonomously sweeping, scrubbing, vacuuming and mopping retail sales floors overnight so staff walk in to clean floors.
sources.transferJustification: Convenience-store sales floors with aisles, fixtures and spilled food/drink are comparable in debris type, floor surface and clutter to a restaurant dining room floor cleaned after hours.

sources.title: Intercontinental Wien Elevates Hotel Cleanliness with Gausium Vacuum 40 and Phantas
sources.claim: Gausium's Vacuum 40 and Phantas were deployed in June 2024 at the InterContinental Wien to handle the hotel's daily floor and carpet cleaning, with the hotel reporting consistent cleaning performance.

sources.title: Whiz Product Overview | Softbank Robotics
sources.claim: SoftBank Robotics' Whiz is a commercially sold autonomous vacuum that vacuums carpet in large commercial spaces alongside cleaning staff, using teach-and-repeat mapping and responsive navigation.

sources.title: Pudu Robotics launches PUDU CC1 Pro AI-powered autonomous cleaning robot
sources.claim: Pudu's CC1 Pro uses onboard AI to detect liquid stains, recognize floor ... type, adjust cleaning intensity and verify its own cleaning results.
sources.transferJustification: Spot-cleaning a spill on an open floor is the same physical act as the scrubber's stain-directed cleaning pass; it substantiates spill cleanup only where the floor is clear of chairs, table bases and seated guests.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR is an autonomous bathroom cleaning robot offered as a monthly service in office buildings; it navigates the building, opens doors, and cleans toilets, urinals and floors and picks up trash during normal facility operations.

sources.title: The Robotics Founder Who Turned a Hotel Chore Into a Real-World AI Breakthrough
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics built a mobile manipulator that autonomously cleans hotel bathrooms and moved it from demonstrations into commercial deployment in real hospitality operations.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Raises $120 Million to Advance Robotic Foundation Models on the Path to Physical Artificial General Intelligence
sources.claim: Dyna Robotics' DYNA-1 stationary dual-arm cells fold napkins to restaurant production-grade quality fully autonomously for 24 hours (99.4% success, 800+ napkins), and the company's robots run 16 hours a day at customer sites including restaurants and hotels.
sources.transferJustification: Restocking a server station means dexterous handling of napkins, small supplies and caddies; Dyna's deployed cells show worker-rate dexterous handling of exactly these restaurant soft goods when the work is presented at a fixed station, but not roaming, in-situ station tidying.

sources.title: Taking out the Trash
sources.claim: An autonomous MiR200 mobile robot fitted with a container transports used packaging waste between the co-packing line and ... at FM Logistics, working around the clock without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: internal waste haulage. It substantiates taking out trash only in the E1 form where waste is presented to the machine at a fixed point and emptied by a tipper, not bag-pulling, tying and dumpster-heaving.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots at Froedtert Hospital hauled more than 6 million pounds ... plus recycling and medical waste in 2024 over corridors shared with staff and patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: waste transport inside an institution. It covers only the haulage leg; humans still pull liners, load carts and dump them, so it does not complete the waiter's trash instance at E2.

tasks.label: Prepare tables for meals, including setting up items such as linens, silverware, and glassware.
