instances.label: Casual/family restaurant, mid-service reset: after a party leaves, the server resets the table in the dining room in 1-2 minutes — placemats or paper settings, rolled silverware, water glasses, menus, condiments — working around seated guests, servers, and bussers, dozens of times per shift.

Pre-shift opening setup of a dining room: before doors open, the server uniformly sets every table (placemats/napkins, forks, knives, spoons, water goblets, salt and pepper, candle), and rolls silverware into napkins at a side station; no guests present, layout fixed.

Fine-dining cover setting: linen tablecloth laid and smoothed, folded cloth napkins, multiple forks/knives/spoons and dessert utensils aligned to precise spacing, polished stemware and charger plates placed; settings adjusted for party size and menu between courses.

Banquet/event mass setup in a hotel ballroom or event room: dozens of round tables draped with linens, then hundreds of identical covers laid from carts and glass racks (silverware, water glasses, wine glasses, napkins), before guests arrive, under time pressure.

Outdoor patio/deck service: setting weathered mixed furniture — weighted or clipped linens, silverware, glassware, rolled napkins — in wind, sun, and rain, often re-setting blown-around items and wiping outdoor surfaces first.

sources.title: 𝜋₀: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0 vision-language-action policy was evaluated on an explicit table-setting task in which the robot autonomously takes place mats, dishes, silverware, napkins and cups out of a bin and arranges them on a table, adjusting per language instruction; demonstrated on fixed dual-arm and mobile manipulator platforms in the lab.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model Offering Fully Autonomous, Round-the-Clock Dexterity
sources.claim: DYNA-1 runs a pair of stationary robotic ... that fold napkins and linens autonomously for over 24 hours with a 99.4% success rate and no human intervention; the company reports commercial installations in laundries and hotels.
sources.transferJustification: Napkin and linen folding is the cloth-handling component of preparing tables; same objects (restaurant napkins/linens), same required neatness, performed at a fixed workstation with items presented to the arms — exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics' fixed dishwashing robot cell is installed in commercial restaurant kitchens and runs 24 hours a day, autonomously grasping and sorting transparent glassware, shiny plates and silverware with millimeter-level perception, after 1.5 years of deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Racking dishes is the inverse handling problem to laying a cover: it requires reliable perception and damage-free grasping of the very items a table setting uses (stemware, plates, silverware) at commercial reliability in a fixed, purpose-built station.

sources.title: Chef Robots Can Now Help Automate Consumer Packaged Goods Assembly
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-enabled robots pick and place discrete items including cutlery kits and sachets into cups, bowls and trays on food production lines; the company reports 100 million servings completed in production at customer facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Placing cutlery kits and small items at specified positions in trays on a conveyor line is the same pick-and-place operation as laying silverware at fixed positions on a fixtured table, at production throughput and accepted commercial quality.

sources.title: Edge | Chicago Dryer
sources.claim: Chicago Dryer's EDGE automatic spreader/feeder machines find, spread and present table linens and sheets flat at high volume in commercial laundries, using patented cornerless linen-finding rather than manual corner clipping.
sources.transferJustification: Spreading a crumpled tablecloth flat and square is the hard part of dressing a table with linen; these machines do that grip-find-spread operation on the same tablecloths at commercial rates once the linen is presented, matching the E1 work-presentation assumption.

tasks.label: Stock service areas with supplies such as coffee, food, tableware, and linens.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual/full-service restaurant, before and during service: server restocks the side/wait station with clean tableware — rolled or loose silverware, plates, bowls, glassware, cups and saucers, ramekins — fetched from the dish machine area or storage racks in bus tubs and dish racks, carried through a busy dining room, and arranged into station drawers, bins and shelves.

Beverage station replenishment during service: brewing fresh coffee and iced tea, filling and swapping urns/decanters, refilling the ice bin, and restocking cups, lids, straws, creamers, sugar caddies, lemons and syrups at the wait station or service bar, while guests and coworkers move through the area.

Linens: retrieving clean napkins, tablecloths, napkin stacks and bar towels from a linen closet or delivery cart, stocking them onto station shelves, rolling napkin/silverware sets, and swapping out the soiled-linen bin — typically in a fine-dining or banquet operation before service.

Dry goods, condiments and paper supplies: carrying cases and bulk containers from the back stockroom (ketchup, hot sauce, sugar packets, wrapped butter, to-go boxes, napkins, check presenters), opening cases, filling condiment caddies and racks, and topping off the station's supply shelves.

Buffet, banquet or cafeteria service line: replacing empty hotel pans with full ones from the kitchen, refilling bread baskets, fruit bowls and dressing containers, and replenishing plates, cutlery and serving utensils at the line while guests serve themselves.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA, a rail-mounted robot arm installed behind convenience-store refrigerated display cases, autonomously picks bottled and canned drinks from crates and places them in the correct shelf positions, up to about 1,000 items a day, deployed across 300 FamilyMart stores; a remote operator takes over on the rare failure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing retail display shelves from supply crates. It is the same act as stocking a service area — picking rigid, hand-sized packaged items (bottles, cans) from a known supply position and placing them in a designated, orderly position on a stocking shelf, at commercial reliability.

sources.title: AI-Enabled Robotics: A Solution for the Food Manufacturing Labor Crisis
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' robotic arms are installed on food-production lines at manufacturers such as Amy's Kitchen and Cafe Spice, autonomously portioning and placing food into trays; the company reports tens of millions of servings assembled in real production environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling serving containers with food on a fixtured line. Replenishing a buffet pan or a food supply container is the same act — depositing measured food into a presented pan or tray — with comparable food-handling precision and hygiene, in a purpose-built line.

sources.title: Introducing Chef+: Our Most Advanced Meal Assembly Robot Yet
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' Chef+ system picks discrete items such as oranges, ... and places them into clamshells and snack boxes on production lines, in addition to portioning scoopable items.

tasks.label: Roll silverware, set up food stations, or set up dining areas to prepare for the next shift or for large parties.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual/family-dining server does closing or opening side work at the server station: takes clean flatware from bus tubs or dish-machine cylinders, wipes/spot-polishes it, lays fork-knife-spoon on a paper or cloth napkin, rolls and bands it, and stocks several hundred rollups in caddies for the next shift.

Server resets the dining room for the next shift: wipes and dries tabletops, squares tables and chairs, lays placemats/napkin rolls, sets water glasses and plateware, refills and aligns salt/pepper and condiment caddies, replaces menus and tent cards across 15-30 tables.

Server stocks and sets up service/food stations: fills ice bins, brews coffee and iced tea, fills water pitchers, refills sauce/dressing/butter containers and portion cups, restocks napkins, straws, to-go boxes, plates and flatware, and lays out serving utensils on a buffet or expo line.

Setup for a large party or banquet: moves and joins tables, positions and aligns chairs, lays linens and skirting, then puts full place settings, glassware and centerpieces on the tables in a banquet room or function space.

Upscale/fine-dining pre-shift setup: polishes flatware and stemware with steam and cloth, presses and lays linen, sets precise multi-course covers with charger, several utensils, glasses, folded napkins and candles, measured to the table edge.

tasks.label: Assist host or hostess by answering phones to take reservations or to-go orders, and by greeting, seating, and thanking guests.

instances.label: Casual/family full-service restaurant during normal service: waiter covers the host stand, greets a walk-in party of 1-4, confirms party size, picks an open clean table in the rotation, grabs menus, walks the party through the dining room past servers and occupied tables, seats them, hands menus, says the server's name and thanks them.

Seating with complications: quoting a wait and working a wait list, a party of 8-12 needing tables pushed together, fetching high chairs/booster seats, guests requesting a booth/patio/window, assisting a guest using a walker or wheelchair, or upscale service touches (pulling out chairs, placing napkins, presenting menus by cover).

Phone rings mid-shift and the waiter answers: takes a reservation (name, party size, time, occasion, seating preference) and writes/keys it into the book or reservation system, or takes a phoned-in to-go order with modifications, rings it into the POS, quotes a pickup time, and confirms.

Door duty: welcoming parties as they walk in (acknowledging them within seconds, offering a pager or telling them the wait), and thanking/saying goodbye to departing parties at the exit, occasionally holding the door or handing back leftovers or a coat.

To-go/pickup handoff at the host stand or counter: greeting a customer or delivery driver who has arrived for a bagged order, locating the correct bag on the shelf, verifying name/order and adding sauces or utensils, taking payment or confirming prepayment, handing it over and thanking them.

tasks.label: Fill salt, pepper, sugar, cream, condiment, and napkin containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Side work in a casual/family sit-down restaurant: server collects salt and pepper shakers from 15-20 tables onto a tray at the service station, unscrews or pops off tops, funnels bulk salt and ground pepper into each shaker, checks for clumped/damp salt, wipes shakers clean, recaps and redistributes them to tables before service.

Restocking sugar/sweetener caddies and condiment packet holders on tables and at the coffee station: sorting mixed packets (white sugar, raw sugar, blue/pink/yellow sweeteners, jam, shelf creamers) by type, discarding torn or bent packets, refilling each caddy to par with packets standing upright and facing the same way.

Refilling table and back-of-house condiment squeeze bottles and jars (ketchup, mustard, hot sauce, syrup, soy, BBQ) from bulk jugs or #10 cans at the prep counter: marrying partly full bottles, funneling or pumping viscous sauce in, wiping rims and necks, capping, dating, and returning them to tables or the line.

Loading napkin containers: refilling counter and table napkin dispensers and napkin holders from bulk packs, breaking open sleeves, counting and compressing stacks, seating them in spring-loaded or box dispensers so napkins feed one at a time without jamming, plus topping off dispenser caddies at a beverage station.

Filling cream and dairy containers at the coffee/beverage station: pouring half-and-half or milk from bulk jugs into creamer pitchers and table creamers, filling small pitchers for tea service, restocking mini-creamer bowls on ice, wiping spills, and returning bulk dairy to refrigeration.

Filling condiment ramekins and portion cups for service (ranch, ketchup, tartar, salsa, dressing) from bulk containers at the pantry/prep station, portioning to a consistent fill level, lidding or covering them, and staging them on the service line.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual/family sit-down restaurant at moderate traffic: greet a party of 2-4 at the door, confirm the assigned open table, walk them across a level dining room with clear aisles, seat them and leave menus.

Peak-hour rush in a crowded dining room: a waitlist queue at the door, aisles intermittently blocked by pushed-out chairs, standing guests and servers carrying trays; table assignment may change mid-walk and guests ask for a booth/window instead; seating must be fast to keep table turns moving.
Upscale/fine-dining room: escort at the guests' pace with conversational hospitality, take or direct coats, pull out chairs, place napkins, present menus and hand off to the captain/server.

Party with special needs: wheelchair or walker user, stroller or small children needing a high chair, or a large group requiring tables pushed together and chairs added before the party is walked over and seated.
Multi-level venue or outdoor patio: leading guests up or down a few steps, over door thresholds/ramps, onto uneven patio paving or a deck, sometimes in wind/rain or dim light.
Bar, diner or quick-casual venue: short 'follow me' from the door to a nearby booth, counter seat or high-top a few paces away.

tasks.label: Garnish and decorate dishes in preparation for serving.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual/family table-service restaurant: at the expo window the server picks up plated entrées and adds standard finishing touches before running the food — lemon wedge on the fish, parsley sprinkle, pickle spear, dollop of sour cream, shredded cheese, ramekin of sauce placed on the plate rim. Mixed plate shapes, dozens of covers an hour, cooks and runners moving through a hot line.

Dessert and beverage finishing at the server/bar station: whipped cream and a cherry on a sundae or pie, chocolate or caramel drizzle, powdered-sugar dusting, citrus wheel or mint sprig on a cocktail or iced tea, candle and plate-writing on a birthday dessert. Small, delicate, quickly wilting or melting items finished immediately before pickup.

Banquet, catering or large-party plated service: a long line of identical plates staged in a banquet kitchen; servers work assembly-line style adding the same garnish to every plate (herb sprig, sauce drizzle, dusting, a berry or vegetable accent) before the plates are covered and loaded onto trays for a timed, simultaneous service.

Fine-dining / upscale restaurant: server or captain finishes plates at the pass under the chef's standard — tweezered microgreens and edible flowers, precise placement of a crisp or quenelle, a sauce swoosh or dots, wiping smudges off the plate rim, checking each plate against the reference presentation before it leaves.

Finishing in the dining room in front of the guest: grating cheese or cracking pepper over pasta, adding whipped cream or shaved chocolate at the table, garnishing a salad or dessert on a gueridon/service cart, finishing a flambé dish tableside among seated guests, chairs and traffic.

tasks.label: Bring wine selections to tables with appropriate glasses, and pour the wines for customers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual/mid-range full-service restaurant: server carries a bottle of wine and matching stemware from the service bar to an occupied table, sets glasses in front of each guest, cuts foil and uncorks (or brings by-the-glass pours on a tray), pours 5-6 oz per guest, and returns to top up during the meal. Dining room is crowded, chairs and guests shift, tables are cluttered with plates.

Fine-dining / sommelier-style service: bottle presented label-first to the host, foil cut and cork drawn tableside, tasting pour offered and approved, older reds decanted, correct crystal stemware (Bordeaux/Burgundy/flute) placed at each cover, precise measured pours, glasses monitored and refilled unobtrusively through several courses.

Wine bar or winery tasting room: guest orders a flight or glass at a counter/table; worker sets the appropriate glasses, pours measured tasting portions of several different wines in sequence, describes each, and re-pours favorites.

Banquet, wedding or catered event: pre-set tables with glassware already in place; server circulates with two bottles (red/white), pours for 8-10 seated guests per table at speed, and makes repeated refill rounds during toasts and courses.

Outdoor patio, rooftop or sidewalk seating at a restaurant/bar: wine bottle in an ice bucket and glasses carried out over thresholds and uneven pavers, poured at tables in wind, sun and variable lighting with foot traffic passing.

tasks.label: Place food servings on plates or trays according to orders or instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital patient tray line: dietary aide stands at a moving belt in the hospital kitchen and, reading each patient's diet card/ticket, portions hot entrée and sides from steam-table pans onto china or insulated plates and adds soup, salad, dessert, bread, beverage, condiments and cutlery pack to the tray; ~4-8 seconds per tray, hundreds of trays per meal, near-zero tolerance for diet/allergy errors.

Nursing home / assisted living / continuing-care kitchen: aide plates each resident's meal from bulk pans onto plates per the resident's diet card (regular, low-sodium, carb-controlled, mechanical soft or pureed, portion-controlled), arranges components on the plate, covers it and sets it on a tray with card, silverware and beverage for dining-room or room delivery; 60-150 residents per meal period.

Institutional cafeteria / staff dining / campus or corporate dining serving line: server behind a steam-table or made-to-order counter portions the items each patron selects onto the patron's plate, bowl or tray, following portion standards and the patron's requests, during a fast lunch rush.

Hotel in-room dining / room service: server plates the ordered items from the kitchen onto china, adds garnish and sauces, covers the plate, and sets the tray or roll-in cart with linen, cutlery roll, condiments, beverage and check according to the order ticket, to hotel presentation standards.

Drive-in / curbside car service (carhop) and similar outside-dining service: worker at the pass assembles the ordered items — wrapped sandwiches, fry cartons, condiment packets, capped drinks — on a carrier tray or in a bag per the ticket for delivery to a parked vehicle.

sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-enabled robotic arms portion ingredients into meal trays and tray compartments on customer production lines, adapting to different ingredients, recipes, portion sizes and trays with quick changeovers (Cafe Spice two-compartment curry/rice trays).
sources.transferJustification: Same act as the task — depositing measured food servings into the correct place on a plate/tray — with comparable objects (scoopable hot and cold foods, compartmented trays) and portion-accuracy requirements; environment is a conveyor line rather than a human serving line.

sources.transferJustification: Related task (produce packing) transfers: placing discrete packaged items into defined positions in a tray/box is the same manipulation as placing wrapped items, cartons and condiments on a meal tray.

tasks.label: Clean or sterilize dishes, kitchen utensils, equipment, or facilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Institutional dish room (hospital, nursing home, senior-living or campus food service): soiled meal trays and bus tubs come back on carts; the aide scrapes plate waste, separates china, plastic tumblers, flatware and tray covers, racks them, runs the rack-conveyor/door-type dish machine, then unloads hot clean ware and puts it away for the next meal period.

Pot-and-utensil sink work in a facility kitchen or nourishment room: hand-washing serving pans, steam-table inserts, cookware, ladles, beverage urns, blender and slicer parts through a three-compartment wash-rinse-sanitize sink, scrubbing baked-on residue, then air-drying and shelving.

Cleaning and sanitizing food-service equipment and surfaces in the pantry/servery: wiping down steam tables and serving lines, tray carts and delivery carts, coffee brewers and urns, beverage and ice machines, refrigerator handles and counters, using sanitizer buckets and test strips between meal services.
Cleaning the facility floors at end of service: sweeping and then mopping or scrubbing the dish room, kitchen, servery and dining-room floors in an institutional building after the meal period.

Hotel in-room dining / room service: retrieving soiled trays and roll-in tables from guest corridors and rooms, wheeling them back to the room-service pantry, washing and polishing glassware, china and silverware, and cleaning the pantry, carts and hot boxes.

sources.claim: The Armstrong system covers the dish-room cycle end to end: soiled, mixed bus tubs in, clean stacked ware out, using the customer's existing dish machine.

tasks.label: Monitor food distribution, ensuring that meals are delivered to the correct recipients and that guidelines, such as those for special diets, are followed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient meal service: aide pulls trays from the delivery cart on a nursing unit, matches each tray card to the patient's name/room, checks with nursing for NPO orders and same-day diet changes, places the tray on the overbed table and sets it up, and pulls/replaces items that violate the diet order.

Institutional kitchen tray line / cart check before dispatch: worker verifies each assembled patient tray against its printed diet ticket (texture-modified, renal, carb-controlled, allergen exclusions), corrects wrong or missing items, and loads trays into the correct unit cart for transport.

Assisted living / skilled nursing dining room: server plates and delivers meals to seated residents, matching each resident to a prescribed diet (pureed, mechanical soft, thickened liquids, no-added-salt, allergies), monitors residents through the meal, swaps out non-compliant items, and reports intake.

Hotel in-room dining / amenity delivery: server checks the order ticket against the tray or bag (including allergy notes), transports it through corridors and elevators to the correct guest room, confirms the guest, hands over or sets up the order, and posts the charge.

School, college or contract-managed cafeteria serving line: attendant portions and serves each student's meal, watches for posted allergy/medical-diet alerts, and ensures every tray leaving the line has the required components for the meal pattern.

Curbside / car-side handoff (drive-in carhop, curbside pickup, catering pickup window): worker checks the packed order against the ticket, carries it out to the correct numbered stall, car or waiting customer, confirms the recipient's name/order, and hands it over.

sources.title: Chef Robotics | Physical AI for the food industry
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-enabled food-assembly robots are in commercial production at more than a dozen food-production facilities, assembling meals to specified recipes on purpose-built lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of prepared meals to a specified recipe. It transfers to 'ensuring dietary guidelines are followed' because compliance is achieved by depositing exactly the specified ingredients and portions into each tray.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: medically tailored meal production. Same objects (portioned foods into meal trays) and the same acceptance criterion as a diet-ticket check - each meal must match a prescribed dietary specification.

sources.title: Industries | Chef Robotics

sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-mix meal assembly with allergen segregation. Transfers to tray-line diet compliance because the machine composes each tray to a specified, changing spec in a fixtured line, the same output a tray-line checker guarantees.

sources.title: Hotel Delivery Robot Deployed in Los Angeles, California

sources.title: In U.S. Industry First, Property Group Puts Robots In All Hotels
sources.claim: Relay+ is described as a fully autonomous self-driving service ... rides elevators independently and completes hotel deliveries in ten minutes or less; a hotel group deployed it across all its properties.

sources.title: Franciscan Health Crown Point Robots Assisting In Kitchen, Environmental Deliveries

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi is deployed in 25+ US hospitals with over a million autonomous deliveries, but its workload is pharmacy, lab and supply logistics rather than patient-facing meal service.

sources.system: BellaBot at The Commons on Marice senior living community

sources.claim: In senior living dining rooms, deployed food-running robots carry meals to residents' tables but a human staff member meets the robot and serves the resident.

sources.title: Sweetgreen Goes All-In with Automated Restaurants - QSR Magazine
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen automated makeline assembles each customer's ordered bowl on a purpose-built line, delivering near-perfect order accuracy and consistent portioning; the format is being rolled out across new stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: per-order automated food assembly on a serving line. Transfers to a cafeteria line because each order carries its own specification (ingredient inclusions/exclusions) and the accepted output is a correctly composed meal for that order.

sources.title: Introducing Starship: On-Campus Food Delivery Robots at Cal Poly Pomona
sources.claim: Starship's autonomous delivery robots carry prepared food orders across university campuses and release the order only when the correct customer unlocks the robot with the ordering app.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: last-mile handoff of a prepared food order. Transfers to curbside/car-side service because the robot must reach the waiting customer outdoors and release the order only to the verified correct recipient.

sources.title: Serve Robotics Deploys 2,000 Robots & Leads U.S. Sidewalk Delivery
sources.claim: Serve Robotics operates the largest US sidewalk delivery fleet, with more than 2,000 autonomous robots delivering restaurant orders to customers in multiple metro areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended delivery of restaurant food orders to a named customer. Same objects (bagged hot food orders) and the same acceptance test - the right order reaches the right person - as a curbside handoff.

tasks.label: Examine trays to ensure that they contain required items.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital patient tray line: at the end of a staffed conveyor trayline in the hospital kitchen, the server checks each assembled tray against the printed diet ticket/tray card - entree, sides, beverage, condiments, utensils, straw, dessert, texture/allergen restrictions - and adds or removes items before the tray goes into the delivery cart. Hundreds of individualized trays per meal period under service-time pressure.

Hotel room service: in the service pantry the server checks the assembled tray or gueridon cart against the order ticket before delivery - covered plate(s), coffee pot and cup, condiments, sugar/cream, silverware roll, napkin, glassware, check/pen - items of mixed size, some under plate covers or in insulated carriers.

Assisted living / skilled nursing servery: staff verify each resident's tray against the diet card at the servery or steam table - pureed/mechanical-soft textures, thickened liquids of a specified consistency, portion restrictions, personal preferences, nourishment supplements - before the tray goes to the dining room or hall cart.

Point-of-delivery check at the patient room or resident's table: before handing the tray over, the server matches the tray card to the patient's name/armband and confirms the tray holds what the diet order calls for (and nothing prohibited), in the room with the patient, family and clinical equipment present.

Drive-in car hop / catering-cart or bagged-order check: at the expo window or staging counter the server verifies the tray or carrier holds every item on the ticket - sandwiches, sides, drinks with lids, sauces, napkins, straws, utensils - before carrying it out to the car or function room.

sources.system: Chef Robotics ChefOS / Chef robotic arm
sources.title: Chef Robotics emerges from stealth after demos at Amy's Kitchen
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' robotic arms portion food into meal trays on production lines, using depth cameras and a weight-sensing platform so each tray receives the specified amount of each component.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic meal-tray assembly. It handles the same objects (individual meal trays with multiple required components) and its vision plus per-pick weight sensing is the mechanism by which a tray is confirmed to hold the required items in the required amounts.

sources.title: Chef Robotics and Packline Partner on End-to-End Meal Production Automation
sources.claim: Chef robots use AI and computer ... track tray positions on a moving conveyor line and are in production at customers such as Cafe Spice, integrated with downstream tray-sealing equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling meal trays on a conveyor line. Establishes that the tray-by-tray perception needed to know what sits in each tray compartment works on production conveyor lines, which is the E1 presentation of the trayline instances.

sources.title: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' tray-assembly robots are commercially deployed at multiple US food manufacturers and had produced tens of millions of meals by late 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-mix meal tray production. Shows the tray-level assembly and verification capability is a sustained commercial deployment at production throughput, not a demo.

sources.title: AI robots automate tray assembly for fresh produce packing
sources.claim: Chef robots place discrete whole items (fruits) as well as scoopable portions into clamshells, snack boxes and trays, i.e. they handle the mixed discrete items that make up a service tray.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing discrete packaged items into a tray or box. Extends tray-completion capability from scooped food to the discrete items (fruit, packaged sides, condiments) a service tray must contain.

sources.system: WIPOTEC-OCS SC-series X-ray scanners / SC-V vision inspection and checkweighers with ejectors
sources.title: Flawless product inspection for ready meals | WIPOTEC-OCS
sources.claim: Inline X-ray/vision inspection machines perform completeness checks on ready-meal trays - detecting a missing component - and automatically eject non-conforming packs from the line.
sources.transferJustification: Same task - examining a meal tray to confirm it contains the required items - performed by an embodied machine that inspects each tray and physically ejects incomplete ones, but only on a purpose-built conveyor line.

sources.title: Hyphen raises $24m to automate the restaurant makeline
sources.claim: Hyphen's Makeline is a robotic assembly machine whose sensors and AI vision monitor portion quality, order accuracy and order size as containers travel through the enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated order assembly with machine-vision order-accuracy checking. The check performed - does this container hold exactly what the ticket calls for - is the judgment the server makes over a tray.

sources.title: Chipotle and Cava Invest $25 Million in Hyphen to Advance Restaurant Automation
sources.claim: Chipotle ran Hyphen's automated makeline in its test kitchen and in live restaurants, producing up to 350 meals per ... at 99 percent order accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling and accuracy-checking individual customer orders. Order-accuracy at or above human expo-checker levels shows the machine can guarantee an order carrier holds the required items.

sources.title: Sweetgreen brings its automated restaurant format to California
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen automated makeline runs in operating restaurants and is credited by the company with near-perfect order accuracy and portioning consistency.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of individualized bowls with order verification. Demonstrates sustained multi-site operation at accuracy comparable to or better than the human check the task describes.

sources.system: RoboEatz Autonomous Robotic Kitchen (ARK) / WellSpan 'Fresh Take Eatery'
sources.developer: RoboEatz with ABB Robotics, Aramark and WellSpan Health
sources.title: Aramark and RoboEatz Develop Robotic Meal Service to Support Healthcare Workers Around the Clock
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic kitchen (RoboEatz ARK, using ABB arms) was installed with Aramark at WellSpan Health to produce customizable meals to order, including for dietary needs, inside a hospital.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic production of a per-order meal with dietary constraints inside a healthcare facility. The robot works within its own enclosed purpose-built cell, showing an E1 cell can sit in a hospital but not that a robot works the hospital's own trayline.

tasks.label: Load trays with accessories, such as eating utensils, napkins, or condiments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large hospital central kitchen: worker stands at a moving tray line (round-belt conveyor) and, per the patient diet card, places a wrapped cutlery set, napkin, straw and condiment packets (salt, pepper, sugar, creamer, butter, jelly) on each system tray; several hundred to a few thousand trays per day.

Hospital 'room service'/on-demand dining: trays assembled order-by-order at an assembly counter or short expo line as tickets print; worker adds silverware roll, napkin, condiments, lid and straw to each individual tray, mixing diets and special requests, then hands off to a delivery ambassador.

Skilled nursing / assisted living / CCRC: worker sets up 100-300 trays per meal at a steam-table serving line or pantry counter (no automated conveyor), adding utensils (some adaptive), napkin, clothing protector, condiment packets and thickener per resident card, then loads trays into delivery carts.

Hotel in-room dining pantry: worker dresses a room-service tray or rolling cart with linen, rolled silverware in a linen napkin, salt and pepper shakers, sugar caddy, condiment bottles/ramekins, plate covers and a bud vase before the food is placed.

Institutional cafeteria / school / corrections / corporate dining: worker loads trays and clamshell meal packs on a serving line with sporks or utensil kits, napkins and condiment packets, and replenishes accessory caddies during service.

Drive-in carhop, curbside pickup or catering delivery packing station: worker assembles the carry tray or bag with napkins, straws, plastic utensils, sauce/ketchup packets and salt matched to the order before it goes out to the car.

sources.claim: B.PRO/BRIMATO's ASV-1 tray-line automation includes a cutlery placing module: packaged cutlery sets are supplied from a dispenser trolley in a machine 'garage', identified by camera, and placed on each tray by a gantry robot fully automatically, with item selection driven by the patient-card barcode.

sources.system: B.PRO ASV-1 + BVA-800 at Universitaetsklinikum Frankfurt
sources.title: B.PRO Catering in hospitals – automated into the future | B.PRO
sources.claim: The ASV-1 tray automation is in service at University Hospital Frankfurt, installed on the hospital's food-portioning conveyor, automatically handling trays, patient cards and plates/bowls fed from dispenser trolleys; the hospital also runs the BVA-800 cutlery packaging system.
sources.transferJustification: Same tray line and same modular system as the cutlery-placing module; establishes that these modules run in a real hospital central kitchen, on a conveyor rebuilt with dispenser-fed automation modules.

sources.system: BRIMATO cutlery sorting/packaging automation (ABS, BVA/CPM series)
sources.date: product page retrieved July 2026 (products in market since ~2016)
sources.title: BRIMATO Catering Automation Technology GmbH: BRIMATO Automatisierung rund um das Besteck.
sources.claim: BRIMATO's cutlery automation sorts and hygienically packs cutlery and automatically adds further items such as salt, pepper, toothpicks or napkins to the sets that are subsequently placed on trays.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the accessory items of this task (cutlery, napkin, salt, pepper) being assembled automatically into the set that the tray-line gantry then loads onto the tray.

sources.date: in market since ~2016; page retrieved July 2026
sources.title: BRIMATO Catering Automation Technology GmbH: The cutlery packaging system BVA-800 automates the hygienically packaging process of cutlery
sources.claim: The BVA-800 packs cutlery sets at 800 sets/hour and automatically adds a standardized serviette to each set; washed cutlery is fed to the machine by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Napkin-plus-utensil assembly step of this task performed by a machine when the cutlery is presented to it, i.e. with the work brought to the machine.

sources.system: Chef Robotics ChefOS piece-picking / CPG kitting
sources.title: Chef Robots Can Now Help Automate Consumer Packaged Goods Assembly | Blog | Chef Robotics
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI food-assembly robots perform kitting on production lines, picking cutlery kits, sauce sachets and seasoning packets out of unstructured bins with vision and placing them at specified orientations into the correct compartments of cups, bowls and trays.
sources.transferJustification: Loading meal trays with utensil kits and condiment sachets is the same pick-and-place of the same accessory objects into the same multi-compartment meal trays, performed on a conveyor line rather than by hand.

sources.system: Chef Robotics AI food assembly system
sources.title: Chef Robotics | Physical AI for the food industry
sources.claim: Chef robots are in production use at more than a dozen ..., assembling meals into customers' own trays and compartments on their own conveyors.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment maturity and the actual operating environment (customer food-production conveyor lines) for the kitting capability cited above.

sources.system: S-TEC / Fraunhofer IPA 'Automatisierung der Speisentablettierung fuer Kliniken' demonstrator
sources.developer: Fraunhofer IPA with Service GmbH Schwarzwald hospital catering
sources.title: S-TEC | Automatisierung der Speisentablettierung für Kliniken
sources.claim: A Fraunhofer IPA / S-TEC project on automating hospital tray-line assembly in existing central kitchens reached only about 80% grasp success at 7 s per pick with a 6-axis suction-gripper arm, and cutlery sets were explicitly an exception it could not handle that way.
sources.transferJustification: Directly this task (placing packaged items and cutlery sets on hospital trays); shows that at an ordinary kitchen tray-line station, rather than on a purpose-built dispenser-fed line, reliability stays below worker quality and cutlery sets fail.

sources.title: B.PRO automation for processes in the catering sector | B.PRO
sources.claim: BRIMATO's catering automation (cutlery sorting/packing and tray-line placement modules) is sold to hospitals, airline caterers, large canteens ... and event caterers, with tray-line solutions offered from about 2,000 trays per day.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the same conveyor-fed accessory-placing automation is applied to canteen, cafeteria and catering tray assembly, supporting transfer to the cafeteria and catering-packing instances at the purpose-built-line tier.

tasks.label: Take food orders and relay orders to kitchens or serving counters so they can be filled.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Monitor food preparation or serving techniques to ensure that proper procedures are followed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital patient tray line: a diet aide/tray service worker watches the assembly line as coworkers plate meals, checking that diet-order procedures, portioning, garnishing, tray-card matching, hot/cold holding and glove/sanitation practices are being followed; flags deviations verbally to the coworker or reports them to the dietary supervisor.

Residential care / nursing home dining room: the server observes how aides and other servers plate and present texture-modified and therapeutic diets (puree, thickened liquids), whether hand hygiene, utensil handling and resident-identification procedures are followed, and points out or reports lapses.

Hotel room service: the attendant checks, before leaving the kitchen, that the plated order was prepared and covered per standard (correct items, plate covers, hot boxes, condiment setup) and observes whether kitchen and expo staff follow presentation and food-safety procedures; raises issues with the chef or supervisor.

Institutional serving line (hospital cafeteria, school, corporate dining, catered function run by the facility): the food server watches other servers' portioning technique, utensil and glove use, hot-hold/cold-hold practice and line replenishment, and corrects technique or notifies the lead.

Training/orientation context: an experienced nonrestaurant server spot-checks a newly hired server's or volunteer's serving technique during a shift, comparing it against facility procedure and coaching or documenting the result for the supervisor.

tasks.label: Remove trays and stack dishes for return to kitchen after meals are finished.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute-care hospital: after the meal pass, a dietary aide walks the unit, enters occupied patient rooms, lifts the used tray (plate cover, bowls, cup with liquid, cutlery, condiment wrappers, sometimes spilled food) off the overbed table, notes/records leftovers, slides the tray into a slot on the tray cart, and wheels the loaded cart back to the kitchen dish room. Patients, visitors, IV poles and personal items are present.

Nursing home / assisted living dining room: after residents finish, the server clears plates, bowls, cups and flatware from tables (many not on trays), scrapes waste, stacks like dishes on a bussing cart or in bus tubs, and returns them to the dish room; residents, walkers and wheelchairs are still in the room.

Institutional cafeteria (school, hospital cafeteria, corporate or campus dining): attendant collects abandoned trays and dishes from dining tables, empties waste, stacks trays and dishes at the dish-return window or onto racks/conveyor, and moves them to the dishroom during a busy meal period.

Hotel/resort room service: attendant retrieves trays and roll-in tables left inside guest rooms or in corridors, consolidates and stacks dishes and glassware, loads them onto a cart, and takes them by service elevator to the kitchen; corridors and rooms are hotel-controlled but layouts and tray placement vary.

Other nonrestaurant service: banquet/catering events, airline or rail catering, correctional or military dining. Worker strips tables or receives returned carts/trays, stacks china, glassware and flatware into racks or tubs and returns them to the kitchen/washing area, often at high volume under time pressure.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics' three-arm dishwashing system operates autonomously in commercial restaurant dish rooms, running 24 hours a day washing ..., with the second installation running fully independently with only restaurant staff attending it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial dish-room dishwashing. It is the same objects (used plates, cups, cutlery with food residue) and the same actions the instance requires once work is brought to a station - taking used dishes off the presentation container, destacking/stacking them and racking them for the wash line.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The same system picks used cups out of bus tubs filled with spilled liquids and peels dirty, greasy plates off stacks, switching grippers autonomously; it also lifts and pushes in dish racks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling soiled tableware in a dish pit. Destacking and stacking dirty plates and handling cups with liquid residue is precisely the manipulation the 'stack dishes for return to kitchen' step requires.

sources.title: W-Robo | Dish Sorting Robot (TechMagic) / finibo (Fujimak)
sources.claim: TechMagic's W-Robo dish-sorting robot, sold with Fujimak as 'finibo', automatically picks tableware off a conveyor dishwasher outlet and sorts/stacks it by type at up to 600 pieces per hour using machine-learned image recognition, installed in commercial washing areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting and stacking tableware presented on a dishroom conveyor. It covers the 'stack dishes' element of this task with the same objects (plates, bowls, cups) in a purpose-built cell where the work is brought to the machine.

sources.title: Franciscan Health Crown Point Robots Assisting In Kitchen, Environmental Deliveries
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots move carts of meal trays between the hospital kitchen and nursing floors and return soiled items, operating in hospital corridors and elevators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital cart logistics. It substantiates only the 'return to kitchen' transport leg at E2; loading of used trays onto the cart is still done by staff, so it does not substantiate the removal/stacking work.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi line performs food running and table bussing in restaurants, hotels and senior living dining rooms, hauling dirty dishes back to the ... area on stabilizing trays that staff load; the robots have no manipulator arm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dining-room bussing transport. It shows the transport half of the task is routine at E2, but because a person must place the dishes on the robot it does not substantiate autonomous removal of trays from tables or bedsides.

sources.title: Iris Ohyama to acquire service robot maker Smile Robotics - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Smile Robotics' ACUR-C is a mobile manipulator with an arm that collects trays of used dishes from tables and carries them away, aimed at restaurants, clinics and nursing homes; it remained a startup prototype and the company was acquired by Iris Ohyama in 2023 with no evidence of production deployments.

sources.system: π0 generalist policy on bimanual/mobile manipulators
sources.title: π0: Our First Generalist Policy
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0 policy was fine-tuned to bus a table autonomously, picking dishes, cutlery and cups into a bussing bin ..., sometimes stacking several dishes together; this is a laboratory research demonstration with imperfect success rates.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same task (clearing used dishes from a table and consolidating them for return), performed autonomously on a fixed table in a lab, which corroborates feasibility of the manipulation when the work is presented to the machine.

tasks.label: Carry food, silverware, or linen on trays or use carts to carry trays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital patient meal service, bulk leg: loading assembled patient trays into enclosed meal carts in the nutrition-services kitchen and moving the loaded carts through service corridors and elevators to nursing-unit galleys/lobbies on schedule for tray line times, then hauling soiled-tray carts back to the dish room; also moving linen and supply carts.

Hospital and skilled-nursing room leg: taking individual trays off the floor cart and hand-carrying them into occupied patient/resident rooms, working around IV poles, visitors, isolation precautions and cluttered bedside areas, placing the tray on the overbed table within reach, and retrieving it after the meal.

Senior living / assisted living community dining room: carrying trays of plated hot meals, beverages and silverware from the kitchen expo to residents' assigned tables during a seating, and carrying soiled dishes and linen back to the dish room, amid walkers, wheelchairs and slow-moving residents.

Institutional cafeteria, college or corporate dining hall, and banquet floor: carrying loaded trays, hotel pans, stacks of dishes, silverware bins and linens between the kitchen, serving lines and dining floor; wheeling utility carts; clearing tray-return stations during a rush.

Hotel room service: carrying a tray or wheeling a covered room-service cart with plates, silverware and linen from the kitchen through back-of-house service elevators and guest corridors to a guest room, knocking, and handing off or setting up in the room.

Drive-in carhop / curbside: carrying a tray of food and drinks out across the restaurant parking lot to a customer's parked car in whatever weather, hanging the tray on the car window or handing it through, and later collecting the tray.

sources.title: TUG Robots Enhance Meal Delivery at Scripps Hospital - Scripps Health
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots carry and transport patient meal trays through hospital hallways and elevators at Scripps Memorial Hospital La Jolla; staff meet the robot at the elevator lobby to take the food to patients.

sources.title: Hospital uses robots to deliver patient meals
sources.claim: Reading Hospital uses a fleet of eight TUG robots to transport patient food from nutrition services to ... building.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
sources.claim: A five-robot TUG fleet at Froedtert Hospital autonomously picks up, transports and drops off heavy carts of soiled linens and waste across a 2.5-million-square-foot campus, completing over 78,000 deliveries in 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: wheeled cart transport of linen/waste on hospital routes, identical to the linen and soiled-tray cart moves in the bulk hospital instance.

sources.claim: A senior living pilot at The Homestead (Springwell Senior Living) evaluated Bear Robotics' Servi and Richtech's Matradee as dining-room food runners delivering food from the kitchen to specific tables in the dining room and collecting dishes.

sources.title: How Food Robots Can Improve Senior Living Dining | Direct Supply
sources.claim: Servi is marketed and sold into senior living communities as a food runner that delivers food to the dining room ... returns dishware to the kitchen.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi family of service robots run food and bus tables using LiDAR navigation in active restaurant and hotel dining environments.

sources.title: Room Service and Delivery Robots: Logistics Automation in Hospitality
sources.claim: A hotel uses Keenon's W3 tray ... autonomous around-the-clock room service, navigating public areas and integrating with elevators to bring meals and amenities to guest rooms.

sources.claim: YOTEL hotels in Boston, Miami, Singapore and ... operate delivery robots that navigate corridors and call elevators to bring amenities and room service orders to guest rooms.

sources.title: Relay Delivery Robots – Leader in delivery robots for hospitals and hotels
sources.claim: Relay delivery robots are sold and operated for autonomous hotel guest-room delivery of room-service items and for food delivery within hospitals.

sources.title: 5 Things to Know About McDonald's New Test Restaurant in Texas
sources.claim: McDonald's Fort Worth test restaurant operates a purpose-built Order Ahead Lane in which a food and beverage conveyor carries the completed order out to the customer waiting in their vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: carside handoff of a completed food order to a customer in a vehicle, the same accepted output as a carhop carrying a tray out to a parked car, achieved here by a machine in a purpose-built lane.

tasks.label: Record amounts and types of special food items served to customers.

tasks.label: Stock service stations with items, such as ice, napkins, or straws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital food-service worker replenishes the tray-line and floor nourishment-room service stations: carries cases of straws, napkins, condiment packets, lids and cups from the storeroom on a cart, breaks open poly-wrapped bundles, loads napkin/straw holders and condiment caddies, scoops or fills the ice bin at the beverage station, and checks par levels between meal periods while other staff work around them.

Institutional cafeteria / corporate or college dining self-serve station (also hospital public cafeteria): mid-service restocking of napkin dispensers, straw and lid bins, cutlery caddies, cup dispensers, condiment pumps and the ice bin at the drink station, done in a crowded serving area during peak hours with customers moving through.

Senior-living / residential-care dining room: before and between meal seatings, stocking the beverage and coffee station with ice, cups, napkins, straws, sugar/creamer, and thickener packets, and restocking the pantry cart used for room service to residents; tight aisles, walkers and residents present.

Hotel floor pantry, room-service side station, or banquet service station: stocking the station with ice from the floor ice machine, linen napkins, straws, condiments, glassware and silverware rollups before a function or shift, moving supplies through back-of-house corridors and service elevators.

Off-premises / mobile setting: catering event tent, outdoor drive-in carhop station, food cart or stadium concession point; supplies unloaded from a van and used to stock a temporary service station with iced coolers, napkin and straw caddies and condiments, with layout improvised at each site and weather a factor.

sources.title: Telexistence to install AI re-stocking robots in 300 convenience stores across Japan
sources.claim: TX SCARA is a rail-mounted robot arm installed behind the refrigerated display case in convenience stores that autonomously picks bottles and cans from stacked crates and places them into the customer-facing shelf lanes, at up to 1,000 units a day, deployed at 300 FamilyMart stores; remote staff intervene only in rare failure cases.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing a customer-facing holder with packaged consumer items from bulk cases. Same core action as stocking a service station (pick packaged item from case, place in the correct customer-facing slot), same object scale, and the robot's workspace is a fixed, purpose-built rail cell with crates presented in known positions, i.e. an E1 presentation.

sources.title: Amazon debuts its first-ever warehouse robot — 'Vulcan' — with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously stows individual items of varied shape into one-foot-square fabric pod compartments already holding other items, using force sensing to make space without damaging goods; deployed at fulfillment centers in Spokane and Hamburg.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting loose consumer items into small, partly-filled compartments. This is the manipulation core of loading a napkin holder, straw bin or condiment caddy — tight insertion among existing stock with contact force control — demonstrated at commercial reliability inside a fenced robotic workcell (E1 presentation).

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick piece-picking cells autonomously grasp a wide range of individual consumer SKUs presented in totes and place them into order containers; deployed across Staples' North American fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous each-picking of mixed packaged goods (including bagged/deformable items) into a target container within a fenced cell. Stocking a service station caddy from presented supply cases requires the same object variety, precision and placement accuracy when the work is fixtured and presented (E1).

sources.system: Follett Ice Manager / Ice Pro DB650SA ice bagger-dispenser

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic transport and filling of ice into a destination bin/dispenser — the ice component of stocking a service station — performed by machine-controlled equipment in a purpose-built plumbed installation (E1 presentation). Bagger models fill containers under push-button/foot control, so only the Ice Manager bin-fill is counted as autonomous.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics' ADAM robot bartender to serve drinks at 2024 MLB All-Star Game
sources.claim: Richtech's ADAM dual-arm robot autonomously prepares and serves drinks — handling cups, ice and dispensers inside an enclosed kiosk/bar cell — at commercial venues including Globe Life Field, T-Mobile Arena and Kennedy Space Center, plus boba and coffee shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling of cups, ice and beverage-station consumables in a purpose-built beverage cell. Shows commercial-grade robotic handling of the same class of service-station items when the station is engineered around the machine (E1).

sources.system: 'From Pixels to Shelf' shelf-stocking mobile manipulator
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: A mobile manipulator autonomously stocked and fronted supermarket shelves with over 98% pick-and-place success across 724 events, but only in a laboratory replicating supermarket conditions with ArUco markers for shelf navigation, and the authors state performance and cost remain inferior to human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile-manipulator shelf stocking. It substantiates marker-assisted, engineered-layout stocking (E1) and, by the authors' own benchmark that the system is inferior to human workers and was validated only in a lab replica, it fails to substantiate worker-quality stocking inside a real E2 facility.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: The Operating Room Bot research prototype autonomously picked supply items from a cart and placed them into the correct storage bins in an operating-room logistics setup, reporting 96% restocking success and 80% retrieval success.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restocking healthcare supply bins from a cart with a mobile manipulator — the same fetch-and-place structure as stocking a hospital service station. It is a laboratory-style OR logistics setup with known bin locations, so it supports only an engineered/E1-style presentation, not an as-found hospital pantry at worker quality.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator is deployed in more than 25 ... and has completed over one million autonomous deliveries, but its work is point-to-point transport of items in secure drawers that staff load and unload, not replenishing dispensers or caddies at a service station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous supply transport inside a real hospital (E2). It shows navigation and delivery are solved in that environment, but the delivered items are loaded and unloaded by humans, so it does not substantiate completing the stocking instance itself at E2.

Salads, cold bowls, fruit and cheese plates and desserts: filling bowls or containers from prepped ingredient pans, adding proteins and dressings, plating side salads and desserts for cafeteria display, patient trays, or room-service orders.

tasks.label: Determine where patients or patrons would like to eat their meals and help them get situated.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital patient room: dietary aide brings the meal tray in, greets the patient, asks whether they want to eat in bed or in the bedside chair, raises the head of the bed, clears clutter and swings the over-bed table into position, sets the tray within reach, opens lids/cartons and makes sure the call light is reachable.

Nursing home / assisted living communal dining room at mealtime: residents arrive with walkers or in wheelchairs; server asks where they wish to sit, escorts or wheels them to a table, brakes the chair or pulls out and pushes in a dining chair, applies a clothing protector, and positions the plate, cup and utensils within reach.

Senior living / senior center dining hall, fully ambulatory patrons: patron enters, server asks where they'd like to sit, leads them to an open table, and the meal is brought to the table where the patron takes it themselves; no physical handling of the person needed.

Assisted living or long-term care in-room tray service: server carries the tray to the resident's room, asks whether they want it at the small table by the window, in the recliner or in bed, clears and moves the side table or repositions the recliner, and settles the resident with the tray in reach.

Hotel in-room dining: attendant wheels the room-service cart into the guest room, asks the guest where they would like it set up (by the window, at the desk, bedside, balcony), unfolds and positions the table, arranges chairs, presents and uncovers the dishes and seats the guest.

Other venues: banquet/senior-center service, school or hospital cafeteria escorting, and curbside/car-hop service where the server determines where the patron will eat (in the car, at an outdoor table) and hooks the tray to the window or settles the patron at a bench.

sources.title: PAL Robotics completes testing of robots with Accerion positioning sensors in hospitals to fight Covid-19
sources.claim: PAL Robotics' TIAGo Delivery and TIAGo Conveyor robots were tested in Barcelona-area hospitals transporting food trays to patient rooms; an actuated conveyor transfers the tray onto a table in the room, aimed at isolated patients who are self-sufficient. No preference-taking or patient positioning is performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital meal-tray transport to the patient room. It bounds what deployed hospital robots do — tray transfer onto a fixed table — and shows they neither elicit where the patient wants to eat nor position the patient, bed or over-bed table.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics

sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital last-mile delivery with a mobile arm. It is the most capable deployed hospital manipulator and its accepted scope stops at item transport, indicating patient-contact set-up work is outside demonstrated capability.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: food running in a senior-living dining room. Same environment and mealtime workflow as the seating task; it shows a commercial robot can bring the meal to the table an ambulatory resident occupies, while resident handling stays with staff.

tasks.label: Run cash registers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Campus/corporate/hospital cafeteria checkout counter at lunch rush: diner arrives with a tray of packaged items and open plates from the hot line; attendant identifies each item, keys/scans it into the POS touchscreen, totals the sale, takes a tap/swipe card payment, and hands over the printed receipt.

Same counter, cash tender: attendant rings the order, accepts bills and coins, opens the drawer, counts back correct change, and returns change plus receipt; must be accurate and fast with a line waiting.

Snack bar, coffee/beverage stand, or concession register: small-ticket items, high peak throughput, payment by staff badge, student meal-plan/declining-balance card, mobile wallet or card; occasional item lookup or simple upsell.

Start/end of shift register duties: count and verify the opening float, run the register X/Z report at close, count the drawer down, reconcile cash to the sales total, and secure the deposit for pickup.

Exception and service handling at the register: voids and refunds, manager overrides, coupons/comps/employee discounts, unpriced or unfamiliar items, split or declined payments, price disputes and questions from patrons, while keeping the line moving.

The kiosk is a fixed machine without manipulators, so it substantiates only the ring-up/payment-capture portion of running a register; the physically actuating portion (accepting notes and coins, dispensing change, printing receipts) is substantiated by the cash-recycler evidence items. Same cafeteria/concession counters and same items.

tasks.label: Scrape and stack dirty dishes and carry dishes and other tableware to kitchens for cleaning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant, mid-service: busser clears a vacated four-top of plates, glassware, flatware and napkins, scrapes food scraps into a waste bin at the bus station, stacks the dishes in a bus tub, carries the loaded tub through an occupied dining room to the dish room, and unloads/racks it.

Cafeteria, food court or corporate dining hall dish-return station: diners deposit trays/tubs at the return window or conveyor; the attendant strips them, scrapes food into the disposal, drops flatware into a soak bin, stacks plates and racks cups, and feeds the conveyor dish machine during a rush.

Banquet/catering event in a hotel ballroom: attendants clear several courses from round tables of 8-10, stack plates and glassware on oval trays or bus carts, wheel them to a back-of-house dish station, scrape and rack, and return for the next course under tight course timing.

Bar/lounge barback: collects used glassware, shakers and small plates from the bar top, high-tops and patio tables, empties liquids and garnish waste, loads glass racks, carries racks to the underbar or main dish machine, and returns clean racks to the bar.

Hospital or school tray-line return: soiled meal trays come back on delivery carts or a conveyor; the attendant strips each tray of plate covers, dishes, cups, flatware and disposables, scrapes waste, and loads dish racks and the flight-type machine on a fixed schedule.

tasks.label: Wipe tables or seats with dampened cloths or replace dirty tablecloths.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual full-service restaurant dining room: after a party leaves and dishes are cleared, the attendant sprays/dampens a cloth, wipes the tabletop (crumbs, grease, syrup, condiment rings), lifts and wipes under the condiment caddy, then wipes chair seats or booth benches and pushes chairs in — all in under a minute per table, with guests and servers moving around.

Cafeteria, food court, or quick-service dining area (school, hospital, corporate, QSR): repeated high-volume wiping of uniform flat tabletops between diners during a rush, damp cloth plus sanitizer, tables in fixed rows with standard fixed or loose seating, premises controlled by the institution.

Bar and lounge area: wiping the bar top and rail between drinks, plus high-top tables and stool seats, dealing with sticky drink residue, condensation rings, napkins and straws, working around glassware, taps and guests seated at the bar.

Banquet hall or fine-dining room: stripping soiled tablecloths and overlays from round and rectangular tables (bundling crumbs inside), laying fresh linen centered with an even drop on all sides and no wrinkles, then wiping chair seats and backs before re-setting.

Outdoor patio or sidewalk café seating: wiping weather- and debris-soiled tables, umbrella-base tables and chair seats (pollen, dust, bird droppings, rain spots) with a damp cloth, on furniture guests have moved around on uneven paving.
Closing or deep-clean pass after service: wiping booth seat backs and crevices, chair legs and rungs, table pedestals and edges, high chairs and booster seats with a dampened cloth and sanitizer.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic contact cleaning of a fixtured, conveyed surface to an accepted production standard. It transfers to E1 table/seat wiping because the workpiece is presented in a known pose and the robot maintains controlled contact over flat and curved surfaces.

sources.transferJustification: Directly the linen half of this task (spreading a tablecloth over a ...), executed by bimanual robots at a fixed table with the cloth presented in a defined starting configuration — the E1 counterfactual.

sources.transferJustification: Assessment of the wiping/surface-cleaning subtask that constitutes this task; used only to bound positive judgments, not to support one.

tasks.label: Set tables with clean linens, condiments, or other supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service casual/family restaurant, mid-shift reset: after a table is cleared and wiped, the attendant places a fresh paper placemat/napkin, rolled silverware bundles, condiment caddy or bottles, coasters and menus for 2-4 covers, then squares chairs. Dining room is busy with guests, servers and bags in the aisles; the reset must be finished in a minute or two to turn the table.

Institutional cafeteria (school, hospital, corporate, senior living): before and during meal periods, put out napkin dispensers, condiment bottles and packet caddies, salt/pepper, flatware bins, trays and paper goods on dining tables and condiment stations. Fixed layout, standard-issue supplies, high volume, low precision requirements.

Buffet / beverage-and-coffee service replenishment during service: refill and restock sugar caddies, creamers, napkin holders, straws, condiment bottles, and put out stacks of side plates and cutlery at service stations and on tables as they run down.

Banquet/catering ballroom setup: lay tablecloths (and skirting) on 20-50 round tables, then set each cover - charger or base plate, three to four pieces of flatware to standard spacing, two glasses, folded linen napkin, salt and pepper, centerpiece - before guests arrive; empty room, tight deadline before doors open.

Fine dining pre-service setup: dress deuces and four-tops with pressed linen cloths (even drop, no wrinkles), polish and place glassware and flatware to precise spacing, fold linen napkins, place condiments/butter and a small centerpiece; the setting is inspected by a manager before service.

sources.title: Chef Robots Can Now Help Automate Consumer Packaged Goods Assembly | Chef Robotics
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' commercially deployed food-line robots pick and place discrete items - including cutlery kits, sauce sachets and seasoning packets - into trays, cups and bowls in specified orientations on production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: kitting cutlery/condiment packets onto trays presented by a conveyor. Setting a table at E1 means placing the same class of objects (wrapped flatware, condiment packets, caddies) onto a surface presented to the machine, at similar precision and orientation requirements.

sources.title: Chef Launches Piece-Picking Capability to Automate Individual Food Items in Meal Assembly - Perishable News
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' robots place individual items into meal trays in a specified orientation on production lines that have produced over 100 million servings since 2022 for customers such as Amy's Kitchen and Sunbasket.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tray assembly. Demonstrates commercial-rate, orientation-controlled placement of small items onto a presented tray, which is the manipulation core of laying out supplies on a table brought to the machine.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics' three-arm dishwashing system runs autonomously 24 hours a day in multiple restaurants, picking and placing dirty plates, transparent glasses and bunches of silverware with millimeter-accurate perception at hundreds of dishes per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dish handling in a fixed restaurant dish station. Same objects as table setting (plates, glassware, flatware), same grasp precision and breakage constraints, at commercial pace, with the work presented to the machine in tubs and racks.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model Offering Fully Autonomous, Round-the-Clock Dexterity
sources.claim: DYNA-1 autonomously folded 800+ napkins in a continuous ... run to client production-quality standards and has been used in customer environments, showing reliable handling of small table linens by stationary dual arms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: napkin folding at a fixed station. Supports reliable machine handling of napkins/small linens presented to the robot, but covers folding only - not draping and aligning a tablecloth over a table.

sources.system: Musashi-W humanoid with dynamic cloth manipulation model
sources.title: Dynamic Cloth Manipulation Considering Variable Stiffness and Material Change Using Deep Predictive Model with Parametric Bias
sources.claim: Draping a cloth over a table remains a research demonstration: the Musashi-W humanoid spread a cloth on a desk 'like a table cloth' and then placed a basket on it in a single integrated laboratory experiment.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related to laying table linen, but it is a one-off lab experiment with no reported success rate, cycle time, or wrinkle/alignment quality, so it does not substantiate worker-quality banquet or fine-dining linen laying.

sources.transferJustification: Related hospitality mobile-manipulation work. It shows what deployed hospitality robots currently do - transport, laundry, drink prep - and that no cited system sets covers on dining-room tables, which is why the E2 counterfactual is not met.

tasks.label: Clean up spilled food or drink or broken dishes and remove empty bottles and trash.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-service in a restaurant/bar: a guest spills a drink or drops food on a table, booth seat or bar top. Attendant grabs a cloth/sanitizer, wipes the surface and seat, picks up wet napkins and food chunks, re-sets the spot, all within a minute or two while guests are seated nearby.

A drink or plate of food is spilled on the dining room or cafeteria hard floor during service. Attendant sets a wet-floor sign, sweeps up solids and mops/dries the spot around seated patrons and chair legs so no slip hazard remains.

A glass or plate shatters on the dining room floor (often with liquid). Attendant contains the area, picks up large shards by hand or with a broom and dustpan, sweeps fine chips from under tables and along booth bases, and verifies no glass remains near food or guests.

Clearing empty bottles, glasses, cans, cups, napkins, straws and food waste from tables and the bar top into bus tubs, recycling and trash bins during and after service; separating trash from dishware and wiping the surface afterward.

Emptying full trash and recycling receptacles in the dining area/tray-return station: pulling the liner, tying the bag, replacing the liner, wheeling or carrying bags through service corridors to the dumpster/compactor, and wiping the bin.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wet floor cleaning in a large occupied retail facility; the mopping-up of spilled liquids and food soil on hard floors is the same physical operation performed by a cafeteria attendant.

sources.claim: The Avidbots Neo autonomous floor ... cleans large public facilities such as airports without pre-programmed routes, adapting to people and obstacles.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous surface cleaning and small-trash pickup inside an institution-controlled facility. It shows facility-tier surface cleaning is deployable, but only in a closed, pre-mapped room, not on dining tables among seated guests.
