sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0 model autonomously busses a table: it picks dishes into a bussing bin and garbage into a trash bin, including shaking trash off plates, in a controlled table setup.

sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 autonomously performs kitchen clean-up in homes it was not trained in, including wiping a spill, putting dishes in the sink and putting items away, though it often does not succeed on the first try.

sources.claim: Independent 2026 assessment confirms Physical Intelligence robots have autonomously wiped surfaces with sponges or towels ... cleaned countertops, with countertop cleaning approaching 'validated in lab' but no integrated, deployment-grade cleaning system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiping soiled horizontal surfaces with ordinary cloths. Comparable objects and precision to wiping a table or bar top, but demonstrated only in lab/home setups, not in a serving dining room.

sources.title: Restaurant Robots — Servers, Bussers & Kitchen (RobotLAB)
sources.claim: The PUDU MT1 commercial sweeping robot autonomously collects dust, leaves and large debris from floors of warehouses, garages and supermarkets, and Pudu cleaning robots use AI waste detection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous collection of hard floor debris. Transfers partly to sweeping up shards of a broken plate on an open floor lane, though not to picking large shards from under occupied tables or verifying none remain.

tasks.label: Maintain adequate supplies of items, such as clean linens, silverware, glassware, dishes, or trays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant, mid-shift: attendant keeps dining-room service/side stations stocked - carries racks of clean glasses, bins of rolled silverware, stacks of plates, napkins and trays from the dish area through a busy dining room and puts them away in station shelves and bins between seatings.

Cafeteria or buffet serving line during meal service: refill tray stacks and self-leveling plate/bowl/cup dispensers, silverware cylinders and station supplies from carts wheeled out of the dish room, working around a queue of diners.

Clean side of the warewashing area: pull clean racks off the dish machine, sort and stack plates, bowls and cups, sort flatware into cylinders, re-rack and polish glassware, and move the clean stock onto shelves/carts so the floor can draw from it.

Barback duty in a bar/lounge: run racks of clean glassware from the glasswasher to the bar wells, overhead racks and back bar, keeping each glass type at par through a busy service in tight space behind the bar.

Banquet/catering setup in a hotel: pull par levels of table linens, china, flatware and glassware from the storeroom, load carts and stage them at service stations in the function room before an event.

Par-level check and storeroom runs: count napkins, to-go items, clean linen and dishware, carry cases and linen bundles from the stockroom to service stations and linen shelves, and report shortages to the manager.

sources.system: HOBART fully-automatic warewash system (FTNi flight-type machines with automatic separating unit, tray stacking carriage, cutlery sorting)
sources.date: 2026 (product line in service; university canteen installation referenced)
sources.title: Fully-automatic systems | HOBART
sources.claim: Commercially sold fully-automatic warewash systems for institutional kitchens produce the clean supply automatically: trays are stacked onto a stacking carriage, cutlery is ejected into baskets and can be fed onward into an automatic cutlery sorter, with the dirty side loaded by an automatic separating unit rather than staff.
sources.transferJustification: This is the clean end of the warewashing line: it delivers the stacked trays and basketed/sorted cutlery that the attendant would otherwise stack and sort by hand - same objects, same accepted output as maintaining supplies of clean silverware, dishes and trays, with the work conveyed to the machine.

sources.date: 2020 product coverage; in catalog as of 2026
sources.title: ACS800 - Hygienic and efficient cutlery sorting solution | Wexiodisk
sources.claim: A commercially available cutlery sorter takes clean, dry flatware fed automatically from the dishwashing line, recognizes and separates up to eight cutlery types into boxes at about 3,600 pieces per hour, and signals when a box of sorted cutlery is full; sold for flight kitchens, hospitals and large canteens.
sources.transferJustification: Replenishing the silverware supply consists of getting washed flatware sorted by type into usable holders; this machine performs exactly that step on clean flatware presented by a conveyor.

sources.system: MEIKO / Fizyr / Yaskawa automated dish sorting and loading system
sources.developer: MEIKO Group with Fizyr and Yaskawa Europe
sources.date: June-September 2025 (demonstrated at Automatica 2025; partnership announced September 2025)
sources.title: MEIKO Group Taps Fizyr and Yaskawa Europe For Automated Dishwashing
sources.claim: A vision-AI robotic cell autonomously identifies and picks unsorted used plates, bowls and cups off a conveyor and places them ... dishwasher, demonstrated for commercial kitchens by Meiko with Yaskawa arms and Fizyr vision.
sources.transferJustification: Racking and stacking clean dishware is the same pick-and-place problem in reverse: identical objects (plates, bowls, cups), comparable precision and fragility, in a conveyor-fed cell - evidence that dishware supply can be handled by machine when presented in a fixtured flow.

sources.system: Kannegiesser AutomaticDry Work Line with Robofeed RFT and SFM-E flat-linen folding machine
sources.title: Next Level Laundry: Kannegiesser
sources.claim: Automated industrial laundry finishing lines feed, fold, sort and stack mixed batches of hotel flatwork autonomously, including a folding machine that sorts and stacks up to ... item types such as sheets and tablecloths, plus automated storage and dispatch of the finished stacks.
sources.transferJustification: The linen half of the task - producing sorted, folded, stacked clean table linen ready to be drawn from - is performed by machine on linen presented in a purpose-built flow.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile case-handling robot unloads cartons from trailers onto conveyors and builds palletized orders using onboard vision, deployed commercially at DHL (10 units across three countries as of June 2025) at roughly 700 cases per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Storeroom replenishment of cased supplies (napkins, to-go items, boxed wares) is case handling of the same object class and precision, performed autonomously where the cases are presented to the machine.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics' ADAM serves drinks at Kennedy Space Center - The Robot Report
sources.claim: A two-armed stationary service robot autonomously grasps and handles cups and prepares and serves drinks at a fixed beverage station in a retail store, having served more than 16,000 drinks ... its Las Vegas location.
sources.transferJustification: Handling drinkware - grasping cups from a dispenser or rack and placing them precisely without breakage - is the manipulation at the core of keeping a bar's clean-glassware supply at par, shown here in a purpose-built station.

sources.title: Bear Robotics (Servi) - RestaurantTools.ai
sources.claim: The restaurant robots deployed at scale in dining rooms are autonomous transport platforms: they navigate with LiDAR and cameras to carry food out and dirty dishes back, but staff load and unload them; they do not pick up or put away wares.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant: it establishes what is achievable in the dining room as found (E2) - autonomous transport only, with human loading and unloading - so the restocking instances are not completed at that tier.

tasks.label: Locate items requested by customers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant dining room: a guest asks for a common table item (ketchup, hot sauce, extra napkins, a straw, a clean fork). The attendant goes to a standard side/service station in the dining room, finds the item among the stocked supplies, and brings it to the guest's table amid seated diners, pushed-out chairs, and moving servers.

The requested item is not out front: attendant searches back-of-house (dry-goods shelving, walk-in cooler, dish area, bar storeroom) for a specific item — a particular sauce or dressing, a specific to-go container size, a specific glass or bottle a bartender asks for — then carries it out to the guest or the bar.

Guest needs a piece of equipment: high chair, booster seat, extra chair, tray stand, coat hook. The attendant locates it in a storage nook, closet, or stack, carries it through the dining room, and positions it at the table.

Guest has lost a personal item (phone, keys, jacket, child's toy, credit card). The attendant searches under booths, tables, seat cushions, and the floor around the table, and checks the lost-and-found bin.

Cafeteria, buffet, or banquet line: a patron asks for a specific item on or behind the serving line — gluten-free bread, a particular dressing, a clean tray, a specific dessert — and the attendant locates it among the line pans, condiment rack, or back stock and provides it.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi is a commercially deployed mobile manipulator that autonomously picks requested supplies out of hospital supply closets and delivers them to the rooms where staff need them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetching a requested item from an institution's storage and bringing it to the person who asked. Transfer to 'locate items requested by customers': same object class (small consumer-sized packaged goods, bottles, boxes), same precision demand (recognize the right item on a stocked shelf, grasp it, set it down at a destination), and the same class of environment (an institution-controlled indoor facility with corridors, storerooms and people moving through).

sources.title: Moxi — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Diligent markets Moxi for fetching items from central supply ... running patient supplies as routine production workflows in hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above — item retrieval from facility stock on request — establishing that the fetch-and-bring loop is a paid production workflow, not a demo.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi's fetch-and-deliver work is at production scale across many US hospitals, including delivering supplies and equipment, with hundreds of thousands of completed runs.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes reliability/scale of the same related task (requested-item retrieval and delivery inside a structured facility), which the worker-quality bar turns on.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Servi+ | RobotLAB
sources.claim: Servi+ autonomously navigates crowded restaurant dining rooms and delivers items from the kitchen to specific guest tables, showing that the dining-room half of the fetch loop is solved commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running items to a named table in a working restaurant. It covers the transport-and-present half of 'locate items requested by customers' in the exact target environment (a busy dining room with guests, chairs and staff), corroborating that E2 dining-room navigation and tableside delivery are reliable today.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics' ADAM serves drinks at Kennedy Space Center - The Robot Report
sources.claim: ADAM is a commercially deployed dual-arm service robot that autonomously picks cups and ingredients from fixed positions in its station and serves the requested drink to guests in cafeterias, casinos, arenas and cafes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: taking a customer's request at a service counter and retrieving the corresponding item from fixtured stock to hand to that customer. Objects (cups, bottles, condiment-scale containers) and placement precision match; it substantiates the E1 counterfactual where the requested item is presented in known positions.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: TX SCARA autonomously identifies and handles specific bottled and canned beverage SKUs and places them on store shelves, deployed at hundreds of convenience stores with only remote error recovery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking a specified packaged item out of mixed stock and placing it accurately in a customer-facing display inside a retail facility. Same object class (bottles/cans/packaged goods) and same 'find the right SKU among many' recognition problem as locating a requested condiment or beverage.

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Amazon Sparrow autonomously detects, selects and handles individual products out of mixed inventory in fulfillment centers, i.e. locating and picking a specified item in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order picking. Under the E1 counterfactual the requested item arrives fixtured and presented in a tote or rack; Sparrow shows that identifying and retrieving the correct one of many diverse small consumer items in such a setting is a production capability.

sources.system: PaLM-SayCan on Everyday Robots mobile manipulator
sources.title: Google Open-Sources Natural Language Robot Control Method SayCan - InfoQ
sources.claim: Open-ended 'bring me X' fetching by a mobile manipulator in a real office micro-kitchen was demonstrated autonomously but at roughly three-quarters end-to-end success, below staff reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetching an arbitrary spoken-request item in a human food-service space. It bounds how open-ended a request can be before reliability falls below worker quality, informing the negative judgments on unstructured searching.

tasks.label: Fill beverage or ice dispensers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fixed ice/beverage station in a restaurant, cafeteria or hotel: keeping the countertop ice-and-beverage dispenser, under-counter ice storage bin, or bar jockey box supplied with ice through service, checking levels and topping them up so self-serve guests and bartenders never run out.

Ice moved by hand around the floor: scooping ice from the ice machine into buckets or a cart and carrying it to varied points of use during service — salad-bar wells, portable beverage tubs, ice-down of bottled drinks, a second service station across the dining room — with staff and guests moving in the aisles.

Quick-service/cafeteria fountain syrup replenishment: in the back-of-house rack, pulling an empty 3-5 gallon bag-in-box, unscrewing/reconnecting the coupler onto a fresh box, lifting the box into the rack, priming the line, verifying pour and brix, and checking the CO2 supply.

Cafeteria/buffet cold-beverage dispensers on the serving line: mixing or brewing juice, lemonade or iced tea and pouring it into the dispenser bowl or urn, changing a milk-dispenser bag and threading its tube through the valve, wiping spills, all while patrons pass the line.

Hot beverage counter: brewing coffee and filling urns, airpots and thermal dispensers, carrying full satellite servers from the brewer to the counter, refilling the hot-water dispenser, and keeping decaf/regular stations stocked during a breakfast or banquet rush.

Off-site catering or outdoor event: setting up and repeatedly refilling portable beverage dispensers (insulated cambros, iced tea urns, water coolers) at a venue whose layout is improvised — tent, park, client site — with supply staged on folding tables and no fixed equipment.

sources.system: Follett Horizon Elite ice machine with RIDE remote ice delivery

sources.claim: Follett's RIDE remote ice delivery equipment, part of the Horizon Elite ice machine series, automatically transports and fills ice into drink-station dispensers, storage bins and bar jockey boxes in restaurants and other foodservice sites, eliminating manual filling by staff.

tasks.label: Carry food, dishes, trays, or silverware from kitchens or supply departments to serving counters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service or casual restaurant during service: attendant/food runner takes plated hot entrees on a tray or by hand from the kitchen expo window across a busy dining room to a server station, pickup counter or tray jack, weaving between guests, chairs and other staff.

Cafeteria (school, corporate, hospital, buffet) serving-line replenishment: carrying hot full/half hotel pans, bowls, platters and sheet trays of food from the back kitchen to the steam table or cold serving counter and setting them into wells or onto the counter while patrons queue.

Carrying clean dishware from the dish room or storeroom to serving counters and service stations: racks of glassware, stacks of plates, bus tubs, silverware bins and trays, moved on foot or by rack/cart to the station.

Bar-back supply run: carrying ice buckets, glass racks, cases of bottles, mixers, juices and garnish caddies from the walk-in, cellar or kitchen through tight service areas to the service bar counter and wells during a busy shift.

Institutional / hotel long-route delivery: moving loaded carts or racks of meal trays, dishware and food pans from a central kitchen or supply department through corridors and service elevators to a satellite serving counter, unit pantry or banquet buffet line.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Servi+ | RobotLAB
sources.claim: The Servi Plus is deployed to deliver food from the kitchen to ... — the same kitchen-to-serving-counter route this task describes.

sources.claim: TUG robots handle the cart pickup themselves: a TUG is dispatched into the production kitchen to collect the tray order and take it to the drop-off point, returning uncollected trays automatically.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking and placing the same class of steel food pans/trays between fixtured racks and conveyors, which is the purpose-built (E1) form of moving pans of food from kitchen to a serving position.

sources.title: Sweetgreen's Automated 'Infinite Kitchen' Readies for a Step Up in 2025 (QSR Magazine)
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen is a deployed in-restaurant automated line that moves bowls along a conveyor and delivers them to a finishing station for a team member, at 500 bowls per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: purpose-built conveyance carrying prepared food from the production line to the finishing/pickup counter inside a restaurant — the E1 form of carrying food from kitchen to serving counter.

tasks.label: Perform serving, cleaning, or stocking duties in establishments, such as cafeterias or dining rooms, to facilitate customer service.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bussing during service in a full-service casual restaurant: clearing plates, glasses, flatware and trash from just-vacated or in-use tables into a bus tub, hauling it to the dish pit, then wiping the table top, seats and crumbs and resetting the table — done on a crowded floor with guests, servers and carts moving around.

Running and serving on the floor: carrying trays of plated food, water pitchers, coffee, drinks and condiment caddies from the kitchen pass or service station to the correct table across a busy dining room, presenting them to the right guests, and carrying dirty dishes back to the ... area.

Institutional cafeteria (school, hospital, corporate, senior living) line duty: swapping and topping off hot/cold food pans, refilling condiment, beverage, tray, napkin and utensil stations, wiping the serving counter and rails, and clearing trays and dishes from the tray return and dining tables during a rush.

Back-of-house and service-station stocking: pulling racks of clean plates, glassware and silverware off the dish machine, hauling them to side stations and shelves, restocking linens, napkins, ice, coffee supplies and condiments, and supplying the service bar with food items and garnishes.

Pre-service setup / post-service reset in a dining room or banquet space: laying and changing table linens, folding napkins, setting silverware, glassware and plates to a standard cover, placing condiment caddies, and squaring tables and chairs.
Dining-room floor and general cleaning between rushes and at close: sweeping, vacuuming, mopping or scrubbing the dining-room and bar floors and spot-cleaning spills under and around tables.

sources.title: Robot folds 800 napkins in 24 hours as Dyna Robotics launches first commercial-ready embodied AI
sources.claim: DYNA-1 folded over 800 napkins in 24 ... with no human intervention at a fixed dual-arm station, a task the company markets for restaurants and laundromats.

sources.claim: Dishcraft's automated dishroom sorts, scrubs, inspects and racks dishes in commercial kitchens after people pre-stack the dishware into the machine — a purpose-built dish-handling cell producing racked clean dishes.

sources.claim: Digit humanoids in live commercial operation at GXO moved over 100,000 totes, picking totes on and off mobile robots, loading conveyors and stacking containers at floor locations inside a working distribution centre.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repetitive handling of standardized containers between fixed stations. Transfers to hauling and placing dish racks, bus tubs, food pans and supply totes when they are presented at known positions; comparable payload and placement precision.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing and handing coffee and tea drinks to patrons from a fixtured station, covering the 'serve coffee' element of the task inside a purpose-built cell.

tasks.label: Carry trays from food counters to tables for cafeteria patrons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Busy corporate, hospital or college cafeteria at lunch rush: attendant takes a loaded tray (plates, soup bowl, drink) from the serving counter and carries it across a crowded floor to a table for an able-bodied patron whose hands are full or who asked for it to be brought over; patron can take the items themselves once it arrives.

Traditional cafeteria-line restaurant (Luby's/Piccadilly/K&W style) or hotel buffet: a dedicated tray carrier takes the customer's tray at the end of the serving line, walks the customer to a seat of their choosing, sets the tray or the individual plates on the table, and carries the empty tray away.

Senior living, assisted living, or hospital cafeteria: attendant carries the tray for a resident or patient who cannot carry or lift it (walker, wheelchair, tremor), places it on the table in front of them, arranges plate, drink and utensils within reach, and responds to spoken requests.

K-12 school cafeteria at lunch period: attendant carries trays from the serving line to tables for young children or for a student with a cast/disability, in a noisy, crowded room with kids moving unpredictably, dropped food and spills; tray is set on the table in front of the child.

Off-peak or small-venue cafeteria/cafe service: quiet dining room, few patrons, short trip from counter to a nearby numbered table; the tray is set at the table and the seated patron takes their food.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Servi — Price, Specs & Demo
sources.claim: Bear Robotics Servi is a commercially sold autonomous food-running robot that carries loaded trays of food across restaurant and hospitality dining rooms to tables, navigating around guests with LiDAR and cameras.

sources.title: Two Months After Robots Were Introduced Into Nursing Homes, Residents Can't See Them Leaving
sources.claim: Servi food-running robots were deployed in real senior-living dining rooms (Front Porch communities) and residents wanted to keep them after the pilot.

sources.claim: In an actual senior-living dining room deployment, the Servi robot drives itself to programmed locations but human staff are still required to load food onto it and take food off at the table.

sources.title: Pudu Robotics Releases Catering and Retail Service Robot, BellaBot Pro
sources.claim: Pudu BellaBot Pro is a commercially released catering service robot using LiDAR/vision fusion navigation to deliver food autonomously in varied dining environments.

sources.claim: Pudu delivery robots are in service in US corporate cafeterias, casino buffets and full-service dining rooms, running food between the counter/kitchen and tables.

sources.claim: Industrial robot cells routinely pick, place and stack food trays at fixed, fixtured positions using vision guidance in fenced production cells.

Comparable object (rigid food tray) and precision; establishes that the pick-from-counter/place-on-surface step is solved when the work is fixtured and presented in a purpose-built cell (E1).

tasks.label: Stock cabinets or serving areas with condiments and refill condiment containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual/family restaurant dining room and server side-stations: collecting tabletop condiment containers (ketchup and hot-sauce bottles, salt & pepper shakers, sugar caddies, syrup pitchers), uncapping, topping off or consolidating, wiping sticky exteriors, recapping and returning them to tables between seatings while guests and staff move through the room.

Self-serve condiment station in a cafeteria, QSR or food court during service: refilling pump dispensers and bag-in-box ketchup/mustard, topping up packet bins, napkins, straws and stirrers, and cream/sugar at the coffee station, working around customers who are actively using the station.

Back-of-house prep area: filling squeeze bottles, ramekins and portion cups from gallon jugs and #10 cans of sauces and dressings, funneling and wiping, labeling and dating, then staging the filled containers in the cooler or on the line.

Replenishment run: carrying cases of bottled condiments and boxes of packets from dry storage or the walk-in through narrow aisles and swinging doors to service stations, opening cases, and stocking under-counter cabinets and shelves in a set order.

Banquet, off-site catering or food-truck service: setting up condiment trays and caddies on buffet lines in a venue whose layout differs each time, sometimes outdoors, and refilling them during the event.

sources.system: ZoneSun ZS-FAL180G5 ketchup/paste bottle filling line
sources.title: ZS-FAL180G5 Ketchup Paste Twist Top Bottle Filling Machine Line
sources.claim: Commercial servo filling lines fill sauce/ketchup bottles, place and apply caps (including leakproof lids and narrow ...) label them automatically, i.e. the whole refill-and-close cycle for condiment bottles when bottles are presented on a conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bottling condiments in a plant. It carries over to 'refill condiment containers' because the objects (squeeze/twist-top sauce bottles), the medium (viscous condiments), and the required output (accurately filled, sealed, clean bottles) are the same; only the presentation of the empties is fixtured.

sources.title: AI-Driven Robotics Help Cafe Spice Leap Over Labor and Line Hurdles
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-guided robotic arms portion viscous sauces and other food ingredients into containers on production lines in more than a dozen facilities, with vision verifying fill level and placement; at Cafe Spice, robot-filled tray acceptance was higher than human-filled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning wet, sticky condiment-like ingredients into containers on a line. It transfers to refilling condiment containers because the material handling problem (viscous sauces, deformable product, fill-level accuracy, no spillage) is the same and quality already meets or exceeds the human benchmark.

sources.system: Syntegon Robotic Pick and Place (RPP) platform
sources.title: Robotic Packaging | Automate Your Packaging & Processing
sources.claim: Vision-guided delta-robot cells are a standard commercial product for picking discrete packaged food items and loading them into trays, cartons or infeed chains at 120 picks per robot per minute.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tray/carton loading of packaged goods. It transfers to stocking caddies, bins and cabinets with packeted condiments because the objects (sachets, small packaged units) and the action (vision-located pick and ordered placement into a container) match, given fixtured presentation.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated store shelves with bottled and canned ... in 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, running under its GORDON AI with remote human teleoperation only to recover rare errors; it is fixed on a rail and is fed by crates staged for it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf replenishment with bottles and cans. It transfers to stocking a serving area or cabinet with bottled condiments (same object class, same ordered-placement precision), but the robot is stationary and the stock is presented to it, so it does not cover fetching from a storeroom.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics' ADAM serves drinks at Kennedy Space Center - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Richtech's dual-arm ADAM robot autonomously prepares and pours drinks at fixtured bar/cafe stations in real venues (Las Vegas cafe, Globe Life Field, Kennedy Space Center), using closed-loop vision to control pour angle and flow rate; humans replenish its ingredient supplies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dispensing liquids into open containers in a food-service venue. It transfers to topping off condiment/coffee-station liquids in precision terms, but only at a purpose-built station whose supplies are laid out and refilled by people.

sources.system: Mobile manipulator shelf-stocking system ('From Pixels to Shelf')
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: An integrated autonomous mobile manipulator for supermarket shelf stocking achieved over 98% pick-and-place success across 700+ events, but only in laboratory experiments replicating store conditions with ArUco markers, and the authors state performance remains inferior to human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile shelf replenishment, the closest analogue to walking stock out to serving areas and stocking cabinets. It shows the E2 version of that work is still lab-bound and below worker quality.

sources.system: π0.5 vision-language-action model on mobile manipulator
sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 controls a mobile manipulator to tidy kitchens and bedrooms in real homes never seen in training, but the developers state the model frequently makes mistakes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general pick-and-place tidying in unstructured settings, the nearest evidence for handling condiment items in an as-found venue. Acknowledged error rates keep it below employer-acceptable quality, so it supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Serve food to customers when waiters or waitresses need assistance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume casual/family full-service restaurant (chain casual, sushi, hot pot, pho, diner) during the dinner rush: the attendant picks up 2-4 plated dishes at the expo window, carries them across a crowded, mapped dining room to the assigned table, and gets the dishes to the seated guests, then returns for the next run.

Cafeteria, corporate/institutional dining hall or senior-living dining room with waitstaff: attendant carries plated meals, trays and drinks from the serving line to seated diners along wide, flat aisles, repeated continuously through a meal period.
Bar, lounge or counter service: bartender helper brings drinks, water, condiments and small plates to patrons seated at the bar rail or nearby high-tops, in a congested standing-room area.

Banquet or catered plated service in a hotel ballroom/event hall: attendant carries a loaded tray of covered plates from a staging area and sets a plate down at each of 8-10 covers per table, timed with other staff so a whole room is served at once.

Fine-dining or small upscale restaurant with narrow aisles and ...: coursed plated dishes carried from the pass and set precisely in front of each ... (correct orientation, correct side), with a brief dish description and immediate response to guest requests.

Outdoor patio, sidewalk seating, deck, or multi-level dining room: food carried over a door threshold, down a step or up stairs, across pavers/decking, in sun, wind or rain, to guests at outdoor tables.

tasks.label: Clean and polish counters, shelves, walls, furniture, or equipment in food service areas or other areas of restaurants and mop or vacuum floors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-meal-period or closing mop/auto-scrub of hard floors in an open dining room, cafeteria seating area or food-hall floor: chairs typically raised or pushed in by staff, large contiguous floor area, spilled food, drink rings, tracked-in grit; finish must be streak-free and dry before reopening.
Vacuuming carpeted areas at end of service: dining room carpet, banquet/function room, entry mats and lobby carpet in a restaurant or hotel food outlet; crumbs, wrappers, edges and along baseboards.

Mopping/detail cleaning tight, cluttered floor areas of the service side: behind the bar over rubber floor mats and around kegs and coolers, beverage/coffee station alcoves, dish-return and bus-station corners, narrow strips under fixed booths and banquettes; mats must be lifted and hosed or swept beneath.

Cleaning, sanitizing and polishing service counters and horizontal surfaces: bar top and bar rail, cafeteria serving-line counters and tray rails, condiment/coffee station tops; items (caddies, napkin dispensers, trays, glassware) must be moved aside and replaced, sticky syrup and food residue removed, surface wiped with sanitizer and buffed dry to a streak-free shine.

Cleaning and polishing food-service equipment and shelving in place: coffee brewers and urns, soda/juice dispensers and drip trays, ice bin lids, toaster and steam-table exteriors, stainless panels, refrigerated case and display glass fronts, and back-bar shelves that require removing and replacing bottles and glassware; no liquid on controls or electrics.

Periodic detail cleaning of vertical and furniture surfaces: walls and wainscoting near booths, window ledges and sills, chair legs and backs, booth seat backs and table bases/pedestals, plus high dusting of ledges and light fixtures in the dining area.

tasks.label: Replenish supplies of food or equipment at steam tables or service bars.

instances.label: Cafeteria/buffet hot line during service: attendant notices a steam-table well running low, fetches a full hotel pan of hot food from the kitchen or holding cabinet, pulls the depleted pan (hot, food-smeared, sometimes with liquid), drops the full pan into the well, sets the serving utensil, and wipes spills - all with guests queued at the line.

Cold station refill: salad bar, deli/condiment station or beverage counter - replacing bins of cut produce, dressings and crocks in ice or cold wells, topping off condiment pumps, cream, sugar, lemon wedges, and re-icing the well.

Restocking equipment/smallwares at the service line or service bar station: stacks of clean plates and bowls into dispensers, racks of glasses and cups, silverware bins, trays, napkins, lids, straws, serving tongs/ladles and chafing fuel, brought from the dish area or storeroom.

Service-bar restock in a restaurant or lounge: carrying cases of beer/soda and liquor bottles from the storeroom to the bar, loading bottle coolers and speed rails, filling ice bins from the ice machine, refilling garnish caddies and mixers, in the narrow bar well behind working bartenders.

High-volume institutional/banquet replenishment (hospital, school, stadium, corporate cafeteria): loading carts with pans, cases and dishware in a central kitchen and hauling them across the facility, sometimes between floors, to keep several steam tables, warmers and service bars stocked through a rush.

tasks.label: Wash glasses or other serving equipment at bars.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Busy bar/restaurant, mid-shift: barback collects bus tubs and racks of dirty pint glasses, tumblers and mugs from the bar top and tables, racks them, runs them through the under-counter glasswasher or the back-of-house rack dish machine, then unloads, air-dries and stacks clean glassware for restock. Standard glassware, high volume, batch turnaround of minutes.

Behind the bar during service, three-compartment underbar sink: hand wash-rinse-sanitize of a handful of glasses and mixing tins between drink orders using brushes and sanitizer dip, in a cramped underbar shared with working bartenders, with seconds-to-a-minute turnaround so the glass is back in use immediately.

Bar tool batch cleaning at shift change or close: shaker tins, strainers, jiggers, muddlers, bar spoons, pour spouts, small pitchers and shaker glasses with sticky syrup, citrus and dairy residue; rinsed, washed (machine rack or sink), sanitized, dried and returned to bartender stations.

Heavy or awkward bar/serving equipment: blender jars with blade assemblies, soda-gun nozzles and holsters, ice bins, rubber bar mats, drip trays, coffee urns and juice dispenser parts; requires disassembly, soaking, hand scrubbing of baked/dried residue, sanitizing and reassembly.

Cafeteria, banquet or hotel dish room: attendant loads racks of returned glassware, cups, trays and utensils onto the conveyor/door-type dish machine, runs cycles, unloads hot racks, stacks and returns clean ware to the beverage station and service bar. Fixed dish-room layout, standard institutional ware, steady batch flow.

Fine-dining or hotel bar stemware: delicate wine glasses, coupes and crystal are washed gently (hand or dedicated glasswasher), then hand-polished with a cloth over steam, inspected against light for spots and lipstick marks, and hung/stacked without chips or breakage.

tasks.label: Garnish foods and position them on tables to make them visible and accessible.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Institutional cafeteria serving line (school, college dining hall, hospital, corporate cafe): attendant garnishes hotel pans of hot food (parsley, lemon wedges, paprika, sauce drizzle), tidies the edges of the pan, drops it into the steam-table or cold well, sets serving utensils and signage, and re-faces/replenishes pans during the meal period while patrons queue alongside.

Hotel or restaurant buffet/brunch display: attendant garnishes and arranges platters and bowls (fruit, cheese, salads, pastries, desserts) on cloth-covered buffet tables with risers and mirrors, positioning them so items are visible and within reach; during service the attendant re-faces, consolidates, and swaps in fresh garnished platters.

Self-serve salad bar or deli grab-and-go display in a cafeteria or market: attendant fills and garnishes inserts and pre-made bowls, seats them in the cold well or display case in the standard planogram order, fronts and rotates product so it looks full and is easy to reach.

Banquet or catered function in a hotel ballroom / event hall: attendant helps build display and action tables, sets chafers and risers, places garnished platters and centerpiece foods at prescribed positions so several hundred guests can see and access them, then tops up and re-garnishes between waves.

Off-premise catering at a client site (office lobby, outdoor tent, private residence): attendant unpacks platters garnished at the commissary, touches up garnish, and positions them on rented or borrowed tables of varying size and height, working around uncontrolled layout, weather, and guest traffic.

tasks.label: Mix and prepare flavors for mixed drinks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant or hotel bar during service: the bar helper mixes drink components to recipe behind a human bar — jiggers or free-pours spirits from the speed rail and back bar, adds juices, syrups, sodas and ice, shakes or stirs, and hands finished mixed drinks to the bartender or server, working shoulder-to-shoulder with staff in a crowded, wet, cluttered well.

Pre-shift bar prep in the bar-back or kitchen: batching sour mix, simple and flavored syrups, purees and pre-batched cocktail mixes in bulk containers — measuring, dissolving sugar, stirring, tasting and adjusting, then labeling, dating and racking the containers for the service bar.

Fresh flavor prep at a craft cocktail bar: juicing cases of citrus, muddling fruit and herbs, starting spirit infusions, making shrubs, flavored syrups and rimming mixes, then straining and bottling them into dasher and squeeze bottles.

High-volume banquet, stadium, casino or cruise service bar: mixing large batches of punch, sangria, margarita/daiquiri and other mixers in bulk for an event, charging frozen-drink machines and dispensers, and hooking up or refilling bag-in-box syrup for the soda guns under time pressure before and during service.

Cafeteria, cafe or casual venue beverage station: mixing non-alcoholic 'mixed drinks' — flavored lemonades, iced-tea and juice blends, flavored sodas and mocktails — from concentrates, syrups and purees, and keeping the dispensers filled during meal service.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing fresh citrus juice, the main flavor a bar helper prepares by hand-juicing limes, lemons and oranges. The machine handles whole fruit and yields bar-grade juice unattended.

tasks.label: Slice and pit fruit used to garnish drinks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift bulk citrus prep at a restaurant/bar prep station: barback pulls cases of limes and lemons from the walk-in, washes them, and hand-cuts several hundred wedges and orange wheels on a cutting board with a chef's knife, then fills and refrigerates garnish caddies.

Mid-service replenishment behind a crowded bar: attendant quickly cuts a few limes/lemons into wedges or wheels on a small cramped board between other duties, working around bartenders, glassware and wet surfaces, delivering the garnish within a minute or two.

Pitted/skewered garnish prep: draining jarred olives and maraschino cherries, occasionally pitting fresh cherries or olives, halving/pitting other stone or tropical fruit (pineapple, melon) into chunks, and loading picks and garnish trays.

High-volume institutional prep in a hotel banquet, stadium or large cafeteria kitchen: hundreds to thousands of uniform lemon/lime wedges and wheels produced on stainless prep tables, sometimes with a countertop wedger, then panned, wrapped and staged for multiple bars.

Craft/specialty garnish work to a bartender's spec: cutting citrus peels and twists with a channel or paring knife, trimming decorative fans/flags, slicing thin wheels for dehydration, precise trimming for a cocktail program.

sources.system: Urschel Model CC Slicer / TranSlicer / DiversaCut (fruit cutting line machines)
sources.date: 2024-05 (page updated); product line in continuous commercial use
sources.title: Fruits Cutting Machines & Equipment - Urschel
sources.claim: Urschel sells industrial slicing and dicing machines that continuously cut whole fruits (including oranges, apples, bananas, mango) into slices and wedges on conveyor-fed food-processing lines; machines run under machine control with built-in infeed/discharge conveyors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial slicing of whole fruit into uniform pieces. Same objects (citrus and other whole fruit), same cut precision as a bar wedge/wheel, but the fruit is conveyed and fixtured to the machine rather than hand-held.

sources.title: Automatic Cherry Pitting Machine Cherry Corer Machine – WM machinery
sources.claim: Fully automatic cherry/olive pitting machines pit stone fruit continuously: fruit is poured into the machine, a mold conveyor belt orients and feeds each fruit, and pits are punched out and discharged, with no per-fruit human handling.

sources.title: JUNIOR CHERRY PITTER — Dunkley International (spec sheet, Cherry Central)
sources.claim: Dunkley pitters are production pitting machines used in cherry processing plants; fruit is fed into rubber pockets on the machine and pitted output is discharged directly to packaging at 600-650 lb/hour on the small model.

sources.developer: SINTEF / Norwegian research team (published in npj Robotics)
sources.title: Sashimi-Bot: autonomous tri-manual advanced manipulation and cutting of deformable objects | npj Robotics
sources.claim: Sashimi-Bot is a three-armed robot cell that autonomously prepares sashimi from raw salmon loins: one arm stabilizes the loin on a cutting board, a knife arm makes force/tactile-controlled slices (~28 s per cut cycle), and slices are plated, all without a human in the ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: knife-slicing a variable natural food item into uniform serving pieces on a cutting board and plating them. Citrus for garnish is firmer and more uniform than salmon loin, and the cut precision required is comparable, so knife control demonstrated in a fixed multi-arm cell transfers to fruit slicing in the same kind of cell.

sources.title: SliceIt! - A Dual Simulator Framework for Learning Robot Food Slicing
sources.claim: SliceIt! trains a dual-arm robot (two UR5e arms with force-torque sensors, one holding the food, the other wielding the knife) to slice food items with controlled contact forces, transferring learned slicing policies from simulation to the real bench-top robot setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic knife slicing of produce with force control in a fixed two-arm cell. Same tool (knife on a board), same class of objects (produce), same requirement of uniform slices, so it substantiates fruit slicing when the work is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Supracut Systems - Industrial Restaurant Automated Citrus Wedger with Courtesy Slice
sources.claim: SupraCut 800 is a commercial countertop automated citrus wedger marketed to and used by restaurants, bars, stadiums and resorts, cutting an average of 15 whole lemons, limes or small oranges per minute into bar-quality wedges (with an optional wheel blade); an operator loads fruit into the machine for each cut.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (cutting citrus garnish wedges to bar standard) in the bar/kitchen itself, but the operator presents each fruit to the machine, so it shows machine-cut wedges meet employer quality while not demonstrating autonomous in-kitchen operation.

sources.title: S195 grid cutter for vegetable processing – KRONEN
sources.claim: The KRONEN S195 grid cutter is a tabletop machine sold for commercial kitchens that cores and segments citrus fruit and other small produce with interchangeable cutting inserts; the operator places each fruit in the insert and actuates the cut.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (segmenting citrus) sited in a commercial kitchen, but each fruit is hand-placed and the machine is hand-actuated, so it does not establish autonomous completion at E2.

tasks.label: Stock refrigerating units with wines or bottled beer or replace empty beer kegs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Neighborhood bar / restaurant bar: barback restocks bottled beer and canned drinks into under-counter reach-in coolers and back-bar sliding-door refrigerators before and during service — walks cases from the stockroom or walk-in, cuts open cartons, pulls existing stock forward (FIFO), kneels to load low shelves around ice bins, bar mats and working bartenders, breaks down cardboard.

Restaurant/hotel: stocking white wines, sparkling wine and Champagne into refrigerated wine cabinets, wine wells and reach-in wine fridges — varied bottle shapes and weights, chilling in time for service, labels faced, fragile glass, some bottles laid in racks.

Replacing an empty half-barrel keg: notices foam/blown keg, wheels or hand-trucks a ~160 lb full keg in a walk-in cooler or basement cellar, disconnects the coupler from the empty, taps the fresh keg (seat, press and twist the Sankey coupler), purges/pours off the line, hauls the empty out.

Cafeteria, campus/corporate dining hall, hotel grab-and-go market or stadium concession: replenishing glass-door refrigerated display coolers (often rear-loaded from an adjacent walk-in) with bottled and canned beverages from cases staged at the cooler, keeping shelves faced and rotated.

Large-venue/banquet pre-event stocking: filling portable bar coolers, tubs and ice bins at satellite bars in an arena, ballroom or event floor with bottled beer and wine from pallets/carts, plus swapping kegs at portable jockey boxes, all within a tight pre-doors window.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores – The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA rail-mounted arm restocks refrigerated shelves with bottles and ... in FamilyMart convenience stores, running autonomously under its GORDON AI with remote human recovery only on errors, at up to 1,000 bottles/cans per day; mass deployment to 300 stores began August 2022.

sources.title: Robot That Stocks Drinks is Newest Thing at the Corner Store (AP) – Manufacturing.net
sources.claim: Journalists observed TX SCARA working in a live Tokyo FamilyMart: it travels behind the refrigerated shelves and its gripper takes each bottle or can from stacked crates staged beside it and places it on the chilled shelf, choosing placement from camera-based stock detection.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: loading a refrigerating unit with bottled/canned beverages from staged cases in a food-retail facility.

sources.title: Telexistence Expands Beverage Shelf-Stocking Service with “TX Ghost” Robots
sources.claim: Telexistence expanded its beverage shelf-stocking robot service with the newer TX Ghost robot, with pilot operations in select 7-Eleven stores in Tokyo, targeting the chilled backroom restocking work done by store staff.

sources.title: BizLink Dresspack Keeps the Beer Kegs Flowing
sources.claim: Founders Brewing runs a FANUC R-2000iC/165F six-axis robot in its keg line that grips full ~160 lb kegs with pneumatic grippers, flips them valve-up, moves them between stations for valve sanitizing/capping, and palletizes them — unattended production operation in a fenced industrial cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (brewery keg handling) transfers to keg swapping: identical objects (full half-barrel kegs, ~160 lb), same lift/orient/place precision, machine-fixtured presentation.

sources.system: KUKA keg handling robots at D.G. Yuengling & Son
sources.title: New Automation Keeps Kegs Moving at America's Oldest Brewery | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Yuengling's Millcreek and Tampa breweries use KUKA robots to handle full half-barrel kegs continuously at roughly 400 kegs per hour in an automated keg line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (brewery keg movement/palletizing) shares the object, weight and placement precision of swapping a keg in a cellar, with the work presented by conveyor.

sources.system: Automatic keg cleaning and filling lines (Czech Brewery System / industry-standard keg racking plants)
sources.developer: Czech Brewery System s.r.o. (and comparable KHS/Comac keg lines)
sources.title: Equipment to filling beer into kegs and washing the kegs – CBS
sources.claim: Commercial keg cleaning and filling lines are fully automatic machines that move kegs on integrated infeed/outfeed conveyors and automatically engage the keg's spear/valve to clean and isobarically fill it, then release it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (keg racking) covers the coupling step of keg replacement: the machine automatically seats and opens the same Sankey-type keg valve a bar coupler engages, then disengages it.

sources.system: A-B-C Packaging automatic decaser (Oliver Winery bottling line)
sources.title: New Integrated Bottling Line at Oliver Winery Nearly Doubles Output – Packaging World
sources.claim: Oliver Winery's bottling line uses an A-B-C Packaging automatic decaser that removes glass wine bottles from cases and places them on the conveyor at 12,000 bottles per hour; comparable robotic case packers (e.g., FANUC M-710 units at Veuve Clicquot) load champagne bottles into cases at high rates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (decasing/case packing glass wine bottles) shows machine handling of fragile 750 mL wine bottles between a case and a target position at production reliability, the manipulation core of loading a wine fridge when bottles are presented.

sources.system: Simbe Tally / Brain Corp mobile manipulator platform
sources.title: Supermarket Robots Guide 2026 | RobotsUSA
sources.claim: As of 2026, the established deployed retail store robots are shelf-scanning/inventory units (e.g., Simbe Tally); mobile manipulators that actually stock product on store shelves are described as forward-looking platforms rather than broadly deployed products.
sources.transferJustification: Negative context: shows no cited mobile stocking robot works a store/bar floor as found, limiting E2 credit to fixed rail installations like TX SCARA.

roles.title: Dishwashers
roles.description: Clean dishes, kitchen, food preparation equipment, or utensils.

tasks.label: Wash dishes, glassware, flatware, pots, or pans, using dishwashers or by hand.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant dish pit during and after service: bus tubs of soiled plates, glassware and flatware arrive continuously; worker scrapes/pre-rinses, racks items, runs a door-type or rack-conveyor dish machine, unloads hot racks, and stacks clean ware for the line. Wet floors, crowded aisle, surge volumes.

High-volume institutional cafeteria dish room (school, hospital, university, corporate or senior-living dining): tray return conveyor feeds a flight-type or rack machine; worker separates trays, dumps waste, sorts flatware into soak bins, loads/unloads at high peak throughput during compressed meal periods.

Pot-and-pan station: heavily soiled stockpots, saute pans, sheet pans, hotel pans, mixing bowls and kitchen utensils with baked-on or burnt-on residue; soaked and hand-scrubbed in a three-compartment sink (or fed to a pot washer), rinsed, sanitized, air-dried and shelved.

Quick-service, fast-casual or coffee-shop warewashing: lower volume, small undercounter machine plus a sink; load is mixed — mugs, plates and cutlery together with prep containers, food pans, tongs, blender jars and equipment parts washed by hand between rushes in a cramped back area.

Bar and fine-dining glassware/china: stemware, pint and cocktail glasses through a rack glasswasher, plus hand-washing and careful handling of fragile stemware, china plates and serving platters that cannot be machine-crashed; polished and returned to service quickly.

Off-site catering or banquet event washing: dishes, chafing pans and flatware handled in a rented hall, tent or temporary field kitchen with improvised sinks or portable warewash setups, variable layout and no fixed dish room.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics' three-arm dishwashing system operates autonomously in live restaurant dish rooms around the clock, washing thousands of dishes.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The same Armstrong system handles the mixed dish-room load — shiny plates, transparent glasses and bulk silverware — using trained perception and interchangeable grippers.

sources.title: Armstrong Raises $12 Million to Bring General-Purpose Robots to Kitchens
sources.claim: Armstrong robots are installed commercially in a large US full-service restaurant chain, running 24/7 alongside the restaurant's existing commercial dish machine at production volumes.

sources.title: This Dishwashing Robot Is About to Change Every Restaurant in America - RoboPhil
sources.claim: Trade coverage confirms the Armstrong systems run unattended in working restaurants, with staff only prompted by on-screen alerts when something goes wrong.

sources.title: Dishcraft Robotics raises funding to help caterers, cafeterias reopen - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Dishcraft's purpose-built robotic dishwashers autonomously cleaned plates and bowls at very high daily volume at a central hub serving corporate, hotel and hospital cafeterias.

sources.title: Robotic dish-scrubber for commercial kitchens could cut dishwashing staffs in half - Axios
sources.claim: Dishcraft's purpose-built approach was limited to proprietary magnetic plates and bowls and could not wash cups, glasses or silverware — a bound on what purpose-built dish machinery covered.

sources.system: Better Engineering bakery tray/pan washing systems
sources.title: Commercial Bakery Equipment: Industrial Parts Washers | Better Engineering
sources.claim: Purpose-built automated tray/pan washing systems clean sheet pans, trays and mixing bowls with baked-on carbonized residue to food-safe standard using high-pressure heated spray under programmable machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial sanitation washing of bakery sheet pans, trays and mixing bowls. Same objects and soil type as commercial-kitchen pot/pan washing (baked-on grease and carbonized food), cleaned to a food-safety standard, but with the ware brought to a fixed purpose-built washer.

sources.system: Better Engineering RTO-2000 jet washer in robotic work cell
sources.title: Parts Washer for Robotic Work Cell – Case Study 22090 - Better Engineering
sources.claim: Industrial washer cells are routinely integrated with a robot that loads and unloads the washing machine, so the whole load/wash/unload cycle runs without a human at the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tending of an industrial spray washer in a fenced cell. The load/unload motions and rigid, greasy metal workpieces are comparable to racking pots, pans and hotel pans into a purpose-built pot washer at E1.

sources.title: Nala Robotics Introduces Autonomous Dishwasher (PR Newswire)
sources.claim: Nala Robotics markets 'Spotless', a cobot-arm dishwashing system for professional kitchens covering cookware, cutlery, dishware and glassware; deployment claims are vendor-sourced and not independently verified.

sources.title: Helix Loads the Dishwasher - Figure
sources.claim: Figure's Helix policy autonomously loads a household dishwasher, singulating stacked plates and reorienting glasses, but this is a lab/home demonstration of one sub-step rather than a deployed warewashing operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dishwasher loading in an unstructured home kitchen. Shows only the loading sub-step at demo maturity, so it does not substantiate whole-task completion at E3.

tasks.label: Maintain kitchen work areas, equipment, or utensils in clean and orderly condition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant dish room during service: keeping dishware, glassware and flatware clean and orderly — pulling items from messy bus tubs, scraping, racking, running the commercial dish machine, unloading and stacking clean ware, keeping the dish table clear for the next load.

During-service upkeep of kitchen work areas in a busy restaurant kitchen: wiping and sanitizing prep counters, cutting boards and reach-in handles between tasks, mopping up spills, clearing scraps, pans and clutter off surfaces, refreshing sanitizer buckets and towels, all while cooks work around the same surfaces.

End-of-shift cleandown of the kitchen and dish area: scrubbing and sanitizing stainless prep tables, three-compartment and prep sinks, the dish machine inside and out, splash walls, shelving and equipment exteriors, then resetting the area for the next day, with no service running.

Deep cleaning kitchen equipment and cookware: degreasing the flat-top/grill, fryer boil-out, cleaning ovens, steam tables and microwaves, disassembling/washing/reassembling slicers, mixers and blenders, pulling and washing hood filters, and scrubbing burnt-on pots, pans and sheet trays at the pot sink.

Institutional or high-volume kitchen (hospital, school, university dining, chain commissary) on a written sanitation schedule: cleaning and sanitizing standardized stainless work counters, carts, tray line and steam table equipment to checklist/HACCP standards after the meal period, with the line shut down.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics' three-arm dish-room system runs autonomously in live full-service restaurant dish rooms, 24 hours a day, taking dishes from bus tubs through the commercial dish machine; the second installation runs without any Armstrong staff on site.

sources.title: Armstrong Raises $12M to Bring General-Purpose Robots to Kitchens
sources.claim: Multiple Armstrong robots are deployed at a large US full-service restaurant chain, washing over a million dishes a ... with standard commercial dish machines, identifying dishes in messy piles with millimeter-level 3D perception.

sources.title: Rosie™ by CleanBotix | Robotic Sanitation for Food Plants
sources.claim: CleanBotix's Rosie is a mobile 6-DoF arm robot that autonomously performs the full open-plant sanitation cycle (rinse, foam, rinse, sanitize) on food and beverage plant equipment and surfaces night after night with minimal oversight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nightly washdown sanitation of stainless food-contact equipment and surfaces. Same soils (grease, food residue), same chemical clean-and-sanitize standard, and the same surfaces a dishwasher cleans at end of shift, so surface-cleaning performance transfers to kitchen work-area cleandown when surfaces are presented unobstructed.

sources.title: Why Robotic Food Plant Sanitation? | Rosie™ by CleanBotix
sources.claim: In controlled A:B testing against human sanitation workers on plant equipment, Rosie left lower ATP residue (6.1 vs 22.9 RLU), required no re-cleans versus 4 of 10 for manual cleaning, and worked at 80% of human speed.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes worker-quality output (hygiene swab results and cycle time) for robotic cleaning of food-contact equipment surfaces, the same acceptance standard applied to a dishwasher's end-of-shift cleandown.

sources.title: CleanBotix Builds Autonomous Food-Processing Robot with MoveIt Pro to Accelerate Market Launch
sources.claim: CleanBotix moved Rosie from prototype to production units within a year and has begun paid pilots with large poultry processors; the control stack supports taught trajectories and semi-autonomous operation, with four to five hours of ....
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates pilot-stage field results for robotic washdown sanitation of food-plant equipment; autonomy is described as taught-trajectory/semi-autonomous, so it is treated as supporting context only.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR autonomously cleans fixtures, surfaces, floors and picks up trash in high-traffic restrooms and is deployed in hospitals and airports as a commercial service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spray-and-clean sanitation of hard fixtures and surfaces inside an occupied institutional building. It shows autonomous chemical surface cleaning at facility standard, but only in fixed-layout, clutter-free rooms mapped in advance — supporting surface cleaning where the work is presented unobstructed, not cluttered live kitchen counters.

tasks.label: Place clean dishes, utensils, or cooking equipment in storage areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant dish pit during/after service: worker pulls racks of clean plates, bowls and glassware off the dish machine, air-dries/wipes them, then carries and stacks them on line shelving, plate lowerators, glass racks at the bar and expo station — wet floor, cooks and servers moving through, shelves at varying heights.

Sorting clean flatware coming out of the dish machine (loose in perforated inserts or cutlery lane), separating forks/knives/spoons, and dropping them handle-up into cutlery caddies/bins at the service station or storage rack.

Putting away clean cooking equipment: stock pots, sauté and sheet pans, hotel pans, mixing bowls, sheet-pan racks, blender parts and slicer components — heavy, varied shapes, nested on low shelving, hung on pot racks/hooks, or returned to specific stations in the kitchen or dry storage room.

Institutional kitchen (hospital, school, university, senior living, cafeteria) with a conveyor/flight-type warewasher: stacking clean trays, plates, bowls and cups onto dish dollies, tray trolleys and mobile storage carts at the clean end, then wheeling carts to the tray line or storage area.

Off-site catering, banquet or event work: washing up in a temporary or shared space and repacking clean china, glassware, chafing dishes and utensils into crates, transport carts and van racks in an as-found location.

sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics has deployed multi-arm dishwashing robot cells in real restaurant dish rooms running 24 hours a day, handling stacked dirty plates, cups from bus tubs, silverware (magnetic fingers) and lifting dish racks, with the second install running without an on-site company minder.

sources.title: Nala Robotics Introduces Autonomous Dishwasher (PR Newswire)
sources.claim: Nala Robotics markets 'Spotless', a cobot-arm dishwasher it says washes, dries, stacks and stores kitchenware in restaurants and senior living venues; the claims come from company press releases with no independent verification of autonomous in-kitchen put-away.

tasks.label: Sweep or scrub floors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift sweep and deck-scrub of the back-of-house cook line and prep area: pick up dropped food, packaging and broken crockery, pull up rubber floor mats, sweep and scrub under and around ranges, fryers, prep tables and reach-ins with degreaser, squeegee water to the floor drain. Greasy, wet, cluttered, low clearances, hoses and cords underfoot.

Dish pit / warewashing area floor: standing water, soap, food slop and grease around the machine and racks; mopped and squeegeed to the drain repeatedly during and after service in a small, tight, wet nook crowded with racks, carts and staff.

Front-of-house dining room after close: chairs placed on tables, sweep or vacuum crumbs from the open floor, then mop the hard floor including aisles, under booths, and around the beverage station and host stand.

Mid-shift spot cleanup: a dropped tray, spilled sauce, oil or broken glass on the kitchen floor or a service aisle, cleaned immediately with broom, dustpan and mop while cooks and servers keep working around the spot.
Back hallways, service corridor, receiving/loading area and staff-area hard floors: sweep and mop long, mostly open stretches of quarry tile or sealed concrete on a nightly or weekly schedule.
Dry storeroom and walk-in cooler/freezer floors: sweep spilled product and packaging debris and mop between pallets, dunnage racks and shelving in cold, tight, obstacle-filled rooms.

sources.title: Tennant Company Sells 10,000th Robotic Scrubber, Underscoring Global Demand for Cleaning Automation
sources.claim: Tennant's autonomous mobile robot floor scrubbers (T7AMR, T380AMR, T16AMR) are a mature commercial product line with 10,000 units sold, cleaning large commercial and industrial hard floors autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (scrubbing floors), on the same hard-floor surfaces; establishes that autonomous scrubbing of open hard floors is a deployed, worker-replacing capability.

sources.title: Robots in retail: Automation revolution in play
sources.claim: Brain Corp's autonomous scrubbers went from a few hundred Walmart stores to a full nationwide deployment ..., cleaning retail sales floors in an occupied structured facility.

sources.developer: Tennant Company / Brain Corp / Sam's Club
sources.title: Aisle-scanning robots now in Sam's Clubs chainwide
sources.claim: Sam's Club added 372 Tennant T7AMR autonomous floor scrubbers to give every club an automated scrubber, i.e. routine nightly/daytime floor scrubbing of a large human retail facility is done by robot.

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo is a fully ... deployed in airports, malls, hospitals, factories, schools and warehouses, with over 1,000 robots fielded.

sources.title: Avidbots: Neo 2W - Material Handling 24/7
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo 2W is built for warehouse and factory floors that carry loose floor debris and dynamic activity, i.e. autonomous scrubbing of industrial hard floors with debris present.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (sweeping/scrubbing hard floors) on industrial floors carrying loose debris, the closest analogue to a cleared kitchen floor with food scraps.

sources.title: Le Meridien Etoile Paris hotel & Whiz Case Study
sources.claim: A 1,025-room hotel runs 18 Whiz autonomous vacuum sweepers, 15 of them dedicated to corridor cleaning, replacing staff time on long back-of-house and guest corridors.

sources.developer: Pudu Robotics (deployed via RobotLAB at QuikTrip)
sources.title: Pudu CC1 At QT: How A 4-in-1 Floor Cleaning Robot Delivers Real ROI In Convenience Stores

sources.title: PUDU CC1 | Intelligent 4-in-1 Commercial Cleaning Robot for Multi-floor Buildings

tasks.label: Stock supplies, such as food or utensils, in serving stations, cupboards, refrigerators, or salad bars.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant or cafeteria dish station during and after service: pulling clean racks off the dish machine and stacking plates, bowls, cups, glasses and sorted flatware onto the clean-side shelving, dish carts and speed racks that the cook line and service stations draw from. Hot, wet, high throughput (hundreds of pieces per hour), staff working alongside.

Carrying clean dishware, glass racks and utensils out of the dish room and putting them away in serving stations, cupboards, expo shelves, cup/glass racks at self-serve beverage stations and the bar, threading around staff, mats and carts during service.

Cafeteria, buffet or salad-bar replenishment during service: refilling inserts with cut vegetables, dressings and toppings, swapping empty hotel pans for full ones fetched from the walk-in, topping off ice, plates, tongs and condiments at the serving station while guests are at the bar.

Restocking reach-in coolers and beverage stations from cases of bottled and canned drinks and packaged single-serve items (yogurt, dressings, milk cartons), rotating older stock forward on standard cooler shelves.

Walk-in cooler stocking: placing prepped pans and deli containers, produce boxes and dairy crates onto wire shelving, rotating FIFO and consolidating part-used containers in a cold, cramped, variably arranged walk-in.

Delivery put-away: hauling cases of dry goods, paper goods and cleaning chemicals from the receiving door down a back hallway into dry storage shelves and cupboards, breaking cases and stocking detergent and towels at the dish station.

tasks.label: Clean or prepare various foods for cooking or serving.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

Prep table knife work on mixed produce to the chef's spec: peel and dice onions and carrots, peel potatoes, slice tomatoes, shred lettuce and cabbage, mince garlic — varying sizes and quality of raw product, using board, peeler and knife amid other workers.

High-volume single-ingredient prep at a chain unit where a dedicated appliance is plausible: process a case of avocados for guacamole (cut, core, peel), run a fry cutter, run an onion slicer — one product, repeated, large batch.

Commissary/cafeteria/hospital or catering kitchen: portion prepped foods from bulk into hotel pans, deli containers and meal trays by weight or count, cover, label and stage for the steam table, grab-and-go case or tray line.

During service, at the pass or makeline: assemble and portion prepped components into bowls, plates and baskets for immediate serving — filling salad/grain bowls, dressing and tossing, topping pizzas, dropping and basketing fried sides, adding garnishes — under rush time pressure.
Protein and messy-item prep: trim and portion meat or fish fillets, devein and peel shrimp, bread or marinate chicken, open and drain #10 cans, thaw and separate frozen product in a cool prep area.

tasks.label: Sort and remove trash, placing it in designated pickup areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant kitchen during and after service: dishwasher pulls full bags from can-liner bins at the dish machine and prep line, ties them, re-lines the cans, and carries the bags out the back door to the dumpster/compactor enclosure, lifting them over the lip; mixed wet food waste, grease-soaked paper, broken glass, cardboard.

Dish room scrapping station: worker sorts material coming off returned plates, trays and bus tubs — food scraps to the disposal/compost barrel, paper and foil to trash, bottles/cans to the recycling bin, cardboard flattened — then empties the scrap barrel into the larger waste container.

Hospital, university or school kitchen: bagged trash, recycling and food-waste totes are consolidated into wheeled carts/barrels that must be moved out of the dish room along back corridors and service elevators and dropped at the designated compactor / loading-dock pickup area, and empty carts returned.

Fast-casual or cafeteria dining room during service: emptying customer trash/tray-return receptacles with guests present, pulling stray recyclables and trays out of the stream, replacing liners, and walking the bags back of house to the compactor.

Bar or banquet venue at closing: heavy bins of bottles, cans and glass sorted from other waste and carried out at night to the recycling dumpster in a shared back alley (uneven pavement, poor lighting, other tenants' containers).

Outdoor haul under variable conditions: trash and recycling wheeled or carried across an open parking lot or down an exterior ramp to a remote dumpster corral, in rain, snow or heat; includes catering/off-site and food-truck trash placed at a designated pickup point.

sources.title: AMP Robotics' Dual-robot Recycling System Increases Productivity

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sortation of mixed municipal waste in a recycling facility. It transfers to the dishwasher's trash duty at E1 because the objects are the same (food-soiled packaging, cans, bottles, paper, cardboard) and the required act is identical — recognize the waste type and place it in the correct designated container — with the waste presented to the machine on a conveyor as a purpose-built setting would present it.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: whole-facility automated sorting and routing of mixed household/commercial garbage. Transfer: this is the purpose-built (E1) realization of 'sort and remove trash, placing it in designated pickup areas' — the same wet, contaminated, heterogeneous waste stream a kitchen produces is taken in, machine-sorted, and deposited into designated bunkers/containers for pickup.

sources.title: Overview | How to Robotize | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker robotic sorting stations sort bulky, heterogeneous waste fractions on the spot, including items up to 40 kg, and run unmanned around the clock in waste-processing facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sorting of bulky mixed waste (including bagged and irregular items) into designated fractions. Transfer: comparable objects and grip requirements to restaurant waste (bags, cardboard, containers, glass) and the same output — waste separated into the correct designated container — in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
