sources.transferJustification: Related task: environmental-services waste-cart logistics inside a hospital. Transfer: identical objects (loaded bulk trash and recycling carts), identical goal (remove accumulated waste from a work area and place it at the designated compactor/dock pickup area), in a structured human work facility with people present.

sources.system: Tesla Optimus; Loki Robotics cleaning/trash robot (as assessed by Epoch AI)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 — Epoch AI
sources.claim: An independent 2026 assessment of autonomous robot capabilities classifies 'take out the trash' as having significant limits in lab: no robot has shown removing a bag from an ... and closing it; Tesla's Optimus demo was in a controlled training warehouse without navigation, and Loki Robotics' one-armed wheeled robot needs teleoperation for many edge cases and is about ten times slower than a ....
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: bagging trash and carrying it to an outdoor bin is the core of the dishwasher's trash duty; this assessment establishes that no cited system does it autonomously end-to-end at worker quality in a human-built setting.

sources.system: RL at Scale (Everyday Robots mobile manipulators)

sources.claim: A fleet of 23 Everyday Robots mobile manipulators autonomously sorted waste at waste stations in three Google office buildings over about two years, moving mis-sorted items between recycling, compost and landfill bins, but the program was a research deployment and did not empty bins or carry waste to pickup areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting mixed office waste into designated bins. It bears on the E2 question for the dish-room sorting instance, but covers only the sorting sub-step at research maturity and does not include emptying containers or moving waste to a pickup area.

tasks.label: Transfer supplies or equipment between storage and work areas, by hand or using hand trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service restaurant during service: carry racks and stacks of clean plates, glassware, flatware and clean pans from the dishmachine clean landing to the line, service stations, bar and storage shelving; wet greasy floors, aisles under 3 ft, servers and cooks moving fast, loads 15-35 lb, some overhead shelf placement.

Restaurant/bar: haul cases of canned goods, dry goods, paper goods, chemicals and bottled beverages from a dry storeroom or basement to the kitchen and dish station using a hand truck or by hand; boxes of varied size stacked on shelves and pallets, sometimes down/up stairs or through a narrow back hallway.

Moving product and equipment in and out of walk-in coolers/freezers and prep areas: milk crates, produce cases, Cambro containers, sheet pans, bus tubs, ice buckets; heavy insulated doors, condensation and cold, floor clutter and pallets inside the box.

Receiving a delivery at the back door or dock and putting it away: unloading cases and pallets left by the driver, hand-trucking them inside, and stacking them on dry-storage shelves or in the cooler, in whatever order the load arrives.

Institutional/high-volume kitchen (hospital, university, school district, senior living, large hotel or casino): move loaded carts, pan racks and pallets of supplies between central receiving/storerooms and the kitchen and dishroom along wide corridors and service elevators, using standardized wheeled carts and racks.

tasks.label: Receive and store supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service/casual restaurant back-of-house: a food and dry-goods delivery arrives at the back door on a hand truck; the dishwasher/porter counts cases against the invoice, breaks down the load, carries mixed cases (canned goods, bulk flour/sugar sacks, cases of oil) through a busy kitchen line to dry-storage wire shelving, and rotates older stock forward.

Restaurant/bar dish room: receive and store dish-machine and cleaning supplies - cases of detergent and rinse aid, 5-gallon sanitizer jugs, degreaser boxes, paper goods, spare dish racks - into a chemical closet, under-counter shelves and dish-area storage, keeping chemicals separated from food per health code.

Restaurant: put away chilled and frozen perishables immediately on delivery - 40-50 lb cases of protein, dairy crates, produce boxes, frozen cartons - into the walk-in cooler and reach-in freezer; heavy doors, cold, wet/greasy floors, tight aisles, date-labeling and FIFO rotation.

Institutional kitchen (hospital, school district, university, hotel/casino commissary) with a loading dock: pallets and roll carts of food, paper and chemical supplies are received, counted against a manifest and temperature-checked, moved by pallet jack or cart to a large dry store, cooler and freezer, then broken down and shelved.

Small urban restaurant with awkward access: the driver leaves the delivery at the curb or on the public sidewalk; the worker must move cases through a narrow service passage or down steep cellar stairs into a basement storeroom, working around pedestrians, weather and clutter.

tasks.label: Clean garbage cans with water or steam.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift in a restaurant/bar back-of-house: dishwasher pulls liners from 32–44 gal Brute-style kitchen, prep and bar cans, wheels them to the mop sink or dish pit, hoses them with hot water and degreaser, scrubs interior and exterior with a long-handled brush, rinses, sanitizes, inverts to drain, and returns and relines them.

Institutional dish room (hospital, school, hotel, corporate cafeteria): several large barrels and rolling waste carts plus lids are washed in a designated wash area with a hot-water hose or pressure/steam washer, sanitized to health-code standard, and rolled back to their stations on a set schedule.

Small receptacles: under-counter prep bins, compost and recycling pails, bus-station bins and can lids washed in the three-compartment or pot sink, or run through the warewasher/utensil washer when they fit, then air-dried and re-placed.

Outdoor dumpster corral or shared back alley: large wheeled totes and grease-fouled cans hosed or steam-cleaned on uneven, greasy pavement, in weather, with parked vehicles, deliveries and passersby around and drainage to a grease trap or floor drain.

Heavy-soil deep clean in the dish room or on the dock: cans with dried-on food, congealed grease, spilled liquids or pest activity require soaking, scraping, degreaser and multiple hot-water passes before sanitizing and drying.

Off-site or mobile foodservice (catering event, food truck, stadium/festival stand): waste cans and totes rinsed and sanitized at a temporary site with a hose or portable pressure washer, with no fixed wash bay and improvised drainage.

sources.system: Douglas Machines BDW-1-HD Barrel & Drum (garbage can) Washer
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page updated; product line long commercial)
sources.title: Barrel Washing Machine | Douglas Machines Corp.
sources.claim: Douglas Machines sells a front-loading garbage can / barrel washer (BDW-1-HD) that runs an automatic 4/6/8-minute wash cycle with heated water through rotating spray arms and a 30-second sanitizing rinse, sized for containers up to 26 in dia. x 38 in tall (e.g., 32-gal Brute cans); the operator only loads the can and starts the cycle.

sources.system: Douglas Machines vat, bin & tote washers
sources.title: Bin Washer & Tote Washer | Douglas Machines Corp.
sources.claim: Douglas Machines' vat, bin and tote washers use heated water and wash/rinse jets that clean both the inside and outside ..., with adjustable cycle times and recirculating tanks — i.e., the machine, not a person, does the scrubbing action on the container surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class (washing/sanitizing bulk refuse and food containers with hot water) applied to bins and totes of the same size and soil type as kitchen garbage cans.

sources.title: Automatic Bin Wash Machine | Cleans any size of EU wheelie bin quick!
sources.claim: Morclean's BinWash AUTO is a fixed bin-washing station with a hydraulic lift that raises a wheeled bin of any EU size into an enclosed housing and cleans it with bi-directional 360-degree rotary heads on one-button operation, with no manual washing or manual handling by the operator; marketed for hospital/medical waste areas.

sources.system: DYNASET JPL High Pressure Bin Washing System (washing robot)
sources.date: 2020 product launch; page current as of 2026-07
sources.title: JPL High Pressure Bin Washing System – Automated Bin Washing
sources.claim: Dynaset's JPL bin-washing robot, mounted on a refuse vehicle, automatically inserts a 3D high-pressure nozzle into a waste bin after it is emptied, washes it and returns it clean, with optional hot-water heating and wastewater capture — machine-controlled nozzle manipulation rather than an operator-held lance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing refuse bins on a collection route. Same objects (wheeled waste bins), same medium (hot high-pressure water) and same acceptance standard (visibly clean, deodorized interior), demonstrating machine-controlled insertion and washing without a human lance.

sources.title: Container Washer: Industrial Box Washing machine
sources.claim: PHS industrial container washers clean the inside and outside of a container with a rotating spray arm plus detergent during an automatic main wash cycle; loading the dirty container into the machine is a simple manual placement step.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class — machine washing of large reusable containers with hot water and detergent — with the same acceptance criterion (clean inside and out) as kitchen garbage cans.

tasks.label: Load or unload trucks that deliver or pick up food or supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Independent or small-chain restaurant with no dock: the broadline/produce/beverage truck double-parks in an alley or at the curb; the dishwasher meets the driver at the liftgate, takes mixed corrugated cases, produce crates, milk crates, bagged product and 5-gallon oil jugs, stacks them on a two-wheeler, wheels them over broken pavement and a threshold (sometimes down basement stairs), and stages them by the walk-in during service. Weather and street conditions as found.

Large institutional or chain foodservice operation with a loading dock (hospital, university dining, hotel, casino, stadium, large chain restaurant): a trailer backs into the dock; the worker breaks down floor-loaded cases onto pallets/carts or rolls palletized freight off with a pallet jack, counts against the invoice, and moves the loads into the receiving area, cooler and dry store.

Outbound loading at the same dock or service yard: stacking and loading empty milk crates, bread trays, empty kegs, pallets and dunnage, dish/linen bins, returned or damaged product and used-oil/rendering containers onto the truck that is picking up.

Heavy or awkward items moved between the truck and the store room: full beer kegs (~160 lb), 50-lb flour and sugar sacks, ice bags, bulk oil, wet seafood boxes packed with drain ice; handled by hand or keg cart, often over a curb, ramp or short flight of steps at a bar or restaurant back entrance.

Catering/commissary work: loading a van or box truck in the kitchen driveway with hotel pans, sheet-pan racks, chafers, beverage tubs and coolers, then unloading them at an event venue's parking lot or service entrance and carrying them inside.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch, a mobile case-handling robot, is commercially deployed by DHL to unload cases from containers and trailers at logistics sites, with an agreement covering 1,000+ additional units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is unloading corrugated cases from a truck/container at a dock; the objects (brown and printed cases up to 50 lb), the stacking geometry and the dock environment are the same ones a foodservice receiver faces on an inbound delivery.

sources.title: Stretch - Mobile Warehouse Robots | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Stretch handles a wide range of unfixtured case types and sizes up to 50 lb and copes with messy, hand-stacked loads inside trailers and containers.
sources.transferJustification: Foodservice inbound cases are the same class of object (corrugated cases, mostly under 50 lb) presented the same way (hand-stacked in a trailer), so case-unloading performance carries over to unloading a food delivery.

sources.title: Lidl to unload containers with Stretch robots from Boston Dynamics in 2026 - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: A grocery retailer piloted Stretch for unloading food-retail containers and is rolling out 22 units to its warehouses.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the case-unloading capability applies to grocery/food cases specifically, the same goods a dishwasher unloads from a food delivery truck.

sources.title: Pickle Unload System - Looking Glass XR Services
sources.claim: The Pickle Unload System autonomously unloads floor-loaded trailers and ocean containers of packages up to ~65 lb at customer docks with minimal operator input.
sources.transferJustification: Hand-stacked (floor-loaded) mixed cases are exactly how a foodservice delivery arrives; the robot works at an ordinary dock with no dock modification, matching the receiving step of this task.

sources.title: Pickle Robot spearheads automatic truck unloading pilot - Supply Chain Management Review
sources.claim: Pickle's truck-unloading robots run in production at customer distribution centers, including United Exchange Corp., a distributor of consumer goods and food items.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical task (taking cases off a truck at a dock) with food-item cases among the freight handled.

sources.title: Walmart and Fox Robotics Enter into Multi-Year Commercial Agreement
sources.claim: Fox Robotics' FoxBot autonomous forklift unloads pallets out of trailers at Walmart distribution centers and has autonomously completed millions of pallet pulls for North American customers.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the palletized half of a foodservice delivery: pulling pallets out of the trailer and moving them off the dock into the building, the same physical result the receiver produces with a pallet jack.

sources.title: FedEx Case Study | Dexterity
sources.claim: Dexterity's Mech robot performs autonomous truck loading at FedEx, stacking mixed, randomly sized boxes into trailers.
sources.transferJustification: Loading a pickup truck with returns and empties is the same physical operation: stacking heterogeneous cases/containers into a trailer to a stable load, at a facility dock.

sources.title: Slip Robotics introduces SlipLift for autonomous trailer loading - Engineering.com
sources.claim: Slip Robotics' SlipLift/SlipBot autonomously load and unload palletized freight into trailers and box trucks at ordinary docks without facility modification.
sources.transferJustification: Loading empties, dunnage and returns onto a pickup truck reduces to placing palletized/stacked loads into a trailer or box truck, which this system does autonomously at standard docks.

sources.title: Automatic depalletizing and palletizing | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Purpose-built industrial robot cells handle very heavy beverage kegs; a US brewery has automated ~150 lb keg handling with KUKA robots.
sources.transferJustification: Kegs are the heaviest awkward item in this task; keg handling is proven only inside fixtured, fenced cells where kegs arrive on conveyors, not loose off a delivery truck.

sources.title: Automatic depalletizing and palletizing | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Automated 'goods-to-truck' cells load heavy sacks onto delivery trucks in route order in a fixtured, purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Loading heavy sacks onto a truck is the E1 version of this task's heavy-item instance: sacks are conveyed to the robot in known positions rather than wrestled off a tailgate.

sources.title: Innovative Automated Logistics Solutions | Copal Handling Systems
sources.claim: Copal's container unloading systems autonomously detect, grasp and place loose-loaded boxes and heavy bags out of containers onto conveyors and pallets.
sources.transferJustification: Bagged goods (flour, sugar) are part of the heavy-item instance; Copal shows autonomous sack/box unloading, but only from containers presented at a fixed unloading station.

sources.system: Stretch and other dock unloading robots (DHL fleet)
sources.title: Robotic unloading becomes more accessible as warehouses weigh applicability | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: Industry reporting on deployed dock-unloading robots notes they are matched to sites with the right operational fit and struggle with irregular loads and very light or heavy products.
sources.transferJustification: Bounds the positive evidence: deployed unloaders handle standard cases and pallets at conditioned docks, not loose kegs, dripping seafood boxes or curbside handoffs.

tasks.label: Prepare and package individual place settings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual/family-dining restaurant back-of-house: after the dish machine, the worker pulls clean metal flatware from bins and makes roll-ups — fork, knife and spoon laid on a paper or cloth napkin, rolled and banded/stickered — several hundred per shift, stacked into bus tubs for the servers.

Quick-service / diner takeout station: assembling and bagging disposable cutlery-and-napkin kits (plus salt, pepper, condiment packets, straw) in batches of hundreds so they can be dropped into takeout and delivery orders; done at a prep table in the kitchen between dish loads.

Hotel banquet or catering kitchen before an event: washed flatware is run through a polisher/dried, counted settings are wrapped in linen or paper napkins, and the finished settings are packed into tubs or racks by the hundreds for the ballroom.

Institutional foodservice (hospital, nursing home, school cafeteria): building napkin-wrapped or bagged cutlery packs and pre-setting patient/resident meal trays with the pack, napkin and condiment items per the diet card, before the hot-food tray line runs.

Fine dining or banquet floor: carrying polished flatware, folded napkins, plates and glassware out to the dining room and laying individual covers on set tables before service, matching the house standard.

sources.title: He invented a machine that rolls silverware into napkins. It could be a game-changer for restaurants
sources.claim: NapSpin is a commercial benchtop machine that automatically rolls a restaurant's own clean flatware into napkins: the operator loads a silverware tray and a napkin tray, sets a count, and the machine produces finished roll-ups unattended.

sources.title: He invented a machine that rolls silverware into napkins. It could be a game-changer for restaurants
sources.claim: NapSpin machines have been sold to food-service customers including a hospital, i.e. the rollup-making machine is in service in institutional kitchens, not only a prototype.

sources.title: NapSpin — The Machine
sources.claim: NapSpin's throughput and loading figures: batch cycles of 50 roll-ups, over 120 roll-ups per hour, two-minute load, with cartridges configurable to the customer's existing utensil patterns and up to five utensils per roll-up.

sources.system: MWES multi-robot silverware wrapping and packaging line
sources.title: Case Studies: Disposable Silverware Napkin Wrapping Automation System
sources.claim: Midwest Engineered Systems built and installed a production system that assembles, wraps, bags and cases individually wrapped disposable place settings (utensils + napkin) for a cutlery manufacturer, running at 100 pieces per minute.

sources.system: MWES multi-robot silverware wrapping and packaging line
sources.title: Case Studies: Disposable Silverware Napkin Wrapping Automation System
sources.claim: The same MWES line needs only an operator to fill bulk utensil hoppers and napkin feeders; the assembly and wrapping itself runs under PLC control, replacing 10-20 manual assemblers with 1-2 machine tenders.

sources.system: MWES dual multi-robot silverware wrapping machines
sources.title: Disposable Silverware Napkin Wrapping Automation System | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: MWES describes the wrapping stations as robotic: multi-robot cells wrap napkins around utensils and robotic pick-and-place positions the fork, knife and spoon before wrapping and bagging.

sources.title: The Roller Xpress in Partnership with Alphamated LLC — PCU
sources.claim: The Roller Xpress is a marketed hospitality/healthcare machine that automatically combines forks, spoons and knives into ..., banded napkin bundle for restaurants, hotels and hospitals.

sources.title: Cutlery dryers & polishers | Sammic US
sources.claim: Commercial flatware polisher/dryer machines automatically dry, polish and de-spot washed cutlery at up to 8,000 pieces per hour, the step that precedes wrapping settings in banquet and fine-dining kitchens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: polishing/drying washed flatware. It is the input step of preparing a place setting in banquet and fine-dining kitchens — same objects (metal flatware presented in bulk to a machine) and the output is the polished flatware the wrapping machines then package.

sources.system: PKR / Twin PKR delta pick-and-place cell (Codian delta robots)
sources.title: Tray Packer | Top Load Robotic Case & Tray Packing
sources.claim: Vision-guided delta-robot pick-and-place cells automatically top-load flexible bags and packages into trays or cases on food packaging lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing lightweight packets into trays on a conveyor line. Pre-setting a meal tray with a wrapped cutlery pack, napkin and condiment sachets involves the same object class (light flexible packets), the same cm-level placement precision into tray compartments, and the same conveyorized line environment.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: An independent 2026 assessment of autonomous robot capability finds the best general-purpose kitchen demonstration (Figure's dishwasher work) handles plates, bowls and glasses but not small cutlery, and has not shown transfer to ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling tableware in a kitchen. It bounds what general-purpose robots can do with the small metal utensils that place settings require, supporting negative judgments at E2/E3.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: Dyna Robotics' DYNA-1 stationary dual-arm system folds napkins and towels autonomously at commercial customer sites — 850+ napkins in a 24-hour unattended run and 200,000+ towels for laundry clients — but its commercial deployments are limited to uniform linen items, not assembled place settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: folding napkins to client quality standards in commercial facilities. It shows deformable-napkin handling is possible at E2, but no cited system combines picking loose flatware with napkin wrapping in a human kitchen, which is why the wrapped-setting instances stop at E1.

tasks.label: Set up banquet tables.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel/convention ballroom, morning of an event: crew (including the dish/utility worker) hauls folding round tables off dollies, unfolds and positions 20-40 of them per the banquet event order diagram, sets 200-300 chairs off chair carts around them, and drapes floor-length linens with even drop, working to a hard set time.

Setting the covers on already-dressed banquet tables: walking the room placing chargers/plates, rolled or loose silverware, folded napkins, and 2-3 glasses per seat at standard spacing for 100-300 covers, with china and glass carried in from the dish room in stacks and racks.

Buffet, carving and beverage station setup: skirting and clipping linens to 6-ft tables, staging chafing dishes with water pans and lighting fuel, placing serving utensils, risers, stacks of plates, glass racks, water pitchers and coffee urns along the line in the banquet hall.

Restaurant private dining room or small catered function inside the restaurant: pushing rectangles/rounds together into a new configuration, laying cloths and overlays, then setting 12-40 covers, done between services with staff and sometimes guests moving through the room.

Off-premise or outdoor catered event (tent, patio, park pavilion, rented hall): unloading tables, chairs, linens and tableware from a truck, setting up on uneven ground or a space taken as found, in wind, heat or dim light.

Staging supplies for a setup: loading and moving carts of clean china, glass racks, flatware bins and folded linens from the dish room/storage through service corridors and service elevators to the banquet room before setting begins.

sources.system: B.PRO automated tray-assembly line (food portioning conveyor)
sources.title: B.PRO automation for processes in the catering sector | B.PRO
sources.claim: B.PRO's automated catering tray line, installed in a university hospital kitchen, places plates on trays with a vacuum module and uses a camera-guided gantry robot to place packaged cutlery sets, positioning up to ten components at predefined positions on each tray.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated meal-tray assembly. It is a place setting brought to the machine - plate, cutlery set, cup and accompaniments laid at predefined positions on a presented tray - so the objects, precision and acceptance standard match banquet cover setting when the work is fixtured and presented as at E1.

sources.system: Chef Robotics CPG component-assembly application (Chef robot arms, RaaS)
sources.title: Chef Robotics Expands into Component Assembly for CPG Manufacturing | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' commercially deployed food-production robots pick deformable, variably posed items such as folded cutlery packs and sachets from unsorted bins with AI vision and place them at a required angle in the correct compartment of a tray or bowl at production speed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tray/component assembly on a packaging line. Placing cutlery packs and small items at specified positions and orientations on presented trays is the same pick-and-place problem as laying flatware and small tableware at a cover once the work is fixtured.

sources.system: pi-0 (π0) vision-language-action policy on bimanual manipulators
sources.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control (arXiv:2410.24164)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0 generalist policy was evaluated on a table-setting task in which the robot takes a placemat, dishes, silverware, napkin ... out of a bin and arranges them on a table, running autonomously under language instructions in the lab.

sources.system: Figure 03 humanoids with Helix-02 VLA policy
sources.title: Helix 02 Bedroom Tidy
sources.claim: Two Figure humanoids running a single learned vision-language-action policy autonomously reset a staged bedroom, including pushing an office chair under a desk, draping a garment on a coat tree, and cooperatively making a bed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: room reset with furniture pushing and bed linen spreading. It is the closest published evidence for moving seating and spreading cloth, but it is a staged single-room demo, not a rate-and-quality linen dress-out of a banquet room.

sources.system: ALORE (autonomous large-object rearrangement with a legged manipulator)
sources.title: [2602.04214] ALORE: Autonomous Large-Object Rearrangement with a Legged Manipulator
sources.claim: ALORE, an autonomous large-object rearrangement system on a legged manipulator, rearranged 32 chairs in eight continuous real-world loops over about 40 minutes without a failure and executed autonomous rearrangement over a ~40 m route.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pushing chairs to target positions indoors. It substantiates repositioning of seating but not unfolding and placing banquet tables or dressing them with linen, so it covers only part of a room set.

sources.system: Aethon TUG / T3 autonomous mobile delivery robots (with ReadyElevator, Carrello carts)
sources.title: Hospital Robots | Solutions for Healthcare - Aethon
sources.claim: Aethon's TUG mobile robots are deployed in hospitals to autonomously deliver meal carts and linen carts to units and return soiled carts, navigating corridors and integrating with elevators; carts are retrofitted to the robot base.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: institutional cart transport of linens and food service ware. Moving a loaded china/linen cart from a dish room through service corridors and elevators to a function room is the same job in a comparably controlled building.

sources.title: Dynamic Cloth Manipulation Considering Variable Stiffness and Material Change Using Deep Predictive Model with Parametric Bias
sources.claim: The musculoskeletal wheeled robot Musashi-W performed a table-setting experiment that included dynamic cloth manipulation: it laid a cloth on a table like a tablecloth and then placed an object on it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying a cloth on a small table in a lab. It is the only cited tablecloth demonstration and is a one-off research trial on a small cloth, far from the even, wrinkle-free floor-length drape a banquet room requires.

roles.description: Welcome patrons, seat them at tables or in lounge, and help ensure quality of facilities and service.

tasks.label: Provide guests with menus.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual/family full-service restaurant or diner at a normal service period: host greets a walk-in party of 2-6 at the stand, pulls the matching number of laminated menus, walks the party through the dining room past occupied tables and servers, and sets a menu down in front of each guest at the booth or table.

Bar, lounge, or coffee shop: host or greeter hands a food/drink menu to a guest seated at the bar or in lounge seating, or across a counter to a walk-in; often single guests or pairs, sometimes standing in a crowded waiting area while the table is prepared.

Fine dining / upscale restaurant: host escorts the party to the table, presents an opened menu to each seated guest from the correct side, hands the wine list to the host of the party, and adds special menus (tasting, dessert, celebration card) with a polished, timed presentation.

Large party or party with special needs: 8-15 guests at joined tables, high chairs, children; host must gather and distribute an assortment - adult menus, kids' menus with crayons, allergen/gluten-free menus - around a long table and to guests still arriving.

QR-code / digital-menu venue: host seats the party and points out the QR placard already on the table, or hands over one shared laminated card or a tablet, fetching a paper menu only when a guest asks.

sources.title: KettyBot - The Future of Delivery and Reception | Pudu Robotics
sources.claim: Pudu's KettyBot reception/delivery robot autonomously plans a path and leads arriving customers to their tables in restaurants; it carries a tray for light items and is sold commercially worldwide.

sources.title: BellaBot Operation guide - Pudu Academy
sources.claim: Pudu's official operating documentation describes a Guiding mode in which the serving robot acts as a receptionist at the door and guides customers to a selected table number; navigation to the table is autonomous once the destination is chosen at the greeting point.

sources.system: Pudu KettyBot deployed by Navia Robotics
sources.title: Navia Robotics - Kettybot is the ideal serving robot for use in cafes, bakeries and small food service establishments
sources.claim: A US restaurant-robot integrator states that in normal operation KettyBot is stationed at the front of the restaurant as an escorting/receptionist robot and carries menus on its tray for guests to take when they are seated.

sources.system: Restaurant service robots (BellaBot-class) in Twin Cities restaurants
sources.title: Restaurant robots are here to serve you | uniondemocrat.com (Minnesota Star Tribune/TNS)
sources.claim: Mobile service robots working in a dozen Twin Cities restaurants escort diners to their tables and carry dishes through the dining room during live service.
sources.transferJustification: Escorting a party to a table through a live dining room is the same navigation-and-presentation act the host performs while delivering menus; carrying dishes shows the tray payload and table-side stop are handled autonomously.

sources.title: BellaBot Transforms Skylark Group Dining - Pudu Robotics
sources.claim: Skylark, a large Japanese family-restaurant chain, deployed about 3,000 BellaBot delivery robots across more than 2,000 restaurants, where they carry food, drinks and tableware to guests' tables and guests take the items off the tray.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: multi-tray table-side delivery of food and tableware in family restaurants at chain scale. Menus are lighter, non-spillable items handled the same way (carried to the table, taken by guests), so reliability carries over.

sources.title: Bear Robotics and SoftBank join forces to mass produce Servi, foodservice robot | Nation's Restaurant News
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi is an ... robot deployed at US chain restaurants including Denny's and a multi-store Chili's pilot, navigating crowded dining rooms to tables without teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously transporting items on trays from a station to a specific table in US casual-dining rooms - the same route, obstacle conditions and table-side stop required to bring menus to a seated party.

tasks.label: Greet guests and seat them at tables or in waiting areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual/family full-service restaurant (chain or independent), moderate traffic with open tables: host greets a walk-in party of 1-4 at the podium, confirms party size, picks up menus, escorts the party across the dining room to a clean assigned table, sets down menus and rollups, and tells them their server's name.

Peak lunch/dinner rush at a full-service restaurant: host greets arrivals, quotes a wait, takes the name into the waitlist, seats/holds parties in a crowded lobby or bar waiting area, pages them, then threads a party of 4-6 through congested aisles and busy server traffic to a just-bussed table, pacing seating across server sections.

Party needing physical accommodation: family with toddlers requiring a high chair or booster fetched and placed at the table, a guest using a wheelchair or walker needing a chair pulled away and a path cleared, or a large group needing chairs and tables pushed together before seating.

Upscale/fine-dining or hotel restaurant: formal greeting and reservation check-in at the podium, taking coats, escorting the party at a measured pace, pulling out and pushing in chairs, unfolding napkins onto laps, and presenting menus individually.

Coffee shop, cafe, lounge or bar: host or greeter welcomes arrivals at the entrance, tells them to sit anywhere or directs/briefly escorts them to open lounge, counter or patio seating, or asks them to wait a moment near the entrance; minimal handling beyond menus.

sources.title: Product FAQs: Your Questions Answered — Bear Robotics
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi, a commercially sold autonomous mobile restaurant robot, has a dedicated Host Mode marketed for greeting and seating guests.

sources.title: Chili's workers find robots to be a helpful addition — Restaurant Business
sources.claim: At Chili's Grill & Bar, Bear Robotics' 'Rita' robot was deployed to ~61 restaurants and is most often used to guide arriving customers to their table in the dining room.

sources.developer: Bear Robotics / Toast – Indian & Asian Fusion
sources.title: How Three Independent Restaurants are Using Robotics to Improve Operations and the Guest Dining Experience
sources.claim: An independent restaurant in Zephyr Cove, Nevada runs a Servi Plus robot named 'Jane' that greets customers, shows table availability ... seats.

sources.title: KettyBot Pro | Pudu Robotics' Delivery & Reception Promotion Robot for Restaurants and Retail
sources.claim: Pudu Robotics sells KettyBot Pro as a reception/concierge robot for restaurants and retail that autonomously greets and guides customers; the KettyBot line is widely shipped commercially.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics Inc. Form 424B4 prospectus (SEC EDGAR)
sources.claim: Richtech Robotics states in its SEC prospectus that its commercially deployed Matradee restaurant robot greets guests at the reception area ... leads them to their table, running full shifts on one charge.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels
sources.claim: Restaurant service robots of this class navigate guest-facing dining rooms autonomously with LiDAR and cameras, and newer models are built for tight restaurant floor plans, but they are trays on wheels without arms.
sources.transferJustification: Same restaurant dining-room environment and same robot used in Host Mode escorting; establishes autonomous navigation among guests and the absence of manipulators.

sources.system: anthropomorphic wheeled service robot (restaurant case study)
sources.developer: restaurant robot supplier studied in Frontiers in Robotics and AI paper
sources.title: Digital transformation in restaurants: key aspects of service robot deployment from project initiation to evaluation
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed case study of a real restaurant robot deployment describes a wheeled robot that greets guests with welcome messages but has no arms, and documents that the facility layout must be assessed and mapped for robot navigation.

sources.title: Are robot waiters the wave of the future? Some restaurants say yes - CBS News
sources.claim: Trade/established press reports that restaurant robots in service in the US greet guests and lead them to their tables, with tens of thousands in use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift walkthrough of a casual full-service dining room before doors open: host walks the floor checking that each table is wiped, correctly set (flatware, napkins, glassware, condiments, menus), chairs squared, booths crumb-free and floors clear; straightens or fixes small deviations and flags the rest to bussers or the manager.

Mid-service table-turn check in a busy full-service restaurant: continuously scanning the room for uncleared or dirty tables, confirming a table has actually been wiped and re-set with clean settings before seating the next party, spotting stray glassware, crumbs, spills and pushed-out chairs, correcting minor items and calling bussers for the rest, all while guests move through the room.

Coffee shop / fast-casual between-customer sweep: checking tabletops after self-bussing customers leave, wiping crumbs and rings, clearing abandoned cups, trays and trash, tidying chairs, and checking the condiment/napkin/lid station is stocked and clean.

Fine dining or banquet pre-service inspection against a written standard: flatware aligned and spaced to the cover, spot-free polished glassware, correctly folded napkins, unstained linen, candles/flowers/table numbers placed, correct cover counts; the host corrects deviations item by item.

Cleanliness patrol of the dining-room and entryway floors during and after service: identifying spills, crumbs, dropped food and debris on hard floors and carpet in the seating area and ensuring they get cleaned promptly.

sources.title: Robot automates dishwashing in commercial kitchens | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Dishcraft's purpose-built robotic dishwashing machine autonomously handles each dish and uses computer vision to re-inspect every item for remaining food residue, re-washing items that fail before racking them as clean.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleanliness inspection of tableware with automatic corrective action. It substantiates the core judgment of this task — deciding whether a dining item meets the cleanliness standard and acting on failures — for restaurant tableware when the work is brought to a purpose-built machine (E1 counterfactual).

sources.title: Dishcraft Robotics raises funding to help caterers, cafeterias reopen | The Robot Report
sources.claim: Dishcraft's vision-based robotic dishwashing ran as a commercial service supplying clean plates, bowls, cups and utensils ... corporate, hotel and hospital cafeterias.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the vision-inspection-plus-correction dishware system was a real commercial deployment, not a one-off demo.

sources.claim: Chef Robotics' deployed food-assembly cells use computer vision to track containers on a production ... image each one before and after deposits, performing automated QA on whether contents are placed correctly in the tray.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying that a presented tray is assembled to a standard and correcting placement. Comparable objects (food-service trays, portions) and comparable precision to checking a place setting, with the work fixtured and conveyed to the machine.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing table-setup components (folded napkins) to a repeatable standard at a fixed station; shows worker-quality reliability on a setup element when the linen is presented to the machine.

instances.label: Full-service casual/family restaurant during a rush: host busses a just-vacated four-top — stacks plates, glasses, flatware and trash into a bus tub, carries it to the dish pit, wipes the tabletop and booth seat, sweeps crumbs, and resets place settings, all while guests and servers move around the aisle.

Food running in a full-service restaurant: host picks up hot plated entrees from the expo window, carries them on a tray or by arm through a crowded dining room, matches ticket to table and seat position, places each plate in front of the correct guest, and adds sides/condiments.

Beverage service: host pours and refills water at occupied tables from a pitcher, carries drinks from the bar on a tray, sets glasses down among crowded tableware without spilling, and collects empties.

Counter-service coffee shop or fast-casual: host/attendant clears self-bus tables (mugs, cups, lids, crumbs, trash) into bins, wipes tabletops and pushes in chairs, delivers order trays or numbered orders to tables, and restocks the condiment station.

Bar/lounge or outdoor patio at peak hours: collecting glassware and bottles from high-tops and among a standing crowd in dim light and noise, delivering drinks to guests, and wiping tables outdoors in wind/weather.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi family are autonomous mobile robots deployed commercially in restaurants for food running, table bussing and drink delivery, but they are tray/shelf transporters without arms — staff or guests load and unload them, so the table-side handling of plates and dishes is not performed by the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (food running and bussing) in the same environment; cited to establish that deployed restaurant-floor robots perform only transport, not the pick-and-place of dishes at the table.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics operates autonomous dish-handling robots live in multiple restaurants around the clock, taking messy bus tubs of dirty dishes and turning them into clean, stacked dishes, handling shiny plates and transparent glassware with millimeter-accuracy perception.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dish handling at a fixed station. It substantiates the E1 counterfactual for bussing — when soiled tableware is presented to the machine in a bus tub/station, the same objects (plates, glasses, flatware) are grasped, sorted and stacked at commercial reliability.

sources.title: finibo: The automated dish sorting robot provides a solution to labor shortages
sources.claim: The finibo / W-Robo automatic tableware-sorting robot picks and sorts dishes flowing off a conveyor dishwasher outlet in commercial dish rooms, a purpose-built cell installed in the washing area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling restaurant tableware at a machine-built station; supports the E1 counterfactual in which dishes from bussed tables are presented to the machine on fixtures/conveyor rather than found on a dining table.

sources.title: A robot barista represents a larger vision for bringing robotics to more areas of retail

sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing and serving beverages to patrons from a fixtured counter cell — same objects (cups, drinks) and same purpose as beverage service, but with the guest brought to the machine rather than the machine to the table.

sources.claim: Dyna Robotics' DYNA-1 stationary dual-arm system autonomously folded more than 700 ... in 24 hours at 99.4% success with no human intervention, transferring zero-shot to a customer (restaurant) environment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: front-of-house table-setting prep (napkin/linen handling) at a fixed dual-arm station; substantiates the reset portion of bussing when materials are presented to the machine (E1).

sources.title: Google Deploys Fleet Of Robots To Sort Trash, Wipe Tables & Open Doors
sources.claim: Alphabet's Everyday Robots ran a fleet of over 100 mobile manipulators autonomously wiping cafeteria tables and sorting trash on Google's campuses; the program was later shut down and the machines were never a commercial product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiping cafeteria tabletops in an institution-controlled facility; shows the surface-cleaning element is feasible, but the fleet was a prototype program, discontinued, and never cleared dishes at service speed.

sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (table clearing) but in homes at demo maturity and household pace; cited to show the mobile-manipulation frontier does not yet meet restaurant-service reliability and speed.

tasks.label: Inspect restrooms for cleanliness and availability of supplies, and clean restrooms when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine mid-shift check of a standard restaurant restroom (2-6 fixtures): scan stalls, sinks, mirrors and floor; flush, wipe water/soap splashes off the counter and mirror, pick up stray paper towels and litter, spot-wipe the floor; dispensers are adequately stocked, nothing else needed.

Check finds a real mess during service: soiled toilet bowl/seat, urine or water pooled on the floor, splattered counter and mirror. Host scrubs and disinfects the fixtures, wipes the counter/mirror, mops and dries the floor before guests return.

Check finds consumables low or the bin full: fetch toilet paper, paper towels, hand soap and seat covers from the stock room, unlock and load the wall dispensers, pull and tie off the full liner, carry it out, and re-line the bin.

Peak-rush check of a single-occupancy or two-fixture restroom in a small cafe, bar or coffee shop with guests queuing outside: knock, enter a cramped room, quick wipe of sink and seat, pick up litter, flush, and be out in a minute or two between users.

Major incident found on a check: vomit, an overflowing or clogged toilet, or other biohazard. Host contains it, closes the restroom and sets out a sign, cleans what is within scope, and escalates to the manager or porter.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots

sources.title: Those viral bathroom-cleaning bots won't be saving our butts anytime soon (Popular Science)

instances.label: Casual/full-service restaurant: host takes a to-go order by phone or at the host stand, rings it into the POS, then when the kitchen plates it transfers hot entrees, sides and salads into clamshells, adds dressings, sauce cups, bread, utensils and napkins, bags it, staples the ticket and stages it on the to-go shelf.

tasks.label: Operate cash registers to accept payments for food and beverages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Counter-service restaurant or coffee shop: host/cashier at the front register rings a guest's order on a touchscreen POS, takes a credit/debit card (tap, insert or swipe on the attached terminal), confirms tip/total, prints and hands over the receipt. Indoor, fixed register station, public queue.

Cash transaction at the register: guest pays with bills and coins, worker keys the tender, opens the drawer, counts out change accurately, hands back change plus receipt; occasional large bills, damaged notes, or 'keep the change' tips. Restaurant/cafe counter, rush conditions.

Full-service restaurant: host settles a guest check at the front register or host stand — pulls up the table's open check, takes card or cash, adds the tip, prints the merchant/guest copies, returns card and receipt; sometimes applies a gift card or coupon.

Problem transactions: declined card requiring an alternate tender, an item charged in error requiring a void, a manager-approved comp or discount, a refund, a disputed total or gift-card balance question, all resolved at the register with the guest present.

Register open/close duties: counting the starting bank into the drawer, mid-shift cash drops to the safe, end-of-shift drawer count, reconciliation against the POS Z-report and reporting overages/shortages.

tasks.label: Prepare cash receipts after establishments close, and make bank deposits.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casual full-service restaurant at close: the host/closer pulls cash drawers from 2-3 POS stations, carries them to the back office, counts bills and coin, runs the POS Z-report, reconciles cash to the report, records totals on the cash sheet, fills a deposit slip, seals the bag and locks it in the safe.

Server and bartender cash-outs at close: collect each employee's envelope of cash plus checks, gift certificates and tip declarations, verify each against the POS cash-out report, consolidate everything into a single night deposit, note any over/short by employee.

Coffee shop or small lounge with a single till: count out the starting bank, count the day's cash receipts and coin, log the total against the register tape, bag the deposit and secure it in the safe or drop box.

The bank run: carry the sealed deposit bag out of the establishment, walk or drive on public streets to the bank branch, deposit at the night depository or with a teller, bring back the validated deposit receipt for the manager's file.

Busy weekend/holiday close with high volume: large mixed cash including heavy coin and small bills, an initial out-of-balance count requiring a recount and a search for a missed drop or unrecorded void, and a change order prepared for the next day before the deposit is finalized.

tasks.label: Inspect work performed to ensure that it meets specifications and established standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel/resort guest-room inspection: after a room attendant finishes, the supervisor/inspector enters the room, checks bed-making and linen, dust on ledges, lamps and headboards, looks under the bed, inspects the bathroom (mirror streaks, hair in tub/shower, toilet, chrome), verifies amenities and supplies restocked, TV remote, HVAC and drapes, fixes small deficiencies or sends the room back, and logs pass/fail with notes in a housekeeping app before releasing the room.

Nightly walk-through of an office/commercial building after the janitorial crew: supervisor tours restrooms, lobbies, elevators, break rooms, offices and stairwells checking that trash was emptied and liners replaced, floors vacuumed/mopped with no edges or corners missed, restroom fixtures cleaned and dispensers restocked, glass and entry mats clean, lights and doors secured; logs deficiencies with photos and issues rework instructions.

Hospital/healthcare EVS inspection: supervisor verifies discharge/terminal cleans and daily cleans of patient rooms, ORs, isolation rooms and public areas, checking high-touch surfaces (bedrails, call buttons, over-bed tables, door handles), curtain changes, waste and sharps handling, often running an objective audit (ATP swab or fluorescent-marker removal check) in PPE and documenting compliance scores for infection prevention.

Periodic/special-project inspection: floor stripping and refinishing, burnishing, carpet extraction, high dusting, window/glass work in schools, retail or offices, usually at night or on weekends. Supervisor checks gloss and uniformity, streaks, wax build-up on baseboards and corners, splash on walls, carpet drying/wicking, and that furniture is returned; approves or orders a redo before the space reopens.

Residential cleaning franchise supervisor inspects a crew's work in a client's private home: varied layouts, clutter, pets and personal belongings, delicate surfaces; checks bathrooms, kitchen appliances and counters, floors and dusted surfaces, confirms items returned to place and no damage, and addresses the homeowner's concerns on the spot.

sources.system: Spot (Spot CAM+IR, Enhanced Autonomy Payload, gas sensor)
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities - anomaly detection, thermal inspection, gauge reading - navigating a 40-acre plant on scheduled routes and self-docking: autonomous mobile inspection exists, but for asset/condition data rather than cleaning-quality auditing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility inspection rounds. Transfer is only partial - Spot autonomously walks routes and captures sensor data on fixed industrial assets, but the source shows no judgment of cleaning quality (dust, streaks, hair, restocking) against a housekeeping specification, and no room entry or manipulation in guest or patient rooms.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor robot autonomously patrols office facilities on scheduled routes doing 'facility checks' and flags anomalies such as leaks, spills, open doors and people to remote human specialists who handle events.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous after-hours facility patrol in offices. It detects gross anomalies (spills, leaks, open doors) but does not verify janitorial specifications - trash liners, restocked dispensers, dusting, restroom fixture cleanliness - nor produce a rework-grade cleaning inspection report accepted in place of a supervisor's.

sources.title: Pudu Robotics launches new AI-powered cleaning robot for large-scale commercial use
sources.claim: Commercial cleaning robots carry visual AI that identifies localized dirt or spills on floors and re-scrubs them while logging debris data: floor-level dirt sensing exists, but as an input to the robot's own cleaning rather than as an audit of human cleaners' work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dirt detection on floors in malls, hospitals and airports. Covers only gross floor soil in open areas; it does not assess bathrooms, vertical or high-touch surfaces, restocking or bed/linen standards, and issues no pass/fail inspection record.

sources.title: Peanut Robotics | Home
sources.claim: Mobile manipulators are being commercialized to clean hotel and commercial restrooms autonomously, navigating rooms by themselves and collecting data - autonomous in-room operation in hospitality, but performing cleaning rather than inspecting and grading finished work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hotel bathroom cleaning. Establishes autonomous navigation and surface perception inside hotel bathrooms, but there is no evidence of evaluating another worker's completed clean against a hotel standard and issuing an accepted pass/fail with follow-up.

sources.title: OrangeQC: Simple, Powerful Janitorial Inspection Software & App
sources.claim: Janitorial and housekeeping quality inspection in practice is executed with mobile checklist/photo apps operated by a human supervisor who walks the site; AI is applied only to score photographs that people submit, with no robotic inspector involved.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited only to document the state of practice - the inspection task is carried out by a human walking the site with an app, and search surfaced no robotic substitute.

tasks.label: Perform or assist with cleaning duties as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel housekeeping supervisor/inspector fills in on guest-room turnovers during high occupancy: strips and remakes beds to brand standard, cleans and sanitizes the bathroom (toilet, tub/shower, sink, mirror), dusts surfaces, empties trash, vacuums, restocks amenities and linen, in ~20-30 minutes per occupied room with variable guest clutter.

Open-area floor care in a large facility (hotel corridors and lobby, airport concourse, hospital corridor, school gym/cafeteria, big-box retail): supervisor runs the ride-on/walk-behind scrubber or vacuums large carpeted spans, covering thousands of square feet on a route during or after operating hours.

Routine cleaning of a high-traffic multi-fixture public restroom in an office building, airport, hospital or school: scrub and disinfect toilets and urinals, wipe sinks, counters and mirrors, pick up litter, mop/dry the floor, leaving it inspection-ready (paper/soap restocking handled on a separate supply run).

Full restroom/locker-room service including restocking soap, paper towel and tissue dispensers, changing liners in large receptacles, detail work on partitions, grout, showers and fixtures, and dealing with clogged or soiled fixtures.

General cleaning round through occupied work spaces (office suites with cubicles, classrooms, exam/patient rooms): empty and reline waste and recycling bins, dust and disinfect desks, tables and high-touch surfaces, spot-clean glass and doors, tidy chairs, detail-vacuum around furniture.

Unscheduled incident response and periodic deep/detail work: mop up a spill, broken glass or bodily fluids in an occupied lobby within minutes; plus scheduled specialty jobs such as carpet extraction, stripping and refinishing hard floors, high dusting, interior glass and deep kitchen cleaning.

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo is a fully ... in routine deployment cleaning hard floors in airports, malls, hospitals, schools and warehouses.

sources.title: Walmart expands use of robotic floor scrubbers | Chain Store Age
sources.claim: Walmart operates autonomous floor scrubbers (Tennant T7AMR with BrainOS autonomy) as production cleaning equipment, expanding from ~300 stores to 1,500 more locations.

sources.title: Whiz Product Overview | Softbank Robotics
sources.claim: SoftBank's Whiz is a commercially leased robot that autonomously vacuums carpet in large commercial spaces including hotel corridors and offices.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR is a commercially offered restroom-cleaning robot (flat monthly pricing, deployment included) that navigates buildings by itself and cleans fixtures, floors and picks ... in high-traffic restrooms at hospitals and airports.

sources.title: This robot will clean toilets for $1,000 a month | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Independent trade coverage describes the Somatic robot autonomously cleaning toilets, mopping, disinfecting and vacuum-drying most areas of a public restroom, refilling its own chemicals and opening doors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial restroom cleaning. It is the same duty performed by housekeeping/janitorial supervisors covering restrooms - same fixtures, chemicals and hard floors in the same institutional buildings.

sources.title: The Robotics Founder Who Turned a Hotel Chore Into a Real-World AI Breakthrough
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics fields a mobile manipulator that autonomously cleans hotel bathrooms in commercial buildings; its demonstrated scope is bathrooms and hard surfaces, not full guest-room turnover (beds, linen, amenities).

sources.title: Watch A New Humanoid Robot Clean A Hotel Room Like It Owns The Place | Forbes
sources.claim: Zerith H1 is a humanoid unveiled for hotel housekeeping shown cleaning floors, scrubbing toilets and restocking amenities; coverage presents it as an early-stage pilot rather than a staffed-quality room-turnover system.

sources.title: Watch: From laundry to making your bed, Isaac 1 humanoid robot is ready for house chores
sources.claim: Weave Robotics unveiled Isaac 1, a home humanoid shown making beds and tidying, operating autonomously in most situations with remote human takeover when it cannot finish a task.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: domestic bed-making and tidying, the closest demonstrated analogue to hotel bed-making; cited to show the capability exists only as a remote-assisted home demo, not at hotel turnover quality or pace.
