tasks.label: Inspect and evaluate the physical condition of facilities to determine the type of work required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel/lodging: inspector-supervisor enters cleaned guest rooms (checkouts and stayovers) and grades them against brand standard — bathroom (hair, water spots, mirror streaks, grout, restocked amenities), bed making, dust on ledges/headboards, under-bed debris, carpet stains, working lights/TV/HVAC, odors — then decides pass, re-clean, deep-clean, or maintenance work order, typically 60-120 seconds per room under checkout-rush time pressure.

Hotel/hospitality public areas and back-of-house: walkthrough of lobby, corridors, elevators, public restrooms, fitness/pool areas, laundry and storage rooms; judging floor finish and carpet condition, glass and metal, trash levels, restroom stock and fixture condition, and deciding which periodic work (extraction, burnishing, high dusting, deep restroom clean) to schedule.

Healthcare facility: environmental-services supervisor rounds patient rooms, discharge/terminal-clean rooms, procedure areas, corridors and public restrooms; verifies high-touch surface cleaning and infection-control standards (visual checks, fluorescent-marker/ATP follow-up), notes damaged surfaces or spills, and assigns re-clean or work orders.

Office/commercial contract cleaning: supervisor performs scheduled quality inspections of tenant floors, lobbies, break rooms, restrooms, stairwells and entryways after (or during) the night shift, scoring against the SLA/APPA level — dusting, trash, vacuum patterns, restroom stock and fixtures, glass, spots on carpet — and determining re-work and periodic floor care needs.

Large open-area facilities (big-box retail, warehouse/distribution, airport concourse, mall): continuous sweeps of extensive hard floor areas looking for spills, tracked-in soil, litter and debris requiring immediate cleaning attention, and dispatching a cleaner to the spot.

Non-routine condition assessments: walking a post-event venue, a post-construction/renovation area, a water-damaged or heavily soiled space, a vacant residential unit, or exterior grounds/parking areas, to scope what type of work (final clean, debris removal, restoration, pressure washing) and how much labor and equipment are required.

sources.title: Badger Technologies and Stop & Shop expand use of Marty the Robot
sources.claim: Badger Technologies' Marty is an autonomous multipurpose robot deployed at scale in grocery stores that patrols the sales floor and detects floor hazards and spills, alerting associates to clean them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous store-floor hazard patrol. It is the floor-condition part of this inspection task — traversing a facility, judging whether the floor condition requires cleaning, and dispatching a cleaner — performed in a comparable institution-controlled indoor facility.

sources.title: Stine Deploys Badger Technologies Autonomous Robots ...
sources.claim: Badger's autonomous retail robots identify cleanliness hazards such as liquid, powder ... bulk-food spills as part of routine store patrols, supporting store cleanliness programs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store hazard/cleanliness scanning. Same perceptual judgment (is this floor area soiled enough to require cleaning work?) in an institution-controlled retail facility with people present.

sources.system: Gausium autonomous cleaning robots (Phantas, Scrubber series)
sources.title: Technology | Gausium Robot Technology | SLAM Navigation, AI & Cloud Platform
sources.claim: Gausium's commercial cleaning robots continuously scan floor cleanliness while navigating facilities and act on detected waste or stains, spot-cleaning where needed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous dirt detection during commercial floor cleaning. It substantiates machine assessment of floor soil level in ordinary human work facilities, the narrow condition-evaluation element shared with this task.

sources.title: 5 Key Features to Look for in a Professional Autonomous Cleaning Robot in 2026
sources.claim: Gausium robots flag conditions they cannot handle themselves (large waste, tangled cables, liquid spills) to human operators through the management app during autonomous cleaning runs in commercial facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exception reporting during autonomous cleaning. It shows a deployed robot deciding that a condition requires human cleaning work and reporting it, i.e. the dispatch output of a floor-condition sweep.

sources.title: Cobalt intelligent indoor security robot | Security Info Watch
sources.claim: Cobalt Robotics' indoor robots autonomously patrol commercial workspaces along designated routes, use AI to identify anomalies, and escalate to remote human specialists when something needs interpretation or response.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor patrol rounds in offices. Demonstrates that traversing an occupied office building on a fixed inspection route and reporting exceptions is within reach; the perception scope, however, is anomaly classes, not cleaning quality.

sources.title: Cobalt Robotics adds leak and spill detection to security robots
sources.claim: Cobalt's autonomously patrolling indoor robots were given leak and spill detection so they can notify staff of water leaks or spills found on a patrol route in offices and similar facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: indoor patrol anomaly detection. Detecting a spill or leak that requires clean-up or a work order is a component of the janitorial inspection round in the same class of structured office facility.

sources.title: Industrial Inspection Solutions | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs autonomous, repeatable inspection missions in industrial facilities, capturing visual, thermal and acoustic data, detecting anomalies such as leaks and hazards, and feeding alerts into facility maintenance workflows; recent releases add autonomous door opening on missions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility inspection rounds generating work orders. It is the closest analogue of 'inspect the physical condition of facilities to determine work required', but the detected classes are equipment/plant anomalies rather than cleaning-standard defects.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics and FieldAI partner to deploy autonomous robots on construction sites
sources.claim: Spot robots equipped with FieldAI's foundation models are deployed on construction sites where they autonomously perform inspection, mapping and monitoring, tracking progress with 3D scans and identifying hazards such as standing water.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous condition documentation in an unstructured site. Shows navigation and data capture in E3 settings, but the output is progress/hazard documentation, not a scoped determination of the cleaning work required.

sources.system: Robot-aided cleaning auditing system (BELUGA-class audit robot)
sources.developer: Singapore University of Technology and Design (Sensors 2021 study)
sources.title: An Autonomous Robot-Aided Auditing Scheme for Floor Cleaning
sources.claim: A research framework demonstrates a mobile robot autonomously auditing the cleanliness of built ... floors, exploring an area and assessing cleaning quality; it remains a laboratory-scale research prototype limited to floor dirt.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: robotic auditing of cleaning quality. It substantiates only floor-level dirt auditing in a test setting, not a supervisor-grade evaluation of rooms, fixtures, supplies and required work types.

tasks.label: Inventory stock to ensure that supplies and equipment are available in adequate amounts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel/resort executive housekeeper or housekeeping supervisor performs the weekly/monthly count in the property's central storeroom and linen room: racked and shelved cases of amenities, paper goods, chemicals, and bagged/stacked linens; walks the aisles with a count sheet or tablet, compares on-hand to par levels, and submits a purchase order.

Hospital, university, or large office EVS/custodial supervisor counts the central custodial store: pallet-racked and shelved cases of can liners, chemical concentrates, paper, gloves and PPE; reconciles counts to usage/issue records and files a requisition so units do not run short.

Daily or weekly par check of floor-level janitor closets, linen closets, and housekeeping carts on multiple floors: small, cramped, cluttered spaces behind doors, with partially used chemical bottles, loose loose-stacked linens, mop heads and open cases; supervisor eyeballs remaining quantity and tops the closet/cart back up from a supply cart.

Contract-cleaning/janitorial supervisor drives a route of several client buildings, checking each small supply closet and the stock carried in the van; estimates how much remains of opened products, notes shortages against the account's supply budget, and loads replenishment items from the van into the closets.

Receiving a supply delivery at the dock or back door: verifying cases and pallets against the packing slip, counting and inspecting for damage or short-ship, signing off, putting the goods away on storeroom shelves, and updating the inventory sheet/system.

Periodic equipment inventory: locating and counting vacuums, floor machines, extractors, carts, ladders and backpack units scattered across floors and closets, checking asset tags, and noting units that are missing or out of service so replacements/repairs are ordered.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally is an autonomous shelf-scanning robot commercially deployed in grocery stores (17 Harmons locations after a pilot) to count on-shelf inventory and drive replenishment decisions in a normal human-staffed store.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory auditing. Transfers to counting a housekeeping/custodial storeroom because the objects are the same class (cased and packaged consumer goods on shelves), the output is the same (on-hand counts, low-stock and out-of-stock flags feeding replenishment), and both occur in an institution-controlled indoor facility.

sources.title: BJ's Gains Efficiency from Robotic Inventory Management
sources.claim: The same Tally system is deployed at scale in BJ's Wholesale clubs, scanning bulk club shelving and upper steel pallet racking up to 24 feet to audit stock levels and flag restocking needs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk/club-format inventory auditing including pallet racking. A hotel or hospital central store is essentially bulk cases on racked shelving, so scanning cased goods at rack height and reporting fill percentage transfers directly to counting custodial stock.

sources.title: GXO Logistics Partners with Dexory to Enhance Warehouse Inventory Management with AI-Powered Robotics
sources.claim: Dexory's autonomous inventory robot completed a GXO pilot and moved into deployment, autonomously scanning racked warehouse inventory up to 13 m high at 10,000 pallet locations per hour and reconciling physical stock against system records.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse cycle counting. Transfers to counting a central custodial/linen store because both require navigating racked aisles in an institution-run facility, identifying cased stock by label, and producing counts reconciled against a stock record.

sources.title: Reducing Inventory Cycle Counting Time with a Drone-Powered Monitoring Solution
sources.claim: Gather AI's drones fly autonomously through customer warehouses without infrastructure changes, reading barcodes, lot codes and text, counting cases and estimating occupancy for cycle counts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse cycle counting of cased goods. Same output (case counts, occupancy, expiry/damage flags) as a supervisor's storeroom count, in a comparable institution-controlled indoor facility.

sources.title: UPS deploys Verity warehouse drones for inventory tracking | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: UPS Supply Chain Solutions deployed Verity's autonomous inventory drones for inventory tracking, and Verity drones augmented with RFID ... reading tags at high accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stock verification in a logistics facility. Supports the counting/verification half of inventorying supplies, but only for palletized/labelled stock in racked aisles, not for closet-level loose or partially used product.

sources.title: How AutoStore Works - Everything You Need to Know | Kardex
sources.claim: AutoStore is a robot-operated storage system in which robots retrieve bins and present them at ports, with software tracking every bin and stock position and triggering replenishment when stock in the grid runs low.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: perpetual inventory in a purpose-built robotic storage cell. When supplies are held in the machine's own fixtured bins, on-hand quantities and low-stock replenishment triggers are produced automatically, which is the accepted output of the inventory task at E1.

sources.title: Kardex launches PortScale to enhance AutoStore inventory accuracy
sources.claim: Kardex PortScale adds real-time weight-based verification at AutoStore ports, measuring weight change during picking and putaway to detect count/pick errors and improve inventory accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated receipt/putaway verification. Supports the E1 counterfactual for checking a delivery in: when goods are presented at the machine's port, quantity verification and stock-record update happen automatically.

tasks.label: Issue supplies and equipment to workers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel shift-start issuance: supervisor/houseperson unlocks the linen and supply room and issues 8-20 room attendants their day's kit - stacks of sheets and towels, guest amenities, chemical spray bottles, liners, plus a vacuum, radio and floor key - loading or checking each cart in a 15-30 minute window before rooms open.

Mid-shift resupply request: a housekeeper or janitor on a floor runs out of towels, trash liners, glass cleaner or mop pads and calls the supervisor, who retrieves the specific item from a locked supply closet or storeroom, carries it to the worker on the floor, and records the issue.

Counter/storeroom issuance at an institutional custodial store (university, school district, casino, airport, large office complex): workers come to the store window at shift change and the supervisor picks assorted consumables off shelves - gloves, rags, wipes, disinfectant concentrate, liners, paper goods - hands them over and logs quantities against the crew's account.

Hospital/large-facility EVS par-level issuance: supervisor pulls bulk stock from the central EVS storeroom (cases of can liners, gallon jugs and concentrate cartridges, boxes of microfiber pads, PPE), splits it against par sheets, and distributes to unit closets and to staff at shift start, documenting chemical handling.

Contract janitorial night-crew equipment issuance in an office building or school: supervisor unlocks the janitor closet/equipment room and issues backpack vacuums, mop buckets, a burnisher or auto-scrubber, floor pads, chemicals and building keys, inspects cords and condition, records the sign-out and collects the equipment at shift end.

Multi-site route supervisor for a cleaning contractor: loads a van at a central warehouse and drops supplies and equipment to crews at scattered client sites - small offices, clinics, retail, post-construction cleanups - handing items over at loading docks, back doors and parking lots in whatever weather and layout each site presents.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator, autonomously picks supplies out of hospital supply closets and delivers them elsewhere in the hospital, in commercial deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Fetching a requested consumable from a supply closet and bringing it to staff on a unit is the same act as a housekeeping supervisor issuing a supply item to a worker: same class of objects (boxed/bagged consumables, bottles, PPE), same institutionally controlled corridors and closets.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi is deployed at scale in US hospitals with nearly 100 robots and over 1.25 million completed autonomous deliveries.

sources.title: Meet Moxi, the newest nurse assistant of Trinity Michigan medical team - Bridge Michigan
sources.claim: Moxi uses an arm and gripper to fetch supplies and equipment and hands them over through badge-secured drawers; payload is about 15 kg.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the hand-off mechanism and payload limit relevant to issuing single supply items to a worker, and the ceiling for bulk case handling.

sources.title: Robocrib TX750 - AutoCrib
sources.claim: Robotic tool-crib dispensing machines automatically issue shop supplies, PPE and tools to badge-identified workers with per-transaction tracking.
sources.transferJustification: Issuing consumables, PPE and tools to identified workers with a usage record is the same output as a supervisor issuing supplies and equipment, with the stock fixtured into the machine as a purpose-built setting would present it.

sources.title: The SmartStore Vending Program - Industrial Vending for the Masses (Fastenal)
sources.claim: Industrial vending devices installed at customer sites issue product against employee badge or key code, tracking and limiting each transaction.
sources.transferJustification: Point-of-use dispensing of consumables and PPE to workers with authorization limits and a transaction record reproduces the supervisor's issuing-and-logging output when supplies are pre-loaded into the machine.

sources.developer: Quadromed / hospital installations (e.g., Brigham and Women's Hospital)
sources.title: New Machines on the Block: Scrubs Dispensers Save Time, Money - Brigham Bulletin
sources.claim: Automated garment dispensing machines are in routine hospital use to issue clean textiles (scrubs) to authorized staff on badge, with returns and inventory tracking.
sources.transferJustification: Issuing folded textiles to identified staff from an automated unit is the closest deployed analog to issuing linens and uniforms to housekeeping workers: same deformable goods, same badge-tracked issue-and-return record.

sources.title: Vertical Lift Module - Kardex (product catalog)
sources.claim: Vertical lift modules automatically retrieve stored trays - including heavy items and equipment - and present them at an access opening, with badge readers controlling and logging who draws what.
sources.transferJustification: Automated retrieval and presentation of stored equipment to an authenticated worker performs the issuing step for bulkier gear once that gear is trayed, i.e. fixtured for the machine.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics Introduces the RightPick 4 System
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic piece-picking systems pick mixed individual items - general merchandise, office supplies, apparel - into order containers and are sold as production fulfillment systems.
sources.transferJustification: Assembling a per-worker kit of assorted consumables from fixtured stock presented by a goods-to-robot system is the same pick-and-place problem as order fulfillment of mixed small goods; it substantiates the E1 kitting step, not open-shelf storeroom work.

sources.developer: AutoStore (integrated by Dematic, Bastian and others)
sources.title: AutoStore Automated Storage and Retrieval System - Dematic
sources.claim: Goods-to-person robotic storage and retrieval systems have robots fetch bins from a grid and deliver them to a port for picking or replenishment.
sources.transferJustification: Supplies brought to a dispensing port by robots is how a purpose-built setting would present stock for issuance; it substantiates the retrieval half of E1 issuing for bulk consumables.

sources.title: Hotel Tech-in: The robot lightening the load for housekeepers - Hotel Dive
sources.claim: An autonomous service robot moves linens and waste around hotel back-of-house daily at a California hotel, but only transports human-loaded material.
sources.transferJustification: Shows hotel back-of-house corridors are navigable autonomously for linen logistics, but the system selects nothing and issues nothing, so it cannot complete the task on its own.

tasks.label: Check and maintain equipment to ensure that it is in working order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Storeroom check of small powered cleaning equipment in a hotel/office/hospital: test-run upright and backpack vacuums, inspect cords and plugs for fraying, change bags and HEPA filters, cut hair/string off brush rolls, check drive belts, replace worn attachments, and set aside anything unsafe.

End-of-route servicing of a robotic/dockable floor scrubber so it is ready for the next shift: return to its station, drain and rinse the recovery tank, refill clean-water solution, and put the machine on charge.

Post-shift servicing of manual walk-behind/ride-on scrubbers, burnishers and carpet extractors in a janitor's closet or loading dock: dump and scrub recovery tanks, clean vacuum screens and filters, inspect and swap worn pads/brushes and squeegee blades, check battery water/charge, coil hoses and cords.

Checking housekeeping carts and chemical systems: cart wheels, shelves and bag rings; trigger sprayers and spray bottles that leak or won't pump; verifying wall-mounted dilution dispensers draw and dilute correctly, replacing tips/hoses and restocking.

Mid-shift breakdown: a machine won't start, loses suction, or leaks; the supervisor diagnoses it on the spot, makes a field fix (reset breaker, clear a clog, replace a belt or hose), or tags it out of service, swaps in a spare, and arranges vendor repair.

Scheduled preventive-maintenance round and equipment audit across the fleet, including laundry washers/dryers (lint traps, hoses), lubricating and tightening, topping up fluids, confirming machines are charged and stored properly, and recording results in the PM log and ordering parts.

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped runs fully autonomous nightly inspection rounds inside an operating cement plant, visiting 450+ predefined equipment checkpoints and reporting anomalies; over 33,000 inspections since early 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sensor-based equipment inspection rounds in a facility. It shows autonomous 'checking' of machinery for faults, but only by looking/listening/thermal imaging at fixed assets — it performs no servicing, no test-running of portable equipment and no wear-part replacement, so transfer to 'check and maintain' is partial.

sources.system: Gausium Scrubber 50 / Scrubber 50 Pro with workstation
sources.title: Scrubber 50 - Commercial Robot Floor Scrubber - Gausium
sources.claim: Gausium's commercial Scrubber 50 robotic floor scrubber, with its optional workstation, autonomously charges itself and refills/discharges water without an operator.

sources.title: LionsBot Introduces the Autonomous Warehouse Cleaning Robot
sources.claim: LionsBot's Rex commercial cleaning robot auto-docks after every cleaning cycle and the station charges it and performs automated rinsing and water exchange of its solution.

sources.title: Roomba Combo 10 Max Robot + AutoWash Dock | SmartScrub
sources.claim: iRobot's AutoWash dock autonomously empties the robot's debris bin and washes and heat-dries its microfiber mop pad, keeping the cleaning machine serviced without human handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated upkeep of cleaning equipment consumables. It substantiates autonomous emptying/washing/drying of one purpose-designed machine's own pad and bin at a fixtured station, not inspection or wear-part service on varied equipment.

sources.title: Hyster trucks to use Rocsys robotic charging
sources.claim: Rocsys' ROC-1 robotic charging system automatically plugs in and charges parked electric terminal tractors at ports, removing the human plug-in step of keeping equipment ready.

instances.label: Hotel: front desk relays a guest complaint that the room was not properly cleaned (hair in the tub, dust on surfaces, missed trash). The supervisor goes to the occupied room, inspects against the brand standard, identifies what the attendant missed, re-cleans the deficiencies personally or sends the attendant back, then follows up with the guest and logs the issue and coaching.

Hospital/long-term care: a nursing unit complains that a patient room or restroom was not cleaned to protocol (soiled fixtures, missed high-touch surfaces, spill left standing). The EVS supervisor responds to the unit, inspects (visual check, sometimes ATP swab or blacklight audit), arranges or performs an immediate re-clean, documents in the EVS/infection-control record, and coaches the tech.

Contracted office/commercial janitorial: a tenant or property manager complains that trash was not emptied, restrooms are out of supplies, or lobby floors are streaked. On the night shift the supervisor walks the affected floors, inspects, remediates (empties, restocks, re-mops), adjusts the route or crew assignment, and reports resolution to the client.

Equipment complaint from staff: a vacuum has lost suction, an autoscrubber leaves water or won't charge, a cart wheel is broken, or a chemical dispenser mis-dilutes. The supervisor takes the machine to the closet/shop, tests it, troubleshoots (clogged hose, worn belt, full bag, damaged squeegee, dead battery, wrong metering tip), makes the minor repair or tags it out and arranges service/replacement, and documents it.

Service-conduct complaint: a client or guest reports an attendant was rude, skipped assigned rooms, or worked outside the scheduled window. The supervisor interviews the complainant and the employee, reviews assignment sheets, room-status logs and badge/camera records, issues verbal or written corrective action, and verifies improvement on later inspections.

Complaint at a variable, uncontrolled site: a residential-cleaning client's home, a post-construction or move-out clean, or a small scattered account. The supervisor drives out, works an unfamiliar layout with the customer's own furnishings and clutter present, inspects the disputed work, remediates on the spot, and settles the complaint with the customer.

Irrigation inspection after installation or repair: run every zone from the controller, walk the property watching head arcs and coverage, look for geysers, misting, leaks, tilted or buried heads, overspray onto walks or buildings, verify valve boxes, backflow and controller programming meet the spec, and flag or adjust heads before accepting the crew's work.

Large managed turf (golf course, sports complex, school district fields, campus): aerial/overview verification of the results of completed irrigation, fertilizer or spray work — locating dry spots, stressed or over-watered areas, striping from missed passes, and irrigation leaks — and flagging areas needing follow-up.

Same large managed turf facilities, ground-level conformance checks after the crew: measure height of cut with a prism gauge, examine mowing/rolling quality and edging around bunkers, bases and warning tracks, check for fertilizer burn, granule spread on hard surfaces, weed-control efficacy and debris, and record the conformance decision.

Boom sprayer or ride-on spreader lays down fungicide, pre-emergent herbicide, growth regulator or granular fertilizer over mapped acreage, worked around irrigation heads, bunkers, trees and scheduled play/use windows.

Targeted/spot treatment at client sites: backpack or hand-can spraying of weeds in mulch beds, gravel, pavement cracks and fence lines, and insecticide/fungicide sprays or soil drenches on ornamental shrubs and trees; must not contact desirable plants, requires identifying the pest and the plant, done around building entries, patios and pedestrians.

Directing the crew rather than applying: assigning licensed applicators to routes and zones, specifying product, rate and sequence, verifying the mix and equipment calibration before crews leave, calling off work for wind/rain, walking properties to inspect coverage, skips and off-target damage, and ordering re-treats after customer complaints.

instances.label: Residential maintenance route: supervisor walks client lawns during service visits, spots off-color or thinning turf, and determines the cause (brown patch, dollar spot, rust, grubs, chinch bugs, drought or dog damage), often by pulling a plug or doing a tug/soap-flush test, then orders the fungicide or insecticide and schedules application. Small yards, pets, shade and irrigation variation, no two properties alike.

Turf on commercial/institutional grounds (office parks, HOA common areas, campuses, municipal parks, cemeteries): supervisor inspects large maintained lawns on a regular round, distinguishes disease or insect damage from abiotic stress, and orders curative or preventive product for the spray tech.

Golf course / sports field turf: near-daily scouting of greens, tees and fairways for early disease pressure (dollar spot, pythium, anthracnose, fairy ring) and insect activity (annual bluegrass weevil, grubs); confirmation with hand lens, microscope or plug, then ordering and scheduling the fungicide/insecticide program.

Ornamental beds, shrubs and landscape trees across client sites: close inspection of many plant species for aphids, scale, spider mites, lace bugs, bagworms, borers, leaf spot, powdery mildew, fire blight and canker, including turning leaves, examining stems and bark and canopies above head height; then ordering horticultural oil, systemic or fungicide.

Interior plantscape accounts and the company's own greenhouse/nursery holding area: scouting potted ornamentals and tropicals on benches or in lobbies for scale, mealybug, spider mites, fungus gnats and mildew, then ordering treatment or biologicals.

Sample-based confirmation of an unclear problem: cutting turf plugs or collecting symptomatic foliage and soil cores at the site, running a flotation or tug test or packaging and submitting to an extension turf/plant diagnostic lab, then ordering the specific labeled product once the causal agent is identified.

tasks.label: Service, clean, or supply restrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nightly full-service clean of a multi-fixture restroom in an office tower, school, or medical office building: empty the waste receptacles and replace liners, restock toilet paper, seat covers, paper towels and soap, clean and disinfect bowls, urinals, seats, sinks, counters and mirrors, spot-clean partitions and touchpoints, and damp-mop the whole floor, all after hours on a route of 8-15 restrooms.

Day-porter service round of a high-traffic public restroom during operating hours (airport concourse, stadium, mall, transit hub, hospital lobby): spot-clean fixtures and counters, pick up floor litter and paper, empty overflowing trash, restock consumables, mop wet spots and set wet-floor signs, working around a steady stream of members of the public.

Cleaning and disinfecting pass over restroom fixtures and floors only, with waste and consumables handled separately on another pass or shift: scrub and sanitize bowls, seats, rims and urinals, wipe sinks, counters and mirrors, and mop the floor, in a standard restroom inside an institution-controlled building.

Supply-only pass: walk the building's restrooms, unlock and refill toilet paper, seat cover, paper towel and soap dispensers from a stocked cart, replace waste-can liners, swap air fresheners and urinal screens, and note broken dispensers or fixtures for maintenance.

Incident or heavy-soil response: an overflowed or clogged toilet to be plunged and the floor squeegeed dry, vomit, urine, feces or blood on floors, walls and partitions, smeared or vandalized surfaces, graffiti, or a torn-out dispenser, cleaned and disinfected on short notice with barricades or closure signs.

Periodic deep clean of a restroom: acid-descale bowls and urinal traps, machine-scrub tile and grout floors and squeegee to drain, wash partitions, doors, walls and dispensers top to bottom, high-dust vents and lights, polish chrome and hardware.

tasks.label: Gather and empty trash.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nightly office-building route: janitor walks floors of cubicles and private offices, lifts liners out of dozens of desk-side wastebaskets and common-area bins, consolidates bags into a rolling barrel or cart, re-lines each bin, and wheels the load to the dock compactor. Bins are cluttered around chairs, cords, and furniture; some contain liquids or recycling that must not be mixed.

Restroom and breakroom trash: soiled paper-towel receptacles, sanitary napkin bins, food waste and coffee grounds, frequently wet or leaking bags that must be tied, removed without spilling, the receptacle wiped, and a fresh liner cuffed on; done several times a day in high-traffic restrooms.

School, hospital, or other institutional interior: classrooms, patient rooms, corridors, cafeteria; separate trash, recycling, and (in healthcare) regulated-waste streams; bins emptied into a cart that is pushed through doors and elevators to a soiled-utility room, then to compactor or dock.

Large public venue during operating hours (airport concourse, mall, stadium, transit hub): high-volume lidded receptacles emptied continuously while crowds move past; heavy wet bags of food waste and drinks lifted out, tied, replaced, and carted to a back-of-house compactor.

Outdoor grounds and dock work at a building or campus: policing lawns, walks, and parking areas for loose litter, tipping or emptying outdoor barrels, dragging bags to a dumpster and hoisting them in, running the compactor, in rain, wind, snow, and uneven pavement.

Industrial/warehouse facility: collecting scrap, packaging, and shop trash held in large standardized containers, gaylords, or wheeled carts at work stations, moving them to a compactor, baler, or tipping station, dumping them, and returning empty containers.

tasks.label: Clean building floors by sweeping, mopping, scrubbing, or vacuuming.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine machine cleaning of large open hard-floor areas in big facilities — big-box/grocery sales floors, warehouse and distribution-center aisles, airport concourses, hospital and school main corridors, gyms and cafeterias. Long repeatable routes on tile/concrete/terrazzo, run nightly or off-peak with a walk-behind or ride-on scrubber/sweeper.

Vacuuming open carpeted areas in office buildings, hotels/conference centers and university buildings — open-plan floors, corridors, meeting rooms, lobbies. Predictable nightly runs; cords, chairs and waste bins are occasional obstacles but the layout is stable.

Sweeping, dust-mopping and damp-mopping small and congested interior spaces with fixed furniture — private offices, clinic/exam rooms, break rooms, entry vestibules, elevator cabs, small backrooms and narrow service corridors. The machine must fit and maneuver among permanent obstacles.

Mopping/scrubbing restroom and locker-room tile floors in offices, airports, hospitals and schools — floor around toilets, urinals, sinks and stall partitions, with disinfectant, often on a several-times-daily schedule in high-traffic facilities.

Detail floor work: stairwells and landings, edges, corners and baseboard lines, under and behind desks, shelving and equipment, plus classrooms and cafeterias where chairs, mats and bins must be lifted/moved and replaced before and after sweeping and mopping.

On-demand response to spills and heavy soil — tracked-in mud, snowmelt and ice-melt salt at entries, spilled drinks and food with solid debris, broken glass, bodily fluids. Worker travels to an arbitrary reported location, sets hazard signage, picks up solids, then spot-mops or scrubs and dries.

tasks.label: Monitor building security and safety by performing tasks such as locking doors after operating hours or checking electrical appliance use to ensure that hazards are not created.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shift-end lock-up of a school, church, clinic or small office: after the last occupants leave, the custodian walks the building, physically locks exterior and interior doors (keys, thumb-turns, dogging panic bars), closes and latches windows, checks nobody remains, and arms the intrusion alarm. Hardware differs door to door and doors are sometimes propped.

Checking electrical appliance use during and after cleaning rounds and removing the hazard by hand: switching off coffee makers, microwaves and equipment left running, unplugging a space heater sitting near paper, turning off lights and machines, pulling an overloaded power strip or frayed cord out of service, and reporting what was found.

After-hours interior security walk-through of an access-controlled office, hospital, lab or corporate campus building: confirm doors are closed and secured, look for people who should not be there, propped doors, unusual sounds, water leaks or alarms, log the round and report anomalies to security or management.

Safety-hazard inspection while making rounds in a large institutional or commercial facility (retail sales floor, warehouse, plant, hospital wing): spotting spills and leaks, overheating equipment or electrical panels, blocked fire exits, burned-out or flickering lights, and alerting staff or logging them for repair.

Night exterior/grounds security check on the institution's own premises: exterior doors and gates closed, perimeter and fence intact, exterior lighting working, parking lot clear of unauthorized vehicles or people, hazards such as standing water ... ice; report findings.

tasks.label: Follow procedures for the use of chemical cleaners and power equipment to prevent damage to floors and fixtures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily machine scrubbing of large open hard-floor areas — retail sales floors, warehouse aisles, school/hospital corridors, airport concourses — with a walk-behind or ride-on autoscrubber: correct pad/brush, correct detergent dilution and water flow, staying off carpet and wet-sensitive surfaces, and not striking walls, displays or fixtures.

Vacuuming large open carpeted areas (hotel and office corridors, lobbies, conference/banquet space, open-plan floors) with commercial vacuum/sweeper equipment: right machine and height setting for the carpet, keeping cord and machine off furniture, avoiding wet spots.

Restroom cleaning with chemical cleaners: applying disinfectant/bowl cleaner at the correct dilution and dwell time to toilets, urinals, sinks and floors without etching porcelain, pitting chrome or damaging partitions and finishes; rinsing and wet-vacuuming or mopping the floor.

Periodic restorative floor care: stripping and refinishing VCT with high-alkaline stripper, swing machine and wet vac; burnishing; hot-water carpet extraction; tile-and-grout or entry pressure washing — sequencing and neutralizing chemicals and protecting baseboards, thresholds and fixtures.

Chemical preparation and equipment set-up in the janitor's closet: diluting concentrates at the dispenser per label ratio, filling machine tanks, mop buckets and labeled spray bottles, donning PPE, and checking pads, brushes, cords and squeegees before use.

Detail and edge work in occupied, cluttered spaces: spot-mopping spills, vacuuming under desks and around chairs and cords, stairs, corners and edges the machine misses, and wiping fixtures, glass and walls with the correct spray and cloth.

tasks.label: Mix water and detergents or acids in containers to prepare cleaning solutions, according to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office/school/retail building janitor closet: fills a 26-35 qt mop bucket at a slop sink with hot water and adds a measured amount of neutral floor cleaner (measuring cup or wall proportioner) per the label dilution, producing a ready-to-use mopping solution.

Janitorial closet chemical station: selects concentrate (disinfectant, glass cleaner, bathroom cleaner), fills and dilutes several trigger spray bottles to the specified ratio, caps, labels and dates them for the cart.
Warehouse, hospital or airport: fills the solution tank of a walk-behind/ride-on auto-scrubber with water at a fill point and adds/sets floor detergent to the specified dose before a scrubbing run.

Facility utility room/restroom: mixes an acid-based descaler/bowl cleaner or a quat disinfectant to a specified concentration in a bucket or sprayer, wearing PPE, and verifies concentration with a test strip.

Exterior/loading dock or parking area taken as found: mixes degreaser or acid concentrate with water into a pressure-washer tank or bucket outdoors, adjusting for weather, drain-off and site conditions.
Periodic deep clean: mixes carpet shampoo/extraction concentrate with hot water in a carpet extractor's solution tank at the specified dilution in an office building.

tasks.label: Strip, seal, finish, and polish floors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: K-12 school summer strip-and-refinish: classrooms and corridors emptied of furniture; sweep/dust mop, apply stripper and let it dwell, agitate with a swing or orbital machine, pick up slurry with wet-vac/auto-scrubber, rinse and neutralize, then apply 3-5 thin coats of sealer/finish with a flat-mop applicator (edges and corners cut in by hand), waiting for each coat to dry, and burnish after cure.

Overnight strip-and-recoat of an office building or bank branch: lobby, corridors, restrooms and break rooms with furniture, partitions, toilets and toe-kicks in place; small irregular rooms, hand edging around baseboards and door thresholds, finish coats applied and floor walkable before staff arrive.

Occupied healthcare or senior-living facility: half-corridor-at-a-time refinishing at night with barricades and wet-floor signs, low-odor products, infection-control rules, patient-room doorways and equipment moved and replaced, work paused for passing traffic.

Big-box retail or supermarket sales floor: top-scrub (deep scrub) to remove worn top coats around gondolas, endcaps and pallets, pick up slurry, then apply one or two coats of finish overnight before opening.

Standalone burnishing/polishing pass on an already-finished floor: nightly or weekly high-speed burnishing of big-box aisles, school corridors or hospital hallways, with dust control, spray-buff touch-up of scuffs, detail work at edges, and uniform gloss expected.

Small, cluttered or specialty spaces: restaurant kitchen quarry tile degrease-and-seal, restrooms, stairwell landings, small church halls and closets; heavy soil or grease, drains and fixtures, work done largely with hand tools, small swing machines, mops and wet-vacs.

tasks.label: Make adjustments or minor repairs to heating, cooling, ventilating, plumbing, or electrical systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lighting and small electrical fixes in an occupied office, school or retail building: replacing burned-out lamps/tubes and exit-sign lamps overhead from a ladder, swapping a ballast or LED driver, resetting a tripped breaker in the panel, replacing a wall switch, receptacle or cover plate, repairing a damaged plug or cord on cleaning equipment.

Clearing clogs in a public restroom or janitor closet: plunging or augering a stopped-up toilet, urinal, sink or floor drain, mopping up the overflow, and confirming the fixture drains and flushes normally, often mid-shift with the restroom in use.

Minor plumbing repairs: stopping a running toilet by replacing a flapper, fill valve or flushometer diaphragm; replacing a faucet washer, cartridge or aerator; tightening or replacing a dripping supply line, P-trap or hose bibb under a sink; verifying the joint is leak-free.

Scheduled ventilation service: pulling dirty panel filters from rooftop units, air handlers and fan-coil units in mechanical rooms or on the roof, sliding in correctly sized replacements, and vacuuming/wiping return grilles and diffusers.

Adjusting heating/cooling controls in response to complaints or routine rounds: setting or resetting thermostats, resetting a locked-out HVAC unit, opening/closing radiator or damper valves, bleeding a radiator, checking boiler gauges and adjusting the water feed or setpoint.

Boiler/furnace tending and other minor mechanical service: replacing a slipping fan belt, lubricating motor bearings, clearing a plugged condensate drain pan and line, brushing/cleaning coils or burners, relighting a pilot in a basement mechanical room.

sources.title: Space robotics start-up GITAI completes successful technology demonstration inside the ISS – GITAI
sources.claim: GITAI's S1 arm autonomously performed switch and cable operations (plus panel/structure assembly) on a task panel installed in the ISS Nanoracks Bishop Airlock — a purpose-built, fixtured work board.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: switch actuation and cable/connector mating on a fixtured panel. This is the same class of object and precision as a janitor's minor electrical work (flipping a breaker or switch, seating a connector) when the device is presented in a fixture, so it supports the E1 counterfactual for the electrical instance.

sources.title: WAIC 2026 | Making Breakfast, Selling Goods, Galbot Showcases Multi-Scenario Capabilities
sources.claim: Galbot S1 autonomously located millimetre-scale screws with vision, inserted them, and drove them with an electric screwdriver; the same platform runs continuously on CATL battery production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered fastening of small screws with a handheld tool. Device mounting screws and terminal screws in switch/receptacle replacement are comparable objects at comparable precision, supporting E1 where the device is fixtured and presented.

sources.title: Averex wiring centre from Kiesling | Rittal - The System.
sources.claim: The Kiesling/Rittal Averex portal machine automatically and autonomously wires control-cabinet mounting plates — cutting, crimping, connecting and routing wires to terminals inside a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making screwed/crimped electrical terminations on components held in a fixture. Wire termination is the core physical step in replacing a switch, receptacle or ballast, so it substantiates the E1 counterfactual for minor electrical repair.

sources.title: Humanoid Robots Complete Trial Project at BMW Assembly Plant | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Figure 02 humanoids ran ten-hour production shifts at BMW Spartanburg for ten months, autonomously picking flat sheet-metal panels from racks or bins and seating them precisely in welding fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing a large flat panel from a rack and sliding it into a fixture at production tolerance. A panel-filter change presented at a fixtured air-handler rack involves the same object class and lower precision, so the capability transfers at E1.

sources.developer: University of Bonn, Autonomous Intelligent Systems
sources.title: Team NimbRo at MBZIRC 2017: Autonomous Valve Stem Turning using a Wrench
sources.claim: The NimbRo mobile manipulator 'Mario' autonomously detected a manipulation panel, selected and grasped a wrench, and turned a valve stem, winning MBZIRC 2017 Challenge 2 on a purpose-built challenge panel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating and turning a valve stem with a hand tool. Adjusting a radiator/damper valve or a boiler feed valve is the same physical act on comparable hardware presented on a panel, supporting E1 for the controls-adjustment instance.

sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot Arm performs valve turning, lever flipping and switch actuation only semi-autonomously, triggered by an operator button press on a tablet.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterise the state of manipulation by mobile robots inside human facilities (E2): operator-triggered, constrained-motion actions rather than autonomous completion of a repair.

sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' 2025 software release made Spot Arm door opening autonomous within recorded Autowalk inspection missions; facility manipulation autonomy remains limited to opening doors on taught routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation during facility inspection rounds. It marks the ceiling of demonstrated autonomous manipulation inside structured human facilities (door opening on taught routes), which falls short of completing any HVAC, plumbing or electrical repair at E2.

tasks.label: Drive vans, industrial trucks, or other vehicles required to travel to, or to perform, cleaning work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Contract cleaner drives a company van or pickup on public streets and highways between customer accounts at night/early morning, carrying vacuums, chemicals and supplies; arbitrary addresses, parking lots, mixed weather.

Janitor operates a ride-on or stand-on floor scrubber/sweeper inside a large facility (big-box store, warehouse, airport concourse, school gym) to scrub and sweep hard floors while occupants and carts are present.

Custodian drives a utility cart, gator or pickup around an institutional campus (school district, university, hospital, industrial park) hauling trash carts, recycling and cleaning supplies between buildings, dumpsters and the loading dock.

Janitor operates an industrial truck (forklift, powered pallet jack, tug) in the dock/back-of-house to move waste containers, compactor bins and pallets of paper goods and chemicals within the building.
Janitor drives a small tractor, outdoor sweeper or plow-equipped machine over the property's lots, drives and walkways to sweep debris or clear snow, in cold, wet, low-light conditions.

sources.title: PepsiCo and Gatik launch commercial driverless trucking deployment - FreightWaves
sources.claim: Gatik operates commercial delivery trucks with no safety driver or observer in the cab, running fixed middle-mile routes over highways and surface streets to about 250 retail locations for PepsiCo, Walmart and Dollar General.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a goods vehicle loaded with supplies on public roads to a commercial destination and into its delivery area — the same act a cleaner performs driving a van between accounts.

sources.title: Waymo Explained: Alphabet's Autonomous Vehicle Company | Built In
sources.claim: Waymo runs fully driverless commercial ride-hailing on public roads in multiple US metros, picking up and dropping off at arbitrary curbside addresses within each service area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a road vehicle door-to-door on public streets. Point-to-point navigation to arbitrary addresses is the driving skill the cleaning-van instance requires; payload differs but the driving does not.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving an industrial truck (forklift/pallet truck/tug) through dock and back-of-house areas to move loads — the same vehicle class and maneuvering a janitor performs with waste containers and supply pallets.

sources.claim: Cyngn's DriveMod autonomous tugger, deployed at John Deere, Pepsi and automotive plants, hauls carts and loads up to 12,000 lb between points in facilities.

sources.claim: Starship's sidewalk delivery robots autonomously carry goods across university campuses and city sidewalks at scale, with over 2,700 robots at 270+ locations and 9 million deliveries completed.

sources.developer: Scythe Robotics (acquired by Autonomous Solutions Inc.)

sources.claim: Scythe's autonomous commercial ride-on-class mower worked outdoors on commercial properties in 30 states, mowing nearly 2 billion square ... in 2025.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving plow/sweeper vehicles over paved outdoor surfaces in winter conditions to clear snow — the same vehicle-operation instance a janitor performs on lots and drives, at larger scale.

tasks.label: Spray insecticides or fumigants to prevent insect or rodent infestation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine preventive crack-and-crevice / perimeter residual spraying inside an occupied building (school, office, hospital kitchen, break room, storage room): janitor works a 1-gal pump sprayer or aerosol with a straw along baseboards, floor-wall junctions, under sinks, behind and under appliances and shelving, around door frames and pipe penetrations; must shift boxes and small equipment, keep chemical off food-contact and cleaned surfaces, and follow label rates.

Reactive aerosol spot treatment of visible pests: an ant trail at a threshold, roaches behind a vending machine, spider webs and egg sacs in stairwell and ceiling corners, flies near a door, a wasp nest above an entry or under an eave; requires spotting the target, reaching it (overhead, ladder, or extension pole), and spraying it directly in an occupied facility.

Exterior treatment of the building's service areas and perimeter: spraying around dumpster pads and corrals, loading docks, exterior door thresholds and a foundation band, plus nests in pavement cracks, mulch beds and shrubs; uneven ground, litter, parked vehicles, wind and weather, layout differing site to site.

After-hours space treatment of an unoccupied room: fogging/ULV or total-release aerosol of insecticide in a trash room, storage room, locker room or commercial kitchen — clear and close the space, post signage, dispense the aerosol over the whole area, then ventilate and re-open.

Confined and concealed applications: crawl spaces, basements, boiler and mechanical rooms, pipe chases and wall voids, floor drains, and rodent burrows or runways outside; dark, cramped, cluttered with piping and equipment, applying dust/fumigant into void openings and burrows or treating drains.

sources.developer: Build With Robots / Fetch Robotics (with City of Albuquerque)
sources.title: Breezy One from Build With Robots, Fetch Robotics disinfects Albuquerque airport
sources.claim: Breezy One, an autonomous mobile robot built by Build With Robots on the Fetch Robotics platform, autonomously navigates a large public facility at night and fogs an EPA-registered chemical agent over the whole space; it has been in nightly use at Albuquerque International Sunport.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: whole-room chemical fogging for disinfection. It is the same physical act as insecticidal space spraying/fogging — an unoccupied area is closed off and an aerosolized EPA-registered chemical is dispensed over it from a moving nozzle, with no manipulation of objects; the article notes the fog penetrates behind and under surfaces, as insect space sprays must.

sources.title: Spraying robot for greenhouse crop protection - Micothon
sources.claim: Micothon's tube/rail spraying robot is sold in a fully automatic version that carries out pesticide spraying of a commercial greenhouse on its own, running on the greenhouse heating pipe rails and moving between rows unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic application of insecticides/pesticides in a greenhouse. Same chemical, same pump-and-nozzle application at similar rates and precision; the rail-guided, fixed-geometry, people-excluded greenhouse is exactly a purpose-built (E1) presentation of spray targets, showing a machine can lay down a pesticide band on defined surfaces along a fixed path.

sources.title: Octopus Robots Poultry Safe robot | WATTPoultry.com
sources.claim: The Octopus Poultry Safe robot works autonomously inside livestock buildings, treating the whole floor area by applying a biocide as a nebulised mist without direct human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous nebulisation of a biocide throughout an agricultural building. Comparable chemical, comparable dispersal hardware and comparable indoor building-scale coverage to insecticidal fogging of a storeroom or trash room.

sources.title: Weeds under control with handy autonomous Kilter spot sprayer
sources.claim: The Kilter AX-1 is an autonomous field robot ... finds targets with machine vision and places a calibrated droplet of pesticide on each one; a German farm has run it in commercial service since April 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous vision-guided spot spraying of a pesticide onto individual detected targets (weeds). Same detect-then-spray act at millimetre precision with a metered chemical dose, showing a machine can spot-treat presented targets rather than only broadcast.

sources.title: Toilet-cleaning robot makes us feel better about all this AI business
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom cleaning robot autonomously sprays disinfectant chemical and water onto toilets, walls and floors in commercial restrooms in hospitals and airports, running unattended day to day after an initial mapping/setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous directed chemical spraying onto fixtures and floor edges in commercial restrooms. Comparable liquid application to building surfaces in an occupied facility, but limited to standardized bolted-down fixtures in a mapped restroom — it does not move clutter or reach into cracks behind equipment.

sources.title: Tech Startup Banking on Wasp-Killing Drone - Pest Control Technology
sources.claim: The only pest-control-specific spraying aircraft in commercial service for elevated nests, AeroPest's Hummingbird, is flown by a technician with a remote controller rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task (spraying insecticide at wasp nests on buildings), but continuous teleoperation means it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Set up, arrange, or remove decorations, tables, chairs, ladders, or scaffolding to prepare facilities for events, such as banquets or meetings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel / conference-center banquet room set or 'flip': pull 60-inch round or 6-ft rectangular banquet tables off stack carts, tip them upright, unfold and lock the legs, position them per the event diagram, then set 8-10 stack chairs per table and drape linens; strike everything back onto carts after the event, often on a tight turnaround between functions.

School gym, church hall, or community-center multipurpose room: wheel dollies of folding chairs and long folding tables out of a storage closet, unfold and lay out rows or banquet seating for an assembly, dinner, or meeting; afterwards fold, stack, and return everything to storage and sweep the floor area.

Office / institutional meeting room prep and reset: change the existing furniture into a requested layout (U-shape, classroom rows, hollow square) by pushing rolling or stacking chairs and light modular tables into position, bringing in a few extra chairs, positioning a lectern or A/V cart, then putting the room back to its default layout afterward.

Decorations: hang banners, bunting, string lights, seasonal or holiday decorations, and event signage from walls, ceilings, and doorways (frequently working off a step ladder), set out tablecloths, skirting, and centerpieces; take all of it down and box it after the event.

Access and staging equipment: carry, erect, and reposition step ladders and rolling scaffold towers, or assemble and remove portable stage/riser sections, dance floor panels, and stanchions for an event or for overhead work; disassemble and return to storage afterward.

sources.system: ALORE (Unitree B2 legged manipulator with Z1 arm)
sources.developer: Academic research group (legged-manipulation lab, China; open-sourced)
sources.title: ALORE: Autonomous Large-Object Rearrangement with a Legged Manipulator (arXiv 2602.04214)
sources.claim: ALORE, a Unitree B2 quadruped with a Z1 arm, autonomously rearranged large furniture (chairs, tables, bins) to commanded target poses, including a long-horizon trial moving 32 chairs in 8 continuous loops over ~40 minutes with no failures and a ~40 m autonomous rearrangement run.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant: pushing/pulling free-standing chairs and tables to specified positions and orientations is the arranging step of preparing a room for an event.

sources.system: ALORE (Unitree B2 legged manipulator with Z1 arm)
sources.developer: Academic research group (legged-manipulation lab, China; open-sourced)
sources.title: ALORE: Autonomous Large-Object Rearrangement with a Legged Manipulator (arXiv PDF)
sources.claim: ALORE's real-world operation depends on the objects being instrumented and pre-modeled: fiducial tags are attached to each object for relative pose during manipulation, graspable regions are predefined, and approximate target-object positions are supplied to the planner.
sources.transferJustification: Same system as evidence 0; establishes that the demonstrated furniture arranging happens in a setting instrumented for the machine rather than an as-found human facility.

sources.system: Figure 03 humanoid with Helix-02 VLA policy
sources.title: Helix 02 Bedroom Tidy
sources.claim: Figure's Helix-02 humanoids, running a single learned vision-language-action policy from pixels to actions, autonomously reset a bedroom, including grasping an office chair with both ... pushing it under a desk using whole-body force generation.
sources.transferJustification: Chair repositioning is a component of meeting-room setup; shows a humanoid can autonomously grasp and reposition a standard office chair, though only as an isolated behavior in a curated test room.

sources.title: Atlas Goes Hands On | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid autonomously moves bulky automotive engine covers between supplier containers ... sequencing dolly in an industrial cell, driven by a list of bin locations, with vision-based detection of fixtures and parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repetitive transfer of bulky rigid items from presentation containers into designated positions in a purpose-built industrial cell; supports the E1 counterfactual in which furniture is presented ready at a pickup station and must be placed at marked positions at production throughput.

sources.date: 2023-01 (funding coverage); in field use at industrial sites
sources.title: Robotics firm Kewazo gets a $10M lift | Construction Dive
sources.claim: Kewazo's LIFTBOT is a battery-powered, remote-controlled robotic hoist that carries scaffolding material to height on construction sites and industrial plants; it transports parts but does not itself erect scaffolding or staging.
sources.transferJustification: Closest cited system to erecting scaffolding; it is a remote-controlled material hoist, so it does not substantiate autonomous erection or removal of scaffolds, ladders, or portable staging.

tasks.label: Clean chimneys, flues, and connecting pipes, using power or hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Building custodian cleans the fire side and flue of an oil/gas/wood-fired furnace or boiler in a school, church, hospital or apartment boiler room: shuts the unit down, opens cleanout doors, runs brushes through fire tubes and the connecting smoke pipe/breeching to the chimney base, vacuums soot into containment, reseals joints.

Janitor sweeps a wood-stove or fireplace flue in a facility building (lodge, camp hall, community center, church): sets drop cloths and a HEPA vacuum, runs rod-and-brush from the firebox or from the roof, removes creosote and ash, cleans the connecting stove pipe and reassembles it.

Cleaner working in an occupied dwelling (private home or apartment unit, for a property manager or cleaning contractor) sweeps a fireplace/wood-stove chimney: protects furnishings, works around occupants and pets, ladder/roof access on a pitched roof, variable and often old masonry construction, damper and smoke chamber cleaned by feel.

Janitor cleans a commercial kitchen exhaust hood, its grease duct riser and the connecting pipe to the rooftop fan in a cafeteria or restaurant: scrapes and degreases duct interior with hand and power tools/pressure washer, containment bags, wipe-down and restart.

Maintenance janitor at a central heating plant or industrial facility clears a large flue-gas breeching, horizontal duct run or chimney base: confined-space entry, scrapers, air lance and industrial vacuum to remove packed ash/soot, then inspects draft.

sources.system: StoneAge AutoBox 3L with Sentinel Automation Technology
sources.title: StoneAge Inc. Releases Sentinel Automation Technology for Automated Heat Exchanger Cleaning
sources.claim: StoneAge's Sentinel automation, integrated with the AutoBox 3L flex-lancing tractor, uses sensors to automatically position high-pressure lances and clean fouled heat-exchanger tube interiors end to end while operators stand outside the blast zone; commercially released and used on customer jobs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing hard fouling deposits from the inside of tubes and pipes with a powered cleaning tool - the same deliverable as cleaning a flue or connecting pipe. Objects (fouled steel pipe interiors), tool class (powered lance/brush) and precision (entering and traversing each bore) are comparable; the demonstrated setting is a fixtured bundle with the machine mounted to it.

sources.system: StoneAge AutoBox 2L / ABX-3L automated flex lancing system
sources.title: StoneAge AutoBox 2L Automated Flex Lancing/Exchanger Tube Cleaning
sources.claim: The AutoBox family of automated flex-lancing systems performs hands-free tube-bundle cleaning, with the lance-driving box mounted to the bundle/tube sheet and the operator removed from the barricaded blast zone.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Sentinel item: powered internal cleaning of pipe/tube runs, performed with the workpiece fixtured and presented to the machine in a purpose-built cleaning setup.

sources.developer: ASME POWER 2010 paper (ISB integration and utility boiler case study)
sources.title: Boiler Cleaning Using ISB (Intelligent Soot Blowing) System Integration: Recent Developments and Case Study
sources.claim: Intelligent sootblowing systems automatically decide and sequence the operation of motorized sootblower lances that insert into boiler flue-gas passages and blast fireside ash and soot deposits off heat transfer surfaces; implemented and case-studied on operating boilers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine removal of soot/ash deposits from the flue-gas passages of a fired heating plant - exactly what the janitor does by hand at a small boiler. The machine works inside a vessel purpose-built with sootblower ports, i.e. the work is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Diamond Power Titanium automated sootblowing control / Titanium ISB
sources.developer: Diamond Power International (ANDRITZ; formerly Babcock & Wilcox)
sources.title: Diamond Power automated sootblowing control | ANDRITZ
sources.claim: Titanium automated sootblowing control (Diamond Power, now ANDRITZ) is a commercially sold controller that runs boiler cleaning equipment on optimized automatic sequences across utility, biomass, waste-to-energy and industrial boilers.
sources.transferJustification: Same as the ISB item: automatic powered cleaning of flue-gas passages in fired heating plant, inside a vessel designed around the cleaning machinery.

sources.system: Hargassner Eco-PK pellet boiler automatic heat-exchanger cleaning
sources.title: Pellet heating technology in detail | All top performances
sources.claim: Commercial pellet/biomass boilers include motorized turbulator scrapers that automatically clean all heat-exchanger flue pipes at intervals and drop the ash to an ash auger, with no operator action.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: soot/fly-ash removal from the flue passages of a small solid-fuel heating appliance - the same deposits and passages a janitor brushes out - performed by a machine in an appliance purpose-built around that mechanism.

sources.system: TAPROGGE tube cleaning system (Type E 1 strainer section)
sources.title: Type E 1 Strainer Section - Efficiency in Energy and Water
sources.claim: Automated, PLC-controlled tube cleaning systems continuously clean condenser tube interiors mechanically while the plant runs, without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic mechanical cleaning of the inside of pipe runs in a plant purpose-plumbed for the cleaning system; supports that pipe-interior cleaning is machine-completable when the pipework is built around the machine.

sources.title: Lifa Air Duct Cleaner Robot Remote Controlled Brushing Machine
sources.claim: In-situ duct and flue cleaning robots sold for buildings are brush/jet crawlers driven by a human operator with a remote controller and camera feed, not autonomous cleaners.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (cleaning duct/flue interiors inside human buildings); cited as negative evidence that this in-building work is done under continuous teleoperation, so it cannot support an E2 judgment.

sources.title: Confined Space Ductwork Cleaning with Custom Robotic Crawler
sources.claim: Confined-space ductwork cleaning inside industrial plant is performed by custom tracked robotic crawlers that are driven and monitored by an operator through a camera feed.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task for in-situ flue/duct cleaning; cited as negative evidence that such work in as-found plant is operator-driven rather than autonomous.

tasks.label: Mow or trim lawns or shrubbery, using mowers or hand or power trimmers, and clear debris from grounds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine in-season mowing of the larger open turf areas on the grounds of an institutional building (school, church, office building, apartment complex): riding or walk-behind mower over maintained lawn panels with scattered trees, signs and curbs, on a weekly schedule, working around occasional pedestrians.

Mowing the small, irregular grass areas of the same property: entry courtyards, narrow strips between walk and street, parking-lot islands, banks and slopes, tight around AC condensers, bollards, benches, planting beds and parked cars.

String-trimming/edging the grass the mower cannot reach — along building foundations, fence lines, sign and light poles, tree rings, walk and curb edges — and shaping/cutting back shrubs and hedges with hand or power hedge trimmers, then policing the clippings.

Clearing leaves, grass clippings, sand/grit and loose debris from hard surfaces on the grounds — sidewalks, building entries, steps, loading areas, parking lot — using a backpack/push blower or push sweeper, timed around building occupants.

Routine litter policing of lawns and landscape beds: walking the property picking up windblown paper, cups, bottles, cans and cigarette butts from turf, mulch and gravel areas before mowing or before the building opens.

Heavy debris clearing after wind, storms or heavy use: gathering fallen branches and wet leaf piles, bagging or hauling bulk trash and dumped items to a dumpster, and emptying exterior trash receptacles around the grounds.

sources.developer: Scythe Robotics (acquired by Autonomous Solutions Inc.)
sources.title: Autonomous Solutions Inc. acquires Scythe Robotics to expand AI-powered autonomy | Landscape Management
sources.claim: Scythe M.52, a fully electric autonomous commercial mower, mowed roughly 2 billion square feet of commercial/institutional turf for dozens of customers across ... US states in 2025, operating with crews on real properties.

sources.system: Husqvarna Automower 560 EPOS / CEORA commercial robotic mowers
sources.title: Get Equipped: Robotic And Autonomous Mowers – Turf Magazine
sources.claim: Husqvarna sells commercial autonomous robotic mowers (Automower EPOS line, CEORA) marketed and specified for facility maintenance, corporate campuses ..., mowing turf without boundary wires.

sources.title: SRU deploys first robotic lawn mower | Slippery Rock University
sources.claim: A university grounds department put a Husqvarna Automower to work mowing a small, high-visibility quarter-acre courtyard lawn between campus buildings.

sources.title: Autonomous Electric Mowers to Reduce University's Fuel Costs - Government Fleet
sources.claim: Arkansas State University added autonomous robotic mowers to its grounds-maintenance fleet, running several units on campus lawns.

sources.system: Ecovacs Goat A3000 LiDAR Pro, Mammotion LUBA 3 AWD, Segway Navimow i215 LiDAR
sources.title: 14 Best Robot Lawn Mowers: Tested in real yards by us of 2026 - Reviewed

sources.title: ViaBot officially launches new parking lot sweeping solution - Automated Warehouse

tasks.label: Steam-clean or shampoo carpets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office building, after-hours periodic hot-water extraction of open-plan carpet, corridors and conference rooms: pre-vacuum, move chairs and light furniture, pre-spray and agitate traffic lanes, extract with a self-contained walk-behind machine plus wand for edges and under desks, place air movers, restore furniture.

Hotel/hospitality carpets: guest rooms, corridors, lobby and banquet space; low-moisture encapsulation or hot-water extraction worked around beds, casegoods and occupancy schedules, with fast dry times required before spaces are released.

School, university or government building deep clean during a break period: classrooms, libraries, offices and dorm rooms; desks and furniture moved out and back, heavy soil, gum and dried spills, multiple extraction passes.

Occupied-hours spot and stain remediation with a portable/box extractor: coffee, ink and food spills, entry traffic lanes, cubicle areas; pre-treat, agitate, extract, blot and set wet-floor signage while occupants are present.
Walk-off/entrance mats and loose area rugs: taken up and shampooed/extracted at a loading dock, service area or in place, then dried and put back.

Healthcare, senior-living, daycare or specialty spaces: carpet with biological soils (urine, vomit, blood), odor and sanitizing treatment, plus adjacent upholstery and carpeted stairs, extracted with sanitizing chemistry.

sources.transferJustification: Home carpet washing is the closest analogue to janitorial shampooing, but this unit is a pre-production household-scale prototype (trial production July 2026) with no third-party efficacy testing, so it does not substantiate completing commercial extraction work.
