roles.title: Maids and Housekeeping Cleaners
roles.description: Perform any combination of light cleaning duties to maintain private households or commercial establishments, such as hotels and hospitals, in a clean and orderly manner. Duties may include making beds, replenishing linens, cleaning rooms and halls, and vacuuming.
roles.sector: Building and grounds cleaning and maintenance

tasks.label: Keep storage areas and carts well-stocked, clean, and tidy.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel guest-floor housekeeper, start/end of shift: loads the housekeeping cart from the floor linen closet — stacks of folded sheets and towels, amenity bottles, soaps, tissue rolls, trash liners, chemical bottles — arranges them in the cart's shelves and bins, wipes the cart down, empties linen and trash bags, leaves cart and closet tidy. Cramped shared back-of-house room, contents vary by day.

Hotel/resort central linen and supply storeroom: receives clean linen carts from laundry and vendor cases of amenities, stacks folded linens on shelves by type, rotates and organizes stock, breaks down boxes, sweeps/mops the floor, keeps aisles clear and par levels visible.

Hospital or nursing-home environmental-services worker: replenishes the janitorial closet and EVS cart from central supply (chemicals, gloves, liners, wipes, paper goods), keeps the closet to compliance standard (labeled, nothing on the floor), cleans and disinfects the cart between units.

Office building / commercial nightly janitorial: restocks the cart from a locked supply room with toilet paper, roll towels, soap cartridges and liners; stages supplies for the route; at shift end wipes the cart, dumps waste and tidies the supply room shelves.

Private-household cleaner: replenishes the caddy and vehicle stock between homes, organizes the client's cleaning-supply closet or laundry-room shelves, notes and replaces used-up products; layout, shelving and contents differ house to house and are not kept to any standard.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robot autonomously senses shelf depletion and replenishes convenience-store refrigerated shelves with bottles and ..., deployed at 300 FamilyMart stores under a RaaS model, with remote teleoperation only as a fallback.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: keeping a stock location replenished. It covers the core 'well-stocked' element — sensing what is low and placing packaged goods (bottles, cans, comparable to amenity bottles and paper goods) into the correct shelf position — at commercial reliability from a fixed restocking station.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics receives strategic investment from Rockwell Automation - The Robot Report

Loading a cart or supply shelf with amenity bottles, soap boxes, tissue rolls and liners is the same pick-from-bin, place-into-container operation on comparable objects and precision, when cart and stock are presented at a fixtured station.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model Offering Fully Autonomous, Round-the-Clock Dexterity

sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling and folding flat textiles into neat stacks. The deformable-object skill needed to build and place folded towel/sheet stacks in a linen stock location is the same, at a fixed two-arm station where the linen is presented.

sources.claim: Dyna Robotics has moved past demonstration to an installed autonomous folding robot at a commercial laundromat in Sacramento, one of the first US commercial laundry deployments of autonomous ....

sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning a wheeled service cart. Covers the 'keep carts clean' element when the cart is brought to a purpose-built machine — comparable object (stainless/plastic cart) and an accepted hygiene standard.

sources.claim: A 2025 integrated mobile-manipulator system for autonomous supermarket shelf stocking achieved over 98% pick-and-place success, but only in laboratory replications of store conditions, and the authors state current autonomous systems remain inferior ... human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile-manipulator restocking of shelves inside a human work facility — the closest analogue to stocking a linen closet or loading a cart in situ. It shows the capability is still lab-stage and below worker quality, supporting negative E2 judgments.

tasks.label: Carry linens, towels, toilet items, and cleaning supplies, using wheeled carts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel guest-floor cart run: housekeeper moves a loaded housekeeping cart (sheets, towels, amenities/toilet items, chemicals) from a floor linen closet or laundry along guest corridors, parks it outside each room, and hauls soiled linen and trash bins back to the laundry chute/laundry room, using service elevators between floors, amid guests and other staff.

Hospital / long-term-care environmental services: moving carts and hampers of clean linen, toilet paper/paper goods and cleaning supplies from central storage or the laundry to unit supply rooms and patient floors, and returning soiled-linen and trash carts, via service corridors and elevators on a scheduled route.

Office, school or commercial-building janitorial round: wheeling a janitor cart loaded with chemicals, paper goods, liners and rags through lobbies, corridors and restrooms, restocking restroom supplies floor by floor, moving the cart between floors by elevator, usually on an evening shift in a nearly empty building.

Private household cleaning: carrying a supply caddy, vacuum and cleaning products from the car into the client's home, moving them room to room and up and down stairs, and carrying fresh linens/towels from a closet to bedrooms and bathrooms; layout, clutter, pets and stairs vary from house to house.

Stocking/replenishing the cart itself: pulling stacks of folded towels and sheets, amenity bottles, soap and toilet paper, and chemical bottles from linen-room or storeroom shelves and loading them in correct par counts onto the cart's shelves and bins before or midway through the shift.

tasks.label: Clean rooms, hallways, lobbies, lounges, restrooms, corridors, elevators, stairways, locker rooms, and other work areas so that health standards are met.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel/motel guest-room clean on checkout or stayover: scrub the bathroom (toilet, tub/shower, sink, mirror, floor), sanitize high-touch surfaces (desk, remote, phone, handles), clear trash and debris left by guests, vacuum, and leave the room inspection-ready in 25-40 minutes, working around guest belongings and unpredictable soil.

Hospital / nursing-facility patient room and clinical area cleaning (EVS): daily and discharge/terminal cleans - disinfect bedrails, tables, call buttons and other high-touch surfaces in a set order, clean the patient bathroom, remove regulated waste, mop floors, around occupied beds, medical equipment and infection-control protocols.

Public-area round in a hotel, office building or school: corridors, lobby seating, elevator cabs and tracks, stairwells and landings, locker rooms and lounges - emptying bins, wiping glass doors and rails, dusting ledges and furniture, spot-cleaning spills, detailing edges and stairs that machines miss.

Scheduled large-area floor cleaning in an institutional facility: scrubbing hard floors or vacuuming carpet across a lobby, concourse or long corridor (tens of thousands of square feet) on a fixed route, during or after operating hours, with people and furniture present.

Public or staff restroom cleaning in a facility (office tower, airport, hospital, school, gym): scrub toilets and urinals, wipe basins, counters and mirrors, disinfect touch points, pick up litter and clean the floor, repeated through the shift in high-traffic restrooms.

Private household clean by a housekeeper: kitchen counters, sink and appliance fronts, one to three bathrooms, dusting furniture and shelves with objects on them, vacuuming and mopping floors, tidying clutter - a different layout, different surfaces and different clutter at every house.

tasks.label: Empty wastebaskets, empty and clean ashtrays, and transport other trash and waste to disposal areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel guest-room servicing: housekeeper pulls the liner from the bedroom and bathroom wastebaskets (mixed contents: paper, food waste, wet tissues, bottles), knots the bag, drops it in the cart's trash sack, wipes the basket if soiled and inserts a fresh liner, while working a 15-30 minute room quota.

Nightly office/commercial cleaning: worker walks a floor emptying 40-100 deskside wastebaskets and paper recycling bins into a rolling barrel or cart bag, re-lining bins as needed, keeping recycling separate, then wheels the barrel to the dock compactor/dumpster.

Private household cleaning: empty kitchen, bathroom and bedroom cans of household waste, tie and replace bags, and carry the bags out through the house to the outdoor bin, curb cart or apartment chute/dumpster; layouts, bin types and clutter differ house to house.

Hospital/clinic room and unit cleaning: empty patient-room and soiled-utility waste containers, segregate regulated medical waste in red bags and untouched sharps containers, close and re-line containers, and carry bagged waste to the unit's soiled-utility/holding room.

Bulk haul in a large hotel or hospital: loaded trash/recycling carts and bagged waste staged in floor holding rooms are moved through back-of-house corridors and service elevators to the loading-dock compactor or dumpster area, and empty carts returned to the floors.

Public areas of a hotel/restaurant/office: empty lobby, corridor and restroom receptacles, empty and wipe out sand-top or patio ashtrays and cigarette urns at entrances, and take the collected waste to the dumpster, working around guests.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots are deployed in hospitals hauling waste carts, including trash, recycling and regulated medical waste, through corridors to disposal areas.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the task element 'transport other trash and waste to disposal areas' with the same loads (waste carts) in the same facility type.

tasks.label: Sweep, scrub, wax, or polish floors, using brooms, mops, or powered scrubbing and waxing machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel guest-room turnover: sweep/vacuum debris from the room's hard floors and damp-mop the tile bathroom floor around the toilet base, tub/shower threshold, vanity and door track, plus the entry/closet hard floor, working around beds, luggage racks and furniture under a 20-30 minute room-turn clock and a guest-ready inspection standard.

Large open hard-floor areas kept by an institution - hotel lobbies, ballrooms, corridors and back-of-house passages; hospital/nursing-home corridors, lobbies and dining rooms; school and office common floors - dust-mopped or swept and then wet-scrubbed, often with a walk-behind or ride-on powered scrubbing machine, sometimes with people present.

Hospital or nursing-home patient room and its ensuite bathroom: damp-mop the floor with disinfectant per infection-control protocol, mopping under and around the bed, IV pole, over-bed table, bedside chair and toilet, using clean-to-dirty technique and a fresh mop head per room.

Private household visit: sweep or dry-mop then wet-mop kitchen, entry, hallway and bathroom hard floors - moving chairs, mats, pet bowls and toys aside, scrubbing dried spills, food residue and grout, and doing corners, baseboard edges and stair treads by hand.

Public/commercial multi-fixture restrooms (hotel public washrooms, hospital, airport, office, stadium): sweep debris, apply cleaner and scrub the floor including around toilet and urinal bases, under partitions and along walls, then squeegee or mop dry.

Periodic deep floor maintenance on resilient floors in a commercial establishment: strip old finish or scrub aggressively, rinse, apply coats of floor finish/wax with an applicator mop, then burnish or polish to a shine with a powered machine, usually after hours over a roped-off area.

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo is a fully ... deployed in airports, malls, hospitals, factories and warehouses - it performs sweeping/wet-scrubbing of hard floors itself inside institution-run human work facilities.

Private-home cleaner: replenish the client's own supplies - fresh toilet paper and hand soap in each bathroom, folded towels on rails and in the linen cupboard, kitchen paper towels and dish soap - drawing from storage locations that differ house to house.

tasks.label: Dust and polish furniture and equipment.

instances.label: Hotel guest-room turnover: within a ~20-30 minute room clean, dust and wipe nightstands, desk, dresser, headboard, TV and lamps, luggage rack, mirror and picture frames; lift and replace guest belongings in stayover rooms; polish wood surfaces; work is spot-inspected by a supervisor.

tasks.label: Disinfect equipment and supplies, using germicides or steam-operated sterilizers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel/motel housekeeper: sanitizes guest-room equipment and supplies with a germicidal solution (TV remote, phone, coffee maker, ice bucket, glassware, bathroom fixtures/amenities) and at shift end disinfects her own equipment — cart, mop handle and bucket, spray bottles, vacuum attachments — cloths sent to laundry. Rooms occupied/vacated on an unpredictable schedule, guests and staff in corridors.

Hospital or clinic environmental-services worker: at discharge/terminal cleaning, wipes hospital-grade germicide onto patient-care equipment in the room — bed frame and rails, IV pole, over-bed table, chair, call button, blood-pressure cuff, wheelchair, commode — observing the disinfectant contact time, working around cords, drawers, and stored items.

Soiled-utility / reprocessing room in a hospital or nursing home: collects bedpans, urinals, commode buckets and wash basins, empties them and runs them through a flusher/washer-disinfector or steam-operated sterilizer; also washes and disinfects mop buckets, housekeeping carts and reusable tools, then returns clean items to storage.

Private-household cleaner: disinfects household equipment and supplies with bleach/quaternary germicide or a handheld steam cleaner — sponges, brushes, cutting boards, sink strainers, trash cans, pet bowls, children's toys, toilet brush — plus her own tools between houses. Layout, clutter and item mix differ at every house.

Cleaner in an institutional/commercial facility (office building, school, gym, airport, medical office): nightly germicidal treatment of shared equipment and fixtures — restroom fixtures, desks and shared workstations, gym machines, door hardware — applied with a pump/electrostatic sprayer or wipes after the space is closed to occupants.

instances.label: Hotel housekeeper: clean linen arrives on the guest floor in bags or carts from the laundry; she separates flat sheets, fitted sheets, pillowcases, bath/hand towels, washcloths and mats, counts them against the floor par sheet, pulls and flags stained or torn pieces, and stacks them squared-up on the floor linen closet shelves and the housekeeping cart, working in a narrow closet alongside other staff.

Worker in an on-premise laundry room (hotel, resort, nursing home, small clinic): takes clean linen from dryers/ironer, folds and sorts it by type and size, counts pieces into stacks for inventory records, applies facility marks/tags (laundry marker, heat-seal label, RFID pouch) or flags rejects, and shelves the stacks in the laundry's linen storage racks.

Hospital / long-term-care housekeeping or EVS aide: receives an exchange cart of clean linen from the contract laundry, verifies and counts pieces against the delivery ticket and unit par levels, keeps gowns, draw sheets, bath blankets and towels separated, and stocks the unit's linen closet/cart under infection-control rules in a busy corridor.

Private-household housekeeper: takes the household's washed and dried sheets, towels and table linens, sorts by set and room, folds, counts complete sets, notes items to be replaced, and puts them away on the shelves of the family's linen closet, which is crowded, non-standard and shared with other stored goods.

Small commercial establishment (gym, spa, salon, B&B, restaurant): the linen-service delivery of clean towels, robes, sheets or table linens is checked and counted against the packing slip, marked or tagged for the establishment, and stored on shelving in a small back-of-house closet.

sources.system: Kannegiesser robotized dry work line (Robofeed RFT feeding robot + XFM Speedline folder + Vectura stack transport)
sources.title: The fully automated dry work line - Success Story of Kruppert Wäsche-Dienst GmbH
sources.claim: Kannegiesser's robotized dry-work line, deployed at the Kruppert Wasche-Dienst commercial laundry processing 3.5 t/h of hotel and restaurant linen, automatically feeds, folds, sorts and ... clean linen of several article types and removes the finished stacks without staff intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Same work as the task — separating clean linen by article type, building counted stacks and moving them to storage — performed on an industrial clean-side line rather than by hand in a linen room.

sources.system: JENSEN / Inwatec laundry automation (Robofeed line, post-wash sorting and finished-stack storage)
sources.title: Laundry automation | JENSEN-GROUP
sources.claim: JENSEN-GROUP, with partner Inwatec, supplies laundry automation that fully automates sorting of linen and garments, the storage of finished (folded) stacks, and robotic feeding of towels into finishing equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the storage element of the task — putting counted, folded stacks of clean linen away into a storage system — in industrial clean-side installations.

sources.title: Flipper CT | Chicago Dryer
sources.claim: Chicago Dryer's Flipper CT is a commercially sold machine that automatically counts and stacks small clean flatwork pieces (face cloths, shop towels, wipers) after folding.
sources.transferJustification: Performs the counting and stacking elements of this task on the same clean linen articles, with the work presented to the machine.

sources.title: Chicago Dryer Flatwork Finishing Equipment | Western State Design
sources.claim: Chicago Dryer's Genesis ATM uses deep-learning vision to pick clean towels of mixed sizes out of a bulk supply and feed them into a sorting towel folder, giving hands-free sorting and folding of clean terry.
sources.transferJustification: Sorting clean towels of different sizes out of a mixed supply is the sorting element of this task, done by machine vision on the very objects the housekeeper sorts.

sources.title: Getting Started with SmartLaundry – Alpenland Laundry Success Story
sources.claim: Kannegiesser's Pack&Label, in use at the Alpenland laundry serving hotels and guesthouses, automatically captures the correct quantity ... clean articles, and laundry carts are marked for dispatch with automatically generated packing lists showing article quantities per customer.
sources.transferJustification: Supplies the counting and marking/identification elements: piece counts are captured automatically at the folder and the storage/transport cart is labelled with the article quantities.

sources.title: Intelligent robots for commercial laundries | IFR case study
sources.claim: sewts' VELUM robot cell, built on FANUC arms with in-house vision, has been in production at the Greif Textile Mietsysteme industrial laundry since November 2022, autonomously picking crumpled clean textiles and feeding 500-600 pieces per hour into folding machines.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates robust robotic handling of individual clean, limp linens (towels, sheets) at production rates — the manipulation skill underlying sorting and stacking clean linen.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics unveils Dyna-1: Autonomous robot achieves 24-hour dexterous task performance
sources.claim: Dyna Robotics' DYNA-1 dual-arm station folded more than 700 napkins over 24 hours fully autonomously with over 99.4% success and no human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Folding limp linen and building neat stacks at a fixed station is the textile-handling and stack-building portion of this task, sustained at worker-comparable reliability.

sources.title: Laundry Folding Robots: What Laundromat Operators Need to Know
sources.claim: Dyna Robotics has installed its autonomous folding robot at a laundromat ..., one of the first US commercial laundry deployments of autonomous ... of napkins and linens.
sources.transferJustification: Shows a fixed folding/stacking station working on household and commercial wash-and-fold linen in real back-of-house operation, i.e. the work brought to the machine.

tasks.label: Sort clothing and other articles, load washing machines, and iron and fold dried items.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private household housekeeper works through a family's laundry in the home's laundry room or basement: sorts a mixed hamper (darks, lights, delicates, kids' clothes, towels, bed linens), pretreats stains, loads and starts the domestic washer, moves loads to the dryer, then folds the dried items into stacks. Several loads run across the visit alongside other cleaning duties.

Private household: ironing/pressing after drying — dress shirts, blouses, slacks, cotton napkins, tablecloths and pillowcases pressed one garment at a time on an ironing board with a steam iron, at varying fabric settings, then hung or folded.

Hotel/motel on-premise laundry: housekeeper or laundry attendant empties linen carts and chutes, sorts sheets, pillowcases, bath towels, bath mats and pool towels by type, pulls out stained or torn pieces and foreign objects, weighs and loads commercial washer-extractors, starts the correct cycle, and transfers finished loads to tumble dryers.

Hotel/commercial wash-and-fold folding station: dried towels, sheets, pillowcases and napkins are pulled from a dryer or cart at a back-of-house folding table and folded/stacked to the property's standard for the linen closet or shelving.

Hospital, clinic or nursing home housekeeping: soiled bed linen, patient gowns, bath blankets and cubicle curtains are sorted under infection-control rules (isolation bags, no shaking, PPE), loaded into industrial washers with the correct wash formula, and clean stock is folded and stacked onto linen carts.

Small commercial establishment (gym, salon, spa, restaurant, medical office, short-term-rental turnover service): cleaner sorts and washes towels, robes, uniforms, aprons and table napkins in domestic-scale or small OPL machines in a back room, presses table linens or uniforms, and folds the dried items into supply stacks.

sources.date: 2024-2026 (product line; Yverdon plant modernization reported Feb 2026)

sources.claim: JENSEN/Inwatec robotic soiled-side systems (THOR robotic separator, HEIMDAL camera/RFID identification, ODIN foreign-object detection) automate sorting of soiled linen and garments in industrial laundries, including healthcare and hospitality linen; installed and running in production plants.

sources.title: Smart automation for every laundry size — Laundry & Cleaning Today
sources.claim: A production laundry in Yverdon was modernized with Inwatec automation: THOR robotically separates bulk-fed soiled laundry into individual items and HEIMDAL identifies garments by colour, pattern, size and fabric ... for automated sorting of workwear, kitchen linen and small pieces.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model...

sources.claim: Dyna Robotics has installed its autonomous folding robot at a laundromat ... — an early commercial deployment of autonomous folding in a working wash-and-fold facility; systems handle t-shirts, towels, napkins and linens at ~60% of human throughput.

sources.title: π0: Our First Generalist Policy
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0 policy autonomously takes laundry out of a dryer, places it on a table and folds shirts and shorts into a neat stack, using either a mobile robot ..., in uncut single-policy runs in the lab.

sources.title: Figure AI humanoid robot goes viral for doing laundry with autonomous precision
sources.claim: Figure's humanoid F.02 running the Helix VLA was shown loading laundry into a washing ... in a home, and Figure later announced autonomous laundry folding with the same architecture; both are single-step demonstrations rather than deployments.

sources.title: Isaac 0 — Weave Robotics
sources.claim: Weave Robotics' Isaac 0, a stationary home laundry-folding robot shipping to California customers since February 2026, folds a load in 30-90 minutes and explicitly mixes autonomy with remote teleoperation by a Weave specialist to finish every fold; it does not sort, wash or iron.

tasks.label: Move and arrange furniture and turn mattresses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel guest-room clean: pull out and push back light, movable pieces to restore the standard room layout - desk chair rolled out and back under the desk, luggage rack repositioned, side chair squared up - on carpet, in a room whose layout repeats floor to floor.

Hotel guest room / deep clean: shift heavier pieces - upholstered armchair, nightstand, dresser, pulling the bed away from the headboard wall - to vacuum and dust behind them, then return each to its marked layout position without scuffing walls or carpet.

Scheduled mattress turning: strip the bed, then rotate 180 degrees or flip a queen/king mattress (60-120 lb, floppy, no handles) on the box spring or platform, often a two-person lift, then remake it. Hotel, dormitory or institutional bedroom.

Private home cleaning visit: move dining chairs, a coffee table, small side tables, floor lamps and area rugs aside to vacuum/mop under them and put everything back as found; occasionally rotate the mattress at a linen change or rearrange furniture at the client's request. Layout, clutter and floor type differ house to house.

Hospital or nursing-home patient room: move the wheeled over-bed table, visitor chairs and the heavy vinyl recliner clear of the bed for terminal cleaning of the floor, then reposition everything to the unit's standard setup around occupied-room equipment and lines.

Office/commercial nightly cleaning: pull task chairs out from under desks and conference tables to vacuum, push them back in and straighten them to a uniform arrangement across a floor of dozens of workstations.

sources.title: Helix 02 Bedroom Tidy
sources.claim: Two Figure F.03 humanoids running the Helix-02 learned vision-language-action policy autonomously reset a bedroom in under ..., including grasping an office chair with both ... pushing it under a desk (whole-body furniture pushing) and jointly making a bed, with no scripted handoffs between subtasks.

sources.title: Figure humanoid robots organize room, hang clothes, and make bed without humans
sources.claim: Independent trade coverage of the same Figure demonstration confirms the robots repositioned furniture and made the bed autonomously, coordinating only through onboard cameras.

sources.title: Mobile ALOHA: Learning Bimanual Mobile Manipulation using Low-Cost Whole-Body Teleoperation
sources.claim: Mobile ALOHA learned to push in chairs autonomously from 50 demonstrations, reaching 80% success - a second, independent data point that autonomous chair repositioning is achievable, though at reliability below a worker's.
sources.transferJustification: Pushing dining/office chairs back into place is the same physical act as the chair-arranging portion of this task, on the same objects and floors.

sources.system: ET-LQC-FLIP mattress inspection conveyor with flipping system
sources.title: ET-LQC-FLIP | Mattress Inspection Conveyor With Flipping System
sources.claim: Elektroteks sells the ET-LQC-FLIP, a commercial machine-controlled station on a mattress conveyor line that lifts, rotates and flips full-size mattresses so operators do not have to; the mattress is presented to the machine by the conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: flipping/rotating a full-size mattress on a factory line. Same object and same physical act (lift, rotate 180 degrees, flip) at the same weight and scale as turning a mattress in housekeeping, with the mattress presented to the machine as a purpose-built setting would present it.

sources.title: 4 cool facts about Hercules, the small-but-mighty robot in Amazon's fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Hercules drive units autonomously lift and transport inventory pods weighing up to 1,250 pounds and deliver them to fixed pick stations inside fulfillment centers, operating in robotic storage fields built around the machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving heavy, furniture-scale objects from a storage position to a designated station and back. Comparable mass and footprint to a dresser, armchair or bed, with centimetre-level placement, when the load is presented on a standardized base as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.title: pi-0.5: a VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 mobile manipulator autonomously performed long bedroom and kitchen chores - making the bed, clearing a bedroom floor, putting clothes in a laundry basket - in entirely new homes it had never seen; the demonstrated repertoire does not include moving furniture or turning mattresses.
sources.transferJustification: Closest home-tier housekeeping autonomy on record; cited to show that state-of-the-art in-home autonomy covers light bedding and object tidying, not furniture relocation or mattress turning.

sources.title: Watch A New Humanoid Robot Clean A Hotel Room Like It Owns The Place
sources.claim: Zerith H1, a wheeled humanoid built specifically for hotel housekeeping, autonomously vacuums floors, scrubs bathrooms, picks up towels and restocks amenities in hotel rooms; furniture moving and mattress handling are not among its reported capabilities.
sources.transferJustification: Same occupation and setting (hotel guest-room housekeeping); cited to show what the most advanced hotel-oriented housekeeping robot does and does not do.

tasks.label: Replace light bulbs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel/motel guest room turnover: housekeeper notices a dead bulb in a bedside, desk or floor lamp (or bathroom vanity), fetches a matching A19/LED screw-in bulb from the cart or linen closet, unscrews the spent bulb, screws in the new one, switches it on to verify, and carries the old bulb away. Standing reach, no ladder, room empty.

Hotel/commercial corridor, lobby, stairwell or elevator lobby: ceiling-mounted, recessed can, or sconce fixture that requires setting up a step ladder or using a pole changer, often removing a glass diffuser, trim ring or shade first, replacing the lamp, and refitting the cover, sometimes while guests pass by.

Private household cleaning visit: client asks the cleaner to change a bulb in a table lamp, kitchen or hall fixture. The home is taken as found — clutter on surfaces, unknown bulb type and wattage, spare bulbs stored in a drawer or closet the cleaner must find, pets or family members present.

Hospital, clinic, dormitory or office suite room cleaned by housekeeping: overbed/reading lamp, vanity or under-cabinet fixture bulb replaced during routine cleaning, sometimes with a patient or occupant in the room; standard institutional fixtures and a stocked supply room.

Specialty fixtures: chandelier or multi-arm fixture with glass shades, decorative sconces, exterior entry lights, or a ceiling troffer with a fluorescent/LED tube requiring twist-lock bi-pin removal and lens panel handling.

sources.system: UMI-FT adaptive compliance policy (robot arm with force/torque-sensing fingers)
sources.developer: Stanford University (Choi, Hou, Pan, Cutkosky, Song et al.)
sources.title: In-the-Wild Compliant Manipulation with UMI-FT (arXiv 2601.09988, ICRA 2026)
sources.claim: Stanford's UMI-FT adaptive compliance policy autonomously performs a lightbulb insertion task on a robot arm: starting with the bulb pre-grasped, it aligns bayonet pins with the socket slot, applies ~15 N to compress the spring electrode, and rotates until the light turns on, in a fixtured lab/tabletop setup with a tuned socket.
sources.transferJustification: Same object class (a real light bulb and lamp socket) and the core insertion motion of bulb replacement; it covers only the insertion sub-step with the bulb already grasped and the socket spring weakened, so it substantiates the manipulation in a purpose-built presentation, not a whole in-situ replacement.

sources.system: Robotiq Screwdriving Solution (UR cobot cell with screw feeder and force sensing)
sources.title: Screwdriving Solution | Robotiq
sources.claim: Commercially sold robotic screwdriving cells autonomously pick fasteners from a feeder and drive them into fixtured workpieces with force sensing and automatic error detection, deployable on assembly lines within weeks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: threaded fastening in a fixtured cell. Screwing a bulb base into a socket is a threaded insertion with comparable alignment tolerance and torque control, and the cell supplies the part from a feeder — exactly the E1 presentation of a replacement bulb.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic screwdriving system for high-mix manufacturing
sources.developer: Research group publishing in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing (Elsevier)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic screwdriving for high-mix manufacturing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic screwdriving systems for high-mix manufacturing detect failed insertions and autonomously retry, adjusting compliance and insertion force, in fixtured industrial workcells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous threaded insertion with failure recovery in a fixtured cell. Bulb seating and unscrewing require the same compliant rotation, torque limiting and retry behaviour; it shows the reliability layer needed for accepted-quality output at E1.

sources.system: Automated LED light bulb assembly line (multi-station special-purpose machinery)
sources.title: LED Assembly Automation in Lighting Production
sources.claim: Fully automated, purpose-built LED bulb assembly lines handle bulbs and lamp heads through dedicated stations (head rotation, riveting, power measurement) without human handling of each unit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling and mating of bulb bodies and lamp bases in purpose-built stations. It shows fragile bulb handling and base rotation are routine when the work is fixtured and presented, supporting the E1 counterfactual only.

sources.system: Soft twisting gripper on Fetch Robotics mobile manipulator
sources.developer: UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering (Tolley lab)
sources.title: This soft robotic gripper can screw in your light bulbs for you | UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering
sources.claim: A soft robotic gripper mounted on a Fetch Robotics arm was shown picking up and manipulating light bulbs, including rotating them in-hand as in screwing, in a university lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-hand rotation of a bulb. Autonomy of the demonstration is not established, so it is treated as teleoperated and does not support any positive judgment; it is listed only to show the state of lab-level bulb manipulation.

sources.developer: Northeastern University (Lipton lab), published in Science Robotics
sources.title: New hybrid robotic arm is the perfect mix of strength and flexibility
sources.claim: Northeastern's TRUNC hybrid rigid/soft arm was demonstrated inserting and screwing a lightbulb ... and turning a valve in a laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the insertion step of this task, but the demonstration's control mode (scripted/commanded vs. perception-driven autonomy) is not established, so it is treated as teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Deliver television sets, ironing boards, baby cribs, and rollaway beds to guests' rooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Guest phones for small supplies that fit in a covered bin or drawer (extra towels, toiletries, coffee pods, a phone charger, a hair dryer, an extra pillow). The attendant takes them from a floor closet or the front desk, rides the elevator, knocks and hands them over at the door of an occupied room in a mid-scale hotel.

Iron and ironing board requested by a guest: pulled from a housekeeping closet, carried (~1.3 m long, awkward) down occupied corridors and up an elevator, then handed to the guest at the door or stood in the room's closet if the guest is out.

Rollaway/folding bed: retrieved from a storage room, wheeled through back corridors and the service elevator, brought into an occupied guest room, unfolded and locked open, made up with sheets, blanket and pillow, and positioned clear of the door and walkway.

Portable crib / pack-'n-play for a family: carried or trolleyed from storage to the room, unfolded and latched, mattress pad and fitted sheet added, placed away from window cords, outlets and the heater, often with the parents present and directing placement.

Heavy equipment such as a television set on a stand, a mini-fridge, a microwave or a luggage rack moved on a cart or dolly (sometimes a two-person carry) into the guest room, set on its stand or shelf, and plugged in/connected before the guest accepts it.

sources.title: Savioke - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Relay hotel delivery robots drive autonomously from the front desk, take the elevator and deliver requested amenities to guests at their room door.

sources.title: Relay Robotics Introduces Relay2, The New High-Capacity Hotel Delivery Robot
sources.claim: Relay is a commercial hotel product with a large operational history of autonomous deliveries, indicating employer-acceptable reliability for amenity runs.

sources.title: Hospitality Robotics: Room Service and Delivery Robots
sources.claim: JEEVES autonomously travels between service loading stations and guest rooms in hotels using SLAM and elevator integration, delivering goods from drawers (payload up to 45 kg).

sources.title: TechForce Robotics Deploys TIM-E Autonomous Service Robot at Del Mar, California, Hotel
sources.claim: An autonomous hotel logistics robot moves bulky loads (linen, waste) across floors of an operating US hotel, using elevator and door integration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (back-of-house linen/waste transport): shows autonomous multi-floor conveyance of bulky hotel loads, but it is not shown retrieving an item and delivering it to an individual guest room door, so it does not by itself substantiate guest-facing bulky delivery.

sources.system: MiR AMRs with Interroll conveyor top module
sources.title: Boosting Flexibility with MiR Robots and Interroll's Conveyor Solution
sources.claim: Industrial AMRs autonomously collect loads presented by fixtured line-side conveyors and transfer them at stationary conveyor stations on a factory floor, without manual loading or unloading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (intralogistics transport): the delivery instance in its E1 form is point-to-point conveyance of an item presented fixtured to the machine and released at a fixtured station - comparable object size and precision, in a purpose-built robot floor.

sources.title: Amazon uses robots that sort, lift, and carry packages—see them in action
sources.claim: Amazon drive units autonomously fetch heavy shelving pods and bring them to workstations where a person removes the item, on a robot-only floor field.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (goods-to-person transport): substantiates that in a purpose-built, machine-structured setting an autonomous vehicle brings a bulky fixtured load to a delivery point where the recipient takes the item off - the E1 form of an item delivery.

sources.title: Hotel Tech-in: The 'cobots' that carry guest luggage
sources.claim: The hotel cobot marketed for carrying bulky guest items follows an accompanying staff member rather than operating autonomously, and operators note bulky requests such as a rollaway bed still require a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (carrying guest luggage and amenities in hotels): the closest system for bulky guest-item transport is human-following, not autonomous, so it cannot substantiate unattended bulky delivery.

sources.title: Two Autonomous Humanoid Robots Seamlessly Work Together to Make the Bed
sources.claim: Two humanoids autonomously reset a staged bedroom, including making a bed ..., in a company demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (in-room bedding manipulation): shows autonomous bed-making, but it is a staged single demo that omits retrieving a folded rollaway or crib from storage, multi-floor transport, and unfolding and latching a frame, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

tasks.label: Hang draperies and dust window blinds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel/motel guest room during turnover or periodic deep clean: housekeeper dusts the window blind slats and sheer panels with a microfiber cloth or duster, wipes the sill, and straightens/re-hangs the drapery panel on its traverse rod if a hook has slipped. Furniture (desk, chair, AC unit) sits in front of the window; layout is standardized across rooms.

Private home cleaning visit: dust venetian, mini, wood or faux-wood blinds and shutters in several rooms using a duster or slat tool, tilting slats to reach both faces, working around plants, framed photos, furniture pushed to the window, pets and clutter; window heights and blind types differ house to house.

Office, hospital patient room, school or clinic on a periodic schedule: dust dozens of identical horizontal blinds along a corridor of rooms, sometimes on a step stool, while occupants, beds and equipment remain in place; institution sets the cleaning standard and inspects.

Hotel or institutional room: re-hang laundered or newly replaced drapery/sheer panels — carrying the panel up a ladder, seating a dozen pin hooks into the rod carriers or rings, evening the pleats and checking the panel hangs plumb and closes fully.

Private home: take curtains down off the rod for washing, then re-hang them — threading rod pockets or clipping rings, re-mounting the rod on brackets if needed, dressing the folds — on windows of differing heights and hardware.

sources.system: ABB FeatherDuster (IRC5-controlled painting robot with rotating feather/vacuum tool)
sources.title: FeatherDuster | ABB
sources.claim: ABB's FeatherDuster is a commercial robotic dust-removal system: a standard ABB robot carries a rotating feather-and-vacuum tool that follows the contours of car bodies moving on a conveyor in a paint line, removing loose dust to the quality standard required before painting; it is programmed offline and runs the cleaning cycle without an operator in the loop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-paint dust removal from a workpiece. It is dusting with a soft feather tool over a surface, executed to an inspected cleanliness standard, in a purpose-built cell where the workpiece is presented in a known pose by a conveyor. Under the E1 counterfactual (blind fixtured and presented to the machine), the same tool class, force regime and path-following carry over to wiping dust off blind slats; it does not carry over to finding and dusting blinds in an occupied room.

sources.system: Dürr EcoClean / EcoRS Clean F feather-roller cleaning robots
sources.date: 2024-05-24 (Audi Ingolstadt announcement); EcoClean product line in use worldwide
sources.title: 18,000th Dürr robot will paint vehicles in Ingolstadt - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr's EcoClean feather-duster cleaning systems and EcoRS Clean F feather-roller robots are installed in automotive paint shops worldwide, including a new Audi Ingolstadt topcoat line, where robots clean dust and dirt particles off car bodies before painting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic feather-roller dusting of a conveyed workpiece in a fenced booth. It substantiates that dust removal by soft rotating dusters under robot control is a deployed, production-quality capability in purpose-built cells — the E1 counterfactual for dusting a blind presented to the machine.

sources.system: Best Technology ultrasonic window blind cleaning tanks (wash/rinse line)
sources.title: Ultrasonic Window Blind Cleaner - Ultrasonic Blind Cleaning Machines & Equipment
sources.claim: Ultrasonic blind-cleaning machines are commercial equipment used by house/office cleaning and restoration companies: window blinds are taken to the machine, which micro-scrubs both faces of every slat on a timed, temperature-controlled cycle in about five minutes, versus 1-2 hours of hand scrubbing.
sources.transferJustification: Same object, same purpose (getting dust and grime off blind slats), with the work brought to a machine and run under machine control — the literal E1 form of 'dust window blinds'. It is not a manipulator, so it is cited as corroboration alongside the FeatherDuster robot rather than on its own.

sources.title: Zerith H1: China's humanoid robot cleans and restocks hotel rooms
sources.claim: Zerith H1 is a hotel-grade housekeeping humanoid shown autonomously vacuuming guest-room floors, cleaning showers, toilets and sinks and restocking amenities, and reported operating in commercial indoor facilities; its published task repertoire does not include dusting window blinds or hanging draperies.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to establish the actual scope of autonomous housekeeping in a structured hotel room (E2): floors, bathroom fixtures, amenity restocking. Window-treatment dusting and drapery hanging are absent, so it does not substantiate this task at E2.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom cleaning robots operate autonomously in hospitals and airports, cleaning fixtures and floors and picking up trash during normal facility operations after a one-time VR mapping setup; their scope is restroom fixtures and floors, not window treatments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous surface cleaning inside a structured human facility (E2). It shows what facility-grade cleaning autonomy covers today — spraying/wiping fixed rigid fixtures and floors — and does not extend to compliant hanging slats or drapery hardware.

sources.title: Figure's Humanoid Robot Picks Up Toys, Wipes Surfaces in New Demo
sources.claim: Figure's Helix 02 demos show a Figure 03 humanoid autonomously tidying ... and a bedroom, including picking up objects and wiping flat surfaces with a cloth, from onboard sensing with no human intervention; no window-blind dusting or drapery hanging is shown.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous home tidying and wiping of flat, rigid surfaces. Wiping a table does not transfer to dusting hanging blind slats (compliant, must be supported and tilted, both faces) or to seating drapery pin hooks in rod carriers, so it does not substantiate this task at E3.

tasks.label: Prepare rooms for meetings and arrange decorations, media equipment, and furniture for social or business functions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel/conference-center ballroom banquet setup per a banquet event order: wheel 6-ft round tables in on dollies, unfold and position them to a diagram, drape floor-length linens, set 8-10 chairs per table, place centerpieces, water and place settings, position podium/riser and head table; time-boxed between events, other staff moving through the room.

Small meeting/boardroom setup in a hotel or corporate office: rearrange existing tables and stackable chairs into a U-shape, classroom or hollow-square layout, set out pads, pens, water pitchers and glasses, wipe surfaces, put out a flip chart, pull down the screen and position/connect the projector or display and test the cable/remote.

Post-function breakdown and reset: strip and bag soiled linens, clear centerpieces, glassware and trash, stack chairs on dollies, fold and stow banquet tables in the storage closet, vacuum and reset the room to the next event's layout.

Decorating a function room for a social event (wedding reception, holiday party, awards banquet) in a hotel, banquet hall, school or church facility: hang banners and streamers, clip table skirting, arrange centerpieces, candles, signage and place cards per client instructions, set gift/registration tables.

Private household or small residence-scale venue: housekeeper prepares the living/dining room for a dinner party or family gathering—move sofas and chairs to open space, extend and set the dining table with cloth, china and glassware, put out flowers and decorations amid the household's own clutter and pets.

sources.title: Helix 02 Bedroom Tidy
sources.claim: Two Figure humanoids running the Helix-02 vision-language-action policy autonomously reset a staged bedroom, including tidying objects, taking out trash, pushing a ... jointly making a bed — the closest demonstrated analogue to room preparation, but limited to a home mock-up and to light objects, with no table/linen/AV work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = resetting/tidying a room. It shares the setting type (a furnished room) and includes repositioning a chair, so it is the nearest evidence for arranging furniture; it does not cover banquet tables, linens, decorations or media equipment.

sources.system: ALORE (Unitree B2 quadruped with Z1 arm)
sources.developer: HKUST research group (Bi, Zhang, Chen, Zhao, Li, Ma)
sources.title: ALORE: Autonomous Large-Object Rearrangement with a Legged Manipulator
sources.claim: A legged manipulator (Unitree B2 + Z1) autonomously repositioned large objects including chairs to assigned targets in real indoor spaces, rearranging 32 chairs in 8 continuous loops over ~40 minutes without failure — a research demonstration of autonomous furniture-scale rearrangement only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = large-object (chair/furniture) rearrangement to target positions. Comparable objects (chairs) and indoor institutional floors, so it bears on the furniture-moving element of room setup; it does not demonstrate table unfolding, linens, place settings, decorations or AV hookup.

sources.title: Intelligent Parking Chair | HAKUHODO
sources.claim: Nissan's Intelligent Parking Chair returns office chairs to preset positions automatically using motorized rollers and ceiling-mounted cameras — furniture repositioning achieved only by building the room around the machine (instrumented chairs plus overhead tracking), and limited to returning chairs to fixed marks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = returning meeting-room chairs to a defined layout. Same objects and setting (office meeting rooms), so it is the best evidence for the E1 counterfactual; it covers only chair repositioning to preset marks, not table layout changes, supplies or media equipment.

sources.title: kachaka Preferred Robotics
sources.claim: Commercially available furniture-moving robots for homes/offices move only dedicated shelves and carts up to 20 kg, showing that deployed furniture automation is confined to purpose-matched furniture rather than arbitrary banquet tables and stacked chairs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = moving furniture within rooms. Same environment class (homes/offices) but restricted to proprietary shelving on a tow base, so it cannot substantiate arranging event tables, chairs, linens or decor.

sources.title: Hotel Cleaning Robot | SoftBank Robotics America
sources.claim: Robots actually deployed in US hotels for housekeeping work are autonomous floor scrubbers/vacuums; hotel operators describe staff being freed to perform banquet-room setup themselves, indicating room-setup work is not automated in deployed hospitality robotics.
sources.transferJustification: Same occupation and setting (hotel housekeeping). Shows the deployed robot's scope is vacuuming, with humans retained for banquet-room setup — evidence about the boundary of current hospitality automation.

sources.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: A generalist manipulation policy (π0.5) autonomously performs multi-step tidying such as putting items away and placing dishes in the sink in homes not seen in training, but demonstrated behaviors are small-object pick-and-place, not furniture arrangement, table dressing or decorating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = long-horizon household tidying in unseen homes. Same environment (private homes) and object scale (dishes, small items) as home party prep, so it bounds what is achievable there; it shows no furniture moving, table setting to standard, or decorating.

tasks.label: Polish silver accessories and metalwork, such as fixtures and fittings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel guestroom bathroom during room turnover: housekeeper wipes and buffs chrome faucets, showerhead, drain, towel bars and mirror frame dry with a cloth to remove water spots and streaks, leaving a spot-free shine; varied fixture geometry, tight spaces around the basin and tub.

Hotel/commercial public areas on a scheduled polish: brass or bronze handrails, elevator door frames and cab panels, kick plates, door hardware and lobby metalwork treated with metal polish or stainless cleaner and buffed by hand while the space stays open to guests.

Private household: hand-polishing sterling or silver-plated flatware, tea service, candlesticks, trays and other silver accessories with silver polish, soft cloths and detail work around chased ornament and weighted bases, then rinsing/drying and returning items to storage.

Private household: polishing installed metalwork — brass door handles and knockers, cabinet hardware, stainless kitchen appliance fronts, bathroom fittings — with appropriate polish, avoiding damage to lacquered or antique finishes.

Institutional/commercial back-of-house (hospital, office building, banquet operation): polishing stainless kick plates, elevator panels, drinking fountains and handrails, plus banquet silver holloware and flatware before service.

sources.system: AM Machinery / Loeser-type robotic polishing and belt-grinding cell
sources.developer: AM Machinery Sales (integrator, supplier of robotic finishing cells)
sources.title: Robotic Cell | Metal Polishing Machinery and machines for metal finishing
sources.claim: Commercial robotic finishing cells perform deburring, belt-grinding and polishing of exactly the class of objects named in the task — water fittings (faucets) and door handles — running unattended for hours once parts are loaded in the cell's magazine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is production/refinishing polishing of the same physical objects the housekeeper polishes (faucet bodies, door handles, fittings); the objects, the abrasive/buff media and the required mirror or brushed finish are the same, only the workpiece is presented fixtured rather than installed.

sources.system: PushCorp force-controlled robotic polishing / FinishX cell
sources.title: Robotic Polishing & Polishing Automation Applications - PushCorp
sources.claim: Force-controlled robotic polishing tooling is sold and deployed commercially to bring stainless steel and aluminium parts to consistent brushed or mirror finishes, with the robot holding uniform force and speed over contoured surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical operation (compliant buffing/polishing of metal to a specified lustre) on the same materials as architectural and bathroom metalwork; transfers when the workpiece is fixtured in the cell.

sources.system: Robotic abrasive belt polishing/buffing work cell (industrial finishing systems)
sources.developer: Industrial finishing integrators reported by Products Finishing
sources.title: Advancements in Automated Polishing, Buffing and Deburring | Products Finishing
sources.claim: Robotic work cells buff stainless hardware families to a mirror finish, with parts fixtured on queuing trays that an operator loads without stopping the robot; described applications include lock and plumbing hardware and aluminium building extrusions.
sources.transferJustification: Lock and plumbing hardware and building extrusions are the fixtures, fittings and architectural metalwork the housekeeping task polishes; the finish target (mirror) equals or exceeds hand-polished housekeeping quality.

sources.system: Roboticom robotic finishing systems for sanitary ware
sources.title: Roboticom Solutions for the Sanitary Ware Industry: robots for perfect surfaces finishing
sources.claim: Robots are used in the sanitary-ware industry for surface finishing (sanding and polishing) of taps and sanitary fittings.
sources.transferJustification: Sanitary-ware finishing covers the faucets, showerheads and bath fittings that a housekeeper polishes; identical objects and finish requirement with the part fixtured in a robot cell.

sources.title: 7 Companies That Are Using Polishing and Buffing Robots
sources.claim: A tableware and cookware manufacturer has used robotic polishing in production for over a decade to buff metal tableware components to a consumer-facing shine.
sources.transferJustification: Buffing tableware metal (holloware-like stainless pieces) to a bright finish is the same operation as polishing silver holloware/serving pieces once the item is presented to the buffing head.

sources.system: Sammic SAS cutlery dryer/polisher (granulate polishing machine)
sources.title: Cutlery dryers & polishers | Sammic US
sources.claim: Purpose-built commercial machines widely used in hotels and restaurants dry and polish silverware/flatware after washing, removing spotting at up to thousands of pieces per hour, with the operator only loading and unloading.
sources.transferJustification: This is the task itself (polishing silver flatware) performed by a machine-controlled device with the work brought to it — the E1 presentation of the household/banquet silver-polishing instance.

sources.title: Burnishing Machine - 160 | Burnishing Silver Equipment | The Swartz Group
sources.claim: Burnishing machines built for hotels' and country clubs' ... holloware are sold and used to restore shine and remove tarnish from silver serving pieces.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the silver-polishing instance, executed by a machine that the work is brought to; covers holloware (trays, tea services) as well as flatware.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile cleaning robot deployed in hospitals and airports cleans restroom fixtures and floors, but its cleaning is a touchless spray-and-extract cycle covering toilets, urinals, floors and trash — not polishing or buffing metalwork to a shine.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the in-situ case: the most mature facility cleaning manipulator lists toilets, urinals, floors, doors and trash, with touchless cleaning, so it does not substantiate buffing installed chrome or brass to a polished finish.

tasks.label: Clean work site after completion of job.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential interior general pest service in an occupied home: after treating kitchen, bath, garage and baseboards, the tech wipes up spray drips and residue from counters/floors, sweeps or vacuums dead insects and dust, collects empty bait tubes, packaging and spent glue boards, picks up the drop cloth and hand tools, puts moved items back, and carries waste to the truck. Cluttered rooms, pets and children present.

Commercial/institutional open-area account (warehouse, grocery, school, office, hospital): after perimeter spraying, baiting or rodent-station service, sweep/vacuum dead insects, dust and stray product from floors and wall lines, wipe treated surfaces, bag spent monitors and packaging, and leave the area presentable before the facility opens.

Food-service or food-plant back-of-house (restaurant kitchen, bakery, processing plant): after treatment, rinse or wipe down floors, drains and equipment exteriors that could have contacted product, sweep dead roaches and debris out from under/behind equipment, remove and bag used glue boards, and confirm no residue remains on food-contact surfaces.

Exterior/perimeter and termite job at a residence: backfill and tamp the treatment trench, patch drilled patio/slab holes, sweep or hose spilled granules, foam or dust off driveway, walkway and siding, coil hoses, collect flags, signage and empty packaging, and load equipment onto the truck. Uneven ground, landscaping, weather.

Rodent or wildlife sanitation cleanup in an attic, crawlspace, garage or dumpster corral: remove carcasses and nesting material, HEPA-vacuum droppings and soiled insulation, disinfect surfaces, double-bag as biohazard, and haul it out through tight, dark, low-clearance access.

End-of-day decontamination at the company shop/yard: flush and rinse sprayer tanks, hoses and dusters, wash out spill trays and the truck bed, triple-rinse and dispose of empty pesticide containers, and secure rinsate and waste per label requirements.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR is an autonomous mobile-manipulator cleaning robot deployed in hospital and airport restrooms; it cleans fixtures and floors, opens doors and picks up trash with almost no staff intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous end-of-shift restroom cleaning in an institutional building. It transfers to post-treatment site cleanup in a facility because the objects (loose trash and packaging, soiled floors, wipeable fixtures/surfaces) and required precision are comparable, and it is performed in the same class of structured, institution-controlled premises.

sources.title: Peanut Robotics | Home
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics fields a commercially deployed mobile manipulator that autonomously navigates and cleans hotel and commercial-building bathrooms, wiping surfaces with cloths after learning the space.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wipe-down cleaning of fixtures and surfaces in hotel/office restrooms. Transfers to wiping product residue and soiled surfaces after a pest treatment: same surface-wiping manipulation with cloths/tools, same mapped human-work facility environment.

sources.title: Pudu Robotics Launches its Latest AI-Powered Autonomous Cleaning Robot - PUDU CC1 Pro
sources.claim: Pudu's CC1 / CC1 Pro is a commercially sold autonomous 4-in-1 cleaning robot (sweep, scrub, vacuum, mop) deployed in retail, hotel and restaurant floors, with AI detection of stains and automatic spot re-cleaning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous floor sweeping/vacuuming/mopping in commercial premises. Transfers to removing dead insects, dust and stray granules from floors after a treatment: same debris scale, same floor surfaces, same institution-controlled interior.

sources.title: Avidbots releases floor-scrubbing robot for industrial spaces - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo 2 autonomous floor scrubber is deployed in over a thousand units worldwide cleaning airports, schools, warehouses and manufacturing floors without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended floor cleaning of large commercial/industrial floors. Transfers to the floor portion of post-treatment cleanup in warehouses, groceries and institutions — same surfaces, same debris, same premises class.

sources.title: Rosie™ by CleanBotix | Robotic Sanitation for Food Plants
sources.claim: CleanBotix's Rosie is an autonomous mobile manipulator (6-DOF arm, wheeled base, precision spray) that performs rinse-foam-rinse-sanitize washdown of food and beverage plant areas, and has been run in a live poultry hatchery production environment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nightly sanitation washdown of food-plant floors, drains and equipment exteriors. Transfers to cleaning a food facility work site after a pest treatment: identical surfaces and soils, same hygiene acceptance standard (ATP/residue), same structured facility.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics Unveils Moxi 2.0 — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators operate autonomously in hospitals, completing over 1.25 million fetch-and-deliver runs including picking up and transporting items through corridors and elevators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grasp-and-transport of supplies and soiled items through an occupied facility. Supports the haul-away component of site cleanup (bagged waste, spent monitors) in a structured facility.

sources.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization (arXiv:2504.16054)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 model let a mobile manipulator perform multi-step cleaning of kitchens and bedrooms in real homes never seen in training, though success is partial and it remains a research demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying/cleaning in unseen homes. Cited to bound the home (E3) case: it is a research demo with partial success rates, not employer-acceptable cleanup, and does not cover residue wiping, tool retrieval or hazardous-waste handling.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The 1X NEO home humanoid relies on teleoperation for household chores; no humanoid has been shown completing a household chore end to end autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household chores including tidying and cleaning. Cited as a negative bound for home (E3) cleanup: the leading consumer system runs under human teleoperation.

sources.title: Robotic solutions for washing-cleaning parts | Stäubli United States
sources.claim: Sealed industrial washing robots run automated high-pressure wash and chemical cleaning cycles on workpieces inside enclosed wash cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pressure/chemical washing of fixtured equipment in a fenced cell. Transfers to rinsing and decontaminating pest-control spray equipment, trays and containers when brought to a purpose-built wash station (same water/chemical jets, same fixtured presentation).

sources.title: Fives | RoboWash™ Robotic Industrial Parts Washer
sources.claim: Fives' RoboWash is a robotic ... parts washer that combines pre-wash, high-pressure wash and drying with fully automated part manipulation by a 6-axis robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated washing of complex parts presented to a fixed robotic cell. Transfers to shop-based decontamination of tanks, hoses and trays presented on fixtures at E1.

tasks.label: Measure area dimensions requiring treatment, calculate fumigant requirements, and estimate cost for service.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Structural (tent) fumigation estimate at an occupied single-family home: walk the property, measure the exterior footprint with a wheel/tape, take wall and peak heights, compute total cubic feet, apply Fumiguide dosage tables (pest, temperature, half-loss time) and price the job.

Termite/general-pest quote inside a cluttered occupied home: measure room dimensions, linear feet of foundation/sill, crawlspace and attic areas, convert to gallons of termiticide or bait stations, and write the estimate.

Commercial/institutional account (warehouse, restaurant, food plant, apartment common areas): measure floor areas and enclosed volumes of a facility with a fixed layout, compute product quantity and quote a service price.

Commodity/space fumigation at a grain elevator, flour mill, railcar or shipping container: determine the enclosed volume of bins/silos/chambers, calculate phosphine or sulfuryl fluoride dose and exposure, and cost the job.

Outdoor turf/landscape/perimeter measurement at a residential yard or small commercial lot: measure treatable lawn square footage and building perimeter, calculate granular/liquid product needed and quote the price.

sources.title: EagleView and Skydio Announce General Availability of Virtual Claims Inspection Solution
sources.claim: Skydio House Scan flies autonomous adaptive scans of residential properties; combined with EagleView's automated measurement workflow it delivers precise property measurements used by adjusters to build estimates. Commercially available since October 2021.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous dimensional capture of a house exterior for an insurance repair estimate. Transfers to fumigation measurement because the same exterior envelope dimensions (footprint, wall/peak heights) are what a fumigator measures to compute cubic footage, at comparable or looser precision.

sources.title: Skydio, EagleView announce huge drone inspection partnership
sources.claim: The Skydio/EagleView residential property capture is automated end to end apart from the operator drawing an initial boundary polygon around the home.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the residential structure scan runs without step-by-step piloting, i.e. limited intervention rather than continuous teleoperation.

sources.system: DroneDeploy Roof Report / automated mapping flights
sources.title: Roof Report – DroneDeploy
sources.claim: DroneDeploy generates roof/structure measurement reports from automated drone flights over residential and commercial buildings, with quoted measurement accuracy of 99.4% when recommended flight practices are followed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated area/edge measurement of building envelopes from autonomous flight. Precision far exceeds what fumigant cubic-footage or perimeter-linear-foot calculations require.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Leica BLK ARC (Orbit/Autowalk)
sources.title: Leica BLK ARC now the first certified reality capture device available for Boston Dynamics' Spot®
sources.claim: Leica BLK ARC mounted on Boston ... Spot performs laser-scanning missions launched from the Spot app that run without human intervention, capturing site conditions in plants, warehouses ... for as-built/BIM measurement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous interior reality capture of industrial buildings. The resulting point cloud yields room dimensions, floor areas and enclosed volumes — the exact inputs a pest-control estimator measures by tape inside a facility.

sources.title: Emesent enables fully autonomous exploration and mapping of GPS-denied environments
sources.claim: Emesent's Hovermap with Cortex 4.0 performs fully autonomous exploration and mapping of unknown GPS-denied spaces: the operator designates a bounding volume and the drone maps it completely and returns, producing survey point clouds used for volumetric measurement of silos, stockpiles and enclosed industrial spaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous volumetric survey of unmapped enclosed spaces. Determining the cubic volume of a bin, silo or warehouse bay is the measurement step of commodity fumigation dosing.

sources.title: Exyn Brings Level 4 Autonomy to Drones - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Exyn's lidar drones operate at Level 4 autonomy, exploring complex GPS-denied spaces beyond visual line of sight with no pilot in the loop, and are marketed and used for accurate stockpile/volume measurement in mines and industrial facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous volumetric mapping without a prior map, i.e. a first-visit measurement job. Supplies the enclosed-volume figure needed for fumigant dosing in bins, mills and warehouses.

sources.system: Drone photogrammetry stockpile/area survey workflow (pre-planned autonomous flight)
sources.title: A Guide to Stockpile Measurements Using a Drone | Full View
sources.claim: Drone stockpile surveys are flown along autonomously executed pre-planned paths and the imagery is processed into size, area and volume measurements — the standard workflow for outdoor area/volume quantification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial measurement of outdoor areas/volumes. Measuring treatable turf square footage or a building perimeter on a lot is the same photogrammetric area measurement at lower required precision.

sources.date: long-standing; described in current industry material (2021-2024)
sources.title: Structural Fumigation with ProFume®
sources.claim: The fumigant-quantity calculation step is already performed by dedicated software: the Fumiguide calculator computes target concentration and total fumigant required from volume, temperature, half-loss time and target pest.
sources.transferJustification: Software, not a robot: cited only to show the non-physical calculation sub-step of this task is fully automated once dimensions exist, so the environment question turns on the measurement step.

sources.title: #1 Lawn & Landscape Estimating Software | RealGreen
sources.claim: Industry estimating software converts measured property areas directly into priced quotes, generating estimates without a site visit.
sources.transferJustification: Software, not a robot: cited only for the cost-estimation sub-step, showing that once dimensions are captured the pricing output is produced automatically at commercial quality.

tasks.label: Spray or dust chemical solutions, powders, or gases into rooms, onto clothing, furnishings, or wood, or over marshlands, ditches, or catch basins.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine interior treatment of an occupied single-family home or apartment: technician inspects, then applies liquid residual with a B&G-style wand to baseboards, cracks and crevices, under sinks, behind/under appliances, and puffs dust into wall voids and electrical boxes; clutter, pets, children, furniture and varied layouts; must avoid over-spray on food surfaces and comply with label site restrictions.

Exterior perimeter and yard treatment at a home or small business: walking the structure with a power sprayer/backpack mist blower applying a 2-3 ft residual band at the foundation and up the wall, treating door and window frames, weep holes, eaves and soffits (de-webbing), shrubs and turf harborage, or a mosquito barrier mist over foliage; uneven terrain, fences, gates, pets, parked cars, weather.

Scheduled service of a commercial/institutional interior (restaurant kitchen, grocery, warehouse, food plant, school, hospital, apartment common areas): inspection plus targeted crack-and-crevice liquid/aerosol application along equipment bases, drains, dock doors and wall-floor junctions, void dusting, sometimes after-hours ULV/space fogging of an emptied room; strict label restrictions in food-handling areas.

Wood-destroying organism work: spraying/foaming borate or termiticide onto framing, sill plates and subfloor in crawl spaces and attics, drilling and injecting into wood or block voids, trenching and rodding soil around a foundation, or pretreating a new-construction slab and framing; tight, dark, dirty, obstructed spaces and active job sites.

Urban ground-based mosquito/vector work: night-time truck-mounted ULV adulticide runs along residential street routes, and daytime catch-basin larviciding where the worker locates each storm drain, lifts or dispenses through the grate, and doses briquettes/liquid; traffic, parked cars, pedestrians, variable basin condition.

Broad-area larviciding of standing-water habitat: applying Bti/IGR liquid, granules or tablets over salt marsh, wetlands, roadside ditches, retention ponds, flooded fields and other breeding sites, much of it remote, boggy or otherwise inaccessible on foot; treated at label rate over mapped acreage.

sources.system: MMCD larvicide application drone program (Hylio/DJI-class spray UAS)
sources.title: How MMCD Uses Drones for Mosquito Control to Save Time and Improve Safety
sources.claim: Metropolitan Mosquito Control District (Minneapolis-St. Paul) operationally uses larvicide-carrying drones over wetland breeding sites; the aircraft fly pre-programmed routes with programmed boundaries and the software determines the amount of larvicide needed, with the human only launching and monitoring.

sources.system: Autonomous unmanned aircraft system for mosquito control (Williams et al.)
