sources.title: The development of autonomous unmanned aircraft systems for mosquito control (PLOS ONE)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed study documents an autonomous multirotor UAS built for mosquito control that flies programmed missions and applies larvicide spray, larvicide tablets, granules and adulticide at rates prescribed for conventional aircraft, with greater precision than manned aircraft.

sources.developer: Leading Edge Aerial Technologies / Central UAS Technologies (operator: Collier MCD)
sources.title: Drones: A Valuable Tool in CMCD's Fight Against Mosquitoes
sources.claim: Collier Mosquito Control District (Florida) operates PrecisionVision 40X treatment drones carrying up to 40 lb of Bti larvicide and has treated more than 1,000 acres ..., including oddly shaped, obstacle-filled sites.

sources.system: South Walton Mosquito District UAS treatment fleet (40-lb payload spray/spread drone plus Skydio X10 mapping)
sources.title: Drones Over the Swamp: How South Walton Is Reinventing Mosquito Control
sources.claim: South Walton Mosquito District's drone program treated 2,521 acres with 21,500 pounds of product in 2025, nearly double 2024, over swamp and other drone-accessible breeding sites in the Florida Panhandle.

sources.system: PrecisionVision 35 larvicide drone (Santa Clara County Vector Control District)
sources.developer: Leading Edge Aerial Technologies (operator: Santa Clara County VCD)
sources.title: Drones Are the Latest Weapon in the Battle to Control Mosquitos
sources.claim: Santa Clara County Vector Control uses drones to spray larvicide over marshlands and other uninhabited, non-residential areas that cannot be reached on foot, replacing helicopter application; drones are not used over residential neighborhoods.

sources.system: UAS in mosquito and vector control (sector-wide)
sources.title: Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) in Mosquito and Vector Control — AMCA Position Paper
sources.claim: Drone-based pesticide application is now mainstream in US mosquito control: a 2023 AMCA member survey found 56% of respondents already using drones, most commonly for larvicide application in rural areas.

sources.developer: Build With Robots / Fetch Robotics / City of Albuquerque
sources.title: Breezy One from Fetch Robotics, Build with Robots disinfects airport
sources.claim: Four Breezy One autonomous mobile robots sprayed a chemical disinfectant through the Albuquerque International Sunport airport every night, decontaminating spaces over 100,000 sq ft in about 1.5 hours without a human operator in the space.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous dispersal of a chemical (disinfectant) mist through the rooms and concourses of a building. It shows navigation and whole-space chemical application in a structured facility, but only broadcast space treatment — no inspection-driven, targeted application to baseboards, cracks, crevices or wall voids as pest treatment requires.

sources.title: Octopus Robots Poultry Safe robot — WATTPoultry Buyers Guide
sources.claim: The Octopus Poultry Safe robot autonomously works inside poultry houses, turning litter and applying a biocide ... so the building is sanitized without direct human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of a biocidal chemical mist throughout the interior of a livestock building. Comparable chemical handling and indoor navigation, but it is an untargeted whole-house nebulisation in an emptied, standardized barn, not the targeted structural pest application at issue.

tasks.label: Recommend treatment and prevention methods for pest problems to clients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Inspect premises to identify infestation source and extent of damage to property, wall, or roof porosity and access to infested locations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine/initial residential service call at a single-family home: technician walks the interior (kitchen and bath cabinets, under sinks, behind and under appliances, pantry, garage, utility closet) and the exterior perimeter, moving stored boxes and pulling appliances as needed, using flashlight and mirror to find droppings, frass, rub marks, grease trails, nests and harborage; traces the infestation to its source and notes cracks, gaps around pipe penetrations, door sweeps and vents that give pests entry. Cluttered, occupied, pets and children present; layout differs at every address.

Rodent or wildlife (squirrel, raccoon, bat) complaint requiring inspection of attic, crawlspace or subarea: technician opens an access hatch or vent screen, crawls through low headroom over joists, insulation, ducts and wiring in the dark, identifies gnawed wire, soiled insulation, latrine areas and nests, judges extent of damage, and traces roofline/soffit/gable-vent gaps and foundation vents used as access. Dust, spiders, standing water, unknown structural condition.

Termite / wood-destroying-organism inspection of a house (annual renewal or real-estate transaction report): sound and probe sill plates, joists, studs and trim with a screwdriver or awl, look for mud tubes on foundation walls and piers, swarmer wings, blistered paint and moisture staining; check eaves, fascia and roof leaks; quantify the extent of damage and identify conducive conditions and entry routes. Legally reportable output.

Commercial food-handling account (restaurant kitchen, grocery back room, food plant, distribution warehouse): inspect equipment voids and motor housings, floor drains, under and behind shelving and pallet racking, dock doors and door seals, ceiling voids and dry storage; check existing monitors and glue boards, judge sanitation and structural gaps, and pinpoint harborage and the source of the activity. Institution-controlled premises, fixed layout, kept to a sanitation standard, work often done off-hours.

Bed bug or cockroach inspection in multi-family housing or a hotel: unit-by-unit examination of mattress seams, box springs, headboards, furniture joints, baseboards, outlet plates and adjoining units; lift and dismantle furniture, determine extent of spread and the likely introduction route between units. Occupied, heavily furnished rooms with tenant belongings.

tasks.label: Drive truck equipped with power spraying equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential route driving: technician drives a light service truck or van fitted with a tank, pump and power spray reel from the branch office to 8-15 suburban homes per day on public streets, parking at the curb or in a driveway at each stop, in ordinary daytime traffic and fair weather.

Commercial/urban account driving: driving the spray truck through dense city traffic to restaurants, apartment complexes, warehouses and offices; navigating one-way streets, alleys, loading zones and parking lots or structures, with frequent stops and tight parking.

Highway and rural runs with a heavy rig: driving a truck carrying a 300-1,000 gal tank and high-pressure spray unit at highway speeds between towns and service areas (termite pre-treats, agricultural/commercial accounts), including rain, night runs, and final access over unpaved farm lanes, ranch tracks or construction-site ground.

Vector-control ULV fogging: driving a truck-mounted ULV fogger at roughly 10 mph along prescribed neighborhood/municipal routes at dusk or at night while the sprayer applies adulticide, tracking the route by GPS and staying out of designated no-spray zones.

Yard and depot maneuvering: positioning and backing the spray truck at the company branch yard or a customer facility's service yard - to the fill/rinse station, the chemical shed, and its parking slot - among other trucks and staff on institution-controlled premises.

Adverse winter conditions: driving the spray truck on snow-covered, slushy or icy public streets and highways in northern service territories, or through severe storms and flooded streets, to reach scheduled accounts.

tasks.label: Direct, or assist other workers in, treatment or extermination processes to eliminate or control rodents, insects, or weeds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential general-pest service run by a lead technician with a helper: walk the house, direct the helper on where to set snap traps and rodent bait stations, apply crack-and-crevice bait/aerosol in kitchen, baths, garage and behind appliances, spray a perimeter band and eaves, de-web, and explain the work to the homeowner. Furniture, clutter, pets and occupants present; every house differs.

Routine commercial/institutional account serviced by two workers: restaurant kitchen, grocery back room, food plant or hospital. Lead directs the helper on checking and rebaiting exterior/interior rodent stations, changing glue boards and insect monitors, treating under and behind equipment, pulling floor drains, plus documentation for audit. Layout fixed but cluttered with stock and equipment; some areas occupied.

Whole-space treatment of a large empty commercial facility after hours: two-person crew posts signage, seals the area, ULV fogs or mists an evacuated warehouse, storage building, food-plant room or vacant tenant space to knock down flying/crawling insects, then ventilates and clears the space for reopening.

Termite or fumigation crew job at a house or small building: lead directs helpers to trench and rod the foundation, drill slab and patio, inject termiticide, treat a crawlspace or attic, or tarp and seal a structure for fumigation and monitor clearance. Heavy hoses, drills, ladders, tarps; confined and uneven access.

Outdoor vegetation/weed control crew at commercial, industrial and residential accounts: lead assigns areas and directs backpack/hose spraying of herbicide on turf, gravel yards and fence lines, along building perimeters, in landscape beds and pavement cracks, working around parked vehicles, curbs, signage and passers-by.

Mosquito/vector control crew operations: supervisor directs technicians treating catch basins, ditches, retention ponds, marshes and abandoned pools with larvicide briquettes and backpack sprayers, and running truck-mounted ULV adulticiding routes through neighborhoods at dusk.

sources.system: BreezyOne (Build With Robots / Fetch Robotics AMR)
sources.developer: Build With Robots with Fetch Robotics
sources.title: BreezyOne deploys a fleet of disinfection robots at Houston airports - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: BreezyOne, an aerosol chemical-dispensing autonomous mobile robot on a Fetch Robotics base, is deployed in fleets at Houston's Bush Intercontinental and Hobby airports and in warehouses, running programmed routes overnight in unoccupied space and fogging a fine mist that coats surfaces, at 150,000 sq ft per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous whole-space aerosol disinfection of a large facility. It transfers to ULV/fog space treatment for insects because the operation is identical in kind - a mobile robot navigating a mapped, evacuated human work facility while a fogger disperses a chemical to cover the whole space - with the same equipment class (fogger), the same acceptance criterion (uniform coverage of an emptied area, no targeted manipulation), and the same environment (warehouse floors, terminals).

sources.title: New Herbicide GUSS sprayer coming to select John Deere dealer locations
sources.claim: Herbicide GUSS is an autonomous herbicide sprayer for orchards, sold commercially through John Deere dealers, that uses LIDAR and nine sensors to stay in the row while applying herbicide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous herbicide application to control weeds under orchard and vineyard rows. Same chemical, same equipment class and same output (a treated ground band) as crew herbicide work on managed grounds; the setting is likewise outdoor premises kept to a standard layout by the operating institution.

sources.title: John Deere Adds GUSS Automation to Its High-Value Crop Autonomy Portfolio
sources.claim: GUSS autonomous sprayers operate in orchards and vineyards with one operator supervising up to eight machines from ... laptop, using GPS, LiDAR and vehicle sensors; John Deere acquired the company in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above; the 1:8 supervision ratio shows the spraying runs with occasional oversight rather than continuous teleoperation, matching the 'limited intervention' standard for crew herbicide application.

sources.title: Carbon Robotics laser weeder targets organic corn and soybean acres - RealAgriculture
sources.claim: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder autonomously identifies and destroys weeds among crops with millimetre accuracy on commercial farms, with an autonomous tractor kit and a remote operations centre providing supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous weed elimination in the field. It transfers to crew weed-control work in that the machine discriminates weeds from desirable plants and treats them individually outdoors, which is the discrimination and precision demand of spot herbicide work on managed grounds.

sources.title: Sprayito (Grande 15 Spot Sprayer) - Burro
sources.claim: Burro's Sprayito is marketed as a fully autonomous spot-spraying robot fitted with WEED-IT precision spray sensors, operating continuously after a one-time setup to spray berms and row centres in orchards, vineyards and nurseries.

sources.title: Drones: A Valuable Tool in CMCD's Fight Against Mosquitoes

sources.claim: Anticimex's SMART offering automates rodent control through fixed intelligent traps and sensors installed in commercial premises; the traps kill and report automatically, but installation, servicing, inspection and all other treatment remain technician work.

sources.title: Pest Control Crawlspace Robots | SuperDroid Robots

tasks.label: Study preliminary reports or diagrams of infested area and determine treatment type required to eliminate and prevent recurrence of infestation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Cut or bore openings in building or surrounding concrete, access infested areas, insert nozzle, and inject pesticide to impregnate ground.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Detached slab-on-grade home, exterior: technician drills 1/2-in holes every 10-12 in through the attached patio, driveway, walkway and porch where they abut the foundation, inserts a sub-slab injector rod through each hole, injects diluted termiticide at label rate (about 4 gal per 10 linear ft) into the soil beneath, then plugs the holes with cement or caps. Must avoid utility lines, plumbing and post-tension cables; outdoors, variable weather, landscaping, pets, uneven grade.

Interior of an occupied house: drilling through the garage slab, along interior slab cracks and expansion joints, at bath traps and plumbing penetrations; furniture, appliances and stored goods moved aside, dust extraction and floor protection used; termiticide injected beneath the slab and each hole patched flush and cleaned up in the customer's presence.

Hollow-block or brick-veneer foundation and crawl space: drilling into masonry voids and mortar joints and through crawl-space skirting, injecting foam or liquid termiticide into the block voids and the soil behind/below; 18-30 in clearance, dirt floor, ducts, insulation, poor light, awkward body positions.

Commercial or institutional building (restaurant, warehouse, apartment block, school): drilling the interior and exterior perimeter slab and expansion joints, often several hundred linear feet, with a hose run from a truck-mounted rig; work around racking, equipment and occupants, usually scheduled after hours, with treatment volumes documented.

Void injection for other pests: drilling small holes in drywall, behind baseboards, into mortar joints, hollow porch steps or exterior stucco/siding and injecting dust, foam or liquid into the void for ants, carpenter bees or roaches; occupied homes and small businesses; holes plugged and surfaces cleaned.

sources.system: DEWALT / August Robotics autonomous concrete floor drilling robot (on the Lionel AMR base)
sources.developer: DEWALT (Stanley Black & Decker) with August Robotics
sources.title: 9 weeks to 9 days: How autonomous drilling is transforming data center construction - The Robot Report
sources.claim: DEWALT and August Robotics field an autonomous mobile robot that reads building CAD plans and drills large numbers of downward holes into concrete slab floors inside buildings under construction, with roughly 1/8-in placement accuracy; it drills only and performs no chemical injection.
sources.transferJustification: Covers only the 'bore openings in building concrete' half of the task: same material (structural concrete slab), similar hole diameters and a programmed hole pattern, but no nozzle insertion or metered pesticide injection into soil.

sources.system: DEWALT downward drilling robot (August Robotics platform)
sources.title: DeWalt unveils world-first downward drilling robot (Video) | Equipment World
sources.claim: The same DEWALT/August system reports 99.97% location and depth accuracy over more than 90,000 holes drilled in pilot programs on jobsite concrete floors, i.e. drilling in concrete at production quality without a human guiding each hole.
sources.transferJustification: Quantifies concrete-drilling reliability for the boring step only; injection of pesticide into the ground beneath the slab is not part of this system.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E. (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Pioneering robotic system Schindler R.I.S.E now operational | Schindler Group
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E. is a self-climbing robot that works unattended inside a concrete elevator shaft, measuring positions, drilling anchor holes in the concrete walls and setting anchor bolts into those holes; commercially deployed on customer high-rise projects since 2020.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (post-installed anchor setting): autonomous drilling into building concrete and insertion of an element into each drilled hole, but in a confined robot-dedicated shaft and with no fluid injection.

sources.system: Electroimpact Quadbots accurate-robot cell with multi-function end effector (MFEE)
sources.title: Neighboring Mobile Robot Cell with Drilling and Fastening (SAE 2017-01-2094)
sources.claim: Electroimpact's 'Quadbots' robotic assembly cell performs, with one end effector on a fixtured aircraft part, the full sequence of drilling a hole, inspecting it, applying sealant through a dispensing nozzle and inserting the fastener, in Boeing production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated drill-and-seal fastening): the E1 analogue of bore-an-opening-then-inject-through-a-nozzle, done by one machine on a fixtured workpiece with metered fluid dispensing; the concrete-material gap is covered by the concrete-drilling evidence.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot (PR Newswire)
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercially sold semi-autonomous mobile drilling robot: an operator moves it into an area and it then drills all BIM-specified holes in concrete ceilings and walls within reach automatically, with integrated dust removal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (jobsite anchor-hole drilling): concrete drilling to a digital plan in a real building, but overhead/wall geometry, operator repositioning, and no chemical injection.

sources.title: Rock bolting rigs | Epiroc US
sources.claim: Epiroc Boltec rock-bolting rigs drill a hole in rock and then inject resin or cement grout into that hole before installing the bolt, using Automatic Resin Injection and an Automatic Cement System, with the operator working from the rig cabin.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (drill hole, inject bonding fluid), but the machine is run by an operator in the cabin, so autonomy is unclear and it cannot support a positive judgment; cited as context only.

sources.title: Pave Robotics: Autonomous Crack Sealing Robot
sources.claim: Pave Robotics' Tracer is an outdoor mobile robot that detects, cleans and fills cracks in asphalt pavement with sealant with minimal human intervention; it dispenses material into surface openings but does not bore holes or inject metered pesticide into soil.
sources.transferJustification: Closest unstructured-outdoor analogue for autonomous dispensing into an opening in a hard surface; it neither bores through concrete nor injects a measured soil-treatment volume, so it does not substantiate this task at E3.

tasks.label: Post warning signs and lock building doors to secure area to be fumigated.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whole-structure tent fumigation of a detached single-family home (drywood termites, CA/FL/HI): after the tarps are on, the technician walks the property, affixes DANGER/fumigation warning placards (with fumigant name, date, phone number) to every exterior entrance and at perimeter access points, closes all exterior doors, installs a secondary lock on each and retains the keys, and confirms the structure is vacated. Landscaping, pets, neighbors, uneven ground and varied door hardware are taken as found.

Fumigation of a commercial/industrial building under an institution's control (flour mill, food plant, warehouse, distribution center): placards posted at every personnel door, dock door and roof access, doors closed and locked or secondary-locked, exclusion zone roped off and a guard/lock log kept, all inside a facility with a fixed layout and controlled access.

Commodity or containerized fumigation at a port terminal, grain elevator or dedicated fumigation chamber: warning placards affixed to the shipping container doors, silo hatch, railcar or chamber door; hatches and access doors closed, sealed and locked; exclusion barrier and signage set at the fixed treatment pad.

Fumigation or whole-building treatment of a multi-unit residential building or hotel managed by a property owner: notices posted on each unit door and at building entrances/stairwells, common-area and unit doors closed and locked, occupancy verified before the fumigant is released.

Localized fumigation or space treatment inside an occupied managed facility (restaurant kitchen, museum vault, greenhouse, single apartment unit): warning signs posted at the treated room's entrances and adjacent corridors, those doors closed and locked for the exposure period, signs removed after aeration clearance.

sources.system: REA LABEL DS / Kawasaki robotic labeler (REA LABEL Robotic Labeler)
sources.developer: REA JET / REA LABEL ES with Kawasaki Robotics
sources.title: Automatic labeling: easier, faster, more reliable
sources.claim: A Kawasaki robot arm with a REA LABEL print-and-apply unit autonomously picks a freshly printed label and applies it to a defined position on a pallet at a fixed labeling station in a GROHE plant, running as part of normal production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated print-and-apply labeling. Posting a warning placard is the application of a printed, adhesive-backed notice to a specified surface; the robot handles the same flimsy printed media and places it to a defined position, in a purpose-built station where the workpiece is conveyed to the machine.

sources.title: Labeller for drum labelling | GHS | bb-automation.com
sources.claim: Fully automatic labelling machines apply GHS hazard-warning labels to drums at defined heights and circumferential positions, integrated into a conveyor line after drum filling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated application of regulatory hazard-warning labels. It is the same output as posting a fumigation warning placard — a compliant hazard notice affixed to the correct surface — achieved without human intervention where the workpiece is presented by a conveyor.

sources.title: The First Completely Automatic CNC Door Opening Solution for Robots
sources.claim: The Safedoor SD100 is a commercially sold, fully electric automatic door opener that lets a robot cell open and close heavy CNC machine enclosure doors without an operator, replacing homemade door-opening rigs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled opening/closing of an enclosure access door in a robot cell. Closing the access door of the treated enclosure is the physical act required by 'lock building doors to secure area', with the door presented in a fixed, known position.

sources.system: Allen-Bradley Atlas 5 (440G) Guard Locking Switch / Guardmaster 442G access box
sources.title: Safety Products | Rockwell Automation | US
sources.claim: Guard-locking interlock switches used on fenced robot and machine cells hold the access door mechanically locked so that people cannot enter the hazardous area while the process runs, releasing only when the hazard is isolated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled locking of an access door to secure a hazardous zone. This is the securing function of the fumigation task — the door to the hazard area is locked under machine control and cannot be opened while the hazard is present.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Spot Arm
sources.date: February 2021 (arm launch); Autowalk door behavior documented through 2025
sources.title: Robot arm opens new doors for Boston Dynamics' Spot
sources.claim: Spot with the Spot Arm can grasp handles and open doors in industrial facilities, with the base repositioning for leverage, but the demonstrated manipulation is operator-cued door opening rather than autonomous placard affixing or key/secondary-lock operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile manipulation of door hardware in human facilities. Cited to mark the frontier of in-facility door handling; it does not cover affixing warning placards or applying/locking secondary locks, so it cannot support a positive E2 judgment.

tasks.label: Set mechanical traps, or place poisonous paste or bait in sewers, burrows, or ditches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential rodent/wildlife job: technician works through an occupied single-family home — kitchen, garage, basement, attic, crawlspace — locating runways and droppings, arming and placing rat/mouse snap traps, glue boards and multi-catch traps behind appliances, on joists and in tight voids, plus setting a cage trap or securing bait in burrows along the foundation and under the deck; pets, children and clutter present.

Commercial/institutional facility interior service: food plant, distribution warehouse, grocery, restaurant kitchen or hospital — installing and re-servicing numbered mechanical multi-catch traps, snap traps and interior bait boxes flush against walls, under equipment lines and pallet racking, replacing captures and bait, all under food-safety and audit documentation rules while staff work around the technician.

Exterior grounds of commercial, retail or multifamily properties: placing and re-baiting tamper-resistant, anchored bait stations around the building perimeter, dumpster corrals, loading docks and utility boxes, and pushing bait into active rat burrows in mulch beds, embankments and under slabs; uneven landscaping, weather, vehicles and public foot traffic.

Municipal/urban sewer and drain baiting: lifting manhole and catch-basin covers in streets and alleys, hanging or wedging wax bait blocks on wire in the sewer throat or securing bait in storm drains and utility vaults, working over traffic with confined-space and gas hazards, then recording each treated structure.

Turf, landscape and agricultural spot treatment of individual burrows: probing for pocket gopher and ground squirrel tunnels on lawns, golf courses, levees, ditch banks and orchards, dispensing measured bait into each tunnel with a probe or spoon, and setting scissor/box gopher traps or mole traps into excavated runways, then covering the openings.

Broad-area outdoor toxicant/bait application over open land: broadcasting rodenticide pellets across acreage, brushy ground or islands where station-free broadcast is label-permitted, and dropping larvicide granules or briquettes into roadside ditches, canals, flooded fields and marsh pockets for a vector-control program.

sources.system: Envico ENV10 / ENV50 heavy-lift baiting drones with bait spreaders
sources.developer: Envico Technologies (Environment and Conservation Technologies), New Zealand
sources.title: Drone Baiting | Envico
sources.claim: Envico Technologies operates heavy-lift bait-spreading drones that disperse rodenticide bait over island terrain from pre-programmed GPS mission plans, including the 2019 Seymour Norte (Galápagos) operation dispersing about 3,000 kg of bait; spreaders support full-swath, directional, trickle and cluster patterns.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial broadcast of rodenticide bait over open ground rather than hand-placement in a burrow. It transfers only to the broad-area outdoor baiting instance, where broadcast application of the same commercial rodent baits is an accepted method and no per-burrow precision is required.

sources.system: ENV10 baiting drone (Island Conservation / Envico island restoration program)
sources.title: Redefining Conservation: How Drones are Revolutionizing Island Restoration - Island Conservation
sources.claim: Drone-delivered bait eradications have been carried out operationally on 12 islands in four countries, with one platform completing over 1,200 flights and more than 500 flights delivering bait across nine islands in a single program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: broad-area aerial bait delivery for rodent control, not trap setting. Cited to establish that autonomous bait dispersal over unstructured outdoor terrain is a repeatedly executed operational capability, which is the substance of the broad-area baiting instance.

sources.system: Autonomous UAS with tablet-dropper and granular spreader modules (DJI S1000+ airframe, Mission Planner/QGroundControl)
sources.developer: Anastasia Mosquito Control District, St. Johns County, Florida
sources.title: The development of autonomous unmanned aircraft systems for mosquito control | PLOS One
sources.claim: A mosquito-control district built an autonomous multirotor UAS with interchangeable modules that spray liquid larvicide, drop 40-gram larvicide tablets to within 1.1 m of a target site, and spread larvicidal granules; missions were flown autonomously from a ground-station flight plan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial placement of toxicant tablets/granules into standing water (ditches, ponds) rather than paste in a burrow. Objects (40 g tablets, granules), the outdoor wet-ditch environment, and the ~1 m placement tolerance match the broad-area ditch-treatment instance.

sources.developer: Central UAS Technologies (operated by Collier Mosquito Control District)
sources.title: Drones: A Valuable Tool in CMCD’s Fight Against Mosquitoes - Collier Mosquito Control District
sources.claim: An operating US mosquito control district uses purpose-built treatment drones carrying up to 40 lb of Bti larvicide to treat retention ponds, canals, flooded farm fields and wet forest, having treated more than 1,000 acres in a season; the aircraft are flown by FAA-certified pilots from the ground.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: granular larvicide application to ditches, canals and wet fields. Cited only as context for the operational scale of drone toxicant application in ditch/marsh settings; autonomy is not established, so it does not by itself support a positive judgment.

sources.system: ROBOTT-NET urban pest control robot (Robotnik mobile platform with arm)
sources.developer: Robotnik / Hispavista Labs / Irabia Control de Plagas (ROBOTT-NET)
sources.title: ROBOTT-NET pilot project: Urban pest control - Robohub
sources.claim: A European pilot project with a pest control company built a mobile robot with an arm that inserts a camera into rodent traps in enclosed spaces and uploads images to the cloud; the demonstrated function is trap inspection, not placing, baiting or arming traps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic servicing of rodent traps. It marks the frontier of in-situ pest-control robotics as trap inspection; it does not substantiate setting mechanical traps or depositing bait, so it supports no positive judgment.

sources.system: Spot quadruped with Spot Arm (Autowalk/Orbit inspection missions)
sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot performs autonomous scheduled inspection missions inside industrial facilities and, in a beta capability, can use its arm to open doors autonomously ... those missions; documented arm work is grasping, dragging and door opening, semi-autonomously or by teleoperation, not deploying pest control devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside structured facilities. Considered as the closest indoor capability, but the cited work is inspection and door opening; nothing in it substantiates locating rodent runways, arming snap traps, or baiting and anchoring stations, so it supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Clean and remove blockages from infested areas to facilitate spraying procedures and provide drainage, using brooms, mops, shovels, or rakes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine residential general-pest service: brushing down spider webs, wasp nests and dust from eaves, soffits, window frames and porch corners with a webbing pole, then sweeping the porch, entry and patio clear of leaves and dead insects so the perimeter band spray can be applied.

Residential interior harborage clearing before treatment: in a basement, garage, attic, crawlspace or under a kitchen sink, moving stored boxes and clutter aside, raking or shovelling out insulation and rodent nesting debris, and sweeping droppings and dead insects from behind appliances in a confined, low-clearance, non-standard space.

Exterior grounds and drainage work at a home or small property: raking leaves and mulch back from the foundation, cleaning out window wells, clearing a clogged gutter, downspout or yard drain grate, and dumping standing water from containers so mosquito and perimeter treatments will hold and the area will drain.

Commercial food-service kitchen roach/fly job: pulling floor mats and light equipment out, sweeping and mopping grease and food debris from under and behind cooking lines, coolers and shelving, and clearing a grease-clogged floor drain before applying residual spray and bait.

Warehouse, food plant or retail backroom: sweeping spilled product, dust and packaging debris from open floor and aisle areas so the perimeter treatment can be applied and monitoring devices placed on clean floor.
Commercial paved exterior: sweeping litter, leaves and spilled refuse from a dumpster pad, loading dock apron or walkway before treating for flies and rodents.

sources.title: Avidbots releases floor-scrubbing robot for industrial spaces - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo 2 / Neo 2W are commercially deployed autonomous floor-scrubbing robots that clean warehouse, manufacturing, airport and other facility floors without human intervention, with over 1,000 units in the field.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility floor cleaning. It transfers to the pest-control instance of clearing loose floor debris from open floor and aisle areas of a warehouse or plant before treatment — same surfaces, same loose debris, same institution-controlled facility — but only for open floor, not under equipment or in drains.

sources.title: Tennant rolls out X16 SWEEP for round-the-clock autonomous sweeping - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Tennant's X16 SWEEP, powered by Brain Corp's BrainOS, is a commercially launched autonomous robotic sweeper built for heavy-duty debris sweeping in warehouses, logistics centers and light ... plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial floor sweeping of dust and bulk debris. Transfers to the pest-control step of sweeping spilled product and packaging debris off warehouse/plant floors before perimeter treatment: identical debris, identical hard floors, same facility type.

sources.system: PUDU MT1 / MT1 Max robotic sweeper
sources.title: PUDU MT1: AI Powered Robotic Sweeper & Industrial Floor Cleaning Robot
sources.claim: Pudu's MT1 is a commercially sold AI-powered autonomous sweeping robot for large indoor and semi-outdoor commercial venues that picks up leaves, bottles, cigarette butts and fine dust.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hard-surface litter and leaf sweeping in commercial venues. Transfers to sweeping a dumpster pad, dock apron or walkway clear of leaves and litter before fly/rodent treatment — same loose debris on paved surfaces at an institution-controlled site.

sources.system: SuperDroid GPK-32 tracked inspection robot (pest control configuration)
sources.title: GPK-32 Tracked Inspection Robot - SuperDroid Robots (Pest Control)
sources.claim: Robots marketed to pest control for crawl spaces are teleoperated tracked inspection platforms that send video to a handheld controller and are designed to avoid entanglement in crawl-space obstructions; they do not clear debris.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest crawl-space system for pest control; it is teleoperated and inspection-only, so it cannot support a positive judgment for clearing debris and blockages from crawl spaces.

sources.title: Figure humanoid robot cleans cluttered living room in new video demo
sources.claim: Figure's Figure 03 humanoid was shown in a March 2026 video demonstration autonomously tidying a staged living room — wiping a table, picking up blocks into a bin and repositioning a pillow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tidying loose objects in a home. Cited to test transfer to clearing infested basements, crawl spaces and drains; it is a single staged video demo with light household objects, no broom/shovel work in confined, soiled spaces, so it does not establish worker-quality completion.

tasks.label: Position and fasten edges of tarpaulins over building, and tape vents to ensure air-tight environment and to check for leaks.

emergingTasks.label: Monitor inventory of chemicals and supplies.

roles.title: Landscaping and Groundskeeping Workers
roles.description: Landscape or maintain grounds of property using hand or power tools or equipment. Workers typically perform a variety of tasks, which may include any combination of the following: sod laying, mowing, trimming, planting, watering, fertilizing, digging, raking, sprinkler installation, and installation of mortarless segmental concrete masonry wall units.
roles.sector: Building and grounds cleaning and maintenance

tasks.label: Mow or edge lawns, using power mowers or edgers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Route mowing of a private residential lawn: crew arrives with truck/trailer, mows a 1/8–1/2 acre front and back yard with a walk-behind or small stand-on mower, working around swing sets, dog waste, hoses, garden beds, downspout extensions, gates and fenced back yards; grass height varies with weather and the interval since the last visit.

Mowing large maintained turf on a commercial or institutional property under contract — office park, apartment complex, HOA common area, school or corporate campus, cemetery — with a zero-turn or stand-on mower: open turf with tree wells, curbed islands, parking lots, irrigation heads, some slopes, occasional pedestrians and parked cars.

Mowing fine sports and golf turf: athletic fields, soccer/football/baseball fields, golf fairways, tees and rough, to a tight height-of-cut with a required striping pattern and a scheduled window around play; premises fenced or otherwise controlled by the club, school or district.

Mowing municipal/public turf open to the public: city park lawns, greenway strips, civic building grounds, boulevard and street-frontage turf — litter, dog waste, benches, playgrounds, pedestrians and pets present, uneven ground and no fencing.

Edging and detail trimming with a stick edger and string trimmer at the same properties: cutting a clean vertical edge along sidewalks, driveways and curbs, trimming along fences, walls, bed lines, tree trunks, sign posts, utility boxes and hydrants where the mower cannot reach, then blowing clippings off hard surfaces.

sources.title: Autonomous Solutions acquires Scythe Robotics - Lawn & Landscape
sources.claim: Scythe's M.52 all-electric autonomous commercial mower is in commercial service with landscape contractors, mowing roughly 2 billion sq ft in 2025 for dozens of customers across ....

sources.title: Scythe debuts new generation of M.52 - Lawn & Landscape

sources.title: Robotics in Today's Yellowstone Landscape

sources.title: Sports turf management - Football & cricket pitch mowers | Husqvarna US

sources.title: Husqvarna rolls out new robotic mowers - Golf Course Industry

sources.system: Toro Greensmaster eTriFlex 3360 with GeoLink Solutions Autonomous Fairway Mower

sources.title: How Robotic Mowers Have Moved from a Curiosity to a Competitive Advantage - NALP
sources.claim: Landscape contractors leave Kress robotic mowers on customer properties where they mow autonomously up to three times a ..., with crews visiting only to do detail work; the contractor is moving away from truck-and-trailer mowing routes.

sources.title: Robot Lawn Mowers | Husqvarna US
sources.claim: Residential robotic mowers are a mass-deployed consumer product maintaining private home lawns autonomously.

sources.title: Luba 2 AWD review: The robotic lawn mower for challenging yards - New Atlas

sources.system: ECHO Robotics professional robotic mowers (TM/Bigmow series)
sources.title: Robotic lawn mowers for parks and gardens | EchoRobotics
sources.claim: ECHO Robotics markets and installs professional autonomous robotic mowers for municipal parks and public green spaces, running unattended for municipal teams.

sources.system: autonomous robotic mowers (City of Sanford, NC grounds fleet)

sources.claim: A US city added autonomous mowers to its grounds maintenance fleet, deploying them on municipal center grounds after successful testing, freeing staff for park and greenway work.

sources.claim: Contractors who adopt robotic mowers still send human crews to properties specifically to do the edging and detail work the robots cannot do.

sources.title: Robot Lawn Mowers with Built-In String Trimmers - Mowing Magic

sources.claim: Owner running-log of the shipped consumer autonomous edge trimmer reports jobs halting on turns and poor positioning exactly where edging is needed (under trees, next to houses), and misdirected trimming runs.

tasks.label: Operate vehicles or powered equipment, such as mowers, tractors, twin-axle vehicles, snow blowers, chainsaws, electric clippers, sod cutters, or pruning saws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mowing large maintained turf at an institution-controlled site — school/college campus, municipal park, cemetery, sports field, golf course, office-park or HOA common lawn — with a zero-turn, stand-on or tractor-mounted deck; open areas with known layout, some pedestrians, trees, curbs and irrigation heads; weekly or twice-weekly cut to a set height with stripes.

Mowing private residential yards on a route: 10-20 properties a day, walk-behind or riding mower, gated back yards, slopes, tree roots, kids' toys, pet waste, hoses and beds; each yard laid out differently and taken as found.
Finish work after mowing on residential and small commercial lots: string trimmer/edger along lawn borders, walks, driveways and bed lines, then backpack blower to clear clippings from hardscape.

Handheld powered cutting beyond turf: chainsaw limbing, bucking downed limbs and felling small trees; pruning saw on branches overhead; powered hedge clippers shaping shrubs and hedges; string-trimming rough, overgrown areas around fences, signs, guardrails and pond banks.

Snow season: running a walk-behind snow blower or plow/blade over driveways, entrance walks and building perimeters at homes, HOAs and commercial sites; storm-condition work, variable snow depth and wetness, ice and parked cars.

Operating a compact tractor or utility vehicle with an implement on institution-managed grounds: towing an aerator, spreading fertilizer/seed, pulling a sweeper or dethatcher, running a sod cutter, and shuttling a loaded trailer of mulch or soil between areas of the site.

sources.claim: Crews set mow zones and no-go zones and the M.52 then mows autonomously, driving itself between linked zones without manual repositioning by crew ....

sources.title: Segway Navimow X3 Series Robotic Mowers Review
sources.claim: Segway's Navimow X3 consumer robotic mowers autonomously mow home lawns and estates up to ..., navigating complex layouts, narrow passages and obstacles with RTK plus vision.

sources.system: Ecovacs GOAT A3000 LiDAR / LiDAR Pro
sources.title: EcoVacs Goat A3000 Review: Best Robot Lawn Mower of 2026
sources.claim: The Ecovacs Goat A3000 LiDAR robot mower autonomously maps and mows real residential yards with hills and tree canopy, and its side-mounted TruEdge string trimmer removed most manual edging in a reviewer's testing.
