sources.claim: Yarbo has launched a fully autonomous edge-trimmer module that trims lawn edges, bed lines and around obstacles that the mower cannot reach, using vision to detect edges.

sources.title: Leaf Blower – Yarbo
sources.claim: The Yarbo leaf-blower module is sold as an autonomous attachment that clears leaves, grass clippings and debris from lawns, driveways and walkways using RTK-GPS, stereo cameras and radar.

sources.title: Yarbo robotic snow blower review: A yard crawler for all seasons
sources.claim: A reviewer mapped a driveway with the Yarbo app, scheduled automated snow removal, and found the snow-blower attachment worked well, earning an Editors' Choice.

sources.title: Autonomous Snowbot Pro hits the sidewalk
sources.claim: The SnowBot Pro is a commercial-grade self-driving snow clearing machine that drives itself along recorded GPS paths to clear sidewalks and walkways for snow-and-ice contractors and property managers.

sources.system: Turf Tank One / Turf Tank Two
sources.title: Fast Growing Turf Tank for Autonomous Sports Field Marking
sources.claim: More than 1,200 Turf Tank autonomous line-marking robots operate on US sports fields at schools, parks departments and universities, each painting a full field in under 30 minutes on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously driving a powered ground vehicle carrying an applicator over an entire turf area to a planned coverage pattern — the same navigation, coverage and turf-surface driving needed to tow an aerator, spreader or sweeper across grounds.

sources.title: Monarch Begins Rollout of Monarch Autodrive Technology
sources.claim: Monarch's driver-optional MK-V tractor has commercially available fully autonomous implement operation (autonomous feed pushing) in dairies, with 360-degree situational awareness during driverless operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless tractor work pulling/running an implement over a controlled worksite; comparable vehicle class, speeds and implement control to towing an aerator or spreader on institution-managed grounds.

tasks.label: Use hand tools, such as shovels, rakes, pruning saws, saws, hedge or brush trimmers, or axes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential property: pruning and shaping shrubs and hedges with a powered hedge trimmer, loppers, hand pruners and a pruning saw — cutting back overgrown foundation plantings, removing deadwood, cutting back perennials, then gathering the clippings. Varied species, uneven ground, close to house walls, windows and fences.

Residential and small commercial planting/soil work with shovel, spade and rake: digging holes for shrubs, perennials and annuals, setting and backfilling plants, moving and spreading topsoil, compost and mulch from a pile or wheelbarrow, raking beds smooth and cutting a spade edge along bed lines.

Leaf, clipping and debris cleanup with rakes: raking leaves, grass clippings, sticks and windblown litter off lawns, out of shrub beds and off walks, dragging piles onto tarps and loading into bags or a truck so the property is left clean.

Detail trimming on institutional/commercial grounds under contract (college campus, office park, HOA, municipal park, cemetery): string/brush trimming grass along walks, curbs, fences, headstones, sign posts and tree trunks, knocking back weedy growth in fence lines, with pedestrians and parked cars present.

Rough, heavy hand-tool work: clearing overgrown brush and volunteer saplings with a brush saw, loppers or machete, limbing low branches with a pruning saw or bow saw, chopping roots and small stumps with an axe or mattock along property edges, fence lines and neglected areas.

sources.developer: EU H2020 consortium led by Univ. of Edinburgh (with Bosch, Wageningen UR)
sources.title: TrimBot2020 Project – Cutting Hedge Research
sources.claim: TrimBot2020 built a mobile outdoor robot that autonomously navigated a garden and trimmed boxwood topiary and rose bushes with arm-mounted cutting tools, guided by stereo vision.

sources.title: TrimBot2020 Project – Cutting Hedge Research
sources.claim: The TrimBot2020 robot's experiments were run in a test garden purpose-built for the project at Wageningen University, with prepared boxwood and rose specimens.

sources.developer: academic research group (published in Computers and Electronics in Agriculture)
sources.title: Design and evaluation of hedge trimmer robot
sources.claim: A five-degree-of-freedom autonomous hedge trimmer robot was ... and evaluated, able to trim simple hedge shapes, as a step toward autonomous pruning robots.

sources.title: Autonomous robot clears 6,000-sq-ft NJ driveway during snowstorm
sources.claim: The Yarbo modular yard robot cleared a 6,000-sq-ft residential driveway autonomously for 20 hours through a snowstorm, after the owner spent time mapping the driveway and setting throw angles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (snow clearing) shows the current state of autonomous ground-work machines in real residential yards: mapped route following with a mounted implement, no tool manipulation or debris collection.

sources.title: Yarbo Blower
sources.claim: Yarbo sells a blower module that autonomously clears leaves, clippings and dirt from lawns, driveways and walkways and gathers debris into piles on mapped residential properties.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (blowing debris into piles) substitutes for the raking half of leaf/debris cleanup; it does not collect, bag or haul the debris, and the M-series leaf collector had not shipped as of the rating date.

sources.title: Yarbo's Mower Pro Garden Robot Is Adding A Weed Whacker For Perfect Lawn Edges
sources.claim: Yarbo demonstrated a string-trimmer module for its yard robot that the company says runs unsupervised; reviewers noted it was a demo whose real-world performance was still unproven, and dealer listings showed shipment only from late August 2026.

sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers from Built Robotics for Solar Projects
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous excavators drive solar piles and dig trenches unaided on utility-scale solar construction sites, with contractors such as Blattner and Bechtel using them across the US.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous excavation/trenching) shows machine-controlled digging of soil outdoors on unstructured sites, but at bucket scale on cleared ground — it does not cover shovel-scale holes among existing plants, plant setting or bed finishing.

sources.title: 8 Transplanters to Help Right-Size Labor in Your Growing Operation
sources.claim: Commercial horticultural transplanting robots plant seedlings into growing medium on fixtured greenhouse lines at tens of thousands of plants per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (opening a hole in growing medium and setting a plant) is the purpose-built-line form of digging-and-planting; it works only with pots/trays presented on a conveyor, not with ground soil.

sources.title: Greenzie releases 5.0 software, advancing commercial-ready autonomy for the landscaping industry
sources.claim: Greenzie's autonomy platform is deployed on hundreds of commercial mowers maintaining commercial properties, i.e. grounds autonomy in the field today covers mowing rather than hand-tool work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous commercial mowing) establishes what is actually deployed on institutional grounds — ride-on mower autonomy — and thus that no deployed system performs hand-tool detail work there.

tasks.label: Prune or trim trees, shrubs, or hedges, using shears, pruners, or chain saws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shearing of foundation shrubs and formal hedges at a private residence: boxwood, privet, yew, holly cut back to shape with a gas/battery hedge trimmer, working around mulch beds, fences, AC units, downspouts, irrigation heads and uneven ground, then blowing/raking clippings.

Scheduled shearing of shrub masses and long hedge runs on institutionally managed grounds (office park, school or hospital campus, HOA common area, municipal park): standard plant palette, repeat visits, pedestrians and parked cars nearby, machine-shear to a flat/rounded face.

Selective hand pruning with bypass pruners and loppers: renewal cuts on flowering shrubs, deadheading roses, removing dead, diseased, crossing or water-sprout stems, thinning ornamentals to species-appropriate form; requires choosing each cut and its location on the stem.

Ground-based small-tree pruning with pole pruner, pole saw or small chain saw: raising canopies over walks and drives, removing low, dead or broken limbs and basal suckers from ornamental and street trees, cuts of roughly 1-4 inches at the branch collar.

Heavier chain-saw work and vegetation clearing: cutting storm-broken limbs, cutting back overgrown vegetation and volunteer saplings along fence lines, walls, signs and utility boxes, sometimes from a ladder or small lift, dropping and stacking brush.

sources.system: AgriNomix/AdeptAg Revolving Trimmer (nursery shaping trimmer line)
sources.date: 2024-05 (product page); trimming lines in commercial nursery use since at least 2019
sources.title: Revolving Trimmer | AdeptAg Trimming Solutions
sources.claim: Commercially sold nursery shaping trimmer in which potted woody ornamentals are conveyed into a fixture, gripped automatically, and sheared to a ball or pyramid form by a revolving cutting head under PLC control - the shearing operation of shrub trimming performed with the workpiece presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nursery shearing/shaping of woody ornamental stock. Same objects (woody shrubs), same tool action (shear new growth to a geometric form) and same accepted output (uniformly shaped shrub) as landscape shrub shearing, executed with the plant fixtured and presented - the E1 counterfactual for this task.

sources.developer: University of Edinburgh consortium (Wageningen UR, Bosch, ETH Zurich, others)
sources.title: A gardening robot for rose, hedge and topiary trimming | H2020 | CORDIS
sources.claim: EU research robot (Bosch Indego base plus Kinova arm and custom cutters) autonomously navigated purpose-built test gardens and performed stand-alone clipping of hedge bushes ... on real plants; project closed end-2019 with no commercial product.

sources.system: Autonomous hedge trimmer robot (vision-guided trimming platform)
sources.developer: academic group, published in Computers and Electronics in Agriculture
sources.title: Design and evaluation of hedge trimmer robot - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Research prototype autonomous hedge trimming robot with vision-based hedge detection and trimming to specified shapes; reported about 96% hedge detection accuracy and 88% trimming success in experiments - below the reliability an employer would accept, and never commercialized.

sources.system: orchard and vineyard selective pruning robots (surveyed research prototypes)
sources.developer: multiple academic groups (review by Chiaberge et al., Politecnico di Torino)
sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Pruning in Orchards and Vineyards: a Review (arXiv:2505.07318)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review of a decade of work on selective robotic pruning of woody plants (apple, grapevine, cherry) finds the area is still a research niche with critical open challenges; no commercially deployed selective pruning robot is identified.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: selective pruning of woody stems on trees and vines. It is the closest mechanized analogue to hand pruning and tree limb removal in landscaping; the review establishes that even in engineered orchard rows such cutting is not yet fielded at production quality.

sources.title: A robotic solution for safer tree trimming | Penn Today
sources.claim: Startup prototype for tree trimming is a rope-climbing, ground-controlled (human-operated) machine, not an autonomous pruner; illustrates that robotic tree limb removal remains operator-driven prototype work in 2026.

sources.title: Priva Kompano | Deleafing robot
sources.claim: Commercially marketed autonomous robot that moves along greenhouse rows and cuts plant material (tomato leaf removal) alongside workers, demonstrating machine-vision-guided cutting of plants in a purpose-built horticultural facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal of plant parts by cutting. Comparable perception-and-cut loop on live plants in rows engineered for the machine; supports feasibility of automated plant cutting only where the plants are presented in a standardized, purpose-built layout, not on found landscapes.

tasks.label: Gather and remove litter.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily/weekly litter police of a commercial or institutional property (office park, apartment complex, retail center, school campus): worker walks turf, mulch beds, shrub lines, curb strips and entryways picking mixed litter - cups, cans, bottles, fast-food bags, paper, wrappers, blown plastic - bags it and disposes of it, usually ahead of mowing.

Residential lawn-service crew policing a client's yard before mowing: pick up blown trash, drink containers, pet waste, kids' toys, fallen sticks and papers from lawn, driveway, beds and fence line; layout, clutter and obstacles differ at every house.

Municipal park, sports field, greenway or roadside litter patrol: mixed litter across picnic areas, playgrounds, benches, shrub beds, fence lines and ditch banks, often wet, partly buried or tangled, with the public present.
Emptying trash and recycling receptacles sited around the grounds - pulling and tying liners, replacing bags, carrying or hauling bagged litter by cart or truck to a dumpster or compactor.

Small-litter (micro-litter) cleaning of lawns, gravel paths and paved plazas at parks, event lawns/festival grounds and campus green space: cigarette butts, bottle caps, wrappers, plastic scraps and glass shards over large open turf areas, daily or after events.
Hardscape litter and debris clearing on a managed property: parking lots, service drives, plazas and walkways swept or blown and litter collected, at a shopping center, campus or business park.

sources.title: Product - Angsa Robotics
sources.claim: Angsa Robotics' outdoor litter robot (HERON) runs unattended shifts of up to 8 hours on grass, gravel and paved areas, mapping the area once and then cleaning autonomously, calling for help only when stuck.

sources.title: Angsa Robotics - ESA Commercialisation Gateway
sources.claim: Angsa's machine is limited to small waste it can detect and vacuum on green space - cigarette butts, caps, plastic scraps, glass - with larger plastic packaging still only in testing.

sources.title: Angsa Robotics: KI-Müllroboter gegen Abfall im Park
sources.claim: Angsa's litter robots are in routine daily use by German municipalities of various sizes (Berlin, Pforzheim, Karlsruhe) cleaning parks, green spaces and festival grounds.

sources.title: Robots Begin Street Cleaning Duties in China's Shenzhen
sources.claim: 36 CowaRobot autonomous sanitation robots clean about 2.7 million square meters of sidewalks, street corners and road sections in Shenzhen under municipal performance evaluation; the company's CTO states that picking litter out of green spaces and emptying trash cans still require human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Street/sidewalk sweeping is the related task: the same robots clear litter and leaves from paved surfaces, which transfers to clearing hardscape (walkways, plazas, lots) on managed grounds; the same source bounds transfer to turf and receptacles.

sources.title: WeRide launches L4 unmanned Robosweeper in Shantou city - Gasgoo
sources.claim: WeRide's Robosweeper S1, an L4 unmanned sanitation vehicle, performs regular day and night street-cleaning shifts on open roads and plazas, with smart-sanitation fleets deployed in several Chinese cities and Singapore.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is municipal street sweeping: an autonomous suction sweeper removing litter and debris from paved public surfaces is the same operation a groundskeeper performs on parking lots, plazas and walkways, with comparable objects and precision.

sources.system: Tesla Optimus; Loki Robotics wheeled robot (assessed systems)
sources.developer: Epoch AI (assessment of Tesla, Loki Robotics)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: An independent 2026 assessment of robot autonomy classifies 'take out the trash' (remove bag from bin, close it, carry it to an outdoor bin) as having significant limits even in lab settings; the best fielded example (Loki Robotics on campuses) is one-armed, roughly ten times slower than ... and needs teleoperation for many edge cases.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is bagging and removing trash from a receptacle, the core of the groundskeeper's receptacle-emptying instance; the evidence shows the manipulation (liner removal, closing, carrying) is not yet autonomous even indoors.

sources.title: AI for Green Spaces: Leveraging Autonomous Navigation and Computer Vision for Park Litter Removal
sources.claim: A research robot built to autonomously navigate grass fields and pick up picnic litter (plastic bottles, wrappers, boxes) reached only an 80% overall success rate, i.e. one item in five missed.

tasks.label: Trim or pick flowers and clean flower beds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weekly maintenance of annual/seasonal color beds at a commercial or institutional property (hotel entrance, office park, campus, retail center): selectively deadhead spent blooms, pinch back leggy growth, hand-pull weeds growing through mulch, rake or blow out debris and litter, tidy mulch line at the edge, all while pedestrians pass.

Residential/estate property beds: mixed perennials, annuals, bulbs, groundcover and shrubs in irregular beds around a house; deadhead and trim spent flowers, cut back finished perennials, pull established weeds and grass runners out of mulch, remove leaf litter, work around hoses, pets, ornaments and uneven edging.

Seasonal bed cleanout at a park, municipal grounds, cemetery or campus: spring/fall changeover — cut back and pull out dead annuals and perennial tops, rake leaves and windblown trash out of beds, re-cut bed edges, spread fresh mulch, leaving a planted bed ready for the season.

Streetscape planters, traffic-island and sidewalk tree-pit flower beds in a public right-of-way: weed, pick out cigarette butts, cups and other litter, deadhead flowers, tidy soil surface, with pedestrians, parked cars, compacted soil and unpredictable debris.

Picking/cutting flowers: harvesting blooms at the right stage from a cutting garden or flower bed at an estate, resort or cemetery for indoor arrangements or display, cutting stems cleanly without bruising and carrying them in.

Bed and container work in an enclosed horticultural facility: trimming/shearing massed uniform flowering plants and keeping production or conservatory display beds weed-free on flat, level floors with standard bench/bed layout.

sources.title: Tertill Reviews
sources.claim: Tertill is a commercially sold, solar-powered robot that patrols a home garden or flower bed autonomously and cuts weed seedlings while avoiding larger plants; it does not deadhead, cut back plants, or remove debris.
sources.transferJustification: Weed cutting in a planted bed is the 'clean flower beds' component; cited to show the closest commercial bed-working robot and its scope limits.

sources.title: Amazon.com: Tertill Garden Weeding Robot
sources.claim: Tertill's operating envelope is narrow: beds must be relatively flat and smooth with a raised border and roughly a foot between plants, which excludes densely planted ornamental color beds and irregular landscape beds.

sources.title: Automated tulip picking with Tulip Picker | Bercomex
sources.claim: The Bercomex Tulip Picker is a commercially sold, fully automatic machine that picks tulip flowers by gripping the stem without damage, with the flowers presented to it in trays on a processing line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: harvesting cut flowers. It is the same physical act as 'pick flowers' — gripping and separating a bloom on its stem without bruising — performed on flowers presented to the machine, i.e. the E1 presentation of a picking job.

sources.date: 2026-07 (product page, undated; machine marketed since at least 2018)
sources.title: Pruning and Shaping Trimmers – Horticulture Equipment
sources.claim: Conveyor-fed contour trimming machines for potted nursery/bedding stock are commercially available: pots are fed automatically past a cutter deck that shears the plant tops to shape.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shearing/trimming plant tops on nursery stock. It is the same cutting operation as 'trim flowers' on massed uniform plants, executed with the workpieces fixtured and conveyed — the E1 presentation of a trimming job.

sources.system: University of Idaho nursery weeding robot ('Jethro')
sources.developer: University of Idaho (Wells, Knopp, Wing; Shovic lab)
sources.title: Robot developed by students makes weeding easier at forest nursery | University of Idaho
sources.claim: An autonomous gantry-style weeding robot demonstrated at a US Forest Service forest nursery identifies weeds among seedlings in prepared nursery beds and kills them with an electric probe at claimed >95% efficiency.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: weeding prepared seedling beds. Comparable objects (small weeds among planted stock) and precision, but in uniform machine-planted nursery rows rather than ornamental landscape beds.

sources.developer: EU H2020 consortium (Univ. of Edinburgh, Wageningen UR, Bosch and partners)
sources.title: A gardening robot for rose, hedge and topiary trimming | H2020 | CORDIS
sources.claim: The nearest demonstrated system for autonomous ornamental trimming outdoors is a research prototype: TrimBot2020 achieved autonomous navigation in purpose-prepared test gardens and clipping of hedge bushes and ...; it was never commercialized.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pruning rose bushes in a garden. Closest ornamental-plant cutting work to 'trim flowers', but only prototype-level in prepared test gardens, so it does not establish worker-quality completion.

sources.title: Robots take to the Dutch bulb fields to spot diseased plants - DutchNews.nl
sources.claim: Autonomous tulip-field robots deployed commercially in Dutch bulb fields identify individual diseased tulip plants by AI vision and treat/destroy them, showing plant-level selectivity outdoors but not bloom trimming or bed cleaning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: selective removal of individual flowering plants in machine-planted bulb beds; shows outdoor plant-level selectivity but on a uniform monoculture crop, not mixed ornamental beds.

sources.title: Electric Sheep Verdie robot uses large world models for autonomous landscaping - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Commercial landscape robotics for outdoor properties is concentrated in mowing; a vendor-announced robot for trimming, edging and leaf blowing (Verdie) has not been independently shown doing autonomous flower-bed work.

sources.system: Yarbo modular yard robot (blower / mower modules)
sources.title: This autonomous yard robot and its lawn mower attachment do all the work, but setup is the chore | Reviewed
sources.claim: Consumer/prosumer yard robots such as Yarbo offer an autonomous leaf-blowing module for residential yards, but independent reviews find performance depends on large, flat, obstacle-free areas and setup is demanding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor debris blowing, one component of 'clean flower beds'; cited to show that even this component is limited to open obstacle-free ground, not planted beds.

tasks.label: Care for established lawns by mulching, aerating, weeding, grubbing, removing thatch, or trimming or edging around flower beds, walks, or walls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential maintenance visit on a private lot: string-trim and edge the lawn along the driveway, front walk, foundation and fence line, and cut a clean edge where turf meets mulch beds; obstacles include downspouts, hoses, kids' toys, shrubs, tree trunks and irrigation heads.

Commercial/HOA/office-park or campus grounds: edging turf along miles of curb and concrete walk, string-trimming around retaining walls, sign bases, light poles, hydrants and bed borders after the mow crew passes; fixed layout, property managed by an institution.

Weeding planting and mulch beds around established lawns at homes and commercial sites: pulling or grubbing broadleaf and grassy weeds out of mulch and from cracks along walks and wall bases, leaving beds clean without damaging ornamentals.

Seasonal mulch installation/refresh: hauling bulk bark mulch by wheelbarrow or blower hose, spreading and raking an even 2-3 in. layer around shrubs, trees and bed edges without burying crowns, then blowing walks clean.

Turf renovation work on established lawns: core aeration with a walk-behind or tow-behind aerator, power raking/dethatching and hauling off thatch, and grubbing out weeds, saplings and roots in neglected turf and bed areas (residential lots, campuses, sports and park turf).

Cemetery/memorial park: trimming turf around upright headstones, flush bronze markers, urns and monument bases, and edging along interior walks and curbs; institution-controlled grounds kept to a standard.

sources.title: Yarbo Adds Fully Autonomous Trimmer to Its Modular Lawn Care Robot
sources.claim: Yarbo sells a modular yard robot with a dedicated autonomous string-trimmer module that trims lawn edges, bed borders and tight spaces; it shipped to consumers from spring 2025 at $499 for the module.

sources.title: Trimmer – Yarbo (product page)
sources.claim: Vendor documentation states the Trimmer runs on a schedule following an RTK-mapped memory path to maintain edge definition, but concedes some manual trimming remains.

sources.title: Trimmer disappointing – Yarbo Forum
sources.claim: In an as-found residential yard, an owner reports the trimmer-equipped robot repeatedly violating no-go zones and colliding with the house, shop and flower beds, forcing a return to manual trimming — evidence it does not reach worker quality in an unstructured yard.

sources.system: Ecovacs GOAT A3000 LiDAR PRO (TrueEdge trimmer)
sources.title: Yarbo Yard Robot Review: Do NOT Buy Until You've Watched This
sources.claim: Independent long-term testing of the best current consumer edge-trimming mowers finds they reduce but do not eliminate manual string trimming in real yards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic edge/perimeter trimming by a mower with a dedicated trimmer. Same tool (string line), same targets (turf edges at walks and beds), so it bounds how well autonomous trimming/edging performs in as-found yards.

sources.title: Can a Robot Weed Your Garden? I Tested the Tertill Weeding Robot to Find Out
sources.claim: A two-month independent test found the solar autonomous Tertill weeding robot kept a garden bed weed-free — but the bed was set up for the machine: started weed-free, flat, bordered with cedar boards to contain the robot, with plants spaced 18 inches apart.

sources.title: Can a Robot Weed Your Garden? I Tested the Tertill Weeding Robot to Find Out
sources.claim: The same test warns the robot is unsuitable for ornamental flower beds and any planting space without room to maneuver — i.e., it fails in as-found landscape beds.

sources.title: Electric Sheep debuts new outdoor maintenance robot – Lawn & Landscape
sources.claim: Electric Sheep demonstrated 'Verdie', a robot for edging, trimming and blowing on landscape crews' sites; autonomy was claimed by the developer but only a launch demo and a stated 2024 rollout plan were shown.

sources.developer: Electric Sheep Robotics / Oso Electric Equipment
sources.title: Oso Electric Equipment acquires Electric Sheep Robotics – The Robot Report
sources.claim: By the October 2025 acquisition of Electric Sheep by Oso Electric, the edging/trimming robot is described in the past tense and the shipping commercial product line is autonomous mowers, indicating no fielded professional edging/trimming robot.

tasks.label: Follow planned landscaping designs to determine where to lay sod, sow grass, or plant flowers or foliage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential landscape installation: crew works from a homeowner's planting plan in a private yard, measures bed outlines off the plan, sets out shrubs, perennials and annual flats at the spacings and groupings shown, then digs and plants each one around house walls, walkways, existing trees and utilities.

New lawn by sod at a house or small commercial lot: worker reads the plan to see which areas are sod, then lays sod rolls/slabs over the prepared, graded soil to the shapes shown, butting seams, cutting pieces around beds, curves and hardscape.

Seasonal color rotation on institution-controlled grounds (corporate campus, hotel entry, hospital, municipal park, cemetery): worker follows a bed design showing species, counts and pattern, marks off rows/blocks and plants annual flats into prepared, mulched beds.

Turf establishment by seed on a large graded, obstacle-free area at an institution-controlled facility (new athletic field, park lawn, campus lawn): worker determines from the plan which areas are seeded lawn versus bed, then sows/drills grass seed uniformly over those areas and rolls/covers them.

Stakeout of the landscape plan on a new construction site or subdivision: worker transfers the drawing to the ground before installation — paint/stake bed lines, tree and shrub locations, and sod-versus-seed limits — amid rough graded soil, stockpiles and other trades.

Municipal streetscape / right-of-way work: planting street trees, median beds and sidewalk planters at the locations and spacings the city's design specifies, working next to traffic, curbs and buried utilities.

sources.title: Tiny Surveyor Robot - Terra Model (Cansel)
sources.claim: TinySurveyor Terra is a commercially sold autonomous stakeout robot that drives a site and marks layout lines and points from uploaded digital design data (LandXML/CSV), used on construction and infrastructure sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction pre-marking/stakeout. It is the same act as landscape stakeout — transferring a plan's coordinates and lines onto bare graded ground so crews know where to install — with RTK precision far tighter than bed-line and plant-location tolerances, on the same kind of unimproved site.

sources.title: Autonomous Highway Layout of Drill Holes and Crash Barriers – Spotland, Denmark
sources.claim: A Danish surveying contractor bought a TinySurveyor in 2019 and used it in production layout work on a 32 km Swedish motorway project, showing field deployment rather than a lab demo.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (site stakeout/pre-marking from a digital design); demonstrates sustained real-jobsite use on rough outdoor construction ground.

sources.title: TinyMobileRobots Marks its 1,000,000th Sports Field
sources.claim: TinyLineMarker robots autonomously paint designed layouts onto turf at sports facilities; the company reported its millionth field marked in 2022.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying out a specified geometry on turf at an institution-controlled grounds facility — the same 'transfer the design to the ground' step groundskeepers perform before sodding, seeding or bedding out.

sources.title: Harvey - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: The HV-100 'Harvey' is a commercially purchased autonomous mobile robot that locates, carries and places container plants into specified rectangular or hexagonal spacing patterns in greenhouses and outdoor nursery beds, accurate to better than an inch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: setting out plant material to a specified layout in an outdoor nursery yard. It shows autonomous placement of plants to a design pattern, but it only sets pots on the ground — it does not dig or plant into soil — so it cannot complete an in-ground planting instance.

sources.title: Visser Transplanter Increases Speed, Efficiency - Greenhouse Grower
sources.claim: Visser's PC 20 Gripper is a commercial automatic transplanting machine that plants plugs into bedding-plant flats, pots and planters at programmed positions, at up to 10,000 plants per hour on a fixtured production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled planting of flowers/foliage into a growing medium at positions set by a programmed layout, with the plants and receptacles brought to the machine — the purpose-built-cell form of 'plant flowers per the design'.

sources.title: How Plant Cuttings Automation Continues to Evolve - Greenhouse Grower
sources.claim: Camera-guided robotic cuttings planters from ISO Group and Visser are in routine commercial use in ornamental production, with a robotic arm identifying each cutting and placing it into a tray cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided placement of ornamental plant material into medium at prescribed positions in a purpose-built line — the E1 analogue of planting flowers/foliage to a plan.

sources.title: Advantages of FarmDroid: Automated Seeding and Plant protection
sources.claim: FarmDroid FD20 is a commercially sold solar-powered field robot that seeds autonomously with RTK GPS, placing each seed at a planned position across a prepared field and recording those positions; hundreds of units are working on farms including for flower seed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sowing seed over a designated, prepared open area to a planned pattern. Grass seeding demands looser position tolerance than crop drilling, uses the same prepared soil and open outdoor ground under institutional (farm) control, and the robot works unattended.

sources.title: Kentucky Farmer Aims to Plant 90% of His Corn, Soybeans Autonomously This Spring
sources.claim: Sabanto's retrofit autonomy has been used to perform planting and other field operations autonomously across thousands of acres in commercial US farming, including farmers planting most of a 2,000-acre crop autonomously in 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous seeding of large prepared outdoor areas with tractor-scale implements — the same operation as drilling grass seed over the lawn areas a landscape plan designates on a large graded site.

sources.title: Mechanical Transplanters for Tree Fruit and Vegetable Seedlings | CAES Field Report
sources.claim: University of Georgia extension guidance published in late 2025 states that autonomous (driverless) transplanters remain concepts with very few commercial options, indicating no fielded system that plants nursery/bedding stock into the ground without a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Negative evidence bearing on the closest related task (mechanized in-ground transplanting): even in prepared crop fields, planting seedlings into soil still requires a human-operated machine.

sources.system: TI-42 tractor-mounted big roll installer; g2 turfrack
sources.title: TI-42 Tractor Mounted Big Roll Installer
sources.claim: Sod installation equipment on the market is tractor-mounted and operator-driven: big-roll installers and sod rollers are attachments a person drives, with no autonomous sod-laying product identified.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the sod-laying instance: the state of the art is a human-operated tractor attachment, so no cited system can lay sod to a plan under machine control.

tasks.label: Water lawns, trees, or plants, using portable sprinkler systems, hoses, or watering cans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private residential property: crew member hand-waters newly installed trees and shrubs, annual/perennial beds, and pots on patios and steps using a hose with a breaker nozzle or a watering can; yard layout, gates, slopes, pets and stored objects differ house to house.

Lawn/turf on residential or small commercial properties without an in-ground system: worker connects hoses, sets and repositions oscillating or impact sprinklers to cover the turf, runs each set for a timed period, then drains and coils hoses.

Commercial/institutional grounds (corporate campus, hospital, hotel, apartment complex, school): grounds crew waters annual color beds, entry planters, hanging baskets and newly planted trees from hose reels, quick couplers or a tank/utility vehicle while pedestrians and vehicles move through the site.

Municipal parks, civic plazas and cemeteries: worker waters memorial and display plantings, park flower beds, urns/bowls and young trees, often early morning or evening, with hose, watering can or a water tank, on mapped but uneven paths shared with visitors.

Golf course or sports-field turf: worker hand-waters dry spots and greens (syringing) with hose and quick couplers, waters newly seeded or sodded turf, and sets portable sprinklers on practice areas; timing is dictated by heat and play schedules.

Company nursery holding yard, hoop house/greenhouse, or interior plantscape: worker waters containerized nursery stock in rows on gravel pads or plants on benches with a wand, and indoor planters with a watering can.

sources.date: 2026-01 (RAINOS 2.0 shown at IPM 2026; product in service since ~2022)
sources.title: RAINOS - The autonomous watering robot | Innok Robotics
sources.claim: RAINOS by Innok Robotics is a commercially sold autonomous outdoor watering robot that drives from planting to planting on cemetery grounds, dispenses a set water quantity per grave, and refills itself at filling stations; the vendor states it has been in continuous operation for three years.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: dispensing measured water to individual plantings (grave beds, bowls, urn graves) outdoors — the hose/watering-can work of a groundskeeper, on grounds kept by an institution.

sources.title: Rainos: Autonomer Gießroboter für Friedhöfe und Parkanlagen (bau.bi / B_I MEDIEN)
sources.claim: Trade-press interview with Innok's founder: RAINOS is an autonomous outdoor mobile robot; after an initial site map is made the operator only selects the plantings and per-plant water amounts, and the robot plans its route, waters, refills autonomously and handles ground swells, potholes, uneven paths, gravel and grades, with safety sensing that slows or stops for people.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: watering plants outdoors on institutionally kept grounds (cemeteries, parks, municipal green space customers named); terrain and obstacles match groundskeeping sites.

sources.title: RAINOS: Der autonome Bewässerungsroboter | Gabot.de
sources.claim: Horticulture trade outlet reports RAINOS navigates autonomously to the areas to be watered and supplies each precisely with its individual water requirement, that it refills itself, and that one cemetery gardening firm cut watering labour by more than 70%; named use settings are cemeteries, tree nurseries and parks.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (watering plantings) plus evidence of worker-quality substitution: a commercial operator replaced most of its manual watering labour with the robot.

sources.title: My Lawn Got Nearly Perfect Water Coverage With This Robotic Sprinkler—And I Installed It Myself (Bob Vila)
sources.claim: Irrigreen's robotic sprinkler heads, installed on buried supply lines and run by a smart controller, water residential lawns autonomously; a professional-landscaper reviewer installed the system and reported near-perfect coverage, each electronically controlled head shaping its own spray pattern.
sources.transferJustification: Substitutes for the worker's portable-sprinkler and hose watering of turf: same accepted output (turf given a measured, uniform application) delivered by machine in a lawn plumbed for it.

sources.title: Irrigreen | Total Landscape Care
sources.claim: Landscape trade press reports Irrigreen 3.0, built on the Sprinkler 3 robotic sprinkler head ... Smart Controller 3, is available for purchase and manufactured in the USA.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates commercial availability of the machine that replaces hose-and-portable-sprinkler turf watering.

sources.title: Greenhouse Equipment: Irrigation Systems – Watering Booms | Prospiant
sources.claim: Commercial greenhouse watering booms — motorized nozzle bars travelling on overhead rails and sequenced by an environmental controller — deliver uniform automated watering to containerized crops and remove the need for hand watering.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (watering plants in containers and flats) done by machine in a purpose-built rail-and-bench setting; the boom explicitly displaces the hand watering the worker would otherwise perform.

tasks.label: Maintain or repair tools, equipment, or structures, such as buildings, greenhouses, fences, or benches, using hand or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sharpening and edge maintenance in the shop: removing mower blades and grinding/balancing them, sharpening edger blades, chainsaw chains, pruners, loppers, hedge shears and shovel edges on a bench grinder or belt sander, then re-oiling and re-mounting.

Routine service of gas/battery power equipment in the maintenance shop or yard: washing decks and blowing off debris, greasing fittings, checking/changing engine oil and filters, spark plugs and air filters, restringing trimmer heads, checking tire pressure and fluids across mixed makes of mowers, trimmers, blowers and chainsaws.

Diagnosing and repairing broken equipment in the shop: mower that won't start (carburetor, fuel line, battery), replacing worn belts, pulleys and cables, patching a flat tire, fixing a hydraulic or oil leak, straightening or welding a bent deck or bracket.

Wood fence and gate repair on the grounds: pulling rotted or broken pickets and rails, cutting replacement boards to size, nailing/screwing them to posts, re-securing loose rails and re-hanging gate hardware, working outdoors on uneven ground in whatever weather.

Repairing site amenities in a park or on campus grounds: replacing weathered slats on benches and picnic tables, tightening or replacing rusted bolts, sanding and repainting/staining, resetting a leaning sign post or trash-enclosure board.

In-place repair of buildings and greenhouses: patching and painting shed/greenhouse walls and trim, replacing a cracked greenhouse pane or torn poly film, repairing vents, doors, hinges and latches, clearing/refitting gutters, resetting a fence post in concrete, small masonry or carpentry patch work.

sources.system: Stäubli TX2-90 in Knecht E 50 RT robot-based knife sharpening system (GLAESS integration)
sources.developer: Stäubli / Knecht Maschinenbau / GLAESS Software & Automation
sources.title: Sharpening knives with a robot | Stäubli United States
sources.claim: A Stäubli TX2-90 robot integrated into Knecht E 50 RT machines performs fully automated sharpening of used knives, handling each knife from a magazine, laser-measuring its worn and unique geometry, and grinding it in batch size 1 for meat-processing plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restoring the cutting edge of worn hand blades. Transfer: like a groundskeeper's mower blade, pruner or shovel edge, each used knife has a different worn shape; the cell measures it and grinds a correct edge autonomously with the workpiece fixtured and presented, the same objects (steel edged tools) and precision class.

sources.system: FANUC LR Mate 200iD with force sensing (material removal application)
sources.title: Robotic Cutting, Deburring, Polishing, Buffing & More | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC force-sensing material-removal robots cut, grind and finish metal blades and sharpen dies with repeatable geometry in industrial cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic grinding/edge finishing of steel blades. Transfer: mower and edger blade sharpening is force-controlled abrasive edge grinding on fixtured steel parts, the same operation, tooling and tolerance the cited cells already deliver.

sources.system: Yaskawa Motoman pallet repair systems (dismantler, board replacement, nailing)
sources.date: undated application page retrieved 2026-07; robotic pallet repair lines in European plants reported since 2013
sources.title: Pallet Repair | Yaskawa
sources.claim: Yaskawa Motoman robotic systems are used in pallet repair centres to sort damaged wooden pallets, dismantle them, replace damaged board elements and nail replacements, with conveyor handling in and out.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repairing nailed softwood structures by finding the broken board, prying it out and nailing a replacement. Transfer: fence pickets/rails and bench or picnic-table slats are the same softwood boards, same nail/fastener sizes and same tolerance, when the panel is presented fixtured on a conveyor as at E1.

sources.developer: research team (published in Sustainability, MDPI); demonstrated at SAIE Bologna
sources.title: Woodot: An AI-Driven Mobile Robotic System for Sustainable Defect Repair in Custom Glulam Beams
sources.claim: Woodot, an autonomous mobile robot with a six-DOF arm and a vision pipeline, locates surface knot defects on geometrically variable glulam timber beams and repairs them by milling out the defect and inserting plugs on a workshop floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous perception-driven repair of defects in wooden members. Transfer: shows a robot can find damage on a non-standard timber workpiece and repair it with a power tool in a shop setting, the perception step needed for bench/fence board repair at E1.

sources.title: RoboTire Installs First Revolutionary Tire Changing System at Discount Tire | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: RoboTire systems installed at a Discount Tire store change four passenger-car tires in under 25 minutes using cameras and machine learning, running the sequence autonomously once an operator initiates it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated servicing of powered machines. It substantiates only one standardized bolt-off/bolt-on operation on a fixed vehicle geometry, not the multi-step fluid, filter, ignition and drivetrain servicing or fault diagnosis of mixed small-engine equipment, so it is cited to bound the negative judgments.

sources.title: Force Sensor | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC robots with force sensing perform force-controlled sanding of wood ..., and deburr castings with controlled contact.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sanding/finishing of wooden furniture. Transfer: sanding a bench or picnic-table slat before repainting is the same force-controlled abrasive operation on the same material and part size, with the workpiece fixtured as at E1.

tasks.label: Rake, mulch, and compost leaves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Autumn whole-property cleanup at a private residence: backpack-blow and hand-rake leaves off the lawn, out of shrub/foundation beds, from fence lines, window wells and around ornamentals, off the drive and walks; windrow onto tarps or into a leaf-loader hose; load into a truck box and haul off to a compost/yard-waste site. Uneven turf, pets, toys, hoses, wet and matted leaves.

Autumn cleanup on institutional/commercial grounds (office park, apartment complex, school or hospital campus, cemetery) under a maintenance contract: blow leaves out of beds and off large turf areas into windrows, vacuum them with a truck-mounted leaf loader or push blower crew, haul to the on-site compost yard or disposal facility; done on a schedule while occupants, cars and pedestrians are present.

Routine seasonal clearing of leaves and debris from paved surfaces: entry walks, plazas, courtyards, stairs, parking lots and residential driveways/patios; blown or swept clean, debris pushed onto turf/beds or collected, surface left presentable, repeated many times through leaf season.

Mulch-mowing a typical fall leaf load into the turf during mowing visits: multiple passes with a mulching deck over lawns, campus turf or athletic fields covered by a moderate-to-heavy layer of leaves, until no leaf layer remains visible on the grass.

Season-long light-litter management on maintained small and medium lawns: thin, continuous leaf drop is chopped or swept off the grass on each visit, keeping the turf clear without a dedicated cleanup crew.

On-site composting of the leaves collected: forming and turning/aerating leaf windrows on the grounds' compost pad, monitoring the piles, and re-turning them through the season so the material breaks down into usable leaf mold.

sources.title: Yarbo Blower — product page
sources.claim: Yarbo's Blower module is a commercially sold attachment for the Yarbo tracked yard robot that autonomously drives mapped work areas in residential yards and pushes leaves and debris toward a designated area.

sources.title: I reviewed the giant Yarbo lawn care robot – here's why the $10k price isn't as crazy as it seems | Stuff
sources.claim: Independent long-term review of the Yarbo system reports the blower module clearing a residential patio and garden path of leaves in about five minutes.

sources.title: Yarbo Blower - reviews/opinions — Yarbo Forum

sources.title: Driverless sweepers — Transport Engineer

tasks.label: Haul or spread topsoil, or spread straw over seeded soil to hold soil in place.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential property (private yard): bulk topsoil dumped on the driveway or curb; worker shuttles it by wheelbarrow through gates and around obstacles, dumps it into planting beds, low spots and thin lawn areas, then shovels and rakes it to an even depth, feathering it around shrubs, tree flares, irrigation heads and hardscape edges.

New-construction or renovation lot (residential subdivision or commercial site): dump trucks deliver bulk topsoil onto a rough-graded open area; worker uses a skid steer, compact loader or tractor with bucket/box blade to haul the piles across the site and spread 4-6 inches of soil to finished grade before seeding or sodding.

Newly seeded lawn area at a house or small commercial property: worker carries straw or seed-mulch bales to the seeded ground, breaks them open and hand-scatters a thin, even layer with a pitchfork or by hand over the seed, covering slopes, swales and edges without smothering the seed.

Large graded slope or disturbed area at a commercial, highway or construction-adjacent site: crew uses a truck- or trailer-mounted straw blower (with tackifier) to blanket several acres of seeded soil for erosion control, one worker feeding bales and another aiming the discharge hose across banks and ditches.

Institution-controlled turf grounds (school athletic field, park, campus lawn, golf course): sand/soil topdressing or topsoil is hauled to the field with a tractor/utility vehicle and spread in even passes with a towed topdresser or box blade over a large open turf area, then dragged/brushed in.

tasks.label: Shovel snow from walks, driveways, or parking lots, and spread salt in those areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private residence on a snow-maintenance route: clear 2–8 inches of fresh snow from the driveway and the front walk with a shovel or walk-behind blower, then broadcast ice melt on the walk and apron. Layout differs house to house (planters, cars in the drive, uneven pavers).

Private residence in difficult conditions: heavy wet snow or refrozen slush, drifts against the garage, the plow ridge left at the apron, front steps and porch, clearance around a parked car — largely hand-shovel work, followed by ice melt on steps and walk.

Commercial/institutional parking lot (retail center, office park, hospital, campus lot): clear drive lanes and open bays with a plow truck, loader or compact plow rig overnight, stack snow at designated piles, then spread bulk rock salt from a hopper spreader over the cleared lot.

Campus, apartment-complex or hospital grounds walkway network: clear a mile or more of sidewalks and connecting paths with a sidewalk machine or shovel crew on a mapped route, then apply granular deicer along the same paths. Institution controls the grounds and sets zero-tolerance clearing standards.

Building entrances, stairs, ramps, dock aprons, courtyards and curb cuts on a managed property: hand-shovel tight areas around bollards, railings, planters and bike racks, chip refrozen ice, and hand-spread ice melt on steps and landings.

Public sidewalk frontage along a city street abutting the client property: shovel/blow the walk and the plow ridge at the curb and crosswalk cut, with pedestrians passing, parked cars at the curb, and no control over what is on the walk.

tasks.label: Care for natural turf fields, making sure the underlying soil has the required composition to allow proper drainage and to support the grasses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled core/solid-tine aeration of a full-size natural turf athletic field (school, municipal or college soccer/football field) or golf fairway: hitch a tine aerator to a compact tractor (or run a walk-behind unit on smaller areas), make overlapping passes at set depth over 1-2 acres, work around sprinkler heads, drain covers and goal anchors, then break up or sweep the cores with a drag mat or sweeper. Field is closed to users while the work is done.

Topdressing the field after aeration to change the surface soil composition: haul and load 20-40 tons of sand or sand/compost mix from a stockpile, spread it uniformly to a set depth with a tow-behind or self-propelled topdresser over the whole field, refill the hopper repeatedly, then brush or drag the material into the aeration holes and blow off the surface.

Assessing soil condition and applying amendments: pull soil cores on a grid for lab testing, check compaction and moisture with a probe/penetrometer, then calibrate a broadcast or drop spreader and apply lime, gypsum, sand-based amendment or granular fertilizer at prescribed rates across the field, or spray wetting agents/liquid nutrition over the same area.

Drainage problem work on a turf field: after heavy rain, walk the field to locate ponding and waterlogged areas, clear and flush silt, clippings and debris from catch basins, inlet grates and drain outlets, cut sand slits/gravel bands with a trencher or sand-injection machine and backfill with sand, and fill in ponding low spots with topsoil/sand mix.

Renovating worn, compacted, high-traffic areas of the field (goalmouths, sidelines, pitcher's mound surrounds, gate entries): scarify or rototill the compacted soil, barrow in and shovel out soil/sand mix, rake and level to grade, seed or cut and lay sod patches, tamp or roll and water in — done by hand and with walk-behind equipment around goals, bases, irrigation heads and fences, often while adjacent areas remain in use.

sources.system: Sabanto autonomy system (Sabanto Steward retrofit kit)

sources.claim: Sabanto's retrofit tractor autonomy system let a commercial farm run a full ground-engaging tillage operation autonomously across a large field, i.e. an unmanned tractor pulling an implement in planned overlapping passes.

It is the same operation class as turf aeration — a tractor operating a ground-engaging implement at set depth in overlapping RTK-guided passes over an open field, with headland turns and implement raise/lower, and no discrete-object manipulation. Precision (pass overlap of a few centimetres, depth control) and machine class match a tractor-mounted turf aerator or topdresser.

sources.title: SwarmFarm and Roesner develop autonomous fertiliser spreader — Future Farming
sources.claim: SwarmFarm's SwarmBot platform performs fully autonomous, unmanned application operations (spot spraying, blanket spraying, mowing) on commercial farms, and has been deployed at scale (over 1.3 million commercial acres, 64,000 operating hours in 2022).

Applying lime, gypsum, granular fertilizer or wetting agents to a turf field is the same operation — metered application at a prescribed rate over a bounded area in guided passes — with comparable rate accuracy requirements and the same machine class (a self-propelled carrier towing a spreader/sprayer).

The turf version is the same act — navigate to GPS points, bore a core to consistent depth in firm soil, bag and label it — on a flatter, better-mapped surface; the article notes the robot bores to consistent depth in hard soil, matching the precision required for turf soil testing.

sources.title: AMP Mowers — FireFly Robotics
sources.claim: FireFly Automatix AMP autonomous fairway mowers are in customer operation at golf courses, running multiple machines across fairways and transiting between them without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fairway mowing. It establishes that a full-size, implement-carrying turf machine can run unattended on managed natural turf at a golf facility — the same surface, obstacles (heads, bunkers, cart paths) and turf-damage tolerances that aeration and topdressing passes face.

sources.system: Turf Tank One / Turf Tank Two line-marking robot
sources.title: Fast Growing Turf Tank for Autonomous Sports Field Marking — Inside Unmanned Systems
sources.claim: Turf Tank's GNSS-guided line-marking robots operate autonomously on natural turf athletic fields at over a thousand US schools, parks departments and universities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous GNSS-guided navigation and material (paint) application on athletic fields. It shows the institution-controlled sports field itself is a workable robotic environment — surveyed boundaries, repeatable coverage paths, staff-supervised operation — which is the environment the aeration/topdressing instances occur in.

tasks.label: Mix and spray or spread fertilizers, herbicides, or insecticides onto grass, shrubs, or trees, using hand or automatic sprayers or spreaders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential lawn granular application: crew member loads a broadcast/push spreader with fertilizer or weed-and-feed at the truck, calibrates the rate, and walks the front and back yard of a customer's home, working around beds, walkways, fences and gates, children's toys and pet waste, then blows granules off drives and walks.

Residential/small-commercial liquid turf application: mixes herbicide or liquid fertilizer concentrate with water in the truck-mounted tank, drags a hose-reel gun or uses a ride-on/backpack sprayer to blanket-treat the lawn at label rate, avoiding drift onto beds, cars and neighbouring property.

Large institution-controlled turf (golf course, sports complex, campus or municipal park): mixes product in the maintenance-yard mix station and applies fertilizer, fungicide or herbicide with a boom sprayer or ride-on spreader over greens, fairways, fields or large open lawns, usually before play/opening hours.

Ornamental shrub and tree applications: mixes insecticide/fungicide or liquid feed and applies it with a high-pressure hose-reel spray gun (or deep-root injector) to foliage of ornamental trees and shrubs on residential and commercial properties, achieving canopy coverage while controlling drift near windows, cars and people.

Spot treatment: backpack or hand-pump sprayer used to kill weeds in mulch beds among ornamentals, in pavement cracks, along fence lines, curb and parking-lot edges across a varied route of properties, discriminating weeds from desirable plants.

tasks.label: Attach wires from planted trees to support stakes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential install: after planting a 1.5–2" caliper shade or ornamental tree in a homeowner's lawn or bed, the worker drives two stakes outside the root ball, loops No. 9 wire through rubber hose sleeves (or arbor straps) around the trunk at the lowest point that holds it upright, runs each wire to a stake, twists/ties it off, and tensions so the trunk can still flex. Uneven turf, mulch, irrigation heads, adjacent shrubs.

Commercial/institutional landscape installation day (office park, retail center, school or apartment complex): crew installs a run of 10–40 trees in parking-lot islands, lawn panels and mulched beds; each tree gets 2–3 stakes with wire-and-hose ties or strap kits, plumbed and tensioned; freshly graded soil, mulch piles, machinery and other trades moving through.

Large specimen tree (3–6"+ caliper B&B or multi-stem) guyed with three cable guy wires at 45–60°, through hose sleeves around the trunk or crotch, down to long stakes, deadmen or duckbill anchors, tensioned with turnbuckles and flagged; ladder or bucket work, judgment on tension and wire height on the trunk.

Municipal street/parkway tree: 2 stakes plus wire or strap ties on a tree planted in a sidewalk cutout, tree lawn or median; confined pit, curb and pavement, pedestrians and traffic passing, utilities marked, warning flags added to guy wires.

Maintenance round on managed grounds (park, campus, HOA, cemetery kept to a standard): inspect previously staked trees, re-attach or replace broken or girdling wires and ties, re-tension after wind events, re-plumb the tree and re-secure the wire to the stake; trees scattered across mown turf and beds.

sources.title: New generation of rebar-tying robot TyBot 3.0 hits the market | Equipment World
sources.claim: TyBOT is a commercially deployed, autonomous wire-tying robot that uses computer vision to locate rebar intersections on bridge decks ... twist-tie them; it is the closest deployed automation of 'tie a wire around two members', but it operates on a rigid, coplanar rebar grid from a gantry frame spanning the deck and does not loop or tension a wire around a variable-diameter trunk and route it to a ground stake.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wire twist-tying of two crossing members. Transfer fails: TyBOT works on a flat, regular grid of rigid steel bars of known diameter in one plane, forming a fixed twist at a contact point; tree staking requires forming a hose-sleeved loop around a living trunk of varying caliper, routing the wire diagonally to a stake, and tensioning to a specified slack. No cited demonstration of that geometry or tension control.

sources.system: INFACO AT1000 automatic vineyard tying machine (also MAX tapener, Pellenc Fixion 2)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: tying a plant to a stake/trellis. Transfer fails on autonomy — the device is hand-carried and hand-positioned by a worker for every tie, so it is a power tool rather than a robotic system, and cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.system: CubiX with RGB-D-camera-based multi small flying anchors
sources.title: An RGB-D Camera-Based Multi-Small Flying Anchors Control for Wire-Driven Robots Connecting to the Environment
sources.claim: A research system, the wire-driven parallel robot CubiX with small flying anchors, autonomously attached its own wire to a tree branch outdoors; this is a laboratory-grade demonstration of wire attachment to a tree, not installation of guy wires between a planted tree and ground stakes at a specified tension.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously attaching a wire to a tree in an outdoor setting. Transfer fails: the wire originates from the robot and is anchored for the robot's own locomotion; there is no trunk-protecting sleeve, no stake, no tension specification, and no evidence of worker-quality reliability or repetition.

tasks.label: Fill sprayer tanks with water and chemicals, according to formulas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lawn/turf care technician at the company branch yard fills a 200-400 gal truck-mounted tank: pulls the rig to the fill station, meters water from a bulk tank, adds liquid fertilizer and herbicide concentrates from bulk shuttles/jugs per the day's route formula, agitates, and logs the load.

Tree-care/ornamental or nursery-greenhouse technician mixes a 25-100 gal skid tank in the shop or on the mix-load pad: partially fills with water, measures liquid concentrates in a jug and weighs/pours wettable powders or water-soluble packets into an inductor, tops off and agitates.

Right-of-way, utility, forestry or park crew mixes small hand-carried tanks (4-gal backpack, 15-25 gal ATV/spot tank) at the truck tailgate in the field: measures a few ounces of concentrate plus surfactant/dye with a cup, adds water from a carboy or nurse tank, shakes/agitates.

Agricultural/custom applicator loads an 800-1,200 gal self-propelled sprayer from a tender trailer at the field edge or a farm chemical shed: water/carrier metered in, multiple liquid products drawn from plumbed mini-bulk shuttles and jugs, AMS or dry products added, containers rinsed.

Aerial applicator ground crew (fixed-wing/helicopter airstrip or drone launch pad) batches loads per recipe in a mix tank and pumps them into the aircraft hopper or drone tank between flights, under time pressure to keep the aircraft turning.

Small-batch mixing at the job site: technician mixes 2-5 gallons of herbicide/insecticide solution into a backpack sprayer or hand can on a customer's driveway, a roadside right-of-way, or a wooded lot, measuring concentrate from a jug into a graduated cup with water carried on the truck.

Farm/orchard/co-op chemical fill site: applicator loads a 800-1,200 gal sprayer or nurse tank with a multi-product tank mix (herbicide, adjuvant, fungicide) drawn from mini-bulk shuttles, jugs and water-soluble packets via an induction hopper, with agitation and sequencing requirements.

Greenhouse/nursery mixing room: grower weighs out wettable-powder or WDG fungicide/miticide on a scale, dissolves it in a slurry pail, adds it plus a surfactant to a 50-100 gal spray rig or stock tank for an injector, and cleans up in an enclosed chemical room.

Golf course / sports-turf chemical building: technician mixes a multi-product tank load (fungicide + growth regulator + wetting agent) into a 300 gal turf sprayer at a covered mix/load pad with metered water, inductor and rinse equipment, early morning before play.

tasks.label: Start motors and engage machinery, such as sprayer agitators or pumps or portable spray equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lawn / tree-and-shrub service route: technician parks the service truck at a residential or small commercial property, starts the auxiliary engine on the skid-mounted tank rig, engages the pump and the mechanical or jet agitation to keep the mix suspended, pressurizes the hose reel and spray gun, then shuts down and moves to the next stop. Conditions differ yard to yard (gates, pets, parked cars, slopes, uneven driveways).

Portable spray equipment for spot work: pull-starting a gasoline backpack mist blower or two-stroke power sprayer, or engaging a battery/hand-pump backpack, to treat landscape beds, fence lines, hardscape cracks, brush clumps and turf spots on customer or public grounds; equipment is carried to the work on foot over unimproved ground.

Broadacre / row-crop application by a farm or custom applicator: start the diesel on a self-propelled sprayer or tractor with a pull-type sprayer, engage the PTO- or hydraulic-driven pump and tank agitation, prime and pressurize the boom sections before beginning the pass; open field, variable ground and weather.

Orchard, vineyard or field-nursery airblast spraying: start the tractor, engage the PTO that drives the fan and the pump, run tank agitation, and set the sprayer working before entering the rows, often at night or in early morning.

Right-of-way, roadside, utility corridor or forestry application: start the auxiliary engine on a truck- or ATV-mounted rig at the roadside, engage the pump and agitator, pressurize a handgun or low-volume boom for guardrail, ditch, powerline-corridor or brush treatment, with traffic, rough terrain and no controlled premises.

Application inside or on the grounds of a controlled facility: greenhouse or container nursery boom/tube-rail sprayer, or a golf course, sports complex, campus or industrial site; start the pump and agitator (or the fill-station agitator at the mix/load pad) and run the spray unit through the treatment.

tasks.label: Lift, push, and swing nozzles, hoses, and tubes to direct spray over designated areas.

Agricultural spraying on farms: positioning and directing boom-sprayer nozzles over row-crop fields or air-blast/handgun nozzles down orchard and vineyard rows, on private farmland with planted rows and mapped field boundaries.
Greenhouse and nursery spraying: moving spray booms, lances or hose reels along benches, pipe rails and container blocks to cover crops inside a grower's production facility.

Institutional grounds: golf courses, sports fields, parks, campuses and cemeteries - pulling hose and swinging spray guns or steering boom sprayers over designated turf areas and shrub beds on premises controlled and maintained by the institution.

Rights-of-way and industrial/roadside vegetation control: directing handgun or boom-truck nozzles along utility corridors, rail lines, roadsides, ditches and industrial yards, over rough ground taken as found with traffic and public access.

Agricultural or right-of-way applicator cleaning out a self-propelled or pull-type boom sprayer at the farm/co-op shop or wash pad between chemical products: runs the rinse-tank cycle three times, flushes booms, removes and cleans nozzle tips and screens plus the tank sump strainer, pressure-washes the exterior and boom, greases pivots, refuels/adds DEF.

Periodic exterior wash-down only: the application vehicle or rig (tank truck, pickup with skid unit, spreader/sprayer truck) is driven to a wash pad or commercial truck wash to remove mud, road film, dust and chemical residue from body and tank; no disassembly or mechanical service involved.

Servicing during a job at the treatment site (roadside right-of-way, field edge, park, utility corridor): clears a plugged nozzle or clogged suction screen, cleans a filter, refuels the pump engine or backpack blower from a fuel can, tightens a leaking fitting or swaps a worn tip with hand tools, in weather and on uneven ground.

Shop-bench servicing of small application equipment: backpack and handheld sprayers, hand cans, hose reels, granular spreaders and gas-powered mist blowers - disassemble, flush lines, clean filters/screens and nozzles, replace worn seals, O-rings and tips, and service the small gas engine (fuel, oil, spark plug, air filter).

Aerial applicator at an ag airstrip: post-flight wash-down of the airframe to remove chemical and insect residue, rinse of the hopper and spray boom/nozzles, cleaning of filters, plus refueling and greasing before the next load.

Same applicator making the fluid hookups at the mix/fill station: coupling cam-lock and quick-connect fill, suction, agitation and inductor hoses between nurse tank, chemical inductor and the sprayer tank parked on the pad; fittings are standard and the pad layout is fixed.

Right-of-way, roadside or forestry crew: connecting high-pressure hose from a truck-mounted reel to a handgun, and reconfiguring between boomless off-center nozzle clusters and handgun tips as terrain changes (ditch banks, guardrail, brush lines); work done on the shoulder or along rail/utility corridors in traffic, mud and wind.

Greenhouse/nursery or interior-landscape applicator: connecting a hose from a fixed injector/pump outlet or hose bib to a spray lance and installing the nozzle selected for the crop and pest, on a fixed bench-and-aisle layout with standard equipment.

Mid-job troubleshooting: a clogged, worn or off-pattern tip or a leaking fitting found during application; the applicator removes the cap, clears or replaces tip and screen, re-seats the gasket and re-couples or wrench-tightens the hose fitting, usually wet, chemically contaminated and beside the road or in the field.

instances.label: Residential lawn service call: technician walks a customer's suburban yard, parts the turf canopy, tugs turf, pulls plugs and digs to check roots/thatch, and distinguishes brown patch, dollar spot, red thread, pythium, grub or chinch bug damage, dog urine, drought or mower injury, then selects fungicide/insecticide or cultural remedy.

Ornamental tree and shrub inspection on residential/commercial landscapes: examines leaves (both surfaces), needles, twigs, bark and canopy of diverse woody species for anthracnose, needle cast, scale, mites, borers, root/crown decay; often overhead or in dense plantings, and prescribes trunk injection, foliar spray or soil drench.

Managed institutional turf (golf course, sports field, school/office campus): scouting greens, fairways or athletic turf for outbreaks; institution controls access and keeps turf to a maintenance standard; diagnosis triggers a preventive or curative fungicide program.

Agricultural field crop scouting by a custom/co-op applicator: walking or driving corn, soybean or specialty crop fields to identify foliar disease (tar spot, rust, white mold, leaf spot) and compare to action thresholds before a fungicide pass; open field, variable terrain and weather.

Greenhouse or nursery scouting: inspecting benched crops and container stock on a fixed row/pipe-rail layout for powdery mildew, botrytis, downy mildew, thrips/mite damage; results feed the IPM program and targeted spraying.

instances.label: Residential or small-commercial lawn seeding: technician walks a broadcast/drop spreader over a home yard (new lawn after grading, or fall overseeding after aeration), working around flower beds, trees, fences, driveways and walkways, calibrating rate, keeping seed off hardscape, sometimes tacking down a thin straw layer by hand.

Erosion-control seeding on a construction site or highway right-of-way: crew runs a truck- or trailer-mounted hydroseeder (seed/mulch/tackifier slurry) or a straw blower with asphalt-emulsion tackifier over graded slopes, ditches and shoulders, aiming the hose or blower tower at 2:1-3:1 banks with rutted, muddy, obstacle-strewn ground and passing traffic.

Dry seed application over rough, hard-to-access ground: broadcasting a native/conservation grass mix on steep banks, waterways, burn scars or reclamation ground where no mulch blowing is specified, currently done with hand-crank or ATV/aerial broadcast application.

Institution-managed turf: overseeding a park, athletic field complex, golf course rough/fairway, school campus or cemetery with a ride-on or tow-behind broadcast spreader over large maintained turf areas with known layout, fixed obstacles, and grounds staff controlling access.

Large-acreage open-ground seeding: sod farm, pasture renovation, cover-crop or hay-grass seeding, or a fenced solar/industrial site, using a tractor-drawn broadcast seeder or drill over open, prepared ground in long parallel passes.

Spot repair seeding: patching small bare areas after trenching, utility work, sod damage or landscape installation - loosening soil, hand-spreading seed and starter fertilizer on patches of a few square feet to a few hundred, then covering with straw or a cut erosion blanket in tight spaces between plantings and structures.
