instances.label: Residential curbside pruning/removal job: chipper towed behind the chip truck and parked at the curb of a private home; ground worker drags cut limbs and leafy brush across the lawn, over a sidewalk and around parked cars, feeds them butt-first into the infeed hopper, keeps the discharge chute aimed into the truck, watches for pedestrians, pets and passing traffic, and clears occasional jams.

Utility line-clearance / roadside right-of-way crew: chipper set up on a road shoulder or ditch area with cones and traffic control; brush dropped from under conductors on sloped, brushy or muddy ground is dragged uphill, sorted from vines and wire debris, and fed continuously for hours while the rig moves pole to pole.

Municipal park, school/corporate campus or golf course grounds: institution-controlled premises with service roads and turf; crew prunes trees and feeds limbs and hedge brush into a chipper parked on a path or lot, working around irrigation heads, benches, roots and occasional visitors.

Storm-damage or emergency cleanup: tangled, wind-thrown limbs mixed with fence pieces, leaves, wire and debris, often in the dark or rain, on blocked streets and driveways; material is heavy, unpredictable in shape and must be triaged before it is fed into the chipper.

Processing at the contractor's yard or a municipal green-waste/transfer facility: accumulated brush and cuttings dumped on a pad are re-processed through a brush chipper or tub/horizontal grinder, with a loader or hand crew moving piles to the infeed; premises controlled by the employer or municipality.

sources.system: Konecranes automated waste handling cranes (Riikinvoima plant, Leppavirta, Finland)
sources.title: Perfect combination for Riikinvoima: Fully automated cranes and remote operating station
sources.claim: At the Riikinvoima energy plant, Konecranes grab cranes take delivered mixed waste from the reception hall/bunker and load it into a shredder, then feed the shredded material into the boiler.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grab-crane feeding of a shredder. Bulky heterogeneous waste is grasped from a dumped pile and inserted into a size-reduction machine's infeed - the same grasp-and-feed action, object variability and low placement precision as feeding limbs and brush into a chipper.

sources.system: Konecranes automated waste handling cranes with Remote Operating Station
sources.title: Perfect combination: Fully automated cranes and remote operating station
sources.claim: The Riikinvoima waste cranes run unattended in full automatic mode most of the time, with staff only supervising from a remote operating station.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the shredder-feeding crane cycle is autonomous rather than teleoperated, with only occasional remote intervention.

sources.date: 2025 (product line, in service at biomass plants for years)
sources.title: Biomass Cranes for Efficient Fuel Handling
sources.claim: Konecranes CXT biomass cranes are unmanned, fully automated grab cranes that move wood-based fuel from a plant's reception pocket to storage and continuously feed the combustion line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated grab handling of loose woody biomass (chips, bark, forest residue) from a tipping/reception area into a process infeed - the same material class and unstructured pile geometry as brush waiting to be chipped, handled with no operator present.

sources.system: ZenRobotics autonomous sorting line / Heavy Picker (Kuljetusrinki Ltd installation)
sources.title: AI and autonomous robot for waste management - Construction Briefing
sources.claim: ZenRobotics AI sorting lines use autonomous robot arms that identify and pick wood pieces (up to 40 kg on the Heavy Picker) out of mixed construction and demolition waste on a conveyor and drop them into designated chutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous vision-guided grasping of heavy, irregular wood pieces presented on a conveyor and depositing them into an opening - comparable objects and placement precision to laying limbs onto a chipper infeed table.

sources.system: Vermeer SmartFeed / SmartCrush (AX17 and other brush chippers)
sources.title: Vermeer Releases AX17 Brush Chipper that Includes Exclusive SmartFeed and SmartCrush Systems
sources.claim: Production brush chippers regulate their own feed: Vermeer's SmartFeed control monitors engine rpm and automatically stops, reverses and works material back and forth without an operator at the controls.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the 'operate the chipping equipment' half of the task: feed-rate control and jam response are already executed by the machine itself under closed-loop control.

sources.title: Video: Gravis Robotics unveils earthmoving autonomy platform
sources.claim: Deployed outdoor heavy-equipment autonomy (Gravis Robotics retrofits on excavators and wheel loaders at construction sites and quarries) performs bulk earthmoving and truck loading, not grasping and feeding loose woody debris.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to characterize the state of outdoor autonomy: bucket-based bulk material moving on job sites, with no demonstrated dragging, sorting and butt-first feeding of springy brush beside a running chipper, pedestrians and traffic.

tasks.label: Operate boom trucks, loaders, stump chippers, brush chippers, tractors, power saws, trucks, sprayers, and other equipment and tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ground-crew wood processing at a residential or commercial tree job: running a chainsaw to buck downed limbs and trunk sections lying in a cluttered yard or street, dragging brush to the curb and hand-feeding it butt-first into a towed drum/disc brush chipper, and blowing chips into the truck box, with homeowners, parked cars and passers-by nearby.

Aerial cutting work: setting up and operating a boom truck / bucket lift (or crane) to position at height and running a chainsaw or pole saw to make selective cuts in the canopy of a yard or street tree near a house roof, fence, service drop or energized conductor, including rigging pieces down; also mechanized side-trim boom saw work on utility rights-of-way with traffic passing.

Stump grinding at a customer site: walking or driving a self-propelled stump grinder through a gate or across a lawn, positioning it around fences, irrigation, driveways and hidden rock, sweeping the cutter wheel through the stump and surface roots to depth, then cleaning up grindings.

Material handling with a loader: operating a knuckleboom grapple loader on a chip/log truck, or a mini skid-steer/compact loader, to pick up heavy limbs, trunk rounds and debris from a lawn or street and load them onto the truck without damaging turf, curbs or vehicles.

Transport and positioning: driving the chip truck towing the chipper (and stump grinder trailer) from the yard to job sites over public roads, spotting the truck and trailer at the curb or in a driveway for the day's work, and making dump runs to the chip yard.

Sprayer operation for plant health care: driving a truck- or ATV-mounted air-blast/hydraulic sprayer to trees and shrubs and applying insecticide, fungicide, fertilizer or herbicide over the canopy or basal area, on properties or along rights-of-way and in row plantings.

sources.title: John Deere acquires semi-autonomous sprayer company GUSS
sources.claim: GUSS autonomous orchard sprayers spray tree crops row-by-row without a driver, supervised remotely; hundreds of machines in commercial use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: orchard spraying. Same equipment class (air-blast sprayer) applying the same chemistries onto tree canopies, with autonomous navigation between tree rows; the arborist spraying instance uses the same machine and the same targets.

sources.system: Konecranes CXT biomass crane / waste-to-energy and biomass crane automation
sources.title: Waste to energy and biomass crane automation | Konecranes
sources.claim: Fully automated, operator-free grab cranes handle wood fuel and biomass in power-plant bays, moving material from the tipping area to storage and filling process hoppers on their own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grapple handling of wood material. A grab crane picking piles of logs/chips/biomass and feeding them into a process hopper is the same physical operation as a knuckleboom loader grabbing limbs and rounds, and as feeding a chipper, done in a purpose-built bay.

sources.system: USNR optimization and controls, automated bucking line (Dempsey Wood Products)
sources.title: Dempsey automates bucking line with optimization and controls from USNR
sources.claim: Sawmill bucking lines are automated: logs conveyed past scanners are cross-cut to optimized lengths by machine-commanded saws rather than by an operator judging each cut.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bucking logs with powered saws. Cross-cutting stems to length is the same cutting operation a groundman performs with a chainsaw; in the mill the log is presented on a conveyor and the saws are machine-commanded.

sources.developer: sawmill equipment industry (USNR, Autolog and others)
sources.title: Sawlines: Scanners, Computers Optimize Machines - Pallet Enterprise
sources.claim: Scanner-driven optimized bucking, in which conveyed logs are measured and automatically cut to length, is standard equipment in North American mills.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sawing wood to length. Confirms that machine-controlled saws cutting presented logs is routine industrial practice, i.e. the E1 form of 'operate power saws'.

sources.title: Outrider builds first-in-industry safety system for driverless yard operations
sources.claim: Driverless yard trucks autonomously locate, hitch, move and spot trailers in logistics-hub yards with mixed traffic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving and spotting a heavy truck with a towed trailer. Same vehicle class and the same precise trailer positioning a crew performs when setting the chip truck and chipper for the day's work.

sources.title: Aurora Innovation, Inc. - Form 8-K, Second Quarter 2025 Shareholder Letter
sources.claim: Driverless Class 8 trucks run commercial freight on public highways with no person aboard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: over-the-road driving of a heavy truck. Covers the highway transport leg of moving the crew's truck and towed equipment, but not curbside job-site setup.

sources.title: Robot avatar safely trims trees around active power lines
sources.claim: Robotic trimming of trees near energized power lines has been demonstrated only as a human-controlled avatar; a person on the ground drives every motion.

sources.title: A robotic solution for safer tree trimming | Penn Today
sources.claim: The current startup effort at robotic canopy tree cutting is an early prototype controlled by a worker from the ground.

sources.title: Fully Autonomous Drone Harvests Its First Tree in World First | Wood Central
sources.claim: An autonomous drone completed a first single-tree harvest in a production forest - flying to the tree, delimbing, felling and carrying the stem clear with nobody at the controls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial delimbing and felling of small plantation stems in open forest thinning; cited as the closest autonomous analogue to canopy saw work, though it is a one-tree first with no structures, wires or selective pruning.

sources.system: Energreen RoboEVO/RoboMAX with stump grinder attachment; Bandit SG-75W wireless remote
sources.title: Stump Grinder for remote control tool carrier robot | Energreen
sources.claim: Field stump grinding by machine is available only as radio-remote-controlled tool carriers and remote-console grinders driven by an operator with a handset.

sources.developer: La Hera et al., SLU / Umea University
sources.title: Exploring the feasibility of autonomous forestry operations: Results from the first experimental unmanned machine
sources.claim: A research unmanned forwarder autonomously drove forest terrain and picked logs off the ground with its crane, the first such experimental machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crane grapple loading of logs from the ground, the same operation as knuckleboom loading at a tree job; cited only as a research demonstration, not production-rate work.

tasks.label: Cut away dead and excess branches from trees, or clear branches around power lines, using climbing equipment or buckets of extended truck booms, or chainsaws, hooks, handsaws, shears, and clippers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility distribution line clearance: crew works from a bucket truck (or climbs) along residential streets and rural roadsides, cutting limbs away from energized primary/secondary conductors with chainsaw, pole saw and hand pruners, dropping or hand-lowering brush clear of the lines, traffic and yards, meeting utility clearance specs and ANSI Z133 electrical-hazard rules.

Residential/private-property pruning of a mature shade tree: climber ascends on rope and saddle (or uses a lift), removes deadwood, thins/raises the crown, makes proper collar cuts on limbs up to several inches, and rigs or drops pieces clear of roof, fence, garden and vehicles, then cleans up.

Municipal / commercial-property street and park tree work: aerial-lift clearance pruning over streets and sidewalks for vehicle and pedestrian clearance, sign/signal clearance, and structural pruning of young street trees, with traffic control set up around the work zone.

Storm-damage and hazard work: removal of broken, hanging or storm-loaded limbs from damaged trees, often at odd angles, over houses or lines, requiring judgment about load, rigging of heavy pieces, and cutting under tension.

Transmission right-of-way and rural roadside work in rough terrain: side-trimming and removal of encroaching branches and brush along the corridor, often off-road, on slopes or in wet ground, using chainsaws, pole saws and climbing where machinery cannot reach.

sources.system: OSU/WSU autonomous pruning robot for planar fruit trees (You et al.)
sources.developer: Oregon State University / Washington State University
sources.title: An autonomous robot for pruning modern, planar fruit trees (arXiv:2206.07201)
sources.claim: The most advanced published fully autonomous tree-pruning robot cuts dormant shoots on planar (trellised) sweet cherry trees in a commercial orchard and achieved only a 58% cutting success rate, with the authors noting it is not fully robust and needs throughput improvements.
sources.transferJustification: Dormant pruning is the closest robotic analogue to 'cut away dead and excess branches': it is branch-cutting on woody plants. It is far easier than arborist work (small shoots, 2-D trellised architecture, ground-level reach, no energized conductors, no rigging), yet succeeds on only 58% of cuts, so it cannot substantiate completion of arborist pruning at any tier.

sources.system: review of autonomous robotic pruning platforms (orchards/vineyards)
sources.developer: Politecnico di Torino (Navone, Martini, Chiaberge et al.)
sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Pruning in Orchards and Vineyards: a Review (arXiv:2505.07318)
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed review of autonomous robotic pruning in orchards ... characterizes the field as a body of research with critical open challenges rather than deployed systems.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the same physical act (selecting and cutting branches on woody plants) in far more structured agricultural settings; its finding that the field remains pre-commercial bounds what can be claimed for street, yard and powerline tree work.

sources.title: Sarcos Robotics Successfully Implements Next-Generation Teleoperation Capabilities of Guardian XT Robotic System
sources.claim: The best-known robotic tree-trimming demonstration on full-size trees, Sarcos' Guardian XT, is a human-in-the-loop teleoperated arm driven by an operator wearing a motion-capture suit and VR goggles, not an autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same task (trimming tree limbs, including near power lines), but it is continuously teleoperated, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.developer: FirstEnergy / Mon Power with aerial saw contractor
sources.title: Mon Power Deploys Aerial Saw to Trim Trees in Hard-to-Access Areas
sources.claim: The mechanized tree trimming that utilities actually deploy along rights-of-way is a rotary saw boom suspended beneath a manned helicopter flown by a human pilot, not a robotic system.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the powerline right-of-way trimming instance; it shows the deployed technology is a human-piloted machine, so it provides no autonomous-robot substantiation.

sources.system: AI chainsaw drone (UC Vision drone with chainsaw/pruner tool)
sources.developer: University of Canterbury UC Vision team and NZ partners
sources.title: AI-driven chainsaw drone offers safer tree trimming near powerlines - NZ Herald
sources.claim: An AI-assisted chainsaw drone for trimming branches near power lines is in field testing in New Zealand, flown by experienced drone operators, with commercial production only hoped for in a following year.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (cutting branches near power lines) but an operator-flown prototype in field trials, not an autonomous system delivering worker-quality output.

sources.system: survey of mechanical/robotic pruners incl. climbing 'Stick Insect' robot and UAV pruners
sources.developer: Forest & Wood Products Australia (research report PRC522-2021)
sources.title: A review of current mechanical & robotic tree pruning equipment (FWPA PRC522-2021)
sources.claim: A review of mechanical and robotic tree-pruning equipment for forestry concluded that few mechanized pruners match manual pruning quality, and only under restricted conditions, while UAV and climbing-robot pruners still have technical and operational hurdles before becoming operational or commercial.
sources.transferJustification: Reviews machines built for the same physical act of removing branches from standing trees; establishes that even in uniform plantation rows no machine matches manual pruning quality except on straight stems with small branches.

tasks.label: Clean, sharpen, and lubricate tools and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-day saw chain sharpening at the tree company's shop/yard bench: chains pulled off two or three saws, brushed free of sap and sawdust, every cutter ground to a consistent angle and the rakers/depth gauges lowered on a bench grinder or in a vise with a file, then chains dipped/wiped in oil so they are ready for the next morning.

Servicing the chainsaw powerhead and bar at the shop: blowing and scraping caked sawdust off the cylinder fins, sprocket and clutch cover, pulling and washing or replacing the air filter, cleaning the bar groove and oiler hole, dressing bar rails, refilling bar-and-chain oil and mixed fuel, refitting and tensioning the chain.

Mid-job touch-up in the field (customer's yard, roadside right-of-way): a chain glazed on dirty bark is hand-filed on the bar at the tailgate or at the base of the tree, bar oil topped off, sap wiped from bar, chain and pruner blades, all in a few minutes between cuts and in whatever weather and footing the site offers.

Hand-tool care at the shop bench: hand pruners, loppers, pole-pruner heads and hand saws are scrubbed of sap and grit, blades wiped with disinfectant, edges honed or filed back to a working bevel, pivots and springs oiled and pivot bolts tightened.

Sharpening a set of chipper knives (and the bed/anvil knife) taken off the drum: each straight knife clamped in the grinder jig or magnetic chuck, ground back to a fresh bevel, deburred, checked for equal width, then wiped and oiled against rust before it goes back on the machine.

Cleaning and lubricating the chipper and bucket truck in the yard: hosing or pressure-washing chips, sap and mud off the feed table, chute and boom, then walking the grease-gun round of zerk fittings on feed rollers, PTO, winch and boom pivots and topping hydraulic fluid per the daily checklist.

sources.system: Markusson Triplematic / Sensomatic automatic chain sharpener (Quadco)
sources.title: Markusson - Quadco
sources.claim: Markusson (Quadco) Triplematic/Sensomatic bench grinders are commercially sold, fully automatic saw-chain sharpening machines that grind the cutting edge, gullet and depth gauge (raker) of every link in one automatic cycle once the chain is loaded; they are marketed to logging contractors and chainsaw service dealers.

sources.system: Knecht E 50 RT robotic knife sharpening cell (Stäubli TX2-90 HE, GLAESS integration)
sources.developer: Knecht Maschinenbau / GLAESS Software & Automation / Stäubli
sources.title: Sharpening knives with a robot | Stäubli
sources.claim: The Knecht E 50 RT cell uses a Stäubli TX2-90 HE six-axis robot to take each knife from a magazine, laser-measure its individual worn shape, then grind, deburr and polish it, processing up to 680 knives per ... in batch size 1.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: regrinding worn butchery knives. Each blade is an individually worn single-bevel steel edge that the cell measures and grinds back to a working edge without losing its shape — the same operation, objects and precision as honing pruner, lopper and hand-saw blades on a bench.

sources.title: RoboWash™ Robotic Industrial Parts Washer | Fives
sources.claim: Fives RoboWash is a commercially supplied robotic industrial washer that manipulates parts automatically through pre-wash, high-pressure wash and drying stages to clean oily, soiled metal parts such as engine blocks and transmission cases.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: degreasing/washing soiled metal components in a fixtured cell. Removing oil, chips and residue from steel parts transfers to washing sap, sawdust and bar oil off chains, blades and tool bodies presented in the same way.

sources.system: Thorvie AV-54 Automatic Jointer/Planer/Chipper Knife Grinder
sources.title: Automatic Jointer Planer Chipper Knife Grinder (AV-54)
sources.claim: The Thorvie AV-54 is a commercially sold automatic knife grinder that sharpens chipper, jointer and planer knives up to 24 inches on a magnetic bed with automatic carriage travel and automatic wheel downfeed, grinding to 0.0005 in per inch.

sources.system: InterClean automatic drive-through truck wash system (and equivalent KKE drive-through bays)
sources.title: Automated Semi Truck Wash - Time Efficient Heavy Duty Wash Cycles
sources.claim: Automatic drive-through truck wash systems installed in dedicated wash bays sense the vehicle and run detergent, high-volume jet and high-pressure or brush stages to clean heavy vehicles without an operator handling the wash.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing a heavy work vehicle. Hosing chips, sap and mud off a chipper or bucket truck in the yard is the same physical operation on the same class of machine, performed here by fixed automated wash equipment in a purpose-built bay.

sources.system: Groeneveld-BEKA Twin / SingleLine automatic lubrication systems
sources.title: Groeneveld Twin: Dual-line lubrication for heavy duty - Groeneveld-BEKA
sources.claim: Groeneveld-BEKA dual-line and single-line automatic lubrication systems are commercially deployed on trucks, trailers, construction and agricultural machines, metering grease to every lubrication point on the machine on a controlled schedule in place of a manual grease-gun round.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: greasing the lube points of heavy mobile equipment. The system delivers metered grease to the same zerk-served bearings and pivots a worker services with a grease gun on a chipper or bucket truck.

sources.developer: Yaskawa Motoman (integrator cell reported by Machinery Lubrication)
sources.title: Automation Drives Grease-dispensing Machine | Machinery Lubrication
sources.claim: A production machine uses a Motoman robot ... place a part and then apply lubricating grease to ... specified contact surfaces, showing robotic dispensing of lubricant onto defined points of a fixtured item in a cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of grease to specified contact surfaces of a fixtured assembly — the same act, scale and precision as oiling the pivot, spring and blade faces of hand pruners and loppers presented in a fixture.

tasks.label: Hoist tools and equipment to tree trimmers, and lower branches with ropes or block and tackle.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/commercial yard tree removal or large pruning: the ground worker ties saws, ropes, wedges and rigging hardware onto a hand line and sends them up to a climber 30-70 ft aloft, then tends the bull rope through a Port-a-Wrap/block-and-tackle, taking shock loads as the climber cuts limbs and lowering each piece into a tight drop zone between fences, shrubs, driveway and house.

Street tree / utility right-of-way pruning along a road: ground worker passes up pole saw, rope and hardware to a climber or bucket operator, then rigs and lowers limbs clear of energized conductors, parked cars and pedestrians under traffic control, coordinating verbally with the aerial worker.

Routine light hoisting: sending a hand saw, lanyard, water, fuel or a single block up to a climber or bucket on a throw/hand line, and hand-lowering or free-dropping small brush; low load, frequent, done many times per job in any setting.

Institution-managed grounds (municipal park, university campus, cemetery, golf course): heavy limb and log lowering over open turf, sometimes with speedline or block-and-tackle to move wood away from monuments, paths or turf, with the grounds closed off by the institution during work.

Storm-damage / emergency work: hoisting gear to a climber in a broken, leaning or partly failed tree and lowering unstable, spring-loaded or fractured limbs over a roof, wires or vehicle, with loads and attachment points that must be judged piece by piece.

sources.system: ANDRITZ log yard crane with Metris ANDI Autonomous Crane AI
sources.title: Log yard cranes | ANDRITZ
sources.claim: ANDRITZ's Metris ANDI crane AI runs log yard gantry cranes fully autonomously, using laser scanners and cameras to locate loose logs and pick, hoist, move and set them down in the yard without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grapple hoisting and lowering of loose logs in a purpose-built log yard. Transfers to the E1 form of this task because the objects are the same material class (heavy irregular woody stems), the machine must raise a load, control its descent and set it down in a defined drop zone, and the setting is built around the crane.

sources.system: ANDRITZ autonomous logyard cranes at Metsa Fibre Kemi mill
sources.title: Metsa Fibre's Kemi bioproduct mill in Finland successfully lifts up the world's first autonomous logyard cranes supplied by ANDRITZ
sources.claim: The world's first autonomously operated log yard cranes were installed and put into service at Metsa Fibre's Kemi bioproduct mill, showing the autonomous crane is a deployed product and not only a demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned crane hoisting/lowering of logs in a mill yard; establishes deployment maturity for the autonomous woody-material hoisting cited above.

sources.system: Konecranes automated overhead cranes (Palm paper roll warehouse, Woerth)
sources.title: Konecranes modernizes Palm's paper roll warehouse with four new automated cranes
sources.claim: Konecranes automated overhead cranes run an entire paper roll warehouse, hoisting loads and setting them at defined storage and handover positions without operators; four more automated cranes are being installed at Palm's Woerth mill.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended hoisting of a load from a known pick point and lowering it accurately onto a known delivery point. This is the E1 form of both halves of the task - raising tooling/equipment to a fixed elevated delivery point and lowering a rigged load into a landing zone.

sources.title: Serpent Robotics - SR-01 Arborist Robot
sources.claim: The only fielded arborist rigging robot found, Serpent Robotics' SR-01, climbs the crew's rigging line and cuts, holds and lowers a limb, but is remote-controlled by a ground operator throughout and still requires the human crew to set the line.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: canopy limb holding and lowering in real trees. Cited to show that in-tree rigging work today is continuously teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment at E2 or E3.

sources.system: Zipline Platform 2 (P2 Zip and tethered droid)
sources.title: Zipline unveils P2 delivery drones that dock and recharge autonomously (CNBC)
sources.claim: Zipline's Platform 2 delivers autonomously by lowering a tethered droid that places a small payload precisely in residential settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tethered lowering of a small payload to a point in an unstructured yard. Cited as the closest unstructured-environment analogue for hoisting tools; it delivers to open ground, not into a canopy to a climber, and payloads are only a few kilograms, so it does not complete this task's instances.

sources.system: Autonomous forwarder crane log grasping (stereo-camera boom-tip control)
sources.title: Real-time target point identification and automated log grasping by a forwarder, using a single stereo camera for both object detection and boom-tip control
sources.claim: A forwarder crane using a single stereo camera achieved a completely autonomous log loading cycle in the field, picking up and loading all logs within reach onto the trailer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crane handling of cut woody material outdoors. Cited as the outdoor state of the art; it handles logs already lying on the ground and is a research demo, so it does not substantiate canopy rigging or tool hoisting at E2/E3.

tasks.label: Climb trees, using climbing hooks and belts, or climb ladders to gain access to work areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential property: climber sets a throwline and rope in a large mature shade tree (oak, maple, elm, 40-80 ft), ties in with saddle and climbing system, ascends and then moves through the spreading crown — limb-walking, redirecting, repositioning — to reach each pruning or rigging work point, carrying handsaw/chainsaw and rigging gear, over a house, fence, and uneven lawn.

Utility line clearance: climber ascends a roadside or backyard easement tree with spurs or rope where a bucket cannot reach, working around and maintaining minimum approach distances to energized primary conductors, on brushy or sloped ground, to reach limbs growing into the conductor zone.

Municipal street tree or park tree / palm: spur-climb for a removal or rope-climb for a crown cleaning on a street tree over a sidewalk and traffic lane, or gaff-climb a 30-50 ft palm to reach the frond crown, with pedestrians and parked cars below.

Ladder access on residential or commercial grounds: worker foots and ties off an extension or orchard ladder against a small-to-medium tree or hedge (10-25 ft) to reach low-canopy limbs with hand pruners or a pole saw, or to enter the canopy and set the climbing line.

Orchard, grove, or nursery rows on institution-controlled grounds: worker climbs a tripod/orchard ladder or steps into the scaffold limbs of uniformly spaced fruit or nursery trees to reach canopy work points for structural pruning, repeated tree after tree down a row.

sources.developer: E-Valley Co., Ltd. (イー・バレイ株式会社), Nagoya, Japan
sources.title: 自動枝打ちロボット：eddy｜イー・バレイ株式会社
sources.claim: eddy (PR-UDC180) is a commercially sold Japanese pruning robot: a worker clamps the 11 kg unit to a trunk and remotely drives it to the start height, after which it climbs and prunes automatically, adjusting speed to cutting load and avoiding obstacles, then descends automatically. Rated for Φ50-180 mm approximately straight conifers (sugi, hinoki) with branches up to Φ30 mm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pruning branches off a standing tree. The machine's means of doing it is exactly the rated task — climbing the trunk to gain access to the branch work areas, carrying a chainsaw — so its climbing performance transfers directly, but only for approximately straight conifer trunks Φ50-180 mm with branches ≤30 mm.

sources.title: Drones Revolutionize Fruit Harvesting With AI-Powered Precision
sources.claim: Tevel's Flying Autonomous Robots fly into fruit-tree canopies to locate and pick fruit under AI/vision control and are deployed in commercial orchards in the U.S., Italy, Chile ... — i.e., they place a working end-effector at work points inside a tree canopy without a ladder.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: orchard fruit harvesting, which workers otherwise do from ladders. The transferable element is the access function — autonomously reaching and stabilizing an end-effector at work positions inside a fruit-tree canopy amid branches — the same purpose a ladder climb serves in an orchard row. It does not demonstrate woody-branch cutting force.

sources.system: Tevel FAR + Darwin Tecnofruit integrated harvester
sources.developer: Tevel Aerobotics Technologies and Darwin wcdi
sources.title: Autonomous fruit harvesting system shown by Darwin, Tevel Aerobotics - Fruit Growers News
sources.claim: Tevel's flying autonomous robots have been integrated with Darwin's Tecnofruit harvesting platform into a system marketed as a fully commercial autonomous fruit harvesting system operating in orchards.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Tevel item: commercial-grade autonomous access to in-canopy work points in orchard rows, substituting for the ladder climb that orchard workers use to reach the same canopy positions.

sources.title: A robotic solution for safer tree trimming | Penn Today
sources.claim: The most advanced effort aimed squarely at replacing arborist tree-climbing is a university startup prototype that is rope-climbing and ground-controlled (operator-driven), not an autonomous fielded system.

sources.title: Robots that can climb trees or restore coral reefs | ETH Zurich
sources.claim: Research-stage climbing robots for trees (MONKEE) can move vertically and sideways on trunks of varying shape, but remain a student focus-project prototype rather than a fielded, tool-carrying arborist system.

sources.system: Aerial saw (helicopter-mounted saw boom) operated by Aerial Solutions for Mon Power
sources.title: Mon Power Deploys Aerial Saw to Trim Trees in Hard-to-Access Areas
sources.claim: The mechanized alternative to climbing in utility right-of-way vegetation management is a piloted helicopter carrying a saw boom, flown by a human pilot with a ground crew; it trims the outside of the canopy and provides no in-canopy work access.

sources.developer: Washington State University / Cornell / Virginia Tech (AgAID Institute)
sources.title: An Integrated Visual Servoing Framework for Precise Robotic Pruning Operations in Modern Commercial Orchard
sources.claim: Robotic pruning of fruit trees — positioning a cutter at canopy pruning points — is still at the research stage, with the cited visual-servoing system validated in simulation rather than in production orchards.

tasks.label: Supervise others engaged in tree trimming work and train lower-level employees.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crew leader on a residential/commercial tree pruning or removal job directs a climber and ground crew: assigns roles, sequences cuts, calls the drop zone, watches for hazards, and corrects technique verbally throughout the job. Output is direction and oversight, not cut wood.

Utility line-clearance general foreman oversees a bucket-truck crew working a roadside right-of-way: conducts the pre-job briefing, verifies clearance specifications and traffic-control setup, monitors minimum approach distances, and instructs crew members on corrections.

Hands-on training session for new groundworkers or apprentice climbers at the shop yard or a training tree: explaining and demonstrating knots, rigging, chipper feeding, chainsaw handling and PPE, then watching trainees practice and giving feedback.
Daily tailgate/toolbox safety briefing before work begins: reviewing the work plan, site hazards, electrical hazards, ANSI Z133 requirements, and answering crew questions.
Evaluating and documenting worker performance: signing off climbing or aerial-lift skill checks, completing apprentice progress records, counseling an employee on deficiencies or unsafe practices.

tasks.label: Trim, top, and reshape trees to achieve attractive shapes or to remove low-hanging branches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential property: crown-raise and reshape a mature yard tree (maple, oak, crape myrtle) — climb or use a bucket, select and cut low-hanging limbs over a driveway, roof or lawn, make proper collar cuts, thin for shape, lower brush over fences/plantings. Homeowner judges appearance.

Public street / sidewalk right-of-way: raise street-tree canopies over roadway and walk to clearance height, remove sucker growth and low branches, shape crown around signs and lights, working from a bucket truck in live traffic with pedestrians and parked cars.

Utility line clearance: side-trim, top or directional-prune trees growing into distribution/transmission conductors along roadside and backyard easements, on slopes and in brush, keeping minimum approach distances to energized lines.

Institutional grounds (municipal park, university or corporate campus, golf course, cemetery): scheduled ornamental shaping and canopy raising of specimen trees over turf and walkways, maintained terrain, access controlled by the grounds department.

Production/nursery setting: shearing and shaping young nursery stock, ornamental hedges and orchard-style fruiting walls into uniform forms in planted rows or container blocks, repetitive geometric shapes, small-diameter wood.

sources.developer: EU H2020 consortium (Univ. of Edinburgh, Wageningen UR, Univ. of Freiburg, Bosch)
sources.title: Details – TrimBot2020 Project
sources.claim: TrimBot2020, an EU research robot built on a Bosch Indego mower base, autonomously navigated an outdoor test garden and trimmed hedges and topiary bushes toward target shapes — the closest autonomous 'shaping woody plants' demonstration, but on small-stem shrubs, at ground level, as a research prototype that was never commercialized.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous shrub/hedge shaping. Transfer to tree trimming is weak — it cuts millimetre-scale shrub twigs at ground level with a hedge cutter, not branches on a standing tree crown requiring climbing/aerial access, limb weight control and collar cuts.

sources.system: Boxwood topiary trimming robot (robot arm with stereo vision, TrimBot2020 lineage)
sources.developer: Wageningen University & Research / University of Freiburg
sources.title: Evaluation of a boxwood topiary trimming robot — WUR Research Portal
sources.claim: Quantitative and human evaluation of the boxwood topiary trimming robot (the TrimBot arm) in a real garden found it trims autonomously but well below usable quality: sphere accuracy rose only from 27% to 51% of surface points within 2 cm of the target shape, cylinders and cuboids barely improved, and human graders scored the best bush 3.1/5.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aesthetic shaping of a woody plant presented to a robot arm — the most favourable (near-E1) version of 'reshape to achieve attractive shapes'. It establishes that even in this easiest case the output is not at worker quality.

sources.developer: University of Canterbury (Profs. Richard Green, Dan Zhao)
sources.title: Industry impressed by chainsaw drone work | Otago Daily Times
sources.claim: A University of Canterbury (NZ) prototype chainsaw drone for trimming branches near power lines cuts roughly 60 mm dead wood, uses AI algorithms for flight near moving branches, and as of mid-2025 was still a funded prototype awaiting commercialisation; it is flown by an operator rather than working autonomously end-to-end.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the utility line-clearance instance, but autonomy is not established (operator-flown demonstration) and capability is limited to ~60 mm dead branches, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Survey of autonomous robotic pruning platforms (orchard/vineyard)
sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Pruning in Orchards and Vineyards: a Review (arXiv:2505.07318)
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed review of autonomous robotic pruning covering 2014–2024 literature frames autonomous pruning of woody perennials as an active research problem with open challenges in perception, skeletonization and control — i.e. no fielded system performing whole pruning jobs at commercial quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pruning of fruit trees and vines in planted rows — the most structured, most heavily researched version of cutting woody stems to a target form. The review's status assessment bounds what is available for nursery/orchard shaping.

tasks.label: Load debris and refuse onto trucks and haul it away for disposal.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential pruning/removal job: crew drags cut limbs and brush across a private lawn, driveway and hedges to the curb, hand-feeds the brush into a chipper towed behind a chip truck, tosses cut wood rounds and small logs into the truck body, rakes and blows up leaves and small debris, then drives the loaded truck through neighborhood streets to a mulch yard or landfill and dumps.

Utility line-clearance / roadside right-of-way work: brush cut along rural or suburban road shoulders and easements, dragged out of ditches, fence lines and slopes to the pavement edge, chipped into a chip body while traffic passes, larger wood loaded by hand or with a knuckleboom grapple truck, and hauled to a disposal or chip drop site.

Municipal/urban street tree pruning: debris dropped on a curbside lane closed with cones, cleared off sidewalk and street quickly, chipped and loaded curbside amid parked cars, pedestrians and traffic, street swept clean, load hauled to the city yard or transfer station.

Institutional grounds work (college campus, park, golf course, cemetery, corporate campus): pruning debris gathered onto paths, lawns or a paved lot, loaded onto a dump truck/trailer or with a compact loader grapple, and hauled to an on-site compost/mulch area or off-site disposal.

At the disposal end / company yard: backing and dumping the chip or dump body at a mulch yard, landfill tipping face or transfer station, dealing with hung-up loads, then loading and piling logs, chips and other wood waste with a skid steer or loader and tidying the yard.

sources.system: Konecranes automated waste-to-energy / CXT biomass grab cranes
sources.title: Waste to energy and biomass crane automation | Konecranes
sources.claim: Konecranes supplies fully automated grab cranes that handle heterogeneous municipal waste and wood biomass fuel operator-free in plant bunkers, covering the whole chain from receiving waste tipped by trucks, through storage and re-casting, to feeding the hopper.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk handling of mixed refuse and wood fuel with a grapple. Transfer: the grab crane grasps tangled, irregular refuse and woody biomass from a heap and moves it to a defined discharge point, the same manipulation problem as grappling brush and wood into a truck body, at the same coarse precision, but in a purpose-built bunker.

sources.system: Konecranes fully automated waste grab cranes at Fortum Klaipeda CHP
sources.title: Fully automated waste cranes keep plant running | Konecranes
sources.claim: Two fully automated Konecranes grab cranes run around the clock at Fortum's Klaipeda plant, moving trucked-in waste from the storage bunker into the incinerator with remote monitoring rather than on-site operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended grapple handling of mixed refuse. Transfer: demonstrates sustained, worker-quality throughput of irregular debris moved from a tipping/storage area to a discharge point without an operator, the loading half of this task, in a purpose-built setting.

sources.title: Sandvik AutoMine Autoload 2.0 eliminates operator intervention in LHD drawpoint loading - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 automates the full loader production cycle - bucket filling at the muck pile, tramming and dumping - so underground loaders run without operator intervention during mucking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous load-haul-dump of loose broken rock. Transfer: it is the same whole cycle as this task - scoop loose material from a pile at a fixed point, transport it, discharge it for disposal - at comparable (coarse) precision, but with the pile and dump point fixed by a purpose-built layout.

sources.system: Pronto.ai Autonomous Haulage System on Cat 775G and Komatsu HD605 trucks
sources.title: Heidelberg Materials reaches autonomous hauling milestone | Pit & Quarry
sources.claim: Pronto.ai's autonomous haulage system drove a mixed Caterpillar and Komatsu haul-truck fleet driverless at Heidelberg Materials' Lake Bridgeport quarry, hauling and dumping more than two million tons ... in about eight months.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless hauling and dumping of bulk material on an industrial site. Transfer: covers the 'haul it away for disposal' leg - loaded truck drives a defined route and discharges at a tip point - with vehicles of the same class as dump/chip trucks, in an institution-controlled site.

sources.title: Cat MineStar Command for Hauling Manages the Autonomous Ecosystem to Increase Haulage Efficiency, Enhance Safety | Caterpillar
sources.claim: Caterpillar's autonomous mining trucks operating under MineStar Command for hauling have autonomously hauled more than 8.6 billion tonnes over eleven years of production operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous haul-and-dump cycles on dedicated haul roads. Transfer: establishes at scale that the transport-and-tip half of this task is routinely done without a driver where the route and dump point are engineered for the machine.

sources.system: Automated log grasping by a forwarder crane (stereo-camera boom-tip control)
sources.developer: Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences / Umea University (Semberg, Nilsson et al.)
sources.title: Real-time target point identification and automated log grasping by a forwarder, using a single stereo camera for both object detection and boom-tip control | Silva Fennica
sources.claim: Autonomous grasping and loading of individual logs by a full-size forestry crane remains at the research-demonstration stage, with real-time full-scale tests reported only recently in test-bed and simplified outdoor settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking up cut wood from the ground with a grapple crane. Shows the closest analogue to loading brush and logs in the field is still experimental, so it cannot support a positive judgment at E2 or E3.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Raises $270 Million in Series B Funding to Accelerate the Future of Autonomous Construction
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics ran supervised-autonomy excavators loading human-operated dump trucks on an active 130-acre construction site, and as of early 2026 was still only targeting its first fully operator-less deployments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously loading trucks with loose material outdoors. Included to mark the frontier: loading remains supervised and is limited to homogeneous soil, so it does not substantiate loading tree debris in unstructured or institutional settings.

tasks.label: Inspect trees to determine if they have diseases or pest problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility line-clearance crew working a distribution right-of-way along a rural road or residential backlot: before and during trimming, the trimmer looks over each roadside tree from the ground and from the bucket for dead/dying crowns, borer exit holes, fungal conks, bark cracks and root-collar decay (e.g., EAB-killed ash) to decide whether the tree is trimmed, flagged for removal, or reported to the forester. Traffic, fences, brush and uneven terrain are present.

Residential tree-care job on a private lot: homeowner reports a declining maple/oak. Worker walks the tree, examines leaves for spots/wilt/chlorosis, scans the trunk and scaffold limbs for cankers, boring dust, scale, conks, sounds the trunk with a mallet, checks the root flare and soil, and gives a determination (disease/pest present, what it likely is, treat vs. remove). Fences, pets, structures, plantings crowd the tree.

Municipal or contract street/park tree round: worker inspects a series of street trees and park trees along a block during pruning rounds, spotting pest infestation (e.g., ALB/EAB signs, aphid honeydew, tent caterpillars), dieback and decay, and logging condition into a tree inventory or work order. Sidewalk, parked cars, pedestrians, varied species and ages.

Aerial close inspection at height: worker on a climbing line or in a bucket lift examines the upper canopy and branch unions of a mature tree up close for cavities, included bark, conks, cankers, borer galleries and dead limbs, reaching and pulling limbs and probing suspect wood, then reports the tree's condition.

Managed nursery or plantation rows: inspecting young container-grown or field-grown trees and shrubs planted in regular rows on a commercial nursery/grove site for foliar disease and pest infestation (mites, scale, blight, leaf spot) before pruning or shipping; access controlled by the operator, uniform stock, level surfaced rows.

sources.title: Corvus Drones, ADI and PlantScout join forces at GreenTech Amsterdam
sources.claim: Corvus Drones sells autonomous drones that fly greenhouse crop-monitoring missions commercially in horticultural facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated plant-health scouting of nursery/greenhouse stock. It bears on the nursery-row instance because the objects (young potted/field nursery plants in regular rows), the perceptual judgment (foliar pest and disease symptoms) and the controlled horticultural setting are comparable; it does not transfer to mature landscape trees.

sources.system: Corvus Drones scouting applications (potted plants, young plants)
sources.title: GreenTech | Corvus Drones BV - Products
sources.claim: The Corvus drone scouting product line reports detection of pests and diseases as well as leaf discoloration on greenhouse-grown plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of pest/disease symptoms on nursery stock foliage. Transfers to inspecting young nursery trees and shrubs in rows (same symptom classes, same kind of structured growing facility), but not to trunk, union or root-collar diagnosis on mature trees.

sources.system: Sharper A6 / Sharperscope automated drone inspection; Sharper CORE analytics
sources.title: Border States enhancing utility drone inspection with Sharper Shape
sources.claim: Automated drone flights are used commercially to capture utility right-of-way and vegetation data, but the delivered analytics are clearance, encroachment and growth models rather than a per-tree disease or pest diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated aerial survey of utility rights-of-way. It shows autonomous data capture over the same terrain as the line-clearance instance, but the product output is vegetation location/encroachment, not the disease and pest determination the trimmer makes, so it does not substantiate completion.

sources.title: Treeswift's Autonomous Robots Take Flight to Save Forests
sources.claim: Autonomous LiDAR drones fly under forest canopy to inventory and map timber stands; the demonstrated outputs are stem counts, dimensions and maps, not disease or pest determinations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous under-canopy forest inventory. It shows a robot can navigate among standing trees in unstructured woodland, but the sensing task (geometry/inventory) does not deliver the pathological judgment required here.

sources.system: Improved YOLOv8 pine wilt disease detection from UAV multispectral imagery
sources.title: Automatic pine wilt disease detection based on improved YOLOv8 UAV multispectral imagery
sources.claim: UAV multispectral imagery combined with deep learning can automatically flag pine wilt-diseased trees at stand scale; the work reported is research-grade detection of already discolored or dead crowns.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial detection of diseased conifers. Closest published analogue to field tree inspection, but flight control is not documented as autonomous, it is a research study, and it detects only late-stage crown discoloration, not the bark, union and root-collar signs the trimmer reads.

sources.title: Automatic crop registration and auto-scouting added to OKO
sources.claim: A greenhouse scouting machine detects pest and disease symptoms on crop foliage, but it is driven down the rows by a human operator with auto-scouting added as an assist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pest/disease scouting of greenhouse crops. Objects (herbaceous greenhouse crops) and mode (operator-driven platform on pipe rails) differ from tree inspection, and autonomy is not established, so it is recorded but not relied on for a positive judgment.

sources.system: Burro autonomous outdoor robots at Petitti Ridge Manor nursery
sources.title: Petitti Family Farms using Burro autonomous robots, with plans to add more
sources.claim: Autonomous outdoor robots are deployed in commercial plant nurseries, but the deployed jobs are transport and spacing of plants, not plant health inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation among nursery stock. Establishes robot mobility in the nursery setting relevant to the nursery instance, but no disease or pest determination is claimed, so it cannot by itself substantiate completion.

sources.system: wheel-based tree climbing robot prototype (Treebot-class designs)
sources.developer: academic research (Conference on Advances in Robotics)
sources.title: Design and analysis of a tree climbing robot
sources.claim: Robots that climb tree trunks to reach and inspect the stem and canopy remain laboratory prototypes, with pest and disease identification named as a still-human job.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic access to the trunk and canopy for inspection. Shows the aerial/in-canopy inspection instance has no fielded robotic solution; the cited design is a prototype only described as one that could be made autonomous.

tasks.label: Provide information to the public regarding trees, such as advice on tree care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Trim jagged stumps, using saws or pruning shears.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aloft on a residential or commercial property (climbing on rope/saddle or in a bucket lift): after a limb is removed with the three-cut method, or after a storm break, the trimmer cuts the remaining jagged stub back flush to the branch collar with a handsaw or top-handle chainsaw, one-handed, avoiding bark tearing and controlling the falling piece.

Ground level, within reach, in a residential or commercial landscape: cleaning up jagged, torn or broken stubs on shrubs and small ornamental trees with hand pruners, loppers or a handsaw, cutting back to a bud, lateral or collar; uneven turf, beds, fences and irrigation nearby.

Utility line-clearance along a roadside right-of-way: working from an insulated aerial lift or with a pole saw/pole pruner, trimming jagged stubs and torn wood left by clearance cuts near energized conductors, with traffic passing, brush underfoot and variable terrain.

Municipal street-tree or public-park storm response: removing hangers and cutting broken, jagged limb stubs back to sound wood from a lift over a sidewalk or street, with traffic control, pedestrians, parked cars and wires in the drop zone.

Institution-controlled grounds (university or corporate campus, cemetery, golf course): scheduled cleanup pruning of stubs left by earlier poor cuts or breakage on ornamental trees along maintained walks and lawns, from the ground or a short lift, with controlled access and a fixed, maintained layout.

sources.system: AA Hooke Park robotic fabrication cell (KUKA KR-150) — Wood Chip Barn tree-fork truss
sources.developer: Architectural Association Design & Make, Hooke Park
sources.title: AA Design & Make students use a robotic arm to build a woodland barn
sources.claim: Irregular natural forked beech branches were harvested, brought to a campus workshop, 3D scanned, and cut/milled to shape by a KUKA robotic arm working from the scan-derived toolpaths — i.e., natural branch wood trimmed at machine-determined positions with the work brought to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic machining of irregular natural branch wood. It transfers to trimming a jagged stub at E1 because the object (rough, non-uniform tree branch), the tool action (saw/mill cut at a scanned, geometrically defined line) and the precision required are comparable, and the E1 counterfactual presents the workpiece fixtured in the cell exactly as here.

sources.system: Hundegger Robot / Robot Max mass timber machining line (Timberlyne)
sources.title: Timberlyne and Hundegger Commission the Most Advanced Robotic Mass Timber Machine Line in North America
sources.claim: A commercial industrial timber line built around a 6-axis robot processes wood elements automatically with dozens of selectable saw and milling tools, cutting to programmed geometry inside a purpose-built machine enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated robotic sawing of timber fed and fixtured by the machine. It substantiates that, once the wood is presented to the machine (the E1 counterfactual), removing material with saws to a specified cut line is done autonomously at industrial reliability.

sources.system: Optimizing lumber trimmer (scanner/optimizer-driven trim saw line)
sources.developer: Sawmill equipment suppliers (e.g., USNR, Balluff sensing)
sources.title: Improving sawmill yield through automation | Machine Geeks
sources.claim: Sawmill trim lines automatically cut and trim the ends off boards with banks of circular saws on the conveyor, with scanners and optimizers deciding each cut, including removing damaged or defective ends.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatically trimming ragged/defective wood ends to a scanner-chosen line. Same material class (natural wood with variable defects), same action (saw cut removing a jagged protrusion), executed in a purpose-built machine line with the work conveyed and fixtured, matching the E1 counterfactual.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute / Cornell CLEREL
sources.title: [2112.00291] Bumblebee: A Path Towards Fully Autonomous Robotic Vine Pruning
sources.claim: An autonomous vision-guided robot cut dormant grapevine canes at selected points along a trellised row, pruning a vine in about 213 seconds with 87% accuracy; field tests in a commercial vineyard showed significant variability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cutting of woody stems at a chosen point with a powered cutter. It shows the perception-plus-cut capability exists when plants are presented in uniform trellised rows, but the 87% accuracy and 3.5 min/vine rate fall short of worker quality outside such purpose-built presentation.

sources.system: Autonomous robot for pruning modern, planar fruit trees (Oregon State / WSU)
sources.title: [2206.07201] An autonomous robot for pruning modern, planar fruit trees
sources.claim: A state-of-the-art autonomous pruning robot working on planar-trained sweet cherry trees in a commercial orchard cut only 58% of target branches across 10 trees, and the authors describe the system as not fully robust and needing throughput improvement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous branch cutting on trees in the most structured commercial planting that exists. Its low success rate is negative evidence that no cited system reaches worker quality for stub trimming in an institution-controlled facility (E2) or beyond.

sources.developer: EU H2020 TrimBot2020 consortium (Univ. of Edinburgh, Bosch, Wageningen, others)
sources.title: TrimBot2020 Project – Cutting Hedge Research
sources.claim: An autonomous outdoor garden robot navigated a test garden and trimmed boxwood topiary and pruned rose stems with an arm-mounted electric cutter under vision control, as a completed EU research prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor pruning of woody shrubs. It is the closest system to ground-level stub cleanup in a garden, but it is a finished research prototype limited to small rose stems and topiary shaping, with no saw capability or demonstrated worker-quality reliability.

sources.title: AirForestry – Efficient, Electric, and Sustainable Forestry from the Air
sources.claim: A heavy-lift drone completed, for the first time, an autonomous sequence in a real forest stand: navigating to the tree, identifying it, delimbing it, felling it and lifting the stem to roadside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mechanical delimbing of a standing stem outdoors. It is a world-first single-sequence demonstration on small thinning trees that destroys the tree, so it does not substantiate repeated, worker-quality collar cuts on trees that must survive.

sources.title: A robotic solution for safer tree trimming | Penn Today
sources.claim: The most prominent tree-care robot in development is a rope-climbing arborist robot that is driven from the ground by a worker using a remote control and camera feed — a prototype under continuous human control.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task's occupation (in-canopy cutting), but it is teleoperated and a prototype, so it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

tasks.label: Clear sites, streets, and grounds of woody and herbaceous materials, such as tree stumps and fallen trees and limbs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cleanup after a residential or small-commercial pruning/removal job: crew drags cut limbs and brush across a lawn, through beds, gates and around parked cars to a curbside chipper, feeds the chipper, loads log rounds into a truck, then rakes/blows the lawn, driveway and street clean. Uneven turf, fences, pets, homeowner present.

Street / utility right-of-way clearing: cut brush and limbs along road shoulders, alleys and easements are dragged out of the travel lane to a chipper truck parked in traffic, chipped, and the pavement swept clear; work proceeds under cones/flaggers with live traffic and pedestrians passing.

Storm or emergency response: wind-thrown trees and broken limbs blocking a street, driveway or lying across a yard/fence are bucked into sections with a chainsaw, dragged or grappled onto a truck, and the site cleared of scattered woody debris; muddy footing, tangled wood under tension, unknown layout.

Stump and root removal: position a grinder (or mini-skid with grinder head) over a yard, boulevard or tree-pit stump, grind flush or below grade dodging fences, utilities and hardscape, then shovel out grindings, haul them off and backfill/level the hole.

Grounds clearing on institution-controlled property (municipal park, campus, cemetery, golf course, utility substation or maintenance yard): collect fallen limbs, storm-dropped wood and brush scattered across mown grounds and paths, haul loads to a brush/chip dump on site, and leave turf and walks clean.

sources.date: 2023-05 (LIGNA launch; first units ordered 2020 for Metsa Fibre Kemi)
sources.title: Log yard cranes - ANDRITZ
sources.claim: ANDRITZ's logyard crane with the Metris ANDI AI operates fully autonomously handling loose logs in a mill woodyard - grabbing, stacking and feeding wood from the receiving area into processing - the purpose-built analogue of gathering loose woody material and feeding it to a chipper.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mill logyard log handling. Same objects (loose logs and slash-sized wood), same act (grapple pick from a heap, transport, feed a chipping/processing line) at the same precision, but in a purpose-built yard where the wood is delivered to the machine.

sources.system: Konecranes CXT Biomass Crane / WTE automated grab cranes
sources.title: Waste to energy and biomass crane automation | Konecranes
sources.claim: Konecranes' CXT biomass grab crane runs operator-free, autonomously moving delivered wood fuel from the truck dumping area into storage and feeding it to the boiler/processing hopper - autonomously clearing a receiving area of loose woody material in a purpose-built plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk wood-fuel handling. Grab-crane clearing of an unsorted heap of woody material from a dump area and feeding it into a processing hopper matches the debris-clearing act (gather woody material, dispose of it into a chipper/hopper) once the material is brought to the machine.

sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Kodama Systems uses robotics to prevent wildfires - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Kodama Systems fields teleoperation/autonomy kits on forestry skidders; on a Stanislaus National Forest thinning project the skidder drove itself along mapped skid trails hauling bundles of felled trees, but the platform is marketed as teleoperation, with grapple work and site decisions left to a remote operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: skidding felled trees out of a thinning site, the closest outdoor analogue to clearing a site of fallen trees; only the loaded haul along a mapped trail is autonomous, so it does not show whole-instance completion outdoors.

sources.developer: Baidu Research Robotics and Auto-Driving Lab / University of Maryland
sources.title: Video: Autonomous excavator shows promise in unmanned material loading tests - Recycling Today
sources.claim: Baidu/UMD's Autonomous Excavator System loaded material with no human intervention for over 24 continuous hours at a waste disposal site - autonomous bucket loading of bulk debris piles inside a controlled facility, but not gathering scattered limbs, feeding a chipper, or finish-cleaning a site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous material loading at a waste site. Shows autonomous heap-to-truck loading in an institution-controlled facility, but the objects are bulk waste/soil taken with a bucket from a prepared pile, not tangled limbs scattered over turf, so it does not carry the full grounds-clearing instance.

sources.system: Energreen RoboEVO / RoboMAX remote-controlled tool carrier with stump grinder
sources.title: Forestry Mulcher tracked robot for slopes | Energreen
sources.claim: The state of the art in mechanised stump grinding and brush mulching is radio-remote-controlled tool carriers (Energreen RoboEVO/RoboMAX with stump-grinder head); an operator commands every motion by remote control.

sources.title: Scythe Robotics debuts video series for M.52 autonomous mower onboarding - Lawn & Landscape
sources.claim: Autonomous machines working on human-maintained grounds today are mowers: Scythe's M.52 is a fully autonomous commercial mower deployed with landscape contractors across 14 states, but it cuts turf and must avoid debris rather than collect limbs or brush.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial turf mowing on maintained grounds. Establishes autonomous navigation on institutional grounds, but the machine neither picks up nor hauls woody debris, so it cannot substantiate debris clearing at E2/E3.

sources.system: Burro / Burro Grande autonomous hauling robots

tasks.label: Collect debris and refuse from tree trimming and removal operations into piles, using shovels, rakes, or other tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential or small commercial property after pruning/removal: crew rakes and hand-gathers twigs, leaves, bark, sawdust and chips off lawn, flower beds, driveway and roof gutters; drags cut limbs across the yard into piles at the curb or beside the chipper; works around fences, gardens, parked cars, pets and the homeowner's belongings on uneven turf.

Utility line-clearance or municipal street right-of-way: brush, limbs and leaf litter dropped onto road shoulder, sidewalk, ditch and adjacent turf must be raked and dragged into piles for the chipper truck while traffic control is active; debris mixed with roadside litter, gravel and guy wires.

Public park, greenway or streetscape planting bed: after trimming, rake clippings and small limbs off turf and paved paths into piles for a loader or truck crew; public present, natural uneven ground, mulch beds and site furniture.

Storm-damage or emergency response cleanup: large broken limbs, split wood, leaves and mixed refuse (fencing, shingles, trash) scattered across a yard or street; debris piled by size at the curb for grapple pickup, footing wet and cluttered.

Fenced institution-controlled grounds (utility substation, industrial campus, nursery/cemetery grounds): after vegetation trimming, rake and gather clippings and limbs from mowed lawn and gravel/paved areas into piles at a designated point; access controlled, layout fixed and maintained.

Consolidation of debris at the contractor's yard, chip drop or green-waste disposal site: pushing, shoveling and raking loose wood chips, sawdust and dumped brush into consolidated piles for loading or grinding, on a flat compacted surface owned by the operator.

sources.date: 2024-2026 (product page; Heavy Picker sold since 2018, 4.0 launched 2024)
sources.title: Heavy Picker | Sorting Robot | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker is a commercially sold sorting robot that works fully autonomously around the clock, grabbing bulky waste objects (up to 30-40 kg) from a conveyor in a purpose-built, fenced sorting cell and dropping them into separate chutes/bunkers, i.e. piles by fraction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sorting of bulky construction & demolition waste. Transfer: the handled objects include woody debris and irregular bulky pieces of the same size/weight class a trimmer moves by hand, and the accepted output is material separated into piles/bunkers — the E1 rendering of 'collect debris into piles' with the work conveyed to the machine.

sources.system: ZenRobotics robotic sorting plant at Solum A/S

sources.claim: Deployed ZenRobotics installations sort mixed bulky waste streams including wood autonomously at commercial facilities, handling objects up to 30 kg at thousands of picks per hour, 24 hours a ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated separation of wood and bulky debris from a mixed stream. Transfer: same material class (wood, bulky refuse) and same end state (segregated piles) as tree-work debris consolidation, in a conveyor-fed purpose-built facility.

sources.developer: Baidu Research Robotics and Auto-Driving Lab / University of Maryland

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavator material loading at a waste disposal yard. Transfer: consolidating and moving loose heterogeneous debris (chips, sawdust, dumped waste) on a flat institution-controlled yard is the same bulk-material handling problem, with no fine manipulation required.

sources.title: Yarbo Leaf Blower | Wellbots

sources.transferJustification: Same platform as the blower module; establishes the reliability envelope of the only commercial autonomous yard-debris machine in unstructured residential settings.

tasks.label: Cable, brace, tie, bolt, stake, and guy trees and branches to provide support.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private residential yard: install a static or dynamic support cable between codominant leaders of a mature shade tree (oak/maple), 20-40 ft up. Climber on rope or bucket ascends, selects anchor points at ~2/3 of the distance above the union, drills through the stems, sets eye/lag anchors or through-bolts, threads and tensions the cable, and inspects the finished system.

Residential or commercial property: brace a split or cracked union / weak crotch with threaded steel rods - locate the crack, drill straight through both stems at height, drive the rod, add washers and nuts, torque it, often paired with a cable above. Bark, decay pockets, and irregular stem geometry must be judged on the spot.

Landscape installation or street planting: stake and guy newly planted trees - drive two or three stakes or duckbill anchors clear of the root ball into unknown soil, wrap the trunk with webbing/strapping or arbor ties, attach and tension the guys, keep the tree plumb, and avoid girdling. Ground-level work on soft, uneven, obstructed ground.

Municipal street tree or public park: cable, guy, or tie back a mature tree or a partly failed/storm-damaged limb near traffic and pedestrians, working from a bucket truck or climbing line under traffic control, with utility lines, parked cars, and passersby around the work zone.

Managed grounds - production nursery yard, campus, botanical garden, or golf course: stake, tie, and guy young nursery stock and recently transplanted trees in rows or beds; insert canes/stakes, secure whips and leaders with ties, adjust or replace ties on previously staked stock.

sources.system: Serpent Robotics robotic arborist (rope-climbing tree robot)
sources.title: A robotic solution for safer tree trimming | Penn Today
sources.claim: The most advanced arborist climbing robot found is a university-startup prototype that is rope-climbing and ground-CONTROLLED (remote human control via a game-style controller with camera feed), aimed at trimming rather than support hardware installation; it is not autonomous and not deployed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-canopy tree work (trimming). It is the closest robotic system to in-tree cabling/bracing, but it is teleoperated, prototype-stage, and has no drilling, bolting, or cable-tensioning capability, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task at any tier.

sources.system: Review of robotic tree pruning equipment (UAV and climbing pruning systems)
sources.developer: Forest and Wood Products Australia (research report PRC522-2021)
sources.title: A review of current mechanical & robotic tree pruning equipment
sources.claim: A published review of mechanical and robotic tree pruning equipment finds the robotic/UAV in-canopy systems surveyed remain prototypes limited by weather and dense structure, not deployable commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work in tree canopies. Establishes that canopy-access robotics generally remains pre-commercial, which bears directly on whether cabling/bracing at height could be performed robotically.

sources.title: Built Robotics Unveils Autonomous Pile Driving Robot, Expediting Solar Rollout (Forbes)
sources.claim: An autonomous machine exists that surveys and drives structural piles into open ground outdoors, showing the driving-a-post element of staking is automatable in isolation, but it handles only steel piles on graded solar sites and performs no trunk strapping, guying, or tying.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving posts/piles into ground. Transfer fails for tree staking because the instance also requires wrapping and tensioning flexible ties/guys around a living trunk without girdling, which this machine cannot do; it also works only on prepared solar sites with uniform steel piles.

sources.title: Equipment | TTA-ISO
sources.claim: Commercial horticultural automation lines apply clips to plants with vision-guided robotics at high throughput, but the clipped objects are grafted vegetable seedlings on a conveyor, not trees tied to support stakes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanically securing a plant with a clip in a purpose-built line. Transfer fails for nursery tree staking/tying: stem diameters differ by an order of magnitude, the machine inserts no support stake, and it cannot wrap or tension a tie around a trunk.
