tasks.label: Prune, cut down, fertilize, and spray trees as directed by tree surgeons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/commercial property crown work: climbing with rope-and-saddle or working from a bucket lift to remove deadwood, reduce limbs, and clear a mature shade or ornamental tree from a roof, driveway, or service drop; handsaw, hand pruners, and chainsaw; brush lowered by hand or rigged, then dragged to a chipper; work as directed by the crew leader/arborist over an occupied yard with fences, cars, and plantings below.

Utility/roadside line-clearance pruning: directional pruning and side-trimming of street and roadside trees away from primary conductors and secondaries along a right-of-way, from an insulated bucket or with pole pruners/pole saw, near traffic and pedestrians, following the crew leader's clearance spec.

Tree removal: sectional dismantling of a dead or hazardous tree in a confined yard or street strip, rigging pieces down over structures, or straight felling in open ground; includes storm-damage work on broken, loaded limbs; chainsaw work from rope or lift, plus cleanup.

Spraying: applying insecticide, fungicide, horticultural/dormant oil, or foliar nutrient to tree canopies from a hose-and-gun or air-blast spray rig on client landscape properties, nurseries, and orchard-like plantings, following label rates and drift precautions as directed.

Fertilizing: deep-root liquid injection around the drip line, soil drench, or broadcast granular application to landscape trees on residential, campus, and municipal grounds, per the arborist's prescription.

sources.system: GUSS / Mini GUSS autonomous orchard sprayer (John Deere)

sources.title: The World's First Drone Tree Harvest in a Real Forest — AirForestry
sources.claim: A heavy-lift drone completed tree harvesting in a production forest and a fully autonomous grip-delimb-fell-carry sequence on a test field — a first-of-its-kind demonstration, not a fielded service.

tasks.label: Remove broken limbs from wires, using hooked extension poles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Storm/emergency response on a residential street: a large broken limb is hung up in primary distribution conductors after a wind or ice event. A line-clearance groundman, working from the ground beside the truck amid debris, traffic, wet conditions and possible energized downed wires, uses an insulated hooked extension pole to work the limb free and drop it clear without damaging the conductor or causing a phase-to-phase contact.

Routine cycle pruning along a roadside or in a customer's backyard: after aerial saw/pole-saw work, the crew spots 'hangers' — broken or cut limbs lodged in secondary conductors, service drops or the canopy above the line — and pulls them out with a hooked extension pole from the ground or from the bucket, dropping them into a clear landing zone.

Rural right-of-way or wooded corridor: broken limbs resting on single-phase distribution lines along a gravel road or cross-country easement, reached over uneven terrain, brush and ditches; the worker positions on foot with a long hooked pole and dislodges limbs of varying size and hang-up angle.

Non-utility or communications lines: broken limbs lying across telecom/cable drops, guy wires or over a sidewalk or driveway in a residential neighborhood; removal with a hooked pole or pole saw while protecting pedestrians, parked cars and the drop line itself.

Institutionally controlled grounds (university or hospital campus, industrial plant, park district, or a utility-owned yard/substation perimeter): private overhead lines with broken limbs lodged on them; access is controlled by the institution, layout is known, but the trees and hang-ups are as found; removed with a hooked extension pole.

sources.title: A robotic solution for safer tree trimming - Technology Org
sources.claim: A tree-cutting robot that climbs trees and removes branches exists as a university prototype, but it is remotely operated by a human, not autonomous, and is only entering piloting.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic system to arborist limb removal; cited to show the state of the art in robotic branch removal is remote-operated prototype work, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Drone-coupled debris-removal robotic module for high-voltage lines
sources.developer: Academic group (published in Robotics and Autonomous Systems)
sources.title: Semi-autonomous mobile robot coupled to a drone for debris removal from high-voltage power lines - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: The only robotic module demonstrated removing foreign objects from live overhead conductors is semi-autonomous, was manually placed on the line in testing, and clears light debris (sneakers, kites, plastics) by burning it with a flame.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (clearing foreign objects off energized conductors). It does not transfer: the objects are light debris incinerated in place, placement on the line was manual, and autonomy is only partial, so it cannot free a heavy broken limb at worker quality.

sources.title: Energized Services - parelectric.com
sources.claim: The boom-mounted robotic arm used in US energized line work is a crew-operated tool for holding and repositioning energized conductors, not an autonomous manipulator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (manipulating conductors on live overhead lines from a boom). It is directed continuously by a lineman, so it cannot substantiate autonomous limb removal.

sources.system: Laser Obstacle Remover (remote laser tree clearing tool)
sources.developer: AccTek / Chinese laser equipment makers, used by State Grid utilities
sources.title: Laser Obstacle Remover - AccTek Group

sources.transferJustification: Same task (clearing limbs/objects off lines) but the unit is aimed and triggered by an operator throughout, i.e., continuous teleoperation, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: C&D Waste | Sorting Bulky Waste | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: Autonomous grasping and removal of heavy, irregular woody debris is commercially deployed only inside waste-sorting plants, where material is presented on a conveyor beneath a gantry picker.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous picking of heavy irregular wood from clutter). It does not transfer to this task: picking is top-down from a conveyor with no infrastructure to protect, whereas the instance requires overhead extraction of a limb entangled in conductors that must not be damaged.

sources.title: Autonomous robotic pruning in orchards and vineyards: A review - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic cutting of woody plant material remains research-stage even in highly structured agricultural rows, with cutters frequently failing to achieve separation cuts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous manipulation and cutting of branches). Cited to show that even in structured, uniform plantings autonomous branch handling is not at worker quality, reinforcing the negative judgment for limb removal from conductors.

tasks.label: Water, root-feed, and fertilize trees.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Deep-root feeding of established landscape trees at a residential or small commercial property: technician pulls a hose from a truck-mounted tank and injects liquid fertilizer under pressure through a soil probe on a ~2.5 ft grid throughout the root zone (6-10 in depth), working around turf, beds, hardscape, fences, buried irrigation and utilities, and dosing per trunk diameter.

Watering newly planted and establishing trees/shrubs at residential and small commercial landscape sites: repeat visits during the establishment period, 15-25 gallons applied slowly into the mulch basin per tree, or refilling slow-release watering bags, using a hose from a spigot or a tank truck; gates, pets, parked cars, sloped and uneven ground.

Watering street trees and right-of-way plantings in the public realm: a crew drives a tank truck along a curbside route, drags a hose to each tree pit or watering bag, meters water into confined pits amid traffic, parked cars, pedestrians and litter, with cones/traffic control.

Scheduled irrigation top-up of trees and plantings on institution-controlled grounds (municipal park, cemetery, college campus, golf course, corporate grounds): grounds crew waters mapped trees and beds along maintained paths and lawn areas at set intervals, refilling from on-site hydrants or filling points.

Fertilizing rows of trees at a nursery, tree farm, or orchard-style planting: broadcast or banded granular fertilizer and liquid nutrient application down planted rows, plus irrigation of lined-out or containerized stock, on graded, machine-accessible ground controlled by the operation.

sources.title: Mobiler Gießroboter arbeitet bewässert Pflanzen autonom (biallo.de)
sources.claim: The RAINOS autonomous watering robot from Innok Robotics is in commercial service at a Hamburg cemetery gardening operation, where it drives to trees and shrubs at night to water them and autonomously drives to one of four filling stations when its tank runs empty; it works alone and reports unexpected obstacles electronically to its owner.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: applying metered water to trees and shrubs in the ground. The robot dispenses water plant-by-plant on outdoor grounds, which is the watering element of this task.

sources.title: RAINOS - The autonomous watering robot | Innok Robotics
sources.claim: RAINOS is a commercially sold outdoor watering robot that drives and waters completely autonomously for up to 14 hours in ..., refills its 215 L tank autonomously at filling stations in under a minute, delivers up to 20,000 litres per day dosed individually per target, and has been in continuous operation for three years.

sources.title: RAINOS - Autonomous robotics for the smart city
sources.claim: Innok reports RAINOS irrigating municipal parks, cemeteries and green spaces at night, with the city of Mönchengladbach already using the robot in everyday operations.

sources.title: RAINOS: Der autonome Bewässerungsroboter | Gabot.de
sources.claim: Trade coverage describes RAINOS as serving watering in cemeteries, tree nurseries and parks, navigating autonomously to the areas to be watered and supplying each with the precise water volume required.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in the nursery variant: autonomous metered watering of nursery/tree-nursery stock.

sources.title: The evolution of agricultural machinery: transitioning to autonomy in orchards and vineyards (Bluewhite)
sources.claim: Bluewhite's retrofit autonomy kit runs conventional tractors driverless in commercial orchards and vineyards performing spraying, mowing and fertilizer spreading, with more than 150,000 acres and 50,000 autonomous hours completed for over 20 specialty-crop growers in California and Washington.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fertilizer spreading and liquid application to rows of permanent tree crops. Same material (granular/liquid fertilizer), same targets (rows of trees), same outdoor row-planting environment as a nursery or tree-farm planting.

sources.title: New Holland, Bluewhite collaborate on autonomous orchard and vineyard solutions - The Packer
sources.claim: Bluewhite's autonomous solutions have been deployed with more than 20 specialty ... across more than 150,000 acres, and are being integrated with New Holland tractors for orchards and vineyards.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes commercial deployment scale for the autonomous orchard input-application platform cited for row-planting fertilization.

sources.system: GUSS / Mini GUSS autonomous orchard sprayer
sources.title: John Deere Expands with GUSS Orchard & Vineyard Sprayers - Control.com
sources.claim: GUSS autonomous orchard and vineyard sprayers, now owned by John Deere, navigate tree rows using GPS, LiDAR and proprietary software with one operator remotely supervising up to eight machines; over 250 machines have been deployed globally.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of liquid inputs, including foliar nutrient/fertilizer sprays, to rows of trees. Comparable liquid metering and driving precision among trunks in the same row-planting environment.

tasks.label: Scrape decayed matter from cavities in trees and fill holes with cement to promote healing and to prevent further deterioration.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential or commercial property: mature shade tree with a decay cavity at the base or lower trunk. Worker probes the hollow, scrapes/chisels punky rotten wood back to sound tissue with gouges, drawknife or small saw, clears debris and water, then packs the void with concrete/mortar (or foam) and shapes it flush with the bark. Extent of decay is unknown until opened; live callus tissue must not be cut.

Cavity aloft: decay pocket at a branch union, old topping wound, or upper trunk on a yard or park tree, reached on climbing line or from a bucket truck. Worker works one-handed at height over an unstable rot pocket, scrapes out decayed matter, then fills and shapes the patch while suspended.

Park, campus, cemetery or historic/heritage tree: large hollow or column of decay. Extensive excavation of decayed wood, drain provision, sometimes rods/bracing, then a cement/mortar fill placed in lifts and faced flush; done to a preservation standard with a supervising arborist inspecting.

Street tree or utility right-of-way tree: small, shallow wound cavity (old flush cut, mower/vehicle wound) cleaned of decayed matter and filled/sealed at the curbside, with traffic and pedestrians passing and a short work window.

Orchard, grove or nursery: small shallow trunk cavities and wound pockets on young or small trees standing in uniform planted rows at ground level; decayed matter scraped out and the pocket filled, repeated over many similar trees.

sources.title: TRC Woodpatch, fully automated wood patching system
sources.claim: Commercial fully automated timber-patching line scans wooden boards, detects defects, mills the defective material out and fills/patches the hole - the closest deployed analogue to 'scrape out decayed matter and fill the hole', but on planed boards of fixed geometry presented on a conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wood defect repair. It transfers only to small, shallow, regular pockets in wood presented to the machine (the E1 counterfactual): same operation of removing defective wood and filling the void flush. It does not transfer to deep, irregular natural decay cavities of unknown extent, nor to work on standing trees.

sources.developer: Deval et al., published in Sustainability (MDPI)
sources.title: Woodot: An AI-Driven Mobile Robotic System for Sustainable Defect Repair in Custom Glulam Beams
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile manipulator on a timber shop floor locates knot defects on geometrically variable glulam beams, mills them out and plugs them, achieving flush placement in 87% of trials with 4.3 mm mean positional error.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous detection, milling and filling of wood defects on non-planar workpieces. Supports the mill-and-fill motion on variable wood geometry when the workpiece is presented to the robot indoors; the objects are machined beams, not bark-covered trunks with wet decay, so it does not substantiate in-field or deep-cavity work.

sources.title: Autonomous Drone Harvests its First Tree in World First for Forestry (Wood Central)
sources.claim: Frontier of autonomous in-field tree work: an electric drone autonomously selected, delimbed, felled and extracted a tree in a working production forest. Operations demonstrated are cutting and handling of stems; no cavity excavation, wound cleaning or filling is performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tree felling/delimbing in an unstructured forest. Cited to show what autonomous field tree robotics currently covers; it does not transfer to cavity work, which requires selective removal of decayed wood inside a hollow and placement of a shaped cementitious fill.

tasks.label: Spray trees to treat diseased or unhealthy trees, including mixing chemicals and calibrating spray equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential customer property: plant-health-care technician parks a truck with a 200-400 gal hydraulic sprayer at the curb, drags 200-300 ft of hose around a house, fences, cars and pets, and sprays the canopy of one to several mature in-ground landscape trees (30-70 ft oaks, maples, pines) to runoff for scale, borers, anthracnose or apple scab; must judge wind/drift, avoid neighboring property, and post notices.

Street and boulevard trees: crew works from a truck-mounted sprayer or lift in the public right-of-way, spraying municipal street trees for pests/disease amid moving traffic, parked cars, pedestrians, overhead utility lines and varying tree species and heights, with traffic cones and drift control.

Institutional grounds (college campus, golf course, cemetery, corporate park, city park): scattered specimen trees on maintained turf, access controlled by the grounds department; technician drives a sprayer rig over the grounds and treats designated diseased trees, often scheduled outside public hours.

Nursery, tree farm or orchard-style block: rows of uniformly spaced young/small trees and container stock treated with an air-blast or boom sprayer for foliar disease and insects; fixed row layout, machine alleys, no public present.

Pre-application preparation at the company yard or tailgate: reading the pesticide label, measuring and diluting concentrate into the tank (or loading product), agitating the mix, and calibrating the spray equipment - checking nozzle output/pressure and setting the application rate before going out on route.

sources.system: GUSS (Global Unmanned Spray System) autonomous orchard sprayer

sources.claim: GUSS autonomous orchard sprayers are commercially deployed at scale in orchards and vineyards, with over 250 machines and millions of acres sprayed, spraying tree crops without an operator aboard.

sources.title: John Deere Formally Adds Autonomous Sprayer Company to its Portfolio
sources.claim: GUSS machines run driverless under remote supervision, one operator monitoring up to eight machines from ... laptop - i.e., autonomous operation with limited intervention rather than continuous teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes autonomy level for the orchard canopy-spraying evidence used for this task.

sources.title: Autonomous Orchard Sprayer Optimizes Use of Labour Improves Safety and Sustainability
sources.claim: The GUSS machine is an air-blast canopy sprayer engineered for orchard/vineyard rows, navigating rows with GPS and LiDAR while spraying the tree canopy.
sources.transferJustification: Air-blast canopy spraying of trees for pest and disease control is the same physical operation as spraying a diseased shade tree, performed on trees presented in fixed row positions.

sources.system: GUSS with Smart Apply Intelligent Spray Control System
sources.title: Deere & GUSS Automation Unveil Electric Option and Smart Apply Upgrade
sources.claim: GUSS sprayers can be equipped with Smart Apply intelligent application control, combining automated blast spraying with sensor-based application accuracy (automatic on-target rate control).
sources.transferJustification: Automatic sensor-driven metering of spray output onto tree canopies substitutes for the manual rate-setting/calibration step of the human task.

sources.system: Raven Sidekick Pro direct injection system
sources.title: Sidekick Pro Direct Injection | Raven Industries
sources.claim: Direct-injection spray systems meter pesticide concentrate automatically into the carrier stream, eliminating manual tank mixing on commercially sold agricultural sprayers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chemical mixing/metering for agricultural spraying. The machine performs the same measuring-and-diluting-to-label-rate function the tree worker performs at the tank, with equal or better dosing precision.

sources.system: Raven Sidekick Pro direct injection system
sources.title: Raven Industries Raven Sidekick Pro Direct Injection Systems (Dultmeier Sales)
sources.claim: The same direct-injection product includes an automatic calibration feature, automating the sprayer calibration step.
sources.transferJustification: Calibrating spray equipment is an explicit part of this task; automatic calibration on a commercial sprayer performs that step by machine.

sources.system: BeMatic Meto spray robot with MetoTrans transport trolley
sources.title: BeMatic Meto Spraying Robot | Royal Brinkman
sources.claim: Rail-guided spray robots that drive and switch paths autonomously to spray crops without anyone present are standard commercial equipment in greenhouse/nursery horticulture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended pesticide spraying of nursery/greenhouse plant stock. Same chemicals and coverage requirement as treating diseased nursery trees, in a setting where plants are presented in fixed positions.

tasks.label: Apply tar or other protective substances to cut surfaces or seal surfaces and to protect them from fungi and insects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/commercial property: after removing a large limb from a mature shade tree (e.g., oak in an oak-wilt area), the climber or bucket operator brushes or sprays wound paint/tar onto each fresh cut face, working aloft on rope or from an aerial lift, over lawn, fences, and structures; cut faces are irregular, at varied heights and orientations, and must be coated within minutes of cutting.

Utility line-clearance / street right-of-way: after cutting brush and small stems along a roadside, fence line, or under conductors, the crew applies cut-stump herbicide/sealant to stump tops and cut stubs at or near ground level with a squirt bottle, backpack sprayer, or brush; uneven terrain, traffic, brush piles, and mixed species taken as found.

Municipal park, campus, cemetery, or golf-course grounds: ornamental and shade trees pruned by the grounds crew, then sealant/pruning paint applied to selected cuts and to any bark wounds, mostly from the ground or a short ladder/lift, with turf, paths, benches, and the public nearby.

Commercial orchard or vineyard block: after dormant or summer pruning of fruit/nut trees or vines planted in uniform trellised rows, a wound protectant (fungicide or sealant) is applied to the pruning wounds across the block within a few days of cutting.

Nursery, garden center, or greenhouse: sealant, grafting wax, or protectant applied to cut/graft surfaces on containerized or bench-held young trees, shrubs, and grafted liners handled at working height inside the facility.

sources.system: GUSS / Global Unmanned Spray System autonomous orchard sprayer
sources.title: John Deere acquires GUSS Automation to expand autonomous spraying in vineyards and orchards
sources.claim: GUSS autonomous orchard/vineyard sprayers navigate planted rows and apply spray materials with one remote operator supervising up to eight machines; over 250 machines deployed globally with 500,000 autonomous spraying hours, now a John Deere business.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine canopy spray application in orchard/vineyard rows. Pruning-wound protectant is delivered by exactly this kind of sprayer pass over the same rows, same materials handling and coverage requirement (evidence 1 and 2), so the autonomous sprayer's demonstrated capability carries over to applying protective substances to pruning cuts.

sources.system: Airblast orchard sprayer applying Topsin M pruning-wound protectant
sources.developer: orchard industry practice reported by West Coast Nut / UC farm advisors
sources.title: Canker Disease in Almond Orchards | West Coast Nut
sources.claim: Applying protective fungicide to pruning wounds on orchard trees is standard practice using an airblast (orchard) sprayer rather than hand brushing, achieving good coverage of the wounds.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the accepted-quality standard for machine (sprayer) application of protectant to cut surfaces in orchards; it is tractor-driven, so it supplies quality/acceptance evidence, not autonomy — autonomy comes from evidence 0.

sources.system: Tractor-driven vineyard sprayers for pruning-wound protection
sources.developer: 研究: Sosnowski et al., Plant Disease (APS)
sources.title: Evaluating Treatments and Spray Application for the Protection of Grapevine Pruning Wounds from Infection by Eutypa lata
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed field trials found fungicide applied to grapevine pruning wounds by tractor-driven sprayers reduced pruning-wound infection to levels similar to hand application with a paint brush.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that spray-rig delivery of a protectant to pruning cuts equals hand-brush application in outcome, so an autonomous sprayer pass (evidence 0) yields worker-quality output for this task in row plantings.

sources.system: iGiotto anthropomorphic spraying robot with cVision 3D scanner
sources.title: Programming coating robots for window frame spraying | Cefla Finishing
sources.claim: Cefla's iGiotto/iBotic industrial coating robots scan each incoming workpiece in 3D inside a spray booth, generate spray trajectories automatically, and run the whole coating cycle without operator programming, coating complex-shaped wood parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic protective coating of variable-geometry wood workpieces presented to the machine. Sealing a cut face is the same physical act — sensing an irregular wood surface and covering it with a viscous protective material — at lower precision than furniture/window finishing, so capability transfers when the workpiece is fixtured and presented (E1).

sources.system: Harvester-head stump treatment equipment (urea / Rotstop spray systems, e.g. Clark Jet Spray, Prentice/Cat stump spray kit)
sources.developer: forest machine manufacturers; study by Natural Resources Institute Finland (Forests, MDPI)
sources.title: Treatment of Picea abies and Pinus sylvestris Stumps with Urea and Phlebiopsis gigantea for Control of Heterobasidion
sources.claim: Commercial harvester heads carry stump-treatment kits that spray urea or Rotstop onto the freshly cut stump surface in the forest, but the spraying is controlled by the machine operator in the cab rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task (applying an anti-fungal substance to a fresh cut surface) in an outdoor forest, but the machine is operator-driven, so it cannot support a positive E3 judgment; it only shows the dispensing act itself is machine-executable.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Pruning in Orchards and Vineyards: a Review
sources.claim: A 2025 review of autonomous robotic pruning in orchards ... characterises in-canopy robotic pruning platforms as an active research area of compact experimental platforms, not fielded products.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation at individual cut points on woody plants. Even in the most structured tree crops this remains research-stage, so no system exists that can locate and coat individual pruning wounds on trees in the field.

tasks.label: Transplant and remove trees and shrubs, and prepare trees for moving.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential yard: removal of a mature shade tree (2–4 ft trunk, 50–80 ft tall) growing beside a house, fence, driveway and service drop. Climber or bucket operator dismantles the tree in sections, rigs and lowers limbs into a tight drop zone, flush-cuts the stem, then the crew chips brush, loads wood and rakes the site.

Residential/commercial landscape beds: removal of overgrown or dead shrubs and small ornamental trees (2–8 in caliper) close to foundations, walkways, irrigation heads and other plantings — cut down with chainsaw/loppers, root ball or stump dug/pulled with hand tools, mattock or mini skid-steer, hole backfilled and debris hauled off.

Municipal street/parkway tree removal: standing dead or storm-damaged curbside tree over sidewalk and traffic lane, often within a few feet of overhead conductors and parked cars. Crew sets cones/flaggers, dismantles from a bucket truck, lowers pieces to the street, chips and clears the roadway before reopening it.

Utility right-of-way / rural roadside: removal of danger trees leaning toward energized lines plus clearing of saplings and brush along the corridor, on uneven ground, in variable weather, sometimes with limited machine access, with wood left on site or chipped.

Transplanting established plants on a landscape site: root-pruning ahead of the move, digging a root ball by hand or with a truck/skid-steer tree spade, wrapping in burlap and wire basket, moving the plant to a prepared hole, setting to correct grade, backfilling, staking, mulching and watering.

Wholesale nursery / garden-center yard (institution-controlled, standard bed layout and gravel or fabric surface): consolidating, spacing and staging container-grown shrubs and small trees so stock is ready to move to shipping or to a planting job.

sources.title: Fully Autonomous Drone Harvests Its First Tree in World First
sources.claim: AirForestry's electric heavy-lift drone autonomously felled a tree and carried the trunk out of a working production forest — the only cited example of fully autonomous tree removal, and a first-of-its-kind milestone rather than a service in production.
sources.transferJustification: Tree felling/removal is the core of this task, but the demonstration is in an open production-forest stand with no structures, conductors, or drop-zone constraints, and includes no debris cleanup or stump work.

sources.title: Swedish startup achieves first fully autonomous tree harvest by drone
sources.claim: In the AirForestry demonstration the drone independently approached, identified, delimbed, felled and transported the tree, establishing that the sequence was autonomous rather than teleoperated.

sources.title: A drone just cut down a tree, stripped its branches, and carried it out of a forest — on its own
sources.claim: The AirForestry drone's payload limit confines it to small thinning stems of roughly 40–140 kg, far below the mass of the yard, street and right-of-way trees arborists remove, which are dismantled in rigged sections.

sources.title: Harvey: A working robot for container crops
sources.claim: Harvest Automation's HV-100 ('Harvey') robots autonomously pick up, carry and place container-grown nursery plants in greenhouses and outdoor nursery beds, navigating with LiDAR around people, sprinkler risers and other robots; they were sold to and used by commercial growers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spacing/collecting containerized nursery stock. It transfers only to the nursery-yard instance of preparing container-grown shrubs and small trees for moving — comparable objects (potted plants up to ~12.5 in containers), comparable precision, same institution-controlled nursery setting. It does not dig, plant, or remove in-ground stock.

sources.title: Robot avatar safely trims trees around active power lines
sources.claim: Sarcos' Guardian XT was promoted for utility tree trimming but is an operator-worn/VR-controlled avatar, i.e. continuous teleoperation, so it cannot support an autonomous-completion judgment for tree work near lines.

sources.title: A Robotic Solution for Safer Tree Trimming
sources.claim: The most recent urban tree-care robotics effort found is a university-startup rope-climbing tree-cutting prototype still to be piloted, indicating no fielded autonomous system for dismantling trees on residential or street sites.

sources.developer: Umeå University / Skogforsk and partners, Sweden
sources.title: Vision-based planting position selection system for an unmanned reforestation machine
sources.claim: Autonomous forest regeneration research (AutoPlant) has achieved only a limited number of autonomous seedling-planting cycles in forest terrain with an unmanned reforestation machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine planting of bare-root/containerized seedlings. It does not transfer to transplanting: no excavation or preservation of an established root ball, no burlapping, no lifting and re-setting of a standing plant, and only a handful of research cycles.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics announces autonomous excavation milestone
sources.claim: Autonomous excavation is real on construction sites (Bedrock Robotics excavators autonomously moving dirt for site preparation), but the demonstrated work is bulk earthmoving, not tree or root-ball handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soil excavation. It does not transfer to transplanting or tree removal — no evidence of cutting a root ball without destroying it, wrapping it, lifting a live plant, or setting and backfilling it at grade.

tasks.label: Split logs or wooden blocks into bolts, pickets, posts, or stakes, using hand tools such as ax wedges, sledgehammers, and mallets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At a residential removal job: after the trunk is bucked into rounds, the trimmer drives steel wedges with a sledgehammer to split 16–30 in. rounds lying on the lawn or driveway, so pieces are light enough to carry past landscaping to the chip truck or to leave as firewood for the homeowner. Uneven turf, obstacles, weather as found.

At the tree company's yard or woodlot: rounds dumped in piles from the week's removals are split with maul and wedges into firewood bolts for sale or crew use, then stacked. Yard is company-controlled but shared with trucks, chippers and crew moving about; logs lie as they were dumped.

At the yard or a nursery: straight-grained bolts are split (froe/mallet, wedges) and trimmed into tree stakes, guy posts or landscape pickets of a specified cross-section and length for staking newly planted trees or building rustic fencing.

On site at a customer property or park: splitting awkward material where it lies — knotty crotchwood, buttress rounds, occasionally metal-contaminated urban wood — or riving rails/pales for a rustic fence feature, working around plantings, slopes and bystanders.

sources.system: POSCH SpaltFix K-710 a-Vario automatic firewood processor
sources.developer: POSCH Gesellschaft m.b.H. (dealer: Jas P Wilson)
sources.title: Posch K-710 a-Vario Automatic Firewood Processor | Jas P Wilson
sources.claim: The POSCH SpaltFix K-710 a-Vario is a commercially sold automatic firewood processor that takes logs up to 70 cm diameter and cuts, splits and discharges them through a full machine cycle without operator input, using optical measuring sensors and a light curtain that stops and restarts the cycle automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: the machine performs the splitting of log sections into billets/bolts that this task performs by wedge and sledgehammer, on the same material and size range.

sources.title: Interforst 2022: Posch's new SpaltFix K-710 a-Vario firewood processor in action | Forestry Journal
sources.claim: Trade press covering the machine's public demonstration at Interforst 2022 confirms the K-710 a-Vario runs a fully automatic cut-and-split cycle initiated by a single button press, for logs up to 70 ... diameter.

sources.system: POSCH log charging / AutoFeed with SpaltFix processors
sources.title: Firewood processor - find the right fuelwood machinery here | POSCH
sources.claim: POSCH also sells log-charging/AutoFeed equipment that keeps the automatic saw-splitter continuously fed from a log deck and cross conveyors, so the purpose-built line presents workpieces to the splitting machine one way.

sources.date: 2024-04 (vendor page); technical review PDF undated but current
sources.title: Automatic firewood processor (TalTech report) / SAMI Autofactory – Reikälevy Oy
sources.claim: The SAMI Autofactory (Autosorter loading table, sorter and transfer conveyor plus Autochopper processor) automates the whole firewood production chain: logs are placed on the loading table and everything after that — sorting, feeding, sawing and splitting — runs automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: automatic sawing and splitting of logs into split billets — the same physical operation as splitting logs into bolts by hand.

sources.title: 2040XP2 | Multitek Inc / Tech Review: Firewood Processors – Forestnet
sources.claim: US-built commercial firewood processors are designed for exactly the awkward, crooked and knotty log stock that resists hand splitting, with live-deck log flippers and shuttle grapples to bring irregular pieces into the trough of the splitting machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (splitting log sections into firewood bolts); cited only for the material range of purpose-built splitting cells, not for autonomy, since cab/joystick involvement is not established.

sources.system: ANDRITZ LogPorter log yard crane with Metris ANDI
sources.title: Log yard cranes | ANDRITZ
sources.claim: ANDRITZ markets a log yard crane with Metris ANDI crane AI claimed to run fully autonomously handling loose wood in a mill woodyard, using laser scanners and cameras; it moves and stacks logs but performs no splitting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (picking loose logs from a yard pile). Cited to show that only the log-handling step, in a dedicated gantry woodyard built around the crane, is automated; no splitting is performed, so it cannot complete this task in an as-found work yard.

sources.developer: Umeå University / SLU et al. (La Hera et al.)
sources.title: Exploring the feasibility of autonomous forestry operations: Results from the first experimental unmanned machine – Journal of Field Robotics
sources.claim: Autonomous handling of logs by machines working in the open, off a prepared line, remains experimental: the first unmanned forestry machine for autonomous log extraction is reported as an experimental platform with initial results, not a deployed product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous log manipulation in unstructured outdoor terrain). Cited as the state of the art bounding E2/E3 claims: it handles whole logs, does no splitting, and is an experimental prototype.

tasks.label: Perform minor repairs or make adjustments to slot machines, resolving problems such as machine tilts and coin jams.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casino gaming floor, machine locked up on a bill/voucher jam: a crumpled banknote or TITO ticket is wedged in the bill validator. Supervisor keys open the main door or validator head, extracts the mangled note/ticket without tearing it, reseats the validator and stacker, closes the door, clears the tilt and confirms the guest's credit while the guest waits.

Casino gaming floor, machine tilt/error condition (door-open tilt, communication error, reboot needed, call-attendant lockup). Supervisor keys the machine, reads the error on the screen or internal display, presses the internal reset button / power-cycles / uses the reset key, closes and secures the door, and verifies the game returns to play.

Casino gaming floor, ticket printer fault: out-of-paper tilt or paper jam in the TITO printer. Supervisor opens the machine, pulls the printer module out on its slide, clears any jammed ticket stock, loads a new thermal roll, feeds and seats the paper past the print head, closes the module, and test-prints.

Coin-handling faults on legacy coin-in/coin-out machines and coin devices: coin jammed in the acceptor, chute or hopper, hopper needing to be freed or refilled, coin comparator cleared. Supervisor opens the cabinet, works the jammed coin(s) out of the mechanism by hand or with a small tool, and re-runs the hopper test.

Minor part swap or mechanical adjustment on the floor: burned-out candle/lamp or button lamp, sticky or dead play button, loose or unseated ribbon/harness connector, unresponsive player-card reader, or swapping a failed printer/validator module for a spare from the slot shop, then testing the machine back into service.

Diagnosis that the fault exceeds a minor repair: supervisor inspects the machine, determines a board/reel/display failure, secures the machine (locks door, places out-of-service placard or removes the chair), documents the fault and calls the slot technician or recommends removal for shop repair.

sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center - DCD
sources.claim: Alibaba's second-generation Tianxun robot autonomously inspects racked servers, locates a faulty hard disk and replaces it in about four minutes; the system is reported in operation at five Alibaba data centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fault-locating and swapping a failed electronic module in standardized equipment inside a controlled facility. It transfers to the reset/module-swap slices of slot servicing (locating an indicated fault on a known machine model and performing a simple, standardized service action on it), but only where the equipment and its interfaces are laid out for the robot, as racks are.

sources.title: Apple adds Earth Day donations to trade-in and recycling program - Apple Newsroom
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy robot autonomously disassembles fixtured iPhones of multiple known models in a purpose-built cell, punching out screws and removing and sorting internal modules at up to 200 devices per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtured teardown of a known consumer-electronics model, removing fasteners and lifting out rigid internal modules. Comparable objects (screwed/latched electronic modules) and precision to pulling and replacing a lamp, button panel or printer module in a fixtured gaming machine presented in a known position.

sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A UR10e arm with RealSense vision and a custom mechatronic screwdriver autonomously locates, identifies and removes screws of several head types across a range of electronic devices on a bench.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided fastener removal on bench-fixtured electronics, the access step for swapping a lamp, button or peripheral module inside a slot machine cabinet presented in a fixture.

sources.title: Casino Robots — Industry Solutions | robotcobot
sources.claim: Robots commercially marketed and deployed on casino gaming floors perform autonomous floor cleaning and food/beverage delivery; no offering covers servicing or repairing slot machines.

tasks.label: Reset slot machines after payoffs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine hand-pay jackpot lockup on a busy casino floor: after the jackpot is verified and paid, the supervisor/attendant inserts the jackpot reset key into the machine's key switch (candle or door lock), gives it a quarter turn, and the machine clears the lockup and returns to play; the patron is seated at the machine and aisle traffic flows around it.

Reset that requires opening the cabinet: unlock the main slot door with the door key, swing the door open, press the internal reset/jackpot button or acknowledge the on-screen prompt, glance at the meters, then close and re-lock the door and confirm the game returns to play.

Reset combined with clearing an accompanying fault after the payoff: ticket printer out of paper or a jammed ticket, a jammed note in the bill validator, or a coin/hopper jam on legacy units — open the machine, clear the jam or thread a fresh paper roll, then clear the lockup and reset.

Reset requiring service-menu or passcode interaction: the attendant enters an employee code or navigates the machine's on-screen service menu (often alongside a handheld/slot-accounting confirmation of the jackpot) and then key-resets the lockup.

Reset at a route or small-venue location (tavern, truck stop, small gaming room) with mixed legacy machine models wedged into corners or wall banks; varying key-switch positions, cramped access, and no uniform cabinet layout.

sources.system: Physical Intelligence π0.6 robot (Robot Olympics key task)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: A vision-language-action policy (Physical Intelligence π0.6) autonomously inserted and turned a key to unlock a lockbox and a door in the 'Robot Olympics' evaluation, but roughly 5x slower than a human, with ~52% average success across tasks and no demonstrated transfer to other locks.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical action as a jackpot reset: seat a small key in a lock cylinder and rotate it. Shows the skill exists autonomously but only on specific, pre-trained locks in a lab setup, at reliability well below what a casino would accept on the floor.

sources.system: Hyper-redundant soft robotic arm with unified compliance/position controller
sources.developer: Zuo, Zou, Wu, Li, Bruder (University of Michigan)
sources.title: Real-Time Compliance and Position Control of a Hyper-redundant Soft Robotic Arm (arXiv)
sources.claim: A hyper-redundant compliant robot arm autonomously performed a key-insertion and drawer-opening task, passively correcting hidden misalignment during key entry using controlled tip compliance, on a fixtured lab bench.
sources.transferJustification: Unlock-with-key then pull open a compartment is the same sequence as unlocking a slot machine's main door; performed with a known lock in a fixtured bench setup, i.e., an E1-style presentation of the work.

sources.title: World's 1st humanoid robot-led EV battery production begins in China
sources.claim: CATL deployed humanoid robots on a battery production line that autonomously insert high-voltage connectors into mating receptacles at greater than 99% success and human-comparable cycle times.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided precision insertion of a small rigid part into a tight receptacle at production reliability. It transfers to seating a reset key in a fixtured key switch — comparable object size, sub-millimetre alignment tolerance, and a purpose-built line where the workpiece pose is known.

sources.system: ArtiMinds RPS force-controlled robot endurance test cell (ignition lock testing)
sources.title: Robot-Based Endurance Tests: Ignition Lock Testing - YouTube (ArtiMinds Robotics)
sources.claim: An industrial robot cell with force-controlled programming performs endurance testing of vehicle ignition locks, repeatedly inserting and turning a key in a lock cylinder held in a test fixture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated robotic insertion and rotation of a key in a lock cylinder inside a fixtured industrial test cell, run unattended for many cycles. This is the exact motion and precision class of a jackpot reset key turn, in an E1 environment.

sources.system: Spot with Spot Arm (Autowalk / Orbit door opening)

sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot with its arm autonomously opens doors during Autowalk inspection missions at industrial facilities, with the feature deployed to beta customers who have opened thousands of doors.

tasks.label: Attach "out of order" signs to malfunctioning machines, and notify technicians when machines need to be repaired or removed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Main gaming floor, mid-shift: a reel or video slot machine faults (bill-validator jam, ticket-printer error, comm/tilt error). The slot shift supervisor walks the bank, confirms the fault, sets a plastic 'out of order' placard on the button deck/screen (or tips the chair), and radios/enters a work order for a slot technician. Patrons are seated at adjacent machines; carpeted, dim, aisles with chairs.

Peak period or specialty location: bar-top video poker at a service bar, or a machine in a high-limit salon, goes down while a guest is playing. Supervisor moves the guest, places the out-of-order sign amid stools, drinks and crowding, and calls the technician by radio/phone.

Peripheral device failure: ticket-redemption (TITO) kiosk, ATM or players-club kiosk stops working. Supervisor prints or grabs a paper 'out of order' notice and tapes it to the kiosk screen/bezel, then phones the in-house tech or outside vendor.

Table-games side of the pit: an automatic shuffler, chip sorter, or electronic table game terminal malfunctions. Supervisor closes the position, lays a 'closed / out of order' placard on the layout or terminal, notifies the technician, and logs the fault.

Machine to be pulled from service: chronic fault or awaiting parts. Supervisor tags the machine out (attaches an out-of-service tag/sign, often at the door or handle), records asset number and fault history, and coordinates with slot technicians/slot operations for repair or removal from the floor.

Foreign currency: an international guest presents foreign banknotes at the cage; the supervisor authenticates the notes, applies the posted rate and fee, and pays out US bills (and coin residual) in the combination requested.

instances.label: Live-shift wipe-down/sanitizing of a bank of slot machines on the gaming floor: touchscreens, button decks, bill validator/ticket printer faces, cabinet glass and toppers, handles, armrests and stool seats, using cloth and spray cleaner while adjacent machines are occupied by players.

Clearing the area around the machines during a shift: removing empty glasses, cups, bottles, napkins and discarded TITO tickets from cup holders, chair seats and carpet; emptying ashtrays where smoking is permitted; putting trash in bins and straightening stools.

Graveyard-shift detail clean of an idle bank: polishing glass and topper signage, dusting cabinet tops, light fixtures and reel glass, cleaning coin trays, bill acceptor faces and card readers, wiping and vacuuming the carpet immediately around machine bases, wiping and squaring up stools.

Vacuuming/sweeping the carpeted aisles and open floor between slot banks (small casino, tavern route location, or graveyard EVS assist), running a vacuum along the aisle and around the machine bases to pick up dry debris.

Spill and mess response: a patron's drink goes over the machine and carpet - wipe the cabinet, button deck and bill acceptor without soaking electronics, blot/spot-clean the carpet, set a wet-floor sign, and return the machine to play; call a tech if liquid got inside.

Light in-service maintenance of the machine: refill the TITO ticket printer paper roll, clear a jammed/crumpled bill from the validator, clean the acceptor and card reader path, swap a failed button lamp, and tag or report the machine for technician repair.

tasks.label: Monitor functioning of slot machine coin dispensers and fill coin hoppers when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Casino gaming floor with legacy coin-operated slot bank: a machine goes 'hopper empty' mid-play; the supervisor draws a weighed/counted coin fill from the cage with dual-key control and a security escort, unlocks the slot cabinet, pours the coin bag into the hopper, verifies and signs the fill slip, resets the machine and completes the patron's payout. Patrons and staff crowd the aisle.

Routine shift rounds over a bank of coin-dispensing machines: check hopper levels and dispenser operation (system exception reports plus physical look-in), top off low hoppers before peak play, log fills and note machines trending toward faults.

Ticket redemption kiosk / coin change machine on the casino floor: system alert shows the coin hopper low; supervisor unlocks the kiosk, loads counted coin into the hopper or cassette, runs a test dispense, secures the kiosk and reconciles the load.

Coin dispenser malfunction: bent/jammed coin or failing hopper motor causes a short pay while a patron waits; supervisor clears the jam, counts and hand-pays the shortfall, documents the incident and tags the machine out of service for the slot technician.

Route/small-venue gaming (bar, tavern, truck stop, small gaming room, older riverboat/tribal floor): supervisor travels between scattered machines in varied layouts with limited back-of-house support, checks coin dispensers and fills hoppers from a coin bank carried to the location.

instances.label: Slot floor jackpot hand-pay: supervisor responds to a locked-up machine on a $1,200-$10,000 taxable win, verifies the win on the meter and in the slot system, records the jackpot, collects player ID/SSN and signature for the W-2G receipt, counts out currency to the player at the machine, and resets the machine. Race and sports book: supervisor working or covering the writing counter takes the customer's cash and verbal wager, records the bet in the wagering terminal, prints and hands over the bet ticket receipt with change; later scans presented winning/void tickets, verifies them, and pays cash from the drawer. Casino sportsbook or racebook, peak-hour lines.

Live table-games pit: floor supervisor verifies and authorizes an unusual or oversized payoff (large winning bet, progressive side-bet hit, table-game hand pay), records it on the table paperwork/system, and pays it off with chips pushed to the player or by delivering a cash hand-pay at the table with the dealer and patrons present.

Keno lounge / bingo hall: supervisor or lead writer records the patron's marked ticket into the keno/bingo system, issues the printed ticket receipt, and pays off winning tickets in cash from the payout bank at the counter or via a runner. Institution-run lounge with fixed counter and standard equipment.

Cage / redemption area: supervisor redeems presented TITO slot tickets, vouchers and small winning bets in cash, records the transactions, issues receipts, and verifies drawer/bank balances; also clears kiosk jams and handles rejected tickets.

instances.label: Theme park, water park, or family entertainment center: the attraction supervisor steps onto the ride platform or deck to help operators with a hard case they cannot resolve — securing a restraint on an atypically sized guest, transferring a guest with a mobility disability into a ride vehicle, calming and handling a distressed or non-compliant rider, or leading a manual unload when a ride stops with guests aboard. Crowds, queue pressure, and safety rules apply.

Indoor recreation/fitness/aquatics facility: the supervisor takes over a safety-critical hands-on procedure a staffer cannot manage alone — assisting a lifeguard with a difficult water rescue and spinal-board extrication, lifting and assessing a member who fell, giving first aid, or spotting/transferring a client with limited mobility during instruction.

Facility setup or breakdown: the supervisor pitches in when staff struggle with heavy or awkward equipment — rolling out bleachers, moving staging, gym dividers, table and chair stacks, pool lane lines or bulkheads, anchoring an inflatable — reconfiguring a room or field to the layout the next program requires, on a deadline.

Equipment troubleshooting the staffer cannot handle: the supervisor diagnoses and clears or repairs a balky machine — jammed bowling pinsetter, projector or sound fault in a theater, jammed ticket scanner or POS, go-kart engine, arcade or ropes-course hardware, a ski lift mis-load — using hand tools and improvised judgment before service resumes.

Outdoor/field program: at a camp, challenge course, trail, ski hill, or waterfront, the supervisor joins counselors or instructors on site to handle what they cannot — rescuing a participant stuck on a high-ropes element, toweing an injured skier down, righting a capsized kayak, managing a group in weather and terrain taken as found.

sources.claim: An autonomous underwater rescue robot cued by pool ceiling cameras can locate a submerged person and bring them to the surface, tested with an 80 kg dummy — one sub-step of a rescue, as a research prototype, not the supervisor's full intervention (extrication, assessment, spinal precautions, incident handling).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aquatic rescue. Closest system to the aquatics instance; cited to show only a sub-step is automated, at prototype maturity, so the whole supervisor-assist instance is not substantiated.

tasks.label: Inspect work areas or operating equipment to ensure conformance to established standards in areas such as cleanliness or maintenance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Health club / YMCA / municipal recreation center supervisor's daily walkthrough: fixed indoor layout of gym floor, studios, courts, locker rooms and restrooms. Checks floors and machines wiped and free of debris, trash emptied, weights racked, upholstery/cables/belts undamaged, hazards and burned-out lights, supplies stocked; logs findings and raises work orders. Patrons present for part of the round.

Amusement or water park attraction-area supervisor's opening walkthrough of the area surrounding the ride: queue switchbacks, midway, load platform, splash decks and staff station. Looks for litter, spills, slick surfaces, damaged fencing or missing signage, and confirms the area is presentable before guests enter. Outdoor, weather-exposed, before park open.

Amusement park attraction pre-opening operational check of the ride equipment itself: cycle the ride empty, verify restraints lock/release and e-stops function, walk the track and ride envelope for debris or loose hardware, confirm the maintenance department's sign-off before carrying guests.

Indoor entertainment venue supervisor (cinema, bowling center, arcade/family entertainment center, trampoline park) inspecting after the cleaning shift and between sessions: auditorium seating and floors, restrooms, lanes and pinsetter areas, game cabinets, attraction padding and netting; verifies crew work meets brand cleanliness standards and flags equipment needing repair.

Aquatic center / community pool supervisor's round: pool deck and gutters, water surface clarity and debris, locker rooms and showers, chemical feed and pump/filter room equipment condition, placement and condition of rescue tubes, backboard and first-aid kit; wet floors, humidity, chlorinated air.

Outdoor recreation supervisor (campground, park district grounds, marina, ski area, ropes/adventure course) inspecting sites taken as found: campsites and fire rings, vault/flush restrooms, picnic shelters, trails and playgrounds, lift terminals or course hardware and harnesses; variable terrain, weather, and no fixed layout site to site.

sources.title: Orbit 5.0 adds features to Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Orbit software applies AI to imagery captured on Spot's autonomous facility patrols to detect visual anomalies such as ... and corrosion without manual review — the same class of cleanliness/condition judgment this task requires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated 'operator rounds' in industrial plants. It is the same act — walking a fixed route through a work area and judging areas and equipment against cleanliness/maintenance standards — on comparable objects (floors, machines, safety equipment) in an institution-controlled facility.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics releases software updates to Orbit fleet management platform, Spot robots - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Orbit's vision-language-prompt inspection flags safety issues such as spills or missing fire extinguishers and monitors equipment wear and tear from images Spot captures on autonomous patrol.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: facility condition rounds. The checklist content (housekeeping hazards, presence of required safety equipment, wear on equipment) matches a supervisor's cleanliness/maintenance inspection; assets differ but the perception and reporting demands are comparable.

sources.title: Automated Inspections Made Simple | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot executes recorded inspection missions autonomously, walking the route, performing the recorded actions at each point and replanning around changes, with results reviewable and routable into enterprise asset-management systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled equipment inspection rounds in plants and on facility grounds. Demonstrates the end-to-end deliverable of this task — an autonomous route, per-point checks, and a logged report/work order — inside institution-controlled premises.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor robot patrols occupied commercial buildings autonomously along mapped routes, using onboard sensing and AI to flag anomalies such as open doors, leaks and unusual conditions to a monitoring team.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: indoor building patrol with anomaly reporting. Same environment class as an indoor recreation venue (fixed layout, institution-controlled) and the same output — a route-based sweep that reports deviations from the normal/expected state of the premises.

sources.title: Badger Technologies robots working 6 Vallarta Supermarkets - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Badger Technologies' Retail InSpect robot autonomously traverses store aisles among shoppers, using onboard cameras to detect liquid, powder and bulk-food spills and debris and alert staff; hundreds of units are deployed in US chains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: floor-condition/hazard auditing in a public-facing facility during trading hours. Directly matches the cleanliness half of this task (spills, debris) in a customer-occupied venue of the same structural type as a cinema lobby, gym floor or bowling center.

sources.title: Knightscope Deploys Security Robots at Casino and International Airport
sources.claim: Knightscope's autonomous security robots are deployed across entertainment properties including casinos and an international airport under a multi-property agreement, patrolling public venues indoors and outdoors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous patrol of guest-occupied entertainment venues and their outdoor lots. Establishes that mapped-route mobile inspection platforms operate reliably in exactly the venue class of this occupation, supporting transfer of Spot/Cobalt-style inspection rounds there.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + FieldAI Field Foundation Models
sources.title: Case Study: Practical Autonomy on Construction Sites | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot equipped with FieldAI's foundation models performs inspection, mapping and monitoring job walks autonomously on active construction sites with no prior maps, GPS or pre-planned routes, delivering site data each morning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unstructured-site walkthroughs capturing progress and inspection data. Shows autonomous traversal and imaging of E3 terrain, but the deliverable is documentation/progress comparison rather than condition judgment over heterogeneous recreation assets.

sources.title: Elios Drone Revolutionizes Amusement Park Inspections
sources.claim: Drone-based inspection of amusement park rides (water rides and a roller coaster) was carried out by a certified human pilot flying the aircraft, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (amusement ride inspection); cited to show the available ride-inspection robotics is pilot-flown, so it cannot support a positive judgment for the ride functional-check instance.

instances.label: Salon, barbershop, nail salon or day spa: the manager walks the floor before opening and between shifts, checking styling stations and treatment rooms for cleanliness (hair clippings swept, counters and shampoo bowls wiped, mirrors clean, capes/towels fresh and stocked), that implements are stored in disinfectant or sealed containers per state board sanitation rules, and that dryers, chairs, steamers and autoclaves are working and undamaged; findings are logged and staff told to correct them.

Health club, gym, wellness or recreation facility: the supervisor makes rounds of the workout floor, locker rooms, showers, sauna and pool deck, checking that machines are wiped and weights racked, floors and fixtures are clean, sanitizing stations and towels are stocked, and that cardio machines, cable attachments and pool equipment show no damage or fault codes; deficiencies are logged for housekeeping or maintenance.

Childcare center or preschool: the director inspects classrooms occupied by toddlers and staff, checking sanitizing of tables, diaper-changing stations and food areas, that toys and mats are clean and undamaged, that hazards (cords, chemicals, blocked exits) are absent, and inspecting outdoor playground equipment and surfacing for wear, against licensing standards.

Hotel, resort or casino guest-services supervisor (concierge, bell, door, valet, spa attendants): inspects the lobby, entry, corridors, bell closet and luggage-storage areas, luggage carts and valet garage for cleanliness, order and equipment condition (cart wheels, bell stand, uniforms area, signage), and dispatches corrections.

Pet grooming salon/boarding kennel or funeral home: supervisor inspects grooming tubs, tables, cages/kennels, drains and clipper blades, or the mortuary prep room's instruments, ventilation, chemical storage, plus chapel and vehicles, verifying sanitation and equipment maintenance in wet, hair/fluid-laden close quarters.

Off-site or in-home client locations: a home-care, in-home childcare or mobile grooming supervisor visits a client's residence or a mobile van and inspects the aide's work areas (kitchen, bathroom, client's room) and the equipment used (lifts, bath chairs, clippers, van fittings) for cleanliness and safe working order, in a setting that differs at every stop.

sources.title: See Your Facility (Boston Dynamics blog: new AI visual inspection in Orbit)
sources.claim: Spot quadrupeds running Orbit missions autonomously patrol a facility, capture images at defined points of interest, and evaluate them against pre-programmed vision-language prompts to flag housekeeping/safety deviations such as spills or missing fire extinguishers and to monitor equipment wear.
sources.transferJustification: This is checkpoint-based conformance checking of work areas and equipment against stated criteria — the same act as a supervisor's walk-through for cleanliness and maintenance — differing only in the wording of the criteria.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Spot is deployed at hundreds of industrial and commercial sites performing routine autonomous inspection missions, and in 2025 its use broadened from individual equipment inspections to whole-facility condition assessment.

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYmal has run nightly autonomous inspection rounds at a working cement plant since early 2025, visiting 450+ predefined checkpoints on six levels and completing more than 33,000 inspections without human supervision, scanning equipment for defects, overheating and leaks.
sources.transferJustification: Routine, route-based verification that plant equipment conforms to maintenance standards is the 'operating equipment / maintenance' half of this task, performed autonomously in an institution-controlled facility.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor robot autonomously patrols occupied commercial interiors (offices, lobbies) around the clock and performs scheduled facility checks, including environmental ..., with remote specialists verifying flagged events.
sources.transferJustification: Scheduled indoor facility checks in human-occupied service buildings are the same walk-through inspection act; the robot navigates people-present corridors and rooms rather than industrial catwalks.

sources.system: Cobalt Robotics robot with spill and leak detection
sources.title: Security Robot: New Spill and Leak Detection Technology | Buildings
sources.claim: Cobalt's patrol robots detect leaks and spills in indoor facilities and notify staff, i.e., a housekeeping/cleanliness deviation is detected automatically during autonomous rounds of an office building.
sources.transferJustification: Detecting a wet spot left by janitorial staff is precisely the cleanliness-conformance finding a supervisor's inspection is meant to produce.

sources.system: GFT AI-powered robotic inspection line (with Google Cloud)
sources.title: GFT Technologies AI-powered robots move from inspection to action for automakers
sources.claim: GFT deployed AI-driven robotic arms on automotive factory floors where a first robot moves a gripper-mounted camera around each presented part to verify condition and detect visual defects in real time, ... a second arm marks the defective parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated visual quality inspection of workpieces presented to a fenced cell. It transfers to the E1 counterfactual of this task — equipment/implements brought to the machine and judged for surface condition and contamination at close range with worker-comparable reliability.

sources.claim: A mobile robot with an on-board audit sensor autonomously explores an area and scores floor cleaning quality, producing a location-wise dirt density map used to audit whether cleaning met standard.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the cleanliness-audit half of the task, though only a laboratory-scale demonstration, so it is used only to corroborate the deployed patrol-inspection evidence.
