roles.title: Animal Trainers
aliases: Explosive Detection K-9 Handler (Explosive Detection Canine Handler)
roles.description: Train animals for riding, harness, security, performance, or obedience, or for assisting persons with disabilities. Accustom animals to human voice and contact, and condition animals to respond to commands. Train animals according to prescribed standards for show or competition. May train animals to carry pack loads or work as part of pack team.

tasks.label: Cue or signal animals during performances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Equestrian performance/competition (dressage, reining, saddle-seat class, rodeo, mounted demonstration): the trainer is mounted and cues the horse through the routine with seat, leg, rein and weight aids plus voice and whip touches, in a show arena with crowd noise, other horses and variable footing, timed to a judge's or announcer's schedule.

Dog performance/competition (agility run, obedience or rally trial, dock diving, flyball, canine freestyle demo): the handler moves with the dog through the course or pattern giving verbal cues, hand and body-motion signals, with leash/collar handling before and after, at a fairground, arena or club ring under a judge.

Marine mammal or bird show at an aquarium, zoo or theme park: trainer works poolside/stage in a scripted show, giving hand signals and whistle bridges to several dolphins, sea lions, raptors or parrots, delivering fish/food reinforcement from a bucket and adapting cues to each animal's response before a live audience.

Film, TV or commercial work: trainer cues an animal (dog, cat, horse, bird) off-camera through a take using hand signals, verbal cues, buzzers, targets and food, on a set or location whose layout, props, lighting and crew differ every job, repeating until the director accepts the take.

Circus, stunt show or theme-park live production: trainer works in the ring cueing multiple exotic or domestic animals (horses, dogs, big cats, camels) through a routine with voice, whip/wand and target cues, on a fixed stage or ring under loud music and lights.

Educational outreach / small-venue performance: trainer cues small animals (parrots, rats, pigs, raptors) with clicker, target stick and food at school assemblies, county fairs, libraries or private events, in rooms and outdoor spaces taken as found with unpredictable crowds.

sources.date: 2020-01 (TensorFlow blog); rented to shelters and pro trainers 2020-2022
sources.title: Autonomous Dog Training with Companion — The TensorFlow Blog
sources.claim: CompanionPro is an autonomous, commercially rented device that cues dogs with lights and sounds and reinforces with a treat dispenser, working basic obedience behaviors (sit, down, stay, recall) in shelter kennels and trainer facilities; it is stationary, works one confined dog at a time, and has not been shown running an animal through a performance routine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cueing of a trained animal plus reinforcement of the response. It is the closest fielded analogue to cueing during performances, but it is a fixed kennel-mounted box cueing one confined dog on four basic behaviors, not a mobile handler running a timed multi-behavior routine before an audience, so it does not substantiate completion of any performance instance.

sources.title: How Companion Uses TensorFlow to Train Pets | Built In
sources.claim: Companion's device uses computer vision and infrared ... to detect the dog's response, is based at and deployed in the San Francisco SPCA shelter, and is rented to shelters, researchers and working-dog trainers.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (machine-cued obedience behaviors in a kennel run); establishes genuine autonomy and real deployment, but only for static single-dog basic obedience, not for cueing an animal through a performance.

sources.title: There's One Terrific Reason to Race Camels Using Robot Jockeys | HowStuffWorks
sources.claim: The only fielded case of a machine cueing an animal through a live public performance — robot jockeys in Gulf camel racing — is radio-controlled by a human operator following the race in a car, i.e. continuous teleoperation rather than autonomous cueing.
sources.transferJustification: Directly analogous to mounted cueing of an animal during a competitive performance, but it is continuously teleoperated, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.title: Watch: Robot dog herds sheep in New Zealand - UPI.com
sources.claim: Robot direction of livestock with a legged robot (Boston Dynamics Spot herding sheep on New Zealand farms using Rocos software) was remotely controlled rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot moving animals by pressure. Even this coarse influence over animal movement was teleoperated, and involves no trained cue-response repertoire, so it does not transfer to cueing animals through a performance.

sources.title: The world's first autonomous poultry robot gives farmers a new reason never to enter their barns
sources.claim: Autonomous robots that influence animal behavior inside a structured facility exist commercially in poultry barns: the Tibot Spoutnic roves a henhouse continuously and prompts hens to keep moving so they do not lay floor eggs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a machine autonomously changing animal behavior inside an E2 facility. It works by aversive proximity on an undifferentiated flock, with no trained cue, no bridge/reinforcement timing and no defined performance output, so it cannot substitute for a trainer cueing a routine.

sources.developer: University of Sydney, Australian Centre for Field Robotics
sources.title: Meet SwagBot, the AI-powered robot cattle herder preventing soil degradation - The Globe and Mail
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic direction of livestock outdoors remains at demonstration stage: SwagBot is an autonomous four-wheeled robot demonstrated moving and monitoring cattle in Australian paddocks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an autonomous machine influencing animal movement in an unstructured outdoor setting. It steers grazing herds rather than eliciting trained behaviors on cue and produces no performance output, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.system: Priefert / Kovac equine exerciser (automatic horse walker)
sources.title: Equine Exercisers / Horse Walkers - Kovac Ranch Equipment
sources.claim: The machines that do control performance animals in purpose-built settings are mechanical exercisers: programmable horse walkers move horses at set speeds and directions inside a dedicated round pen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a purpose-built (E1) machine that makes performance animals move on a schedule. It compels gait by physical enclosure on a fixed circle rather than cueing trained behaviors, and yields conditioning rather than a performance, so it does not complete any instance of this task.

tasks.label: Talk to or interact with animals to familiarize them to human voices or contact.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pet-dog trainer at a client's house or apartment: sits on the floor with a puppy or newly adopted dog, talks in a calm voice, hand-feeds, strokes the chest and back, handles paws, ears and muzzle, gets the dog used to being touched by strangers, leashed and picked up; adjusts pace continuously to the dog's body language, backing off at signs of fear and re-approaching. Furniture, other pets, children and noise vary house to house.

Shelter, boarding kennel or daycare trainer doing socialization rounds: enters runs with fearful, under-socialized or high-arousal dogs, talks softly, tosses then hand-delivers treats, progresses to touch, collar grabs, leashing and walking out of the kennel, so the dog tolerates handling by staff, vets and adopters. Fixed kennel layout, institution-controlled premises.

Same shelter/boarding kennel setting, but the slice of the work that is purely vocal/engagement: short repeated sessions of talking to a kenneled dog through the run, pairing a spoken marker and verbal cues with food rewards so the dog stays engaged, is comfortable with human speech directed at it and responds to spoken words. No handling required in this slice.

Horse trainer/handler in a barn, stall, round pen or arena: gentling a foal or unhandled young horse — approach and retreat, speaking steadily, rubbing the neck, working hands over the whole body, legs and feet, sacking out with cloth and ropes, haltering and leading, so the horse accepts human touch and voice. A 400-1,000 lb flight animal that can strike, kick or bolt; the trainer reads ear, eye and muscle tension moment to moment.

Zoo, aquarium or marine-mammal trainer: relationship-building and desensitization sessions with dolphins, sea lions, birds of prey, big cats or hoofstock at habitat edges and behind-the-scenes areas — voice and bridge conditioning, tactile desensitization (rubdowns, touching flukes, flippers, mouth, injection sites), building the trust that later allows voluntary husbandry behaviors. Institution-controlled facility with protected-contact barriers and strict safety protocol.

Service/assistance-dog or animal-actor trainer socializing animals to people in community settings: walking a young dog through stores, sidewalks, transit stations and clinics, letting strangers speak to and pet it, reassuring by voice, or acclimating an animal actor to an unfamiliar set crew. Layout, crowds and stimuli are as found and change site to site.

sources.title: Autonomous Dog Training with Companion — The TensorFlow Blog
sources.claim: CompanionPro (Companion Labs) is an autonomous dog-training appliance that watches a dog with onboard computer vision and interacts with it via speakers, lights and a treat dispenser; the company reports acclimating hundreds of dogs in shelters ... to the device, with the dog left to interact with it unsupervised.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the 'talk to / interact with animals' element: the machine delivers spoken markers and verbal cues to dogs and reinforces them, i.e. vocal interaction with a live animal. It performs no physical contact with the animal.

sources.title: SF SPCA Partners with Companion on an Innovative Approach to Training
sources.claim: The San Francisco SPCA installed CompanionPro devices in its shelter facilities after two years of testing; the device autonomously marks behavior with a spoken 'yes', dispenses treats, and introduces verbal commands, teaching shelter dogs sit, down, stay and recall ... responsiveness.
sources.transferJustification: Deployment evidence for vocal interaction with kenneled shelter dogs in an institution-controlled facility (E2). It does not touch or handle the dogs.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Dairy Farming: How Robots Benefit Cows & Farmers - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: The Lely Astronaut A5 milking robot autonomously makes physical contact with unrestrained live cows in a purpose-built barn stall, using a laser-guided arm to clean the udder and attach teat cups while the cow feeds, then cleans the udder again and releases the cow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic physical contact with a large live animal. It marks the commercial state of the art for machine-to-animal touch, but it is one fixed husbandry procedure on a self-presenting animal in a purpose-built stall, not adaptive gentling, and it habituates the animal to a machine rather than to human voice and hands.

sources.system: Soft robotic affective interface for chick-robot interaction (Queen Mary University of London)
sources.developer: Centre for Advanced Robotics @ Queen Mary, QMUL
sources.title: A Soft Robotic Interface for Chick-Robot Affective Interactions
sources.claim: A soft robotic interface providing warmth, breathing-like deformation and face-like cues was tested with newly hatched chicks in a laboratory arena; the chicks approached and made contact with the device, showing acceptance, in a research-stage evaluation of affective animal-robot tactile interaction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: habituating a young animal to tactile contact with an agent. It shows the research frontier — a static heated pad-like interface accepted by day-old chicks in a lab arena — far short of a trainer's adaptive handling and voice work with dogs, horses or marine mammals.

tasks.label: Conduct training programs to develop or maintain desired animal behaviors for competition, entertainment, obedience, security, riding, or related purposes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pet-dog obedience training with a handler present: group class at a training center or pet-store classroom, private lesson at a client's home, or a board-and-train session. Trainer works the dog on leash (heel, loose-leash walking, sit/down/stay, recall, greeting manners), manages distractions and other dogs, fits collars/harnesses, demonstrates mechanics and transfers the behaviors to the owner.

Kennel/room-based basic-cue training for dogs at a shelter, doggie daycare, or boarding facility with no handler in the room: repeated short daily sessions shaping sit, down, stay and recall ... a verbal cue with food reinforcement, plus settling/anxiety-reduction work, so the dog is responsive and more adoptable.

Horse training at a barn, round pen or arena: groundwork and lunging on a line, desensitizing to tack and equipment, saddling and bridling, mounted schooling of gaits/leads/transitions, trailer loading, and manners for farrier/vet, with the horse's temperament and soundness read moment to moment.

Scent-detection drilling for a working dog at a detection-dog training facility: presenting target and blank odor samples in a scent wheel/box line inside a training room, marking and reinforcing correct indications, raising discrimination difficulty and proofing against distractor odors, session after session.

Working-dog field training with a handler: patrol/protection and building, vehicle and area search problems for police or security K9s; and service/assistance dog task training (retrieve, brace, alert) plus public-access outings in stores, on sidewalks and on transit, including handler-team training.

Zoo, aquarium or entertainment animal sessions: shaping husbandry and performance behaviors in a marine-mammal pool, a zoo training enclosure, or on a film/show set using bridge (whistle/clicker), targets, fish or food reward, gated protected contact, and reading a large unrestrained animal in real time.

sources.title: Autonomous Dog Training with Companion — The TensorFlow Blog
sources.claim: CompanionPro is a fixed device with camera, speakers, lights and treat dispenser that autonomously shapes basic obedience behaviors (sit, down, stay, recall) in dogs with no trainer in the room; sold B2B to shelters and dog businesses.

sources.title: Autonomous Dog Training with Companion — The TensorFlow Blog
sources.claim: The device has been run with hundreds of dogs inside shelters and daycare facilities; the supervising human leaves the room and the dog then works with the device on its own.

sources.developer: Companion (Companion Labs) with San Francisco SPCA
sources.title: SF SPCA Partners with Companion on an Innovative Approach to Training
sources.claim: An animal shelter reports that Companion's automated training taught its shelter dogs the basic obedience behaviors to high responsiveness, and that it is installing CompanionPro devices in its facilities.

sources.developer: Timothy L. Edwards, University of Waikato
sources.title: Automated Canine Scent-Detection Apparatus: Technical Description and Training Outcomes (Chemical Senses)
sources.claim: An automated 17-segment scent carousel with infrared indication sensors and an automated feeder trained naive dogs, without researcher mediation, to classify odor samples at near-perfect accuracy within about 20 half-days.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, automated: this is the odor-imprinting and discrimination drilling a detection-dog trainer performs, with sample presentation, indication detection and food reinforcement all machine-controlled.

sources.developer: Detection dog research group (Frontiers in Veterinary Science)
sources.title: An Automated Canine Line-Up for Detection Dog Research
sources.claim: A three-olfactometer automated canine line-up presents odors and trains dogs to hold an alert at the sample port, with computer-controlled sensing and reinforcement, in a detection-dog research setting.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, automated: machine-presented odor trials with automated alert detection and reinforcement are the core repetitive drill of scent-detection training.

tasks.label: Feed or exercise animals or provide other general care, such as cleaning or maintaining holding or performance areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dog boarding/training kennel morning and evening routine: measuring and delivering per-dog portions (some with medication or special diets), refilling water, then scooping solid waste from indoor/outdoor runs, hosing and disinfecting the runs, changing bedding and running laundry, with dogs shifted or present.

Horse training/boarding barn, individual box stalls: mucking out shavings or straw beds (picking manure and wet spots, saving clean bedding), re-bedding, dropping hay flakes and grain/supplement buckets per horse, scrubbing and filling water buckets, sweeping the aisle.

Horse facility turnout areas: picking droppings from paddocks, dry lots and run-in areas, topping up group hay and delivering individual concentrate rations to horses kept in groups (active-stable/pasture-board setups), checking fences and water troughs.

Exercising dogs: leash walks around the facility grounds or neighborhood, structured play-yard sessions with groups of dogs, fetch and conditioning work, monitoring behavior and breaking up rough play while exercising.
Exercising horses: hand-walking or hot-walking after work, lunging in a round pen, ponying or treadmill/aqua-treadmill conditioning sessions of set duration and speed, plus turnout in and out.

Maintaining performance/training areas: dragging and watering the riding arena footing between sessions, raking and leveling rings, resetting rails and cones, and sweeping/scrubbing/disinfecting indoor training room and grooming-area floors.
