tasks.label: Observe animals' physical conditions to detect illness or unhealthy conditions requiring medical care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dog trainer at a board-and-train / service-dog or guide-dog training kennel: during daily rounds and sessions, checks each dog in the program — watches gait and energy, inspects eyes, ears, coat and stool, runs hands over the body for ticks, hot spots, lumps and lameness, checks paw pads and nails, notes appetite/water intake — and flags dogs needing veterinary attention. Dogs move freely, resist handling, and signs are subtle (mild limp, ear infection, GI upset).

Horse trainer at a boarding, show or racing barn: morning and post-work rounds on 10–25 horses — runs hands down legs feeling for heat, filling and digital pulse, picks out and inspects hooves for stones/thrush/abscess, checks eyes and nostrils for discharge, looks at feed left, water and manure, watches for colic or tying-up signs, jogs or lunges a horse to judge soundness, takes a temperature when suspicious, and calls the vet or farrier.

Companion-dog trainer working in the client's private home or in a class held in a park, store or rented hall: during the session notices the dog is limping, guarding a body area, scratching, has ocular/nasal discharge, is overweight or overheating; handles the dog to check the suspect area and advises the owner to seek veterinary care before continuing training.

Marine mammal / zoo animal trainer at an aquarium or zoo: daily husbandry session — visual check of skin, eyes, blowhole/nares, respiration rate, buoyancy and appetite, plus trained voluntary behaviors in which the animal presents flukes, flippers or mouth for palpation, temperature or sample collection; records findings on the welfare log and alerts veterinary staff to abnormalities.

Police/military or detection K9 handler-trainer in the field: after a deployment or outdoor training run, checks the dog on site for heat stress, dehydration, cut or burned pads, lacerations, foreign bodies and limping; hands-on assessment in a parking lot, field, rubble pile or vehicle, often in heat or poor light, and decides whether to pull the dog and go to a vet.

sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: Challenges and opportunities
sources.claim: Scout (formerly ChickenBoy) is a ceiling-rail autonomous robot in broiler houses that uses thermal/optical cameras and environmental sensors to detect sick and dead birds ... flag welfare problems in a flock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of sick animals in a livestock house. Transfer to this task fails: the robot makes flock-level, non-contact judgments about thousands of near-identical broilers in a barn built around it, whereas trainers make individual clinical judgments on dogs, horses and marine mammals that require handling, palpation, hoof/paw inspection and gait assessment.

sources.title: Cumberland introduces Scout robot to promote poultry health and performance – AgriNews
sources.claim: Scout is marketed and sold commercially as a ceiling-suspended robot continuously monitoring broiler chickens for early disease detection in poultry houses.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (automated sick-bird detection in a purpose-fitted barn); it substantiates commercial deployment but not individual hands-on health assessment of trainers' animals.

sources.title: The history of the milking robot Lely Astronaut
sources.claim: Robotic milking systems detect udder-health problems automatically while the cow stands in the robot box, flagging abnormal milk and cell counts for treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: detecting an unhealthy condition (mastitis) in an animal brought to a purpose-built robotic station. Transfer fails because the detection is a narrow milk-sensor inference specific to lactating dairy cows; it provides no capability to assess limbs, hooves, skin, eyes, gait or demeanour in horses, dogs or marine mammals.

sources.developer: Australian Centre for Field Robotics, University of Sydney
sources.title: Meet SwagBot, the AI-powered robot cattle herder preventing soil degradation
sources.claim: SwagBot is an autonomous field robot demonstrated in Australian pasture that assesses pasture and is reported to monitor livestock health while herding cattle; it remains a university research platform.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor robotic monitoring of livestock condition. Transfer fails: the reported health monitoring is coarse and unquantified herd-level observation of grazing cattle by a research prototype, not the individual, hands-on illness detection a trainer performs.

tasks.label: Evaluate animals to determine their temperaments, abilities, or aptitude for training.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pet/companion dog trainer intake evaluation: at a training school, boarding/daycare facility, or the client's home, the trainer greets and leashes an unfamiliar dog, observes greeting behavior and body language, tests handling tolerance (collar grab, body touch), food/toy motivation, reactivity to strangers and other dogs, runs known cues, and produces a written/verbal assessment placing the dog in a class or program.

Shelter/rescue behavior evaluation (SAFER/Match-Up style): staff trainer walks the dog out of a kennel on a leash into an assessment room, does look/tag/sensitivity handling tests, a food-bowl guarding test with a fake hand, toy and squeeze tests, and a dog-dog introduction, then scores temperament and adoptability/behavior-modification needs.

Working/service-dog program candidate testing: puppy aptitude tests on a litter at a breeding kennel (startle recovery, restraint, retrieve/possession drive, social attraction, footing/novel surfaces) and candidate screening for guide, service, police, or SAR work on training grounds and in public access outings; trainer records scores and selects/rejects dogs.

Detection-dog ability testing: a trainer evaluates a candidate or working dog's odor-detection ability and proficiency using scent line-ups/wheels in a training room — target and blank samples presented in fixed positions, dog searches and alerts, responses scored for accuracy, latency and false alerts, producing a proficiency record.

Horse evaluation: in a barn aisle, round pen or arena, the trainer approaches and halters the horse, assesses reaction to handling, grooming and feet, leads and lunges it for movement and mind, then usually saddles and rides to judge temperament, athletic ability and suitability/aptitude for a discipline or for sale or program placement.

Zoo, aquarium, exotic and performance/film animal evaluation: trainer works an individual animal (marine mammal, bird, big cat, farm or film dog/cat) in its habitat, holding area or on set, gauging food motivation, tolerance of the trainer's proximity, desensitization level, and readiness/aptitude for husbandry, show or on-camera behaviors, and reports suitability.

sources.developer: Canine Olfaction Research and Education Laboratory, Texas Tech University (N. J. Hall lab)
sources.title: An Automated Canine Line-Up for Detection Dog Research (Frontiers in Veterinary Science)
sources.claim: An automated computer-driven olfactory line-up apparatus (three olfactometers, motorized port panel, IR nose-hold sensors, Bluetooth PetTutor feeder) presents odor samples, detects and objectively scores a dog's alert responses, delivers rewards, and logs latency, sniff time and accuracy to file — i.e., it evaluates a detection dog's scent-detection ability inside a purpose-built apparatus in a lab room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: measuring a detection dog's odor-recognition performance. It transfers to the trainer's evaluation of a dog's detection ability because the apparatus itself presents the stimuli, records the dog's response, and scores accuracy/latency — the same output a trainer's proficiency evaluation produces, on the same animals, in a scent-line-up format trainers already use.

sources.title: Autonomous Dog Training with Companion — The TensorFlow Blog
sources.claim: CompanionPro is an autonomous, camera-and-treat-dispenser dog training machine deployed in shelter kennels (SF SPCA) and with working-dog trainers; it works dogs on basic obedience cues on its own but is stationary, cannot leash, touch, restrain or introduce a dog to another dog, and is not reported to produce temperament or aptitude evaluations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated obedience training of the same animals in the same shelter/kennel settings. It bounds evaluation capability: the machine only issues cues and rewards from a fixed position, so it cannot perform the handling, leash-work and social-introduction components that a temperament or aptitude evaluation requires.

sources.title: Dogs Obey Commands Given by Social Robots - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: In controlled experiments a social robot issuing a 'sit' command obtained compliance from dogs only about 60% of the time — robot-animal interaction is limited to single simple cues, far below the multi-part behavioral batteries used to judge temperament.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: eliciting a trained response from a dog, the elemental step of any aptitude test. Reliability near 60% for one cue, with autonomy not established, shows no robotic system can elicit and interpret the range of responses a temperament evaluation needs.

sources.title: There's One Terrific Reason to Race Camels Using Robot Jockeys | HowStuffWorks
sources.claim: Robot jockeys that ride racing camels — the only mounted animal-work robots in routine use — are radio-controlled by human operators driving alongside the track, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: riding/controlling a large animal, which is how horse trainers assess a horse's temperament and ability under saddle. These machines are continuously teleoperated, so they cannot support an autonomous ridden evaluation.

sources.title: Cargill Aims to Improve Worker Safety with Remote Controlled Herding Robot for Livestock - AgFunderNews
sources.claim: The state of the art for moving and handling animals inside a controlled facility is a remote-controlled cattle-herding robot tested in Cargill beef plants; it herds under human control and performs no assessment of individual animals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic movement/handling of live animals in an institution-controlled facility. Being remote-controlled and limited to herding, it cannot substantiate autonomous handling-based behavioral evaluation of individual animals.

tasks.label: Administer prescribed medications to animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Training/boarding barn: horse on a prescription (bute powder, crushed SMZ tablets, ulcer or joint medication) that is measured and top-dressed or mixed into the horse's grain ration at feeding time; trainer must confirm the horse cleaned up the full dose and did not sort it out.

Training/boarding barn: horse given oral paste or liquid by dose syringe (omeprazole paste, dewormer, banamine, oral antibiotic suspension) — halter the horse, hold the head, insert the syringe over the tongue, depress the plunger and hold the head up until swallowed, on a fidgety or head-shy horse.

Boarding/training kennel, day-training facility, or (for service-dog trainers) a puppy raiser's or client's home: dog given a prescribed pill, capsule, or liquid — pilled by hand or hidden in food/pill pocket, dose verified as swallowed and logged; several dogs on rounds, some spitting pills out or refusing.

Kennel or barn: targeted topical route on a conscious animal — eye ointment/drops into a dog's or horse's eye, ear drops with canal massage, or medicated ointment applied to a specific wound, hot spot, or skin lesion, with the animal held still.

Barn or kennel: subcutaneous or intramuscular injection given by the trainer per veterinary prescription (allergy immunotherapy shot for a dog, IM antibiotic or vaccine in a horse's neck, insulin), animal held or cross-tied, correct site, aspiration/needle handling, sharps disposal.

Zoo or marine mammal facility: medication hidden in fish/food or delivered through a trained voluntary behavior (open mouth, present flipper, gate to a station) during a session with a dolphin, sea lion, big cat, or elephant; trainer must ensure the whole dose is ingested and not spat out.

sources.system: SureShot (Pharm Robotics, FANUC arm + Intel RealSense 3D vision)
sources.title: Pharm Robotics inoculates dairy cows at large farm - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Pharm Robotics' SureShot uses an RFID-triggered industrial robot arm with needleless injection to inoculate dairy cows held in a purpose-built two-part bumper restraint at the milking barn; deploying to early customer sites and MVP/rotary-parlor testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic injection of prescribed veterinary pharmaceuticals into a large restrained mammal. Transfers to a trainer's IM/SQ injection of a horse because the object (large-mammal neck/hip musculature), the precision (site acquisition by 3D vision, single injection depth), and the environment (animal immobilized in a machine-built restraint) are comparable; it does not transfer to an unrestrained animal in a stall or kennel.

sources.title: Pharm Robotics advances automated dairy cow healthcare - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Pharm Robotics states SureShot autonomously administers vaccines and reproductive/medication regimens individualized per cow on commercial dairies, with continued progress toward full automation in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (robotic injection of prescribed medication into restrained livestock); cited to establish autonomy and current status of the injection system.

sources.system: VARIO smart automatic calf feeder with additive dispenser
sources.title: Additional dosing unit - Förster-Technik
sources.claim: Förster-Technik's additive/dosing unit on its automatic calf feeder automatically doses vet-prescribed supplements, vitamins, electrolytes or medication into an individually RFID-identified calf's feed according to a per-animal plan, at a feeding station in a calf barn.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic per-animal oral dosing of vet-prescribed additives/medication into feed at an identification-controlled feeding station. Transfers to a horse's prescribed powder/tablet dosed into its ration: same route (oral, in feed), same precision requirement (measured dose to the right individual), and the same style of machine-built feed station the animal walks up to.

sources.title: Vaccination - Maskon
sources.claim: Skala Maskon's fully automated fish vaccination machine anesthetizes, singulates, orients and injects vaccine into up to 40,000 salmon smolt per hour with one operator, in hatchery vaccination lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine administration of injectable medication to live animals. It substantiates injection only where the animal is conveyed, immobilized and presented to the machine (purpose-built line), reinforcing an E1-only reading and giving no support at E2.

sources.title: Automatic Milking Robot | Lely Astronaut A5 Next
sources.claim: The Lely Astronaut milking robot automatically applies a topical udder-care product to a cow's teats after each milking inside the robot box.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous topical application of a liquid to a live animal's body. It covers only broad-area spraying of a large, stereotyped body region inside a purpose-built stall; it does not substantiate placing drops in an eye or ear canal or ointment on a specific lesion of a conscious dog or horse.

tasks.label: Keep records documenting animal health, diet, or behavior.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Evaluate animals for trainability and ability to perform.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intake/behavior evaluation of a client's dog at the trainer's facility (board-and-train kennel, training school, or shelter behavior room): trainer leashes and walks the dog, checks food/toy motivation, cues sit/down/recall, does handling and body-sensitivity checks (ears, paws, collar grab), tests response to a stranger approach and to a neutral dog, notes startle and recovery, then delivers a suitability and program recommendation.

In-home evaluation of a client's dog before enrolling in obedience or behavior work: unfamiliar house layout, family and other pets present, trainer greets and handles the dog, sets up doorway/greeting and resource-guarding provocations, tests leash manners on the street outside, and judges trainability and prognosis.

Selection testing of candidate dogs for working roles (police/detection, protection, search) at a kennel and training field: trainer throws and tugs a toy to score prey and hunt drive, hides a reward in a search area, walks the dog over slick/grated footing and stairs, exposes it to noise and strangers, and rates suitability for the program.

Evaluating a horse at a barn/arena for training or purchase suitability: trainer catches and leads the horse, checks manners for grooming, tacking and foot handling, lunges it to see gaits and responsiveness, then rides it to assess willingness, response to leg and rein, spookiness, and readiness for the intended discipline.

Standardized aptitude/temperament testing of puppies or young dogs for an assistance-dog or breeding program in a dedicated test room: social attraction and following, restraint on the back, elevation, touch and sound sensitivity, retrieve, novel-object and umbrella startle, scored on a rubric to decide who continues in the program.

Zoo/aquarium trainer assessing an animal (dolphin, sea lion, parrot, big cat, elephant) for participation in husbandry or presentation behaviors: working the animal at a station or protected-contact barrier, testing reinforcer preference, attention span, tolerance of tactile desensitization and novel apparatus, and judging readiness to advance.

sources.title: SF SPCA Partners with Companion on an Innovative Approach to Training - San Francisco SPCA
sources.claim: CompanionPro, an autonomous camera-plus-treat-launcher device, is deployed in shelter and daycare kennels where it teaches dogs basic obedience behaviors with no person present; it issues cues and reinforcement but never handles, leashes or restrains the dog and does not administer handling, reactivity or startle tests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous obedience training of dogs in an institutional kennel. It is the nearest physical system to evaluating a dog because it delivers cues and observes whether the dog responds, but it covers only food-motivated cue response and involves no contact with the animal, so it does not transfer to the handling, leash, stranger/dog reactivity and startle components of a trainability evaluation.

sources.title: Autonomous Dog Training with Companion — The TensorFlow Blog
sources.claim: Companion's device has been run with hundreds of dogs in ..., but dogs must first be acclimated to the machine, and it works only in its fixed kennel installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous canine training. Establishes the scope of the only fielded animal-training machine — a fixed, non-contact food-reinforcement device — which bounds what any cited system can do toward evaluating an animal.

sources.title: Dubai’s Camel Races Embrace Robot Jockeys
sources.claim: The only fielded machines that ride and drive a large animal are camel-racing robot jockeys, which are remote-controlled whip units operated by a human from a vehicle running alongside the track; they are teleoperated and make no assessment of the animal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounted control of a large animal. Shows that the one deployed mounted machine is continuously human-operated, so no cited system can autonomously perform the ridden portion of a horse evaluation.

sources.system: Digitally-enhanced dog behavioral testing (sensor + ML scoring of a Stranger Test)
sources.title: Digitally-Enhanced Dog Behavioral Testing: Getting Help from the Machine
sources.claim: State-of-the-art automation of canine behavioral testing is sensing plus machine learning layered on a test a human still administers: a human stranger performs the protocol while sensors and models help score the dog. No robot administers or scores the test on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: administering and scoring a canine temperament test. It shows the provocation-applying half of an evaluation is still performed by a human and the automated part is software-only, hence not a robotic system that could substantiate completion.

tasks.label: Advise animal owners regarding the purchase of specific animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: A dog obedience trainer at a training facility (or by phone/video) counsels a prospective owner on which breed, age, and temperament of dog would suit their household, activity level, experience, and living space, and where to source it responsibly.

A trainer accompanies or advises a client evaluating a specific puppy or adult dog at a breeder or shelter, discussing the animal's temperament, health/pedigree paperwork, and trainability, then recommending for or against the purchase.

A horse trainer advises a client shopping for a riding or show horse: reviewing the horse's history, conformation, way of going, and suitability for the rider's skill and discipline, and giving a buy/don't-buy recommendation with price guidance.

A service, guide, or detection-dog program trainer advises an agency or private client on selecting a candidate dog, explaining selection criteria, likely washout risk, and cost, and recommending specific sources or individual dogs.

A trainer of exotic or specialty animals (parrots, reptiles, marine or performance animals) or of working livestock dogs advises an owner at a pet store, expo, farm, or by correspondence on whether and which specific animal to purchase, including husbandry and legal considerations.

tasks.label: Train horses or other equines for riding, harness, show, racing, or other work, using knowledge of breed characteristics, training methods, performance standards, and the peculiarities of each animal.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily schooling rides on performance horses in training (dressage, hunter/jumper, western pleasure, reining) in an indoor or outdoor arena at a commercial boarding/training barn: the trainer tacks up, mounts, works the horse through gaits, transitions, lateral work and jumps, adjusting aids ride-by-ride to the individual horse's stiffness, temperament and progress toward show standards.

Starting/backing a young horse (2-4 y.o.) at a training barn: round-pen work, sacking out/desensitizing, bitting, ground driving, accepting saddle and girth, first mounting and first ridden steps, over weeks of short sessions, reading the colt's tension moment to moment and staying safe on a green, reactive animal.

Race-training work at a racetrack backside or private training center: jogging, galloping and breezing Thoroughbreds/Standardbreds on the track, teaching the horse to rate, switch leads, work in company, and school at the starting gate under an exercise rider/trainer, on a shared track with other horses and outriders.

Remedial/handling training on a client's private farm or hauled-in horse: lunging and long-lining, teaching ground manners, trailer loading, standing for clipping/farrier, and fixing specific problems (bucking, barn-sour, spooky), in whatever paddock, aisle or small arena the site offers.

Off-property conditioning and exposure training: trail and hill work, cross-country schooling over natural terrain, hauling to unfamiliar show grounds and schooling the horse in a busy warm-up ring with crowds, banners and loudspeakers.

Harness/driving and specialty work: long-lining a horse to ground-drive, hitching to a cart or wagon, training draft or carriage teams and pack animals to work in harness or carry loads, in a farm yard, driving arena and along quiet roads.

sources.system: Camel-racing robot jockeys (RAQBI / K-Team type units)
sources.developer: K-Team / RAQBI and Gulf camel-racing operators
sources.title: There's One Terrific Reason to Race Camels Using Robot Jockeys | HowStuffWorks
sources.claim: Robot jockeys used on racing camels — the closest thing to a machine 'riding' a large equine-type animal — are lightweight remote-controlled whip units operated by humans driving alongside the track; they do not train the animal or control it autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: riding/urging a large ridden animal in competition. Cited to show the state of the art is a teleoperated whip actuator strapped to the animal, not an autonomous rider capable of the ridden schooling, gait work and individualized correction that horse training requires.

sources.developer: Various manufacturers; study by J. Murphy, University College Dublin
sources.title: Innovative Use of an Automated Horse Walker When Breaking in Young Horses — Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science
sources.claim: Automated horse walkers are commercial machines that move horses at set speeds on a fixed circular track; a research study tested backing (first mounting) young horses inside a walker, but the machine only supplies controlled forward movement while human trainers and riders do the training.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conditioning/exercising horses on a machine. It substantiates only machine-paced walking/trotting in a purpose-built enclosure; the mounting, aids, timing and individual judgment that constitute starting or schooling a horse are still performed by people, so it cannot complete a training instance.

sources.title: Training With Horse Exercisers — Molenkoning
sources.claim: Commercial horse exercisers are programmable but limited to setting pace, gait frequency and lap times for fitness work; they contain no capability to teach responses to aids, school movements, or handle a horse's behavioural problems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fitness conditioning of horses. Shows the only widely deployed automated equine machine is an open-loop pacing device; it does not perceive the individual horse's responses or shape behaviour, so no transfer to the training task.

sources.system: Robotic steer / mechanical cow training robots
sources.developer: S. N. Cubero (Curtin University), published in Procedia Engineering
sources.title: Robotic Horse-Training Technologies for Cutting and Campdrafting Competitions (ResearchGate)
sources.claim: Purpose-built 'robotic horse-training' equipment for cutting and campdrafting consists of remote-controlled mechanical steers that the horse works against; the machine substitutes for the cattle, while a human trainer still rides and trains the horse.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: equipment used in training performance horses. The robots are remote-controlled props replacing livestock, not the trainer; the ridden training work remains human, so they cannot complete a horse-training instance at any tier.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Dairy Farming: How Robots Benefit Cows & Farmers — IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous robots working with large livestock perform a fixed procedure on a voluntarily presented animal inside a purpose-built stall (laser-guided teat-cup attachment), demonstrating the narrow scope of autonomous animal-contact robotics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous physical interaction with a large domestic animal. Cited as a capability boundary: the routine is a single fixtured manipulation on a restrained, food-motivated cow, with no behaviour shaping, leading, riding or individualized correction, so it does not transfer to equine training.

tasks.label: Use oral, spur, rein, or hand commands to condition horses to carry riders or to pull horse-drawn equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Starting/backing a young horse (2-3 yr old) at a training barn: round-pen and arena groundwork, voice and hand cues, sacking out, saddling, bitting, long-lining, then first mounted rides teaching go/stop/turn from rein and leg. Trainer must read the individual horse's fear and resistance and adjust session by session over weeks; risk of bucking, bolting, injury.

Schooling/tune-up rides on client horses in an indoor or outdoor arena at a boarding-and-training stable: mounted work with rein, seat, leg/spur and voice to install and refine responses (transitions, bending, leads, collection, reining/western maneuvers) to a standard the owner or show judge will accept.

Conditioning and desensitizing rides outside the arena: hacking on trails, farm roads, open fields and along traffic; teaching the horse to accept water crossings, machinery, dogs, wildlife and footing changes while responding to rein, leg and oral commands. Terrain, weather and encounters vary and are not controlled.

Harness/driving training: teaching whoa/gee/haw voice commands with long lines, then hitching to a cart, sled, or forecart and driving the horse (or pair) in an arena, farm yard, or training track until it will safely pull equipment on command. Includes standardbred jog/training miles at a track.

Specialty conditioning for public work: preparing mounted-patrol, parade, therapeutic-riding or carriage horses by riding them through crowds, flags, sirens, umbrellas, city streets and obstacle courses, using rein, leg and voice to keep the horse obedient amid novel stimuli.

sources.title: There's One Terrific Reason to Race Camels Using Robot Jockeys | HowStuffWorks
sources.claim: Robot jockeys used in Gulf camel racing are small remote-controlled devices strapped to the animal that whip and adjust reins; they are commanded continuously by human operators driving alongside the track, and they race rather than train animals.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing machine that applies rein/whip aids to a large ridden animal. It does not transfer: it is continuously teleoperated, is used in races rather than to condition animals to commands, and is mounted on camels in a fenced race track, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of horse training.

sources.system: Kurtsystem (car system and 10-horse rail/cabinet system), Kingwood Stud, Lambourn
sources.title: Kurtsystems: A kinder way to do a cruel job?
sources.claim: The Kurtsystem is a multi-million-dollar riderless pre-training machine in which young racehorses are tethered in cabins on a covered monorail track and worked at set speeds with progressively weighted saddles; human operators fit the saddles, load the horses and monitor data, and horses still go on to conventional ridden training.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical pre-conditioning of young racehorses to carry weight. It does not transfer to this task because the machine issues no oral, spur, rein or hand commands and does not teach the horse to respond to a rider's aids or to pull equipment; it is a preparatory sub-step performed with human operators handling and monitoring the horses.

sources.system: Free Flow Equineciser automated horse exerciser
sources.title: Free Flow Horse Exercisers | Automated Horse Exercisers | Centaur Equinecisers
sources.claim: Commercial automated horse exercisers (hot walkers/equinecisers) move several loose horses around a fenced circular pen at operator-set speeds for fitness and cool-down; they give no command-response training and require staff to lead horses in and out.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-driven exercise of horses in a purpose-built circular pen. It does not transfer: the machine only sets a pace for loose horses, applies none of the oral, spur, rein or hand commands named in this task, and does not condition a horse to carry a rider or pull equipment.

sources.title: A new robotic horseback-riding simulator for riding lessons and equine-assisted therapy
sources.claim: Robotic equine systems that exist for riding are simulators - machines that reproduce a horse's motion so people can practice riding or receive therapy - not machines that train live horses.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of equine robotics: the robot replaces the horse for a human rider rather than replacing the trainer. No transfer to conditioning a live horse to commands.

tasks.label: Retrain horses to break bad habits, such as kicking, bolting, or resisting bridling or grooming.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At a commercial training/boarding barn: re-educating a horse that resists haltering, bridling, clipping or grooming. Trainer works in a stall, aisle, cross-ties or round pen over repeated sessions — approach-and-retreat, pressure-and-release, touching ears/muzzle/girth area, sliding the bit in — reading flight/tension cues in real time and stopping before the horse escalates.

Under-saddle rehab at a training facility's arena: riding a horse that bolts, rushes, bucks or jigs; the trainer must sit the explosion, apply rein/leg/seat corrections with correct timing, use one-rein stops and circling, and rebuild forward-and-whoa responses over weeks until the horse is safe for the owner.

Rehabilitating a dangerous or defensive horse on the ground at the trainer's barn: kicking, striking, biting, pulling back when tied, rearing while led. Requires reading threat displays, positioning safely around a reactive 1,000+ lb animal, and progressively restoring tolerance to handling.

Off-site situational habits at a client's private farm or on the road: horse that will not load in a trailer, will not stand for the farrier or vet, or spooks/naps on trails and near traffic. Layout, footing, weather and bystanders vary site to site; work happens in driveways, pastures, lanes and trails.

At a racetrack backside or performance training center: restarting an off-track Thoroughbred or fixing a racehorse's habits (bolting on the track, refusing the starting gate, washing out, rearing at the gate) within the facility's schedule and rules.

sources.title: RealCow Robotic System — SuperDroid Robots
sources.claim: The RealCow is a commercially sold robotic/mechanical cow used in arenas to school cutting and cow horses, but it is driven by a hand-held push-button remote and the horse is ridden by a human trainer; it modifies no horse behavior on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing 'horse-training robot': it is a moving target used as a training aid for cutting horses. It does not handle, ride, or retrain the horse, is remote-controlled, and therefore cannot substantiate completion of behavioral retraining at any tier.

sources.system: Automatic milking system (Lely Astronaut-class robotic milker)
sources.title: This Robot is Udderly Good at Its Job — Milking Cows! — Science on Tap
sources.claim: Automatic milking robots autonomously manipulate live large livestock (locating and attaching teat cups on cows) in a purpose-built stall, showing the frontier of autonomous physical interaction with big animals — but they perform a fixed repetitive procedure on voluntarily presented, food-motivated cows, not behavioral rehabilitation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous physical handling of a live large animal. Transfer does NOT carry: the robot performs one scripted udder procedure on a habituated cow inside a fixed crate; it does not read escalating equine flight/aggression cues, apply timed pressure-and-release, ride, or judge behavioural progress, which is the whole of this task.

sources.developer: Racewood-type equine simulator manufacturers / Scottish equestrian centres
sources.title: Meet RoboCob, Scotland's first robot stallion to train horse riders
sources.claim: Robotic horses (equine simulators) exist and are used in equestrian centres, but they train human riders; no live horse is handled or retrained by the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Named 'robot horse training' technology found in search, but the trainee is the human rider; it provides no evidence that a machine can retrain a live horse's habits.

sources.title: Westland Equine Walkers
sources.claim: The automation actually installed in horse facilities is mechanical exercise equipment — programmable hot walkers that move tethered horses in a circle — which conditions horses physically but performs no behavioural retraining and cannot groom, bridle, or ride.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated handling/exercise of horses in a barn. It shows the deployed ceiling of equine automation: a tether on a rotating arm. No perception of the horse's behaviour and no manipulation, so it cannot substantiate breaking habits such as kicking or resisting bridling.

tasks.label: Train dogs in human assistance or property protection duties.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Assistance-dog task training at a program's training center/kennel campus: shaping and chaining service tasks (retrieve dropped keys/phone, tug open doors and drawers, press buttons, brace/counterbalance, medical-alert response) with a young dog, using leash, harness, clicker/marker, food and toy reinforcement, reading subtle body language and adjusting criteria session by session.

Public-access and generalization training for an assistance dog in real settings: sidewalks, grocery stores, restaurants, buses/trains, elevators, crowds and other dogs; proofing settle-under-table, loose-leash heeling, ignoring dropped food, and performing trained tasks reliably amid unpredictable distractions.

Guide-dog harness work on town/city training routes: teaching straight-line travel, curb stops, obstacle and overhead clearance, traffic checks and intelligent disobedience, with the trainer under blindfold or handling the harness and correcting/rewarding in live traffic conditions.

Personal-protection / guard-dog bite development on a club or kennel training field: building drive on tug and sleeve, targeting and grip work with a decoy in a bite suit, alert-barking on property, out/call-off under handler command, and threat-discrimination scenarios.

Police/security K9 patrol scenario training at an agency training ground or a training warehouse/building: building searches, handler protection, apprehension of a padded decoy, vehicle extractions, recall off a running decoy, with the trainer running the scenario, handling the long line and coaching the dog.

Foundation obedience and impulse-control conditioning of candidate assistance/protection dogs housed at a kennel or training facility: many short daily repetitions of sit, down, stay/duration, place, recall and eye contact with food reinforcement in a kennel run or indoor training room before specialty work begins.

sources.title: Autonomous Dog Training with Companion — The TensorFlow Blog
sources.claim: CompanionPro is a commercially sold, autonomous dog-training appliance (camera, onboard AI, lights, speaker, treat launcher) that runs unattended obedience sessions with dogs in shelters and daycare ..., teaching sit, down, stay and recall.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended basic-obedience conditioning of kennelled dogs. It transfers to the foundation-obedience phase of assistance/protection-dog programs because the behaviors (sit, down, duration stay, place, recall), the reinforcement schedule, and the kennel/training-room setting are the same; it does not transfer to task-specific service work, harness/leash handling, or decoy protection work.

sources.developer: Companion Labs, Inc. with San Francisco SPCA
sources.title: SF SPCA Partners with Companion on an Innovative Approach to Training
sources.claim: A shelter (San Francisco SPCA) deployed CompanionPro devices in its own facilities to deliver automated training to dogs in its care, showing the device operating in an institution-controlled human work facility rather than only a lab.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (automated basic-obedience/behavior conditioning of kennelled dogs); cited to establish the environment (a shelter kennel facility, E2) in which the autonomous device actually operates.

sources.system: NC State autonomous canine training system (sensor harness + treat dispenser)
sources.title: New Tech Uses Hardware, Software to Train Dogs More Efficiently | NC State News
sources.claim: A research system combining a sensor-instrumented dog harness with an automated treat dispenser trained dogs autonomously, but only reinforced a single posture (sit) detected from harness sensors; the authors position it as an aid used alongside human-directed training.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated posture conditioning in a purpose-built lab arrangement. It bounds what automated canine training has demonstrated — single simple postures with fixtured sensing — and does not extend to shaping service tasks, harness/route work, or protection work.

tasks.label: Organize or conduct animal shows.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Zoo or aquarium keeper-trainer conducts a scheduled public presentation (sea lion, dolphin, or free-flight bird show) in the facility's show theater: stages animals, cues a repertoire of behaviors, times food reinforcement, adapts when an animal breaks from the routine, narrates a conservation message over a microphone, and keeps animals and the seated audience safe.

Trainer presents animals in competition or exhibition at showgrounds: hauls horses or dogs in, warms up, then rides or leads the animal through the class in front of a judge (stacking, gaiting, patterns, obedience exercises) under ring procedures and time pressure.

Traveling stunt-dog, agility, or dock-diving exhibition at a county fair, festival, or sports halftime: trainer sets up equipment on unfamiliar ground, runs several dogs through a scripted but adaptable routine amid crowd noise, and MCs the act.

Small educational animal show at a school, library, nursing home, or private party: trainer transports birds of prey, reptiles, or trick dogs, sets up in a room taken as found, handles and restrains animals close to children, and presents behaviors while talking to the group.

Organizing/staging a show: building the schedule and entry list, setting the ring or course (jumps, agility obstacles, props, PA, barriers), staging animals and handlers in order, and running the event through to its finish.

sources.title: Autonomous Dog Training with Companion — The TensorFlow Blog
sources.claim: CompanionPro is an autonomous device that trains dogs on basic obedience behaviors (sit, down, stay, recall) using computer vision, lights, sounds and a treat ..., used by shelters, daycares and dog-training businesses with no human trainer in the room.
sources.transferJustification: Closest machine for the related task of cueing and reinforcing trained animal behavior. It does not transfer to conducting an animal show: it is a fixed kiosk in a kennel run that never leashes, transports, stages or physically handles an animal, runs no multi-animal performance routine, provides no narration or audience interaction, and manages no public-safety duties in an arena.

sources.title: Lely refines Astronaut A5 Next robotic milker - Farmers Weekly
sources.claim: Lely Astronaut robotic milkers autonomously locate and attach teat cups to individual cows in a purpose-built milking box; over 50,000 units are installed on commercial dairy farms.
sources.transferJustification: Shows reliable autonomous physical contact with a large live animal in a purpose-built station — the most structured animal-handling automation in commercial use, i.e. the E1 counterfactual case. It does not transfer to conducting a show: the cow presents herself in a fixture, the machine performs one fixed husbandry procedure, and no cueing of performance behaviors, routine sequencing, or audience presentation is demonstrated.

sources.developer: Australian Centre for Field Robotics, University of Sydney
sources.title: Meet SwagBot, the AI-powered robot cattle herder preventing soil degradation
sources.claim: SwagBot autonomously herds cattle to selected pastures in open paddocks and monitors livestock and pasture condition, demonstrated on farms north of Sydney.
sources.transferJustification: Closest evidence of a robot directing live animals' movement in an unstructured outdoor setting (related task: moving and positioning animals). It does not transfer: herding pushes a group in a direction with no trained-cue repertoire, no reinforcement timing, no handling or presentation of an individual animal, and no judged or audience-facing performance.

emergingTasks.label: Teach owners how to train their dogs.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

emergingTasks.label: Teach people with visual impairments to use guide dogs.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Animal Caretakers
roles.description: Feed, water, groom, bathe, exercise, or otherwise provide care to promote and maintain the well-being of pets and other animals that are not raised for consumption, such as dogs, cats, race horses, ornamental fish or birds, zoo animals, and mice. Work in settings such as kennels, animal shelters, zoos, circuses, and aquariums. May keep records of feedings, treatments, and animals received or discharged. May clean, disinfect, and repair cages, pens, or fish tanks.

tasks.label: Feed and water animals according to schedules and feeding instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boarding kennel, doggy daycare, veterinary boarding or grooming facility: twice-daily rounds for 20-60 dogs and cats in runs and cage banks. Worker reads each animal's feeding card, scoops owner-supplied or house dry food (often with canned topper, supplement or pill hidden in food), carries bowls down the aisle, opens run gates with the animal present, sets and later collects bowls, and refills or replaces water bowls.

Boarding, training or racing stable: morning and evening feeds for 15-40 horses. Worker throws measured hay flakes into stalls or feeders, mixes grain/pellets with supplements per each horse's chart into individual buckets, hangs or dumps buckets in stalls with horses present, tops up water buckets or checks automatic waterers and pasture troughs.

Zoo or aquarium section round, bulk or dispensable diets: hay, browse pellets and produce for hoofstock and primates, prepared flake/pellet or frozen ration for fish and invertebrate exhibits. Worker weighs out diets in the commissary, carts them to holding areas and habitats, and scatters or places feed while animals are shifted off exhibit.

Zoo or aquarium section round, hand and behavioral feeding: thawed whole fish for penguins and pinnipeds fed by hand during training sessions, whole-prey and bone-in meat for carnivores placed in dens, live insects and pinky mice for reptiles and birds, browse hung in enclosures, hand/syringe feeding of neonates and geriatric animals, with amounts adjusted to observed appetite and body condition.

Laboratory animal facility (vivarium): daily/weekly provisioning of thousands of rodent cages on ventilated racks plus aquatic racks — topping pelleted chow in wire-bar hoppers, checking or replacing water bottles and automatic drinking valves, providing special diets per protocol, feeding zebrafish tanks on schedule, and logging per-cage records.

In-home pet sitting or drop-in visits: worker enters a client's house per a written care sheet, portions dry and refrigerated wet food for one to several pets with different diets, adds prescribed medication, sets bowls in designated spots, dumps and refills water bowls, and confirms each animal ate.

sources.title: Automatic Feeding Robot | Feeding System | Lely Vector
sources.claim: Lely Vector is a commercial automatic mixing-and-feeding robot that autonomously prepares and delivers precisely mixed rations to each animal group in a barn from a purpose-built feed kitchen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: livestock ration feeding. The physical act is the same as the caretaker's — delivering measured feed portions to penned animals on a set schedule and per group-specific feeding instructions — but requires a purpose-built feed kitchen and barn feed alley.

sources.title: LELY Vector Robotic Feeding System - Modern Agriculture Magazine
sources.claim: The Vector robot navigates and distributes feed autonomously using sensors and lasers, with humans only refilling the feed kitchen every few days.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: livestock ration feeding. Establishes that scheduled ration delivery runs without a human in the ... between infrequent feed-kitchen refills, the autonomy standard needed for the caretaker's feeding round.

sources.title: Quick Feed Automatic Feeders
sources.claim: Timer-driven automatic feeders are commercially sold and used in pet boarding facilities, dog kennels and horse stables, mounted on stall exteriors or flush to kennel walls, dispensing kibble, grain or pellets at programmed times.

sources.title: Automatic Pet Feeder For Cats and Dogs | Feeder-Robot
sources.claim: A commercial app-scheduled automatic feeder dispenses controlled portions of dry food to cats and dogs multiple times per day without a person present.

sources.title: Edstrom® Animal Watering System | Avidity Science
sources.claim: Plumbed automated watering systems with species-specific drinking valves supply drinking water continuously to caged and penned animals and are installed in the overwhelming majority of North American animal facilities.

sources.title: Automatic Dog Water Dispenser: Dog Valve | Avidity Science
sources.claim: Automatic drinking valves designed for dog runs give kennel-housed dogs continuous fresh water without a caretaker filling bowls.

sources.developer: Doyle et al., published in eLife
sources.title: ZAF, the first open source fully automated feeder for aquatic facilities | eLife
sources.claim: An open-source fully automatic feeder delivers a standardized daily food amount to every tank in a research aquatic facility rack.

sources.title: Rearing Conditions and Automated Feed Distribution Systems for Zebrafish (Danio rerio)
sources.claim: A commercial robotic feeding system for zebrafish racks is produced for research aquatic facilities.

sources.title: Feeding Experimentation Device version 3 (FED3)
sources.claim: An in-cage pellet dispenser delivers food to rodents in standard vivarium home cages on programmed schedules with minimal experimenter intervention.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech / zoo collaboration, published in HardwareX
sources.title: ForageFeeder: A low-cost open source feeder for randomly distributing food - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: An automated feeder installed in a zoo gorilla habitat distributes cut produce into the enclosure on its own timing schedule, replacing part of the keeper's manual feed placement; the same paper notes conventional automated feeders cannot handle typical zoo diets.

sources.title: Automatic Feeder Kit – Full Install Package | Stable Grazer
sources.claim: A commercial stall-mounted equine feeder holds multiple pre-loaded meals and drops hay and grain into the stall at programmed intervals.

tasks.label: Provide treatment to sick or injured animals, or contact veterinarians to secure treatment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boarding kennel / doggy daycare: caretaker spots a dog that is vomiting, limping, coughing, or has diarrhea; isolates it, gives owner- or vet-prescribed oral pills/liquid, eye or ear drops, or topical ointment, checks hydration and appetite, cleans a torn nail or abrasion, and phones the owner and on-call veterinarian. Dogs are conscious, variably cooperative, and must be restrained by hand.

Animal shelter / humane society: intake or in-kennel treatment of a sick or injured cat or dog (upper respiratory infection, ringworm, mange, bite wounds, emaciation, orphan kittens). Caretaker administers vaccines, dewormer, oral antibiotics, subcutaneous fluids, wound flushing and bandaging, and tube- or bottle-feeds neonates under standing vet orders, escalating to the shelter veterinarian.

Racing/boarding stable or equine facility: groom treats a horse's leg injury or hoof abscess — cold-hosing, poulticing, applying liniment or ointment, standing wraps and bandages — gives oral paste medication or electrolytes, monitors for colic or lameness in a stall or aisle, and calls the veterinarian for anything beyond first aid.

Zoo or public aquarium keeper: notices an animal off feed, limping, or with a wound; delivers medication hidden in food or via a behaviorally trained voluntary injection in protected contact, applies topical treatment to reachable species, nets and moves a sick fish or bird to a quarantine system, and pages the staff veterinarian. Species range from primates and hoofstock to birds and fish.

Laboratory animal facility / vivarium: technician performs daily health checks on racked rodent cages, finds a mouse or rabbit with barbering wounds, dermatitis, dehydration, or post-surgical complications, provides supportive care (softened food, fluids, analgesic dosing per protocol, topical treatment) or reports to the attending veterinarian for treatment or euthanasia.

Pet store / aviary / ornamental fish holding room: caretaker finds a sick bird (fluffed, discharge) or fish (ich, fin rot, injury), moves it to a quarantine cage or tank, doses medication in water or food, adjusts heat and water quality, and contacts the consulting veterinarian.

sources.title: The use of Stingray optical delousing technique to control sea louse abundance under commercial conditions (Aquaculture Europe 2016)
sources.claim: Stingray Marine Solutions' optical delousing nodes autonomously detect and laser sea lice on farmed salmon in commercial sea cages — an automated treatment of an external parasite condition in live animals, deployed commercially since 2014.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parasite treatment of farmed food-fish in sea net pens. It is the closest deployed autonomous 'treatment of animals' system found, but it treats one parasite on one species of free-swimming salmon in a purpose-set cage; it performs no illness assessment, no handling, quarantine, wound care or medication dosing, so it does not carry over to treating sick pets, horses, zoo animals or ornamental fish.

sources.developer: University of British Columbia (open-source academic system)
sources.title: PiDose: an open-source system for accurate and automated oral drug administration to group-housed mice
sources.claim: PiDose is a fully automated, cage-mounted system that identifies group-housed mice by RFID and delivers accurately dosed oral drug in drinking-water drops over weeks without experimenter handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chronic oral drug dosing of healthy research mice. It relies on voluntary licking by mobile, healthy animals and does not detect illness, handle or restrain an animal, treat wounds, or give injections or fluids, so it cannot substitute for caretaker treatment of a sick or injured rodent.

sources.developer: Japanese academic consortium (published in Nature Communications)
sources.title: ARViS: a bleed-free multi-site automated injection robot for accurate, fast, and dense delivery of virus to mouse and marmoset cerebral cortex
sources.claim: Automated injection robots for rodents operate only on anesthetized, head-fixed animals in a purpose-built research rig, executing an experimental brain-injection procedure rather than clinical treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated needle placement and injection into a live animal. Transfer fails because the animal is anesthetized and rigidly fixtured by a human, the target is a research substance in the brain, and no assessment, restraint of a conscious animal, or nursing care is performed.

sources.title: The Role of Robotics in Veterinary Surgery – What Does the Future Hold?
sources.claim: Robotics in veterinary practice as of 2025 is confined to human-guided, master-slave surgical platforms used by veterinarians at a few referral centres; there is no autonomous robotic system that nurses or medicates sick pets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic intervention on companion animals. It is fully surgeon-teleoperated and therefore cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous caretaker-level treatment.

tasks.label: Examine and observe animals to detect signs of illness, disease, or injury.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boarding kennel / doggy-daycare attendant does daily health rounds on 20-60 dogs and cats: watches gait, appetite, water intake, stool and vomit in runs, then hands-on checks ears, eyes, gums, skin, paws and any lumps or wounds while leashing, feeding or grooming; flags concerns to the manager or on-call vet and logs them. Animals are unfamiliar, of many breeds and temperaments, some fearful or reactive. A minority of these rounds occur in a client's home during pet-sitting visits.

Animal shelter caretaker performs intake and daily rounds on incoming strays and surrenders: restrains an unknown dog or cat, scans for microchip, checks for fleas/ticks/ringworm, ocular and nasal discharge, dehydration, emaciation, wounds, limping, ear mites, and observes for kennel cough or URI over subsequent days; records findings for the shelter vet. Animals are frightened, sometimes fractious or contagious.

Zookeeper morning and evening observation rounds over terrestrial exhibits and holding areas (primates, hoofstock, big cats, birds, reptiles): counts animals, watches each individual's posture, gait, appetite, feces and social behavior against its known baseline, checks for wounds from conspecifics, and records keeper notes; occasional tactile checks through protected-contact training panels. Naturalistic exhibits with vegetation, pools, hides and variable weather.

Aquarist / fish-facility caretaker walks a bank of tanks or holding systems, feeds, and watches fish stocks for parasites and lesions (ich, fungus, fin rot, sea lice), abnormal swimming or buoyancy, gill flaring, and dead or moribund individuals; nets out affected fish and logs the finding. Uniform tanks, controlled lighting, largely single- or few-species stocks per system.

Laboratory animal technician performs cage-side health checks on racks of ventilated mouse and rat cages: looks through each cage for hunched posture, ruffled coat, porphyrin staining, weight loss, tumors, fight wounds, dystocia or dead animals; removes and handles individual animals when a problem is suspected and files a health report. Highly standardized, barrier-controlled vivarium.

Groom at a training stable or racetrack checks each horse before and after work: runs hands down tendons and fetlocks feeling for heat, filling or pain, picks out and inspects hooves for thrush, bruising or a loose shoe, checks eyes, nostrils, appetite, manure and attitude in the stall, and jogs or watches the horse move to spot lameness; reports to the trainer. Barn aisle, wash rack and track, with a live 1,000-lb animal that may fidget or kick.

sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: Challenges and opportunities - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Scout (formerly ChickenBoy, Faromatics/AGCO) is an autonomous ceiling-suspended robot in broiler houses that patrols above the flock with thermal and visual cameras and flags sick and dead birds, litter problems and leg-health issues without contacting the birds — i.e. an embodied machine that observes animals to detect signs of illness.
sources.transferJustification: Same task verb (observe animals to detect illness/injury) but on a uniform single-species flock; cited to mark the boundary of what autonomous animal-observation robots do, since it performs flock-level dead/sick-bird flagging rather than the individualized, hands-on exams of kenneled dogs, zoo animals, caged rodents or horses.

sources.title: Technology - Stingray Marine Solutions AS
sources.claim: Stingray Marine Solutions' submerged laser nodes use machine vision to identify sea lice on free-swimming farmed fish and automatically fire a guided laser pulse at each parasite, running continuously without an operator in the pen.
sources.transferJustification: Fish-health inspection: the system performs the detection half of the caretaker's fish round (spotting external parasites on live fish in a holding system) autonomously and continuously, on comparable objects (free-swimming fish in an enclosure) and at finer precision than a human counter.

sources.title: Stingray controls parasites in fish farms with machine vision and laser | Business Norway
sources.claim: The Stingray system is a machine-vision plus laser platform that has been sold commercially since 2014 and controls sea lice on ..., preventive basis in commercial fish-farming pens.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes commercial maturity and unattended operation of the fish-health detection system cited for the aquarist instance.

sources.title: Stingray directs 'laser focus' on second factory | Fish Farming Expert
sources.claim: Stingray laser units are deployed at scale in commercial salmon pens: more than 2,000 lasers produced and in use across Norway with major farming customers.
sources.transferJustification: Scale-of-deployment evidence for the same fish-health detection system; supports that the capability is real rather than a demo.

sources.title: AI in the Barn: Where is Technology Taking the Horse Industry? - The Plaid Horse Magazine
sources.claim: Equine lameness detection today is delivered by smartphone/AI apps and wearable sensors (e.g. Sleip, trialled by the British Horseracing Authority) operated by a person filming the horse, not by any robot that inspects the horse.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as a negative boundary: the state of the art for detecting equine injury is software run by a handler who presents and jogs the horse, so no embodied system performs the groom's leg/hoof/gait exam.

tasks.label: Mix food, liquid formulas, medications, or food supplements according to instructions, prescriptions, and knowledge of animal species.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boarding kennel or animal shelter feed kitchen: worker reads each animal's feeding card, scoops measured dry kibble from bins, opens and portions canned food, adds joint/probiotic supplements or a prescribed tablet or powder, stirs it into the food or a pill pocket, and labels dozens of bowls per service. Ordinary human kitchen fittings (cans, cabinets, sinks), varied bowl sizes, staff moving around.

Zoo or aquarium commissary: prepare 100-300 species-specific diets per day from a diet sheet - weigh produce, chopped meat, thawed fish, insects, browse and grains, mix gruels and hand-rearing or geriatric slurries, and add measured vitamin/mineral supplements (e.g., thiamine for fish) into labeled pans for each exhibit.

Nursery / hand-rearing of neonates and sick animals in a shelter, zoo or veterinary boarding ward: mix powdered milk replacer or critical-care formula with warm water to a precise dilution and temperature, whisk out lumps, fill bottles or syringes, and blend in electrolytes or a vet-prescribed medication for each individual on a per-feed schedule.

Equine barn or racing stable feed room: mix grain, pellets, chaff, soaked beet pulp or bran mash, top-dress supplements and vet-prescribed medication into individual feed buckets per each horse's chart, adjusting quantities for work level and condition.

Laboratory animal facility or research breeding colony: prepare medicated drinking water and medicated/special diets and supplement gels per protocol (drug concentration per liter, acidified or chlorinated water), mix and record batches for racks of cages.

In-home pet sitting / house-call care: in the client's own kitchen, follow the owner's written instructions to portion and mix the pet's food, stir in a supplement, or mix a prescribed medication into wet food, using whatever containers and utensils the household has.

Zoo or aquarium: cleaning exhibits and off-exhibit holding — raking and hosing habitat substrate, scrubbing dens, crates and transport boxes, brushing algae from pool walls and viewing glass, vacuuming pool bottoms, and disinfecting keeper equipment between areas.

tasks.label: Exercise animals to maintain their physical and mental health.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boarding kennel / doggy daycare: staff take an individual dog from its run into a fenced play yard or indoor play room for a 15-30 minute exercise session — leashing and moving the dog through the building, throwing balls, running and playing, watching for overheating or lameness, then returning the dog and noting the session on its card.

Daycare or shelter off-leash playgroups: 6-15 mixed dogs turned out together for group exercise; the caretaker stands in the yard reading body language, redirecting rough or over-aroused dogs, breaking up scuffles, rotating dogs in and out by temperament and energy level.

Leash walks outside the facility: shelter, boarding or pet-sitting staff walk dogs on sidewalks, neighborhood streets and trails for exercise, sniffing/mental stimulation and toileting — handling pulling and reactivity, passing other dogs and people, traffic, weather, and picking up waste.

Equine facility (boarding barn, training stable, racetrack backside): grooms hand-walk hot horses after a workout, turn horses out into paddocks, lunge them in a round pen, or halter and load horses into a mechanical hot walker / exerciser for their daily conditioning.

Zoo or aquarium keeper: scheduled exercise and enrichment sessions — shifting animals between holding and exhibit yards, cheetah lure runs, elephant or big-cat exercise walks, marine-mammal training/exercise sessions, placing puzzle and foraging devices to drive activity for varied species.

Cats, rabbits, birds and small mammals in shelters, catteries, pet stores or research vivaria: daily out-of-cage or in-room play/exercise time with wand toys, lasers, exercise pens, wheels and climbing structures, with the caretaker handling the animal and monitoring its condition.

tasks.label: Collect and record animal information, such as weight, size, physical condition, treatments received, medications given, and food intake.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boarding kennel, daycare, vet-clinic ward or shelter: at check-in (or a scheduled re-check) the caretaker retrieves the dog/cat/small pet, walks or lifts it onto a floor or table scale, gets it to stand still, reads the weight, confirms identity (tag/microchip) and enters weight/size into the animal's paper or software record.

Daily care rounds in a kennel, doggy daycare, shelter or rescue: for each animal in each run, record how much of the meal was eaten, water consumed, urination/defecation and stool quality, medications and treatments given, plus notes on demeanor, coughing, limping, vomiting or wounds, written on the kennel card or entered in boarding/shelter software.

Animal shelter intake: scan for a microchip, weigh the incoming animal, estimate age, sex, breed and size, examine and note physical condition (body condition score, coat, wounds, parasites, dentition), record vaccinations/dewormer/flea treatment given, and enter it all into the shelter management system.

Zoo or aquarium keeper daily records: weigh out prepared diets, observe and record how much each animal or group consumed, log behavior and condition observations (feces, gait, injuries, shed/molt), record voluntary training-station weights and treatments delivered, and enter the day's report into ZIMS or equivalent.

Laboratory animal facility: individually weigh rodents on a balance at cage checks or study time points, body-condition-score them, note clinical signs (hunched posture, porphyria, wounds), and record treatments/dosing and food/water consumption in colony or study management software.

Equine stable or racing barn: record each horse's feed and water intake (cleaned up vs leftover feed), hay consumption, manure, body weight from a livestock scale or weight tape, condition of legs and feet, and log all medications and treatments in the barn's regulated medication record.

Sheep, goats and pigs handled by this machine (roughly 30-90 kg, uncooperative, must stand still on a load cell) are comparable in size and behaviour to kennel dogs, and livestock weigh crates deliver the precision a kennel weight record needs.

tasks.label: Observe and caution children petting and feeding animals in designated areas to ensure the safety of humans and animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Zoo or farm-park contact yard (goats, sheep, alpacas) on a busy public day: the caretaker stands inside the yard among 20-40 visitors, watches each child's hands, cautions about gentle petting and flat-palm feeding, blocks or shoos animals that crowd or nip a toddler, steers a child clear, and pulls an over-stressed animal out to the rest pen.

Aquarium touch pool (rays, small sharks, tide-pool invertebrates): staff posted at the rim enforce two-finger touching, stop children from grabbing, lifting or chasing animals, keep them from leaning or dropping objects into the water, watch animals for avoidance behavior, and direct handwashing on exit.

Mobile/traveling petting zoo brought to a private backyard birthday party or a school lot: temporary pens on unfamiliar ground, no fixed layout, mixed ages including unsupervised toddlers, variable weather and footing; the attendant hands out feed cups, cautions children not to chase or hit the animals, and physically separates animal and child when needed.

Supervised animal-encounter station at a zoo, fair, or stable (pony ride, rabbit/chick handling, reptile touch line): children come one at a time, the caretaker restrains or holds the animal, positions the child's hands, cautions about noise and sudden movement, and ends the encounter if the animal reacts.

Animal shelter or rescue meet-and-greet: a family with young children visits an adoptable dog or cat in a visitation room or yard; the caretaker instructs the children on approach and petting, reads the animal's body language, cautions or repositions the child, and ends the visit if the animal shows stress.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous monitoring-and-warning of people inside a controlled facility. It shows perception plus alerting in an E2 setting, but not reading child/animal interaction risk, contextual verbal cautioning of children, or the physical separation of an animal and a child that this task requires.

It shows robots can speak to visitors autonomously, but demonstrates no risk assessment of live-animal handling and no ability to act when a child or animal is in danger.

tasks.label: Clean and disinfect surgical equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Companion-animal clinic or shelter surgical suite: after a spay/neuter or mass removal, the caretaker/assistant carries the used instrument pack to the prep room, rinses blood and tissue off hemostats, scissors, needle holders and retractors, scrubs hinges and serrations with enzymatic detergent and a brush, runs the ultrasonic cleaner, rinses, dries, lubricates box locks, inspects for damage, then wraps and autoclaves the pack.

High-volume spay/neuter, referral or teaching hospital sterile-processing room: 20-60 instrument packs a day moved in batches through enzymatic soak, instrument washer or ultrasonic, drying, sorting back into standardized pack counts, pouching/wrapping, and repeated autoclave cycles with indicator checks and cycle logs.

Between-procedure cleaning and disinfection of the surgical suite's fixed and non-immersible equipment: wiping blood, hair, and prep solution off the surgery table, overhead light handles, anesthesia machine and monitor surfaces, warming pad and scale; cleaning clipper blades and the suction canister; applying disinfectant with required contact time.

Reprocessing anesthesia and ancillary reusables after surgery: endotracheal tubes, rebreathing circuits and masks, laryngoscope blades, suction tubing - soaked in disinfectant, lumens brushed, rinsed, hung to dry, and returned to storage.

Zoo, aquarium, equine or mobile setting: instruments used for a field immobilization, barn-side procedure, or mobile spay/neuter van clinic are cleaned at a utility sink or portable station with limited equipment, often heavily soiled with hair, mud, or blood, then packed and run through a tabletop autoclave.

Delicate or complex items requiring manufacturer-specific reprocessing: flexible endoscopes with channels, ophthalmic/microsurgical and cannulated instruments, and powered orthopedic equipment - leak testing, channel flushing/brushing, high-level disinfection or special-cycle handling.

tasks.label: Transfer animals between enclosures to facilitate breeding, birthing, shipping, or rearrangement of exhibits.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boarding kennel, doggy daycare, or animal shelter: staff leash, coax or carry an individual dog out of its run and walk it to a transfer run, a clean kennel, an outdoor pen, a play group, or a whelping/quarantine area, then secure the latch and update the kennel card. Dogs range from 5 to 120 lb and include fearful, reactive, leash-shy and post-surgical animals; other dogs bark and lunge in adjacent runs.

Shelter cattery, pet store, aviary or vet boarding: moving cats, rabbits, guinea pigs, ferrets, birds and reptiles between cages, carriers, colony rooms and adoption-floor condos for cage cleaning, intake, litter/birthing separation or exhibit rearrangement. Animals are scooped, netted, hand-restrained or coaxed into a carrier; scratching, escape and stress are the main hazards.

Laboratory animal facility: transferring mice and rats between cages at a change station or biosafety cabinet — dirty-to-clean cage transfers, setting up breeding pairs/trios, separating pregnant dams into birthing cages, weaning and sexing litters into new cages, and boxing animals for shipment. Animals are picked up by tail base, cup or tunnel; identity cards and colony records must match.

Zoo or public aquarium: shifting carnivores, primates, hoofstock, birds, reptiles or aquatic animals between exhibit, night houses and holding pens through shift doors and raceways for exhibit rearrangement, keeper cleaning, breeding introductions and separations, and crate-training/loading animals for shipment to other institutions. Animals are trained to shift on cue but may refuse; two-person safety protocols apply.

Equine boarding barn, racetrack backstretch or breeding farm: haltering a horse in its stall and leading it to a paddock, wash rack, round pen, foaling stall or trailer, through barn aisles and gates, then swapping other horses into the vacated stall. Horses may be fresh, studdish, lame or foals at side.

Aquarium fishroom, ornamental fish wholesaler or pet store: netting or bagging fish and invertebrates and moving them between display tanks, quarantine systems, breeding tanks and holding vats for stock rearrangement, spawning setups or shipment; water parameters must be matched and handling stress minimized.

sources.system: PhenoSys RFID sorting system with automated gates
sources.developer: PhenoSys GmbH / Humboldt University (Winter, Schaefer et al.)
sources.title: A sorting system with automated gates permits individual operant experiments with mice from a social home cage
sources.claim: A commercially available RFID sorting system with automated gates autonomously routes individually identified mice one at a time out of a social home cage through a tube into an adjacent compartment, running 24/7 without a human present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routing identified rodents between connected enclosures for behavioral testing. It shows machine-controlled, identity-verified movement of rodents between two enclosures, but only for tagged adults in a tube-connected apparatus; it does not pick up animals, sex or wean pups, or close them into clean or shipping cages, which is most of the caretaker instance.

sources.system: Vivarium cage-handling robots (Mount Sinai CCMS installation; Getinge/Tecniplast robotic cage handling systems)
sources.developer: Getinge, Tecniplast, IWT (installations at Mount Sinai and other institutions)

sources.claim: Robotic automation deployed in US and European vivaria handles cages — emptying, washing, stacking and transporting them — while the animals themselves are still moved cage-to-cage by human staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cage processing in the same facility type. It establishes that the mature, deployed robotics in vivaria act on empty cages in a purpose-built cage-wash line, not on live animals, so it does not substantiate robotic transfer of rodents between cages.
