sources.title: Alvarado Helps Sahara Sam's Oasis Streamline Patron Access
sources.claim: A waterpark installed Alvarado tandem full-height turnstiles with TAS12 devices reading barcoded wristbands; GateWatch counting software integrated with the turnstiles gives a continuous recorded count of patrons admitted.
sources.transferJustification: Same substitution as above: the machine collects/validates the admission credential and generates the recorded admission count that a ticket taker would otherwise tally by hand.

sources.system: Alvarado UltraQ-AMT admission turnstile with GateLink10 admission control software
sources.title: UltraQ AMT - Alvarado dormakaba Group
sources.claim: Alvarado's admission control software driving its motorized admission turnstiles and gates is installed in hundreds of entertainment and sports facilities, indicating routine commercial deployment of automated ticket validation and admission counting in human venues.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes breadth of deployment of the same count-and-record admission hardware across stadiums and entertainment venues, the settings of the task's instances.

sources.system: Alvarado SU500 optical counting turnstile + GateWatch10
sources.title: SU500 - Alvarado dormakaba Group
sources.claim: Alvarado counting turnstiles output entry counts directly to server-based patron counting software, i.e. the recording step (a persistent count record/database) is machine-generated without a human tally.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the 'record' half of the task: the count is written automatically to an auditable database rather than onto a worker's tally sheet.

sources.system: SKIDATA sMove access gates (Stadium de Toulouse, Toulouse FC)
sources.title: SKIDATA Toulouse FC
sources.claim: A Ligue 1 stadium runs its three main entrances on about 50 SKIDATA sMove motorized access gates that validate QR tickets and feed every entry into a live count, giving operations accurate real-time attendance figures.
sources.transferJustification: The gate line performs the collection and simultaneous counting/recording of admissions for a 32,880-seat stadium, the output a gate supervisor would otherwise tally and record.

sources.system: Deltronic Labs Ticket Eater TT-2000 / DL-9000
sources.title: TT-2000 Standalone Ticket Eater - Betson Enterprises
sources.claim: Commercial 'Ticket Eater' machines take paper tickets handed over by patrons at amusement venues, count them with a microprocessor-controlled high-speed auto-feed mechanism, destroy them, and print a receipt recording the count.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: counting redemption tickets collected from patrons at an amusement venue. Same objects (small paper tickets), same required output (an accurate counted total printed as a record), same accuracy demands; it replaces staff who previously counted tickets by hand.

sources.system: Alvarado IntraQ self-validation entry pedestals (Texas Performing Arts, UT Austin)
sources.title: Guest Self-Validation Pedestals Improve Entry Throughput - Alvarado dormakaba Group
sources.claim: A university performing-arts complex replaced staff handheld ticket scanning with Alvarado self-validation entry pedestals at its theatre entrances, reading printed and digital barcodes reliably and at double the throughput of attendants, feeding the venue's entry counts.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the same admission-capture-and-count hardware family deployed in performing-arts theatre lobbies (the setting of several instances), where entry counts previously depended on staff and volunteer ticket collectors.

tasks.label: Lead tours and answer visitors' questions about the exhibits.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Museum, historic house, or visitor-center attendant leads a scheduled walk-through of galleries for a small public group, narrating background on each exhibit and fielding questions along the way.

Visitor in the lobby or gallery approaches the usher/ticket taker with an ad hoc question about a display or artifact ('what is this piece?', 'where is the dinosaur hall?'); attendant answers, adds context, and points or gives directions.
Stadium, arena, theater, or concert-hall tour: lobby attendant walks ticketed visitors through back-of-house areas and trophy/memorabilia displays, narrating venue history and answering questions.

Large school or camp group tour: attendant leads children through exhibit halls, keeps the group together and paced, delivers age-adapted commentary, reminds visitors of rules, and answers rapid-fire questions.

Special-exhibit, VIP, donor, or accessibility-accommodated tour: attendant gives a tailored narration, adjusts pace and route for mobility or hearing needs, and answers detailed or unexpected questions about the exhibits.

tasks.label: Manage inventory or sale of artist merchandise.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Selling at a built-in merch point in an arena, amphitheater or large theater concourse during a show: 15-40 SKUs of tees, hoodies, hats, posters; card-dominant payments; surges before doors, at intermission and at load-out; several sellers behind a counter answering size questions and handing over folded goods.

Running a one-person merch table at a club or mid-size venue: folding table in a dim, loud lobby, stock in road cases under and behind the table, cash plus mobile POS, seller pulls the right size/design, makes change, chats with fans, keeps the display tidy through the night.

Setting up and tearing down the merch stand: unpacking road cases and cartons, folding and stacking shirts by size, hanging display samples and price banners, restocking between rushes, then packing everything back into cases at the end of the night.

Count-in and count-out inventory with settlement: counting stock by design and size before doors and again after the show, entering counts into the merch POS/inventory system, reconciling units sold against cash and card totals with the tour or venue manager.

Roving sales: walking the seating bowl, aisles, lawn or festival grounds with a tray, cart or armload of programs, souvenir items and merch, approaching patrons, taking payment and making change in a dense standing or seated crowd.

sources.title: A New Era of Stadium Retail: Vidir's Merchandise Vending Machine
sources.claim: Vidir's Merchandise Vending Machine, an automated storage-and-retrieval unit, was installed in the concourse at the Winnipeg Blue Bombers' stadium and autonomously stores and delivers fan apparel (hats, jerseys) to purchasing fans on game day.
sources.transferJustification: Sports fan apparel sold in an event-venue concourse is the same product class, price point and transaction as artist merch sold at a venue merch point; the machine performs selection, payment and physical hand-over of the garment to the patron.

sources.title: Galbot brings in $300M to scale mobile manipulator deployments - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Galbot's G1 mobile manipulator runs 'Galbot Store', an unmanned retail format in which the robot retrieves packaged products from shelves and hands them to customers; the company says these stores operate in over 30 cities in China.
sources.transferJustification: Unmanned convenience/pharmacy retail requires the same physical core as a merch sale in a venue: take the customer's order, retrieve the correct packaged item from stock, complete payment and hand it over, inside a facility open to the public.

sources.system: Super Mercato tour merch vending machine
sources.title: Now you can buy concert merchandise from a vending machine using Apple Pay [Video] - 9to5Mac
sources.claim: A custom merchandise vending machine ('Super Mercato') toured with the band Phoenix, selling apparel and other tour merch to concertgoers by card or mobile wallet without a merch seller.

sources.title: PAL Robotics' StockBot at Decathlon stores (IFR case study)
sources.claim: PAL Robotics' StockBot autonomously navigates Decathlon apparel/sporting-goods stores during opening hours with shoppers present and reads RFID-tagged stock to produce a full daily inventory with item locations, replacing manual stock counting.
sources.transferJustification: Counting tagged apparel stock in a retail facility is the same physical activity as counting merch stock in and out at a venue: locating and enumerating garments by SKU and feeding the counts to the inventory system for reconciliation.

sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robot restocks refrigerated shelves with bottles and ... in roughly 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, running autonomously with rare remote human assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Shelf replenishment from case stock in a customer-facing retail facility is the rigid-goods analogue of restocking a merch display; it shows autonomous restocking in an E2 store but only for rigid packaged items, not folded garments or display build-out.

sources.title: Uniqlo's new robots can pick up and pack t-shirts just like human workers
sources.claim: Fast Retailing (Uniqlo) and Mujin deployed dual-arm robots in an automated Tokyo warehouse that identify, pick up and pack t-shirts and other apparel into boxes, a soft-goods handling task previously done only by people.
sources.transferJustification: Picking, handling and packing folded t-shirts is the manipulation core of merch restocking and pack-out, demonstrated only in a purpose-built warehouse cell where the garments are presented to the machine.

sources.title: SpeedFolding: Learning Efficient Bimanual Folding of Garments (arXiv:2208.10552)
sources.claim: UC Berkeley's SpeedFolding bimanual system autonomously smooths and folds randomly placed garments at 30-40 folds per hour with about 93% success in a fixed laboratory workcell.
sources.transferJustification: Folding and stacking shirts for display and re-packing is a large share of merch stand setup/restock; SpeedFolding shows this is autonomous only in a purpose-built cell with the garment presented on a fixed table, and still far below human speed.

tasks.label: Assist patrons in finding seats, lighting the way with flashlights, if necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Performing-arts venue (theater/concert hall), pre-show on the flat or gently ramped orchestra/main level: usher reads the patron's ticket at the aisle head, walks the party down a carpeted aisle to the correct row, indicates the seat, hands a program; house lights up, continuous stream of arrivals.

Stepped seating: mezzanine/balcony of a theater or a multiplex auditorium with stadium seating; usher leads patrons up or down flights of steps in the aisle, past narrow rows and seated patrons, to a numbered row, often in dimmed light before curtain.

Darkened house during the performance: latecomers or patrons returning from the restroom are led with a small flashlight down a dim aisle, the beam kept on the floor/steps; the usher must find the row/seat number in near darkness, seat them quietly, and avoid disturbing the audience.

Stadium, arena, or ballpark seating bowl during ingress: usher stationed at the top of a section aisle checks or scans tickets and walks fans down the concrete steps to their row amid dense two-way crowd flow, vendors, strollers, spilled drinks, and bright or floodlit conditions.

Patrons needing physical assistance: elderly or unsteady patrons offered an arm, wheelchair users escorted or pushed to accessible seating, visually impaired guests guided by touch, families with strollers; usher walks at their pace, folds down seats, moves obstacles and companion chairs.

Outdoor or temporary venue: festival lawn, fairground, outdoor amphitheater, high-school field, or hall with folding-chair rows set up for the event; usher leads patrons across grass, gravel, matting and cable runs to a temporary row/block that differs from event to event, often at dusk or after dark.

sources.title: KettyBot PRO Operation Guide Version: V1.1 Model: PNT
sources.claim: Pudu's KettyBot, a commercially deployed hospitality service robot, has an escort function in which a staff member or guest selects a table number and the robot autonomously leads the customers to that specific seating position in a restaurant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading a restaurant guest to an assigned table. It matches ushering in shape (walk a patron from an entrance to a specific numbered seating position and hand them off) and in environment (flat-floored, institution-run venue with moving people and furniture).

sources.title: Pudu Kettybot Robot | RobotLAB
sources.claim: KettyBot performs the guest-leading function with autonomous path planning and obstacle avoidance in crowded, tight commercial spaces; it is sold as a standard commercial product.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; this source establishes that the leading behavior is autonomously planned rather than teleoperated, and that it works in crowded, narrow-clearance venues.

sources.system: LG Airport Guide Robot / CLOi GuideBot
sources.title: LG Airport Robots Take over Korea's Largest Airport
sources.claim: LG's Airport Guide Robot, deployed at Incheon International Airport, scans a passenger's boarding pass and then escorts the traveler to the correct departure gate through a crowded public terminal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reading a passenger's ticket-equivalent (boarding pass) and physically escorting a latecomer to an assigned numbered location inside a large, institution-controlled public venue with heavy pedestrian traffic — the same read-ticket-then-walk-the-patron-to-their-place structure as seating a patron.

sources.title: LG CLOi GuideBot | LG Global
sources.claim: LG sells the CLOi GuideBot commercially as an autonomous-driving guide robot with an escort mode that walks visitors to a requested destination in facilities such as airports and exhibition halls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wayfinding escort inside a managed public facility; the destination-escort behavior is the walking-the-patron-to-their-seat component of ushering, on flat institutional floors.

sources.title: Spencer robot completed tests guiding KLM passengers at Schiphol
sources.claim: The SPENCER robot guided KLM transfer passengers through Amsterdam Schiphol terminal, moving off automatically, matching the group's walking pace, avoiding obstacles and reporting remaining distance to the gate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: socially aware guiding of a group of people through a busy terminal. It transfers to leading a party of patrons along an aisle: same pace-matching, obstacle avoidance and crowd navigation, in a flat institution-controlled venue.

sources.system: Nickelytics/USL stadium delivery robot fleet (Grubhub partnership)
sources.title: Delivery robots could roll into Al Lang Stadium - St Pete Catalyst
sources.claim: Wheeled autonomous service robots trialed in a stadium setting are restricted to accessible, step-free areas; stairs remain an unsolved barrier for the fleet.
sources.transferJustification: Limiting evidence for the seating-bowl instance: mobile service robots in stadiums operate only where the floor is step-free, so they cannot walk a fan down a stepped section aisle.

tasks.label: Schedule or manage staff, such as volunteer usher corps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Page individuals wanted at the box office.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Manage informational kiosks or displays of event signs or posters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Before doors open at a theater, arena, or concert hall, the usher/lobby attendant sets out freestanding signage around the lobby and concourse: A-frame/sandwich boards, easels holding show posters, stanchion sign holders, 'will call' and directional signs; positions them at designated spots, straightens them during the event, and collects and stores them afterward.

Updating printed content in displays: swapping posters and inserts in wall-mounted display cases and snap frames, changing show cards on easels, updating a lobby letter/marquee board or reader board with the current event title and times, removing outdated notices.

Stocking and tidying an information kiosk or counter: fetching programs, maps, flyers, season brochures and event schedules from a storeroom, filling and straightening the literature rack slots, discarding outdated stock, keeping the counter neat during the run.

Staffing/monitoring the information kiosk while patrons are present: handing out programs and maps, answering wayfinding questions at the kiosk, keeping a digital touchscreen kiosk working (wiping the screen, rebooting or re-loading the event content, clearing a printer jam, flagging faults to facilities).

Outdoor entry-plaza and gate signage at stadiums, fairgrounds, and festivals: zip-tying banners to fences and railings, staking yard/directional signs into turf or ballasting A-frames against wind, repositioning weather-affected signs, and striking everything after the event.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid, in live commercial operation at GXO's Flowery Branch fulfillment site, autonomously picks totes on and off mobile robots and stacks containers at different designated floor locations, passing 100,000 totes moved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated pick-and-place of tote/container-sized objects, including setting them down at designated floor locations. A folding A-frame sign or easel presented at a known pose is comparable in size, weight and rigidity, and the placement precision required (a marked floor spot) is the same, so the capability transfers to placing and retrieving freestanding signage when the work is presented as a purpose-built cell would present it.

sources.system: Figure 02 at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg
sources.title: BMW successfully tests humanoid robots at Spartanburg plant
sources.claim: Figure 02 worked in BMW's Spartanburg body shop inserting sheet metal parts into specific ... with sub-centimeter accuracy, a dexterous production step performed by the robot in a live plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise insertion of thin flat parts into fixtures. Sliding a printed poster or insert into a fixtured snap frame, or seating letters into a reader-board track, requires the same class of flat-part alignment and insertion precision at a fixed station, so performance carries over when the frame is presented on a fixture.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robots restock beverage display shelves in FamilyMart convenience stores around the clock, running on the GORDON AI autonomously during normal operation with remote teleoperated recovery only for rare errors; stock is placed behind the robot by store workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing a customer-facing display from stock presented to the machine, deciding from sensing which slots are low. Filling a literature rack with programs or flyers is the same replenishment loop against a pre-registered shelf layout, with lighter items and comparable placement precision, when the stock is presented at the machine as it is here.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously picks individual products of varying shapes and sizes out of containers and places them into specific totes in fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bin picking of heterogeneous, often flat or semi-deformable retail items at a fixtured station. Handling stacks of printed programs, flyers and poster sheets presented in bins involves the same grasp-selection and placement problem, supporting the fixtured-station (E1) versions of the poster-change and literature-restocking instances.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics hits 1M picks with Moxi robot in healthcare settings - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi, the largest commercial deployment of mobile manipulation alongside people, autonomously navigates hospitals and picks supplies out of supply closets to deliver them across the building; its manipulation is limited to fetching and transporting supply items rather than positioning fixtures or merchandising displays.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E2 case: this is the most mature mobile manipulator working in a structured human facility, and its accepted work is fetch-and-deliver of supply items, not carrying and positioning signage or filling display racks among patrons.

sources.title: August Robotics | Case Study — Messukeskus
sources.claim: August Robotics' Lionel autonomously marks exhibition floor plans at convention centres such as Messukeskus in Finland, having marked over 300 million square feet worldwide; it navigates event venues autonomously but performs marking only, with no object manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous event-venue setup work (marking booth positions on the hall floor). It establishes that autonomous navigation and precise positioning inside event venues is commercially routine, but because the robot has no manipulator it cannot substantiate placing signs or changing posters at E2.

tasks.label: Give door checks to patrons who are temporarily leaving establishments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Movie theater: a patron steps out mid-show for the restroom or concessions; the usher/ticket taker at the auditorium door or lobby hands them a printed re-entry pass or returns their stub, noting the auditorium number, and readmits them later. Calm, low-volume, indoor lobby.

Sports arena or stadium 'pass-out' gate: at a designated exit door during the event, the ticket taker scans/inspects the patron's ticket and issues a printed re-entry pass or ticket stub amid steady crowd flow, then checks it on return. High throughput, noisy, institution-controlled concourse.

Concert hall, club show, or music festival: at intermission or a smoking-break exit, the attendant applies an ink hand stamp or a tamper-evident wristband directly to each departing patron's hand/wrist, dozens per minute, in dim light with a pressing, sometimes intoxicated crowd.

Outdoor amusement park, fair, or ballpark gate: gate attendant issues a re-entry pass, validated wristband, or hand stamp to guests leaving for the parking lot or car, in sun/rain/wind with families, strollers and bags, at high throughput.

Casino, convention center, or museum event: attendant at an exit/hospitality desk checks the patron's badge, ticket or wristband and issues a re-entry sticker, pass or badge reprint, occasionally handling exceptions (lost stub, comped guest, VIP).

sources.system: PDC Smart RFID Wristband Kiosk (Precision Dynamics Corp.)
sources.title: RFID wristbands made a splash at Denver water park | Kiosk Marketplace
sources.claim: PDC's self-service Smart RFID Wristband Kiosk was installed at Hyland Hills Water World, Denver, where it takes guest input and payment and then programs and dispenses a physical RFID credential wristband to the guest on the spot; the same kiosks are marketed and used for self-service ticketing and admissions at amusement parks, waterparks, resorts and event venues.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended issuance of a physical admission/access credential to a patron standing in an entertainment venue. A door check is the same object class (a small paper/plastic token or band) issued in the same setting by the same physical act — verify entitlement, then dispense to the patron's hand.

sources.system: Pyramid polytouch ticketing kiosk (AMC / Cinemark deployments)
sources.title: First 4-in-1 self service kiosk | Kiosk Industry
sources.claim: Pyramid polytouch self-service kiosks are deployed in US cinema lobbies for AMC and Cinemark, printing tickets and scanning QR/bar codes; the AMC units integrate a thermal printer, card reader and bar/QR-code scanner and have been rolled out across the circuit after a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: printing and handing a paper ticket to a patron in a theater lobby after scanning a bar/QR code. A re-entry door check is the same paper artifact, issued after the same credential check, in the same lobby.

sources.system: Amano McGann Overture-2000 Series Entry Terminal
sources.date: 2023 (undated vendor product page, product line commercially deployed for years)
sources.title: Amano-McGann Overture | DGM Systems
sources.claim: Amano McGann Overture entry terminals automatically dispense thermal barcode tickets to arriving patrons at controlled entry lanes (indoor and outdoor parking facilities including theme-park, hotel, hospital and event facilities), with the same ticket later validated for exit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an unattended machine issues a physical paper check to a person passing a control point, which that person later presents to be validated. This is functionally and physically the door-check act, at gate throughput and in weather-exposed outdoor lanes.

sources.title: Ottonomy Ottobot airport delivery robots set to expand to two more airports - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Ottonomy's Ottobot has operated as a fully autonomous indoor delivery robot at Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport since late 2020, navigating public terminal areas among travelers and handing over purchased goods, which passengers retrieve by scanning a QR code to open ... compartment at their gate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous machine-to-patron handover of a small item inside a crowded, institution-controlled public facility. Shows that identifying an entitled person (QR credential) and releasing a physical item to them works at E2 among unscreened members of the public.

sources.title: Austin-based Blackdot launches futuristic way to tattoo | KXAN Austin
sources.claim: Blackdot's automated tattoo device marks human skin at a commercial studio in East Austin: the client is positioned at the machine and a robotic arm applies the design to the skin, with the studio taking paying customers since its 2023-2024 launch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a machine applying a mark to a presented human limb at a fixed station. This is the closest substantiated analogue to ink-stamping a patron's hand, but only with the limb positioned and held for the machine — a purpose-built presentation, not a moving queue.

sources.title: Self-Service Ticket Kiosks | Digital Ticketing | REDYREF
sources.claim: Self-service ticket/registration kiosks are deployed at conferences, ... events, where attendees check themselves in and the kiosk prints their badge and event credentials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: credential check plus on-the-spot printing and release of a physical pass to an attendee in a convention/casino-type venue — the same act and artifact as issuing a re-entry pass at an exit desk.

tasks.label: Work with others to change advertising displays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Multiplex cinema lobby/hallway: with a co-worker, swap the one-sheet posters in wall snap-frames and backlit light boxes for the week's new titles — open the frame, pull the old poster, align and insert the new one, close and clean the face — around patrons during operating hours.

Cinema exterior: change posters in the outside display cases along the facade/box-office wall, working from a step ladder on the sidewalk in wind, sun or rain, one person steadying while the other seats the poster.
Cinema exterior marquee/attraction board: with a partner, pull and re-set individual plastic track letters or slide-in panels for new titles and showtimes, using a pole or ladder outdoors.

Cinema lobby: unbox and assemble a multi-piece die-cut cardboard standee or promotional display for the coming release (unique geometry each title, tab-and-slot panels, header, easel back), site it, weight/secure it, and break down and discard the outgoing standee.

Arena, stadium or large venue concourse: as part of a crew, take down and hang sponsor banners, vinyl signage and rotating ad panels on walls, railings and ceilings using ladders, lifts, zip ties and clips between events.

Live theater / performing arts center lobby: between productions, change framed show posters, easel placards, glass display-case cards and sponsor boards, moving easels and stanchions and matching the house layout.

sources.system: MWES vision-guided four-robot picture frame assembly line (FANUC robots)
sources.developer: Midwest Engineered Systems (MWES) for a picture frame manufacturer
sources.title: Flexibility & Production Speed with Robotic Vision | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: A commercial four-robot FANUC assembly line with machine vision assembles picture frames, inserting glass, paper mats and back ... into fixtured frames with vision-based alignment and pressing, producing 900 assembled frames in two hours including changeovers across seven frame styles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory assembly of framed prints. It transfers to changing a poster in a display frame because the objects are the same (a paper sheet of poster size and a rigid frame), the required precision is the same (sheet squared inside the frame lip), and the line already performs the decisive step — picking sheet media and seating it inside a fixtured frame — under vision guidance at production reliability.

sources.system: Durst P5 Robotics (two KUKA arms); Zünd/RobotFactory cobot board loading
sources.title: The Rise of Robotics: Automating Wide Format Print Production (FESPA)
sources.claim: Durst's P5 Robotics option uses two KUKA robot arms to de-stack, register and precisely place large-format print sheets (including thin papers, foils and boards) into and out of a wide-format press, a commercially offered print-shop cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading/unloading large-format graphic sheets in a print production cell. It transfers to poster changing because the handled objects are exactly poster-size printed sheets and rigid display boards, and the cell demonstrates reliable single-sheet separation and placement to a known registered position — the manipulation core of swapping a poster in a fixtured frame.

sources.system: INSITE by Douglas case erectors / standard automatic case erectors
sources.developer: INSITE by Douglas Machine (and other packaging OEMs)
sources.title: INSITE Case Erectors | Box Formers | INSITE by Douglas
sources.claim: Automatic case erectors form corrugated displays/cases from flat knock-down blanks, but each machine is set up for a defined case format rather than for one-off, novel display geometries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated erection of corrugated blanks. It only partially transfers: these are fixed-format machines tooled for one repeated carton, whereas a movie standee is a one-off multi-panel structure with a unique tab-and-slot geometry per title, so the evidence does not substantiate completing the standee instance.

tasks.label: Distribute programs to patrons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-size theater, concert hall or performing-arts center: usher stands at an auditorium door or head of aisle through the 30-40 minute admission window, holding an armful of playbills and handing one to each entering patron at a steady, moderate flow (a few patrons per minute per door), while greeting and pointing toward the aisle.

High-volume handout: large Broadway-scale house at the curtain rush, or an arena/ballpark gate where staff push programs, rosters or giveaway inserts into the hands of a dense, fast-moving stream of fans passing turnstiles - hundreds of items per staff position within a few minutes, jostling crowd, sometimes outdoors.

Small or community venue - church hall, school auditorium, black-box or community theater: one attendant at a folding table or doorway hands programs to 50-300 patrons arriving over an hour; improvised layout that differs from show to show, but the premises are run and kept in order by the presenting organization.

Pre-show seat placement in the empty house: before doors open, staff walk the rows laying a program (sometimes with a loose insert) on each of several hundred to a couple thousand fixed seats or into seat-back pockets, finishing inside a set window before the house opens.

Lobby program table or rack: attendant stays at a stocked table in the lobby, hands programs to patrons who walk up and ask, gives extras to groups, keeps the stack fanned and presented, and directs patrons who ask where to get one.

Late/intermission distribution inside the darkened house: handing programs or cast-change slips to latecomers being seated and to patrons already in their rows, moving quietly along narrow aisles in low light while the performance or interval is under way.

sources.system: ATR flyer-distributing robot (Robovie-based) with distributional handing model
sources.developer: ATR Intelligent Robotics and Communication Labs / Osaka University (Shi, Shiomi, Smith, Kanda, Ishiguro)
sources.title: A model of distributional handing interaction for a mobile robot (RSS 2013)
sources.claim: An autonomous humanoid robot distributed printed flyers to ordinary pedestrians in a shopping-mall hallway, approaching each target and extending its arm; it achieved a 73.3% acceptance rate, close to the best human flyer distributors observed (78%) in the same mall. The robot also autonomously printed the flyer and picked it up with its gripper before selecting a target.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same act as distributing programs: presenting a sheet of printed matter to a member of the public who takes it from the robot's hand, in an indoor public facility, with uninstructed people walking past.

sources.developer: ATR / Osaka University (Shi, Satake, Kanda, Ishiguro)
sources.title: A Robot that Distributes Flyers to Pedestrians in a Shopping Mall, International Journal of Social Robotics
sources.claim: The journal version reports the flyer-handing behavior model implemented on a humanoid robot and validated in a field experiment in a real shopping mall, a structured, institution-run indoor public facility.
sources.transferJustification: Handing flyers to passers-by is the same physical operation, object class (loose printed sheets) and precision as handing programs to patrons entering a venue.

sources.title: Autonomous Flyer Delivery Robot (ICIRA 2018, Springer LNCS)
sources.claim: A service robot with an internal cassette that singulates stored A5-A7 flyers and feeds a fresh one to its palm roughly every 8 seconds after the previous one is taken, with autonomous cassette and battery swapping, performed flyer delivery to the public without human intervention at public exhibitions in Taiwan.
sources.transferJustification: Storing a stack of printed matter, singulating one copy and presenting it at hand height for a member of the public to take is exactly the mechanics of distributing programs from a stack.

Setting up and taking down equipment in place: stringing volleyball/badminton nets on standards, rolling out and locking portable basketball hoops, erecting canopies, batting cages, inflatables, tables and carnival game booths in the gym, court, field or midway, then breaking them down and returning parts to storage.

Golf course cart barn / bag room: staging carts for tee times, retrieving and parking returned carts in rows, plugging in chargers, storing and pulling member bags and pull-carts from numbered racks, keeping the log of fleet and bag locations.

Waterfront or outdoor adventure concession: hauling kayaks, canoes, paddleboards, tubes, paddles and PFDs between a rack/barn and the shoreline staging area, racking them at close of day, rinsing and counting them; sand, slope, wind and wet gear.

tasks.label: Provide assistance to patrons entering or exiting amusement rides, boats, or ski lifts, or mounting or dismounting animals.

instances.label: Permanent amusement park or carnival ride: attendant stands on the loading platform, directs the incoming group into ride vehicle rows, steadies guests as they step into a moving-or-stationary car, seats them, pulls down and physically verifies lap bars/over-the-shoulder harnesses, dispatches, then opens restraints and helps guests step out onto the unload platform, hundreds of cycles per shift amid crowds.

Same ride platforms, but the patrons need hands-on help: lifting a toddler onto a carousel horse, steadying an elderly guest, or transferring a guest from a wheelchair into the ride seat and back out at unload, per the ride's accessibility procedure.

Ski area chairlift loading station: attendant lines skiers/snowboarders up at the wait-here line, slows or stops the lift for children and beginners, steadies the chair behind riders, helps anyone who falls or drops a pole get clear of the load zone, in cold, snow and wind.

Ski area lift unload area (chairlift top station or gondola station): attendant watches each chair/cabin dismount, slows or stops the lift when a rider falls, misses the unload, or gets clothing/skis caught, and keeps the exit ramp clear so following chairs can unload.

Boat/watercraft rental dock at a lake, marina, or river livery: attendant fits life jackets, holds a kayak, canoe, paddleboat or pontoon against the dock, gives patrons a hand stepping in and out of a rocking hull, and pushes them off or pulls them in on return.

Riding stable or pony-ride concession: attendant holds the horse's head steady at the mounting block, gives the rider a leg up, adjusts stirrups and girth, and steadies horse and rider for dismount at the end of the ride.

tasks.label: Verify, collect, or punch tickets before admitting patrons to venues, such as amusement parks and rides.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Main-gate admission at a permanent amusement/water park or large attraction: attendant at a turnstile lane scans or taps guests' tickets, mobile passes, RFID wristbands or season passes, checks date/validity and pass identity, and admits the party through the gate; continuous high-volume flow, families with strollers, fixed entry plaza.

Ride- or lift-entrance verification inside a park or at a ski area: attendant at the queue/loading gate checks wristband color, ride pass or fast-pass reservation, or punches a strip of ride tickets, before letting each party through to board; outdoors, repetitive, weather and glove conditions, fixed permanent installation.

Traveling carnival or county-fair midway: ride jock collects paper ticket coupons or punches/taps a ride card at each ride entrance on a midway that is set up fresh at each fairground; mixed crowds, dust, rain, night lighting, no fixed layout or entry barriers.

Recreation facility entry desk or gate (skating rink, bowling center, pool, trampoline park, arcade/FEC, mini-golf): verify a paid ticket, wristband, membership or reservation and admit the patron into the play area; indoor, fixed counter/turnstile, moderate flow.

Exception handling at the admission point: expired or wrong-date ticket, season-pass photo mismatch, third-party voucher or school-group list, guest who lost a ticket, accessibility entry, disputed re-entry hand stamp; requires conversation, judgment and discretion before admitting or refusing.

tasks.label: Fasten safety devices for patrons, or provide them with directions for fastening devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fixed-site thrill ride (roller coaster, drop tower, spinning flat ride) at a theme or amusement park: attendant walks the loading platform, pushes down over-the-shoulder harnesses or lap bars against each rider's torso, tug-tests each restraint and confirms secondary seat belts for 16-32 riders of widely varying body size, all within a 60-90 second dispatch window, then signals the ride is clear.

Family/slow ride with lap-bar restraints (dark ride omnimover, ferris wheel, log flume, mine train, family coaster): attendant seats guests, sees that the lap bar comes down and locks over the party, gives verbal directions ('bar down, hands inside'), and visually verifies each row before dispatch.

Kiddie ride (kiddie cars, carousel horses, small train, bounce ride): attendant kneels or reaches into each seat to buckle a webbing seat belt around a small, often squirming child, threads it correctly over the lap, adjusts slack, latches the individual lap bar, and confirms the child is seated back before the cycle starts.

Ski lift / snow tubing / mountain coaster loading at a resort: lift operator loads skiers and riders onto a moving chair in snow and wind, instructs them to lower the restraining bar, helps children or beginners get the bar down, and slows or stops the lift when loading goes wrong.

Adventure attraction (zip line, aerial ropes course, climbing wall, bungee trampoline): attendant fits a full-body or sit harness onto each patron's body, routes and tightens waist and leg straps over street clothing, fits and buckles a helmet chin strap, and clips the carabiner/belay device, checking fit on adults and children of many shapes.

Go-kart track, bumper boats, water park or boat rental: attendant fastens or checks a lap belt on a kart or boat seat, buckles helmet chin straps, and fits and buckles life vests on patrons before they launch, often in a fast-moving queue of walk-up customers.

instances.label: Thrill-ride operator at a fixed amusement/theme park (roller coaster, drop tower, spinning ride): works the control console and PA spiel, sizes and physically tug-checks each lap bar/shoulder harness/seatbelt, enforces height and loose-article rules, clears the platform, dispatches, and e-stops for guest issues. Paved station built for guest flow, crowds and children present, all weather.

Family/kiddie ride and dark-ride operator at a fixed park (carousel, teacups, kiddie flat rides, boat/track dark ride): lifts or steadies small children into vehicles, latches bars and buckles belts, keeps riders seated, starts and stops the cycle, unloads and helps guests with mobility needs. Continuous crowd interaction on an open loading platform.

Water park attraction attendant at the top or bottom ... slides / wave pool: stages and hands out tubes and mats, positions each rider in the correct body posture, dispatches at safe intervals by sight and signal, catches and clears tubes at run-out, monitors wet slippery decks, and stops the attraction when a rider stalls.

Attendant at a family entertainment center or recreation area running powered equipment: go-karts, bumper boats/cars, laser tag, batting cages, driving-range dispensers, rental gear. Explains and demonstrates operation, fits helmets and buckles harnesses, starts and stops the track or machine, marshals the course and retrieves stalled karts/boats.

Traveling carnival / county-fair ride jock on a portable ride (Tilt-A-Whirl, Scrambler, portable Ferris wheel) set up on a fairground, parking lot or field: takes tickets, loads and unloads riders, manually latches and checks bars, runs the ride from a lever/panel while watching the crowd, ground and layout differing at every stop.

Operating or driving a passenger conveyance in a recreation area: ski-area chairlift/gondola attendant (start/stop, slow for loading, assist boarders), park tram, trackless train or skyride operator, or pilot of a tour/rental boat on facility grounds, carrying the public on a fixed route with narration and boarding supervision.

roles.title: Costume Attendants
roles.description: Select, fit, and take care of costumes for cast members, and aid entertainers. May assist with multiple costume changes during performances.

tasks.label: Create worksheets for dressing lists, show notes, or costume checks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide dressing assistance to cast members or assign cast dressers to assist specific cast members with costume changes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quick change in the wings during a running live performance (musical, opera, dance): the dresser strips the performer out of one costume and into the next in 20–90 seconds in near-darkness and cramped quarters, handling zips, hook-and-eye closures, Velcro, quick-rig shoes, hats and body mic packs while the performer stands, breathes hard and then runs on stage.

Pre-show dressing in the dressing room: helping cast into base layers, corsets and lacing, period gowns, fitted jackets, tights, boots and gloves; smoothing, fastening, checking that everything is secure and correct against the costume plot before places is called.

Film/TV/commercial work on a studio lot: dressing actors in a costume trailer or on a soundstage and making continuity adjustments between takes (re-tucking, re-pinning, re-buttoning, straightening collars and hems) on the actor's body under time pressure from the AD.

Dressing in non-standard spaces: outdoor location shoots, parade or festival marshalling tents, hotel-room and school-gym changing areas for touring or industrial shows, where layout, lighting, weather and available surfaces differ every time.

Specialty and heavy rigs: getting a performer into a mascot/character suit, animal costume, armor, padding, or a costume worn over a flying harness or prosthetic; typically two dressers, plus safety and sightline checks before the performer moves.

Wardrobe supervisor work: building the dresser-to-cast-member track plot for a show, briefing and assigning dressers to specific performers and changes, then directing them live during the run and reassigning or stepping in when a change goes wrong.

sources.system: CMU 'One Policy To Dress Them All' robot-assisted dressing system (robot arm + learned RL policy)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute (Wang, Sun, Erickson, Held)
sources.title: CMU Robot Puts on Shirts One Sleeve at a Time — Robotics Institute, Carnegie Mellon University
sources.claim: Frontier robot-assisted dressing: a learned policy on a robot arm pulled a garment sleeve onto seated participants' arms, covering on average 86% of arm length across 510 trials with 17 participants and five garments in a lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing of a person with a garment. It is the closest analog to a costume attendant dressing a performer (deformable garment manipulated onto a live human body), so its limits — one loose sleeve, one seated cooperative arm, no fastenings — bound what is possible on costume dressing.

sources.system: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University (Hao, Wang, Ravie, Hegde, Held, Erickson)
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions (CoRL 2025 project page)
sources.claim: State of the art as of CoRL 2025 is still a single-arm system pulling a sleeve onto a person's arm in a laboratory, the new contribution being tolerance of limb motion and visual occlusion; no full-garment donning or fastening is shown.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assisted dressing of a moving human limb, the sub-skill most relevant to helping a performer into a costume; it establishes that the 2025 frontier is a single sleeve in a lab, far short of a whole costume change.

sources.system: Bimanual robot-assisted dressing, spherical-coordinate GMM/GMR strategy
sources.developer: University of York and Honda Research Institute EU (Zhao, Lian, Tyrrell, Gienger, Zhu)
sources.title: Bimanual Robot-Assisted Dressing: A Spherical Coordinate-Based Strategy for Tight-Fitting Garments (arXiv:2508.12274)
sources.claim: Tight-fitting garments defeat single-arm dressing robots; a 2025 bimanual strategy for tight garments is validated only in laboratory experiments with learned trajectories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: donning tight garments on a human limb. Theatrical costumes (corseted bodices, fitted period jackets, dance unitards) are tight-fitting, so this result shows the very garment class costume attendants handle remains unsolved even in the lab.

tasks.label: Arrange costumes in order of use to facilitate quick-change procedures for performances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Live theater (Broadway/regional musical): after laundry and repairs, the attendant re-hangs each performer's costume pieces on that performer's dressing-room rack and on the offstage rolling racks in the show's running order, grouping each 'look' (garment, undergarments, shoes, accessories) together and labeling positions by scene and track.

Presetting a quick-change booth or wing station before a performance: each piece hung on a numbered hook in exact order, garments pre-rigged (zippers open, sleeves inside-out, socks in shoes), shoes toed out, hat/wig/gloves placed within arm's reach on a small shelf in a cramped, dimly lit drape booth adjacent to the stage.

Film/TV production: costumer sorts the day's costumes onto labeled racks in a wardrobe trailer or costume department by character, scene number and shooting order, keeping continuity sets and doubles together so pieces can be pulled fast between setups.

Theme park, cruise ship or Las Vegas resident show wardrobe room: high-volume, repeated nightly with a stable running order and standardized, tagged stock; attendant restages dozens of tracked costume sets on racks in order of use for each show cycle.

School, community, dance recital or one-night touring stop: costumes arranged in order of use on a few portable rails in a makeshift backstage (gym, cafeteria, tent, unfamiliar venue), with pieces arriving in hampers and the layout different each time.

sources.date: 2020-06-15 (product page; systems in commercial service for years)
sources.title: Laundry Sorting System: the Sorting you Need with Dispatch - Metalprogetti
sources.claim: Commercial dispatch/sorting conveyors for hanging garments automatically store and then release garments to reproduce a customer's required output order, including putting them in a specified sequence and grouping several garments together.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sequencing hanging garments in a laundry/dry-cleaning plant. The objects are the same class (garments on hangers on rails), the required precision is the same (correct garment in the correct rail position/sequence), and the deliverable is identical to a costume rack put in running order.

sources.title: Softrol Garment Sortation Systems | Laundry Ledger
sources.claim: Fully automated garment sortation systems are installed in industrial laundries: RFID is scanned at speed, garments are conveyed, buffered, sorted and delivered as completed per-wearer bundles at 6,000-12,000 garments/hour with one or two operators monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated final sort of tagged garments into per-wearer bundles. Costume attendants likewise group each performer's tagged pieces and order them; identification is by tag/RFID in both cases, and accuracy near 100% matches or exceeds hand sorting.

sources.date: vendor brochure, in commercial use as of 2025
sources.title: Garment on Hanger System (Dematic brochure)
sources.claim: Garment-on-hanger warehouse systems sequence hanging apparel automatically into a required delivery order by route, department, size and style, with precise spacing on the rail.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sequencing hanging garments on overhead rails in a distribution centre. Same object class (garments on hangers), same output (a rail in a prescribed order); ordering by a data-defined key transfers directly to ordering by scene/running order.

sources.title: Nimble - Fully Autonomous Fulfillment
sources.claim: A commercial robotic fulfillment operator picks apparel, lingerie, footwear and accessories fully autonomously in purpose-built robotic fulfillment cells for named brand customers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous piece-picking of soft goods, footwear and accessories into sequenced orders. Costume ordering also requires grouping non-hanging pieces (shoes, gloves, small accessories) with the right look; object class and required placement precision are comparable in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: ALOHA Unleashed: A Simple Recipe for Robot Dexterity
sources.claim: An end-to-end learned bimanual policy autonomously flattens a shirt, picks a hanger off a rack, inserts it into the collar and hangs the shirt back on the rack, in a fixed two-arm tabletop workcell, with 75% success on the easy variant and 70% on the messy variant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing a garment onto a hanger and onto a rack, the manipulation core of arranging costumes on a rail. It shows the manipulation is possible in a fixtured cell but only at ~70-75% per attempt, below theatrical-wardrobe reliability.

sources.title: Video: Figure's humanoid robots organize room, hang clothes, and make bed without humans
sources.claim: Two humanoids running a single learned vision-language-action policy autonomously reset a staged bedroom, hanging up a coat, tidying objects and making a bed in ... two minutes, without teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hanging a coat and tidying garments in an as-found room. It marks the frontier of mobile garment handling outside fixtured cells - single coarse hangs in a staged room - and does not show identification and ordered staging of many specific costume pieces.

tasks.label: Design or construct costumes or send them to tailors for construction, major repairs, or alterations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-house alterations and major repairs on existing costumes in a theater/opera/studio wardrobe or costume shop: opening and re-stitching seams to take in or let out a bodice, re-hemming a skirt or trousers to a pinned line, replacing a broken zipper or hooks, patching a torn velvet gown or a stretch dance unitard, pressing and finishing. Garments are one-off, already assembled, of mixed fabrics, and must be returned show-ready.

Constructing a new costume in the shop from a design or rented pattern: drafting or draping the pattern, cutting fashion fabric, lining and interfacing, machine and hand sewing, inserting boning/closures/linings, adjusting after a fitting, finishing and pressing. Each garment is bespoke, in materials chosen for the production (brocade, sequinned stretch, wool, leather-look).

Designing costumes for a production: research, sketches/renderings, pulling and selecting fabric swatches, draping muslin mock-ups on a dress form, and presenting the design for approval by the designer or director.

Routing garments out to an outside tailor, draper, or costume house: pulling the identified costume piece, attaching the work ticket describing the construction/alteration required, bagging or boxing it, and dispatching it for courier pickup or delivery; receiving and checking the returned work.

Costume crafts and non-garment construction or major repair in the shop: millinery, thermoplastic or foam armor pieces, dyeing and distressing, appliqué and trim application, shoe modification, rebuilding headdresses and masks.

sources.system: Siemens/Sewbo robotic sewing workcell (denim deployment with Levi's, Bluewater Defense)
sources.title: A Deployment Case Study in Robotic Apparel Automation: Digital Twin Integration, Interoperability, and Workforce Enablement
sources.claim: A robotic sewing cell integrating a collaborative robot with conventional ..., suction fixtures and stiffened pieces was piloted on a denim factory floor, automating individual sub-operations (2D back-pocket subassembly, 3D shaping seams) at ~180 s per trial and 90% trial success — not whole-garment or bespoke construction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory garment sewing. It is the closest robotic analogue to costume construction/alteration; cited to show the state of the art is product-specific sub-operations on pre-cut, stiffened flat pieces in a fixtured cell, not bespoke 3D garment work.

sources.title: Sewbots® – Softwear Automation
sources.claim: Softwear Automation's commercial Sewbot workline autonomously sews T-shirts from cut fabric in a machine-vision workline; its installed base is standardized, high-volume products (T-shirts, towels, bath and car mats), each with a product-specific workline.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated apparel manufacturing. Cited to test whether garment construction could be done at E1; the system builds one standardized product per purpose-built workline, so it does not cover one-off costume construction in mixed materials.

sources.system: Robotic bottom-hemming cell (bimanual robot + automatic bottom hemmer)
sources.developer: Siemens Technology / USC / Henderson Sewing (ARM Institute project)
sources.title: Invigorating an Established Yet Fragile Textile Industry | Manufacturing USA
sources.claim: An ARM Institute project demonstrated a bimanual robot picking a T-shirt from a stack, reshaping it, and feeding it into a dedicated automatic bottom hemmer — a single hemming operation on a standardized knit garment inside a purpose-built station.

tasks.label: Examine costume fit on cast members and sketch or write notes for alterations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Regional theater/opera/dance costume shop fitting: performer stands on a fitting platform in the shop's fitting room wearing a built or pulled costume (period gown, doublet, tailored coat); the attendant checks shoulder set, waist, hem and closure, pins and chalks the take-ins and hem line, and writes an alteration note on the fitting sheet with photos.

Film/TV or commercial production fitting in a costume trailer or production fitting room: several looks per actor in a short session, garments off the rack or from stock, attendant checks fit over the actor's body and undergarments, pins sleeve and trouser lengths, and writes/sketches alteration notes for the on-set tailor.

Quick fit check backstage during tech/dress rehearsal or a pre-show call: cramped dressing room or wings, partially costumed performer under time pressure and low light, attendant spots a gaping neckline, tight armhole or dragging hem, marks it with a pin or safety pin and notes the overnight alteration.

Theme park, cruise ship or touring show wardrobe: high-volume fitting of standardized character/show costumes on newly cast performers or replacements, checking sizing against inventory, hem and take-in needs, and logging alteration notes into the wardrobe tracking system.

Movement-tested fitting for dance, aerial, stunt or quick-change costumes in a rehearsal studio or shop: performer executes choreography, lifts, or a quick-change while the attendant observes binding, riding up, and closure failure, then notes gusset, stretch panel, or rigging alterations.

sources.title: Euveka Launches Morphable Robot Mannequins
sources.claim: Euveka's commercially sold robot mannequin morphs a mechanized form to a scanned person's parameters so pattern makers can prototype garments in the client's size; the machine reproduces morphologies but does not itself evaluate a costume on a cast member or produce alteration notes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is garment prototyping on a shape-shifting form. It does not transfer: the robot changes its own shape to preset measurements rather than examining how a specific costume fits a live performer, and it outputs no alteration notes.

sources.developer: MIT Self-Assembly Lab with Ministry of Supply
sources.title: Video: Heat-gun-toting robot could create bespoke clothing on the cheap
sources.claim: MIT Self-Assembly Lab and Ministry of Supply demonstrated a six-axis robot arm that heat-shrinks a knit dress to a wearer's measurements; the arm alters the garment on a form to preset targets rather than examining fit on a person and recording alterations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated custom fitting of a knit garment. It does not transfer: the robot works to numeric measurements on a form in a lab cell, performs no visual/tactile fit assessment on a wearer, and produces no alteration notes for a tailor.

sources.title: Safe Robot-Assisted Dressing via Multi-Modal Sensing
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing remains a laboratory research problem focused on safely pulling a garment onto a human limb with force limits, not on assessing garment fit or specifying alterations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is manipulating clothing on a human body, the nearest robotic contact-with-worn-garment capability. It does not transfer: the goal is donning a simple garment on a limb in a lab, with no fit evaluation, pinning, marking, or alteration note output.

sources.system: 3D body scanning booths (e.g., TG3D static booth) and app-based measurement extraction
sources.title: Best 3D Body Scanners for 2026: How to Choose the Right Solution for Your Business
sources.claim: Current commercial fit-capture technology for apparel is static scanning hardware plus software (no moving parts, measurement extraction), and made-to-measure workflows still require human verification and hand measurements before a fitting decision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is capturing body dimensions for garment making. It does not transfer and is not a robotic system: it is sensing plus software with no moving parts, it measures the body rather than an already-worn costume, and it issues no alteration instructions.

tasks.label: Distribute costumes or related equipment and keep records of item status.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Live theater/opera/dance production: before a performance the wardrobe attendant pulls each performer's costume pieces (garments on hangers plus shoes, hats, undergarments, mic belts) from stock racks and sets them at that performer's named dressing-room station in wear order; after the show collects pieces and notes missing/damaged/soiled items on the run sheet or wardrobe database. Backstage dressing rooms and wardrobe room of a theater controlled by the producing company.

Film/TV production on a studio lot or soundstage: costumer distributes each principal's and background player's set-up for the day to trailers, holding, or the fitting room, matched to continuity notes, and logs each item's status (issued, worn, aged, damaged, returned to stock) in the costume inventory/continuity records.

Film/TV production on location: costumer distributes costumes and accessories to background actors and cast from a truck or tented holding area at an outdoor/found location (street, field, warehouse, park), issues and collects sized pieces on the fly in weather and crowding, and logs sign-out/return per person.

Theme park, cruise line, casino or large venue costuming: issue-window distribution of standardized stock costumes to hundreds of cast members per shift - retrieve the correct garment pieces in the employee's assigned sizes, hand them over, scan barcode/RFID to record the checkout, and log returns and soiled/damaged items at the return window.

Costume shop or rental house: pull and assemble costume packages for a production or rental client from stock (hanging garments, accessory boxes), tag/bag them, check them out against an inventory database, then receive returns and record condition, cleaning, and repair status.

Bulk distribution within the venue: moving loaded costume racks, hampers and bins of accessories/equipment from the wardrobe department to dressing rooms, quick-change stations, or a rehearsal hall elsewhere in the building, and recording what was delivered where.

tasks.label: Clean and press costumes before and after performances and perform any minor repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-performance wash-and-dry loads in the venue's wardrobe laundry room: gathering sweat-soaked washables (shirts, socks, tights, dance belts, underdressings, aprons), sorting by color/fabric, pretreating, running domestic or small commercial washers and dryers, hanging or laying flat to dry, returning items to the right actor's rack overnight.

Pre-performance steaming and pressing of standard costume pieces: running a hand steamer over dresses, coats and trousers hanging on rolling racks, and pressing shirts, collars, aprons and pleats on an ironing board with correct heat and pressing cloth, so garments look crisp under stage lights.

Minor repairs at the wardrobe table between or after shows: replacing lost buttons, snaps and hook-and-eye tape, restitching a split seam or dropped hem on an assembled 3-D garment, tacking down trim, beads or feathers, matching thread and stitch to the costume, often on boned or lined pieces.

Spot-cleaning and refreshing non-washable, embellished or built costumes: sponging makeup, blood, food or sweat marks from sequined, beaded, leather, fur or corseted pieces, alcohol/vodka spray to deodorize, brushing and airing, hand-washing delicates in a sink.

Emergency clean/press/repair under time pressure during a run or on tour: a quick steam or stitch in a cramped dressing room, quick-change booth or location trailer between scenes, working around the performer's schedule and in unfamiliar rooms with whatever kit is on hand.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sewing of fabric. Cited for the limit of transfer: the cell joins flat cut panels of known geometry in a fixture, whereas costume repair means diagnosing damage and stitching a specific spot on an assembled, three-dimensional garment.

tasks.label: Collaborate with production designers, costume designers, or other production staff to discuss and execute costume design details.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fitting call in a theater/studio costume shop: with the costume designer present, the attendant puts the build or pulled garment on the actor, discusses silhouette, hem and sleeve length, closure placement and comfort, then pins, chalks and tapes the changes on the body, records the notes, and dresses/undresses the actor between looks.

Pre-production wardrobe room: working from the designer's sketches, swatch boards and costume plot, the attendant pulls, sources and assembles complete looks (garments, undergarments, shoes, hats, jewelry) from stock, rentals and purchases, checks each piece against the design and the actor's measurements, labels and racks them by character and scene, and flags gaps or mismatches back to the designer.

Costume shop bespoke execution of design notes on one-off costumes: shortening hems, taking in seams, adding trim or appliqué), rigging quick-change closures (snaps, hooks, velcro, breakaway seams), aging/distressing fabric, hand-sewing on delicate or embellished goods, then presenting the result to the designer for approval and rework.

Repetitive spec sewing for an ensemble: the designer specifies one uniform detail repeated across many identical simple pieces (e.g., hem a run of matching skirts, sashes or aprons to a set length, topstitch matching bands) on flat, plain fabric with straight seams and a single measurement.

On set or on location for film, TV or a live event: between takes or during a tech rehearsal the attendant confers with the costume designer, script supervisor or director and immediately executes the fix \piece, re-pinning a drape, steaming, adding dirt or blood, re-rigging a fastener \time time pather pressure, amid crew, cables, weather and moving equipment.

Production/design meeting and paperwork: attends meetings with the costume designer, director and stage management to discuss the costume plot, quick-change logistics, track assignments and budget, then updates change sheets and briefs the dressers.

sources.system: π0 (pi-zero) generalist policy on mobile and bimanual arm platforms
sources.title: π0: Our First Generalist Policy
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0 policy, fine-tuned for laundry, autonomously unloads a dryer and folds clothing into a stack — the current frontier of autonomous deformable-garment manipulation, limited to folding/tidying rather than fitting, altering or assembling costumes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laundry folding. It shows robots can grasp and manipulate limp cloth autonomously, but the objects are simple knit garments handled on an empty table, with no measurement, no sewing, no fitting to a person and no conformance check against a design; it does not transfer to executing costume design details.

sources.claim: ARM Institute robotic sewing projects (Siemens, Sewbo, Henderson Sewing, ISAIC, Bluewater Defense) demonstrated robotic hemming, pocket setting and curved stitching, and built denim pants with closed-loop visual servoing in a purpose-built cell at the Levi Strauss Innovation ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: apparel manufacturing sewing. Hemming flat cut panels to a fixed spec in a fixtured cell is comparable in material and operation to hemming a run of identical simple ensemble pieces, so it transfers to that narrow slice; it does not cover alterations on constructed, embellished one-off costumes.

It picks known catalog items presented in bins inside a caged cell; assembling a costume look requires judging period, color, texture, size and character fit against a designer's sketch and flagging mismatches, which is not substantiated by SKU-based picking.

Getting a sleeve onto a cooperative user in a lab is far below fitting-room work — pinning, chalking and tape-marking a garment on a live actor to a designer's verbal direction — so it does not substantiate the fitting instance at any tier.

tasks.label: Monitor, maintain, or secure inventories of costumes, wigs, or makeup, providing keys or access to assigned directors, costume designers, or wardrobe mistresses/masters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic physical inventory/audit of costume, wig, and accessory stock in a theater, opera, or studio wardrobe storage room: walking dense racks and shelves, counting and locating pieces against the inventory list, flagging missing or misplaced items and updating the stock record.

End-of-day securing of the wardrobe department: putting costumes, wigs, jewelry and makeup into cabinets, cases and locked rooms, locking up, and issuing/collecting keys or coded access for the director, costume designer, or wardrobe supervisor who needs entry after hours.

Monitoring and restocking consumables and small stock: makeup, brushes, wig supplies, hosiery, undergarments, dress shields; counting what is left, pulling replacements from supply stock, and refilling individual performer kits, drawers and bins.

Post-performance check-in of costumes and wigs: receiving pieces from dressers/dressing rooms, verifying each unit is complete, and returning garments to their assigned hanging/shelf location in stock (or to laundry/repair) so the inventory stays accurate.

Touring production or location shoot: inventorying and securing costume stock in road trunks, hampers, costume trailers and temporary backstage/holding spaces that differ at every stop, packing/unpacking and locking cases, controlling who has access.

Attendant loads a van or car with racks, garment bags and boxes, drives across town to a costume/prop rental house or lending theater, unloads at their door or dock, and completes the return with their staff.

Small ad hoc returns: handing borrowed jackets, jewelry, dance shoes or a wig back to an individual performer, another department (props/hair) or another company, and putting the show's own leftover pieces back into labeled bins on the stock shelves.

instances.label: Theatre/opera/dance company costume shop: periodic inventory of the stock room — hundreds of untagged garments, hats, shoes and accessories on crowded rolling racks and in bins. Attendant pulls each piece, identifies garment type/period/size, inspects condition (seams, hems, closures, stains, moth damage), logs it in the stock database and re-hangs it.

Backstage wardrobe room, post-performance or end-of-run check-in: every returned costume piece is counted against the costume plot and inspected for sweat, stains, popped seams, lost trim and broken closures; items are flagged for repair, laundering or replacement on the run sheet.

Film/TV production: inventorying racks, hampers and boxes of purchased, rented and pulled costumes in a costume trailer, base-camp tent or rented storage space on location; recording item, size, source and post-shoot condition, with layout and lighting different at each site.

Theme park, cruise line or other large costuming operation: cycle count / stock check of thousands of RFID-tagged costume pieces on issue-room racks and in bulk storage, to determine which types and sizes are on hand and where, reconciling against the costuming system.

Costume rental house or university/regional stock: pre-production stock survey — walking the racks to determine what period, color, size and serviceable-condition pieces exist for an upcoming show, producing an availability/pull report for the designer.

instances.label: Theater/opera/cruise-showroom dressing rooms after and between performances: collect worn costumes from chairs, hooks and floor, re-hang each on the correct performer's labeled rack, bag items for laundry, wipe makeup counters and mirrors, restock tissues/hangers/supplies, empty trash and sweep so the room is set for the next call.

Wardrobe stock/costume storage room upkeep: keep hanging stock on rolling racks in order by show, character and size; return costumes to their bays and pull them again; keep shoes, hats and accessories in labeled bins on shelves; keep garment bags, dust covers and aisles in order and inventory locations accurate.

Wardrobe laundry area upkeep: sort soiled costumes into loads by fabric and color, run washers/dryers, hang or fold clean items and get them back to their racks, empty lint traps, wipe machines and counters, keep detergent, hangers and supplies stocked and the room clear of piles.

Theme park or large-production costuming facility: assign lockers to cast/crew and keep locker rooms in order — clean floors, benches and mirrors, empty trash, restock supplies, clear costumes and personal items left behind, re-label/re-key lockers as people rotate on and off shows.

Wig room upkeep: keep wigs on labeled blocks/stands, store hairpieces and falls in their boxes, sanitize brushes, combs and tools, wipe the styling station, manage pins, nets and product stock, and keep the ventilated area clean.

Film/TV location work: keep the wardrobe trailer or a temporary dressing/holding area orderly — set up and re-stow racks, bins and steamers in a cramped, changing space, keep continuity items separated, tidy and pack out at wrap.

Transfer: the objects are the same (garments on hangers), and the function — keeping a hanging stock in a known, retrievable, labeled order and returning/pulling items — is the substance of maintaining a costume storage area, here done in a purpose-built (E1) structure.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model

Transfer: supports the folding step of laundry-area work at a machine-presented station, but it is a stationary single-skill station and does not cover loading machines, putting stock away or cleaning the room.

It covers only the surface-cleaning slice of locker-room upkeep; it does not open or clear lockers, collect left-behind costumes, restock supplies or assign lockers, so it cannot complete that instance.

sources.title: Avidbots - Robotics 24/7

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hard-floor cleaning in structured human facilities. It shows only floor cleaning transfers to dressing/locker/wig rooms; it performs no object handling, so it cannot complete room-reset instances that centre on collecting and re-hanging costumes and tidying stations.

sources.title: Newly unveiled Isaac 1 humanoid can fold laundry and clean your home

sources.transferJustification: Related task: whole-room tidying and putting items away. It is the closest analogue to dressing-room and wig-room reset, but it relies on human teleoperation fallback and deliveries are only scheduled for fall 2026, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Watch A New Humanoid Robot Clean A Hotel Room Like It Owns The Place

sources.transferJustification: Related task: hotel guest-room turnaround (picking up towels/clothes, restocking, cleaning). Autonomy rests on a vendor video from a months-old startup with no independent deployment evidence, so it is treated as unverified and cannot substantiate dressing- or locker-room upkeep.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid - The Robot Report
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, the leading consumer tidying robot, depends on teleoperation rather than autonomy for household chores as of late 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household tidying and putting clothes away. Confirms that mobile manipulators handling mixed garments and clutter in rooms built for people are still teleoperated, supporting negative judgments for dressing-room, wig-room and trailer upkeep.
