Run the cleaning cycle for flat non-clothing textiles: sort soiled table skirts, linens, flags and banners, wash and dry (or send for dry clean), then fold to a standard and shelve/inventory them in wardrobe stock.

Repair damaged non-clothing items in the costume shop: restitch a torn flag seam or blown drapery hem, patch a burn or hole in velour, replace grommets, ties, snaps, hook-and-loop or pleater tape on a table skirt or drape; hand and machine sewing on an existing, non-fixtured item.

Inspect items between uses, spot-treat stains (makeup, food, beverage, mud) by hand with solvent/spotting agents, deodorize and refresh, then fold or roll and pack into hampers, bins or road cases for storage or touring; unpack and re-inventory on the other end.

On-site handling of heavy hanging goods at the venue: hang/rig stage draperies, legs and borders on battens or pipe, skirt and clip banquet or set-dressing tables, mount and dress flags and bunting, then steam them in place with a wand steamer on a ladder or lift.

instances.label: Routine floor care in a health club, spa, hotel, school/university athletic facility, retail fitting-room area or theater coatroom: sweeping, dust-mopping, vacuuming carpet, and damp-mopping or auto-scrubbing the hard tile/rubber/vinyl floors of the locker room, changing area and adjacent corridors, usually overnight or during off-peak hours.

Cleaning and disinfecting the restroom fixtures inside the locker/changing room: toilets, urinals, wash basins, vanity counters and mirrors, plus mopping the floor around those fixtures, on a daily or several-times-per-day cycle.

Cleaning wet areas: scrubbing shower stalls and their walls/floors, whirlpool and steam-room surfaces, sauna benches, tile grout, and clearing hair from floor drains — reaching into confined, wet, vertical surfaces with brushes, hoses and squeegees.

Collecting used towels, discarded wraps and litter from floors, benches and lockers, emptying towel hampers and trash receptacles, hauling them to laundry/dumpster, and restocking paper goods, soap and amenities.

Wiping and disinfecting benches, locker exteriors and handles, vanity counters, hair-dryer stations, mirrors and door hardware, plus spot cleanup of spills, wet footprints and hair during operating hours with patrons present in the room.

instances.label: Health-club / country-club / campus rec-center locker room towel desk: a stream of members arrives at the counter, presents a card or membership check, and the attendant pulls one or more clean folded bath or workout towels off the stack, hands them over, verifies entitlement, and drops returned towels in the hamper.

Day spa, Korean/Turkish bathhouse or hotel wet-area linen station: guest checks in at the counter and is issued a towel set, wrap sheet, or robe from shelved linen; attendant selects the right sizes and items and hands them to the guest before they enter the baths.

In-area linen service inside the wet zone: attendant carries fresh towels and sheets into steam rooms, sauna anterooms and wet lounges, hands warm towels or wrap sheets to bathers, spreads a fresh sheet on a bench or table, and picks up discarded linen; hot, humid, slippery floors, undressed patrons moving about.

Restocking and clearing: attendant wheels carts of clean folded linen from the laundry and refills towel bins and shelves at the locker room, sauna entrance, shower area and pool deck, then collects soiled towels from hampers, benches and wet floors and carts them back; done between rushes with members present.

Upscale restroom attendant (hotel, casino, club, stadium): hands each patron a folded linen or paper hand towel at the sink, takes the used towel into a hamper, and keeps the towel stock and counter replenished and tidy through unpredictable, sometimes crowded traffic.

On-request delivery: a guest at a poolside lounge chair, cabana, dressing room or guest room asks for extra towels or a fresh sheet, and the attendant fetches them from the linen store and brings them to the guest where they are.

sources.title: Helix Learns to Fold Laundry
sources.claim: Figure's Helix VLA model drives a humanoid to pick individual towels from a mixed pile, fold them and stack them in a basket fully autonomously at a fixed workstation - the deformable-linen handling underlying issuing a towel from a stack.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laundry folding. It shows the hard part of towel service - separating one towel from a pile of deformable cloth and presenting it neatly - but only at a fixed table with the linen presented to the robot.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model Offering Fully Autonomous, Round-the-Clock Dexterity
sources.claim: DYNA-1 ran stationary dual arms folding restaurant napkins continuously for over 24 hours with no human intervention, showing sustained, worker-rate separation and folding of individual cloth items in a purpose-built workcell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: napkin folding in a fixed two-arm cell. Comparable objects (small linen), comparable precision, and it demonstrates the reliability needed to hand out linen - but only with the linen brought to the machine.

sources.system: ICON Automatic Hard Roll Towel Dispenser
sources.title: Kimberly-Clark Professional ICON Automatic Hard Roll Towel Dispenser (58750)
sources.claim: Motorized touchless hand-towel dispensers physically feed and cut a towel for each restroom user from a roll pre-loaded into the machine's magazine; they are standard commercial restroom equipment.

sources.title: Towel dispenser - Roommatik
sources.claim: A commercial self-service towel dispenser for pools, spas and gyms identifies the guest and delivers a clean towel from compartments that staff have pre-loaded one towel at a time; it also takes the towel back and reconciles the count.

sources.title: Policies | UConn Recreation
sources.claim: Towel Tracker RFID kiosks are installed in US university recreation-center locker rooms to issue and take back towels in place of a staffed towel desk; the machine unlocks a stocked compartment and the patron removes the towel themselves.

sources.title: RFID Captures Each Time Guests Throw in the Towel
sources.claim: RFID Journal's account of the same kiosk confirms the machine only releases a door lock and the user physically removes the towel - the machine does not handle the linen.

sources.title: Next-gen room service: How Relay 2 robots are revolutionizing the hotel experience | FOX 5 New York
sources.claim: Relay 2 autonomously navigates hotel corridors and elevators to bring room towels and bed linen to guests, but hotel staff must load the item into the robot's bin.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guest-room amenity delivery in a hotel. It covers only the transport leg of bringing towels to a client; the towel is retrieved from the linen store and loaded by a person.

sources.system: PF Series Commercial Small Piece Folder
sources.title: Commercial Small Piece Folder | PF Series | B&C Technologies
sources.claim: Commercial small-piece folders take towels fed onto a conveyor and automatically fold, sort by size and stack them ready for use - deployed laundry equipment producing the stacked towel supply.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: folding and stacking towels in a laundry. It substantiates producing and stacking the clean towel supply when linen is fed to the machine, i.e. restocking under E1 presentation, not carting and shelving linen in a locker room.

tasks.label: Collect soiled linen or clothing for laundering.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Health club / fitness center locker room: attendant circulates through the men's and women's locker rooms during and after peak hours, empties towel hampers, picks wet used towels off benches, shower floors and sink counters, ties off liner bags, loads them into a rolling laundry cart and wheels the cart to the on-site laundry room or dock. Members are undressing and moving through the space throughout.

Spa, resort or country club locker room and treatment area: attendant gathers used robes, slippers, bath sheets, hand towels and treatment-table linens from cubbies, hooks, hampers and treatment rooms, keeps damaged or heavily stained luxury items separate for spotting, and moves the sorted bundles to the laundry or to the linen service pickup point.

Athletic team locker room (high school, college or professional): after practice or a game the attendant collects uniforms, practice jerseys, compression gear, socks, jocks and towels from the floor, benches and individual lockers, sorts them by garment type/player or into mesh loop bags, and carts the heavily soiled, sweat- and mud-laden load to the team laundry room.

Hospital, clinic or industrial plant changing room: attendant empties soiled scrub and uniform bins, records or scans returns against issued items, bags the contaminated garments per infection-control rules, and moves the bagged load to the soiled-linen holding room for the contract laundry pickup.

Theater, arena or entertainment venue dressing room: after a performance the attendant collects costumes, undergarments, dance tights and towels from racks, chairs and the floor, checks pockets and pinned areas, separates wash-at-venue items from dry-clean-only pieces, and bags or racks them for the laundry or cleaner.

sources.title: THOR I Robot Separator - Single Piece Separation of Laundry
sources.claim: Inwatec's THOR robot separator autonomously grips and separates bulk-fed soiled textiles — garments, towels and linen — on the soiled side of an industrial laundry at 1,200-1,500 pieces/hour, replacing the manual sorting of dirty laundry for washing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: soiled-side sorting in a commercial laundry. It is the same physical act as the attendant's collection step — grasping limp, wet, crumpled towels, robes and garments out of a bulk pile and routing each to the wash — on the same objects, with no greater precision demanded.

sources.title: Building the future of laundry robotics with Elastic | Elastic Blog
sources.claim: THOR soiled-laundry sorting robots are in commercial service, with over 100 Inwatec robots deployed at laundries worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (soiled-side separation and sorting); this item establishes that the systems are deployed in production laundries rather than being demos.

sources.system: Inwatec automatic soiled workwear sorting (robot separator + X-ray + vision sorting)
sources.title: Fully automatic sorting of Soiled Workwear | Inwatec
sources.claim: Inwatec's fully automatic soiled-workwear line takes conveyor-fed dirty garments, separates them one by one with a robot, X-rays them to reject items containing pens, scissors or other foreign objects, and vision-sorts the accepted garments by category.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: soiled workwear/uniform intake. It matches the attendant's collection of soiled clothing (scrubs, uniforms, costumes) including the pocket/pin check, since the X-ray stage performs the same foreign-object screening the worker does by hand.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots at Froedtert Hospital pick up, transport and drop ... heavy carts loaded with soiled linens and waste through hospital corridors and elevators; the carts are loaded by staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-facility soiled-linen logistics. It covers only the haul-to-laundry leg of the instance; the robot has no manipulator and cannot empty hampers or gather loose towels, so it cannot complete the instance in an E2 locker room.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi is a mobile manipulator deployed in over 25 U.S. hospitals with more than 1.25 million autonomous ...; its listed jobs include fetching supplies, delivering lab samples and removing soiled linen bags staged for it, not emptying hampers or gathering loose textiles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital soiled-linen bag removal by a mobile manipulator in an E2 corridor. It is the closest deployed E2 system to this task, but it handles prepared bags at fixed staging points rather than collecting soiled textiles from bins, benches and floors.

sources.title: Watch A New Humanoid Robot Clean A Hotel Room Like It Owns The Place
sources.claim: Zerith H1, a wheeled humanoid for hotel housekeeping, was shown in a company video tossing used towels into a laundry hamper and restocking a hotel bathroom; independent trade coverage in 2026 still describes it as an early-stage pilot rather than a staff replacement, and autonomy for the towel-handling segment is asserted only by the vendor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hotel housekeeping textile pickup in an institution-controlled room (E2). Autonomy of the towel-handling segment is not independently established and the system is a pilot, so it cannot support a positive E2 judgment.

sources.system: π0.5 (pi-0.5) on a mobile bimanual manipulator
sources.title: π0.5: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 model let a mobile manipulator autonomously place clothes in a laundry basket ... tidy in previously unseen real homes, but the developers state the policy is far from perfect and makes both semantic and motor errors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking loose clothing off floors and furniture into a laundry basket in an unfixtured room — the manipulation core of this task. Reliability is explicitly imperfect and the work is a research demo, so it does not meet worker-quality completion.

tasks.label: Maintain a lost-and-found collection.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Health club/spa or theater attendant receives an item turned in at the desk (jacket, water bottle, phone, gym bag, earbuds), records a description in the lost-and-found log or app, tags/bags it, and shelves it in the correct bin in the storage room or closet.

End-of-shift sweep: attendant walks the locker room, showers, benches, fitting rooms or coat racks, collecting garments, towels, toiletries and small items left behind on floors, hooks and in open lockers, and carries them to the lost-and-found area.

A patron reports a lost item; the attendant questions them, searches the shelves and bins (often digging through piled clothing) for a match, verifies ownership, hands the item over, and records the release; sometimes arranges shipping to an out-of-town owner.

Periodic purge/organization of the collection: pulling items past the hold period, laundering or bagging clothing, boxing items for donation or disposal, re-sorting and tidying the shelves, and reconciling the log.

Handling valuables and sensitive finds (wallets, cash, credit cards, jewelry, keys, phones, medication): separate documentation, securing in a locked drawer or safe, and handoff to a manager or security with chain-of-custody records.

sources.title: Amazon robot tests show they're not ready to replace humans (The Register)
sources.claim: Amazon's robotic stow workcells autonomously place diverse, previously unseen e-commerce items into cluttered fabric pod bins at rates approaching human stowers, in a real fulfillment-center deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse stow. Putting an unlabeled, arbitrary object (apparel, bottles, small electronics) into an assigned storage bin and registering its location is the physical core of logging and shelving a found item; objects and precision are comparable.

sources.title: Stow: Robotic Packing of Items into Fabric Pods (overview)
sources.claim: The same Amazon stow system reached over 85% success on diverse items in real-world deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse stow into cluttered soft bins, i.e. shelving a found item into a mixed lost-and-found bin.

sources.title: New Amazon robots fall short of human efficiency (Cybernews)
sources.claim: Amazon's companion robotic pick system retrieved requested individual items from cluttered pods with 91% success over a six-month deployment, rejecting about a fifth of requests to humans.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving one specified item from a cluttered mixed bin — the physical core of finding and pulling a claimed item out of a lost-and-found bin.

sources.title: Amazon's Vulcan robot uses force sensing to stow items (The Robot Report)
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot, with force-sensing end effectors, picks and stows about three quarters of warehouse inventory at human-comparable speed inside fulfillment-center workcells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dexterous stow/pick in packed soft bins; comparable to placing and extracting clothing and personal effects in packed lost-and-found bins.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics Introduces RightPick 4 System (Automation.com)
sources.claim: Commercial piece-picking cells handle items never seen before, including apparel, general merchandise and cosmetics, with reduced human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unstructured-mix piece picking. Lost-and-found items are unlabeled and heterogeneous, so generalization to unseen objects is the key transfer property.

sources.title: KNAPP and Covariant Partnership Advances AI Robotics for more Efficient Warehouses
sources.claim: KNAPP's Pick-it-Easy Robot running the Covariant Brain is deployed in customer warehouses (including GXO apparel operations) and grips items of widely varying shape, weight and packaging, including floppy polybagged apparel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: apparel piece picking. Garments are the most common lost-and-found item class, so demonstrated handling of loose/polybagged apparel transfers to sorting and storing found clothing.

sources.title: Business Talk AI: Let's talk about Artificial Intelligence for recycling with AMP Robotics
sources.claim: AMP's Cortex robots autonomously identify and sort mixed, uncatalogued material streams into separate destinations at high accuracy in over a hundred deployed facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: visual classification and sortation of arbitrary mixed objects into category bins — the physical core of purging a lost-and-found into donate/discard/keep streams.

sources.title: Cleveron 402 - Cleveron
sources.claim: Cleveron's robotic parcel machines autonomously accept deposited items, shelve them, reorganize storage, and dispense the right item to a claimant on code entry; they are in commercial retail use internationally.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated deposit, custody storage and verified release of individual items — the intake/claim loop of a lost-and-found, performed by a purpose-built machine.

sources.system: Assessment of current autonomous robots on household tidying and industrial tasks
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: An independent 2026 capability assessment finds household/facility manipulation tasks such as tidying a room (placing loose clothes and objects into their proper receptacles) are not commercially deployed, unlike navigation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous room tidying (picking loose clothing and objects off floors and furniture) — the same capability needed to sweep a locker room for left-behind items; cited to support a negative judgment only.

tasks.label: Clean and polish footwear, using brushes, sponges, cleaning fluid, polishes, waxes, liquid or sole dressing, and daubers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Country/golf club locker room: attendant collects members' leather golf shoes after a round, brushes grass and packed mud out of spike plates and welts, wipes uppers with sponge and cleaning fluid, applies polish/conditioner with a dauber, buffs to a shine, re-laces and returns the pair to the member's locker. Arbitrary brands, sizes, colors, soiling levels.

Golf/athletic club cleaning-only turnaround on heavily soiled golf or turf shoes: knock off and brush away mud and grass from outsole, cleats and sidewalls, wipe the upper, dry; no polish applied; shoes returned to lockers or bag storage before next play.

Private club, hotel or downtown athletic club valet shine service: guest's leather dress shoes (calfskin, cordovan, some suede) left overnight or for same-day service - clean with fluid, apply color-matched cream/wax polish with a dauber, buff to a high shine, dress edges and soles, return matched to the right locker or room.

Athletic equipment room / team locker room: equipment manager cleans players' training shoes, turf shoes and cleats after practice - scrub with brush and cleaning fluid, wipe, deodorize/disinfect, dry and re-rack for the next session, dozens of pairs a day.

Spa or health-club locker room: attendant wipes down and sanitizes loaner/rental footwear (sandals, slippers, court shoes) and gives members' shoes a quick wipe-and-buff on request, then restocks them by size.

sources.title: Nike B.I.L.L. Bot Initiated Longevity Lab — NIKE, Inc.
sources.claim: Nike's B.I.L.L. is an in-store robotic cell that, once a worn sneaker is loaded, 3D-scans it and cleans the upper, sidewalls and outsole with water-based cleaning products (about 45 minutes per pair); it ran as a public service pilot at Nike Town London on four sneaker models.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine cleaning of customers' worn sneakers. Same objects (used footwear), same operation (scrubbing uppers, sidewalls and outsoles with cleaning fluid), inside a purpose-built enclosure the shoe is loaded into - i.e. the cleaning half of this task.

sources.title: ClearX shoe-cleaning robot uses sensors to wash and dry footwear
sources.claim: Brolan's ClearX is a shoe-cleaning machine shown at CES 2026 that senses shoe material and soiling and then automatically washes, scrubs, dries and optionally disinfects footwear without operator guidance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cleaning and sanitizing of worn footwear placed into the machine; covers the cleaning and disinfecting operations of this task for athletic and loaner footwear.

sources.title: This robot will clean your shoes in just 90 minutes - Trusted Reviews
sources.claim: A follow-up demonstration at Beyond Expo 2026 showed the same Brolan shoe-cleaning robot running an unattended clean-and-dry cycle of roughly 90 minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cleaning of worn footwear loaded into an enclosure; supports the cleaning-only instances of this task.

sources.developer: Università Politecnica delle Marche with footwear manufacturer
sources.title: Smart Automation in Luxury Leather Shoe Polishing: A Human Centric Robotic Approach (arXiv 2411.09603)
sources.claim: A collaborative robotic polishing cell for luxury leather shoes - force-controlled manipulator with polishing tool, shoe-locking fixture and polish dispenser, trajectories authored per shoe model in CAM - was implemented on an industrial production line, but human operators still supervise and perform the final finishing that achieves the accepted appearance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying polish to leather shoe uppers under force control - same material, tool action and objects as shoe polishing, but on fixtured new shoes of pre-programmed models, and the accepted finish still requires a human pass.

sources.title: Human-Centered Design of a Collaborative Robotic System for the Shoe-Polishing Process (Machines 10(11):1082)
sources.claim: An earlier prototype of the same shoe-polishing cell (UR5e cobot, shoe-locking system, polish dispenser) polishes a fixtured leather shoe autonomously, but an operator supervises the pass, decides when to stop, and then performs light manual finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wax polishing of leather shoes held in a fixture; the closest published evidence to the polishing half of this task, and it stops short of a finished result.

sources.system: Cooperative human–robot leather shoe polishing (patina growing) cell
sources.developer: academic/industry collaboration published in Int. J. Adv. Manuf. Technol.
sources.title: Cooperative human–robot polishing for the task of patina growing on high-quality leather shoes
sources.claim: A robot performs leather-shoe patina/polishing passes autonomously once its path has been generated, with the human able to grasp the collaborative tool to redirect it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot applies polish/patina to leather shoe uppers in a fixtured cell - same objects and finishing action as this task's polishing step, though the path must be authored per shoe.

sources.system: Automatic shoe brush / motorized shoe cleaner machines
sources.title: Guide to Shoe Brush Machines - Liberty Industries
sources.claim: Commercially sold motorized shoe-brush machines run powered rotating brushes that scrub the soles and sides ... worn footwear at facility entrances (cleanrooms, plants).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-driven brushing of dirt off soles and sidewalls of worn shoes - the debris-removal step of cleaning golf and turf footwear, done by the machine rather than by hand.

tasks.label: Check supplies to ensure adequate availability, and order new supplies when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Health club / gym locker room attendant does the periodic par-level count in the back-of-house linen and supply room: stacks of clean towels on wire racks, cases of shampoo/soap/lotion, boxes of razors, combs, cups, tissue and cleaning chemicals on open shelving; compares counts to par, writes a shortage list and submits/places the order with the supplier or manager.

Health club / spa attendant does the daily walk-through of the locker room itself during operating hours with members present: checking wall-mounted shower dispensers, grooming-station amenity trays and jars, under-vanity cabinets, towel bins and the hair-dryer/toiletry counter, judging which items are running low and flagging what must be reordered.

Country club / resort spa locker room attendant inventories textiles and amenities: robes, slippers, towels, staff uniforms and prepackaged amenity kits held on storage-room shelving and carts (plus items out at laundry), records counts on a par sheet and places the vendor order.

Retail store fitting-room (dressing room) attendant checks fitting-room consumables — hangers, size dividers, return tags/tag rolls, garment bags, mirror wipes and cleaning supplies — held at the fitting-room counter and in stockroom bins, and requests or orders replenishment from the store's supply system.

Coatroom attendant at a theater, restaurant, hotel or club does a pre-shift supply check at the coat check station: hanger count on the rails, numbered claim tickets/tag rolls, garment and umbrella bags, chits and pens stored in the counter and closet; orders more tickets or hangers when stock is short.

sources.title: Simbe upgrades vision platform with AI-powered capabilities - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally is an autonomous mobile robot ... navigates a store on its own, scans shelves, and detects products running low before they go out of stock, generating proactive replenishment signals — the same perceive-stock-level-then-trigger-reorder loop the attendant performs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = retail shelf inventory audit. It transfers to an attendant's supply check because the objects are packaged consumer goods and stacked bulk items on shelving, the required precision is a coarse below-par/low-stock threshold rather than exact counts, and the environment is an indoor institution-controlled facility with people moving through it.

sources.title: How Simbe Robotics' retail robots help stores and brands - Fast Company
sources.claim: Tally robots autonomously navigate stores and scan shelves without human control, and the platform is fielded at scale across roughly a thousand stores on three continents.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (shelf/stock auditing); cited to establish that the autonomous inventory-checking capability is a fielded product rather than a one-off demo.

sources.title: Harmons Grocery rolls out Tally inventory robot in Utah stores as Simbe upgrades Vision platform - Retail Technology Innovation Hub
sources.claim: Deployed Tally robots perform daily automated scans that replace manual stock checks and include shelf-to-stockroom comparisons, i.e. they audit back-of-house stock levels as well as front-of-house displays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = stockroom/shelf stock audit replacing manual checks. Transfers to checking a linen or supply room because the same volumetric scanning of stacked goods on racks yields the below-par list that drives the reorder.

sources.system: Tally (Simbe Robotics) at BJ's Wholesale Club
sources.title: Simbe scales inventory robotics deal with BJ's Wholesale Club - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Tally has been rolled out chain-wide at 237 BJ's Wholesale Club ..., where it images bulk pallets and tall club shelving and reconciles counts against the inventory system while the sales floor is open to shoppers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = counting bulk cases/pallets of consumer goods. Bulk cases of towels, toiletries and paper goods in a club or gym storeroom are the same class of object at the same coarse counting precision.

sources.title: UPS deploys Verity warehouse drones for inventory tracking | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: Verity's autonomous inventory drones fly unattended inside a working distribution facility, photograph stock locations and reconcile counts, cutting manual inventory hours in half at a UPS site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous stock counting in an institution-controlled storage facility. It supports the storeroom half of the attendant's check: locating each storage position and reporting what is short, at threshold-level precision.

sources.date: 2017 (product commercially fielded; listing describes customer deployment at scale)
sources.title: Development of an RFID Inventory Robot (AdvanRobot)
sources.claim: Keonn's AdvanRobot is a mobile autonomous RFID robot that inventories all tagged items (typically garments and textiles) in a store or low-ceiling warehouse to ~99.8% accuracy, completing a whole large store in one overnight run.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated counting of garments/textiles held on racks and shelves. Robes, uniforms and linens in club and hospitality operations are routinely RFID-tagged, so the same robot produces the par-sheet counts the attendant compiles.

sources.system: Omnicell XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System
sources.title: Ballad Health unveils three new Omnicell XR2 Central Pharmacy Dispensing Robots at Bristol Regional Medical Center
sources.claim: Omnicell's XR2 is a purpose-built dispensing robot that holds stock inside its own enclosure, tracks every unit in real time and drives inventory optimization and replenishment; three units are in service at Bristol Regional Medical Center.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = keeping perpetual stock counts and flagging replenishment for consumable supplies. When the supplies are brought to the machine and held in its purpose-built storage, the machine performs the 'is there enough / reorder now' judgment the attendant makes.

sources.system: AutoCrib industrial vending / automated supply dispensing systems
sources.developer: AutoCrib (and comparable vendors, e.g. Fastenal FAST Vend)
sources.title: Industrial Vending Machines on the Rise | Electronics360
sources.claim: Automated industrial vending/dispensing cabinets hold consumable supplies (PPE, gloves, small consumables), record every issue automatically and generate reorders when stock falls to minimum levels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = tracking consumable supply levels and reordering. With the supplies fixtured inside the machine (the E1 counterfactual), it delivers exactly the attendant's output: an accurate low-stock determination and a replenishment order.

tasks.label: Report and document safety hazards, potentially hazardous conditions, and unsafe practices and procedures.

tasks.label: Maintain inventories of clothing or uniforms, accessories, equipment, or linens.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Health club/fitness center locker room: attendant keeps the towel, robe and amenity stock going — pulls clean towels from the linen closet, restocks shelves and bins in the locker room, counts what goes to and comes back from laundry, logs daily counts and flags shortages and losses to the manager.

Athletic team clubhouse/equipment room (high school, college, pro): attendant maintains the inventory of jerseys, practice gear, shoulder pads, helmets and shoes — issues items to players and logs returns by number/size, puts laundered gear back into player bins, and runs end-of-season counts flagging missing or damaged items.

Hotel/spa/club back-of-house linen room: attendant receives laundered towels, sheets and robes, counts them against the delivery sheet, sorts and stacks them to par levels on shelves and carts, sets aside torn/stained pieces, and records stock on hand.

Theater/studio dressing room wardrobe: attendant inventories costumes, accessories, shoes and wardrobe supplies, checks items in and out per performer between calls, hangs and stores them by character/act, and notes damage or missing pieces.

Coatroom at a venue (theater, club, museum, banquet hall): attendant accounts for checked coats and bags against claim tags during and after the event, keeps hangers and tag stock in order, and reconciles unclaimed items at close.

Periodic full stocktake/audit in a hotel, casino or institutional uniform storeroom where garments carry RFID/barcode labels: attendant walks the racks and shelves counting tagged items, reconciles against the system record, and reports discrepancies.

sources.title: Improving operations and product availability at stores globally — PAL Robotics' StockBot at Decathlon stores (IFR case study)
sources.claim: StockBot, an autonomous mobile robot with RFID readers, autonomously counts apparel and sporting-goods stock in Decathlon stores, producing a full daily inventory with item locations; rolled out across stores in many countries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous stocktaking of tagged clothing/equipment in an institution-controlled facility. Same objects (garments, sporting goods), same output (an accurate count reconciled to the inventory record) as a uniform-storeroom stocktake.

sources.system: InvoTech UHF-RFID Uniform System with automated uniform conveyor
sources.developer: InvoTech Systems (with garment conveyor supplier), at FireKeepers Casino Hotel
sources.title: FireKeepers Casino Hotel implements RFID tech to control uniform inventory
sources.claim: A casino hotel maintains a perpetual uniform inventory for ~1,500 staff with an RFID system tied to a conveyor that automatically delivers the correct ... to each employee and records the issue.

sources.system: B2K Uniform System (automated uniform conveyor / smart locker)
sources.date: 2026-07 (page retrieved; installations documented as case studies)
sources.title: B2K Uniform System | Uniform Systems | Metalprogetti UK
sources.claim: Automated uniform conveyor systems perform automatic storage, conveying and distribution ... and garments; installed case studies include The Standard Hotel London, Nobu Hotel Mayfair and Geneva University Hospitals.

sources.title: THOR I Robot Separator - Single Piece Separation of Laundry
sources.claim: The THOR robot separator autonomously picks individual garments, towels and linen out of bulk-fed loads on an industrial laundry line at 1,200–1,500 pieces per hour using 3D cameras.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: single-piece separation and sorting of towels/linens/garments. Maintaining a linen inventory requires exactly this per-item physical handling and identification, here done autonomously on a purpose-built line.

sources.system: HEIMDAL RFID / camera identification module (with THOR)
sources.title: Creating the future in laundry automation — JENSEN-GROUP
sources.claim: In the same automated sorting line, the HEIMDAL module identifies each item either by reading its individual RFID tag or by machine-learning cameras, giving per-item tracking of laundry stock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic per-item identification of linens/garments in process. This is the record-keeping half of maintaining a linen inventory, performed by the machine rather than by a counting attendant.

sources.title: Amazon announces new fulfillment center robots, Sequoia and Digit
sources.claim: Amazon's Sequoia system uses mobile robots, gantries and robotic arms to containerize, store and retrieve inventory of diverse consumer goods in a fulfillment center, identifying and storing received inventory up to 75% faster.

sources.title: Automatic coat check system: quick, safe, user friendly – Metalprogetti

sources.claim: RFID towel-dispensing cabinets that issue clean towels to members, accept returns, assign each towel to a user and maintain the towel inventory are in use at hotels, ....

sources.title: Uniform Distribution Conveyor System - Metalprogetti
sources.claim: An automatic dispenser distributes folded garments and small objects, and is used in spas, wellness centers ... to distribute bathrobes and towels, holding up to 180 items per module.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model Offering Fully Autonomous, Round-the-Clock Dexterity
sources.claim: A pair of stationary robotic ... running the DYNA-1 model autonomously folded 800+ napkins over 24 hours at production quality with no human intervention, with reported transfer to laundry folding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sustained autonomous manipulation of flat textiles at a fixed workstation, comparable to folding and stacking towels/linens when keeping stock at par — the physical half of linen inventory work, done where the work is presented to the machine.

tasks.label: Issue gym clothes, uniforms, towels, athletic equipment, and special athletic apparel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Health/fitness club or hotel gym: attendant at the locker-room desk or towel window issues clean folded towels (sometimes a robe, locker key, or amenity) to members who present a membership card or scan in; high volume at peak hours, patrons queue, occasional requests for extra towels.
Hospital, casino, or hotel uniform/linen room: attendant issues scrubs, work uniforms, and lab coats to staff by employee record and size, enforces a one-out-one-in credit, and logs the issuance.

High school or college athletic equipment room: attendant issues practice uniforms, shorts, socks, towels, and general gear (balls, racquets, pinnies) at a check-out window to athletes or rec-center users identified by ID or roster number, records the checkout and handles returns.

Team game-day / specialty issuance: equipment attendant hands out specific game jerseys, cleats, helmets, shoulder pads and specialty apparel to named athletes in the locker room or at the field, verifying fit, swapping sizes, and handling last-minute substitutions during a time-critical pregame window.

Spa, resort, or country club: attendant issues bathrobes, slippers, spa towels, and rental items (golf towels, shoes, clubs) to guests at the locker-room attendant station, matching size and guest record.

sources.developer: IPA / Quadromed (scrubEx), deployed at UCSF Health
sources.title: Scrub Stations | UCSF Department of Surgery - Resident Portal
sources.claim: scrubEx automated uniform dispensers are deployed inside hospital locker rooms and mechanically dispense a correct-size scrub set to a staff member who taps an ID badge, replacing attendant-issued garments.

sources.developer: IPA (scrubEX), deployed at Brigham and Women's Hospital
sources.title: New Machines on the Block: Scrubs Dispensers Save Time, Money - Brigham Bulletin
sources.claim: Brigham and Women's Hospital replaced open scrub racks and staffed issuance with scrubEX dispensing machines that hand out a pair of scrubs in ... in about four seconds after a badge tap; linen handlers only restock the machine.

sources.system: Metalprogetti Automatic Distribution Systems (B2K uniform conveyor)
sources.title: Automatic Distribution Systems: 24/7 Collection and Delivery - Metalprogetti
sources.claim: Metalprogetti sells and installs automated garment distribution systems that store and automatically dispense work uniforms to users 24/7 in hospitals, hotels and factories, replacing counter issuance by staff.

sources.title: Uniform Distribution Conveyor System - Metalprogetti
sources.claim: Metalprogetti's 'Folder' unit is a commercial automatic dispenser for folded garments and small objects that is used in spas, wellness centres and sports complexes to distribute bathrobes and towels to users - i.e. exactly the towel/robe issuance done by locker-room attendants, performed by a machine that is stocked by staff.

sources.title: HUG uses B2K for Automatic Uniform Management – Metalprogetti
sources.claim: Geneva University Hospital operates a Metalprogetti automatic distribution system ... with size-based management and per-item traceability, demonstrating an installed institutional deployment of automated uniform issuance.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and moves individual products of many kinds out of stock containers into specific order totes in production fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order picking of individual diverse retail items (including polybagged apparel and small sporting goods) from bins into a designated tote. This is the retrieval-and-present step of issuing gear from an equipment-room stock: comparable object variety, size and precision, with items presented in containers.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout – GeekWire
sources.claim: Sparrow operates inside a fenced protective metal structure in the fulfillment center and handles a wide variety ... items with a suction end-effector, establishing that its demonstrated environment is a purpose-built, guarded robotic cell.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the previous item (individual-item picking); cited here to establish the E1 character of the environment in which that picking is done.

sources.system: Inwatec THOR robot separator / ODIN sorting line
sources.title: Fully automatic sorting of Soiled Workwear | Inwatec | Robotics for Industrial Laundries
sources.claim: Inwatec's robot separators singulate individual garments from bulk batches on conveyor-fed lines in industrial laundries, showing commercial robotic handling of individual deformable textile items in purpose-built machine lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic singulation and sorting of individual towels/uniform garments in a laundry. It substantiates that machines can reliably grasp and route single textile items of the type attendants issue, when those items are presented by a purpose-built feed.

sources.system: Towel Tracker / RFID towel rental cabinet
sources.title: Towel Rental Machine and Towel Rental Cabinet - FRESH Equipment
sources.claim: RFID towel cabinets/rental machines marketed to gyms, fitness clubs, pools and hotels automate towel distribution and return with card or payment authentication; the mechanism is largely an access-controlled cabinet, so the machine's own manipulation role is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Context only for towel issuance in fitness clubs; treated as teleoperated/unclear and not used to support any positive judgment.

tasks.label: Provide assistance to patrons by performing duties such as opening doors or carrying bags.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Health club / fitness center locker room: a member arrives with a gym bag and armful of gear; the attendant takes the bag, carries it to the member's locker or bench, stows it, hands over towels, and retrieves it at departure. Wet, humid, crowded aisles; bags of every size and shape.

Country club / golf club locker room and bag room: attendant meets the member at the door, carries golf bag, shoes, and garment bag between the drop-off, the bag room, the locker room, and the cart staging area; heavy (30-50 lb) awkward loads, doors between clubhouse zones.

Hotel, resort, or spa locker/changing room: attendant greets the guest at the entrance, opens the door, carries the guest's bag and belongings to a changing room or locker, stores them during the visit, and returns them at checkout.

Coatroom at a theater, casino, museum, banquet hall, or upscale restaurant: attendant opens the entrance/coatroom door for arriving patrons, takes coats, shopping bags, umbrellas, and small luggage, carries them to racks or bins, and hands them back at pickup during a rush.

General patron courtesy and door duty across these venues: standing at the entrance to hold and steady the door for patrons whose hands are full, helping an elderly or encumbered patron carry items across the floor, walking alongside and handing items over on request in a stream of foot traffic.

sources.system: YOBOT (ABB articulated-arm robot at Yotel New York)
sources.title: News: An ABB Industrial Robot Provides Automated Luggage Storage and Retrieval at New Yotel in Manhattan
sources.claim: YOBOT, an ABB articulated-arm industrial robot in a glass enclosure in the Yotel New York lobby, takes guests' luggage deposited at a hatch and stores and retrieves it from a wall of 117 lockers - i.e., it carries and stows a patron's bag for them in a purpose-built machine enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act as the attendant duty rated here - relieving a patron of a bag, carrying it, stowing it in a locker and returning it - with the same objects (suitcases, duffels up to ~50 lb) and the same low precision demand; only the venue differs (hotel lobby vs. locker room).

sources.title: Robots Are Coming To A Hotel Near You, But Are Consumers Ready?
sources.claim: The Yotel luggage robot remains in service and handles more than 30,000 bags per year, indicating sustained employer-accepted service quality for the bag-carrying duty.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes currency and throughput of the same bag-handling substitute for a human porter/attendant.

sources.system: Henn na Hotel cloakroom robot arm
sources.title: Inside the Henn na Robot Hotel - The Robot Report
sources.claim: At the Henn na Hotel, a robotic arm in a glass-walled cloakroom takes guests' bags placed in a deposit door and stores them in lockers, fetching them back when the guest returns.
sources.transferJustification: This is a cloakroom/locker attendant duty - taking a patron's item, carrying it to storage and returning it - executed by a robot in a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.title: Automatic coat check system: quick, safe, user friendly – Metalprogetti
sources.claim: Metalprogetti's Automatic Cloak Room is a commercially sold automated coat-check machine installed in theaters, museums, casinos and restaurants; patrons deposit and reclaim coats and items at the machine, which conveys and stores each garment in a numbered slot.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the coatroom variant of carrying patrons' items to and from storage; the machine performs the transport and stowage the attendant would otherwise do by hand, for the same objects (coats, bags, umbrellas).

sources.title: Lifting aid available at every workstation in Schiphol's baggage halls
sources.claim: At Schiphol Airport a robot has for more than six months been independently loading departing passengers' bags from the handling line into carts and containers, showing autonomous machine handling of heavy, varied passenger bags in a purpose-built hall.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (baggage handling) with the same objects and mass as golf bags and duffels a locker room attendant lifts; substantiates that heavy irregular patron bags can be moved and stowed by machine when presented on a fixtured conveyor.

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi, a one-armed mobile manipulator deployed 24/7 in US hospitals, autonomously opens doors and operates elevators while making deliveries in corridors shared with staff and patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating standard human doors inside an occupied institutional facility. It shows door manipulation for the robot's own passage, but not holding a door open as a courtesy for an approaching patron or taking items from a patron's hands.

sources.title: Relay Robotics Introduces Relay2, The New High-Capacity Hotel Delivery Robot
sources.claim: Relay2 hotel delivery robots autonomously navigate hotels and ride elevators to bring items from the front desk to guest room doors, but staff load the bin and the guest unloads it; the robot performs no lifting, handover, or stowage of a guest's own bag.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting items to patrons inside a structured hospitality facility. It bounds what is available at E2 - bin transport only, with humans doing the loading and the patron-facing handling.

sources.title: Piaggio Fast Forward presents kilo the revolutionary robot with smart following technology
sources.claim: Piaggio Fast Forward's kilo cargo cobot follows a person and carries up to 130 kg along preset paths, and has been pitched for hotels and airports to move guest luggage; the human must load and unload it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: carrying luggage alongside people in hospitality settings. Establishes the E2 ceiling - a person-following cart that must be hand-loaded, not a system that takes a bag from a patron and stows it in a locker.

tasks.label: Operate washing machines and dryers to clean soiled apparel and towels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Health club / fitness center towel service: attendant empties soiled-towel hampers from the locker room, carries or wheels the load to the club's on-premises laundry room, loads two or three human-facing commercial washer-extractors, doses detergent (often auto-dosed), selects the cycle, later transfers heavy wet terry towels to tumble dryers, unloads, and folds/stacks for restocking. High volume, uniform white cotton towels, runs all day between other duties.

Athletic team locker/equipment room (college, pro, or high school): attendant collects practice jerseys, uniforms, socks, compression wear and towels, sorts by player/mesh bag, pretreats grass, mud and blood stains, chooses settings appropriate to performance fabrics, runs washers and dryers, then removes items that must air-dry or hang, and returns each player's items to their locker.

Spa, salon, or country club locker room: mixed smaller loads of robes, wraps, sheets and cotton towels, some heavily soiled with massage oils, hair color or self-tanner requiring pretreatment or separate wash; some items hang-dried; folding to a presentation standard for the locker room and treatment rooms.

Small facility with one stacked residential-size or single small commercial washer/dryer in a closet or back room (boutique studio, hotel fitness room, small dressing room): a few small loads of towels and staff apparel run between other duties, cramped access, machine controls at the front, laundry basket on the floor.

Theater, dance, or performance dressing room attendant: laundering costumes, dancewear, tights and delicate garments between shows — delicate/hand-wash cycles, garment bags, spot cleaning, low-heat or air drying, hanging and steaming; time-critical turnaround and high damage sensitivity on one-of-a-kind pieces.

sources.system: Kannegiesser PowerTrans batch washer / SmartLaundry automated linen flow (monorail bag storage, press, lift shuttle, dryer)
sources.title: Partner in laundry technology: Kannegiesser - USA (EN)
sources.claim: Industrial laundries run a fully automated wash aisle: sorted soiled-linen batches held in a monorail bag store are automatically loaded into a batch (tunnel) washer, pressed, and loaded into the dryer by lift shuttle conveyor, with wash programs selected automatically from the batch database.

sources.system: Inwatec THOR robotic soiled-linen separator/sorting system
sources.title: Building the future of laundry robotics with Elastic | Elastic Blog
sources.claim: Robotic separators that grab bulk soiled towels, linen and garments from a conveyor and singulate them for sorting into wash batches are deployed at scale in industrial laundries worldwide.

sources.system: Inwatec Robot Separator + ODIN X-ray + vision-based sorting line for soiled workwear
sources.title: Fully automatic sorting of Soiled Workwear | Inwatec | Robotics for Industrial Laundries
sources.claim: A robotic line handles soiled workwear garments fully automatically: a robot separator singulates garments fed by conveyor, an X-ray machine rejects garments containing foreign objects left in pockets, and a vision system sorts the garments into wash categories before washing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting/handling soiled garments before washing. It transfers because team uniforms and staff apparel are the same class of garment as rental workwear, handled at the same soil level, in the same purpose-built laundry line that then washes and dries them.

sources.system: sewts VELUM (FANUC robot + AI vision) towel handling cell at Greif Textile Mietsysteme
sources.title: Intelligent robots for commercial laundries | IFR case study
sources.claim: A commercial robot cell picks washed terry towels and bathmats out of bulk and feeds them crease-free into folding machines, in continuous production at an industrial laundry since November 2022 at 500-600 items per hour.

sources.system: Figure 02 humanoid with Helix VLA model
sources.title: Wild Video Shows Humanoid Robot Loading a Washing Machine Pretty Well | Futurism
sources.claim: A humanoid robot autonomously loaded dirty laundry from a basket into a household washing machine using a learned vision-language-action policy; it was a one-off home demonstration and the robot did not operate the machine's controls or run the dry cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading a human-facing washing machine. Cited as the closest evidence for a machine-operating step in a human setting; it is a single lab/home demo without cycle selection, dryer transfer, or sustained worker-quality reliability.

sources.system: DYNA-1 folding robot at Monster Laundry (Sacramento laundromat)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: Autonomous towel folding by stationary robot arms is in real commercial laundry service, but the deployed capability is limited to folding simple uniform items, not loading or operating washers and dryers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: folding clean towels in a laundromat (an E2 facility). It shows deformable-towel handling at commercial reliability, but covers only the finishing step and provides no evidence of loading, cycle operation, or wet-load transfer between washer and dryer.

sources.system: Noematrix multi-robot hotel laundry cell (single-arm lifting mobile robot + mobile chassis units)
sources.title: WAIC 2026 | Medicine Retrieval, Laundry Washing and Drying, Noematrix Robots Demonstrate "Real Work" | Gasgoo
sources.claim: A multi-robot hotel-laundry workflow covering washing, drying and finishing, with a mobile single-arm robot loading/unloading and operating equipment, was shown at a conference exhibit; the source does not establish that the manipulation was autonomous rather than teleoperated, and it is an exhibition demonstration.

tasks.label: Activate emergency action plans and administer first aid, as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Health-club/spa locker room: a patron reports a minor injury (cut foot on wet tile, scraped shin, nosebleed, blister, bruise). Attendant retrieves the first-aid kit, dons gloves, cleans and dresses the wound or supplies an ice pack, checks the patron is okay, and files an incident report.

Sauna/steam room or post-workout collapse: a patron becomes faint, dizzy, nauseated or overheated. Attendant assesses responsiveness, helps them to a bench or the floor, cools them, gives water, monitors, summons the manager/EMT, and stays with them until they recover or EMS arrives.

Facility-wide emergency (fire alarm, severe weather, power failure, pool-chemical or gas incident, lockdown): attendant activates the emergency action plan — sounds/confirms the alarm, sweeps locker room, showers, sauna and dressing stalls for partially dressed or mobility-limited patrons, directs them to exits or shelter, and reports the area clear.

Slip-and-fall or equipment accident in the locker room or dressing area with a suspected fracture or head injury: attendant keeps the patron still, controls bleeding with pressure, calls 911, sends staff to meet the ambulance, cordons the wet or hazardous area, and hands off to paramedics.

Unresponsive patron / cardiac arrest in a locker room or shower: attendant calls the code, gets the wall AED and kit, checks breathing and pulse, starts chest compressions, applies AED pads and follows prompts, and continues until EMS takes over.

sources.system: A-CPR automatic chest compression and external defibrillation device
sources.developer: Yonsei Wonju College of Medicine (Roh, Hwang et al.)
sources.title: Development of an automatic device performing chest compression and external defibrillation: An animal-based pilot study - PubMed
sources.claim: An automated CPR apparatus combining chest compression and defibrillation has been tested only in a swine/manikin pilot; it is a device applied to an already-positioned subject in a lab, not an autonomous responder that recognizes an emergency and delivers first aid to a patron.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical CPR on a cardiac-arrest victim. Cited to show the state of the art is an animal-model device requiring humans to expose, position and attach it, so it does not carry over to a locker-room CPR/AED response.

sources.developer: Foxconn / Kawasaki Heavy Industries with NVIDIA
sources.title: Nurabot to assist nurses with routine tasks | Digital Watch Observatory
sources.claim: The most capable deployed healthcare service robot performs autonomous navigation, medication and supply delivery, ward patrol and visitor guidance in hospital wards — no hands-on patient care or emergency first aid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile work inside a structured human facility (hospital ward). Shows that even the leading deployed care-setting robot only transports and guides; it establishes mobility but not the physical casualty care this task requires.

sources.title: Knightscope K5 Autonomous Security Robots Deployed at Dozens of Self-Storage Facilities Nationwide
sources.claim: Deployed autonomous security robots patrol structured facilities and raise alerts/emergency calls, but they take no physical action on people and do not evacuate or treat them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous patrol and incident alerting in a controlled facility. Cited to show the deployed capability closest to 'activating an emergency action plan' stops at detection and notification, with no sweeping, escorting or physical assistance of patrons.

sources.title: Eldercare robot helps people sit and stand, and catches them if they fall | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: The leading robot for physically supporting and lifting a person (including catching a fall) is a laboratory prototype that is driven by remote control, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically supporting/lifting a person who has fallen, the closest analogue to assisting a fainted or fallen patron. Teleoperated prototype, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: 'Robot medics' provide remote medical treatment in hazardous environments
sources.claim: Robotic casualty assessment and triage in the field has been demonstrated only with teleoperated ground vehicles under continuous human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assessing and triaging an injured person. Directly analogous to the assessment step of first aid, but the system is teleoperated, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion.

tasks.label: Procure beverages, food, and other items as requested.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private/country club or golf club men's or women's locker room: a member relaxing at a locker or lounge chair asks the attendant for a beer, cocktail, bottled water or a sandwich; the attendant relays/collects the order at the club bar or grill, carries it back through the locker room (tile floors, benches, bag racks, members in various states of dress) and hands it to the member, charging it to the member account.

Health club, hotel spa or resort locker room: a guest at a locker or in the wet area requests a fresh towel, bottled water, razor, robe, sandals or a toiletry item; the attendant retrieves it from the linen/stock closet or the refrigerated case behind the desk and brings it to the guest at the locker, sauna door or lounge.

Professional or college team locker room on game day: attendant stocks coolers and stalls with sports drinks, water, protein shakes and post-game food, and fetches individual items on request from players and coaches during a crowded, time-compressed pre-/post-game window with gear, tape, laundry and media on the floor.

Theater, concert or TV-studio dressing room: attendant fetches coffee, water, meals or a snack from the green room, catering table or nearby vendor for performers, moving through dark, cable-strewn backstage corridors and wings between cues and quick changes.

Upscale retail, bridal or department-store fitting room: attendant brings a client a beverage (water, coffee, champagne) and simultaneously procures requested merchandise — a different size or color, shoes, undergarments, accessories — from racks or the stockroom and delivers it into the fitting room.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi is a commercially deployed one-armed mobile manipulator that autonomously picks requested supplies out of hospital supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms — i.e., fetch-and-deliver of small requested items inside a staffed human facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply fetch-and-delivery. It matches 'procure items as requested' — a staff member requests a small consumable, the robot retrieves it from a stock closet and brings it to a person in a people-filled facility, the same object class (towels/linens, bottles, toiletries, packaged supplies) and the same corridor-and-room navigation as a locker-room attendant runs.

sources.title: Deploying physical AI to aid clinicians using AWS with Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Moxi's fetch-and-deliver service runs at commercial scale and reliability across many hospitals, including autonomous elevator use and high-traffic corridors.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; establishes the reliability/scale needed for 'worker quality' rather than a one-off demo.

sources.title: The robot butler is coming to a hotel near you - KONE Corporation
sources.claim: Relay hotel robots autonomously deliver guest-requested items — snacks, coffee, toiletries, towels — from staff stations to guest rooms, riding elevators on their own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hotel amenity/room-service running. Identical object mix (beverages, snacks, toiletries, towels) and identical service pattern — guest requests, staff load, robot transports and presents the item — inside an institution-controlled building.

sources.title: Relay2 delivery robot offers 2x payload, new elevator integration
sources.claim: Relay2, a current-generation hotel delivery robot, autonomously transports food-delivery cartons from the lobby to guest rooms with cloud-based elevator integration and doubled payload.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-building food and beverage running in hospitality; same payloads and same corridor/elevator route structure as procuring food for a patron elsewhere in a club or hotel.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Introduces Servi Q
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi platform is sold and deployed for autonomous food and beverage delivery in restaurants, cafés, hotels and venues, including tight corridors and congested service areas, without changing the floor plan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: food/beverage running from bar or kitchen to a seated guest. The locker-room attendant's beverage run is the same act — collect the drink at the bar, carry it through a people-filled room, present it to the patron.

sources.system: Starship delivery robots at Eagle Vines Golf Club
sources.title: Technology by the tees: Self-driving robotic carts serve golfers at American Canyon club
sources.claim: At a golf club, Starship self-driving delivery carts fetch food, beverages and balls ordered by members through an app; club employees load the cart and the vehicle drives the order out autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: club food-and-beverage procurement on request. Same customers, same club institution, same order-collect-deliver loop as the locker-room attendant's beverage run, differing only in the delivery leg being outdoors.

sources.system: Robot.com (Kiwibot) delivery robots at Harbor Links Golf Course
sources.title: Golf Course Food Service Gets a Robot Upgrade: First in the USA
sources.claim: Autonomous food and beverage delivery ... have been operating in service at a US golf course since spring 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: club F&B order fulfilment; corroborates that club-managed premises can be served by autonomous delivery robots at commercial reliability.

sources.title: Meet ADAM, the Nvidia-Powered NHL Arena Bartender Robot
sources.claim: ADAM, a dual-arm robotic mixologist installed at a fixed bar station, prepares and serves cocktails and mocktails to patrons at major sports venues.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing and handing over a requested beverage at a purpose-built station. Supports the E1 counterfactual in which the patron/order is brought to a fixtured machine that procures and dispenses the drink.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Piece-Picking System for Warehouse Order Fulfillment
sources.claim: RightPick 4 is a commercially sold autonomous piece-picking system that grasps and places individual items, including previously unseen ones, in verticals such as general merchandise and apparel distribution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order fulfilment piece-picking of consumer goods and apparel at a fixtured station. Supports the E1 counterfactual for procuring a requested garment or item when the goods are presented to the machine in totes rather than found on a sales floor.

sources.title: Pudu KettyBot Pro | RobotLAB
sources.claim: Commercially sold service-delivery robots are marketed and configured for gyms and locker rooms to carry fresh towels, water bottles and other member items autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Vendor/integrator source for the exact setting of interest (fitness facility locker rooms); used only as corroboration for the Moxi and Relay evidence, not as the decisive item.

tasks.label: Provide or arrange for services such as clothes pressing, cleaning, or repair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Health club, spa or country club locker room: a member leaves workout clothes, a golf shirt or a dress shirt for laundering/dry cleaning. Attendant tags and bags the items, logs the ticket, hands them to the in-house laundry or an outside vendor, then retrieves the finished garments and hangs them in the member's locker.

Country club / athletic club locker room: attendant presses or steams a member's shirt, slacks or blazer on the back-room press or ironing board (and buffs shoes), returning the garment to the locker before the member's tee time or club dinner.

Theater, TV/film or dance dressing room: wardrobe/dressing room attendant steams and presses costumes on the rack between calls and re-hangs them in order for the next scene, working under curtain-time pressure with varied fabrics and trims.

Backstage or club emergency garment work: sewing on a popped button, tacking a torn hem or split seam, and spot-cleaning a makeup, sweat or food stain from a costume or a member's jacket minutes before it is needed.

Retail apparel or bridal fitting-room attendant: steams wrinkled try-on garments, re-hangs them and returns them to the sales floor, and routes items needing alteration to the in-house tailor with a ticket.

Hotel, restaurant or event-venue coatroom: a checked coat is soiled or damaged; the attendant bags and tickets it, arranges cleaning/repair through the hotel valet or an outside cleaner, follows up, and returns the garment to the guest.

sources.title: Robots to the rescue: Dry clean guests' clothes in minutes - HB To Go (Hotel Business)
sources.claim: Presso's garment care machine performs pressing, cleaning and drying of a guest's garment automatically inside a cabinet using computer-vision-driven 'stretcher robotics'; a garment is ready to wear in about 5-6 minutes (10-15 for a suit). Machines were live in US hotels.

sources.title: Robots to the rescue: Dry clean guests' clothes in minutes - HB To Go (Hotel Business)
sources.claim: The Presso machine is a self-service unit: the user brings the garment to the machine, puts it inside and identifies it, and the machine does the ... — i.e. loading/unloading of the garment is done by the person, not the machine.

sources.title: Presso Joins Forces with WASH Multifamily to Introduce 5-Minute "Press & Refresh" Machines
sources.claim: Presso machines were being rolled out commercially through WASH Multifamily to apartment and hotel properties, pressing and refreshing garments in as little as ....

tasks.label: Attend to needs of athletic teams in clubhouses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Laundry cycle for a pro/college team clubhouse: gather soiled uniforms, socks, towels and warmups strewn on stall floors and hampers after practice or a game, pretreat grass/dirt stains, run washers and dryers, then fold towels and hang/return each player's clean garments — overnight turnaround before the next day's workout.

Pre-game stall/locker setup: hang each player's correct jersey, pants and warmups by number, lay out folded towels, undershirts, socks, sliders, toiletries and gum in each of ~30 stalls, arrange shoes and gloves, and restock shared supplies (tape, powder, drinks in stall fridges).

Clubhouse food and beverage service: receive catering, set out the pre/post-game spread in chafing dishes on buffet tables, portion and hand out plates, keep coolers and fridges stocked with iced water, sports drinks and snacks, then clear plates, break down the spread and run dishes.

Cleaning and sanitizing the clubhouse wet areas after the team leaves: scrub showers, toilets, urinals and sinks, mop/scrub locker room and training-room floors, wipe mirrors and counters, empty trash — restoring the room to standard before the next day.

Ad hoc personal service to players and staff: shine/clean cleats and dress shoes, break in and lace gloves, tape bat handles, sew or repair gear, fetch coffee or a forgotten item, run errands off-site, handle visiting-team and family requests during a game.

tasks.label: Store personal possessions for patrons, issue claim checks for articles stored, and return articles on receipt of checks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Coat check at a restaurant, hotel, theater or museum: patron hands over a coat (often with scarf, hat, umbrella, small bag) across a Dutch door; attendant hangs it on a numbered hanger on a rack or conveyor, tears off and hands over the matching claim ticket, and retrieves the garment on presentation of the ticket at the end of the evening or intermission.

Nightclub, banquet hall or event-venue coat-and-bag check: high-volume intake at the door and a heavy simultaneous rush at closing; mixed items (coats, purses, backpacks, shopping bags, helmets), dim/noisy conditions, ticket numbers, cash/tip handling, occasional intoxicated patrons.

Health club, spa, swim club or country club locker room: attendant takes members' valuables, bags, shoes or golf gear for safekeeping behind the desk or in an assigned locker, issues a locker key, wristband or claim tag, and returns the items when the member checks out.

Arena, museum, casino or attraction bag/parcel check: visitors deposit backpacks, laptop bags, purchases and suitcases at a check counter or bag-storage room; items are placed in numbered lockers or on shelves against a claim tag and handed back on presentation of the tag.

Exception handling: patron has lost or mismatched the claim check, or the article is bulky/irregular (stroller, ski gear, crutches, musical instrument, garment bag); attendant verifies ownership by description or ID, searches the racks/shelves, resolves disputes over misplaced or damaged articles, and releases the item.
