roles.description: Prepare bodies for interment in conformity with legal requirements.

tasks.label: Conform to laws of health and sanitation and ensure that legal requirements concerning embalming are met.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-embalming legal clearance at a funeral home: confirm the death certificate/burial-transit permit is filed, verify written embalming authorization from the authorizing agent, check for medical examiner/coroner release, note reported communicable disease, and enter the case in the prep-room log before starting work.

Working the case to OSHA bloodborne-pathogen and state-board sanitation rules: don gown, gloves, face shield and respirator; topically disinfect the decedent's surface, orifices and any wounds with an EPA-registered disinfectant; use forceps/engineering controls for sharps; keep the hydroaspirator and drainage within code; wear/observe formaldehyde exposure controls and ventilation.

Post-case decontamination of the preparation room to health-code standard: bag soiled linens and PPE, scrub and disinfect the embalming table, sinks, drains, counters and floor of blood and tissue, clean, disinfect and store instruments, and restock supplies so the room is ready for the next decedent.

Regulated medical waste and fluid disposal compliance: segregate sharps into approved containers, red-bag infectious waste and tissue, discharge drainage to the sanitary sewer per local ordinance, store sealed containers in the designated locked area, and complete labels/manifests for the licensed hauler.

Cases with special legal requirements: known infectious disease (TB, hepatitis, CJD), coroner hold, disinterment, or out-of-state/international shipment requiring an embalming certificate and a sealed or zinc-lined container; apply enhanced precautions and produce the required certificates and container seals.

Facility and records compliance: maintain state-board embalming records and case logs, keep formaldehyde exposure monitoring and training records, verify ventilation, eyewash and PPE stock, and present the preparation room for unannounced state board or OSHA inspection.

sources.title: The use of a UV-C disinfection robot in the routine cleaning process: a field study in an Academic hospital
sources.claim: UVD Robots' autonomous UV-C mobile robot was studied in routine cleaning at an academic hospital, running pre-mapped autonomous disinfection cycles in clinic rooms — the closest deployed capability to keeping a work room sanitary, but it only irradiates surfaces after human cleaning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: terminal room disinfection in a hospital. It bears on the embalmer's duty to keep the preparation room sanitary, but the robot only adds UV irradiation to a room already cleaned by hand, so it does not complete a prep-room decontamination.

sources.title: UV-C Disinfection Robots · RobotLAB
sources.claim: Vendor documentation for hospital UV-C robot deployments states manual cleaning is still required for visible contamination, confirming UV robots are an adjunct rather than a replacement for soil removal and wipe-down.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patient-room turnover cleaning. It shows the limit of deployed disinfection robots — blood and tissue soil on an embalming table still requires human removal — so it cannot substantiate completion of prep-room sanitation.

sources.title: Neo floor scrubbing robot for healthcare an HHS customer story
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor-scrubbing robot is commercially deployed in US acute-care hospitals, demonstrating autonomous floor cleaning inside a structured human facility but nothing beyond floors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital floor cleaning. Floor scrubbing is one element of prep-room sanitation, but the machine handles only open floor area and no tables, instruments, drains or waste, so it cannot complete the instance.

sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection
sources.claim: A research robot combining wiping and UV-C disinfection was validated in real-world testing at a hospital, indicating that robotic removal of surface soil in clinical rooms is still at demonstration stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact wiping plus UV disinfection of clinical surfaces. It is the nearest capability to wiping down an embalming table, but it is a research prototype with no evidence of worker-quality biohazard soil removal or instrument reprocessing.

sources.title: The Growing Demand for Funeral Professionals in an AI-Driven World
sources.claim: Industry review of automation in funeral service reports only limited, software-level AI assistance (scheduling, documentation, communications); no embodied robotic system performing embalming-room sanitation or legal compliance work was identified.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: it documents that funeral-sector automation is software-only, supporting the negative finding that no robotic system performs the physical health-and-sanitation compliance duties of an embalmer.

tasks.label: Apply cosmetics to impart lifelike appearance to the deceased.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine case in a funeral home preparation room: embalmed body supine on a porcelain table; embalmer applies massage cream, tinted cream or liquid foundation to face, neck and hands, blush/cheek color, lip color and powder, matching complexion to a family photograph, then checks the effect under viewing-room lighting.

Discoloration case in the prep room: jaundice, post-mortem staining, bruising, dehydration or chemotherapy pallor requires color-corrective undertones, opaque cosmetics or airbrush application feathered into surrounding skin so the correction is invisible at casket distance.

Trauma, autopsy or extended-postmortem case: cosmetics applied over restorative wax fills, sutures and rebuilt features, including eyebrow/eyelash and hairline work, to recreate a recognizable, lifelike likeness from photographs.

Final touch-ups after dressing and casketing, done in the funeral home chapel, church or visitation room shortly before the viewing: reaching into the casket at an angle, correcting shine, purge, leakage or slipped cosmetics, sometimes with family present or arriving.

Short-notice or unembalmed viewing at a hospital morgue, medical examiner facility, or refrigerated holding area: minimal cosmetics on a refrigerated, unembalmed body to make the face presentable for identification or a brief family viewing.

sources.system: LUUM next-generation AI lash extension robot
sources.title: LUUM Launches Next-Gen AI-Powered Lash Robot
sources.claim: LUUM operates commercial studios where an AI-guided robot applies eyelash extensions to clients' eyes in salon/retail settings, with lash artists supervising; this is the closest deployed example of a robot performing a cosmetic beautification service on a human face.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic beauty service on a living human face in a controlled facility. It shows face-adjacent precision under machine control, but it performs one templated operation (isolating and bonding lash extensions) on a fixtured, awake client; it does not blend tinted cosmetics over facial contours, match a complexion to a photograph, or cover discoloration, so it does not substantiate completion of mortuary cosmetic application.

sources.title: Blackdot creates AI-powered tattoo device to reduce pain
sources.claim: Blackdot operates an automated tattoo device that deposits ink into human skin in a commercial Austin studio, demonstrating machine-controlled pigment application to skin, but limited to small planar designs on a stabilized body area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying pigment to human skin under machine control. Transfer is weak: the device works on a small, flattened, mechanically stabilized skin patch reproducing a supplied vector design, whereas the task requires blended, color-matched cream or airbrush cosmetics over the whole face, neck and hands of a deceased person and an aesthetic 'lifelike' judgment; it therefore cannot substantiate completion.

sources.title: The Last Word: Gemma Robotics' Elizabeth Williams on Her Startup's Autonomous Makeup Application Machine
sources.claim: Gemma Robotics (BeautAI) claims a patented automatic makeup application machine that applies makeup in under three ..., but the company was in stealth mode with only patents and company-supplied images; no independent demonstration of unattended, worker-quality full-face makeup was found.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cosmetic application to a living face. Autonomy and performance are unverified (stealth-mode company claim plus patents), and the concept targets seated, cooperative users choosing preset 'looks' rather than complexion-matched mortuary cosmetics on a supine deceased body, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Babaoshan Funeral Parlor 3D printing restoration studio and disinfection robot
sources.title: 3D Printing for Mourners: Chinese Funeral Home Turns to 3D Technologies to Reconstruct Faces of the Deceased for Open Casket Funerals
sources.claim: At the most technologically advanced funeral homes, machine assistance covers 3D-printed facial molds and a mobile disinfection robot, while coloring and cosmetic finishing of the deceased remains manual work by mortuary cosmetologists.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting (funeral home preparation area). It establishes what robots actually do in mortuary facilities as of the frontier: room disinfection and 3D-printed reconstruction aids, with face coloring and cosmetics still performed by human restorative artists.

tasks.label: Join lips, using needles and thread or wire.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult decedent, non-autopsy, in a funeral home preparation room: embalmer positions the mandible, packs cotton/places a mouth former or seats the decedent's dentures, fires wire barbs into the mandible and maxilla with a needle injector, twists the wires to draw the lips together, then aligns and shapes the lip line to a natural closed-mouth expression and seals it.

Edentulous or emaciated elderly decedent with no dentures available: thin, dehydrated, easily torn lip tissue; embalmer must build out the mouth with cotton/mouth former, may use a mandibular (muscular) suture threaded with a curved needle through the septum, gums and under the chin, and hand-tie it to restore natural fullness and lip line.

Autopsied case where the mandible/skull has been disturbed: needle injector anchoring is unreliable, so the embalmer runs a mandibular suture through the jaw and nasal septum with needle and ligature thread, re-establishes jaw position, and ties the closure while judging tension to avoid a grimace or a puckered mouth.

Trauma, burn, gunshot, oral cancer or decomposition case: lips and surrounding tissue are lacerated, missing or fragile; the embalmer closes with fine baseball/interrupted sutures or wire, sometimes combined with waxes and sealants, matching the lip contour to a photograph of the person in life for an open-casket viewing.

Small or atypical anatomy or off-site work: infant/child case, or a trade embalmer working in another firm's prep room or a hospital morgue with unfamiliar instruments, closing a very small mouth with fine suture where the margin for a visible error is tiny.

sources.system: SutureBot benchmark on the da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK)
sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University, NVIDIA, Stanford University, University of Toronto
sources.title: SutureBot: A Precision Framework & Benchmark For Autonomous End-to-End Suturing
sources.claim: State-of-the-art surgical robotics research reports that no fully autonomous needle-grasp / tissue-insertion / knot-tying suturing pipeline has been demonstrated end-to-end on physical hardware; the benchmark's own framework still requires a human to specify insertion and exit points via a GUI.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous suturing with needle and thread. Joining lips uses the same primitive (needle penetration of tissue plus knot/wire tying); this source shows the primitive is not yet autonomously solved even on a fixtured lab phantom, let alone on a face.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Autonomous Robot Improves Surgical Precision Using AI (NVIDIA Technical Blog)
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performed supervised-autonomous laparoscopic bowel anastomosis suturing on live pig tissue using a specialized circular suturing tool and fluorescent tissue markers, on an operating table in a research operating room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue suturing. It is the strongest existing demonstration of machine-controlled needle work on tissue, but it lays a running suture along a marked tubular bowel presented to the tool; it does not position a jaw, pack cotton, set dentures, anchor wire in bone, or judge a cosmetic lip line.

sources.title: Autonomous robot surgeon removes organs with 100% success rate (New Atlas)
sources.claim: An AI-driven da Vinci system autonomously executed the steps of a gallbladder removal on ex vivo pig specimens in a laboratory, showing task-level surgical autonomy on fixtured tissue, but the procedure involved grasping, clipping and cutting rather than needle-and-thread closure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue surgical manipulation. Demonstrates autonomy on tissue held in a fixed lab setup, but includes no suturing, no wire anchoring in bone, and no aesthetic acceptance criterion, so it does not carry over to completing a mouth closure.

sources.system: Autonomous dental implant robot (ADIR / Yakebot-class r-CAIS system)
sources.developer: Chinese academic-industrial teams (e.g., Peking University / Yakebot)
sources.title: Clinical evaluation of autonomous robotic-assisted full-arch implant surgery: A 1-year prospective clinical study
sources.claim: Autonomous dental implant robots drill and place implants inside patients' mouths under machine control, guided by a rigidly fixed marker splint and a preoperative CT plan, in a dental clinic; this is the closest autonomous intraoral bone work but covers no lip, suture or wire-tying step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous work inside the oral cavity on jaw bone. It shows a robot can reach maxillary/mandibular bone accurately when the head is rigidly registered, but the mouth-closure task additionally requires wire/suture handling, knot tying and cosmetic lip alignment, none of which this system performs.

tasks.label: Close incisions, using needles and sutures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult case in a funeral home preparation room: after arterial injection through the right common carotid, the embalmer closes the 5-10 cm neck/clavicular incision — approximating skin and subcutaneous tissue, running a baseball or worm stitch with a curved needle and ligature thread, tying off, trimming, and applying sealer; area may be visible at an open-casket viewing so the closure must be cosmetically clean.

Closure of hidden arterial raise sites — femoral, axillary, or supplemental injection points — on a routine adult body on the embalming table; running suture through fatty or muscular tissue, knotted and sealed, leak-proof but not cosmetically critical.

Closure of the trocar puncture site on the abdomen after cavity treatment: a small round opening closed with a purse-string suture (or trocar button secured with suture) placed at the standard site two inches left and above the navel.

Autopsy case received from a hospital or medical examiner: closing the thoraco-abdominal Y-incision and the coronal scalp incision with heavy cord and a large curved needle through thick, cold, often edematous tissue after viscera are returned and the cavity packed; long suture lines that must not leak during transport and viewing.

Difficult tissue cases: obese, edematous, jaundiced, decomposed, or tissue-donor recovery bodies with long harvest incisions, plus trauma cases needing inversion, bridge, or hidden restorative sutures in fragile or torn skin; the embalmer varies stitch type, thread, and needle to hold friable tissue and prevent leakage.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: STAR performed a full intestinal anastomosis suture line autonomously (under surgeon supervision) in live pigs in a research operating-room setting, using a specialized laparoscopic suturing tool and 3D/NIR vision guidance — the closest demonstrated analog to running a suture closure in soft tissue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of a running suture line in soft tissue. It is the nearest analog to closing an embalming incision, but it uses a dedicated bowel-anastomosis tool on small-bore intestine inside a laparoscopic port under surgeon supervision, not a hand-held curved needle approximating skin and fat over a 5-15 cm incision on a cadaver, and knot securing is not shown as autonomous.

sources.system: SutureBot benchmark (da Vinci Research Kit, dVRK)
sources.title: SutureBot: A Precision Framework & Benchmark For Autonomous End-to-End Suturing (arXiv:2510.20965)
sources.claim: As of late 2025, researchers in the same laboratory state that no fully autonomous suturing pipeline spanning needle pickup, tissue insertion, and knot tying has been demonstrated on physical robot hardware; SutureBot is a lab benchmark on the da Vinci Research Kit with state-of-the-art VLA policies still far from reliable completion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-to-end robotic suturing including knot tying, the operation an embalmer performs repeatedly to close an incision. The authors' own assessment establishes that whole-closure autonomy, including securing the suture, is not yet demonstrated on hardware in any environment.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic System with Optical Coherence Tomography Guidance for Vascular Anastomosis (arXiv:2410.07493)
sources.claim: micro-STAR performed vascular anastomosis autonomously on ex vivo tissue in a laboratory bench setup with OCT guidance, but still required human intervention on roughly one suture in ten.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous multi-suture closure of a tissue opening. The 10% intervention rate on millimetre-scale vessels in a bench fixture indicates suture-by-suture autonomy is not yet at the reliability an employer would accept for an unattended 20-40 stitch cadaver closure.

sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: SRT-H performed a multi-step surgical procedure (cholecystectomy: clip application and cutting) fully autonomously on ex vivo pig gallbladders mounted on a laboratory bench with a da Vinci Research Kit; the demonstrated repertoire does not include suturing or wound closure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: long-horizon autonomous manipulation of soft tissue. It shows current frontier autonomy on fixtured ex vivo tissue but covers grasping, clipping, and cutting rather than needle-and-suture closure, so it does not substantiate completing an incision closure.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine
sources.claim: The Virtobot robotic system is used in a forensic medicine institute morgue to perform automated surface scanning and CT-guided post-mortem needle placement on human cadavers, showing robots can work on bodies in an institutional mortuary, but limited to inserting needles for sampling rather than suturing incisions closed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic needle work on a human cadaver in a mortuary. It substantiates robotic access to and needle insertion in cadaver tissue in an E2 facility, but not the grasping, approximation, running stitch, knotting and trimming that closing an incision requires.

tasks.label: Incise stomach and abdominal walls and probe internal organs, using trocar, to withdraw blood and waste matter from organs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine non-autopsied adult case in a funeral home preparation room: after arterial injection, the embalmer makes a small puncture about two inches left and superior to the umbilicus, inserts a trocar connected to a hydro-aspirator, systematically probes and pierces the hollow viscera (heart, lungs, stomach, intestines, bladder) in the thoracic, abdominal and pelvic cavities to withdraw blood, gas and waste, then injects cavity chemical and seals the opening with a trocar button.

Difficult non-autopsied case: obese, edematous, gas-distended or early-decomposed body with purge. Requires judging tissue resistance, altering probe angles to reach viscera through fat and fluid, repeated/extended aspiration, extra cavity fluid, and often re-aspiration hours later before viewing without tearing tissue or causing leakage.

Autopsied or organ-donor case: cavities already opened and viscera returned in a bag. Worker treats the loose viscera directly, aspirates residual fluid from the emptied cavities and pelvic basin, uses the trocar for unopened regions and hypodermic treatment of the abdominal/thoracic walls, then dries and closes the cavity.

Post-surgical, trauma, or device-bearing case: adhesions, drains, packing, colostomy, recent abdominal surgery, or pacemaker/implant. Anatomy is distorted, the trocar path must be chosen case by case, and unreached areas require supplemental hypodermic injection before closure.

Infant, child, or extremely frail/emaciated adult case: small-gauge (infant) trocar, minimal aspiration pressure, very limited working space, high risk of visible damage to thin tissue; work must leave the body presentable for an open casket.

Known infectious-disease case handled under enhanced precautions in the prep room (full PPE, respirator, strict sharps control, splash containment) while performing the same trocar aspiration and cavity injection sequence.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich (Virtopsy project) with ACMIT/Austrian partners
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine
sources.claim: Virtobot 2.0, a robotic system installed in the Zurich forensic medicine institute's post-mortem CT suite, performs automated 3D surface documentation and image-guided needle placement into corpses for tissue and liquid sampling; it does not incise the abdominal wall, probe multiple organs, aspirate cavity contents, or inject cavity fluid.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: robot-controlled instrument insertion into a dead human body in a mortuary facility. It is a single CT-planned needle trajectory to one target with the body immobile on a scanner table; a later application of the same platform is described as semiautomated. It does not cover the multi-quadrant probing, hollow-organ piercing, suction and cavity-fluid injection this task requires, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole task at any tier.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performed a supervised-autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis on live pigs in a research operating room - the most advanced autonomous soft-tissue manipulation demonstrated - but only for one narrow suturing sub-step, with ports and exposure set up by humans.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of abdominal soft tissue with a surgical instrument. It shows autonomy is limited to a single pre-planned suturing step on exposed bowel in an animal lab; it includes no trocar navigation through undissected viscera, no aspiration of cavity contents, and no cadaver work, so it does not transfer to completing cavity embalming.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid robots configured for laparoscopic surgery
sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Zekai Liang et al.)
sources.title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery | Nature
sources.claim: A July 2026 Nature study evaluating general-purpose humanoid robots (Unitree G1) on in vivo laparoscopic cholecystectomy in pigs achieved the surgical tasks only through remote teleoperation, indicating that dexterous instrument work inside the abdomen is not yet autonomous even for state-of-the-art humanoid platforms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manipulating instruments through abdominal ports on a body. Because it is explicitly teleoperated, it cannot support a positive judgment and instead marks the current ceiling for humanoid instrument work on bodies.

sources.developer: Jumlongkul et al. (Mae Fah Luang University, Thailand)
sources.title: Robotic-Assisted Surgery for Cadaveric Skull Opening: A New Method of Autopsy Procedure
sources.claim: The only robotic device reported for instrument work on cadavers in an autopsy room, a robotic autopsy saw for skull opening, is a remote-controlled tool operated by a human standing a couple of metres away, not an autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered instrument work on a human cadaver in a mortuary. It is human-guided throughout and addresses only skull opening, so it substantiates no autonomous completion of trocar cavity aspiration.

tasks.label: Clean and disinfect areas in which bodies are prepared and embalmed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small funeral-home preparation room immediately after an embalming case: scrub and disinfect the porcelain/stainless embalming table and its drain, flush and disinfect the machine hose, aspirator and trocar, wash and disinfect instruments, bag soiled sponges/gowns in red biohazard bags, drop blades in the sharps container, damp-mop the floor with a phenolic/quat disinfectant.

End-of-day or between-case wet mopping/scrubbing of prep-room and adjoining prep-area floors (garage, cot storage, hallway) with hospital-grade disinfectant; tile or sealed concrete floors with a floor drain, obstructed by table legs, cot wheels, hoses and buckets.

Between cases: wiping and disinfecting counters, cabinet fronts, the dressing/casketing table, instrument trays, the embalming machine housing and controls, the removal cot/stretcher and its cover, and refrigeration-unit shelves, using disinfectant spray/wipes and cloths.

Periodic deep clean (weekly/monthly, or after a decomposed or infectious case): scrubbing walls, splash zones and grout, cleaning light fixtures and ventilation grilles, flushing and disinfecting floor drains and traps, emptying and disinfecting the body cooler, deodorizing the room.

Immediate cleanup during a case: purge, blood or embalming-fluid spill on the table, floor or equipment while the body is on the table and the gowned embalmer is mid-procedure; absorb, disinfect per bloodborne-pathogen protocol, and resume work.

High-volume institutional setting (medical examiner's morgue, anatomy lab, military or trade embalming center): multiple stations in a larger tiled washdown room with hose bibs and central drains; cleaning several tables, sinks, instrument stations and the open floor between cases to documented infection-control standards.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's Bathroom Cleaning Robot autonomously cleans fixtures, floors and picks ... in high-traffic restrooms, and is offered as a deployed commercial service in hospitals and airports with near-zero staff intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning and disinfecting a small tiled wet room with plumbing fixtures and biological soils. Transfers to prep-room floor/fixture cleaning (same chemicals, same institution-controlled interior), but the robot's programs are fixture-specific and it does no instrument reprocessing or sharps/biohazard handling.

sources.title: Avidbots partners with US provider to deploy floor-scrubbing robots in hospitals | BetaKit
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor-scrubbing robots were deployed at scale by healthcare support provider HHS to scrub floors in US acute-care hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wet scrubbing/disinfecting hard floors in a healthcare facility. Same act as mopping and disinfecting a prep-room floor, same chemistry and institution-controlled interior setting.

sources.title: T380AMR Robotic Floor Scrubber | Tennant Company
sources.claim: Tennant's T380AMR is a compact (20-inch) commercially sold robotic scrubber designed for autonomous scrubbing of narrow aisles and small spaces in hospitals, retail and schools.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wet floor scrubbing in constrained indoor rooms; directly comparable to mopping a small preparation-room floor, though edges, corners and floor drains still need manual detail work.

sources.title: Automated Sanitation for Poultry Hatcheries | Rosie by CleanBotix
sources.claim: CleanBotix's Rosie, a mobile robot with a 6-DOF arm and precision spray system, autonomously performs rinse-foam-rinse-sanitize washdowns of predefined areas in a poultry hatchery after the sanitation crew stages the area; the company reports it working in a live production environment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chemical washdown sanitation of a biosecure processing room (equipment, walls, floors, drain zones). Same physical act as hosing, foaming and disinfecting an embalming room, but only in areas engineered for spray cleaning and staged for the machine by a human crew.

sources.system: STERIS washer-disinfectors and AMSCO cart/utensil washers
sources.title: What is a Medical Washer-Disinfector? | STERIS
sources.claim: Automated washer-disinfectors and cart washers in hospital sterile processing departments clean and thermally/chemically disinfect blood- and tissue-soiled surgical instruments, trays and large case carts inside enclosed machine chambers on validated cycles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: decontaminating blood/tissue-soiled instruments and wheeled equipment to a validated standard. This is the E1 presentation of the embalmer's instruments, trays and cot: soils, chemistry and disinfection standard equal or exceed funeral-home practice, but the work must be racked and loaded into a purpose-built chamber.

sources.system: IWT Pegasus / ARES cage- and rack-washing automation
sources.title: IWT AUTOMATION - Tecniplast - PDF Catalogs
sources.claim: IWT/Tecniplast vivarium automation installs robotic dirty-side handling integrated with tunnel washers that take soiled cages and racks through washing to clean-side operations without operator intervention for up to 90 minutes; over 100 robots are reported installed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated decontamination of biologically soiled work equipment in a biocontainment facility. Robotic handling plus tunnel washing is the purpose-built (E1) analog of cleaning and disinfecting embalming tables, trays and cots when the work is brought to the machine.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection
sources.claim: A research team demonstrated an autonomous robot that navigates a hospital environment, physically wipes surfaces with a manipulator and follows with UV-C irradiation; it is a laboratory/prototype system, not a deployed product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wiping and disinfection of hospital surfaces. Cited to bound the E2 judgment: autonomous wiping of varied furniture and equipment exists only at prototype stage, below worker quality and reliability.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots at Froedtert Hospital hauled trash and regulated medical waste along hospital corridors, completing more than 78,000 deliveries in 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving regulated medical waste inside a healthcare institution. Covers only the transport sub-step of prep-room waste removal; no cited system bags soiled sponges/PPE or handles sharps.

tasks.label: Dress bodies and place them in caskets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult case in a funeral home preparation room: an embalmed body of average build on a porcelain/steel prep table is dressed in underclothes, shirt/blouse, trousers or dress, socks/hose and jacket (garments often slit up the back and tucked), then transferred with a hydraulic body lift or a two-person team lift into the casket, positioned on the casket bed, head turned and hands folded.

Difficult body: bariatric/obese (250-400+ lb), or stiff with rigor mortis, or edematous/skin-slip, or a refrigerated unembalmed body. Limbs must be flexed and massaged, garments forced or cut and re-pinned, skin protected from tearing, and the dead weight moved into the casket with a lift plus two staff.

Autopsied, traumatic, burned or decomposed case, or a body with an infectious-disease designation: plastic coveralls/unionall and sealed undergarments applied over dressing and suturing, leaking areas managed, PPE used, then careful casketing with additional support and padding.

Infant, child, or minimal-service case: small delicate body dressed in a gown, christening outfit or shroud, or a body simply wrapped/gowned for a cremation container or rental casket insert; small casket interior arranged and body placed by hand.

Specialty or family-directed dressing for public viewing: military dress uniform with insignia and ribbons, religious garments (temple clothing, habit, shroud), tailored suit with tie, jewelry, glasses, gloves, hairpiece; after casketing the clothing is smoothed, tie and collar set, hands and shoulders adjusted to sightline, and personal items placed.

sources.system: Dual-arm dressing pipeline (Baxter/mobile manipulator, Imperial College Personal Robotics Lab)
sources.developer: F. Zhang and Y. Demiris, Imperial College London
sources.title: Learning garment manipulation policies toward robot-assisted dressing | Science Robotics
sources.claim: Frontier autonomous robot-assisted dressing reaches a single loose hospital gown put onto a passive medical training manikin lying on a bed in a laboratory; no fastenings, trousers, jackets, or body transfer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing of a passive human-shaped body. It is the closest published capability to dressing a corpse, and it shows the frontier is one unfastened gown on a manikin in a lab, far short of a shirt, trousers and jacket on a rigid or heavy cadaver plus casketing.

sources.system: AIREC (AI-driven Robot for Embrace and Care)
sources.title: Japan tests AIREC robot to roll patients, easing caregiving challenges
sources.claim: The most advanced care humanoid for handling passive human bodies can roll a person over and put on socks in a university laboratory, and is still a research prototype not expected in care facilities until about 2030.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manipulating and partially clothing a passive adult human body (rolling, sock donning). Even this narrow subset is a lab prototype, indicating no system can dress a whole limp body and lift it into a casket at worker quality.

sources.developer: RIKEN and Sumitomo Riko Company Limited
sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: Robots able to lift a whole adult human body from a bed exist only as experimental prototypes; the developers themselves stated none had been deployed in care facilities, and the line was never commercialized.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting a passive adult body from a bed into a ..., mechanically analogous to lifting a body from a prep table into a casket. The prototype status and operator-guided control mean it cannot support autonomous casketing.

sources.system: Flexible robotic biopsy system for post-mortem sampling
sources.developer: Hamburg University of Technology (MTEC) with University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf
sources.title: Robotic Tissue Sampling for Safe Post-Mortem Biopsy in Infectious Corpses
sources.claim: Robotic systems that act on human corpses in institutional mortuary/forensic settings exist only for narrow instrument tasks such as CT-guided needle biopsy on a body inside a bag, with clinician oversight; nothing addresses dressing or casketing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation performed on a human corpse in a controlled institutional facility. It establishes the ceiling of demonstrated robot work on cadavers - a guided needle insertion - and gives no basis for whole-body garment application or transfer into a casket.

sources.system: Electric mortuary body lifts (e.g., Mortuary Lift Company / Material Flow mortuary lifts)
sources.title: Mortuary Lifts – Safe Body Handling | Material Flow
sources.claim: The commercial state of practice for moving deceased bodies onto tables and into caskets is operator-controlled hydraulic/electric mortuary lifts, not machine-controlled robots.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the casketing half of the task: the only fielded machinery is an operator-driven lift, confirming there is no autonomous system that transfers a body into a casket.

sources.title: The Fascination With Robots Folding Clothes Explained - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: General-purpose humanoid garment manipulation as of late 2025 is at the level of folding flat towels under learned policies, well short of donning fitted garments on a body.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: deformable garment manipulation. Folding a flat towel on a table is far simpler than threading a slit shirt and trousers onto a rigid or edematous cadaver, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task at any tier.

tasks.label: Make incisions in arms or thighs and drain blood from circulatory system and replace it with embalming fluid, using pump.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine unautopsied adult decedent in a funeral home preparation room: embalmer positions the body on a porcelain/stainless table, selects and raises the femoral (or axillary/brachial) artery and accompanying vein through a 2-4 inch incision, ligates, inserts arterial tube and drain tube, connects to a centrifugal injection machine, runs one-point injection with concurrent drainage while monitoring distribution, then removes tubes, ligates vessels and sutures the incision closed.

Routine case handled in a high-volume centralized/trade embalming facility or mortuary service prep suite (multiple tables, standardized machines and fluid dilutions, several cases per shift), same femoral/axillary raising, injection and drainage sequence, done under time pressure for shipping or same-day viewing.

Difficult vascular or tissue condition: obesity, generalized edema, severe arteriosclerosis or clotting, dehydration, jaundice or renal-failure chemistry. Vessels are hard to locate or accept fluid poorly; the embalmer must change fluid strength/pressure/rate, massage and manipulate limbs to clear clots, and add sectional or multi-point injection (opposite thigh, arms) to achieve uniform distribution and drainage.

Autopsied or organ/tissue-donation case: circulatory continuity is broken, so limbs must be injected separately through the axillary/brachial and femoral/iliac vessels (six-point injection), with vessel stumps located and clamped, drainage handled at the cut ends, and hypodermic/surface treatment supplementing arterial work.

Compromised remains: trauma, burns, prolonged refrigeration or early decomposition, infant/pediatric or emaciated elderly cases with tiny or friable vessels. Vessel location and cannulation require exploratory dissection, very gentle handling, low pressures and frequent judgment calls about whether to abandon a site and move to another.

sources.title: SRT-H: A Hierarchical Framework for Autonomous Surgery via Language Conditioned Imitation Learning (arXiv 2505.10251; Science Robotics 2025)
sources.claim: Nearest robotic capability to arterial raising/ligation: the SRT-H system autonomously performed the dissection, clipping and cutting steps of a cholecystectomy on ex vivo porcine gallbladders mounted in a fixed bench/phantom setup with a da Vinci Research Kit. It is step-level autonomy on one rehearsed procedure, not whole-case cadaver embalming.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous soft-tissue dissection and vessel/duct clipping. Transfer is NOT sufficient: the demo is a single rehearsed step on a standardized ex vivo organ in a laboratory rig, whereas the embalming instance requires opening skin on a variable human body, distinguishing and raising artery from vein, tying ligatures, cannulating both vessels, driving an injection machine while judging fluid distribution over 30-60 minutes, and closing the incision. No source shows any of the latter.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Autonomous robotic laparoscopic surgery for intestinal anastomosis (Science Robotics)
sources.claim: Nearest robotic capability for autonomous soft-tissue suturing: the STAR robot performed autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis in porcine tissue in a laboratory operating setup, with a surgeon supervising and near-infrared markers placed by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous suturing of soft tissue, which resembles ligating a raised vessel and closing the incision. It does not substantiate completion of this task: STAR performs one suture line on prepared, marked bowel in a lab, with a surgeon supervising; it does not locate or raise vessels, cannulate them, or operate an embalming machine.

sources.title: The VascuLogic VenousPro Can Improve Patient and Practitioner Experience
sources.claim: Nearest robotic capability for autonomous vascular access: the VenousPro image-guided venipuncture robot autonomously inserts a needle into a superficial arm vein in living patients, reporting high first-stick accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous needle placement in an arm vein. Transfer fails: embalming arterial injection is not percutaneous needle work but open dissection to raise, ligate and cannulate an artery and a drain vein in a pressureless, often clotted or edematous cadaver, followed by machine-driven perfusion and closure; the venipuncture robot performs none of these steps.

tasks.label: Remove the deceased from place of death and transport to funeral home.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nursing home / assisted living / inpatient hospice call: deceased (often 60-120 kg, limp, sometimes contracted or soiled) lies in a resident-room bed. Worker confirms identity/paperwork with staff, positions the removal cot beside the bed, sheet-transfers and bags/covers the body, secures straps, wheels it through corridors and elevators to a service exit avoiding residents and families, loads the cot into the removal van, drives to the funeral home, and unloads into the prep room or cooler.

Private residence removal (home hospice or unattended death): body may be in a hospital bed, on a couch, on the bathroom floor, or wedged in a narrow bedroom; cluttered rooms, pets, stairs, storm doors, family members present. Worker maneuvers a cot or uses a stair-chair/scoop, sometimes with a partner, removes the body with dignity past grieving relatives, loads into the van, drives back, and unloads at the funeral home.

Hospital release: body is in a patient room bed or already in the hospital morgue cooler on a tray or rack. Worker signs release forms, transfers the body onto the removal cot, moves it through service corridors and elevators to a loading dock, secures and loads the van, drives to the funeral home, and unloads to the prep room.

Medical examiner / coroner facility release: body is bagged on a rack or tray in a county morgue, sometimes autopsied, refrigerated or in poor condition. Worker completes chain-of-custody paperwork, slides the body onto the cot, loads the van at the morgue dock, drives to the funeral home, and unloads.

Removal from an uncontrolled scene: accident or crime scene under police direction, outdoor location, workplace, or a decomposed/traumatic case; uneven ground, weather, bystanders, non-standard positioning (floor, ditch, vehicle), requiring pouches, backboards, and sometimes a long drive back to the funeral home.

sources.developer: RIKEN and Sumitomo Riko Company Limited
sources.title: Engineering a robot that assists in direct nursing care
sources.claim: ROBEAR, the most-cited human-lifting care robot, can lift a person from a bed into a ... in laboratory demonstrations, but it is an experimental machine directed by a caregiver, and its developers state no such robot had been deployed in care facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting an adult human body from a bed. Closest analogue to transferring a deceased body onto a removal cot; cited to show the state of the art is an unfielded lab demo, not a system that could complete the removal.

sources.title: Battlefield Extraction-Assist Robot | Military Wiki
sources.claim: The Battlefield Extraction-Assist Robot, designed to pick up and carry a human body out of an environment, is remotely controlled rather than autonomous, and was a research/testing program rather than a fielded product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving and carrying an incapacitated human body from a found location. It is the nearest demonstrated capability to body removal, but it is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Aurora Begins Commercial Driverless Trucking in Texas, Ushering in a New Era of Freight
sources.claim: Driverless Class 8 trucks now run commercial freight on public highways without a human in the cab, covering only the road-transport leg of the task and not any loading, body handling, or building navigation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous on-road vehicle operation. It substantiates only the driving sub-step of the removal call; the instance also requires lifting, bagging, and cot handling, which this system cannot do.

sources.system: Patient transport / transfer robots (Robotic Bed, SASUKE, RIBA class)
sources.developer: Panasonic, Muscle Corp., RIKEN (survey by Frontiers in Robotics and AI authors)
sources.title: A Survey of Robotic Systems for Nursing Care
sources.claim: Academic surveys of nursing robotics list patient lift-and-transfer robots (Robotic Bed, SASUKE, RIBA-type machines) as research projects, indicating no commercially deployed robot that autonomously moves an adult body between a bed and a wheeled transport surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized transfer of a human body between support surfaces. Establishes that such systems remain projects/prototypes rather than systems performing the transfer at worker quality with limited intervention.

tasks.label: Perform the duties of funeral directors, including coordinating funeral activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Attach trocar to pump-tube, start pump, and repeat probing to force embalming fluid into organs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine unautopsied adult in a funeral-home preparation room after arterial injection: embalmer inserts a large trocar about two inches left of and superior to the navel, fan-probes to puncture and aspirate stomach, intestines, bladder, heart and lungs, then attaches the trocar to the cavity-fluid pump/gravity tube and re-probes the abdominal and thoracic cavities to distribute 16-32 oz of cavity chemical, finishing with a trocar button.

Difficult unautopsied case: obese, edematous, gas-distended, jaundiced or partly decomposed body. Requires heavier force to penetrate, repeated re-probing to reach organs, clearing clogged trocar/tubing of solids and clots, extra cavity chemical, re-aspiration hours later, and control of purge and leakage.

Autopsied body: viscera treated in the bag with cavity chemical, cavity walls swabbed/painted, and the trocar attached to the pump/hypo tube used for limited hypodermic and cavity-wall treatment of the shoulders, upper extremities, thighs and pelvic area before the incisions are closed and packed.

Small or altered-anatomy case: infant/child, or organ- and tissue-donor body with removed viscera and packing; smaller-gauge trocar or infant trocar, reduced fluid volumes, careful probing to avoid distortion of visible surfaces.

High-volume trade/central embalming facility or hospital morgue prep room: same aspiration-and-cavity-injection sequence performed on many bodies per shift with standardized tables, aspirators and machines, under time pressure and infection-control protocols.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich (Virtopsy project)
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine
sources.claim: Virtobot 2.0 is a robotic system installed at a forensic-medicine institute that performs automated, CT-image-guided placement of introducer needles into corpses for tissue and liquid sampling; needle-placement accuracy was measured on a biopsy phantom, and routine use to date has been for surface documentation.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: autonomous insertion of a rigid needle through the body wall of a human cadaver inside a mortuary/forensic facility, i.e. comparable object and environment. It does not transfer to cavity embalming: Virtobot places single planned needles to CT-defined targets (accuracy validated on a phantom) and performs no repeated blind fan-probing of hollow organs, no suction/aspiration management, no attachment to a cavity-fluid pump and no injection of chemical, so it does not substantiate completion of this task at any tier.

sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: SRT-H, built on the da Vinci Research Kit, autonomously performed the dissection/clipping/cutting steps of gallbladder removal on ex vivo pig tissue in a laboratory bench setup with endoscopic visual feedback.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous instrument manipulation in soft biological tissue. Transfer fails for cavity embalming because SRT-H works on excised, fixtured tissue under direct endoscopic vision on a research bench, whereas trocar cavity treatment is performed blind inside an intact human torso using anatomical landmarks and tactile feedback, with aspiration, clog clearing and fluid-distribution judgment that were not demonstrated.

sources.title: Humanoid robots perform live surgery in world first (Fox News)
sources.claim: The first use of general-purpose humanoid robots to perform minimally invasive surgery in live animals was reported in July 2026, and the robots were under continuous human teleoperation rather than autonomous control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose humanoid manipulation of medical instruments on a body. It cannot support a positive judgment because the demonstrations are continuously teleoperated, which the rating rules exclude, and they involve laparoscopic surgery on live pigs rather than autonomous trocar aspiration and cavity injection on human remains.

tasks.label: Reshape or reconstruct disfigured or maimed bodies when necessary, using dermasurgery techniques and materials such as clay, cotton, plaster of Paris, and wax.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Funeral home preparation room: minor facial restoration on an otherwise intact body — suturing or waxing small lacerations, abrasions, IV/tracheostomy and catheter sites, pressure sores or skin tears; filling shallow depressions with restorative wax, feathering edges, sealing and blending with opaque cosmetics so the area is invisible at viewing distance.

Restoration after a full autopsy or after tissue/bone donation: rebuilding the cranial vault contour and scalp line with plaster of Paris, cotton and mastic; re-suturing and sealing thoracic and cranial incisions; restoring limb and neck contour where bone or long tissue was recovered, then re-draping so nothing shows above the casket line.

Correcting emaciation, dehydration or edema from long illness: tissue-building injections, cotton or wax packing in sunken cheeks, temples, eye sockets and neck, or reduction of swollen features, matched to a family-supplied photograph so the deceased looks like themselves rather than like the illness.

Severe traumatic disfigurement — motor vehicle crash, gunshot, fall, or industrial injury — requiring hours of reconstruction: wiring or splinting fractured bone, packing and suturing avulsed tissue, sculpting missing nose, lip, ear, cheek or jaw from wax and clay over a cotton/plaster armature, hair and eyebrow restoration, then color matching to surrounding skin.

Restoration of bodies with burns, advanced decomposition, skin slip or maceration: debriding and sealing damaged skin, wax coverage of large discolored or denuded areas, deodorizing and containment, and judging in consultation with the director how much of the body can be made presentable for a partial or full viewing.

sources.developer: Children's National Health System / Johns Hopkins University
sources.date: 2016-05 (Science Translational Medicine); follow-on autonomous anastomosis work 2022
sources.title: Supervised autonomous robotic soft tissue surgery | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot ... () performs supervised-autonomous suturing and cutting of soft tissue in laboratory/operating-room settings on ex vivo and in vivo porcine bowel — the closest robotic capability to suturing/tissue handling on a body, but limited to a single repetitive sub-step on fixtured tissue with a surgeon supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue suturing. It shares soft, deformable biological tissue with restorative art, but it executes one pre-selected stitching routine on presented tissue; it does not assess a disfigurement, choose materials, sculpt missing anatomy, or match a likeness, so it does not carry over to completing a reconstruction.

sources.system: SculptDiff / hierarchical text-to-3D robotic clay shaping
sources.title: SculptDiff: Learning Robotic Clay Sculpting from Humans with Goal Conditioned Diffusion Policy
sources.claim: SculptDiff and follow-on work demonstrate autonomous robotic clay sculpting, but only of simple coarse 3D target shapes (letters, cones, cylinders) on a lab table, far below the anatomical fidelity and surface finish required for facial restoration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous clay sculpting. Materials overlap (clay/wax-like deformables), but demonstrated goals are simple geometric shapes on a fixtured block of clay, not building a recognizable human feature onto irregular damaged tissue, so capability does not transfer to this task.

sources.system: Virtobot / mobile autonomous surface-scanning robot for legal medicine
sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich / partners
sources.title: A mobile robotic approach to autonomous surface scanning in legal medicine
sources.claim: Robotic systems do operate on human remains in forensic-medicine facilities: a mobile robot autonomously plans viewpoints and performs 3D surface scanning of a corpse, and the Virtobot system performs automated post-mortem needle biopsy. These are imaging and needle-insertion tasks, not restoration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic work on a cadaver in a mortuary. It establishes that a robot can sense and position around a body, but it only scans or inserts a needle; no manipulation, sculpting, or restoration of tissue is performed, so it cannot substantiate completion of reconstruction.

sources.system: 3D-printed facial prosthesis workflow at Beijing funeral parlor
sources.developer: Babaoshan Funeral Home (Beijing) with partner lab
sources.title: Beijing's funeral parlor uses 3D tech to recreate faces for the deceased - People's Daily Online
sources.claim: Machine assistance in restorative art that exists in practice is confined to 3D-printed facial prostheses produced from a photograph at funeral parlors; a human technician still models, fits, colors and blends the piece onto the deceased.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fabrication of a replacement facial part. A 3D printer makes a component off-body; the reshaping of the actual remains — attaching, packing, waxing, texturing and color-matching — remains entirely manual, so it does not substantiate robotic completion of the instance.

tasks.label: Pack body orifices with cotton saturated with embalming fluid to prevent escape of gases or waste matter.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine unautopsied adult case in a funeral home preparation room: after arterial and cavity treatment the embalmer tears/rolls cotton, saturates it with cavity or embalming fluid, and packs the nostrils and the throat (via the mouth, with long forceps) firmly enough to block purge, then repositions features, closes the mouth and checks the face for distortion from over-packing.

Difficult case in a prep room — autopsied, traumatic, decomposed, edematous or long-refrigerated body: heavy packing of throat, nasal passages, cranial cavity (autopsied calvarium), and any wounds/tracheostomy or drain sites, with repeated re-checks and re-packing over hours as purge continues; tissue is fragile or leaking.

Case requiring packing of the lower orifices (anus, vagina) plus nose and throat: the embalmer must roll and turn a heavy, limp adult body on the table, spread tissue, insert saturated cotton with forceps deep enough to hold, and confirm no seepage before dressing.

Infant, child, or very small/fragile body (including autopsy-released neonates) in a prep room: tiny orifices, delicate tissue, small cotton wads and fine instruments, with cosmetic appearance for viewing paramount.

Off-site or field work: embalming or post-embalming packing done at a private residence, a rural home, a hospital/nursing-home morgue with improvised space, or a disaster/temporary mortuary, using portable equipment on a cot or table in a room taken as found.

sources.system: SR-NOCS autonomous swab robot (Lifeline Robotics / University of Southern Denmark)
sources.developer: University of Southern Denmark / Lifeline Robotics
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: An autonomous swab robot station inserted swabs into the noses and throats of 52 human subjects under force-compliant control in clinical studies, showing autonomous instrument insertion into a human orifice — but with a rigid pre-mounted swab, a cooperative seated subject with head positioning, and a single simple insertion, not manipulation of saturated cotton wads with forceps into multiple cavities of a cadaver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic swab insertion into the nasal/oral cavity. It is the closest demonstrated robotic action on a human orifice, but it inserts a rigid held swab a fixed depth into a positioned living head; embalming orifice packing requires tearing, saturating and forceps-packing deformable cotton to a firm fill in throat, nose and lower orifices of a limp body, which the system does not do.

sources.system: RPMB robotic post-mortem biopsy system (UKE Hamburg / TUHH)
sources.developer: Hamburg University of Technology and University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf
sources.title: Robotic Tissue Sampling for Safe Post-mortem Biopsy in Infectious Corpses (arXiv 2201.12168 / IEEE TMRB)
sources.claim: A robotic post-mortem biopsy system with automatic insertion planning took needle biopsies from 20 human corpses inside body bags in a forensic-medicine CT suite, showing robots can act on cadavers in an institutional mortuary setting, but only for planned rigid-needle punctures, not orifice packing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic instrument insertion into a human cadaver in a mortuary. It shares the workpiece (a deceased body) and an institutional setting, but the action is a CT-planned needle puncture under clinician supervision; it involves no deformable-material handling, no forceps packing and no assessment of a firm, leak-proof fill.

sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help (ScienceDaily / Science Robotics)
sources.claim: The STAR robot autonomously performed intestinal anastomosis on live pigs, the most advanced autonomous soft-tissue manipulation demonstrated, but in a laparoscopic laboratory setup with markers and a purpose-built suturing end effector, not free-form packing of cotton into body cavities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of soft biological tissue. It shows dexterous autonomous work on deformable anatomy, but with a specialized suturing tool on marker-tagged, laparoscopically exposed tissue; it does not demonstrate grasping, saturating and packing loose cotton into anatomical orifices to a judged firmness.

tasks.label: Conduct interviews to arrange for the preparation of obituary notices, to assist with the selection of caskets or urns, and to determine the location and time of burials or cremations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Insert convex celluloid or cotton between eyeballs and eyelids to prevent slipping and sinking of eyelids.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult case in a funeral home preparation room: body supine on a porcelain table, eyes nearly closed and tissue in good condition. Embalmer separates each eyelid, slides a convex plastic eye cap over the globe under upper and lower lids, seats the barbed surface against the lid lining, and closes the lids to a natural, symmetric line before or during arterial injection.

Dehydrated, emaciated or elderly case (long illness, ICU, hospice) with sunken globes and hollow orbits: eye caps alone leave a depressed contour, so the embalmer adds cotton or tissue-builder padding beneath the cap, judges contour by eye against photographs, and adjusts padding until the closed lids look natural.

Case presenting with partially open, rigid, or adhered lids and a dried cornea: embalmer must massage/relieve rigor around the orbit, moisten and gently free the lid margins and lashes, then place the cap and secure the lids with eye adhesive so they do not gap during viewing days later.

Trauma, autopsied, or post-donation case: periorbital swelling, lacerations, or an orbit emptied by corneal/eye enucleation. Requires packing the orbit with cotton, sometimes building a mound to support the cap, restoring lid position and symmetry before cosmetic work.
Infant or small child case: very small orbits, delicate lids and lashes, often miniature caps or a shaped cotton pledget only, with high cosmetic scrutiny by family.

Delayed/refrigerated or early-decomposition case with fragile, slipping skin around the eyes: lids and conjunctiva tear easily, so placement must be made with minimal traction, sometimes substituting cotton for a rigid cap.

sources.title: Lash Extensions From An AI Robot: Is This The Future Of Beauty?
sources.claim: Luum's lash robot applies individual eyelash extensions to a client's lashes in a salon, working millimeters from the eye under a lash artist's supervision — the closest commercial precedent for machine work at the eyelid margin, but it does not retract lids or place any object on the eyeball.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching extensions to eyelashes on a living, prepped client. Transfer fails for eye-cap setting: the client's lids are taped/held by a human artist, the robot never separates lids, never places a convex cap on the globe, and never restores orbital contour with cotton on a flaccid cadaver.

sources.system: ARTAS iX / iXi Robotic Hair Restoration System
sources.title: ARTAS® Robotic Hair Transplant | Venus Treatments USA
sources.claim: The ARTAS iX robot autonomously harvests and implants hair follicles on the human scalp under physician supervision, showing image-guided sub-millimetre robotic work on human skin, but only on a rigid, tensioned scalp with a fixed frame — not on mobile eyelid tissue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise robotic manipulation of human skin/hair. Transfer fails: the scalp is flattened and immobilised by a mechanical tensioner and the tool only punches and inserts along one axis; no eyelid separation, no placement of a formed cap under a lid, no cosmetic contour judgement.

sources.developer: University of Zurich Institute of Forensic Medicine (Virtopsy project)
sources.title: Virtobot - A Robot System for Optical 3D Scanning in Forensic Medicine
sources.claim: The Virtobot system performs image-guided, automated needle placement into cadavers in a forensic institute's scanner room, showing that robots can act on human remains in a purpose-built setting, but only for needle trajectories, not delicate facial feature setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic intervention on a cadaver in a mortuary/forensic facility. Transfer fails: a single rigid needle inserted along a planned trajectory does not demonstrate bimanual separation of eyelids, grasping and seating a convex cap on the globe, or the cosmetic acceptance standard of feature setting.

sources.system: Autonomous intraocular microsurgical robot (targeted retinal injection)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic intraocular surgery for targeted retinal injections | Science Robotics
sources.claim: Autonomous microsurgical robots have performed targeted retinal injections inside the eye, but only through a fixed trocar port in an already-opened, immobilised eye in a laboratory/surgical setting; nothing in this line of work manipulates the external eyelids.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic manipulation at the eye. Transfer fails: the instrument enters through a surgeon-made port in a speculum-held eye; the robot never opens lids, handles cotton, or places an eye cap, and the demonstration is a research prototype.

tasks.label: Assist with placing caskets in hearses and organize cemetery processions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Funeral home: after the visitation/chapel service the casketed body (casket plus remains, commonly 300-500 lb) is closed, rolled on a church truck through hallways and the porte-cochere, and slid onto the hearse's roller deck; flowers and pall handled, family often watching, no scratching or jarring permitted.

Off-site venue (parish church, synagogue, private chapel, fraternal hall): the hearse is unloaded at the curb or steps, the casket is wheeled or hand-carried with pallbearers up steps and through narrow doors to a bier at the front, then reloaded after the service; layouts differ at every venue, with weather and crowds of mourners.

Graveside at the cemetery: the hearse stops on a cemetery lane, the casket is taken out and moved over turf (often soft, sloped or muddy) under a tent to the lowering device over the open grave/vault, flowers arranged; after the committal the casket is lowered and the vault sealed.

Organizing the cemetery procession: staging hearse, family coach and private cars in the funeral home lot, affixing funeral flags/placards and instructing drivers on headlights and spacing, coordinating the police escort, leading the cortege on public streets and routing it to the correct cemetery section and grave.

Delivery to a crematory or mausoleum: the hearse backs to the receiving door, the casket is unloaded onto a trolley or charging bier, moved through back-of-house, and charged into the cremator or placed into a crypt.

sources.title: Insertion Machines of different types - Höganäs Borgestad
sources.claim: Crematec insertion (charging) machines transfer a coffin containing remains from a presented bier into the fixed opening of a cremator through a fully automatic powered sequence, in a purpose-built crematorium charging room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: charging a casket into a cremator. Same object (full-size casket with remains, hundreds of kg) and the same motion as sliding a casket onto a hearse deck or into a crypt from a fixed bier, with the same no-damage precision requirement, in a purpose-built setting.

sources.title: American Crematory Equipment Catalog
sources.claim: A US-marketed automatic crematory charger drives full-size caskets weighing up to 1000 lb from the charging bier into the retort without manual pushing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine transfer of a loaded casket from a fixtured bier into a fixed opening; the payload class (caskets up to 1000 lb) matches the caskets embalmers load into hearses and set into vaults or crypts.

sources.system: Lastel automated coffin storage and delivery system
sources.title: Japan's death industry reaps grim profits (NBC News / Reuters)
sources.claim: The Lastel funeral facility in Yokohama stores coffins containing bodies in a refrigerated automated storage system and delivers them through hatches into viewing rooms when families arrive.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine storage and presentation of coffins holding remains. It shows automated, dignified conveyance of casketed remains from a storage position to a designated presentation position in a purpose-built facility - the same transfer as placing a casket at a bier or in a hearse when the work is fixtured.

sources.system: Daifuku automated columbarium (AS/RS with stacker cranes)
sources.title: Innovating Remembrance – The Elegance of the Automated Columbarium | DAIFUKU
sources.claim: Automated columbarium systems use stacker cranes to store and retrieve urns of cremated remains and deliver them to a designated altar position on request.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated placement of human remains into a fixed niche and retrieval for ceremony - the entombment/placement step of interment performed by machine in a purpose-built memorial building.

sources.system: LoadMatic / LoadMatic Lite automated trailer loading system
sources.title: Simplify The Transition to Automated Truck Loading with LoadMatic Lite | The Joloda Hydraroll Group
sources.claim: Automated truck loading systems move palletised loads from a fixed conveyor position directly into a docked road vehicle's cargo deck automatically at the touch of a ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring a heavy rigid load from a fixed presentation point into the deck of a docked road vehicle over rollers/skates - mechanically the same as sliding a casket into a hearse fitted with a roller deck when the vehicle is docked at a fixed loading position.

tasks.label: Maintain records, such as itemized lists of clothing or valuables delivered with body and names of persons embalmed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Wash and dry bodies, using germicidal soap and towels or hot air dryers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-embalming wash in a funeral home preparation room: an intact adult decedent lies on a porcelain embalming table; the embalmer sprays/sponges the whole exterior with germicidal soap solution, washes face and hair, cleans hands and nails, rolls the limp (or rigid) body to wash the back and buttocks, rinses and dries with towels.

Post-embalming wash and dry on the same table: after arterial injection and cavity work the body is rewashed to remove blood, embalming chemicals and drainage, incisions and orifices are cleaned, hair is shampooed and blown dry with a hot air dryer, and the whole body is towel-dried and positioned before dressing and casketing.

Difficult-condition case in the prep room: autopsied body with cranial and torso sutures, trauma/road-accident case, early decomposition with skin slip, edematous or bariatric (300+ lb) decedent; requires gentle low-pressure washing, extra germicidal soaking of soiled areas, careful lifting/turning with a lift assist, and blotting dry without tearing fragile skin.

Infectious or heavily soiled case: decedent with contagious disease, C. diff/MRSA, or extensive fecal/urine/purge contamination; embalmer in full PPE washes and rewashes the body with germicidal soap, disinfects the table and surroundings, and dries with disposable towels.

Non-embalming or ritual case in the mortuary prep room or a hospital morgue: body bathed and dried for refrigeration, direct cremation, green burial, or identification/viewing; sometimes performed with family or clergy present (e.g., ritual washing observed), requiring modesty draping and a specified sequence of washing and drying.
Infant, child, or fetal remains: very small, fragile body washed by hand with germicidal soap in a basin or on the table, gently dried with soft towels, hair dried, before dressing for viewing.

sources.system: Mirai Ningen Sentakuki (Future Human Washing Machine)
sources.date: 2025-11 to 2026-03 (Expo debut 2025-04; on sale from late 2025)
sources.title: Japan's Human Washing Machine Is Here and You Can Try It for Free — Tokyo Weekender
sources.claim: Science Co.'s 'Mirai Ningen Sentakuki' is a commercially sold, fully automatic bathing pod that washes, rinses and air-dries a living occupant head to toe in about 15 minutes; the occupant walks in, reclines and the machine runs its cycle. It performs no manipulation, turning or scrubbing of an unresponsive body and uses fine bubbles rather than germicidal soap.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated bathing of a living person. Object is a human body and the action is wash+dry, but the transfer fails: the pod requires a self-supporting, cooperative occupant who enters and holds a reclined posture, applies no germicidal soap, cannot turn a body to wash the back or clean purge/soiling, and its AI cycle is regulated by the occupant's vital signs.

sources.system: Miraburu Assist Bath (ミラブル アシストバス)
sources.title: Expo-Inspired 'Human Washing Machine' Tech Debuts in Japan's Nursing Care, Slashing Bathing Burdens — BigGo Finance
sources.claim: The nursing-care derivative of the same technology, 'Miraburu Assist Bath', was introduced at an assisted-living home in Osaka in June 2026; it cleans by soaking the bather in microbubbles with no cleaning agent, and is aimed at reducing the burden on caregivers rather than replacing hands-on washing of an immobile body.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assisted bathing of frail elderly. Closest deployed system to whole-body washing of a non-ambulatory person, but it is a walk-in tub for living residents, uses no germicidal agent, does not dry or reposition the body, and has never been shown used on decedents.

sources.title: Panasonic News Release: HOSPI-Rimo and new models of hair-washing robot
sources.claim: Panasonic's hair-washing robot autonomously performs a complete hair-wash cycle (wetting, shampoo, rinse, conditioning, drying) on a person reclining at a washstand; it was a prototype shown at exhibitions and trialed with hospitals, covering only the hair sub-step of the task.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated shampooing. Covers only hair washing/drying of a living seated person whose head is placed in a basin; it is a sub-step of the instance and does not wash or dry the body.

sources.title: Bathing assistive devices and robots for the elderly — ScienceDirect review
sources.claim: The I-SUPPORT robotic bathing platform is a research prototype (soft robotic arm plus motorized chair in a shower cabin) that assists elderly users with parts of the showering sequence; the user remains an active participant and the system was validated in clinical trial installations, not deployed commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic washing of a human body. It assists rather than completes the wash, works only with a seated cooperative living user, and has no capability to lift, turn, dry or handle a decedent.

sources.title: Robots closer to performing bed baths (w/ Video) — Phys.org
sources.claim: Georgia Tech's Cody robot autonomously executed wiping motions that cleaned debris from a person's arm and leg, a research step toward robotic bed baths; it cleaned small marked areas of skin on a compliant living subject.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bed bathing. Demonstrates only localized wiping of exposed limbs of a cooperative living subject in a lab; no whole-body wash, no turning, no drying, no germicidal disinfection.

sources.developer: Sharif University of Technology (A. Meghdari et al.)
sources.title: Automated Processes of Preparing and Washing Deceased during Pandemic (ResearchGate)
