sources.claim: The only published machine specifically intended to wash and dry a deceased human body, the 'PaakShooy' semi-automatic corpse washing/drying/shrouding cell, exists as a conceptual design with simulation and animation; no built, operating installation is documented.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (washing and drying a deceased body) but only a conceptual design, graphic simulation and animation; no hardware demonstration is reported, so it cannot substantiate completion at any tier.

tasks.label: Arrange for transporting the deceased to another state for interment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform special procedures necessary for remains that are to be transported to other states or overseas, or where death was caused by infectious disease.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Domestic out-of-state shipment by common carrier: in the funeral home preparation room, the embalmer performs a thorough arterial embalming with a higher-index fluid and full cavity treatment, aspirates and re-aspirates, seals orifices with packing, applies leak-proof plastic garments and absorbent, dresses and caskets the remains, then places the casket in an air tray or combination shipping unit, secures/straps it, and attaches burial-transit permit and shipping documents for airline or livery pickup.

Overseas repatriation: embalming performed to the destination country's/consulate's standards (often documented certificate of embalming), remains dressed and placed in a hermetically sealed zinc- or lead-lined casket whose liner is soldered/gasket-sealed and pressure-relieved, the casket crated in a wooden air-freight box, and the shipment prepared with consular, customs, and airline known-shipper paperwork.

Death from a common infectious disease (hepatitis B/C, HIV, tuberculosis, MRSA, COVID-19): embalmer works in full PPE with enhanced ventilation, does thorough topical and internal disinfection of the remains before and after arterial injection, uses stronger disinfectant/arterial chemicals, manages sharps and aspirated fluids per OSHA bloodborne-pathogen rules, then decontaminates the prep room, instruments, and table and bags regulated medical waste.

Complicated case being shipped: autopsied, organ/tissue-donor, obese, traumatic, or partly decomposed remains requiring multi-point (six-point) injection, hypodermic and surface treatment, packing and extra suturing of autopsy or recovery incisions, sealing powders/gels to guarantee leak-proof transport, and restorative work so the remains are acceptable on arrival at the receiving funeral home.

Highly hazardous or no-embalm case (viral hemorrhagic fever, prion/CJD, jurisdictions or families prohibiting embalming of an infectious decedent): remains kept in a sealed leak-proof pouch that is not opened, exterior of the pouch disinfected, pouch placed directly into a sealed casket or shipping container, container sealed and labeled, and health-department/airline authorizations obtained for transport.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Bern / University of Zurich
sources.title: Virtobot--a multi-functional robotic system for 3D surface scanning and automatic post mortem biopsy
sources.claim: The Virtobot is an industrial six-axis robot in a forensic-medicine imaging suite that performs 3D surface scanning of bodies and automatic image-guided post-mortem needle biopsy on cadavers with ~3.2 mm accuracy; it does not perform vascular access, embalming, packing, dressing, or casketing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated needle biopsy of a cadaver in a mortuary/forensic setting. It shows a robot can register to a body and place a needle, but the embalming task requires raising and cannulating vessels through an incision, ligating, monitoring drainage and distribution, trocar cavity aspiration, suturing, dressing and sealing a shipping container. No part of that sequence is demonstrated, so the transfer does not support completing any instance.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot autonomously performed intestinal anastomosis suturing on live pigs, showing autonomous soft-tissue suturing on a single, presented, fixtured tissue target in a research operating room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue suturing, comparable in tissue type to closing embalming incisions. It is a single sub-step performed on tissue already exposed and presented by humans in a lab; it does not cover whole-body positioning, vessel raising, fluid injection and distribution, cavity aspiration, disinfection, dressing or container sealing, so it cannot substantiate completion of any instance.

sources.title: Hospitals Set Disinfection Records; LightStrike Germ-Zapping Robots Complete 35 Million Cycles in Healthcare Facilities Worldwide
sources.claim: Xenex LightStrike ultraviolet robots are commercially deployed in over 1,000 healthcare facilities to disinfect room surfaces; they are wheeled units positioned by staff and only irradiate surfaces, performing no manipulation of bodies, instruments, or containers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: terminal room disinfection in a healthcare facility, which resembles decontaminating a preparation room after an infectious case. It covers only ambient surface irradiation after humans have removed the remains and cleaned the surfaces; it cannot disinfect or handle the remains themselves, so it substantiates no instance.

sources.title: Development of a nursing-care assistant robot RIBA that can lift a human in its arms
sources.claim: RIBA, a nursing-care assistant robot with human-type arms, was demonstrated transferring a person between a bed and a wheelchair, but it is a research prototype guided by an operator's tactile input rather than an autonomous body-handling system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and transferring a full human body, the handling core of moving remains into a pouch, casket, or shipping tray. The demonstration is operator-guided rather than autonomous and involves a cooperative living person, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment for any instance.

tasks.label: Supervise funeral attendants and other funeral home staff.

tasks.label: Serve as pallbearers, attend visiting rooms, and provide other assistance to the bereaved.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Attending a visitation/viewing at the funeral home: greeting and directing arriving mourners, managing the register book and memorial folders, staffing the room for 2-4 hours, adjusting the casket lid, flowers, lighting and seating, answering questions, responding to distressed guests, and closing the casket at the end.

Serving as pallbearer/casket bearer at the funeral home or church: rolling the casket on a church truck through chapel doors, hand-carrying a 200-400 lb casket with five other bearers through doorways and down entry steps, loading and securing it into the hearse, all in view of the family and in coordination with the funeral director's cues.

Pallbearing and committal at the cemetery: unloading the casket from the hearse, carrying it over turf, gravel and slopes to the grave, setting it on the lowering device above the open excavation, and handling flowers and the pall, in rain, heat, mud or snow.

Direct personal assistance to bereaved individuals: escorting elderly or infirm family members to seats and to the limousine, offering an arm or a wheelchair, fetching water, tissues or a chair, steadying someone who becomes faint, carrying personal effects, and returning the deceased's jewelry or belongings to the family.

Setting up and breaking down service spaces: arranging chairs in rows in the chapel, placing the register stand, photo easels and podium, positioning floral tributes around the casket, then after the service loading flower arrangements into family vehicles and resetting the room, plus tent and chair setup graveside.

sources.system: DFW Europe AIM automatic charging bier (Automatic Insert Machine)
sources.title: Charging Bier DFW Europe Manual / Automatic Coffin Insert Machine
sources.claim: Commercially marketed automatic charging biers transfer an adult coffin from a transport trolley into a cremator fully automatically after a single touch-screen activation, in a purpose-built crematorium charging bay.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bearing a coffin to its final position (cremator hearth rather than hearse or grave). Same object class and mass (adult coffin), same requirement for damage-free, dignified placement at a fixed target, executed in a purpose-built setting where the coffin arrives fixtured on a trolley - the E1 form of the pallbearing instance.

sources.system: Lingzhou series AGV remains transport robots (LINGZHOU 1/2/3)
sources.date: October 2024 product pages; site updated February 2025

sources.claim: A funeral-industry manufacturer sells a line of AGV remains-transport robots that move coffins and remains of 100-500 kg autonomously inside funeral homes, crematoriums and morgues, positioning them at designated locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: internal coffin transport in funeral facilities. Same object (coffin, comparable mass) and same destination-positioning requirement as casket bearing, but on flat prepared floors along fixed routes, without stairs, hearse loading, or a procession of mourners.

sources.system: Lastel automated coffin storage and delivery system
sources.title: Japan's Lastel 'Corpse' Hotel Allows Check in Only to the Dead
sources.claim: A deployed Japanese funeral facility uses an automated storage-and-retrieval system that delivers chilled coffins through hatches into viewing rooms where families pay respects; human employees still arrange the flowers and receive the bereaved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: presenting the coffin in a viewing room. It automates only the coffin-delivery sub-step through a purpose-built hatch; press coverage of the same facility shows an employee adjusting flowers inside the viewing room, so attending the room itself remains human work.

sources.title: Pepper the robot to work as a Buddhist priest for cut-price funerals
sources.claim: The only robot fielded in a funeral-service role performs a purely ceremonial, non-manipulative function: a humanoid programmed to chant Buddhist sutras at ....
sources.transferJustification: Directly in the funeral-hall setting, but the system has no load-bearing manipulation (Pepper's payload is a few hundred grams) and performs no casket handling, room attendance duties, or physical assistance to mourners.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: The most mature commercial humanoid mobile manipulation in a structured human facility is limited to moving standardized totes and stacking containers on flat warehouse floors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile pick-and-place of uniform containers in an E2 facility. It bounds today's envelope - standardized rigid totes, no people-facing service, no multi-person coordinated carry, no handling of heterogeneous flowers, chairs or caskets.

sources.title: 1X's $20,000 NEO Humanoid Robot Launches With A Catch: It Needs Humans To Do Your Chores
sources.claim: Consumer humanoids marketed for people-facing household assistance still require a remote human operator for essentially all complex tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general person-facing assistance in human spaces. Its reliance on teleoperation shows no fielded system autonomously escorts, steadies, or physically assists people, which is what assisting the bereaved requires.

tasks.label: Direct casket and floral display placement and arrange guest seating.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Funeral home chapel / visitation room setup before a viewing: roll the casket on a church truck into the front position and square it to the room, set the casket spray, arrange 10-30 floral pieces (easel sprays, baskets, potted plants) around and behind the casket with cards visible, then set out and align 50-100 folding or stacking chairs in rows with a center aisle and reserved family rows. Carpeted indoor room, staff only, done before guests arrive.

Service at a church, synagogue, fraternal hall or other outside venue: direct pallbearers and staff wheeling the casket up the aisle to the front/altar and set it on the church truck at the correct angle, place floral tributes per the venue's rules, and arrange reserved family seating (ribbons on pews, or added chairs). Layout differs by venue but the premises are institution-controlled.

Graveside / committal service at a cemetery: direct placement of the casket on the lowering device under the tent, set the casket spray and standing sprays around the grave and the greens, and set out two to four rows of folding chairs for the family on turf that may be sloped, soft or wet, in whatever weather is present.

Turnaround between back-to-back services: strip the chapel of the previous family's flowers (out to the flower car or cemetery), restack and re-set chairs into a different configuration for a larger or smaller crowd, reposition the casket for the procession, and re-dress the room for the next family, often within an hour.

Non-traditional venue: home visitation in a private residence, veterans hall, park pavilion or lodge - existing household furniture must be moved aside, the casket placed in a living room or hall, portable chairs carried in and set in rows, and flowers placed on side tables and stands in a space taken as found.

sources.date: 2023-02 (product line in commercial deployment for years; page updated 2025-11)
sources.title: Robotic Palletizing Systems | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC M-410 series palletizing robots, deployed commercially in fenced industrial cells, place heavy and bulky items (payloads to 700-800 kg) at programmed positions in flexible patterns, which is the geometric core of placing a casket, floral stands and chairs when the items are presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy-payload palletizing. It transfers to casket/floral/chair placement at E1 because the physical demand is the same - lifting a bulky 100-350 kg item presented at a known pose and setting it down at a programmed position and orientation with repeatable accuracy.

sources.title: Harvey - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: Harvest Automation's HV-100 mobile robots autonomously locate, pick up, transport and place potted plants into precise target positions on greenhouse and nursery beds, indoors and outdoors, with placement accuracy better than an inch, and are sold commercially to growers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nursery pot spacing. Comparable objects (potted plants/floral units of similar size and weight) and comparable precision (placing each unit at a specified position in a laid-out pattern), supporting floral display placement where the pieces are presented in a standardized way.

sources.developer: HKUST (Guangzhou), Robotics and Autonomous Systems Thrust
sources.title: ALORE: Autonomous Large-Object Rearrangement with a Legged Manipulator (arXiv)
sources.claim: ALORE, a legged manipulator system, autonomously rearranges large furniture - chairs, tables and bins - to target positions and orientations indoors; in a real-world trial it moved 32 chairs across 8 continuous loops over ~40 minutes without a failure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving chairs to commanded target poses. Same objects (chairs) and same output (chairs at specified positions/orientations) as 'arrange guest seating', though demonstrated in a research building rather than a chapel.

sources.system: DFW Europe AIM automatic charging bier / coffin insert machine
sources.date: 2018-01 product page (equipment in commercial crematorium use)
sources.title: Charging Bier DFW Europe Manual / Automatic Coffin Insert Machine
sources.claim: DFW Europe's Automatic Insert Machine (charging bier) receives a coffin from a transport trolley and transfers it into position fully automatically, including opening and closing the door - a commercial, purpose-built machine that positions a full-size coffin without a person handling it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated coffin transfer in a crematorium. Same object class and weight as a casket, and the same operation - moving a presented coffin along a fixed path to a defined final position - supporting casket placement when the work is brought to the machine.

sources.system: Automated columbarium ASRS (Ruriden / Shinjuku Rurikoin Byakurengedo / Kuramae Ryoen class facilities)

sources.claim: Japanese automated columbaria use a behind-the-scenes robotic storage-and-retrieval system that fetches the memorial urn/shrine and presents it at a viewing altar for arriving mourners, then returns it; these facilities are in commercial operation in Tokyo and Nagoya.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine placement of the memorial display in front of seated mourners. It shows a purpose-built funerary facility where the display object is positioned for guests entirely by machine, supporting the E1 counterfactual for casket/display placement.

sources.title: Event Hall - Chair Towing | SquareDog Robotics
sources.claim: SquareDog Robotics' Follower autonomously tows trolleys of folding chairs between storage and setup zones inside an event hall, reducing porter headcount during turnarounds - but it transports chair trolleys rather than setting individual chairs into rows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chair logistics in an as-found event venue (E2). It substantiates only the transport leg; no cited system unfolds, aligns and rows chairs, or arranges floral tributes and a casket, in an as-found venue.

tasks.label: Arrange funeral home equipment and perform general maintenance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Set up the chapel/visitation room before a service at a funeral home: roll out and align rows of folding or fixed chairs, position the church truck/bier and place the casket at the front, set flower stands and floral pieces, place the register stand, easels and portrait, adjust podium, lighting and AV. Work happens indoors in a fixed-layout room the firm controls; the arrangement must look precise and dignified before families arrive.

Tear down and reset after a service: wheel the casket on the church truck out to the hearse and load it, move flowers and easels out, fold/stack and re-rack chairs, return biers, drapes, church trucks and AV to storage, and reset the room for the next visitation, often on a same-day turnaround.

Prep-room turnaround and equipment maintenance after an embalming: wash down and disinfect the embalming table and floor, flush and service the embalming machine and hydroaspirator, clean/sanitize and sharpen instruments, change filters and traps, bag and stage biohazard and sharps waste, restock chemicals, gowns and gloves.

Routine cleaning of public areas of the funeral home: vacuum carpeted chapel, lobby and hallways, scrub/mop hard floors, clean and restock restrooms, and empty trash on a scheduled basis between services.

Building and grounds upkeep: replace burned-out bulbs, change HVAC filters, minor plumbing/carpentry/paint touch-ups, lubricate and service the casket lift, tighten church-truck and cot hardware, seasonal lawn mowing and snow/ice clearing of the lot and entry.
Fleet upkeep: wash, rinse and dry the exterior of the hearse, lead car and removal van so they are presentable for the next service, done at the funeral home lot or a nearby commercial wash bay.

sources.system: ALORE (legged manipulator large-object rearrangement system, HKUST-Guangzhou)

sources.claim: ALORE, a legged mobile manipulator, autonomously rearranged large objects including chairs to target positions and orientations in real-world trials, running 8 continuous loops moving 32 chairs over ~40 minutes without failure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: office chair/table rearrangement. Chairs are the same objects and target-pose precision that chapel seating setup requires; the demo shows autonomous multi-object placement rather than a single scripted move.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: returning seating to a specified layout. It shows chair-arrangement completed by machine when the room is purpose-built around the machine (motorized chairs plus ceiling tracking), which is the E1 counterfactual for room setup.

tasks.label: Assist coroners at death scenes or at autopsies, file police reports, and testify at inquests or in court, if employed by a coroner.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Coroner-employed embalmer/technician responds with the death investigator to an unattended death in a private residence: photographs and documents the body in situ, notes lividity/rigor, collects medications and personal effects, bags the decedent, lifts and maneuvers the remains (often heavy, in a bed, bathroom, or up/down stairs) onto a cot, and loads the van for transport to the morgue.

Scene response outdoors or in a public/industrial setting: roadway fatality, a body in a field or water, a workplace fall, or decomposed/traumatic remains. Work occurs in weather, alongside police and fire, requires careful recovery of fragmented or fragile remains and scene evidence before removal and transport.

Assisting at an autopsy in the coroner's/ME's morgue: receiving and identifying the body, undressing and photographing, X-rays, positioning on the table, assisting the pathologist with the Y-incision and evisceration, weighing and sectioning organs, collecting specimens/fluids, returning viscera, suturing the body closed, washing it, cleaning the suite and instruments, and preparing the decedent for release.

Preparing and filing investigative/police reports and case paperwork in the coroner's office: scene forms, chain-of-custody and property receipts, body-release and disposition documents, entries into the case management system.

Testifying at a coroner's inquest or in criminal/civil court about scene observations, identification, custody of remains, and autopsy assistance, including pretrial preparation with the prosecutor or coroner.

sources.system: Mobile robotic RGB-D surface scanning system (Hamburg University of Technology / Institute of Legal Medicine UKE)
sources.developer: Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH) with University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf
sources.title: A Mobile Robotic Approach to Autonomous Surface Scanning in Legal Medicine
sources.claim: A mobile robotic manipulator autonomously performs full-body RGB-D surface scanning of actual corpses inside a legal-medicine (forensic morgue) environment, automating only the external documentation step of the autopsy workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: photographic/external documentation of the decedent, one sub-step of assisting at an autopsy. It shows a robot working on real corpses in a morgue, but it does not handle, position, open, eviscerate, close, or clean the body.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Bern / Zurich
sources.title: Virtobot--a multi-functional robotic system for 3D surface scanning and automatic post mortem biopsy
sources.claim: The Virtobot robotic arm in a forensic medicine institute performs automated 3D surface scanning and CT-guided post-mortem needle biopsy of cadavers, i.e. imaging-based sub-steps of a virtual autopsy rather than the technician's autopsy-assist workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-mortem imaging and tissue sampling in a forensic institute. Comparable objects (cadavers) and setting, but the system only scans and places biopsy needles; it does not perform the manual handling, dissection assistance, closure, or cleanup that constitute the instance.

sources.title: RIBA the friendly robot nurse
sources.claim: A research nursing robot can lift a human body of up to ~61 kg between bed and wheelchair, but does so under a caregiver's tactile guidance and monitoring rather than autonomously, and only in a prepared indoor care setting.

It shows the state of the art is guided, low-capacity, flat-floor transfer in a care facility, well short of autonomous recovery of remains in a home or outdoors.

sources.title: Police 'Robot Dogs' Raise Concerns as More Departments Adopt Them
sources.claim: Legged robots fielded by US police at incident scenes are remotely operated reconnaissance platforms used for standoffs and hazardous incidents; they do not autonomously process scenes or handle remains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic presence at active incident scenes, the closest analogue to attending a death scene. The deployments are teleoperated observation only, with no body handling, evidence collection, or documentation output.

sources.claim: A prototype robotic autopsy saw / cadaveric skull-and-tissue cutting manipulator was built and preliminarily tested in an autopsy room, addressing a single cutting step of the autopsy.

tasks.label: Press diaphragm to evacuate air from lungs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult case: intact, unautopsied body lying supine on the porcelain embalming table in a funeral home preparation room; while setting features / before arterial injection, the embalmer places both hands on the lower thorax-upper abdomen and presses firmly to force residual air out of the lungs, watching for escape of air and any purge at the mouth or nose.

Large/obese or grossly edematous adult body on the prep table; heavy, sustained body-weight pressure is needed through a thick or fluid-filled abdominal wall, with a high chance of provoking stomach or lung purge that must be caught and aspirated as it comes.

Frail case: emaciated, very elderly, osteoporotic, or early-decomposition body; pressure must be judged and moderated to avoid fracturing ribs, tearing slipping skin, or driving out decomposition gas and purge onto the face and clothing.

Autopsied, organ-donor, or trauma case: thorax already opened, lungs or viscera removed or returned in a bag, sternum/ribcage cut; the maneuver must be adapted (pressed on remaining tissue, done during cavity work, or skipped) and combined with trocar aspiration.
Infant or small child case: very small, fragile thorax; light, carefully placed pressure with fingers or one hand on a body only a few pounds in weight.

sources.title: Product focus - AI and robot massage | spabusiness.com
sources.claim: Aescape is a commercially deployed, fully autonomous robotic massage system: a purpose-built table with two robotic arms that 3D-scans the body lying on it and applies programmed, adjustable pressure to the body's soft tissue without a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic massage. It is force-controlled contact with a whole human body presented on the machine's own table, localized from a 3D scan of the body's contours, at pressures comparable to a hand press on the trunk - the same physical operation the diaphragm press requires, minus the corpse-specific judgment.

sources.system: Aescape robotic massage tables at Equinox clubs
sources.title: Equinox, Aescape Launch Pre and Post-Workout Massages - Athletech News
sources.claim: Aescape's robots are in routine commercial service in gyms and spas at meaningful volume, indicating the scan-then-press behaviour works repeatably on many different human bodies, not just in demos.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (robotic massage); this item establishes deployment scale and reliability on varied human bodies.

sources.title: LUCAS 3, v3.1 chest compression system | Stryker
sources.claim: The LUCAS 3 mechanical chest compression device is a machine-controlled piston that, once clamped to a supine human torso, repeatedly compresses the thorax to a set depth of about 5.3 cm at 102 compressions per minute; tens of thousands of units are in emergency service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical chest compression. It is the same physical act on the same object - a machine pressing down on the lower sternum/thorax of a supine human body with tens of kilograms of force to displace the chest and expel lung air. The device's cycle runs under machine control once the body is presented and clamped, which is exactly the E1 condition of work brought fixtured to the machine.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted bed bathing. Cited to bound the frontier for contact with a body on a facility's own bed/table: only light compliant wiping has been shown, not judged heavy pressure on a corpse, which is why the prep-room (E2) case is not substantiated.

roles.title: Crematory Operators
roles.description: Operate crematory equipment to reduce human or animal remains to bone fragments in accordance with state and local regulations. Duties may include preparing the body for cremation and performing general maintenance on crematory equipment. May use traditional flame-based cremation, calcination, or alkaline hydrolysis.

tasks.label: Clean the crematorium, including tables, floors, and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily sweeping/vacuuming and mopping of the crematory room floor: fine bone ash and soot settle around the retort, plus spills; the room is small and furniture-dense (gurneys, cooling pans, container stock, lift table) with sealed concrete floors.

Wiping down and disinfecting the stainless prep/transfer table, cot/gurney and adjacent counters after body handling: spray disinfectant, wipe hard nonporous surfaces to a visibly clean, sanitary standard.

Post-cremation cleanout of the retort chamber: raking and brushing residual ash and fragments off the warm hearth into the cooling pan, clearing spalled refractory/brick debris, leaving the chamber clean before the next case (no carryover between decedents).

Cleaning the cremated-remains processing station between cases: brushing/vacuuming the cremulator or processor bowl, trays, magnet, scoops and the dust-covered processing table so that no remains carry over to the next family's cremains.
Periodic deeper facility cleaning: refrigeration/holding room and storage/garage floors, wiping soot and dust from the retort exterior, control panel, vent hoods, ledges and shelving.

tasks.label: Document divided remains to ensure parts are not misplaced.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crematory operator records, in the cremation log/chain-of-custody form, that a decedent's cremated remains were divided among multiple containers (e.g., an urn plus several keepsake urns) for different family members, noting the number of portions, their weights, and the recipient designated for each.

Operator enters into the crematory's tracking software/paper file the identification-tag number and disposition of partial or separated remains received from a hospital or anatomical program (amputated limb, fetal remains, surgical specimens) so the portion can be matched back to the correct case file.

Operator completes chain-of-custody paperwork when a portion of remains leaves the facility separately — shipped to a distant family member, sent for a scattering service, or retained for DNA/memorial diamond processing — recording carrier, date, and receipt signature.

Operator reconciles and audits divided-remains records at shift end or during a state inspection, cross-checking log entries, container labels, and identification-disc numbers against the case file and correcting discrepancies.

Operator documents unusual divisions — commingled or partial remains from a mass-fatality or disinterment case, or remains split between burial and cremation — writing a narrative note in the case record to explain the disposition of each part.

tasks.label: Embalm, dress, or otherwise prepare the deceased for viewing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full arterial embalming of an unautopsied adult in a funeral-home/crematory preparation room: position and disinfect the body, raise the common carotid or femoral vessel through an incision, insert cannula and drain tube, inject fluid with the embalming machine while massaging to distribute it and watching for distension or discoloration, aspirate the thoracic and abdominal cavities with a trocar, inject cavity fluid, suture and seal the incisions and trocar site.

Setting features and cosmetizing for an open-casket viewing: shave the face, close the mouth with needle injector or suture, place eye caps, wash and style the hair, apply massage cream, restorative wax and airbrush or hand-applied cosmetics to face, neck and hands to match a supplied photograph, and touch up after the family's first look.

Dressing and casketing: put underwear, hosiery, shirt or dress, trousers, jacket and shoes onto a heavy, limp or partly rigid body on a prep table (often cutting garments up the back), lift/transfer the body into the casket with a hoist or two-person lift, position the head on the pillow, cross and set the hands, and arrange clothing, jewelry and casket interior for viewing.

Minimal preparation before direct cremation with an identification or brief family viewing: wash and disinfect the unembalmed body, close eyes and mouth, comb hair, shroud or dress in simple clothing, place the body in a cremation container or rental casket in the crematory holding/viewing area, and position it presentably on the cot or in the container.

Difficult cases: autopsied, donor, trauma, decomposed, edematous, bariatric or infant remains requiring multi-point injection, cavity/viscera treatment, packing and suturing of postmortem incisions, restorative art to rebuild facial features, and improvised dressing before the body can be viewed.

sources.title: Hierarchical Surgical Robot Transformer (SRT-H)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous incision, dissection, clipping and suturing of soft tissue, the closest analogue to raising a vessel, cannulating and suturing during embalming. It substantiates only sub-step tissue manipulation on small fixtured ex vivo specimens in a laboratory, with no vessel raising, cavity aspiration or whole-body work.

tasks.label: Pick up and handle human or pet remains in a respectful manner.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crematory receiving/holding area: moving a decedent enclosed in a cremation container (cardboard/alternative container or casket, 40-400 lb) from the transfer van or church truck onto a cart, into refrigerated holding, and later back out and over to the charging area; container kept level, ID card and paperwork kept with it, no jostling, families sometimes witnessing.

Charging station in the crematory: positioning the containered decedent on the loading table/charger, aligning it with the retort opening and inserting it into the hot chamber, then withdrawing the table and closing the door.

Prep room: hands-on handling of an unencased decedent - sliding a limp body in a pouch or shroud from a mortuary cot or cooler tray onto a tray or into a cremation container, straightening limbs, covering, checking the ID band, removing pacemakers/jewelry; includes bariatric (300+ lb), autopsied, decomposed and infant cases.

After the cycle: raking and brushing hot bone fragments off the chamber floor into a collection pan, cooling, pulling out metal with a magnet/by hand, running the fragments through a processor, and transferring the cremated remains (human or pet) into the labeled urn, bag or temporary container without loss or co-mingling.

Pet crematory intake and loading: receiving bagged/wrapped animals (birds and cats up to 150 lb dogs) delivered in totes from veterinary clinics, weighing and tagging each, holding them in the freezer, then retrieving the correct animal and placing it individually on the tray/into the chamber for a private cremation.

Removal call at a place of death - private residence, hospice room, nursing home: rolling/lifting the decedent onto the cot, covering and strapping, negotiating narrow halls, stairs and doorways, and loading into the removal vehicle, often with family watching.

sources.claim: Automated storage and retrieval systems installed in columbaria store and retrieve thousands of urns of human cremated remains, with a stacker crane handling each container gently and tracking its identity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: identity-tracked storage, retrieval and conveyance of containers holding human remains inside a purpose-built rack. It substantiates machine handling of remains containers to a dignity standard the industry accepts, in an E1 setting, which is the same material-handling act as moving a cremation container within a crematory.

tasks.label: Place corpses into crematory machines to reduce remains to bone fragments using flame, heat, or alkaline hydrolysis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Unattended standard adult flame cremation at a funeral-home or standalone crematory: the decedent, already in a combustible cardboard/wood container, is staged on a cot or transfer table in the crematory; the operator checks the ID tag and paperwork, wheels the container to the preheated retort, opens the door, transfers the container onto the loading table/rollers and into the chamber, closes the door and starts the cycle.

Witnessed/attended cremation with family present in an adjoining viewing area: the same load performed slowly and with decorum, sometimes from a finished or rented casket, with the family watching through glass and occasionally pressing the start button; equipment must be quiet, clean and out of sight afterwards.

Oversize or otherwise difficult human case: a bariatric decedent (300-600 lb) in an oversize container loaded into an oversize retort, or leaking/decomposed remains, wicker or non-standard containers, requiring extra lifting force and careful squaring-up at the chamber opening.
Individual pet cremation: a single bagged or boxed animal taken from the freezer, placed on the hearth or loading tray of a small front-loading pet cremator, door closed and cycle started.

Multi-animal load at a pet crematory: several animals of widely differing size and shape arranged in one chamber, on trays or with separators, for partitioned-individual or communal cremation, or a large animal loaded with a hoist/loading table.

Alkaline hydrolysis (water cremation): a shrouded, uncontainered body is placed on the stainless steel cradle/basket, loaded into the pressure vessel, the vessel door sealed and the alkali/heat cycle started.

sources.system: Crematec / TABO insertion machines (S-55, S-110, AS-55, GA-55, GA2-55)

tasks.label: Pulverize remaining bone fragments into smaller pieces, using specialized equipment, such as a cremulator or grinder.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard adult human flame cremation at a funeral-home or dedicated crematory: after the retort cools, the operator brings the ash pan (roughly 3-7 lb of bone fragments, already swept out and passed over with a magnet) to the processing station, tips it into the cremated remains processor, runs a 30-90 second cycle, discharges the powdered remains into a plastic bag/urn with the ID disc, and brushes/vacuums the drum clean so nothing carries over to the next decedent.

Human cremation leaving dense, incompletely reduced skeletal material (large-frame or heavily calcified decedent, or a short/cool cycle): large fragments must be broken down, the processor run for a longer or second cycle, and residual small hardware (staples, screws, bone pins) found during processing removed; occasional jams or overload trips must be cleared before the batch is finished to a uniform, unidentifiable consistency.

Private/individual pet cremation at a pet crematory: many small batches per shift (cats and dogs, a few ounces to a few pounds each), each processed in a small pet cremulator and emptied into a labeled tin or urn, with the drum wiped or blown out between every animal because commingling of individual pets is a serious service failure.

Large-animal or bulk processing: equine/large-dog remains or a communal pet batch, tens of pounds of coarse fragments, run through an equine-size cremulator in several loads, with the output emptied into a large container or divided among scatter tubes.

Alkaline hydrolysis (water cremation) case: the soft, chalky, wet bone remains are removed from the vessel and dried, then processed in the same cremulator; the volume is larger and whiter than flame cremains and the fragments crush easily, but everything must be recovered and transferred to the urn.

Very small remains: a bird, rodent, kitten, or fetal/infant case where only a few grams of fragments exist; the operator often works by hand (mortar and pestle, small blender, or a careful short cycle in the smallest processor) because full recovery of the tiny quantity matters more than throughput.

sources.claim: The DFW Europe Cremulator, one of the best-selling ash mills in Europe, docks to the crematory ash pan, separates ferrous and non-ferrous fragments into collecting drawers, grinds the remainder to powder in 90 seconds, and automatically fills the urn.

sources.system: BL-500 Horse / Equine Cremated Remains Processor
sources.title: Ancillary All Products - B&L Cremation Systems, Inc.
sources.claim: An equine-scale cremated remains processor pulverizes large-animal remains, shuts off automatically, and tilts to empty the processed remains directly into the chosen urn.

sources.system: Rocklabs AMS Prep Line (Automated Modular Solution)
sources.title: Scott | Rocklabs AMS Prep Line / Doubling Throughput at Ken's Bore
sources.claim: A fully automated, robot-served preparation line crushes, pulverizes and dispenses solid samples in a purpose-built cell, with RFID tracking of each container and automated self-cleaning between batches to prevent cross-contamination; it is running in production at Mineral Resources' Ken's Bore ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated laboratory sample pulverizing. The robot cell performs exactly the mechanics this task requires — tipping a container of brittle solid fragments into a mill, running a milling cycle, dispensing the powder into a tracked receptacle, and self-cleaning so no material carries into the next batch — at comparable masses and with a stricter no-cross-contamination standard than a crematory requires.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: milling brittle mineral samples. Establishes that machine pulverizing spans the batch sizes seen in crematory work, including the few-gram small-pet case where hand grinding is otherwise used.

sources.claim: Bone remains left by alkaline hydrolysis are processed in the same cremulator used after flame cremation, so cremulator evidence applies to water-cremation cases.
sources.transferJustification: Same equipment and same step: the AH variant of this task differs only in that the (softer) bone is dried first, then run through an ordinary cremulator, so the cremulator evidence transfers directly.

sources.title: American Crematory Equipment Catalog
