tasks.label: Remove jewelry, watches, or other personal items from the deceased prior to cremation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crematory/funeral-home preparation room: operator removes rings and a wedding band from the fingers of a deceased adult before cremation, often with rigor mortis, swelling, or arthritic knuckles, sometimes using lubricant, tape, or a ring cutter as a last resort; the item must come off without tearing skin or damaging the ring, and is then logged, photographed, and bagged for the family.

Preparation room: removal of necklaces, chains, religious medals, bracelets, earrings, body piercings, and wrist watches — requiring the operator to lift or turn the head and limbs of the body, work a small clasp or buckle behind the neck or under the wrist, and free chains tangled in hair or clothing.

Final pre-cremation check of a dressed body in the casket/alternative container: operator looks over and pats down the body, removes eyeglasses, hearing aids, hairpins, and the contents of clothing pockets (wallet, phone, keys, rosary, photographs), decides per the authorization form what stays with the deceased and what is returned, and completes the chain-of-custody paperwork.

Pet crematory: removal of collars, ID tags, harnesses, leashes, bandanas, and clinic tape/catheters from animal remains of widely varying size and species, often stiff, wrapped in a blanket or towel, or partially frozen from cold storage, with the collar returned to the owner.

Intake of a body arriving in a pouch on a cot from a hospital, nursing home, hospice, or medical examiner: operator opens the pouch and body-covering, inventories and removes any remaining jewelry or personal effects in conditions that vary (decomposition, autopsy incisions, bariatric or contracted bodies, infectious precautions), usually witnessed and documented by a second person.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance
sources.claim: RABBIT is an autonomous robot-assisted bed-bathing system that performs washing, rinsing and drying motions on human limbs in a laboratory setting; it is the closest demonstrated case of autonomous robot contact manipulation on a human body, but it only wipes skin with a compliant sponge end-effector and does no fine manipulation of jewelry or clothing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted bed bathing. Transfer does NOT hold — bathing requires only broad, compliant wiping strokes over a limb, whereas removing jewelry requires locating small metal items on/under skin and clothing, opening millimetre-scale clasps, and sliding rings over knuckles with force control on a rigid, non-cooperative body. Cited to document the frontier, not to support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robot-assisted dressing research puts long-sleeve garments onto the arms of living, cooperating participants in a lab, using policies trained in simulation and fine-tuned with vision and force feedback; the demonstrated skill is limited to sleeve-on-arm garment manipulation, not removal of rings, watches, clasped necklaces or pocket contents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing of a human arm. Transfer does NOT hold — the objects (bulk deformable garments) and precision (centimetre-scale sleeve alignment) differ from jewelry clasps and rings, and the setting is a lab with a live, cooperating subject rather than a mortuary body. Cited to bound the state of the art.

tasks.label: Sweep or vacuum the cremation chamber to retrieve remains for storage in an urn or other container.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard human cremation at a funeral-home crematory with a fixed-hearth retort: after the 2-3 hour cycle and a 15-30 minute cool-down, the operator opens the door and uses long-handled rakes, hoes and brushes to pull all bone fragments and ash from the still-hot brick chamber into a cooling pan or chute, checking hearth joints and corners, recovering the ID tag, then vacuuming residual ash before the next case.

High-volume standalone crematory running several retorts back-to-back: chamber must be swept out quickly while still at several hundred degrees, with a high-temperature ash vacuum used for residual fines; strict chain of custody, no commingling between consecutive cases, remains transferred to a labeled pan/container for processing.

Individual (private) pet cremation at a pet or veterinary crematory: small or multi-chamber units, small and fragile remains ranging from a few grams to a few kilograms; each chamber, tray and pan is meticulously brushed and vacuumed so no remains of one animal carry into the next, and remains go into an individually labeled container.

Difficult conditions on an older or small retort: worn refractory with cracks and spalled brick, heavy residue or clinker from an oversized case, coffin nails, screws and metal implants mixed with fragments, awkward reach and a warped door; operator brushes residue off brick surfaces and hearth edges in heat and dust wearing PPE.

Non-flame variant and adjunct clean-out: alkaline hydrolysis, where bone remains are retrieved from the vessel basket, rinsed and dried before processing; or clearing the cooling pan, chute and transfer path so that all of an individual's remains reach the container.

sources.system: SHC-J161 Automatic Ash Collection Cremation Machine (movable chamber bed / 'ash picking' cremator)
sources.developer: Shandong Shanhaichuan Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Automatic Ash Collection Cremation Machine for Funeral Equipment - Human Cremation Machine and Human Cremator
sources.claim: The most automated commercial cremators use a movable hearth bed that automatically carries the cremated remains out of the chamber into a cooling chamber and onto an ash-collection table, but the collection of the ashes themselves is still done by staff, so the machine does not complete retrieval into a container.
sources.transferJustification: This is the closest existing automation of the rated task: it mechanizes emptying the chamber, but the vendor states staff still collect the ashes, so the whole instance (remains recovered into an urn or container) is not machine-completed even in a purpose-built cremator.

sources.system: FT Model HSC High Speed Cremulator and Ash Transfer Cabinet
sources.title: FT - Model HSC - High Speed Cremulator by Facultatieve Technologies
sources.claim: Automated cremated-remains handling equipment in crematories covers only the downstream step: an operator-filled ash pan is emptied into an enclosed processor that pulverizes and discharges into the urn; the pan is filled by a human raking the chamber.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (pulverizing remains and filling the urn). It shows machine handling begins only after a human has retrieved the remains from the chamber into the ash pan, so it does not substantiate completion of the sweep/vacuum retrieval step.

sources.system: BL-499 cremated remains processing center; B&L Crematory Vacuum
sources.title: Ancillary All Products - B&L Cremation Systems, Inc.
sources.claim: US crematory suppliers likewise automate only remains processing after collection; the BL-499 is an automatic processing centre fed with already-collected remains, while chamber clean-up relies on operator-held crematory vacuums.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (processing collected remains). The companion chamber clean-up product from the same maker is a hand-held vacuum for an operator, showing no robotic system performs the chamber retrieval itself.

sources.system: R3 Vac autonomous industrial vacuum robot (comparable: Cleanfix S170 Navi, SoftBank Whiz)
sources.title: R3 Vac: Autonomous Industrial Vacuum Robot | Singapore
sources.claim: Commercially deployed autonomous cleaning robots vacuum open floors in human facilities, collecting debris into an onboard hopper; none enter furnace chambers or recover a specific, complete set of fragile fragments into a designated container.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous vacuuming in structured facilities). Transfer fails: the work here is inside a hot refractory chamber reached with long-handled tools, requires near-complete recovery of an identified individual's brittle bone fragments and their deposit into a labelled urn or pan, none of which floor-vacuuming robots demonstrate.

tasks.label: Transport the deceased to a funeral home or crematory using a van, hearse, or other vehicle.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: First call at a hospital, nursing home or inpatient hospice: operator drives the removal van to the facility, checks in, takes a cot to a patient room or morgue cooler, transfers the decedent (often 150-250 lb, limp) onto the cot with a sheet slide, covers and straps, wheels through corridors, elevators and a service dock past staff and visitors, loads the cot into the van, drives public streets to the funeral home/crematory, unloads and places the remains in the cooler or prep room with ID tag and paperwork.

Home or residential hospice death, often at night: van parked on a street or driveway, entry through an as-found house with narrow halls, stairs, furniture, pets and grieving family present; decedent must be lifted from a bed, recliner or bathroom floor onto a cot or stretcher, sometimes in a body bag with a two-person lift, moved out of the house with dignity in view of the family, loaded into the van and driven to the crematory.

Transfer run between a funeral home and a third-party crematory: remains already in a casket or cardboard cremation container on a church truck at the funeral home's prep-room door or dock; operator rolls the container onto the van's roller floor or uses a lift gate, secures it, drives across town, then unloads and moves the container onto a transfer trolley/charging bier in the crematory, verifying identification and authorization paperwork.

Pickup at a medical examiner/coroner facility or hospital morgue release area: decedent already pouched on a standard mortuary tray or shelf in a refrigerated rack; staff assist in the release, operator slides the tray/pouch onto his cot at the rack, signs the release, loads at a dedicated dock, drives to the crematory and offloads.

Difficult or non-routine transports: bariatric (300-600 lb) removals needing extra personnel and heavy-duty cots, decomposed or trauma cases requiring containment, scene removals outdoors or at accident sites under police direction, and long-distance or airport air-tray transfers involving loading a shipping container into a van or livery vehicle.

sources.title: Charging Bier DFW Europe Manual / Automatic Coffin Insert Machine
sources.claim: Fully automatic charging bier transfers a coffined body from a transport trolley into the cremator: after touchscreen activation the coffin is inserted, the loading door cycles and the charger stows itself, with no person bearing the load.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the delivery/hand-off end of transporting the deceased to a crematory. Same object (coffined adult remains), same purpose-built crematorium, machine moves the load from a presented trolley position to its destination without a person bearing the weight.

sources.title: Japan's Lastel 'Corpse' Hotel Allows Check in Only to the Dead (PHOTOS) | IBTimes
sources.claim: A purpose-built mortuary facility uses an automated storage and retrieval ... to hold coffined bodies in chilled racks and deliver them on demand through hatches into viewing rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine transport of the deceased between two points inside a facility. Identical payload (a coffined body on a standardized tray) and identical acceptance criteria (correct decedent delivered intact and undisturbed); only the route is internal and fixtured.

sources.system: Lingzhou Series AGV Remains Transport Robots
sources.title: Home - Crematorium equipment suppliers | Mteptech.com
sources.claim: Commercially offered AGV transport robots are built specifically to move human remains and coffins autonomously inside funeral homes, crematoriums and morgues, positioning and carrying loads of 100-500 kg.

sources.system: ek robotics AGV / driverless transport systems
sources.title: AGV - Automated Guided Vehicles | NEURA Mobile Robots GmbH
sources.claim: Driverless AGV fleets perform routine load transport across industries, with the vendor listing a crematorium among the sites where its 12,000-plus vehicles run.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixed-route intralogistics transport of heavy unit loads. A tray- or coffin-borne decedent is a comparably sized rigid load on a standard carrier, and the vendor already lists crematorium use, so the transport leg carries over when the route is purpose-built.

sources.date: 2025 (driverless operations with select customers; article Dec 2025)
sources.title: Outrider launches enterprise-class support for its autonomous yard trucks - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Autonomous electric yard trucks move loaded trailers between dock doors and ... in controlled logistics yards, performing backing, hitching and brake-line connection without a driver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless vehicle movement of a loaded, docked payload between fixed points in a fenced facility, substantiating the vehicle leg of this task when origin and destination are purpose-built dock positions.

sources.title: Waymo begins fully autonomous ops with 6th-gen Driver, targets 1M weekly rides | Electrek
sources.claim: Driverless robotaxis carry passengers on ordinary public streets without a safety driver in many US cities, showing the road-driving leg is solved in traffic - but the vehicle does no loading and passengers board themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-to-point driving on public roads. It covers only the driving segment; it involves no handling, transfer or securing of a decedent, so it cannot by itself substantiate completion of any instance.

roles.title: Funeral Attendants
roles.description: Perform a variety of tasks during funeral, such as placing casket in parlor or chapel prior to service, arranging floral offerings or lights around casket, directing or escorting mourners, closing casket, and issuing and storing funeral equipment.

tasks.label: Greet people at the funeral home.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform a variety of tasks during funerals to assist funeral directors and to ensure that services run smoothly and as planned.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-service setup in the funeral home chapel or parlor: wheel the casket in on a church truck and position/level it at the front, drape and dress the bier, arrange 5-20 floral tributes of varying size on stands around the casket, set photo easels, memorial table with personal items, register stand and book, straighten chairs, set lighting and music before the family arrives.

Mourner-facing duties during visitation and the chapel service: greeting arrivals at the door, handing out memorial folders, seating the family and guests, escorting elderly or disabled mourners (offering an arm, wheelchairs), watching the register book, quietly responding to family requests, dismissing rows to the procession line, and closing the casket at the family's cue.

Casket and equipment handling inside the funeral home building: transferring the casket between prep/display rooms and the chapel on a church truck, moving it through doorways and corridors, loading it into and out of the hearse at the garage bay, and issuing from and returning to storage the funeral equipment (church trucks, chair trucks, stands, candelabra, lowering device, tent) used for that service.

Off-site service at a church or other venue: unloading the hearse and van, carrying floral pieces and easels into an unfamiliar sanctuary, setting register stand and photo displays, coordinating with clergy, ushering mourners, and assisting pallbearers with the casket in and out.

Graveside/committal service at a cemetery: setting the tent, chairs, greens and lowering device over an open grave, carrying floral sprays across turf, guiding mourners over uneven, sometimes muddy or snowy ground, assisting with casket placement on the lowering device, then striking and reloading everything, in whatever weather occurs.

Procession and vehicle duties: driving the hearse or family coach, marshalling and leading the cortege on public streets at procession speed with flags and lights, directing arriving traffic and parking cars in the funeral home or cemetery lot, and opening doors for the family.

sources.system: DFW Europe Automatic Insert Machine (AIM) automatic charging bier / catafalque coffin transport system
sources.title: Charging Bier DFW Europe Manual / Automatic Coffin Insert Machine
sources.claim: DFW Europe's Automatic Insert Machine (AIM) charging bier automatically transfers an adult coffin from a transport trolley into a cremator inside a purpose-built crematorium, opening and closing the loading door and stowing itself afterwards; commercially marketed since 2008.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated coffin handling in a crematorium. The object is the same class of item a funeral attendant moves (a full-size adult coffin/casket of comparable mass and bulk), moved from a fixtured trolley to a precise target position in a machine-built facility, which is what an E1 counterfactual of in-building casket movement requires.

sources.system: Daifuku automated columbarium (AS/RS with stacker crane and prayer booths)
sources.title: Innovating Remembrance – The Elegance of the Automated Columbarium | DAIFUKU
sources.claim: Daifuku's automated columbarium uses an AS/RS stacker crane to store thousands of urns and, on a card scan, autonomously retrieve the correct urn and deliver it to a prayer booth for a family's memorial visit; deployed commercially, chiefly in East Asia.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: issuing and storing funeral items on demand and presenting them for a memorial. It is the same industry and the same kind of duty (retrieve the right item from storage, deliver it to the place of the service, return it afterwards), performed in a purpose-built machine environment.

sources.system: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile delivery robot
sources.title: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robot showcased at RIA
sources.claim: Aethon's TUG is a fully autonomous mobile robot deployed in over 100 hospitals that hauls carts of up to 1,000 lb along ordinary hospital corridors shared with staff and visitors, without floor magnets or stripes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transport of heavy wheeled loads through an institutional building among the public. It shows corridor-level transport of a casket-weight rolling load is feasible in an E2 facility, but the TUG only docks and tows standardised carts on mapped routes; it does not position, drape, or load a casket.

sources.title: Agility Robotics’ Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid, the most mature commercially deployed mobile manipulator in a work facility, has moved over 100,000 totes ... Georgia warehouse, handling standardised totes between AMRs, conveyors and floor stacks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general mobile manipulation in a structured facility. It marks the current ceiling of deployed humanoid manipulation — uniform rigid totes on known fixtures — well short of arranging varied floral tributes, easels and chairs into a chapel display, so it bounds rather than supports the setup instances.

sources.system: Pepper humanoid robot in Buddhist priest role
sources.title: Pepper the robot to don Buddhist robe for its new funeral services role - The Japan Times
sources.claim: The only robot publicised in an actual funeral role is SoftBank's Pepper, programmed by Nissei Eco to chant Buddhist sutras at ...; the routine is pre-programmed speech and gesture and involves none of the physical attendant duties.
sources.transferJustification: Directly funeral-sector, but a scripted speech/gesture demonstration with no manipulation or mourner handling; treated as non-supporting for every physical instance.

tasks.label: Close caskets at appropriate point in services.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Funeral home chapel/visitation room: at the close of visitation the attendant makes final adjustments (smoothing the decedent's clothing and the interior throw, removing eyeglasses or jewelry the family asked back, leaving keepsakes inside), then quietly lowers the half-couch lid and latches it on the director's cue, often just after the family is ushered out for their last goodbye.

Church or other place of worship: casket closed in the narthex/vestibule before it is wheeled into the sanctuary and the pall is placed, or reopened and reclosed after the service; timing coordinated with clergy and pallbearers, with mourners, flower stands and church furniture crowding the space.

Back-of-house at the funeral home (prep room or garage), no mourners present: final check that nothing and no one is disturbed, tuck the interior fabric clear of the rail, lower the lid, and engage the cam-lock/gasket seal with the key before the casket is loaded into the hearse.

Graveside committal at a cemetery: casket displayed open under the tent for a final viewing, then closed at the bier before lowering — uneven turf, wind or rain, floral sprays and standing mourners immediately around the casket.

Non-standard venue (private residence, fraternal or community hall, cultural/religious variant): casket in a cramped living room or rented hall with a layout that differs each time; family members may take part in the closing, place items inside, or require a specific rite before the lid comes down.

sources.system: AIM automatic coffin insert machine (charging bier)
sources.title: Charging Bier DFW Europe Manual / Automatic Coffin Insert Machine
sources.claim: The closest death-care automation to casket handling is the DFW Europe AIM charging bier, which after an operator touch-screen action automatically transfers an already-closed coffin into the cremator and operates the oven door; it does not close, latch or seal casket lids or work around a decedent's presentation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized handling of a coffin in a crematory. It shows death-care automation exists only for moving sealed coffins along a fixed path; it never manipulates an open casket's lid, interior fabric or the decedent, so it does not transfer to closing a casket at a point in a service.

sources.system: Batesville Manchester casket assembly line (welding/paint/press-tending robots)
sources.title: How a Casket Is Assembled | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Casket lids are handled by automation only in the factory, where lids are welded on an automated line and robots serve the paint shop and stamping presses; no cited system closes a finished lid over a decedent.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: casket-lid fabrication in a purpose-built plant. Objects are the same scale, but the machines weld blank panels held in fixtures; they do not lower a hinged finished lid over an occupied, fabric-lined interior or engage a gasket seal, so the capability does not carry over.

sources.system: Safedoor SD100 automatic CNC door opener
sources.title: Made4CNC Launches World's First Completely Automatic CNC Door Opening Solution for Robots
sources.claim: Automated closing of a heavy hinged panel exists in industry only as a dedicated mechanism bolted to one specific machine: the Safedoor SD100 opens and closes a CNC machine door on command from a robot cell, with no perception of what lies inside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered closing of a heavy panel in a fenced machine-tending cell. It is a single-purpose actuator matched to one door; it cannot approach a varied casket, verify or arrange the interior, or judge the moment to close, so it does not substantiate the whole task even at E1.

sources.system: Pepper Buddhist-priest funeral robot; automated conveyor columbaria
sources.title: High tech, IT and robots are at forefront of Japan's funeral industry boom - The Japan Times
sources.claim: Robots that have actually entered funeral services are non-manipulative ceremonial devices — a humanoid programmed to chant sutras and automated columbaria that shuttle urns — none performs the physical care of the casket or the body.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic participation in funeral rites. The demonstrated behaviour is speech and gesture on a fixed stand; there is no manipulation of a casket, so it cannot support completion of casket closing in any environment.

tasks.label: Direct or escort mourners to parlors or chapels in which wakes or funerals are being held.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Multi-service day at a funeral home: attendant stands at the entrance/lobby during a visitation, greets arriving mourners, asks which family they are there for, and directs them down the hall to the correct one of two or three parlors while also pointing out the register book and restrooms.

Single-service funeral home or small chapel: attendant meets guests at the door or in the parking area and gives verbal directions to the one chapel, keeping arrivals moving and the doorway clear in bad weather or heavy arrival periods.

Just before the service begins: attendant walks the immediate family from a private family room down the aisle to the reserved front pews, timing the entry with the officiant's cue and indicating where each group should sit.

High-attendance or off-site service (church, community hall, graveside): attendant manages the flow of a long viewing line, routes latecomers to an overflow room, and directs mourners between chapel, reception room, and the procession staging area.

Elderly or mobility-limited mourner: attendant walks at the person's pace to a seat near the front, sometimes offering an arm or holding a door, and conveys where the accessible entrance and seating are.

tasks.label: Place caskets in parlors or chapels prior to wakes or funerals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Funeral home visitation parlor: attendant moves a loaded casket (roughly 150–400 lb with the body, on a church truck) from the prep/casket room or cooler through interior doorways and carpeted halls into the parlor, sets it at the head of the room against the drape, sets brakes, squares it, adjusts height/skirt and opens the lid before the family arrives.

Offsite church or synagogue service: casket unloaded from the hearse at the entrance, transferred onto a church truck, wheeled up a ramp or short flight of steps and down the center aisle, aligned squarely before the chancel/altar at the required orientation, pall draped; aisle widths, thresholds and floor surfaces differ from venue to venue.

Difficult placement: oversized or very heavy casket (wide/steel, 500+ lb loaded) or awkward access — narrow doorway, stairs, small elevator, older building, gravel or grass approach — requiring several attendants, lift assists and careful maneuvering without marring the casket or the room.

Crematorium or cemetery chapel: casket delivered by hearse to the committal chapel and placed on the catafalque/bier at the correct height and orientation, centered on the curtained platform, ahead of a short committal service.

Non-institutional venue: home wake in a private residence, a lodge/fire hall, or a graveside tent — casket carried through a house door or across uneven ground and set on a bier in the room or spot the family chose, with furniture moved as needed.

sources.system: Crematec insertion machine / coffin handling system
sources.title: Insertion Machines of different types - Höganäs Borgestad
sources.claim: Crematec (Höganäs Borgestad) coffin insertion machines run a fully automatic cycle that lifts a coffin and moves it to a precise destination inside a purpose-built crematorium charging area; the same product line handles coffins weighing up to about 250 kg.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring and positioning a full-size loaded coffin from a fixtured bier to a precise target location. Same objects (caskets of the same mass and dimensions), similar placement precision (aligning with a charge opening), in a purpose-built machine-oriented room, which is what an E1 counterfactual for casket placement requires.

sources.system: OY fully automatic integrated body/coffin loading conveyor (charging bier)
sources.title: Cremation Charging Bier - Crematorium equipment suppliers | Mteptech.com
sources.claim: OY/Mteptech charging biers automatically transport a loaded coffin from a matched trolley height into the cremator on a single touch-screen command; the maker says these loading conveyors are widely used in Chinese funeral homes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-executed transfer of a casket from a presented trolley to a fixed destination. Comparable object mass and required alignment; demonstrates that when a casket is presented fixtured in a purpose-built setting, machines move and place it unaided.

sources.title: Innovating Remembrance – The Elegance of the Automated Columbarium | DAIFUKU
sources.claim: Daifuku's automated columbarium uses AS/RS technology to autonomously retrieve the remains and deliver them to a prayer/worship booth where the family pays respects; such automated conveyor columbaria are in commercial operation at Japanese temples and urban facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing the remains at the ceremonial viewing position before mourners arrive. Same purpose and acceptance standard (remains correctly presented in the memorial room on schedule), executed unattended in a purpose-built chamber; differs in the container handled (urn box rather than casket), which the crematory charging evidence covers.

sources.system: DFW Automatic Charging Bier / Automatic Insert Machine (AIM)
sources.title: Charging Bier DFW Europe Manual / Automatic Coffin Insert Machine
sources.claim: DFW Europe markets a full-automatic integrated charging bier that transfers a coffin automatically, and has sold this coffin insert machine since 2008; the company also supplies catafalques for ceremony rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic movement and placement of a loaded coffin in a purpose-built crematorium bay; same object class and comparable placement tolerance as setting a casket on a bier.

sources.system: Lingzhou Series Remains & Caskets Transport AGV Robots
sources.title: Home - Crematorium equipment suppliers | Mteptech.com
sources.claim: Mteptech markets the Lingzhou series of AGV robots built specifically to transport remains and caskets inside funeral homes, crematoriums and morgues, positioning loads of 100–500 kg; deployment scale is not documented.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (moving caskets within a funeral facility), but autonomy and any real deployment are unverified vendor claims, so it is recorded as unclear and is not used to support a positive judgment above E1.

sources.title: Crematoria Equipment - Austeng Cremator
sources.claim: Austeng supplies an automated charge bier for crematoria that it says handles the largest coffins as a one-person operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling of the heaviest/oversized coffins on a fixtured bier, relevant to the heavy-casket instance; operator involvement is not specified, so it is treated as unclear and only corroborates the Höganäs and OY machines.

tasks.label: Offer assistance to mourners as they enter or exit limousines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Family limousine loading/unloading under the funeral home's own porte-cochere or driveway after the visitation or service: attendant opens the coach door, holds it, offers a hand or forearm to each mourner stepping down, guards heads and hems on the door frame, holds an umbrella in rain, closes the door once everyone is seated. Mostly ambulatory adults, several elderly, some crying or unsteady.

Curbside arrival/departure at a church, synagogue, or other place of worship on a public street: limousine stops at a public curb in traffic, attendant steps into the roadway, opens doors, steadies mourners over an uneven curb and around parked cars and bystanders, coordinates with the procession's timing.

Cemetery: limousine halts on a narrow cemetery lane; attendant helps mourners out onto grass, gravel, mud, or snow, offers an arm across uneven turf to the graveside tent, then reverses the process afterward, in whatever weather the day brings.

A mourner with a substantial mobility impairment at any of the above locations: an elderly widow or a disabled relative using a walker, cane, or wheelchair who needs a firm two-hand assist or partial weight-bearing support to pivot out of a low limousine seat, plus stowing/retrieving the mobility device.

Residence pickup: limousine collects immediate family from a private home; attendant walks to the door area, offers an arm down porch steps and along a private walk or driveway, and hands each person into the car; layout differs at every house.

sources.title: China's humanoid robot stuns by opening car door in a 'world-first'
sources.claim: AiMOGA's humanoid Mornine autonomously located a handle and opened a car door inside a working Chery dealership, ... onboard sensing and learned full-body control — a sub-step of the task (door opening) but with no physical contact with or support of a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening a vehicle door in a commercial showroom. It shares the door hardware and the indoor structured setting, but it covers only the door-opening sub-step and involves no contact with, steadying of, or escorting of a passenger, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole instance.

sources.title: Eldercare robot helps people sit and stand, and catches them if they fall | MIT News
sources.claim: MIT's E-BAR is the closest research system for physically supporting and catching an unsteady elderly person, but it is a laboratory prototype driven by remote control rather than an autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: providing bodily support to an unsteady older adult standing, sitting and walking — the physical core of assisting a mourner out of a limousine. It fails to transfer because it is remote-controlled, unreleased, and demonstrated only in a lab home mock-up.

sources.title: Mobility support robot | FUJI Corporation
sources.claim: Commercially sold transfer-support machines that bear a frail person's weight (FUJI Hug) are caregiver-operated devices: a human positions the care receiver against the body holder and presses buttons on a remote controller.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring a person who cannot rise unaided (bed to wheelchair). It is the nearest commercial analogue to physically handing a frail mourner out of a car, but a caregiver must position the person and drive the machine, so it is not autonomous assistance.

sources.developer: WHILL, Inc. with Aicher Airport Services / Unifi Aviation
sources.title: WHILL Launches Autonomous Services at Munich Airport
sources.claim: WHILL autonomous wheelchairs deployed at Munich Airport and Detroit Metro carry passengers with reduced mobility to their gates autonomously, but human staff still perform the boarding assistance — guiding the passenger, helping them board and stowing their items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving mobility-limited people through a structured facility. Transfer fails: the autonomy covers only driving between waypoints on a flat terminal floor, and the human-contact step (helping the person board) is explicitly still done by staff.

tasks.label: Clean funeral parlors or chapels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-visitation/post-service turnaround of a viewing parlor or chapel: pick up leftover programs, tissues, cups and floral debris from seats and carpet, empty wastebaskets and tissue boxes, wipe fingerprints and spot-clean spills, restraighten chairs, then vacuum, all in a 20-40 minute window between services in a furnished, carpeted room.

Routine floor-care round (usually overnight or early morning): vacuum the carpeting of the chapel, viewing parlors, lobby and corridors, and dust-mop/damp-mop hard floors in the entry and hallways; building is empty, seating is in place, layout is fixed.

Detail dusting and polishing inside the parlor/chapel: wood pews and chair backs, casket biers and church trucks, side tables, lamps, picture frames, urn display cases, handrails, glass entry doors and mirrors, using cloths, polish and glass cleaner on many differently shaped delicate objects.
Cleaning and disinfecting the adjoining public restrooms used by mourners: toilets, urinals, sinks, mirrors, floors, emptying trash and restocking paper goods, done between or after visitations.
Cleaning the family lounge / coffee-and-refreshment area after a visitation: wipe counters and tables, clear coffee urn and cups, wash or load dishes, sweep crumbs, empty trash, restock supplies.
Periodic deep cleaning of the chapel: carpet shampoo/extraction, upholstery cleaning of pew cushions, washing interior windows and light fixtures, cleaning the entry canopy and porch.

sources.title: Brain Corp: Tennant X6 ROVR powered by BrainOS | Autonomous floor scrubber | Overview
sources.claim: Tennant's X6 ROVR autonomous floor scrubber, running Brain Corp's BrainOS, cleans floors autonomously in large commercial facilities; Brain Corp/Tennant autonomous scrubbers are in service in airports and similar public facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hard-floor scrubbing/mopping in institutional buildings. Transfers to mopping a funeral home's entry and corridors: same floor surfaces, same obstacle-avoidance requirement, same institution-controlled indoor setting.

sources.title: Whiz - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: SoftBank's Whiz is a commercially sold autonomous vacuum sweeper deployed at scale (thousands of units) that vacuums carpeted floors in offices, hotels and airports after being taught routes once.

sources.title: SoftBank Robotics America and NISSCO Announce Partnership to Bring Whiz, the Autonomous Vacuum Sweeper, to Distributor Members Nationwide
sources.claim: SoftBank Robotics reported more than 10,000 Whiz units deployed globally, making it the most widely used autonomous ....

sources.title: Commercial Robot Vacuums for Hotels and Residential Buildings (Tailos)
sources.claim: Tailos' Rosie commercial vacuum robot autonomously vacuums furnished indoor spaces including hotel guest rooms, hallways and meeting rooms, working alongside housekeepers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vacuuming carpet in small furnished rooms (hotel guest rooms, meeting rooms). Transfers to vacuuming a carpeted viewing parlor or chapel: same carpet, same seating/furniture obstacles, same institution-controlled indoor premises.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR is an autonomous bathroom-cleaning mobile manipulator deployed in hospitals and airports; it cleans toilets, urinals and floors, opens doors and picks up trash during normal facility operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning public restrooms in institutional buildings. Transfers to a funeral home's public restroom: identical fixtures (toilets, urinals, sinks, tile floors), identical chemicals and quality standard, institution-controlled premises.

sources.title: Primech launches upgraded bathroom cleaning robot
sources.claim: Primech AI's HYTRON mobile-manipulator restroom robot autonomously navigates and performs multiple restroom cleaning tasks in commercial buildings, having completed first commercial trials before its 2025 next-generation launch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous restroom fixture and floor cleaning in human-occupied facilities; the funeral home public restroom is the same fixture set and the same class of premises.

sources.title: π0.5: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 model lets a mobile manipulator attempt general room-cleaning and tidying (wiping spills, putting objects away) in previously unseen rooms, but the developer states the system is far from perfect and frequently errs, i.e. below worker-acceptable reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general room tidying/wiping with varied objects, the closest published analogue to a parlor turnaround; cited to show the best available generalist system is explicitly error-prone and not at worker quality.

tasks.label: Arrange floral offerings or lights around caskets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full floral setup of the funeral home chapel/visitation room: 15-40 pieces delivered by several florists (standing sprays on wire easels, baskets, potted plants, wreaths, a casket spray). Attendant unwraps, checks cards, drapes the casket spray on the open casket lid, flanks the casket with easel sprays, tiers baskets on stands, groups family pieces closest, hides easel legs and boxes, and sets the casket spotlights.

Re-set at an off-site venue (church, synagogue, fraternal hall): flowers stripped from the chapel, loaded into a flower van, then carried in and re-arranged around the casket at the chancel within a tight window before the service, respecting the venue's rules on where pieces may stand, then reloaded afterward.

Graveside at the cemetery: sprays and baskets carried from the flower car across turf to the tent, casket spray set on the casket over the lowering device, remaining pieces set around the grave and later on the filled grave; wind, rain, slope and soft ground require weighting and re-straightening.

Small or simple service (few pieces, small viewing room), plus mid-visitation adjustments: late-arriving deliveries added, pieces shifted at a family member's request, wilting or fallen pieces tidied, all while mourners are in the room.

Lighting-focused setup: positioning and aiming portable casket lighting units/spotlights, candelabra and drape lights around the casket, adjusting brightness and angle so the deceased and the casket look right to the family and for photos.

sources.title: Placing flower bunches in buckets with robots - DERO GROEP
sources.claim: Commercially sold robotic cell that autonomously grasps bunches of cut flowers and mixed bouquets and places them into buckets on a production line, handling a wide range of flower types with vision-assisted flexible robotics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling and placing cut-flower bunches/bouquets in a purpose-built line. Transfer: the objects are the same class of delicate, deformable floral product and the act is grasp-and-place at designated positions, which is what arranging floral pieces at fixed positions around a fixtured casket reduces to at E1.

sources.title: Harvey - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics (IEEE Spectrum)
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robot commercially deployed in nurseries and greenhouses that locates, lifts, transports and sets down potted plants into ordered layouts, indoors and on outdoor fields, using lidar to adjust each plant's placement and avoid people and obstacles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spacing/organizing containerized plants. Transfer: comparable objects (potted plants and floral containers of similar size and weight), comparable precision (each pot set to a surveyed position), demonstrating autonomous grasp-transport-place of plant material into a prescribed layout.

sources.title: Using robotic arms to make floral arrangements - FloralDaily
sources.claim: Robotic arm in a purpose-built retail kiosk that assembles individual cut flowers into a finished arrangement; the developer reports a dozen-rose arrangement produced in about four minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: composing a floral arrangement in a fixtured kiosk. Cited as corroboration only; autonomy is not established from the source, so it does not by itself support a positive judgment.

sources.system: UR10 cobot cell at Betacom (LED road lights)
sources.date: Case story published on Universal Robots site, current as of 2026
sources.title: Cobot Applications - Universal Robots
sources.claim: Vision-free but precision pick-and-place cobot cells are in production use for lighting manufacture: a UR10 picks circuit boards and LED lenses and locates them accurately onto fixtured assemblies in an LED road-light plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise placement and orientation of rigid lighting components in a fixtured cell. Transfer: at E1 the light unit is presented in a known pose and must be set and aimed at a fixed pose beside a fixtured casket, an equal-or-lower precision rigid-body placement.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of mobile manipulators in human work facilities (hospitals) performs point-to-point delivery of supplies and pharmacy items; its manipulation repertoire is fetching and carrying totes and operating doors/elevators, not dexterous arrangement of delicate display objects.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize what deployed E2 mobile manipulation actually covers (delivery/fetch-and-carry), supporting the negative judgment that no cited system arranges floral tributes in a human-occupied chapel.

tasks.label: Clean and drive funeral vehicles, such as cars or hearses, in funeral processions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-service exterior cleaning of the hearse and limousine at the funeral home: wash, rinse, dry, polish chrome trim, clean wheels and glass so the coach is show-ready before the family arrives. Done in the funeral home's garage bay or on its lot.

Interior cleaning of funeral vehicles between services: vacuuming the passenger cabin and the casket deck, wiping down glass, leather and trim, removing floral debris, dirt and clippings tracked in at the cemetery.

Driving the hearse in the funeral procession: pulling up to the chapel/church door, then leading or following the cortege at slow speed over public streets with a lead car or police escort, entering the cemetery and positioning the coach precisely at the graveside.

Driving the family limousine or flower car in the procession with mourners aboard: keeping formation in the cortege on public streets, following the hearse, stopping at the church and at the grave site.

Non-procession vehicle movement on the funeral home's own premises: staging vehicles in the correct order, pulling the hearse into the garage or under the porte-cochere, shuffling cars in the lot after services.

sources.title: Waymo launching driverless robotaxis in 5 more cities
sources.claim: Waymo operates a fully driverless commercial robotaxi service on public roads in multiple US metros, driving passengers point to point, including curbside pickups and stops, at large scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless passenger transport. Transfers to driving a hearse or family limousine because it is the same act (piloting a full-size road vehicle along a route among pedestrians and traffic and stopping at a designated point), the same vehicle class, and the Waymo Driver has been integrated on several vehicle platforms.

sources.system: May Mobility autonomous vehicles (Toyota Sienna platform)
sources.title: May Mobility expands autonomous driver-out vehicle operations to second U.S. city
sources.claim: May Mobility runs driverless (no human in the vehicle) low-speed autonomous shuttle/ride services on public roads and inside controlled communities and campus-like districts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixed-route low-speed driverless passenger transport in controlled communities. This is the closest analogue to driving a cortege vehicle at walking pace along a mapped route inside a controlled memorial-park campus.

sources.title: World first: Bosch and Mercedes-Benz's driverless parking system approved for commercial use
sources.claim: A driverless SAE Level 4 valet parking function moves cars by themselves inside a commercial parking garage, collecting and returning vehicles without a driver, approved for commercial operation at Stuttgart Airport's P6 garage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless repositioning and parking of a full-size car inside a controlled facility. This is the same act as staging and shuffling funeral vehicles on the funeral home's premises: low-speed maneuvering, tight clearances, precise final placement.

sources.title: Car Wash Robotics – Next-Gen Systems Can Help Further Trim Labor (Auto Laundry News)
sources.claim: AI-driven robotic arms perform a complete touchless exterior wash of cars at a commercially operating site, keeping nozzles at a controlled distance from every body surface for full-coverage, damage-free cleaning.

sources.title: Westmatic's Transit-Master bus wash system keeps CATA vehicles looking good
sources.claim: Automatic drive-through brush wash machines installed in transit depots wash large vehicles (buses, coaches, tractor-trailers and cars) as they are driven slowly through the purpose-built wash structure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated exterior washing of oversize vehicles in a fleet facility. A hearse or stretch limousine exceeds ordinary tunnel dimensions, and depot bus-wash machines routinely handle vehicles of that size and larger.

sources.system: STAGS (stationary gantry system) interior cleaning robot
sources.title: Car Wash Robotics – Next-Gen Systems Can Help Further Trim Labor (Auto Laundry News)
sources.claim: A gantry-mounted robotic system with multiple arms and air/mist/steam attachments performs vehicle interior cleaning at car wash sites, with software that locates the car and interprets the cabin layout on the fly; one functional beta site was operating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic interior cleaning of passenger vehicles (vacuuming carpets/seats, cleaning cabin surfaces). Funeral-vehicle interior cleaning involves the same surfaces and debris, in a comparable purpose-built stall.

sources.title: Tesla Robotaxi Hubs Start Installing Car Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: A large robotic arm with swappable tools that vacuums debris, picks up trash and wipes interior surfaces has been installed as a functional automated cleaning robot at a robotaxi fleet hub.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated interior cleaning of fleet vehicles at a depot stall — same objects (cabin surfaces, seats, glass, loose debris) and same precision as cleaning a funeral car's interior.

tasks.label: Act as pallbearers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Church/place-of-worship funeral: attendant is one of six bearers lifting a loaded casket (roughly 250-450 lb total) out of the hearse at the curb, carrying it up entrance steps, through doorways, down the center aisle at a slow matched cadence in full view of mourners, and setting it on a church truck/catafalque; reversed at the end of the service.

Graveside committal at a managed cemetery: bearers take the casket from the hearse and carry it 20-100 ft across mown lawn, gravel or soft/muddy ground, sometimes on a slope or in rain, snow or wind, then align and lower it precisely onto the straps/rollers of a lowering device over the open grave under a tent.

Funeral home / chapel work: bearers lift the casket from a church truck or dressing-room bier and load it into the hearse on the paved portico (and unload it later), on flat standard indoor floors with standard funeral equipment, before or after visitation.

Difficult conditions: oversize/bariatric casket (500+ lb loaded), narrow stairwells, tight turns, elevators, an ice- or mud-covered path, or a rural family/church cemetery or private venue with no paved access and uneven, unmaintained ground.

Mixed team: funeral home staff supplement family members or a military honor guard as bearers, sharing the same casket load with humans of differing height and strength, matching their step and pace, taking handoffs from the honor guard and the flag-fold ritual.

sources.system: DFW Europe AIM automatic charging bier (coffin insert machine)
sources.title: Charging Bier DFW Europe Manual / Automatic Coffin Insert Machine
sources.claim: A commercially sold automatic coffin charger (AIM) in crematoria transfers a full-size occupied coffin from a transport trolley into the cremator fully automatically after a single touch-screen activation, then stows itself away.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine transfer of a coffin (same object, same 150-250 kg loaded weight, same requirement not to damage or tilt it) from a presented, fixtured position to a defined destination. Pallbearing's physical output is exactly this transport-and-set-down of a casket; the AIM shows it is done by machine in a purpose-built docking arrangement.

sources.title: OTTO Motors' Heavy-Class AMRs Exceed One Million Production Hours
sources.claim: Heavy-class autonomous mobile robots autonomously move pallet-scale loads far heavier than a loaded casket along routes inside factories and warehouses, with over a million production hours logged.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transport of a heavy load over a fixed route. The transport leg of pallbearing (moving a 150-250 kg casket from vehicle to service position) is within payload and precision limits when the casket is presented on a fixture, as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.title: FANUC M-2000iA/2300 Robot | 2.3t Heavy Payload Robot
sources.claim: Super-heavy-payload industrial robots lift and precisely position objects up to 2,300 kg, including whole cars and bulky castings, placing them onto machine fixtures inside fenced cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting a large, heavy, rigid workpiece from a known fixtured position and setting it down precisely on another fixture. That is the lift-and-place core of pallbearing (bier to catafalque, or bier to lowering-device straps) once the work is presented as a purpose-built cell presents it; casket weight is an order of magnitude below the robot's rating.

sources.system: INTEC MLC-8000 lift controller in coffin sinking system, Leipzig South Cemetery
sources.title: Lift controller MLC-8000 successfully used in a coffin transport system
sources.claim: A crematorium coffin sinking/transport installation at Leipzig South Cemetery moves the coffin platform between funeral hall and crematorium, partly by automatic call button and partly under deadman control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: purpose-built machine conveyance of coffins between funeral-hall and crematory levels. Corroborates that coffin movement is mechanized only where the path and fixtures are built for the machine; the deadman control means it cannot itself support a positive autonomy judgment.

sources.system: PAINT partner-agnostic cooperative transport policy on legged robot teams
sources.developer: ETH Zurich (Cao, An, Li, Coros, Hutter)
sources.title: PAINT: Partner-Agnostic Intent-Aware Cooperative Transport with Legged Robots
sources.claim: State-of-the-art cooperative carrying by teams of legged robots is demonstrated with an 8 kg long box carried jointly with a human leader in ...; heavier furniture-scale payloads over uneven terrain are shown only in simulation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to team casket-carrying: it is the closest research analogue (multi-agent carry of a long object, including with a human partner), and shows real-world payloads roughly two orders of magnitude below a loaded casket, on flat lab ground rather than church steps or cemetery turf.

tasks.label: Supervise funeral processions and assist with cemetery parking.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-service parking direction at the funeral home or church: guests arrive over 30-120 minutes for visitation or the service; the attendant stands in the lot, waves each car into a space or row, separates cars that will join the procession from those that will not, keeps the coach lane and fire lane clear, and sends overflow to street or adjacent lots.

Marking and forming the procession at the funeral home: attendant places magnetic 'FUNERAL' flags on hoods/roofs of participating vehicles, tells drivers to turn on headlights and stay bumper-to-bumper, arranges hearse, family limousine, clergy and guest cars in the correct order in the departure line, handles latecomers, and signals the dispatch.

Escorting the procession over public roads: attendant drives a lead or flag car (or rides as escort), sets a slow pace, holds intersections so the line is not broken by cross traffic or signals, watches the mirror for stragglers, and coordinates with police motorcycle escorts and cemetery gate staff, in mixed public traffic and any weather.

Cemetery arrival: 20-50 procession vehicles enter within a few minutes on narrow, unmarked cemetery lanes; the attendant waves them forward, stops them in a single file near the grave in arrival order, keeps the coach and family cars in position and the lane clear for the hearse and the vault/lowering equipment, and keeps cars off the turf and graves.

Post-service dispersal and equipment recovery: attendant collects the magnetic funeral flags from mourners' cars, directs vehicles out of the cemetery in sequence and back onto the public road, holds cross traffic at the gate, and retrieves cones, 'funeral' signs and headlight decals.

sources.date: 2020 (page undated; Lyon operation ongoing, private-5G upgrade reported Aug 2025)
sources.title: Trimble GNSS/INS powers autonomous parking robot, "Stan." | Trimble Resource Center
sources.claim: Stanley Robotics' 'Stan' is a fully autonomous outdoor valet parking robot in commercial operation at European airports; customers leave arbitrary passenger cars at a drop-off cabin and the robot lifts and parks them in a secure, robot-only yard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: airport valet parking. It substantiates the 'assist with parking' output — customers' ordinary passenger cars end up parked in an orderly, dense arrangement with occupants on foot — using the same class of objects (mixed passenger vehicles) and centimetre-level placement precision, in a purpose-built robot-only lot (E1 presentation via drop-off cabins).

sources.system: Stan robotic valet fleet, Lyon-Saint Exupéry P5+ car park
sources.developer: Stanley Robotics / VINCI Airports (Aéroports de Lyon)
sources.title: WORLD PREMIERE: Lyon Airport with Stan, the valet robot reinvent car parking
sources.claim: The P5+ outdoor car park at Lyon-Saint Exupéry ... is operated entirely by valet robots as a paid public service: passengers book online, leave the car in a dedicated cabin, and robots park and return it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated public car-park operation. It shows a whole customer car park run without human parking attendants, i.e. the parking-direction function of an attendant discharged by machines when the lot is purpose-built around them.

sources.system: Automated Valet Parking (AVP), Stuttgart Airport P6
sources.title: Driverless parking service begins commercial operation at Stuttgart Airport
sources.claim: Bosch and Mercedes-Benz obtained German regulatory approval for commercial SAE Level 4 Automated Valet Parking in the APCOA P6 garage at Stuttgart Airport, where suitably equipped cars park and return themselves driverlessly using garage-installed infrastructure sensors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless parking of customer vehicles in a sensor-instrumented garage. It supports the parking output only where the facility is instrumented for the machine and the vehicles are specially equipped — conditions that amount to a purpose-built (E1) setting, not arbitrary mourners' cars.

sources.title: China deploys traffic robot to direct vehicles, pedestrians in streets
sources.claim: A humanoid traffic robot deployed at a Hangzhou intersection performs standardized stop/go gestures synchronized with the traffic-light network and flags violations, but it is a pilot that stands on one spot supporting human officers rather than independently managing vehicle movements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: directing road traffic. Included to show the state of the art in robotic vehicle direction: a fixed-position signalling pilot slaved to the light cycle with an officer standing by, which does not transfer to marshalling a funeral procession or waving mourners' cars into cemetery lanes.

tasks.label: Deliver floral arrangements or other items to family members of the deceased.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At the close of visitation or the funeral service in the funeral home chapel, the attendant gathers standing sprays on wire easels, baskets, wreaths and potted plants from around the casket and carries them out through the lobby and doors to family members' cars in the parking lot, fitting them into trunks, back seats and SUV cargo areas without crushing the blooms or spilling water.

In the funeral home office or arrangement room, the attendant retrieves and hands the family the cremated remains in an urn or temporary container, the deceased's personal effects (clothing, eyeglasses, jewelry), the register/guest book, memorial folders, prayer cards, certified death certificates and keepsake items, going through an inventory or receipt with the next of kin.

After the service the attendant loads the remaining arrangements into the flower car or van, drives to the family's private residence, carries the arrangements up the walk and steps, and hands them to a family member at the door or sets them inside; layout, parking, pets, weather and steps differ at every address.

At the cemetery the attendant unloads arrangements from the flower car and carries them across turf and gravel paths to the grave tent, and at the close of the committal takes individual roses from the casket spray and gives one to each family member seated under the tent before carrying leftover pieces back to family vehicles.

At the family's request, the attendant delivers leftover floral arrangements a day or two later to a nursing home, hospice, hospital or the family's church, carrying them in through the entrance and handing them to staff or residents at a front desk or day room.

sources.system: Shinjuku Rurikoin Byakurengedo automated columbarium (robotic urn storage/retrieval system)
sources.title: How Japan's 'virtual cemeteries' are reshaping mourning
sources.claim: An automated columbarium in Tokyo delivers the cremated remains of the deceased to visiting family members: the family presents an electronic card and a robotic storage-and-conveyance system fetches their urn from a vault and presents it at a private altar booth, then returns it.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same task at a purpose-built facility: an item associated with the deceased is machine-retrieved and delivered to family members who come to a fixed hand-off point, with no attendant carrying it.

sources.system: Cleveron 402 / 401 robotic parcel locker (Walmart Pickup Tower)
sources.date: 2019-08 (article); product line still sold and deployed as of 2025-11
sources.title: Automation comes to grocery pickup | Grocery Dive
sources.claim: Robotic parcel lockers automatically retrieve a specific customer's stored order and present it to that person at a console within about ten seconds; Cleveron units are the technology behind Walmart's in-store pickup towers and grocery pickup kiosks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated hand-off of a stored item to a named recipient. It transfers because the funeral-attendant instance, brought to a purpose-built setting, reduces to a machine retrieving the family's designated item from a fixtured store and presenting it to them.

sources.title: Placing flower bunches in buckets with robots - DERO GROEP
sources.claim: A patented robot cell automatically collects bunches of cut flowers and mixed bouquets and places them into buckets, handling a wide range of flower types at up to 5,000 bunches per ... in flower-processing lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grasping and moving delicate floral product without damage. It transfers to moving funeral arrangements only where the flowers arrive fixtured and presented on a line, i.e. a purpose-built setting.

sources.title: Super Trooper: Autonomous robot helps gardeners transport potted plants | SICK
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile handling robot transports potted plants weighing up to 10 kg around tree and garden nurseries, navigating with 3D LiDAR in outdoor horticultural conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pick-up and transport of potted plants, the same class of object as the potted plants and basket arrangements funeral attendants move, but in a nursery laid out for the machine.

sources.title: Meet Moxi, the newest nurse assistant of Trinity Michigan medical team - Bridge Michigan
sources.claim: Moxi autonomously navigates hospital hallways and elevators, uses an arm and gripper to fetch medications, equipment and lab specimens from supply areas, and delivers them in secure torso drawers to staff on the units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving a designated small item inside a human work facility and delivering it into a person's hands. Comparable object size and precision to an urn box, effects bag or memorial packet handed to a family member.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi is commercially deployed at scale: nearly 100 robots in over ... US hospital facilities, with more than 1.25 million deliveries completed and over 100,000 autonomous elevator rides.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes maturity and reliability of the item-delivery capability inside structured human facilities, supporting a worker-quality judgment for small-item hand-offs.

sources.title: Next-gen room service: How Relay 2 robots are revolutionizing the hotel experience | FOX 5 New York
sources.claim: Relay hotel robots autonomously ride elevators and travel corridors to bring guest-requested items such as towels, toiletries and food to the guest room door, calling the room and opening their lid for the guest; the higher-capacity Relay2 carries larger items like linens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous delivery of an item to a member of the public inside a structured facility, showing the corridor navigation and hand-off portion of the funeral-home instance is feasible at E2.

sources.system: Serve Robotics sidewalk robots; DoorDash Dot; Boston Dynamics Spot delivery test
sources.title: Physical AI's Biggest Challenge Is the Last 50 Feet | PYMNTS.com
sources.claim: As of mid-2026 sidewalk delivery robots operate at commercial scale but the doorstep hand-off remains unsolved: robots cannot climb stairs, and legged doorstep delivery (Boston Dynamics Spot riding in a van) is still only in testing.
sources.transferJustification: Supports the negative judgment at E3: no cited system carries an item from a vehicle up a private walk and hands it to a resident at the door.

tasks.label: Carry flowers to hearses or limousines for transportation to places of interment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: After a chapel service at the funeral home: attendant gathers 10-30 mixed floral pieces (easel sprays on wire stands, the casket spray, baskets, potted plants, wreaths) from around the casket and chapel, carries them by hand or on a flower cart through the foyer and out the doors, and packs/wedges them into the flower car or the hearse's rear compartment so nothing tips during the procession, working quickly among mourners and staff.

Off-site service at a church, temple, or fraternal hall: arrangements are carried down the aisle and exterior steps to a van, hearse, or limousine parked at the curb; layout is unfamiliar and differs site to site, doors must be held, and weather (rain, wind, snow, heat) is whatever it is.

Pre-service handling at the funeral home: florist deliveries are received at the back entrance, staged in a prep room or garage, then a few pieces (family flowers, casket spray) are carried out and loaded into the flower car or limousine trunk before the cortege leaves; level indoor floors, no public present.

At the cemetery (place of interment): attendant unloads the arrangements from the hearse/flower car, carries them across turf, gravel paths or a grade to the graveside tent, and sets them around the grave and casket; ground may be muddy, sloped or snowy and each grave site differs.

Minimal case: one or two pieces (a single casket spray or a couple of baskets) carried a short distance over level floor from a small visitation room to a hearse parked in the funeral home's attached garage or covered porte-cochere, with no crowd and no time pressure.

sources.date: product page retrieved 2025-09; product line in commercial use since ~2018
sources.title: Smart Placing: the robotic arm that picks up the plants and places them in a tray
sources.claim: A commercial robotic arm picks live potted plants off a carrier system and places them, undamaged, into trays presented automatically at a fixed station in a purpose-built packing line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pot-plant packing. Objects are live plants that bruise like funeral flowers; the machine grasps each presented piece and sets it into a supplied tray - the same pick-from-fixture / place-into-presented-rack motion that loading a fixtured flower rack requires at E1.

sources.system: WPS Smart Placing / Smart packing line (installations incl. Ammerlaan-Sosef, Gartneriet PKM)

instances.label: Routine floor care in the public areas of the funeral home: vacuuming carpet in the chapel and visitation rooms between viewings, mopping/scrubbing the hard floors of the lobby, hallways and entry. Interior detail cleaning round: cleaning and restocking the public restrooms, dusting furniture, casket displays and woodwork, wiping glass and door handles, emptying wastebaskets throughout the building, straightening/resetting chairs, kneelers and register stand after a service.

Mowing the turf on the funeral home grounds (front lawn, side yards, sometimes an adjoining chapel/cemetery lawn) on a weekly schedule during the growing season; mixed sun/shade turf with trees, monuments, signage and a parking lot edge.

Seasonal outdoor clearing: blowing/collecting leaves, clippings and litter off the lawn, walks and parking area in fall; clearing snow off the entry walks, portico and drive after winter storms so families can enter safely.

Washing and drying the funeral coach (hearse), lead car and family cars before and after each service, so the fleet is spotless for processions; done at the funeral home garage/wash area or a nearby wash facility.

Hands-on upkeep of funeral equipment and the building: cleaning and lubricating church trucks, cots and casket carriages, checking wheels/casters, servicing the graveside lowering device and tent/chair inventory, replacing bulbs and doing touch-up paint or small repairs, plus weeding/trimming beds and shrubs near the entrance.

tasks.label: Embalm, dress, cosmeticize, and casket the deceased.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult case in a funeral home preparation room: position and wash the body, set features (eye caps, mouth closure), raise the carotid or femoral vessels through an incision, ligate and cannulate, run arterial injection with drainage while massaging to check fluid distribution, aspirate and inject the cavities with a trocar, suture incisions, wash and dry the remains.

Dressing and casketing prepared remains in the prep room: putting undergarments, hosiery, shirt/suit or dress on a 150-250 lb rigid or flaccid body (often splitting garments up the back), then transferring the body into the casket with a lift or two-person lift, positioning head on the pillow, arranging hands, smoothing garments and casket interior for viewing.

Cosmetizing for viewing in the prep room: applying massage cream, cream or airbrush cosmetics matched to a family photo and skin tone, treating discoloration, shaving, cleaning and shaping nails, washing, drying and styling hair, and touch-ups in the chapel before the family's private viewing.

Difficult preparation cases: autopsied remains requiring multi-point (six-point) injection, treatment and return of viscera, cranial reconstruction; trauma or restorative-art cases needing suturing, wax modeling and reconstruction; jaundiced, edematous, or early-decomposition remains needing custom chemical strength and hypodermic treatment.

Special-handling cases: bariatric remains needing mechanical lifts and extra staff, infant or child cases with tiny vessels and delicate handling, frail or skin-slip remains, and infectious/contagious cases requiring full PPE and containment procedures, each carried through prep, dressing and casketing.

It is the nearest robotic work on human remains, but it performs a single planned needle puncture through a bag under CT; it does not make incisions, raise and cannulate vessels, run and monitor arterial injection, aspirate cavities, suture, dress, cosmetize or casket, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

It substantiates only percutaneous needle entry into a superficial vein of a fixtured living forearm; embalming requires a surgical incision, blunt dissection to raise the carotid or femoral artery, ligation, arterial tube placement, drainage management and cavity trocar work, none of which this system performs.

tasks.label: Transport the deceased to the funeral home.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential first call: attendants drive a removal van to a private home or home-hospice death, walk into a bedroom (sometimes a bathroom, floor, narrow hallway or stairs), transfer the deceased (often 150-250 lb deadweight, unembalmed, sometimes rigor or fluids) from bed to a removal cot with a sheet/body bag, cover and strap, wheel over carpet/thresholds/lawn, load into the van in front of grieving family, drive to the funeral home, unload and place in the prep room cooler.

Nursing home, assisted living or inpatient hospice removal: attendants are met by staff, go to the resident's room, transfer the deceased from the bed to the cot, use the service elevator and back exit as facility policy requires, load into the van at a rear door, drive to the funeral home and place the deceased in the prep room or cooler.

Hospital removal: paperwork/ID check at security, pickup from the hospital morgue where the deceased is already bagged and tagged on a tray in a refrigerated rack; slide the body onto the cot, wheel through service corridors to a loading dock, load the van, drive to the funeral home, unload into the cooler.

Medical examiner / coroner's office release: after autopsy, the bagged deceased on a tray is released from the cooler; the attendant checks release paperwork, transfers to the cot, loads into the van at the dock and transports to the funeral home prep room.

Transfer of already-encased remains: pick up a casketed body or air-tray shipping case from an airline cargo terminal, another funeral home, or a crematory; move the unit load with a church truck/roller lift onto the van floor or lift gate, secure it, drive to the funeral home and unload.

tasks.label: Assist with cremations and the processing and packaging of cremated remains.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Charging the retort: at a funeral-home or cemetery crematory, the attendant checks the cremation authorization, ID tag and name plate, brings the casket or cardboard alternative container out of the walk-in cooler or off a church truck, aligns it with the cremator door, opens the door, slides the container in, closes the door and starts the cycle. Containers range from 30 lb infant cases to 400+ lb bariatric cases.

Running and monitoring the cremation cycle: selecting the program for body weight/container type, watching chamber and afterburner temperatures and stack opacity on the control panel, adjusting air/burners, occasionally repositioning the case with a long rake to improve airflow, and taking the unit through burn-down and cool-down over roughly 1.5-3 hours.

Recovering the remains from the chamber: after cool-down, raking and sweeping every fragment of that individual's bone from the brick hearth into the clean-out chute and pan (often finishing with a brush or vacuum so nothing is commingled with the next case), letting the pan cool, then pulling out casket hardware, screws, hip and knee prostheses and other large metals with a magnet and by hand.

Processing: tipping the cooled bone fragments from the pan into a cremulator/processor, running it until the remains are a uniform sand-like consistency, separating out residual small metals (staples, dental work, orthopedic pins), and emptying the processing chamber completely so no remains carry over to the next case.

Standard packaging: transferring the processed remains into a sealed plastic bag with the numbered metal ID disc, placing the bag in the standard temporary container or box, applying a label with the decedent's name and case number, completing the log/chain-of-custody paperwork, and shelving the container for family pickup or preparing it for postal shipment.

Non-standard packaging: filling a family-supplied decorative urn (screw-bottom, threaded lid, sliding panel, marble, biodegradable scattering tube), or dividing the remains among several keepsake urns, jewelry pendants and scattering tubes, cleaning residue from the urn exterior, and securing the closure without spillage.
